title: Project Coordinator
Director, Health, Safety, & Organizational Resilience
description:
Competition number: 26-106

Salary: $131,945.00 - $156,298.00/Year Job Type: Permanent Full Time Closing Date: November 4, 2026 Position Overview:
The Director of Occupational Health, Safety & Organizational Resilience provides enterprise-wide strategic leadership for the transformation, modernization, and continuous improvement of the City's Occupational Health & Safety (OHS) Program. As a key member of the City's leadership team, the Director will shape and execute a forward-looking Corporate Safety Strategy that strengthens organizational resilience, reduces risk, and advances a culture of safety excellence across a diverse municipal workforce.

The Director will lead organizational change and influence leaders at all levels of the organization to embed safety, risk management, prevention, and employee well-being into strategic and operational decision-making. This position will build alignment across departments, engage union and employee partners, and create the conditions necessary for sustainable adoption of new policies, practices, systems, and behaviours.

The Director will provide strategic advice to senior leadership on occupational health and safety, enterprise risk, regulatory compliance, emerging workplace risks, and organizational readiness. The role will balance strategic leadership with operational oversight, translating the City's safety vision into measurable outcomes, strengthened organizational capability, and sustained cultural change.

Success in this role will require a leader who can influence, build trust across diverse stakeholder groups, navigate competing priorities, and create shared accountability for safety outcomes. Formalizing governance mechanisms, notably through a cross-functional team (CFT), which brings together operational, administrative, and safety leaders to provide coordination, consistency and accountability.

As the Director Occupational Health, Safety & Organizational Resilience, your key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

•Lead the development and execution of the City's Corporate Safety Strategy, establishing strategic priorities, objectives, performance measures, and accountabilities that align occupational health and safety with the City's broader strategic direction.

•Lead the transformation and modernization of the City's OHS Program, redesigning policies, processes, systems, and practices to reflect legislative requirements, leading practices, emerging risks, and the evolving needs of the organization.

•Lead organizational change associated with the transformation of the safety program, developing and executing change management strategies that build awareness, create alignment, address resistance, engage stakeholders, and achieve sustained adoption of new approaches and practices.

•Influence and partner with senior leaders, departmental leadership teams, managers, and employees to embed safety and risk management into strategic planning, operational decision-making, workforce practices, and organizational performance.

•Build organizational alignment and shared accountability for safety, using strong influencing, relationship-building, consultation, negotiation, and communication skills to bring diverse stakeholders together around common objectives.

•Establish and strengthen corporate safety governance, defining clear roles, responsibilities, accountabilities, escalation processes, and decision-making structures to support consistent and effective safety practices across the organization.

•Drive measurable improvements in safety performance, leveraging data, trends, leading and lagging indicators, risk assessments, and organizational insights to identify priorities and evaluate the effectiveness of safety strategies and interventions.

•Provide strategic advice and recommendations to the senior leadership team and Council, as appropriate, on significant health and safety risks, regulatory requirements, organizational exposure, emerging issues, and opportunities to strengthen workplace safety and resilience.

•Develop and maintain trusted relationships with managers, employees, union representatives, and other key stakeholders, fostering collaboration, credibility, transparency, and shared ownership of safety outcomes.

•Lead and develop a high-performing team of safety professionals, building organizational capability, professional expertise, leadership capacity, and a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

•Oversee significant incident investigations and organizational learning, ensuring rigorous root cause analysis, appropriate corrective and preventive actions, and effective follow-through to reduce recurrence and address systemic risks.

•Anticipate and respond to emerging risks, monitoring legislative and regulatory developments, industry trends, workforce trends, and changing operational environments to ensure organizational readiness and compliance.

•Champion continuous improvement and safety innovation, identifying opportunities to improve processes, leverage technology and data, enhance employee engagement, and increase the effectiveness and accessibility of safety programs.

•Lead strategic safety communications and engagement, ensuring employees and leaders understand the City's safety priorities, their individual and collective responsibilities, and the purpose and benefits of organizational change.

•Strengthen organizational resilience and readiness by identifying systemic vulnerabilities, enhancing prevention and response capabilities, and ensuring the City can effectively adapt to emerging occupational health and safety challenges.

•Champion a proactive safety culture and employee well-being, moving the organization beyond compliance toward prevention, learning, accountability, and sustained safety excellence.

Essential Qualifications:
The successful candidate will bring a minimum of ten years of progressive leadership experience in occupational health and safety, operations, public safety, human resources, or a related field, including significant experience leading organizational transformation, change management, continuous improvement, or enterprise-wide initiatives. Experience in a unionized and/or municipal environment would be considered an asset.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

•A university degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Human Resource Management, Occupational Health & Safety, or a related discipline, supplemented by post-secondary education in Occupational Health & Safety or a related field.

•A recognized professional certification in Occupational Health & Safety.

•Comprehensive knowledge of applicable occupational health and safety legislation, regulations, standards, and leading practices.

•Demonstrated success developing and executing enterprise-level strategies and transformational programs.

•Proven ability to lead and sustain organizational change, including the ability to build commitment, manage resistance, and translate strategy into practical and sustainable action.

•Exceptional ability to influence, build consensus, navigate competing interests, and create alignment among diverse stakeholders.

•Strong political acumen and the ability to operate effectively within a complex public-sector environment.

•Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships and influence senior leaders, managers, employees, union representatives, and external partners.

•Experience using data, performance measures, and risk intelligence to inform strategic decisions and demonstrate measurable outcomes.

•Exceptional communication, presentation, negotiation, consultation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate complex issues clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences.

•Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, develop, and engage high-performing professional teams.

•Strategic thinking combined with the ability to translate organizational priorities into practical implementation plans and measurable results.

•The ability to balance long-term strategic priorities with operational realities while maintaining focus on organizational outcomes.

An equivalent combination of education, training, and progressive leadership experience may be considered.

Applications will be accepted through our online system only. Qualified applicants should submit their resumes through the City's online application system.

The successful applicant may be eligible to participate in a Flexible Time Options Program which includes the option of working a 4 or 5-day work week, subject to business requirements.

## Equal Opportunity Employer:

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of the communities in which we live and which we serve. We encourage and support applications from Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, and members of visible minority groups. Candidates who belong to such groups, who are qualified, will be given preference at the time of selection.

Applications will be accepted through our online system only. Qualified applicants should submit their cover letters and resumes to:

City of Saint John

Attn: Hiring Committee

www.saintjohn.ca (careers)

Only those applicants being considered further will be contacted.

title: Supervisor, End User Services
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Supervisor, End User Services to join our IT Operations & Projects Canada & International team in Sudbury, Ontario.

Reporting to the Manager, IT Infrastructure & End User Services, the Supervisor, End User Services is accountable for the reliable and cost-effective delivery of workplace, end-user, field service, and mission-critical communications services across Vale Base Metals Canada and International operations.

The successful candidate will lead a team of IT professionals and service providers responsible for workplace technology, field support services, and operational communications technologies. This role plays a key part in ensuring operational readiness, service performance, vendor governance, lifecycle management, cybersecurity compliance, and the successful transition of new technologies into sustainable operations.

## In this role, you will:

## People Leadership & Stakeholder Management

• Lead and develop a team of End User Service professionals through coaching, mentoring, performance management, and career development.

• Foster strong relationships with operations, technology teams, vendors, and service providers.

• Promote a culture of safety, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer service excellence.

• Support workforce planning, resource allocation, and capability development.

## Network Governance & Architecture

• Service Delivery & Operations

• Develop and maintain the roadmap and operating model for end-user and workplace technology services.

• Monitor end-user service performance and ensure achievement of agreed service levels and operational objectives.

• Lead the response to major incidents, service disruptions, and operational issues.

• Drive continual improvement initiatives focused on customer experience, service reliability, and operational efficiency.

• Maintain accurate assets, lifecycle, configuration, and service ownership information.

• Identify risks, operational gaps, and supportability concerns within network solutions.

## Risk, Compliance & Governance

• Ensure compliance with Vale technology standards, cybersecurity requirements, privacy legislation, and audit controls.

• Monitor operational risks and implement mitigation strategies.

• Support business continuity and operational readiness for critical communications services, including radio, push-to-talk, and satellite technologies.

• Contribute to budget planning, financial stewardship, and cost optimization initiatives.

## Vendor & Technology Management

• Manage vendor relationships, contracts, service levels, and performance metrics.

• Partner with project, engineering, IT, and OT teams to ensure new technologies transition effectively into operations.

• Establish support models, documentation standards, lifecycle plans, and operational ownership for deployed technologies.

• Drive service quality improvements and accountability across internal and external service partners.

## About You

## Experience

• Minimum 8 years of experience in IT operations, end-user computing, workplace technology, or field service environments.

• Demonstrated leadership experience managing technical teams and third-party service providers.

• Experience in service delivery, operational support, incident management, and vendor management.

• Proven ability to manage operational performance, budgets, and service improvement initiatives.

• Experience supporting large-scale enterprise technology environments.

## Education

• College Diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Technology, or a related discipline.

• Bachelor's Degree is considered an asset.

## Skills & Competencies

• Strong understanding of ITIL service management practices and operational support processes.

• Strong leadership, coaching, and team development capabilities.

• Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and relationship-building skills.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.

• Experience with lifecycle management, operational readiness, service ownership, and continuous improvement.

• Ability to lead effectively in both office and industrial operating environments.

## Preferred Qualifications

• ITIL Foundation or related Service Management certification.

• PMP, Agile, or other project management certifications.

• Experience in mining, industrial, manufacturing, or operational technology environments.

• Experience managing enterprise workplace technologies and mission-critical communication systems.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans, and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are required for modern technologies such as AI and defence. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all.

We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other

fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Pay Grade: 15V

## Minimum Starting Salary: CAD $110,000

Apply by: Friday, Oct 23, 2026

Horizon Health Network in beautiful New Brunswick is looking for a Director of Pharmacy Professional Practice to join our team!

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) is seeking a strategic, influential and systems-oriented leader to join our team as a Director of Pharmacy Professional Practice and who should be able to identify organizational priorities and advance innovative, sustainable change through collaboration and thoughtful execution. Working for Horizon gives you a career that provides an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers.

You have a worked in a senior pharmacy leadership role for a minimum of five (5) years. You have experience in managing clinical pharmacy services and personnel including project management and program planning. You have an intermediate proficiency level in Microsoft Office applications.

You possess an entry-to-practice degree in Pharmacy, (e.g., Bachelor of Science in Pharmacy or Doctor of Pharmacy) and are licensed to practice in New Brunswick or eligible for licensure with the New Brunswick College of Pharmacists. Consideration will be given to those with advanced pharmacy education.

You are willing and able to travel throughout the province and possess a valid New Brunswick Driver's License.

You can write and speak English at an advanced level of competency.

## What you will do

The Director, Pharmacy Professional Practice will be joining our team at a very exciting time in our organization with a multi-year initiative to redesign our pharmacy practice model in the acute care, ambulatory care and primary care settings. Another initiative is also in progress to renovate and modernize our main pharmacies and compounding areas including our outpatient oncology clinic pharmacies. Horizon is also a key partner in provincial initiatives to develop and implement a new integrated clinical information system across our organization.

The Director, Pharmacy Professional Practice is responsible to:

• Lead the development, implementation and evaluation of a region-wide approach to evidence-informed, patient focused pharmacy care which aligns with a collaborative care model, scope of pharmacy practice and pharmacy practice standards

• Lead and/or support pharmacy research and education initiatives

• Lead and participate in recruitment and retention activities for pharmacy professionals and learners

• Communicate and collaborate within the regional department and at times involving leaders and decision-makers in other programs and departments

Core competencies for non-bargaining positions are based on the LEADS in a Caring Environment leadership capabilities framework: Lead Self, Engage Others, Achieve Results, Develop Coalitions, and System Transformation.

In addition to LEADS, all positions need to demonstrate compassion, patience, and professionalism in all interactions, consistently upholding a respectful and supportive environment for patients, clients, families, and colleagues. ## JOB PURPOSE

The Nurse Practitioner (NP) provides primary health care services, illness/injury prevention, chronic disease management and community development services, using a population health approach in an interdisciplinary team of providers. In keeping with the Horizon Health Network strategic plan, the provincial CHC framework, and the Community Health Program standards, the service model is based on the principles of primary health care with a primary goal of supporting communities in meeting their health care needs. The NP is a registered nurse with advanced educational preparation in nursing. As a member of the interdisciplinary team, the NP provides direct care to scheduled and unscheduled patients across the lifespan with a variety of health conditions. The NP evaluates patient outcomes, provides consultation to, and consults with other team members. The NP also utilizes research, leadership and educator knowledge and skills to support/provide health promotion, illness and injury prevention, and community development initiatives.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Baccalaureate degree in Nursing, Master's degree in Nursing preferred.

• Registration with NANB as a Nurse Practitioner.

• Current BCLS.

• Comprehensive knowledge in caring for clients across the health continuum and throughout the client's lifespan.

• Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills.

• Demonstrated organizational and leadership skills.

• Demonstrated ability to work cooperatively with other members of a team toward common goals.

• Demonstrated ability to function independently in the role with recognized decision-making and problem-solving skills.

• Demonstrated ability to critically analyze theory and research literature and apply to practice.

• Good work and attendance record.

• Physically able to perform assigned duties.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

## Health Assessment and Diagnosis

• Completes a comprehensive health assessment including, but not limited to, physical, psychological, cultural, spiritual and social needs of the patient/client.

• Orders, obtains, performs and interprets diagnostic and laboratory screening tests in accordance to schedules "A" and "B" of the NANB Rules Respecting Nurse Practitioners.

• Establishes a diagnosis.

• Initiates appropriate treatment plan in cooperation with the patient/client and other team members as indicated.

## Health Management of Acute and Chronic Conditions

• Demonstrates knowledge of current best-practice guidelines for the delivery of care

• Prescribes, adjusts and renews medications in accordance to Schedule "C" of the NANB rules respecting Nurse Practitioners.

• Monitors, evaluates and alters therapies and/or treatments when appropriate.

• Initiates timely referral or collaboration with other team members, as indicated.

## Health Promotion and Disease Prevention

• Demonstrates knowledge and understanding of health promotion services and facilitates primary, secondary and tertiary prevention strategies for all patients/clients

• Incorporates risk reduction and disease and injury prevention strategies for all patients/clients

• As part of the interdisciplinary team, participates in the development and implementation of community/population health interventions

## Professional Role and Responsibilities

• Maintains the competencies as outlined in the Competency and Standards of Practice for Nurse Practitioners in Primary Health Care.

• Actively participates as a team member to provide comprehensive care to all patients/clients.

• Exemplifies and promotes excellence in advance practice nursing care.

• Utilizes nursing and other research to support clinical knowledge and evidence-based practice

• Assumes responsibility for self-directed professional development

• Establishes a network of referral sources to accommodate the provision of care to patients/clients. Referral sources are internal and external to the organization.

• Functions as a resource person, preceptor and mentor to Nurse Practitioner students, peers and other health professional

• Participates in the development of the Nurse Practitioner advanced practice.

• Participates in the professional education activities at the clinic.

NOTE: The above are basic and prime responsibilities; related and allied duties may be assigned from time to time as may become necessary to the operation of the Health Authority.

## COMPETENCIES

• Professional Responsibility and Accountability

• Health Assessment and Diagnosis

• Therapeutic Management

• Health Promotion and Prevention of Illness and Injury

• Patient/Client Focus

description:

Working at Service New Brunswick is more than just a job — it's an opportunity to build a meaningful career. Guided by our vision of "Excellence in Service Delivery", our teams provide high-quality, innovative public services for customers with a focus on value for all New Brunswickers.

Known for our people-oriented workplace culture, we foster an environment where innovation, inclusivity, and teamwork are celebrated. We are proud to be recognized as one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers for 2026!

• Human-Centered: We prioritize well-being and flexibility for our employees.

• Driven by Growth: We invest in your professional development and career advancement.

• Celebrating Excellence: We recognize and reward outstanding contributions.

As a member of the Property Assessment Services team, the successful candidate will be responsible for administering the Assessment Act and its regulations.

• Inspecting and gathering data for residentially costed and unimproved property types

• Conducting residential land valuations including sales validations and preparation of land value maps

• Determining market factors for residential, farm and recreational properties and finalization of assessed values

• Conducting individual valuations of unimproved and improved residential, farm and recreational properties

• Undertaking requests for review inspections and preparing decisions for sign-off

• Preparing for and participating in appeal board hearings

## ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS:

• A university degree in Business Administration or Commerce, or

• Another university degree, plus 1 year of related experience

Subject to the response to this competition, an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Written and spoken competence in English is required. Please state your language capability.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please state your language capability on your application and ensure that preferred language for assessment is clearly identified.

For an applicant to meet the Residential Assessor II classification, the following Educational Requirements are also necessary:

• NB Property Law Course / BUSI 112 / DTR 1904 / IMA-401 and IMA-412;

• BUSI 330 / GUI 3102 / IMA-301;

• BUSI 400 / GUI 2103 / IMA-305; and

• NB Assessment Course / BUSI 443 / IMA-300

Most of the required courses have a BUSI, DTR, GUI, or IMA identification number. These are the identifications used by UBC, Laval, and the IMA which are the current education providers for the Appraisal Institute of Canada (AIC), the International Association of Assessing Officers (IAAO) or the Institute of Municipal Assessors within Canada.

If an applicant has successfully completed courses equivalent to current entry requirements for the Residential Assessor II classification from a previous course stream at that time, consideration may be given provided the applicant also meets all other requirements of the job posting. The applicant must demonstrate that they have completed all related requirements (through written confirmation by the AIC, IAAO or IMA) by the closing date of the competition. If an applicant intends to rely on course equivalencies, they must provide verification of equivalencies conferred by the course provider by the closing date of the competition.

The onus will not be on the screener to review transcripts of courses to determine that the listed courses did or did not meet the requirements. All candidates must provide written proof of education with their application to be considered for this competition.

• Frequent travel within the region is required, therefore candidates must possess a valid New Brunswick driver's license and have their own means of transportation.

• Candidates will be required to undergo Criminal History Clearance prior to appointment.

SPECIAL/OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS: Successful completion of assessment-related courses as required annually by management.

Can include but is not limited to work experience in the following sectors/fields:

• Customer Service; Construction; Banking; Real Estate; Accounting; Finance; Land Survey; Engineering.

• Commitment to Learning

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Information Seeking

• Integrity

• Ability to use Office Technology, Software and Applications

• Knowledge of Applicable Legislation and the Corporation's Policies and Procedures

• Planning and Organizing Skills

• Records and Information Management

• Specialized Subject Matter Expertise and Knowledge

• Residential Assessor II – $2,357 - $2,961 bi-weekly – Pay Group 4 - Technical Inspection, Laboratory and Medical

We strongly encourage you to submit your application via the online portal here, by using the "Apply" button to increase the efficiency and maintain a consistent candidate experience. Please ensure your application is completed by October 21, 2026.

This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

In the unlikely event that you experience technical difficulties or are unable to complete your application online, contact PC@snb.ca. Please ensure your application is completed by October 21, 2026 and indicate competition number R85-2026/27-473.

We thank all those who apply, however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

Veterans who demonstrate they are among the most qualified shall be given preference at the time of appointment.

description:
Title: Truck and Transport Mechanic (Service Tech I)
Salary: $33.95 hourly
BSA: $268.03 biweekly benefit spending allowance.

## Description:

Are you a Red Seal Service Technician who takes pride in keeping essential fleets moving? Join the City of Fredericton's Fleet Services team and put your expertise to work maintaining and repairing transit vehicles that help keep our community connected every day.

The City of Fredericton is seeking skilled fleet maintenance professionals to join its Fleet Services Division. Reporting to the Foreman, Fleet Services, the Service Technician is primarily responsible for performing maintenance and repairs on the City's transit fleet, with opportunities to work on other municipal fleet equipment as operational needs require. The successful candidate will utilize their technical expertise and previous experience to perform high-quality work at the journeyman level within the Truck and Transport & Heavy Equipment section. Assignments may be provided through written or verbal instructions, and completed work is evaluated through testing and the operational performance of vehicles and equipment.

Qualifications:

We recognize that candidates bring diverse experiences and backgrounds. Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate how their qualifications meet the essential requirements of the position. Additional valued qualifications may strengthen an application but are not required.

## Essential

To be considered for this position, applicants must demonstrate the following:

• Minimum prerequisite is Journeyman Truck & Transport Mechanic (Red Seal) certification OR finishing the final block training with demonstrated eligibility to challenge the Red Seal exam.

• Valid NB driver's license, class V.

• Knowledge of standard practices and equipment of the Truck & Transport & Heavy Equipment mechanic trade(s); knowledge of the principles of operation of gasoline and diesel engines and of mechanical repair methods applicable to a variety of fleet vehicles.

• A clear Criminal Record Check as well as a clear Driver's Abstract, are required as conditions of employment.

Equivalent combinations of education, training, and experience may be considered where they provide the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the essential duties of the position. Applicants are encouraged to describe how their background aligns with the requirements of the role.

## Valued

The following qualifications are not required but may strengthen an application:

• Five years of relevant experience in Truck and Transport & Heavy Equipment Repair field.

• Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety practices of the trade.

• Ability to understand and carry out oral and written instructions.

• Ability to diagnose or trouble shoot engine and electrical problems.

• Must have complete set of tools to perform the work listed above.

• Knowledge of Motor coach and Transit/Bus fleets would be an asset.

• Knowledge of Fire Suppression Assets and equipment including pumps would be an asset.

• Knowledge in Snow removal equipment and attachments, along with material spreading controls would be an asset.

## What You'll Do

• Adjust, troubleshoot, diagnose, repair or replace parts and components of heavy equipment/trucks and other related components.

• Installation of electrical equipment and accessories including 2-way radios, pay terminals, cameras, and other associated technologies.

• Perform scheduled maintenance service such as oil changes, lubrications and tune ups and tire changes.

• Complete reports to record problems and work performed.

• Other related duties as required.

Competitive, Progressive Pay Structure:
Grow your earnings with clearly defined technician levels based on experience, ability, and licensing:

• Service Tech I: $33.95/hour

• Service Tech II: $35.94/hour

• Service Tech III: $37.07/hour

• Advance your career while increasing your earning potential.

Generous Benefits Support:
Receive a biweekly Benefit Spending Allowance (BSA) of $268.03 to help offset the cost of your health and dental coverage. Any unused BSA credits can be allocated to a Health Spending Account (HSA) or taken as additional taxable earnings.

## Total Compensation Package:

A Service Tech earns approximately $77,850.36 - $84,362.17 annually, including base pay plus a biweekly benefits allowance of $268.03 with additional value from pension and comprehensive benefits.

Reliable Hours & Job Stability:
Benefit from a guaranteed 40-hour work week and long-term employment stability with a trusted employer.

Work-Life Balance You Can Count On:
Enjoy a predictable Monday-to-Friday schedule from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., giving you the freedom to plan your personal time with confidence and make the most of your evenings and weekends. While occasional overtime may be required to support operational needs and service delivery, all eligible hours worked outside of regular business hours are compensated at the applicable overtime rate.

Expand Your Technical Expertise:
Work with a wide range of equipment and brands, giving you valuable hands-on experience that strengthens your skills and career growth.

## Build a future with an employer that supports your life today and tomorrow.

At the City of Fredericton, we believe great employers offer more than just a salary. They provide stability, purpose, flexibility, and the confidence to plan for the future. That's why our total rewards package goes beyond your base salary to support your health, well-being, financial security, and work-life balance at every stage of your career and life.

## Health & Wellness Designed Around You

Your base pay is complemented by a biweekly flexible benefit spending allowance that helps you build the coverage that best fits your needs. Choose from comprehensive health, dental, and insurance options, and access confidential support through our Employee and Family Assistance Program.

## Time to Recharge

Enjoy vacation entitlements that grow with years of service, plus the option for eligible employees to purchase additional prorated leave each year, giving you greater flexibility to balance work and life.

## Retirement Security

Build long-term financial security through a shared risk pension plan, with contributions from both you and the City.

## Meaningful Work. Lasting Impact.

Help shape a vibrant, inclusive, and growing Fredericton. Your work will play a role in delivering services that make a significant and positive difference in the community.

## Our Commitment

The City of Fredericton is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace. We welcome applications from Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, racialized persons, and other equity-deserving groups. Qualified candidates who self-identify may receive preference in line with employment equity goals and applicable legislation.

If you require accommodation, please advise Human Resources so we can work with you to meet your needs

## Apply Now!

Please submit your application on or before October 23, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. AST.

title: Occupational Health and Safety Officer I- Competition Number: 2026/27-040-850860P
description:
## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context:

The Western Region maintains and supports approximately 1,100 NL Housing rental properties on the west coast of Newfoundland through offices in Corner Brook and Stephenville. The region provides a wide range of services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations including eviction prevention, and monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance. A variety of programs designed to support low to moderate income households and homeowners are also delivered. Regional staff members are involved in the delivery of the Provincial Home Repair, Home Modification, Home Energy Savings, Partner Managed Housing, and Rent Supplement Programs.

## Position Details

Competition Number:2026/27-040-850860P

Employment Type: Permanent

Department/Region: Western Region

Location: Corner Brook

Posting Status: Internal

Closing Date: September 16, 2026

Salary Scale: $55,993 to $61,984 (CG-28 $26.92 to $29.80 per hour) 40-hour work week

Duties:

Reporting to the Regional Maintenance Manager, the Occupational Health and Safety Officer will support the effective implementation and ongoing administration of the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) programs, policies, procedures, and safe work practices. The officer will promote awareness of and compliance with established OH&S requirements and applicable federal and provincial legislation, regulations and standards and will ensure staff are informed of the relevant updates or changes to policies, procedures and safe work practices throughout the Western and Labrador Regions. The officer will identify hazards and emerging safety concerns and recommend new or revised safe work practices where required to address workplace risks. The incumbent will develop and deliver OHS training to staff; conduct workplace inspections, safety audits, assessments and provide guidance to managers and employees on health and safety requirements and responsibilities. The Officer will work collaboratively with employees, supervisors, managers, and contractors to address safety concerns, investigate incidents, promote safe work practices, and ensure compliance with applicable requirements. The Officer will also prepare hazard assessments, daily logs, and technical reports; conduct industrial hygiene and environmental assessments where applicable; investigate workplace hazards; and provide recommendations to address safety concerns. The officer will also serve as an active member of the OH&S Committee and contribute to the identification and resolution of the workplace health and safety issues. The Officer will maintain current knowledge of OHS legislation, standards, and best practices through ongoing training and professional development and contribute to the continuous improvement and promotion of a safe and healthy workplace

## Screening Criteria

title: Upper River Valley Registered Nurse Class D (RNCD) - Nurse Practitioner PCN 1156411
description:
## JOB PURPOSE

The Nurse Practitioner (NP) provides primary health care services, illness/injury prevention, chronic disease management and community development services, using a population health approach in an interdisciplinary team of providers. In keeping with the Horizon Health Network strategic plan, the provincial CHC framework, and the Community Health Program standards, the service model is based on the principles of primary health care with a primary goal of supporting communities in meeting their health care needs. The NP is a registered nurse with advanced educational preparation in nursing. As a member of the interdisciplinary team, the NP provides direct care to scheduled and unscheduled patients across the lifespan with a variety of health conditions. The NP evaluates patient outcomes, provides consultation to, and consults with other team members. The NP also utilizes research, leadership and educator knowledge and skills to support/provide health promotion, illness and injury prevention, and community development initiatives.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Baccalaureate degree in Nursing, Master's degree in Nursing preferred.

• Registration with NANB as a Nurse Practitioner.

• Current BCLS.

• Comprehensive knowledge in caring for clients across the health continuum and throughout the client's lifespan.

• Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills.

• Demonstrated organizational and leadership skills.

• Demonstrated ability to work cooperatively with other members of a team toward common goals.

• Demonstrated ability to function independently in the role with recognized decision-making and problem-solving skills.

• Demonstrated ability to critically analyze theory and research literature and apply to practice.

• Good work and attendance record.

• Physically able to perform assigned duties.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

## Health Assessment and Diagnosis

• Completes a comprehensive health assessment including, but not limited to, physical, psychological, cultural, spiritual and social needs of the patient/client.

• Orders, obtains, performs and interprets diagnostic and laboratory screening tests in accordance to schedules "A" and "B" of the NANB Rules Respecting Nurse Practitioners.

• Establishes a diagnosis.

• Initiates appropriate treatment plan in cooperation with the patient/client and other team members as indicated.

## Health Management of Acute and Chronic Conditions

• Demonstrates knowledge of current best-practice guidelines for the delivery of care

• Prescribes, adjusts and renews medications in accordance to Schedule "C" of the NANB rules respecting Nurse Practitioners.

• Monitors, evaluates and alters therapies and/or treatments when appropriate.

• Initiates timely referral or collaboration with other team members, as indicated.

## Health Promotion and Disease Prevention

• Demonstrates knowledge and understanding of health promotion services and facilitates primary, secondary and tertiary prevention strategies for all patients/clients

• Incorporates risk reduction and disease and injury prevention strategies for all patients/clients

• As part of the interdisciplinary team, participates in the development and implementation of community/population health interventions

## Professional Role and Responsibilities

• Maintains the competencies as outlined in the Competency and Standards of Practice for Nurse Practitioners in Primary Health Care.

• Actively participates as a team member to provide comprehensive care to all patients/clients.

• Exemplifies and promotes excellence in advance practice nursing care.

• Utilizes nursing and other research to support clinical knowledge and evidence-based practice

• Assumes responsibility for self-directed professional development

• Establishes a network of referral sources to accommodate the provision of care to patients/clients. Referral sources are internal and external to the organization.

• Functions as a resource person, preceptor and mentor to Nurse Practitioner students, peers and other health professional

• Participates in the development of the Nurse Practitioner advanced practice.

• Participates in the professional education activities at the clinic.

NOTE: The above are basic and prime responsibilities; related and allied duties may be assigned from time to time as may become necessary to the operation of the Health Authority.

## COMPETENCIES

• Professional Responsibility and Accountability

• Health Assessment and Diagnosis

• Therapeutic Management

• Health Promotion and Prevention of Illness and Injury

• Patient/Client Focus

description:
Position: Senior Director, Valuation Services

Salary: $137,018.87 - $161,198.67 (Starting salary will reflect the successful candidate's relevant experience and demonstrated skills)

Position Type: Full Time, Permanent

Location: Remote First, within Nova Scotia

Department: Assessment Operations

Apply: Online via Career Beacon by clicking "Apply Now"

## About Property Valuation Services Corporation

Property Valuation Services Corporation (PVSC) is an independent, not-for-profit organization that provides property assessment services and information to Nova Scotia municipalities and property owners.

We employ approximately 135 people who live and work in over 60 communities across the province.

Local governments use our annual property assessments to establish their municipal property tax rates, which fund important local services and infrastructure, and build communities.

## About the Opportunity

Reporting to the Vice President, Operations, the Senior Director, Valuation Services oversees assessment operations, valuation services, workforce capacity, and performance to support the delivery of Nova Scotia's annual assessment roll under the Nova Scotia Assessment Act.

The Senior Director aligns people, priorities, and resources to meet operational and service commitments while working closely with quality assurance colleagues.

As a key member of the operations leadership team, the Senior Director turns organizational priorities into action and is accountable for assigned areas that support effective assessment services.

## What You'll Do

Operational Leadership and Delivery

• Oversee the timely delivery and defence of Nova Scotia's annual assessment roll.

• Guide Assistant Directors and align priorities, resources, and work plans with the annual assessment cycle.

• Monitor operational readiness, performance, risks, and resource needs, acting as required.

People Leadership and Talent Development

• Lead, coach, and support the Assistant Director team.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and employee engagement.

• Strengthen leadership capacity through development, workforce planning, succession planning, and mentoring.

Strategic Support and Operational Integration

• Translate strategic priorities into clear operational plans and deliverables.

• Connect people, processes, technology, and data to support operational priorities.

• Provide practical advice on operational risks and opportunities, and lead improvements to service delivery.

Valuation Quality and Operational Excellence

• Promote consistent standards, processes, controls, and reporting across operations.

• Provide operational oversight for industry accepted valuation approaches, methodologies, models, and tools.

• Work across valuation, data science, and technology teams to strengthen practices and service delivery.

• Lead process, technology, and business improvements that enhance organizational effectiveness.

Stakeholder and Industry Relationships

• Build strong relationships with municipal clients, industry representatives, and colleagues across PVSC.

• Represent PVSC in stakeholder meetings, industry forums, committees, and professional associations.

• Evaluate emerging trends and apply leading practices to improve operations.

Take on other related duties and contribute to additional initiatives, as assigned.

## What You'll Bring

You have a bachelor's degree in business administration, commerce, public administration, or a related discipline, along with at least 10 years of property assessment experience, including 5 years in progressively responsible leadership roles. An equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience may also be considered.

You also hold an industry designation from a recognized organization, such as the Appraisal Institute of Canada, International Association of Assessing Officers, Institute of Municipal Assessors, or Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors.

You bring the ability to:

• Apply extensive knowledge of property assessment, valuation, mass appraisal, industry standards, and the assessment cycle.

• Interpret the Nova Scotia Assessment Act, related legislation, and government structures.

• Lead and develop large operational teams through coaching, succession planning, and performance management.

• Manage performance, resources, risks, and service delivery in a complex environment.

• Analyze issues, make sound decisions, solve problems, and resolve conflict.

• Lead change, improve processes, and develop practical recommendations.

• Communicate clearly and build strong relationships with internal and external partners.

The following experience and credentials are considered assets:

• Experience leading large operational teams through change and modernization initiatives.

• Project management, leadership, or continuous improvement certifications.

Special Requirements

• This role requires occasional travel throughout Nova Scotia. A valid Class 5 driver's license and access to reliable transportation are required.

## Why You'll Enjoy Working Here

At PVSC, you'll be part of a workplace where people feel valued, supported, and connected, while being trusted to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact. We believe great results come from great people, so we invest in growth, encourage new ideas, and succeed together through shared accountability and continuous improvement.

## Qualifications and Occupational Experience:

• The minimum educational qualification for this position is a Bachelor's degree with a focus on adult education, neuroeducation, special education, psychology, social work, or other related field. Certificate in Applied Disability Studies is considered an asset.

• You have a minimum of three years of recent and relevant occupational experience developing and supporting academic accommodation plans for students with disabilities in a post-secondary environment.

• You have strong demonstrated experience using computer applications such as the Microsoft Office Suite, E-mail, Microsoft Teams, and have relevant experience with case file management, assistive technologies, and learning management systems.

• You have specific knowledge and understanding of using online environments to support students.

• You are comfortable working in a digital environment; you take responsibility for acquiring knowledge about advancing technology; and you are committed to using technology to create an exceptional student experience.

• You have demonstrated knowledge of adult learning and student development principles, disabilities, and learning support intervention.

• You have experience in workshop preparation, delivery, and facilitation.

• You have experience supporting/providing service to students and prospective students.

## Relevant Skills and Knowledge

• You demonstrate a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, accessibility and anti-racism.

• You demonstrate a high level of problem solving, critical thinking and professional judgement while acting independently to serve students holistically and equitably under parameters of policy and external agreements.

• You possess excellent interpersonal skills that enable you to interact with a diversity of people and support resolution of issues.

• You demonstrate understanding of and skill in interviewing techniques and professional boundaries, including privacy and confidentiality.

• You are known for your superior customer service skills and are able to create a relationship of trust beyond the immediate interaction.

• Your superb team working skills enable you to contribute positively to a team environment

• You have specific technical occupational knowledge and skill in assistive technology and developing accommodation plans.

• You have specific knowledge and understanding of diverse populations including Indigenous populations.

• You understand universal design principles to model and promote accessibility among students, colleagues, and educational partners

• You possess excellent coordination skills specifically related to organizing supports and accommodations for students.

• You have proven records management skills and abilities in keeping confidential case notes, creating and maintaining electronic student files, data logging and tracking.

• Excellent communication skills while working with colleagues and serving students in both physical and virtual environments.

Responsibilities

## What you will be doing…

Reporting to the Manager, Student Supports, and under the functional guidance of the Manager, Student Accessibility Services, you are accountable for leading accommodation planning and approval for students with disabilities. This includes but is not limited to supporting student accommodation requests, collecting student documentation, evaluating student requests in relation to their documentation and the nature of programming, applying professional judgement and expertise related to the impact of disability in the NSCC environment and consulting with qualified assessing professionals as needed.

For example, you will:

• Provide learning strategies to complement student accommodation plans including, but not limited to, improving learning skills, integrating technology, accessing learning resources and tools and developing communication plans with faculty.

• Organize services, refer students to appropriate learning supports, assess eligibility for funding programs, facilitate government mandated funding applications, and comply with external government partners' processes and legislation.

• Further the College's vision of equity in relation to our legal duty to accommodate in accordance with the Human Rights Commission, liaise with the Centre for Teaching and Learning and collaborate with faculty members on the implementation of accommodation plans and supports.

• Contribute to and participate in campus initiatives and signature events.

As part of the Student Supports team, you will participate in, or at times lead, the organization of campus events, activities, or committees that contribute to the distinctive student experience, such as Orientation, Wellness Week, and Convocation. You are passionate about supporting students and providing excellent customer service.

To achieve regular status; all probationary, full or part-time Professional Support employees of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Professional Support employees whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with experience engaging stakeholders at multiple levels.

• 2 years of underground mining experience is an asset, however EITs with less experience are encouraged to apply.

Often referred to as the "Hub of the North," Thompson is a city deeply intertwined with the mining industry, particularly due to its rich deposits of nickel. title: IT Asset Management (ITAM) Manager
description:
Position Type:
Permanent

If you're looking for a fulfilling career that can make a real difference in your life, and the lives of others, you've come to the right place.

As a national health solutions partner, we put people first in everything we do - and that begins with our team of 8,000+ professionals who bring a cross-section of diverse life experiences and career expertise to Medavie. By collaborating and innovating together, our employees are creating industry-leading solutions in insurance, primary care and emergency medical services that impact millions of lives in Canada each year.

Our mission is to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest - and it's reflected in our award-winning culture. We celebrate individuality and value the diverse perspectives and skills our employees contribute. We go beyond providing competitive pay and comprehensive benefits to offer opportunities for personal and professional growth, flexible work options, meaningful experiences, and supportive leadership. Medavie is where employees can be their best selves, feel they belong, and achieve their full potential. Be part of it by applying for a position with us today.

## The Opportunity

We are looking for a strategic and collaborative leader to establish, govern, and continuously evolve our enterprise IT Asset Management (ITAM) practice.

In this role, you will help shape how technology assets are managed across their lifecycle, ensuring our hardware, software, cloud subscriptions, licensing, and related lifecycle data are visible, trusted, compliant, and aligned with business needs. Your work will directly support service reliability, financial stewardship, risk management, and informed decision-making across the enterprise.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys building mature practices, strengthening governance, improving data quality, and influencing outcomes across technical, operational, financial, and business teams. You will play a key role in helping the organization maximize the value of its technology investments while enabling scalable, efficient, and well-governed services.

## What You'll Do

• Lead and continuously mature the enterprise IT Asset Management practice across hardware, software, licensing, cloud subscriptions, and related lifecycle data.

• Develop, own, and maintain the ITAM practice framework, including policies, standards, governance controls, lifecycle processes, and operating procedures spanning acquisition, deployment, maintenance, optimization, and retirement.

• Champion trusted asset data by improving visibility, accuracy, ownership, and lifecycle integrity across asset inventories, registers, configuration records, and service management systems.

• Strengthen governance and compliance practices by leading software licensing oversight, audit readiness activities, evidence management, and controls related to unmanaged or unauthorized assets.

• Partner with IT Operations, Finance, Procurement, Security, service owners, and technical teams to support lifecycle planning, renewals, capacity management, cost optimization, risk management, and service reliability objectives.

• Define requirements for ITAM tools, data integrations, dashboards, reporting, and automation that improve enterprise visibility, decision-making, and operational efficiency.

• Deliver timely, meaningful reporting, insights, and recommendations that help optimize technology investments, reduce waste, support contract and audit readiness, and enable sound operational and investment decisions.

• Drive continuous improvement by redesigning processes, advancing practice maturity, strengthening integration with adjacent ITSM and security practices, improving data quality, and implementing scalable lifecycle controls.

## What You Bring

Education: Post-secondary degree or diploma in Computer Science or an equivalent combination of education and experience. A bachelor's degree in Information Technology or Computer Science is preferred.

• 10+ years of relevant experience in IT Asset Management, IT Service Management, and/or IT Operations.

• Strong knowledge of IT asset lifecycle management, including acquisition, deployment, maintenance, optimization, and retirement.

• Working knowledge of asset registers and inventories, software licensing, compliance, reporting, and governance controls.

• Strong understanding of how ITAM integrates across ITSM practices, including Change, Configuration, Security, and service delivery.

• Experience with ITAM and ITSM tools, reporting, data management, integrations, dashboards, and automation. Experience designing, maturing, and governing enterprise-scale ITAM practices is preferred.

• ITIL 4 Foundation certification is required. Additional IT Asset Management certifications are preferred.

Language Requirement: Bilingualism (EN/FR) is considered an asset. English is requirement, written and verbal, to provide services to our customers and communicate with internal stakeholders

Reliability Status Clearance (Enhanced Level B): This includes fingerprinting, a criminal record check and a credit check. You must have resided in Canada for at least five years and hold Permanent Resident or Canadian Citizenship status.

Why Join This Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity to build and shape an enterprise capability that influences how technology is governed, optimized, and invested in across the organization.

While this is an individual contributor role, you will have significant influence through practice leadership, governance, stakeholder partnerships, trusted reporting, and cross-functional decision support. You will work across multiple disciplines, bringing together technology, operations, finance, procurement, security, and service management to improve how IT assets are managed and how technology value is realized.

If you enjoy creating structure, improving processes, building trusted data foundations, and helping organizations make better decisions, this role offers meaningful visibility and impact at an enterprise scale.

description:
## JOB PURPOSE

The ER Registered Nurse provides high-quality, patient centered care in the Emergency Department (ER) as the primary area of responsibility. The role also includes orientation and cross-training in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), with the expectation of providing clinical coverage in the ICU as needed.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Current registration in good standing with the Nurse's Association of New Brunswick.

• Bachelor's Degree preferred or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Minimum 2 years Acute Care Nursing experience; ICU and/or ER nursing strongly preferred.

• Critical Care or Emergency Nursing Certification considered an asset.

• Current BLS, ACLS and BCMI required; TNCC, PALS, ENPC, and/or NRP considered and asset. Willingness to obtain necessary certification within 1 year of hire.

• NB Critical Care Course or equivalent. Willingness to take same.

• Demonstrated ability to perform under pressure with strong assessment, prioritization, and critical thinking skills.

• Excellent communication and teamwork skills.

• Commitment to evidence-based practice and continuous quality improvement.

Working Conditions

• Rotating shifts, including days, evenings, nights, weekends and holidays.

• Frequent standing, walking, lifting, and repositioning of patients; use of specialized equipment.

• Exposure to infectious diseases, biohazards, hazardous medications, and emotionally stressful situations.

• Fast-paced, high-acuity environment requiring rapid decision-making and multi-tasking.

Reporting Structure

Will report directly to the ED nurse manager with accountability to Professional Practice and Clinical Educators/Resource Nurse.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

ER (Primary Care)

• Maintain competence in emergency nursing skills.

• Provide care to patients across the lifespan, including triage, stabilization, and treatment.

• Assist with resuscitations, trauma care, and urgent procedures.

• Support seamless transfer of patients from ER to other units as necessary.

• Familiarity with pediatric and obstetrical emergencies.

• Stabilization and initial management of acute/critical presentations (trauma, MI, stroke, sepsis, overdose and psychiatric emergencies).

ICU (Secondary Area)

• Deliver specialized nursing care to the critically ill patients, including assessment, monitoring, intervention, and evaluation.

• Manage advanced therapies and equipment (ventilators, hemodynamic monitoring, vasoactive infusions et cetera)

• Collaborate with physicians, respiratory therapists, and other members of the healthcare team to implement individualized care plans.

• Respond promptly to changes in patient condition, initiating emergency interventions when necessary.

• Provide education updates, and psychosocial support to patients and families.

Hospital-Wide Duties

• Respond to ACT calls to provide critical care expertise at the bedside outside of ICU.

• Assist with intra- and inter-facility transfers, ensuring safe stabilization, documentation and communication.

• Maintain accurate and timely documentation in patient records.

• Adhere to hospital policies, procedures, and best practice guidelines.

• Contribute to patient safety, infection control, and continuous quality improvement initiatives.

• Participate in professional development, staff and personal education, and interdepartmental collaboration.

Employees are responsible to be aware of and understand Horizon's Terms of Employment

• Advanced assessment skills (neuro, cardio, respirator, renal and multi-system).

• Proficiency with invasive and non-invasive monitoring (arterial lines, central lines et cetera).

• Ventilator management and advanced airway support.

• Medication administration and titration.

• Hemodynamic monitoring and interpretation.

• Proficiency with ACLS and resuscitation protocols.

• Post-operative critical care management.

• Pain and sedation management.

• End-of-life care, palliative measures, and family support in critical situations.

• Strong clinical decision making and critical thinking under pressure.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

• Ethical decision-making and advocacy for patients and families.

• Cultural competence and trauma-informed care.

• Teamwork and conflict resolution in high stress environments.

• Coordination and leadership during codes, ACT calls and rapid responses.

title: Fredericton Registered Nurse Class D (RNCD) - Nurse Practitioner PCN 1152373
description:
## JOB PURPOSE

The Nurse Practitioner (NP) provides primary health care services, illness/injury prevention, chronic disease management and community development services, using a population health approach in an interdisciplinary team of providers. In keeping with the Horizon Health Network strategic plan, the provincial CHC framework, and the Community Health Program standards, the service model is based on the principles of primary health care with a primary goal of supporting communities in meeting their health care needs. The NP is a registered nurse with advanced educational preparation in nursing. As a member of the interdisciplinary team, the NP provides direct care to scheduled and unscheduled patients across the lifespan with a variety of health conditions. The NP evaluates patient outcomes, provides consultation to, and consults with other team members. The NP also utilizes research, leadership and educator knowledge and skills to support/provide health promotion, illness and injury prevention, and community development initiatives.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Baccalaureate degree in Nursing, Master's degree in Nursing preferred.

• Registration with the College of Nursing of New Brunswick (CNNB) as a Nurse Practitioner.

• Current BCLS.

• Comprehensive knowledge in caring for clients across the health continuum and throughout the client's lifespan.

• Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills.

• Demonstrated organizational and leadership skills.

• Demonstrated ability to work cooperatively with other members of a team toward common goals.

• Demonstrated ability to function independently in the role with recognized decision-making and problem-solving skills.

• Demonstrated ability to critically analyze theory and research literature and apply to practice.

• Good work and attendance record.

• Physically able to perform assigned duties.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

## Health Assessment and Diagnosis

• Completes a comprehensive health assessment including, but not limited to, physical, psychological, cultural, spiritual and social needs of the patient/client.

• Orders, obtains, performs and interprets diagnostic and laboratory screening tests in accordance to schedules "A" and "B" of the NANB Rules Respecting Nurse Practitioners.

• Establishes a diagnosis.

• Initiates appropriate treatment plan in cooperation with the patient/client and other team members as indicated.

## Health Management of Acute and Chronic Conditions

• Demonstrates knowledge of current best-practice guidelines for the delivery of care

• Prescribes, adjusts and renews medications in accordance to Schedule "C" of the College of Nursing of New Brunswick (CNNB) rules respecting Nurse Practitioners.

• Monitors, evaluates and alters therapies and/or treatments when appropriate.

• Initiates timely referral or collaboration with other team members, as indicated.

## Health Promotion and Disease Prevention

• Demonstrates knowledge and understanding of health promotion services and facilitates primary, secondary and tertiary prevention strategies for all patients/clients

• Incorporates risk reduction and disease and injury prevention strategies for all patients/clients

• As part of the interdisciplinary team, participates in the development and implementation of community/population health interventions

## Professional Role and Responsibilities

• Maintains the competencies as outlined in the Competency and Standards of Practice for Nurse Practitioners in Primary Health Care.

• Actively participates as a team member to provide comprehensive care to all patients/clients.

• Exemplifies and promotes excellence in advance practice nursing care.

• Utilizes nursing and other research to support clinical knowledge and evidence-based practice

• Assumes responsibility for self-directed professional development

• Establishes a network of referral sources to accommodate the provision of care to patients/clients. Referral sources are internal and external to the organization.

• Functions as a resource person, preceptor and mentor to Nurse Practitioner students, peers and other health professional

• Participates in the development of the Nurse Practitioner advanced practice.

• Participates in the professional education activities at the clinic.

NOTE: The above are basic and prime responsibilities; related and allied duties may be assigned from time to time as may become necessary to the operation of the Health Authority.

• Health Assessment and Diagnosis

• Therapeutic Management

description:
Position Type:
Permanent

Closing date:
2026-10-15

Emergency Medical Care Inc. (EMC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS) that manages and operates ground ambulance, air medical transport and the medical communications operations in Nova Scotia through a performance-based contract with the provincial government's Emergency Health Services (EHS) Operations division and the Department of Health and Wellness. As well, EMC operates TeleHealth/811 medical communications for Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island for the Department of Health.

We access all communities in Nova Scotia in a timely and efficient manner with our fleet of more than 180 ambulances and support vehicles operating out of 60+ stations. We respond to 165,000+ calls annually across the province, which are actively managed through the EHS Operations Medical Communications Centre, the hub of all emergency (911) and non-emergency (hospital transfers) medical calls.

The EHS Operations LifeFlight program provides even greater accessibility by responding to patients on scene or through inter-facility transports by our critical care team via helicopter, fixed wing, or ground ambulance.

In addition, paramedics in Nova Scotia participate in various programs both urban and rural such as community-based paramedic programs, collaborative emergency centres, and emergency preparedness and special operations, to name a few.

There are lots of opportunities waiting for you in Nova Scotia. Apply now to learn more about our service and available positions.

## Nature and Scope:

Work within a collaborative, inter-professional team to appropriately manage and support caller access to health care services to meet their non-emergent, non-life-threatening health situations. The MCC-N will perform secondary telephone based medical triage of lower acuity 911 EHS calls, performing patient assessment, formulating treatment plans and assisting patients in arranging appropriate care using information and with the support of evidence -based, computer decision support software, clinical guidelines, protocols and other resources. The MCC-N will use critical thinking, therapeutic communication and clinical decision-making skills to assess, plan, implement, educate and evaluate the patients' health situation and/or informational needs.

## Duties and Responsibilities:

• Demonstrates accountability for own nursing practice by complying with the Canadian Nurses Association (CAN) Code of Ethics, and Nova Scotia College of Nursing Standards for Nursing Practice.

• Delivers appropriate patient care within the RN's scope of practice and the MCC-N scope of employment.

• Provides nursing care within the standards defined by professional nursing body, which has been legislated by the province to regulate and license registered nurses.

• Provides telephone based clinical care advice, alternate care pathway and service referral to individuals through the effective application of registered nursing skills, clinical judgment, computer-based decision support software, appropriate evidence-based clinical guidelines, and other relevant information databases/resources.

• Using in-depth clinical knowledge, applies process to identify patient care needs, risks and safety issues, educational opportunities, and appropriate health care referrals.
