title: ETO (Electro-Technical Officer)
description:
Since 1982, Norbulk has been a provider of ship management services, providing technical ship management, crew management, technical services and commercial ship management. We are a privately owned company, with a long term focus, investing in our seafarers and shore staff to equip them with the skills and knowledge needed to further their careers and continually improve our marine operations. Norbulk is headquartered in Bermuda, with offices in North America, Europe, The Middle East and Asia. Norbulk carries out ship management for all vessel types. At Norbulk, we are committed to Health and Safety of our seafarers and the protection of the environment.

Our Saint John, New Brunswick office manages two Canadian Oil Tanker Vessels and we are currently recruiting an ETO (Electro-Technical Officer) with Ocean Service Ltd.

EDUCATION:

Diploma in Electrical Engineering or equivalent marine qualification.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Responsible to the Chief Engineer for the maintenance and condition of electrical equipment assigned to his care, in accordance with the instructions issued by the Chief Engineer. Duties include but are not limited to:

· Monthly inspections of the vessel's electrical equipment with special attention being paid to tankship electrical equipment in respect to hazardous areas outside machinery spaces and accommodation areas.

· Providing a monthly report on the serviceability of electrical equipment for the Chief Engineer with special attention to gas tightness and intrinsic integrity of tankship equipment.

· Isolating electrically operated machinery or circuitry to enable maintenance or other work to be carried out safely (See NS HSM - Health and Safety Manual).

· Weekly checks of ship's emergency batteries and GMDSS equipment.

· Assist as necessary during entering/leaving port.

· Assist in the preparation of requisitions for electrical equipment stores and spare parts and submit them to the Chief Engineer for approval.

· Maintain an inventory of the materials on hand and on order to make both the normal routing supplies and specific demands for stores.

· Carry out receipt checks and sign for the materials and goods when delivered, ensuring they are properly labelled, preserved, stowed and secured to avoid loss from damage or deterioration.

· Maintain control over the issuance and usage of tools and materials and other goods in his charge to prevent waste.

· Upon joining the vessel, the Electrical Officer must report to the Master and then the Chief Engineer. He must consult with the Officer he is relieving regarding the machinery and equipment for which he will be responsible. He will then inspect such machinery and equipment, reporting any deficiencies to the Chief Engineer.

· Complete NS PER 006 (Handover Report) & NS SAF 001 (Shipboard Familiarisation Record).

· The Electrical Officer is additionally responsible for the serviceability and cleanliness of the vessel's electrical systems and equipment including but not limited to the following items:

- Main, auxiliary and emergency switchboard;

- Alternators (including the routine testing of the emergency unit);

- Starters and motors;

- Cargo handling equipment (where appropriate);

- Electrical and electronic control equipment for engine, cargo and deck machinery;

- Communications equipment;

- Accommodation, lighting and galley services;

- Refrigerated container power boxes/sockets;

- Maintenance of power sources for GMDSS equipment.

Qualifications:

Certificates: Electrician Certified Marine Advanced First Aid, Marine Emergency Duties, Marine Medical, Passport (must be able to travel to the States), Securities Training with Designated Duties, WHMIS, Confined Space, Basic Oil and Chemical Tanker Familiarization, Seaman's Discharge Book, and Fatigue Management. Marine certification will take priority; however, for a strong candidate we are willing to assist in receiving the proper certification.

Our ideal candidate is solutions oriented, has a strong work ethic, and works well in a team environment. Our full time employees work 40 days on 40 off, and have a competitive benefits package for them and their families. We provide paid travel to and from the vessel; therefore, the position is open to anyone living in Canada.

If you or someone you know in your professional network is interested in this exciting opportunity please send you CV to norbulksjnorbulknb.com

We thank all applicants for their interest, however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

• Mentor and develop staff using a supportive and collaborative approach, assigning accountabilities, set objectives, establish priorities, monitor, and evaluate results.

• Lead, accountable for and oversee the annual development and implementation of the operations business planning process and budgets.

• Work in conjunction with the Director, System Performance to ensure the application of clinical competency maintenance programming that allows clinical management staff to maintain clinical skills and registration.

• Coordinate labor contingency plans in conjunction with Human Resources.

• Oversight and coordination of special events and/or disasters that will impact our provincial system in whole or part.

• Ensure the appropriate staffing/training policies and procedures are in place at the supervisory level to ensure the consistent application of operational, contractual, procedures on a daily/weekly/annual basis.

• Responsible for business continuity in the event of situations impacting MHNL's ability to deliver service.

• Serve as a management liaison on various boards and committees; and

• Provide leadership by participating, supporting, and ensuring accountabilities for all initiatives that foster a culture of patient safety and a safe work environment.

## Professional Qualifications & Competencies:

• Post-secondary education is required in the health sciences field, or related field or approved equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Post graduate studies or master's degree, preferably in the business field, is preferred.

• Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience, preferably in EMS management within a high-performance accredited system.

• Experience in the service and/or health care sector is an asset.

• Valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 4 Drivers License (or equivalent) or the ability to obtain one, with a satisfactory driving record.

• Member in good standing of your licensure association.

• Demonstrated experience in a geographically dispersed, complex, multi program/service environment including multi-unionized environments.

• Demonstrated ability to effectively lead in times of meaningful change.

• Experience with operations and financial performance.

• Specialized knowledge in business development planning and project management is required; and

• Possess an active paramedic license in good standing with your professional association.

• Are an effective two way internal and external communicator who can build and foster positive relationship with employees and stakeholders.

• Are a visible leader with a proven record of empowering and leading employees successfully.

• Are someone who can demonstrate a broad understanding of principals of financial management and marketing expertise necessary to assist with negotiations while using cost-benefit thinking to set priorities and manage expenditures.

• Are an individual with intimate and vast knowledge of the Newfoundland and Labrador health care and delivery of emergency services.

• Are a leader who models a high standard of ethics, is honest and fair in all dealings; and

• Have the ability to formulate objectives and priorities by implementing plans consistently with the long-term interest of the organization in a global environment capitalizing on opportunities and managing risks.

## Salary Range

• $130,000 to $150,000 annually.

The Base Pay range may vary depending on the successful candidate or other relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience and education/training. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Medavie employees may participate in various performance-based incentive programs. Payments under these programs are discretionary and subject to both individual and organizational results.

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

## Who we are

MHNL is the selected proponent to design, manage and operate a single, integrated road and air ambulance service in Newfoundland and Labrador. We are an incorporated, wholly owned NL-based subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS), the largest contracted provider of emergency management services in Canada and a national leader in primary health care solutions, including mobile integrated health and community paramedicine programs.

Together with Medavie Blue Cross, MHS is part of Medavie, a national health solutions partner and innovative leader in benefits management, health management, and healthcare delivery. Backed by our team of over 8,200 dedicated professionals, we exist to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest.

We're one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, and certified Rainbow Registered as an organization that champions diversity, equity and inclusion. We foster a culture of caring where people are celebrated beyond their roles and valued for who they are and what they contribute.

If you share our mission of improving the wellbeing of Canadians, join our team.

## What it's like to work with us

We are more than just a workplace - we are a people-focused, visionary organization dedicated to fostering well-being and making a meaningful impact on the lives of our employees and the Communities we serve.

We celebrate individuality and value the diverse perspectives and skills our employees contribute. We go beyond providing competitive pay and comprehensive benefits by offering opportunities for personal and professional growth, meaningful experiences, and supportive leadership. At Medavie, you'll find more than just a job - you'll find a pathway to a full and rewarding career.

## We welcome diversity

We believe our employees should reflect the communities we serve and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds. To provide the best experience possible, we will support you with accommodations or adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process. Simply inform our Recruitment team of your needs. We are committed to making sure recruitment, retention, advancement, and compensation are fair and accessible while following all relevant human rights and privacy laws .

## We put safety first

Employees of MHNL are accountable to our patients and coworkers by participating in and supporting all safety-related initiatives, as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture that focuses on patient safety and a safe workplace.

Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Medical Office Administrator
description:
Medical Office Administrator

## WHO WE ARE

Our Health Centre is a non-profit community health centre serving the Municipality of the District of Chester and the Tancook Islands. Now approaching our tenth year, we operate a Same Day Clinic five days a week, along with specialty clinics including our new peri/menopause clinic, and programs that reach well beyond the exam room. Our programs and services are shaped by what our community members tell us they need.

We are small enough that every person here influences how care is delivered, and ambitious enough to keep testing new models to bring the best possible services and programming to our community. If you want your work to make a tangible difference in the community you live in and to help build something, this is where you want to be.

## AT A GLANCE

• Location
Onsite: Chester, Nova Scotia

• Term
Permanent. 30 to 40 hours per week over 4 to 5 days, based on the clinic schedule.

• Schedule
Approximately one evening per week (until 8 pm) and occasional Saturday coverage. Schedules are provided one month in advance whenever possible.

• Compensation
$23.00 to $26.00 per hour, based on experience.

## WHAT WE OFFER

• Health and dental coverage, 70% employer-paid

• Employer RRSP contributions of 5%, increasing to 6% as of April 2027

• 12 paid personal and sick leave days per year

• Two weeks of vacation to start, increasing with years of service

• Time in lieu available for hours worked beyond scheduled hours

• Benefits commence after successful completion of a three-month probationary period. Leave entitlements are prorated for scheduled hours.

## ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Medical Office Administrator is responsible for the day-to-day administrative coordination of all clinical services, including the Same Day Clinic and associated programs. This is a front-facing role, working directly with the patients and community members who come through our doors. The Medical Office Administrator works alongside the administrative assistant, and there are regular shifts where this position is the only administrative staff member on site.

The role ensures efficient workflows, accurate medical records and billing, effective scheduling and coverage, and high-quality support for both physicians and community members. It carries a high degree of independence. We are looking for someone who works collaboratively within a small team, takes full ownership of their work, and takes pride in getting things right the first time.

Given the sensitive nature of clinical information and community interactions, this position requires the highest standards of confidentiality, professionalism, accuracy, and sound judgment.

## TO APPLY OR LEARN MORE

To apply, send your resume and cover letter to Roger Bower, Executive Director, at ed@ourhealthcentre.ca. Applications will be reviewed as they are received, with the first review beginning October 16, 2026. The position will remain open until filled.

To learn more about Our Health Centre, visit www.ourhealthcentre.ca. For a full job description, contact Roger Bower directly.

employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 49809

Department: Public Works

Under Article 13 of the Collective Agreement between the Nova Scotia Department of Public Works and the Canadian Union of Public Employees, Local 1867, the following opportunity is being posted.

Please quote the competition number and the Zone you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Us
At the Department of Public Works, we are responsible for building and maintaining a sustainable provincial infrastructure for Nova Scotians. From highways and bridges to government buildings and registration of vehicles, safety and quality of life are top of mind. We support Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways, 4,100 bridges, and 9 provincial ferries.

Our Fleet Services Division is pivotal in ensuring the Public Works Fleet is running smoothly; ensuring the safety of our provincial road network.

About Our Opportunity
As the Mobile Service Mechanic, you will have the opportunity to work on our wide variety of equipment that maintains our roads and highways. You will be responsible for maintaining Utility Tractors, Rubber Tire Loaders, Graders, Tandem Trucks and all associated attachments including wings, plows, and sweepers.

Primary Accountabilities
You will not only repair, rebuild and make adjustments to our fleet, but also determine the reasoning for equipment malfunctions. To minimize such occurrences, preventative maintenance is a critical component in this role.
We will ensure you have the right tools to do the job, and there is nothing more important than your safety. You have a clean workspace, and your ideas and input are valued and considered. Your coveralls and other personal protective equipment (PPE) are provided. We also have an annual footwear and tool reimbursement allowance as you must bring your own mechanical tools.

Qualifications and Experience
Some high school and an Inter-Provincial Red Seal Certificate of Qualification in Truck and Transport plus a minimum of five (5) years of diversified mechanical experience.

Upon hire, applicants will be required to successfully complete Nova Scotia Motor Vehicle Inspection (MVI) training as part of their probationary requirements.

A valid Class 5 drivers' license is a condition of employment, and an acceptable driver abstract must be submitted before employment begins. Air Brake endorsement is an asset.

Knowledge and experience of computer-controlled engine diagnostic technology, electrical schematics, dealer purchased engine programs, online service manuals, and safety inspections are considered assets.

Air Conditioning Certification and a Motor Vehicle Inspection license would also be considered assets.

You consistently demonstrate initiative in your role, remaining up to date in changes to equipment, methods and technology within the mechanical field. Strong communication skills are necessary for the times when you will be helping staff diagnose and resolve equipment issues. You must also be able to work effectively with minimal supervision as most of your time will be spent working independently. Professionalism and a high standard for client and customer service is required.

You will be assessed on the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, interview, and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by noise, smoke and gas fumes and at times adverse weather conditions while operating in a field environment. Considerable standing, lifting, carrying and moving about is a requirement of this position.

Additional Information
There is one (1) opportunity in Ashfield/Judique in Zone 6 covering the Antigonish/Judique/Port Hawkesbury Fleet Services area including Zones 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9.

Normal hours of work are 8:00am - 4:30pm. If equipment breaks down, we will count on you to help things get up and running again. Therefore, you will be on-call outside of your regular work schedule.

This opportunity is for a 52-week Year-Round position – the duties of which are full time and continuous in nature.

You must bring your own mechanical tools.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless Career Paths.

The maximum a new Faculty can expect to receive is nine steps or $97,388.02.

Qualifications

## Qualifications and Occupational Experience:

• The minimum educational qualification for this position is a relevant undergraduate degree with a major in the related subject area of Communications and/or Math and/or a Red Seal in the Building Trades, specifically Carpentry, Automotive Service, Welding or Electrical. A Bachelor of Education degree would be considered an asset.

• You have a minimum of five years (full-time equivalent) of recent and related occupational experience and knowledge in general Trades and Transportation practices, specifically in communications within Trades and Trades Math, enabling you to provide learning experiences that mirror current practices in your field.

• You have specific technical occupational knowledge and skill in writing, presentation practices, job search processes, the mechanics of writing, and can relate these areas specifically to the Trade and Transportation fields of practice.

• You are familiar with and comfortable using computer applications such as the Microsoft Office Suite, e-mail and VISIO drawing program. Experience using a Learning Management System such as Brightspace would be considered an asset.

• You have demonstrated experience liaising with business and industry in your field.

• You are comfortable working in a digital environment; you take responsibility for acquiring knowledge about advancing technology; and you are committed to using technology in support of an exceptional student experience, including multi-media technologies and a variety of platforms that will engage students in online and blended learning.

• Ideally, you have related experience in delivery of educational programs or training to adults.

• Occupational experience that includes experience in providing performance feedback will be considered an asset.

• You have knowledge and experience in applying WHMIS, Occupational Health and Safety and occupation-specific safety practices.

• You are comfortable using multi-media technologies and a variety of platforms that will serve to engage students in online and blended learning capacities. The ability to teach effectively in an online/blended environment which includes building knowledge of best practices for the delivery and management of courses delivered whole or in part online, using a course management system to communicate with students and to foster and support a collaborative online learning community with and between students will be an important factor in your success. Candidates who do not have previous online/blended teaching experience must be open to and willing to participate in training for this delivery model.

## Relevant Skills and Knowledge:

• You demonstrate a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, accessibility, and anti-racism

• You possess excellent presentation skills and can facilitate content effectively and engagingly to a variety of audiences

• You are known for your superior interpersonal skills and can manage interpersonal relationships and issues effectively

• Your superb team building skills will enable you to develop a positive classroom dynamic and productive collegial relationships

• Your commitment to excellence, to life-long learning and to community involvement make you an ideal candidate for Faculty at NSCC

Responsibilities
As a member of the Institute of Skilled Trades faculty team, you will:

• Provide theoretical and practical instruction in Related Subjects specifically in the areas of Trades Math and Industry Readiness courses. Other secondary areas may include Environment and Ethics, Business Ethics and practices, and sustainability related topics. This includes in person and online instruction.

• Collaboratively design and deliver educational experiences for a diverse group of learners. This will include preparation, instruction, assessment, and evaluation of students using a broad range of flexible teaching and learning practices and technologies such as Learning Management Systems (e.g. Brightspace) and classroom technology.

• Related duties include but are not limited to academic and career advisement, participating on committees, program marketing, curriculum revision/development through collaborative practice within faculty working groups, supporting and monitoring work placements, liaising with business and industry, representing the College as required and upholding NSCC policies and procedures.

• Ensure health and safety practices and procedures are followed in your classroom, shops and labs.

• Maintain currency with the latest industry practices relevant to your program and to continually develop your understanding of 21st century teaching and learning practices. This position may involve different delivery modalities (e.g. in-class, online, blended online/in-class), off-site instruction and alternate work hours such as weekends and evenings.

As a condition of employment, Faculty at NSCC must complete a part-time adult education program delivered by NSCC. This adult education program is a significant investment on the part of NSCC in the learning and development of new employees. To achieve regular status, all probationary, full or part-time Faculty of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Faculty whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

Imagine working with autonomy and practicing to your full scope while building meaningful connections with your clients. As a VON nurse, you'll deliver holistic person-centred care to children, youth, adults, seniors, and support their families. You'll have the opportunity to work in clients' homes, in our clinics, virtually, and engage in community outreach. If you're ready to bring your skills directly into the homes and hearts of our clients and enjoy driving, then this is the perfect opportunity for you.

## What we offer:

• Work to your full scope of practice

• Ongoing professional development to enhance your skills and knowledge

• Comprehensive orientation program to ensure your success

• Competitive salary and vacation time

• Defined Benefit Pension Plan with company contributions for eligible employees

• Comprehensive benefits package (health, dental, LTD) for eligible employees and an Employee Assistance Program

• Smartphone to help you stay organized and connected throughout your day

• Travel compensation and mileage

## What you'll do:

• Client assessments to develop individual care plans

• Provide primary care in collaboration with other healthcare professionals

• Simple and advanced wound care, including complex and negative pressure wounds

• Chronic Disease Management, e.g. diabetes care and education

• IV therapy and CVAD management

• Phlebotomy and specimen collection

• Dialysis Management

• Rehabilitative programs

• Palliative and End of Life Care

• Medication management

• And many other critical nursing skills

## What we're looking for:

• Must be licensed as a Registered Nurse in the province of practice

• Community health experience is an asset

• Must enjoy driving, have a personal vehicle and possess both a current driver's license and proof of vehicle insurance

• A satisfactory Criminal Records Check is required; a Vulnerable Sector Search and/or Child Abuse Registry Check may also be necessary

• Must be able to wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

VON Canada: Careers that fit your life. Join our team today!

A quick note: This posting is for recruitment purposes. Full job descriptions are available.

Individuals in the role are required to walk, sit, stand, and climb stairs throughout the day, with some tasks requiring fine hand movements.

title: Licensed Practical Nurse I
description:
Zone: Central Zone
Location: DHT - Doctor Hugh Twomey Health Center, Botwood
Licensed Practical Nurse I
Central Zone - DHT LTC - A
Temporary Full-time (Approximately 6 months with possible extension)
NAPE HS
41811RP1
Hours: 75 (12 hours; Days, Nights)

Salary: CGL29 (CAD30.16 - CAD33.22 per hour)

Competition Number: VAC0017864

Posted Date: 2025-10-28

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Definition of Work:
Work involves providing nursing care and treatment services for the physically ill, disabled and/or cognitively impaired clients under the direction of a Registered Nurse. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Physical Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Constantly moves/lifts up to 10-15lbs, regularly moves/lifts up to 50lbs; required to restrain/reposition/move/lift up to, or above, 50lbs with co-worker assistance and repetitively required to complete pushing/pulling with medium force (22-44lbsF).
• Constantly stands/walks. May work in awkward or cramped positions to assist with care. Work repetitively involves reaching/stretching, bending/twisting and repeated bouts of low-level postures such as squatting, crouching or stooping.
• Potential for exposure to blood, bodily fluids and/or other contagion. May be exposed to patients/residents with potential risk for aggressive behavior.
• Work Environments present potential for exposure to scented/chemical products and/or other allergens within publicly accessible areas.

Required qualifications:
• Graduation from high school with a diploma recognized by the Newfoundland and Labrador Department of Education and Early Childhood Development.
• Graduation from a practical nursing program approved by Central Health.
• Current BLS certification.
• Current registration with the College of Licensed Practical Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.
• Demonstrated effective interpersonal and communication skills.
• Demonstrated competency in working to the full scope of practice (as per the CLPNNL and Central Health’s policies and procedures) and standards of care relevant to designated client population.
• Completion of other skills and post basic competencies as required.
• Work collaboratively as a member of an interdisciplinary care team and support the Registered Nurse in caring for clients with unpredictable outcomes as required.
• Work under the direction of a Registered Nurse for patients where the acuity or complexity of care requires an advanced level of knowledge and skill beyond the scope of practice for Licensed Practical Nurses.
• Demonstrated proficiency in Wound Care Management and Medication Administration including IM, IV and subcutaneous injections.
• Consistent demonstration of Central Health’s corporate values; Compassion, Accountability, Respect, Stewardship and Quality.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

title: Crosswalk Guard
description:
Competition number: 26-104

Salary: $18.29/Hour Job Type: Temporary Part Time Closing Date: October 21, 2026 Position Overview:
Do you like working with kids? Want part-time work that makes a real difference?

Join us as a crosswalk guard!

You are someone who likes to help people. You are pleasant, responsible, and flexible. You like being outdoors. Maybe you are a recent retiree, or a university or college student with classes mostly in the middle of the day. You'd like a few hours' work a week.

You could make an ideal crosswalk guard!

Here's the job:

•You will be responsible to help school-aged children safely across roads and intersections near their school.

•Hours vary from school to school, but a typical split shift for you could be 7:30-8:30 a.m. plus 3:00-3:45 p.m. (or 2:15-3:45 p.m., for schools with younger children who finish earlier).

•You work only on days when school is in, which means you get summers off! Also, March break, storm days, statutory holidays, etc.

•You will be part of a team but work mostly independently.

•You will be courteous at all times, not only to the children but to members of the public.

•The key task is ensuring a safe environment. Safety first, always. You leave only after the last child has crossed.

Here's what we need from you:

•You are free to work split shifts.

•You understand how the City regulates traffic in school zones.

•You will successfully complete a security clearance and a vulnerable sector check.

That's it! We don't require a specific educational level. We are looking for the right people - people who care about children, work well with them, and will keep them safe. And whose life would be enriched by a few hours' paid and purposeful work a day, keeping young Saint Johners safe on their way to and from school.

If this is you, click on "I am interested."

## Equal Opportunity Employer:

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of the communities in which we live and which we serve. We encourage and support applications from Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, and members of visible minority groups. Candidates who belong to such groups, who are qualified, will be given preference at the time of selection.

Applications will be accepted through our online system only. Qualified applicants should submit their cover letters and resumes to:

City of Saint John

Attn: Hiring Committee

www.saintjohn.ca (careers)

Only those applicants being considered further will be contacted.

title: Trades Worker II - Power Engineer
description:
Zone: Eastern Urban Zone
Location: Multi Site; Primary Site - St. Clare's Mercy Hospital
Trades Worker II - Power Engineer
Facilities Management
Permanent, Full-Time
NAPE HS
08811POS
Hours: 75 bi-weekly (12-hour rotating shifts; days, nights, evening, weekends)

Salary: CG-29 (CAD 27.61 - CAD 30.67 per hour)

Competition Number: VAC0029906

Posted Date: 2026-10-07

Closing Date: Open until filled

Job Summary
The Trades Worker II - Power Engineer operates high pressure steam plants and auxiliary equipment such as steam boilers, hydronic boilers, air handling units, cooling systems, related system controls, heat exchangers, chillers, medical gas systems, compressed air systems, emergency power systems, uninterruptible power supply systems, and reverse osmosis system. The Trades Worker II performs regular checks and verifies correct operation of safety controls for systems described; performs demand and preventative maintenance on boilers and other equipment/systems as needed and operates various power tools. They calibrate equipment/machinery; record and interpret readings of all plant equipment and various systems; maintain records; perform chemical tests on water systems for boilers and other equipment and test emergency power system. The Trades Worker will schedule and prepare for annual inspection and cleaning of high-pressure steam boilers, hot water tanks, motors and pumps. They will also provide training to students and new employees. This position works independently on shift and is responsible for the plant and other assigned equipment/systems.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Constantly lifts, carries or moves objects up to 11 lbs., regularly between 11 - 44 lbs. and occasionally over 44 lbs.
Regularly requires physical effort using tools that require accurate control and steadiness; maintaining physical balance, standing, walking, climbing, using gross and fine motor skills, and working in awkward or cramped positions requiring strength and/or endurance.
Work is impacted by time pressures/deadlines, interruptions and lack of control over work
pace as priorities change, services being interrupted, etc.

Job Qualifications
Successful completion of a high school diploma or equivalent.
A valid fourth (4th) Class Power Engineer's Certificate as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador is required.
Class 5 Driver's License is a condition of employment.
Experience in Power Engineering is preferred.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

title: Senior Emergency Management Coordinator
description:
Title: Senior Emergency Management Coordinator

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Regina, SK)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (CRC) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

## In this role, you will:

## Volunteer Management:

• Oversee the recruitment, onboarding, and local roster management of volunteers across service lines.

• Contribute to workforce planning by identifying local operational needs, volunteer gaps, and internal promotion opportunities.

• Implement and lead volunteer connection strategies through regular communication, activities, and informal recognition.

• Supervise volunteers deployed for PDA services , providing guidance, mentorship, and performance feedback to ensure readiness and compliance with service protocols

## Personal Disaster Assistance (PDA) Service Execution:

• Lead the local execution of the PDA service line, ensuring effective service delivery in alignment with established standards.

• Maintain a state of readiness for local PDA activations and ensure adherence to PDA agreements.

• Oversee and complete all PDA-related processes and systems to support timely and effective response.

• Ensure proper management of requisite PDA supplies and assets as per the service delivery plan.

• Build partnerships with local governments, community leaders, and response organizations to enhance response capacity.

## Response Readiness & Emergency Preparedness:

• Participate in and support emergency preparedness and community risk reduction activities, including annual campaigns.

• Coordinate and support the implementation of local emergency response plans in accordance with program standards.

• Support or lead the setup and operation of relief efforts during emergency responses.

• Deploy as needed in response roles and contribute to operational workforce planning.

• Engage in response debriefs and after-action reviews to enhance service quality and continuous improvement.

## What we are looking for:

• A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience and relevant qualifications in volunteer management, community development, emergency management, planning and evaluation or a related field and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Ability to adapt knowledge and practices to varying situations or equipment

• Experience in volunteer management, including recruitment, engagement, supervision, and training.

• Experience in developing and implementing emergency response plans and conducting preparedness initiatives.

• Strong understanding of emergency management principles, disaster response protocols, and community preparedness strategies.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, databases, and volunteer management systems.

• Valid driver's license and clean driver's abstract.

• Skills to investigate problems and propose solutions, including interpreting information in unfamiliar areas, consulting with others, and innovating on standard procedures.

• Communication skills, diplomacy and empathy to interpret information and deliver advice, clarify stakeholder needs, offer solutions, and resolve escalations in new or sensitive situations

• Fluency in English is required; French is an asset.

• Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends, as required during emergency responses.

## Working Conditions:

• Role will be working primarily in an office environment when not deployed to an emergency response operation.

• Some domestic travel in generally safe environments

• Some travel by vehicle may be required.A valid provincial driver's license is required.

• All roles within the Humanitarian Services (HS) team contribute to emergency response efforts directly or indirectly.

• All CRC roles are required to adapt work and priorities to support emergency response efforts, be present in person as required to support service delivery and deploy to emergency responses when appropriate and/or required (personnel availability and request for exceptions will be discussed with line management).

• For CRC roles that are assigned a function in the Emergency Relief operational structure (in field and virtual), personnel may be required to be part of an on-call roster and be available for scheduled on-call work

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada. At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

Since 1987, the Alzheimer Society of New Brunswick has been committed to supporting individuals living with dementia and their care partners through education, navigation, advocacy, and support services that help them live well throughout their journey.

## Job Summary

Reporting to the Manager of Support and Navigation, the Clinical Therapist plays a key role in supporting the emotional well-being of individuals living with dementia and their care partners. The successful candidate will provide trauma-informed, person-centred, and culturally responsive counselling services in individual and group settings.

Working collaboratively with clients, families, community partners, and internal teams, the Clinical Therapist will support individuals living with dementia and their care partners as they navigate the emotional, psychological, and practical impacts of the disease. In addition to providing therapeutic services, the successful candidate will lead the development, implementation, and evaluation of a pilot counselling program for people living with dementia, offered in both English and French, helping to expand access to specialized dementia-focused supports across New Brunswick.

This is a part-time position (three days per week). Services may be delivered in person, virtually, or through a hybrid approach based on client needs and program requirements.

## Typical Duties and Responsibilities

• Provide individual, family, and group counselling services to people living with dementia and their care partners.

• Conduct assessments and develop individualized support and treatment plans based on client needs and goals.

• Utilize evidence-informed therapeutic approaches to support client well-being and quality of life.

• Deliver counselling services in person, virtually, or through a hybrid model, as appropriate.

• Develop, implement, pilot, and evaluate a dementia-specific counselling program for people living with dementia in both English and French.

• Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential clinical documentation in accordance with professional and organizational standards.

• Collaborate with clients, families, internal teams, and community partners to support coordinated service delivery.

• Participate in case consultations, team meetings, and interdisciplinary discussions as appropriate.

• Contribute to the development of educational resources, tools, and supports for clients and care partners.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with community partners and stakeholders.

• Represent New Brunswick on national working groups, committees, and collaborative initiatives as requested.

• Participate in ongoing professional development and maintain current knowledge of best practices in dementia care and counselling.

• Uphold ethical and professional standards in accordance with applicable regulatory and professional requirements.

• Assist with administrative duties and organizational initiatives as required.

• Travel within New Brunswick as required.

## Qualifications

• Master's degree in counselling, Counselling Psychology, Social Work, or a related field.

• Current professional registration or licensure, or eligibility for registration, in New Brunswick (e.g., Licensed Counselling Therapist or Registered Social Worker).

• Minimum of two years of counselling experience, preferably within community-based, non-profit, mental health, or social service settings.

• Experience providing counselling services in both virtual and in-person environments.

• Training and experience in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and other evidence-informed therapeutic approaches.

• Demonstrated understanding of the impact of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias on individuals, families, and care partners.

• Experience working with older adults, caregivers, and individuals experiencing significant life transitions is considered an asset.

• Knowledge of trauma-informed, strengths-based, and person-centred practices.

• Strong clinical assessment, communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills.

• Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and manage sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

• Ability to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a team.

• Experience facilitating groups, workshops, or educational sessions is considered an asset.

• Strong community awareness and the ability to develop collaborative partnerships.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and experience using electronic documentation systems.

• Must carry, or be eligible to obtain, professional liability insurance in accordance with regulatory requirements.

• Bilingualism in English and French is required.

• Possession of a valid New Brunswick driver's licence and access to reliable transportation.

• Ability to travel within the region and work occasional evenings as required.

• The successful candidate must provide and maintain a satisfactory Criminal Record Check and Vulnerable Sector Check as a condition of employment.

## What We Offer

• A supportive, collaborative, and mission-driven team environment where your work makes a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and families affected by dementia.

• The opportunity to design and lead an innovative counselling program that will help shape future dementia support services in New Brunswick.

• Opportunities for professional growth, learning, and ongoing development.

• A comprehensive benefits package and a positive, inclusive workplace culture that values compassion, respect, collaboration, and excellence.

The Alzheimer Society is committed to equity, diversity, and inclusion, and welcomes applications from all individuals. We are committed to ensuring an inclusive and accessible recruitment process for all candidates.

320 rue Maple Street, Suite 100
Fredericton, N-B E3A 3R4

If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: First Link Clinic Coordinator
description:
## First Link Clinic Coordinator

Location: Saint John NB
Job Type: Full time/On-Site

Our impact is growing, and so is our team! Join us as we expand programs and take our initiatives to the next level.

Behind every person with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, there are hundreds of people dedicated to helping them. The Alzheimer Society is the leading not-for-profit health organization working nationwide to improve the quality of life for Canadians affected by Alzheimer's disease and other dementias and advance the search for a cause and cure. Active in communities right across Canada, the Society has programs and services near you. Since 1987, we've been dedicated to providing help for people with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias and their caregivers. That help comes in many ways.

## Job Summary:

As the primary point of contact for individuals and families seeking support, information, and guidance related to dementia, the First Link Clinic Coordinator plays a vital role in building trusting relationships and providing person-centred support. Working within a healthcare setting, the First Link Clinic Coordinator collaborates with healthcare providers, clinic staff, community organizations, and support services to connect clients with appro-priate resources and ensure they receive timely, compassionate, and coordinated support throughout their de-mentia journey.

This is a full-time, on-site position based within a clinical setting, and candidates must be available to work in person during regular clinic hours.

## Distinguishing Characteristics:

The ideal candidate is compassionate, organized, and skilled in client support, with the ability to navigate sensi-tive conversations and complex situations. This position serves as a key liaison between individuals living with dementia, their care partners, healthcare professionals, and community resources. The successful candidate will be committed to providing exceptional client service while helping individuals and families access the infor-mation, programs, and supports they need to maintain quality of life.

## Typical Duties and Responsibilities:

• Provide person-centred support, education, and navigation services to individuals living with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, as well as their care partners.

• Receive and respond to referrals from healthcare providers and clinic staff in a timely and professional manner.

• Conduct needs assessments to identify client strengths, challenges, and support requirements.

• Connect clients and families with appropriate community resources, support services, educational op-portunities, and dementia-specific programs.

• Maintain ongoing communication and follow-up with clients and families to ensure changing needs are identified and addressed.

• Build and maintain collaborative relationships with physicians, nurse practitioners, allied health profes-sionals, clinic staff, and community partners.

• Maintain accurate, confidential, and up-to-date client records in accordance with privacy legislation and organizational policies.

• Provide information packages, educational resources, and toolkits to clients and families.

• Participate in case consultations, care planning discussions, and interdisciplinary meetings when appro-priate.

• Deliver presentations and educational sessions to healthcare providers, community organizations, and the public as required.

• Support awareness initiatives that promote understanding of dementia and available supports within the community.

• Maintain the CRM database and ensure timely and accurate data entry for reporting purposes.

• Participate in provincial and national initiatives, meetings, and committees as requested.

• Travel within the region as required.

• Perform other duties related to client service delivery and organizational priorities as assigned.

## Qualifications:

• Post-secondary education in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience.

• Experience working in healthcare, community services, social services, client support, administration, or a related environment.

• Experience working within a healthcare or clinical setting is considered an asset.

• Ability to build positive and collaborative relationships with healthcare professionals, clients, families, and community partners.

• Demonstrated understanding of the impact of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias on individuals, families, and care partners.

• Strong interpersonal, communication, and active listening skills, with the ability to navigate sensitive and emotionally challenging conversations.

• Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

• Strong organizational, time management, problem-solving, and administrative skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.

• Ability to work independently while contributing positively as part of a team.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and experience using databases, client information systems, or CRM platforms.

• Bilingualism (English and French) is considered a strong asset.

• Possession of a valid New Brunswick driver's licence and access to reliable transportation.

• Ability to travel within the region and work occasional evenings or weekends as required.

• The successful candidate must provide and maintain a satisfactory Criminal Record Check and Vulnera-ble Sector Check as a condition of employment.

## What We Offer:

• A supportive, collaborative, and mission-driven team environment where your work makes a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and families affected by dementia.

• Opportunities for professional growth, learning, and ongoing development.

• A comprehensive benefits package, including health and dental coverage, paid time off, wellness initiatives, and retirement contributions.

• A positive and inclusive workplace culture grounded in teamwork, respect, compassion, and innovation.

The Alzheimer Society is committed to equity, diversity, and inclusion, and welcomes applications from all individuals. We are committed to ensuring an inclusive and accessible recruitment process for all candidates.

Annual Salary: $48,000.00 per year

The Alzheimer Society of New Brunswick
320 rue Maple Street, Suite 100
Fredericton, N-B E3A 3R4

The MCRT is an Emergency Service responding to unknown clients/unpredictable situations in a variety of community settings as determined by need and coordinating when needed with other services such as police/paramedics. The MCRT responds within specific geographic boundaries which includes Sheshatshiu and North West River. This position will also provide virtual support to other sites.

Current and continuing practicing licensure with the College of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador (CRNNL).

The successful applicant will be required to submit a satisfactory Certificate of Conduct.

Position: Valuation Support

## About Property Valuation Services Corporation

Property Valuation Services Corporation (PVSC) is an independent, not-for-profit organization that provides property assessment services and information to Nova Scotia municipalities and property owners.

We employ approximately 135 people who live and work in over 60 communities across the province.

Local governments use our annual property assessments to establish their municipal property tax rates, which fund important local services and infrastructure, and build communities.

## About the Opportunity

Reporting to the Assistant Director, you will help keep property information accurate and up to date. You will support the assessment of commercial, residential, mobile home, and condominium properties by reviewing information about land, ownership, building permits, property sales, and leases.

## What You'll Do

• Review maps, deeds, survey plans, and real estate information to confirm property boundaries and ownership.

• Gather property information and prepare files for property sales reviews.

• Review building permits, prioritize requests, and match permits to the correct properties.

• Confirm each property's classification and tax status, updating records when changes occur.

• Maintain accurate land, ownership, location, and lot size records.

• Update property records and send notices to property owners when required.

• Provide mapping and ownership information to support property assessments and related projects.

• Help maintain the annual property assessment roll and improve the accuracy of property information.

• Contact property owners to gather information and explain potential tax related changes.

• Work with municipalities, government partners, and PVSC to resolve land and ownership questions.

• Coordinate land related questions with the provincial Land Services team.

• Help resolve appeals related to property boundaries or ownership and update records as needed.

## What You'll Bring

A high school diploma and 3 years of related work experience, or an equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience.

You will bring the ability to:

• Interpret building plans and spatial documents, including subdivision and survey plans, site plans, legal descriptions, deeds, wills, leases, and other legal documents.

• Research and cross reference information from multiple sources to identify inconsistencies and resolve data, ownership, or process issues.

• Approach questions with curiosity, use available reference tools, and recognize when additional information or investigation is needed.

• Analyze information, solve problems, exercise sound judgment, and make accurate, well supported decisions.

• Understand the real estate market and how property information can affect the valuation process.

• Maintain a high degree of accuracy when working with property, ownership, taxation, and assessment information.

• Learn and apply legislation, processes, databases, mapping tools, spreadsheets, software, and new technologies.

• Communicate clearly and professionally with property owners, municipalities, government partners, and colleagues.

• Work independently, manage priorities, and take ownership of assigned work.

• Adapt priorities as operational needs change throughout the assessment cycle.

The following knowledge and experience are considered assets:

• Knowledge of Nova Scotia property assessment legislation and land registration systems.

• Familiarity with International Association of Assessing Officers standards.

• Use of LIN-NS and iasWorld databases to research property information and interpret leases and site plans.

## Why You'll Enjoy Working Here

At PVSC, you'll be part of a workplace where people feel valued, supported, and connected, while being trusted to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact. We believe great results come from great people, so we invest in growth, encourage new ideas, and succeed together through shared accountability and continuous improvement.

description:

Marine Atlantic is dedicated to creating an environment which promotes employee growth, career development, and job satisfaction. Our employees embody our core values; they are diverse, safety-oriented team-players who exhibit integrity and commitment, and always strive for excellence.

Marine Atlantic is currently seeking motivated and committed Deckhands who are eager to learn and grow within the Marine Industry. Successful applicants will primarily work as a Deckhand and will receive training to become a Quartermaster, allowing them to step into that role once training is complete and operationally required. These positions are permanent, spare and relief positions that are scheduled across our fleet and each tour based on operational requirements.

Marine Atlantic is committed to a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace. Preference may be given to members of the following equity deserving groups: women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, visible minorities and 2SLGBTQIA+ community members. If you are a member of one or more of these groups, please state to which group(s) you identify in your application.

Quartermaste main function is helmsman duties, entering and departing port and as required at sea. When not performing helmsman duties at sea this position will act as an additional lookout and assist the OOW as required. In port the Quartermaster will act as gangway or bridge watch.

Deckhand duties have several components; including, but not limited to emergency responsibilities, completion of documentation, fire/security patrol, deck patrol, and lookout.

## Additional Key Areas of Responsibility - Quartermaster

• Follow safe work procedures and work within MOHS regulations.

• Actively participate in all emergency and security drills as per the duties assigned in the Muster list.

• Perform/Switch to Emergency Steering and Autopilot.

• Understand the Emergency Steering Procedures, the location

• of the steering repeaters and magnetic compass.

• Follow helm orders as directed by the Master or OOW.

• Ensure all crew and visitors sign the gangway logbook and verify visitors ID as required.

• Verify and collect passenger tickets as required.

• Ensure gangway and walkways are clear of slip, trip and fall hazards.

• May be called out for mooring operations.

• Fire plan locations for shore fire department's while in port.

• Assist in the accomplishment of company objectives by performing other related duties as required.

## Key Areas of Responsibility- Deckhand

• Daily checklists for fall Protection, Forklifts, Man Lifts, Confined Spaces, manual sign-offs of tools, Occupational Safety & Health manual, International Safety Management reviews and Emergency Procedures

• Daily and routine work which includes painting, cleaning, and securing

• Housekeeping as it relates to the vessel's exterior decks and vehicle decks

• Rectification of Inspection iems as directed by the Bosun and/or the Occupational Safety & Health Committee

• Hourly fire and security patrol rounds of the entire vessel above the vehicle decks as per vessel plan

• Continually patrolling the vehicle decks and direct any unauthorized passengers to the passenger areas

• Inspecting lashings and tightening where required at sea and reporting it to the Officer on watch when in port

• Reporting any cargo shifting, fuel leaks, vehicle damages, fire hazards, lighting issues, and slip trip and fall hazards

• Working diligently to promote a safe working environment.

• Assisting in the accomplishment of vessel functions by performing other related duties as required

## What qualifications do I need to be considered for this opportunity?

## Education Certification and Experience

• Bridge Watch Rating Certificate STCW 95 or Able Seafarer Certificate STCW 95

• Valid STCW 6.1 and STCW 6.2 Certificates

• Transport Canada mandated Marine Medical Examination

## Additional Qualifications

• Ability to work in confined spaces

• Strong desire to learn and develop skills as a Quartermaster

## Asset Qualifications

• MED Refresher Certificate

• Passenger Safety Management

• Confined Space Certification

• Marine Basic First Aid

• Previous experience as a helmsman

title: Data, Analytics and AI Business Consultant
description:
Position Type:
Permanent

If you're looking for a fulfilling career that can make a real difference in your life, and the lives of others, you've come to the right place.

As a national health solutions partner, we put people first in everything we do - and that begins with our team of 8,000+ professionals who bring a cross-section of diverse life experiences and career expertise to Medavie. By collaborating and innovating together, our employees are creating industry-leading solutions in insurance, primary care and emergency medical services that impact millions of lives in Canada each year.

Our mission is to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest - and it's reflected in our award-winning culture. We celebrate individuality and value the diverse perspectives and skills our employees contribute. We go beyond providing competitive pay and comprehensive benefits to offer opportunities for personal and professional growth, flexible work options, meaningful experiences, and supportive leadership. Medavie is where employees can be their best selves, feel they belong, and achieve their full potential. Be part of it by applying for a position with us today.

## The Opportunity

Medavie is looking for a business-focused Data, Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (DAA) Consultant who can translate business needs into clear, high-value opportunities. As part of the Enterprise Transformation Office, you will serve as a trusted connection between Business areas and Shared Services and Medavie's enterprise DAA functions, supporting opportunities from initial identification through delivery, adoption, and value realization.

In this highly collaborative role, you will act as a strategic business advisor, using advanced facilitation, business analysis, and business case development expertise to uncover opportunities across the value chain. You will lead structured conversations with business leaders and subject matter experts to identify challenges, clarify desired outcomes, assess process improvement opportunities, and shape them into compelling DAA use cases and investment proposals.

A key focus of the role is helping business leaders make informed decisions by developing clear business cases that articulate expected benefits, costs, assumptions, risks, dependencies, and value realization measures. You will help quantify potential business outcomes, assess investment rationale, and build the evidence required to support enterprise prioritization and funding decisions.

Working closely with Technology Consultants, AI and Data specialists, business leaders, and delivery partners, you will help ensure opportunities are well-defined, understood, and positioned for successful enterprise assessment. Success in this role requires strong business judgment, exceptional facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills, practical AI and data fluency, and the ability to build credibility across both business and technical audiences.

You will give Divisions and Shared Services a strong voice in shaping Medavie's enterprise DAA agenda while helping ensure solutions deliver measurable business value and sustainable adoption.

## What You Will Do

• Act as a trusted front door between a Business Division or Shared Service and enterprise DAA functions, partnering closely with Technology Consultants in AI and Data throughout the idea lifecycle.

• Plan and facilitate structured discovery sessions, workshops and stakeholder discussions to uncover business needs, align perspectives, resolve ambiguity and build shared understanding of desired outcomes.

• Build a deep understanding of divisional strategy, priorities, operations, workflows and performance measures to identify unmet needs, repeated effort, delays, handoffs, decision bottlenecks, and customer or employee pain points.

• Surface and shape DAA opportunities that connect divisional needs and intended outcomes to enterprise strategy and priority value areas.

• Develop and document clear, decision-ready business cases, including the problem statement, options considered, expected benefits, costs, value drivers, assumptions, risks, dependencies and investment rationale.

• Partner with business, Finance and other specialists to quantify benefits and costs, assess trade-offs, and establish practical measures for tracking value realization.

• Elicit, analyze and document business requirements, process impacts and success measures using a senior business analyst approach.

• Confirm that opportunities are clear, meaningful and value oriented before they move forward for enterprise assessment and prioritization.

• Help connect and cluster related use cases that address broader end-to-end challenges across the value chain.

• Guide well-shaped use cases through the enterprise process and into delivery, engaging specialists in areas such as process reengineering, risk and finance when needed.

• Support sustained adoption and integration of DAA solutions so they achieve intended business outcomes and captured value.

• Translate business problems into data, analytics, automation and AI opportunities while preserving the business context as ideas move through the enterprise DAA process.

• Maintain two-way alignment by bringing business priorities, decisions, constraints and feedback to the Enterprise Transformation Office, and communicating enterprise direction, sequencing, progress and enablement needs back to the business.

• Stay current with emerging DAA capabilities, including generative AI, and continuously improve how opportunities are identified, framed and prepared for decision-making.

## What You Need to Succeed

Education: A degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Business Administration or a related field.

• Minimum 5+ years of business-facing experience, ideally in a senior business analyst, business architecture, transformation or consulting capacity, partnering with Business areas or Shared Services to identify and advance technology opportunities.

• Demonstrated experience facilitating complex workshops and stakeholder discussions, including discovery, requirements elicitation, option assessment and alignment across diverse groups.

• Strong experience developing and documenting business cases, including quantifying benefits and costs, assessing trade-offs, and defining measures of value.

• Experience in AI processes, information technology or a related field.

• Experience translating business challenges and process inefficiencies into use cases, requirements or clearly defined business needs.

• Experience connecting complex business challenges to scalable data, analytics, automation or AI-enabled solutions.

• Deep domain expertise in healthcare, government programs and/or insurance, with the ability to establish credibility and trust within the business.

• Practical fluency in AI, analytics and data, with the ability to explore how business challenges can be addressed through technology-enabled solutions.

• Strong facilitation, relationship-building and stakeholder alignment skills across business, technology, the Enterprise Transformation Office and support functions.

• Clear communication skills and the ability to bridge technical and non-technical language.

• Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with competing priorities, evolving mandates and a high degree of ambiguity.

• Relevant experience or certifications in business analysis, AI, analytics, data management or digital transformation are considered an asset.

Language Requirement: Bilingualism (EN/FR) is considered an asset. English is requirement, written and verbal, to provide services to our customers and communicate with internal stakeholders

Reliability Status Clearance (Enhanced Level B): This includes fingerprinting, a criminal record check and a credit check. You must have resided in Canada for at least five years and hold Permanent Resident or Canadian Citizenship status.

Pay Range: $88,200 - $110,200
