title: P1484 - Senior Planner - Heritage Conservation
employer: City of Moncton / Ville de Moncton
description:
VISION:A city that inspires

MISSION:Working together to enhance the quality of life for all residents

VALUES:Sustainability, Inclusivity, Innovation, Accountability, Excellence, Bilingualism

SENIOR PLANNER - HERITAGE CONSERVATION

DEPARTMENT - Job # P1484

JOB SUMMARY:
This position reports directly to the Director of Planning and Development.

This position is responsible for managing the City's Heritage Conservation Service including preparing an annual work plan outlining the City's Heritage Conservation objectives. This position works as a subject matter expert for the Heritage service and provides administrative support to the City's Heritage Conservation Board including providing advice on the City's Heritage Conservation By-laws, heritage applications and policy matters, overseeing the Local Historic Places Register and ensuring that other applicable standards and guidelines of the New Brunswick Heritage Conservation Act are met.

APPLYING FOR THIS POSITION:
The City of Moncton is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants must submit their application through an online system that can be found at www.moncton.ca/careers .
We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those invited for interviews will be contacted.

For more information, please contact the Human Resources Department at
506-877-7707 or visit www.moncton.ca/careers for information on the hiring and application process at the City of Moncton.

WORKING AT THE CITY OF MONCTON:
Moncton is a vibrant and culturally rich community. It is the first officially bilingual city in Canada, as well as one of the best places in Canada to do business. Moncton is also known as the economic, sports, tourism and entertainment hub of Atlantic Canada. City of Moncton employees strive to maintain the city's reputation as one of the best places in Canada to live, study, work and play.

This is a non-unionized position.
The City of Moncton offers an attractive salary and benefits package.

## City of Moncton Salary and Wage Scale

EDUCATION:

• High School graduate or GED equivalency.

• A university degree in Architecture, Urban Design, Urban Planning or related discipline that specializes in Heritage Planning and Urban Design is required.

• Membership in or eligibility for membership to the Canadian Association of Heritage Professionals, Royal Architectural Institute of Canada or Canadian Institute of Planners.

EXPERIENCE:

• Candidates must possess a minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience, preferably working with larger urban centre municipalities with at least two (2) years in heritage planning and historic resource management.

• Must have two (2) years of supervising and project management experience.

• Knowledge and experience with staff supervision, heritage preservation and renovations, the construction industry, the architectural or engineering fields, advisory boards, and regulatory bodies is considered an asset

LANGUAGE:

• English Essential. The ability to communicate in French is an asset, but not a requirement.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS:

• Knowledge of Heritage Conservation and Community Planning Act legislation, National Building Code of Canada and ability to perform legislative functions associated with Provincial Legislation.

• Strong theoretical and practical understanding of heritage conservation, urban design, and community planning principles, methods and procedures is demonstrated.

• Experience with Conservation Decision Making processes including the process to designate historic buildings and places.

• Possess building knowledge of heritage building envelopes, facades and materials, including conservation treatments to buildings that assist with preservation, rehabilitation and restoration.

• Familiar with Canada's Historic Places Standards and Guidelines for the Conservation of Historic Places in Canada.

• Understanding of the Urban Planning Department's policies, priorities, processes and procedures is demonstrated.

CONTACT:

• This position will have significant impact on the image of the department and will have frequent contact with internal and external customers. Requires courtesy and diplomacy for exchanging information through calls from the general public, members of council, civic administration, media, heads of agencies, commissions, and local or national organizations. This position requires a high degree of discretion as matters of a confidential nature are dealt with regularly.

• Requires behavioural characteristics that reflect the best interest of the corporation and the community at large.

• Must use judgment and a high degree of customer service skills in dealing with contacts.

SUPERVISION:

• Ability to instruct and supervise junior planning staff relevant to the assigned work program.

• Can provide some supervision to urban planning, technical planning and other support staff.

• Must be able to work with minimal supervision and make decisions that reflect the established objectives of the department. Also requires initiative or ingenuity to resolve frequent minor problems in situations not always covered by established practices, procedures or policies.

CONDITIONS OF WORK:

• All employees must comply with Council and Corporate adopted policies. (i.e. Attendance Management, Respectful Workplace and Health and Safety).

• Normal working hours shall prevail, under agreeable working conditions in an office environment. This position will be frequently be required to work beyond the normal workday to attend regular public Council meetings, attend Heritage Conservation Board, Planning Advisory Committee, Downtown Development and Revitalization Committee meetings, as well to process Heritage Conservation and Grant applications in a timely manner to meet specific deadlines, deliver public presentations, facilitate public hearings and public consultation on municipal planning matters.

• Frequently required to attend evening meetings and make public presentations.

title: Technologist
description:
Who We Are
We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are seeking a Technologist, Mineral Processing to join our Research & Innovation team at Mississauga, Ontario.

This is a permanent position reporting to the Senior Manager, Mineral Processing.

The Technologist plays a key role in supporting mineral processing research, development, and testing activities across laboratory, mini-plant, and plant environments. The successful candidate will contribute to the execution of experimental programs, preparation and characterization of mineral samples, operation and maintenance of testing equipment, and collection of high-quality technical data to support innovation and continuous improvement initiatives.

Working closely with engineers, metallurgists, mineralogists, specialists, and operations teams, the Technologist will help advance mineral processing technologies and support the development of sustainable, efficient processing solutions for Vale Base Metals.

## About You

You are a safety-focused and hands-on technical professional who enjoys working in a laboratory and industrial environment. You have a strong interest in mineral processing and research, possess excellent attention to detail, and are committed to generating accurate and reliable results.

You thrive in a collaborative environment and are comfortable supporting multiple projects while maintaining high standards of quality, safety, and operational excellence.

## In this role, you will:

• Demonstrate a strong commitment to Vale's safety standards, policies, and procedures while promoting a culture of safety excellence.

• Prepare, set up, and execute laboratory and mini-plant test programs in accordance with established procedures and project objectives.

• Support the design and assembly of experimental setups and pilot-scale testing systems.

• Prepare and characterize ore samples through crushing, grinding, screening, and other sample preparation methods.

• Conduct particle size analysis and other laboratory measurements required to support metallurgical investigations.

• Prepare polished mounts and samples for mineralogical analysis and characterization.

• Operate, calibrate, troubleshoot, and perform routine maintenance on laboratory and pilot plant equipment.

• Collect, validate, record, and communicate test results while maintaining accurate technical documentation.

• Ensure laboratory housekeeping standards are maintained and workspaces remain safe, organized, and compliant.

• Source, order, and maintain inventories of laboratory supplies, consumables, and equipment.

• Provide technical support for plant trials and on-site operational testwork when required.

• Collaborate with engineers, metallurgists, mineralogists, and research teams to support innovation, continuous improvement, and technology development initiatives.

## Experience

• Experience in laboratory, mineral processing, metallurgical, mining, or related industrial environments is considered an asset.

• Experience with sample preparation, laboratory testing, pilot plant operations, or process development activities is preferred.

• Experience operating, maintaining, and troubleshooting laboratory equipment is advantageous.

• Familiarity with data collection, reporting, and technical documentation practices is beneficial.

## Education

• College Diploma in Mineral Processing, Metallurgical Engineering Technology, Chemical Technology, Mining Technology, or a related technical discipline.

• Equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience may be considered.

## Skills & Competencies

• Strong commitment to health, safety, and environmental stewardship.

• Knowledge of mineral processing and metallurgical testing techniques.

• Mechanical aptitude with the ability to operate and maintain laboratory equipment.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

• Attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.

• Ability to follow established procedures and maintain high-quality standards.

• Strong organizational and time management skills.

• Effective verbal and written communication skills.

• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and data recording systems.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans, and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## Why Mississauga

Vale Base Metals' Mississauga office, located in one of Canada's fastest growing and most diverse cities, is the epicenter of the company's technology development team. This office focuses on advancing Vale Base Metals' competitive edge and refining growth strategies to ensure long-term sustainability. The innovative and dynamic environment of Mississauga perfectly complements Vale Base Metals' commitment to technological excellence and sustainable development.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all.

We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other

fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

title: Chief of Police
description:
Competition number: PF 26-014

Job Type: Permanent Full Time Closing Date: October 21, 2026 Position Overview:
The Saint John Board of Police Commissioners (the "Commission") is seeking a forward-looking police leader to serve as its next Chief of Police.

Reporting to and receiving direction from the Commission, the Chief of Police serves as the Chief Executive Officer of the Police Force and the senior law enforcement leader for the community.

The Chief will lead a police service focused on effective, lawful, ethical and community-centred policing. You will provide visible leadership across the organization, champion public trust and community partnerships, and connect the Commission's strategic direction to the decisions and actions of members across the Force.

As Chief, you will lead and administer the Force in accordance with the Police Act, provincial policing standards, Commission policies and the Commission's strategic direction. You will be accountable for organizational performance, professional conduct, public confidence and community safety outcomes.

The Role

As Chief of Police, you will maintain an effective, transparent working relationship with the Commission and comply with its lawful direction and instructions. You will develop, implement and oversee professional police procedures and ensure members carry out their duties professionally, fairly and in compliance with applicable law, standards, policies and collective agreements.

You will report regularly to the Commission on operations, organizational performance, progress against the strategic plan, policy compliance, risks, emerging issues and matters requiring Commission awareness or action. You will maintain accountability for the performance, conduct, professionalism and communications of the Force and its members.

In leading the Force, you will:

· Champion an inclusive community policing service-delivery model built on public trust, community partnerships and problem solving, grounded in the principle that "police are the public and the public are police."

· Create and sustain an inclusive, participatory working environment for sworn and civilian members, full- and part-time employees, contract workers and volunteers.

· Provide visible leadership across the organization so members understand strategic priorities and how their decisions and actions contribute to community safety and well-being.

· Promote a culture of openness to new ideas, creativity, innovation, teamwork, learning, accountability and continuous improvement.

· Convey a positive and credible image of the Police Force to the public, community partners, stakeholders and media.

· Model integrity, authenticity, transparency, professionalism, fairness and respect in all decisions, communications and relationships.

Organizational Leadership

You will manage and direct the Police Force to meet or exceed applicable policing standards while taking into account local conditions, evolving risks and community expectations.

You will prepare and propose annual budget options to the Commission, identifying anticipated operational impacts and alignment with strategic priorities and objectives. You will directly supervise, develop and mentor Deputy Chief(s), senior leaders and other direct reports, sworn and civilian.

You will establish and oversee fair, unbiased and transparent systems for hiring, development, supervision, evaluation, recognition, compensation, promotion and discipline. You will prepare the organization for the future through succession planning and the ongoing development of middle and senior managers.

You will build and maintain constructive relationships with labour associations, municipal partners, community organizations, partner agencies, provincial bodies and policing counterparts. You will also participate in the City's Public Safety Committee meetings.

The Ideal Candidate

You are an experienced and respected police executive who understands the opportunities and challenges of leading a small or medium-sized police service. Ideally, you have served as a Chief of Police or Deputy Chief, or held a comparable senior executive leadership role, within a small or medium-sized Canadian municipal police service or detachment.

You understand that leadership in a police service in a regional city requires both strategic perspective and a visible, hands-on leadership presence. You are comfortable working directly with the Commission, senior leaders, members of the Force, municipal partners, labour associations, community organizations and other policing and public-safety partners.

You have demonstrated your ability to work with partners to reduce crime, improve community safety and well-being, and respond to complex public-safety challenges. You have successfully managed in a unionized environment and bring experience with large operational budgets, financial planning and controls, procurement, resource allocation, and related financial and administrative responsibilities.

You have a proven record of building trust within diverse communities and across all ranks and employee groups within a police organization. You are a visible and credible leader who communicates effectively, develops people and builds strong organizational teams.

You understand modern independent civilian police governance and oversight, including the Commission's role as employer, supervisor and strategic governance body. You know how to build an effective relationship with a civilian police commission while respecting the distinct responsibilities and accountabilities of the Chief and the Commission.

You are comfortable navigating uncertainty and taking accountability for matters you can influence, not only those you directly control. You bring adaptive leadership, systems thinking and complex problem-solving skills, together with an inclusive orientation, empathy, innovation and a commitment to continuous improvement.

You will bring the judgement and leadership experience to guide the Force through its next chapter while maintaining the trust of its members, the Commission and the community it serves.

Working in the Community

The Chief works primarily in an office and meeting environment and regularly attends Commission meetings, internal meetings, public events, community forums and partner-agency engagements.

As Chief, you will maintain a visible and accessible presence with members of the Force, community partners and the public. You will maintain required police qualifications and may travel outside the jurisdiction for professional meetings, networking and related duties.

The Chief is expected to reside locally and to be available for significant operational, public-safety or organizational matters as required.

Requirements

You will ideally bring post-secondary education in a field relevant to policing, community safety and well-being, public administration, leadership, law, criminology or a related discipline.

Experience leading organizational transformation, equity-focused initiatives, community partnerships and modern police-service delivery is also preferred.

Competition # : 50064

Department: Justice

Type of Employment: Permanent and Term

About Us
The Court Services Division of the Nova Scotia Department of Justice is dedicated to excellent service and the provision of fair and accessible administration of justice, including court administration and security.
The Division provides administrative support to the courts listed: Nova Scotia Court of Appeal, Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (including Family Division), Provincial Court, Small Claims Court, Probate Court, and Bankruptcy Court. The courts act independently from the government to address individual cases.
For more information on the Department of Justice Court Services please visit our website: https://novascotia.ca/just/Court_Services/

About Our Opportunity
As the Court Officer (Judicial Support), you may coordinate and manage court hearings held in all levels of Court, provide support to the Judiciary, and act as the liaison between the Court, and members of law enforcement agencies, the legal profession, and the public. You will also act in the role of the clerk of the Court in all courts, including jury sittings and perform quasi-judicial duties assigned as a Staff Justice of the Peace as appointed under the Justice of the Peace Act. You will perform your duties in accordance with, and as assigned under, the Court Officials Act.

Primary Accountabilities
The Judicial Support responsibilities include:

• Communicate with legal professionals and self-represented individuals to co-ordinate and manage court hearings held at all levels of court.

• Provide confidential administrative and organizational support to the Judiciary.

• Act in the role of the clerk in all courts, including jury sitting and performing quasi- judicial duties as a Staff Justice of the Peace.

• Train and mentor new staff in day-to-day operational activities.

• Under the Judge's direction, draft and prepare complex orders and decisions arising from court hearings, review and apply relevant acts, statutes, policies, and procedures to all court documentation.

• Record and transcribe court proceedings by means of electronic recording equipment.

• Facilitate all aspects of court hearings from opening court, calling cases, swear or affirm witnesses or interpreters and translators, while simultaneously operating all required technology that may be required to support virtual court or hybrid models of court or appearances.

• Exercise care and control of exhibits, including transportation, until transferred to the Exhibit Custodian.

• You may be required to perform duties in Court Administration.

Qualifications and Experience
The successful candidate must have two years of post-secondary education in a related discipline plus one-year related experience, ideally in a legal environment, or an acceptable equivalent.
The successful candidate must also:

• Have experience and competency in keyboarding (combination of speed and accuracy), data entry, transcribing, and other standard computer applications including MS Office products.

• Have experience with virtual platforms such as MS Teams and video conferencing.

• Possess excellent proofreading, spelling, and grammar skills.

• Have superior organizational abilities and strong prioritization skills

• Have excellent attention to detail

• Have the ability to meet tight deadlines.

• Work independently and as part of a team.

• Have tact and discretion.

• Demonstrate an understanding and knowledge of the Rules and Statutes that govern the courts as well as a sound working knowledge of legal documents, forms, court procedures and legal terminology.

• Demonstrate a high level of initiative and problem-solving abilities and readily accept responsibilities. Errors can result in significant impacts for justice system participants.

• Be fair and impartial to all clients using a high degree of confidentiality while exercising your excellent interpersonal and communication skills, particularly listening skills, when dealing with difficult people in complex, sensitive and stressful situations.

We will assess the above qualifications using one or more of the following tools: written examination, typing test, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.
Legal research skills and bilingualism, with oral and written skills in English and French, would be considered assets.

Equivalency
Include, but not limited to:

• A 1-year certificate/diploma in a related discipline plus 2 years of related experience

• 3 years of related experience with exposure to the justice system

PLEASE NOTE: Candidates will not be considered for an interview if applications are incomplete or are missing information. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day (typically the hours are 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, this may vary depending on operational needs).

• Your personal resiliency is essential to meet the emotional demands of this position. You may be immersed in high stress situations and encounter distraught and difficult individuals.

• Handling of some exhibits may be mentally or physically disconcerting.

• May involve extensive keyboarding as well as long hours sitting in a formal courtroom environment.

Additional Information
This competition is seeking to fill three (3) permanent employment opportunity, located in Dartmouth, NS.
Candidates may be required to obtain training in Firearms Safety in relation to handling evidence and may be required to successfully complete the Nova Scotia Certified Transcribers qualification. This position will require an enhanced level of security screening for an external application.
Some travel and overtime may be required.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless career paths

Closing Date: 2026-10-13

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Emergency Housing Officer - Competition Number:2026/27-047-200813P
description:
## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context:

The Community Partnerships and Homelessness Department provides research and analysis of best practices in social and transitional housing, homelessness prevention; and supports the development of the Provincial Housing & Homelessness Plan. The Department supports the CEO and the Minister Responsible for Housing through the development of position papers and briefing materials to support engagement and partnership across the housing continuum. The Department also provides oversight of the corporation's eviction prevention framework, tenant and community relations program as well as the delivery of the provincial supportive living program, emergency accommodations (including shelters), as well as transition houses.

## Position Details

Competition Number:2026/27-047-200813P

Employment Type: 1 Permanent Position

Department/Region: Community Partnerships and Homelessness

Location: Head Office, St. John's

Competition Status: Internal

Closing Date: October 9, 2026

Salary Scale: $51,615 to $57,330 per annum (CG-30, $28.36 to $31.50 per hour), 35-hour work week. Where applicable a shift differential will apply as per the Collective Agreement.

Note: The shift schedule and compensation model is currently under review and subject to change.

Duties: The incumbent will act as a resource person for the general public, clients, community agencies and other government departments to provide general information, guidance, support, and advice regarding policies, procedures and processes relating to the Emergency Housing Program. The Emergency Housing Officer determines eligibility for services by conducting preliminary investigations and/or gathering of information from external/internal sources; this may include, but is not limited to: assessing/verifying financial information, assessing complex needs and determining housing status, by consulting with homeless shelters, conducting in-person and telephone interviews with clients, and securing declarations to obtain information of a highly confidential nature. The incumbent provides information and refers clients to programs and services offered by NL Housing and other government departments/agencies. The Emergency Housing Officer maintains a caseload of clients in shelters, private accommodations and other living arrangements and coordinates with Social Work resources to ensure they are progressing through the housing continuum. The incumbent inputs daily call statistics and prepares service authorizations. The incumbent maintains regular contact with participants and organizations via phone, in person, appointments or on-site visits, and attends case conferences. The EHO also works as a part of the wider collaborative team to conduct shelter inspections. Work also includes representing NL Housing on various internal/external committees, reviewing and providing input on corporate policy, and contributing to the development of briefing notes. The incumbent must be able to organize and prioritize work in a fast-paced environment. This position is part of the after-hours on-call rotation. Other related work may be required.

## Screening Criteria

Completions of a Bachelor's degree in the social sciences (psychology, sociology) or business. (Equivalencies may be considered)

Experience working in a case/client service environment

Experience working with individuals with complex needs

## Assessment Criteria

Knowledge of social/government programs (including those offered by NL Housing) and the process for accessing these programs

Knowledge of complex social behaviours

Knowledge of client management and business application software

Crisis management and dispute resolution skills

Ability to effectively exchange information

Ability to maintain confidentiality

Relationship building

Within the IT Strategy & Business Solutions (ITSBS) Branch, the Enterprise Strategist leads the development, governance, and execution of a comprehensive enterprise architecture strategy supporting K-12 education and Early Childhood Development across New Brunswick.

The ITSBS Branch operates in a complex environment. It aligns provincial IT systems, district needs, digital learning tools, cybersecurity, and service delivery relationships with the department`s strategic priorities.

About Us
The Correctional Services division of the Department of Justice is responsible for the administration and operation of community and custody-based programs and services for adults and young persons. Within the Correctional Services core business area there are two programs: community corrections & correctional facilities. Each of these program areas is broken down into closely related activities that have a specific impact on the program's target group.
Community Corrections has 22 offices across the province from Yarmouth to Sydney and is responsible for the supervision of both adult and young persons serving community-based sentences. The sentences include probation, conditional sentence, custody and supervision, conditional supervision and Intensive Rehabilitative Custody and Supervision. Probation officers also supervise those released from custody on conditional releases and prepare pre-sentence investigations to assist the Courts in the sentencing process. Evidence based Program facilitation and supports to specialized courts in areas of domestic violence, mental health and wellness are also part of the role of a Probation Officer as well as Restorative Justice casework and collaboration with community justice agencies.
Four (4) adult correctional facilities and one (1) youth centre provide the safety and security of person in custody while providing programs that address dynamic criminogenic factors to assist with their successful, reintegration back into the community.
Nova Scotia Correctional Services utilizes an evidence-based approach in both Community Corrections and custodial facilities. Core Correctional Practices (CCP) is the foundational practice that drives reintegration and rehabilitation practices deployed within Correctional Services. Utilizing CCP, Correctional Services staff can effectively interact, manage behavior, and help facilitate change, within target populations.
For more information on the Department of Justice Correctional Services please visit our website: https://novascotia.ca/just/Corrections/

About Our Opportunity
Under the supervision of the Kitchen Manager, the Cook is responsible for food preparation and the delivery of food services to young persons, staff, patients and visitors of the correctional facility. The Cook is responsible for operating within the budget for the food services program. The position is responsible for the supervision and direction of young persons working in the kitchen program; security of the kitchen; sanitary procedures and inspections; care, control and storage of equipment and materials.

• Ensure kitchen workers adhere to safety, sanitation, and personal hygiene standards.

Successful completion of a Journeyman Certificate (Red Seal), and at least four years of experience as a cook is required. Consideration may be given to an acceptable equivalent of training and experience. A Food Handler's Course is required. Previous experience working in a secure environment would be a definite asset. During the interview, the successful candidate will demonstrate strong interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively with staff members and offenders. title: Senior Specialist Engineer
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Senior Specialist Geotechnical Engineer to join our Geotechnical - Dams team in Sudbury. The role is a permanent on-site position.

The Senior Specialist Geotechnical Engineer provides technical leadership for the safe design, operation, monitoring, and closure of tailings storage facilities, dams, and related water management infrastructure. The role evaluates geotechnical performance through inspections, monitoring data analysis, and risk assessments to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, industry standards, and design objectives. Working closely with internal and external stakeholders, the incumbent develops risk mitigation strategies, supports dam safety and governance programs, and delivers engineering solutions that protect people, the environment, and the business.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Support the design, operation, monitoring, and closure of tailings facilities, dams, embankments, and water management systems.

• Conduct inspections and assess facility conditions, performance, and risks.

• Review monitoring data and perform geotechnical analyses to evaluate stability, seepage, deformation, and overall performance.

• Develop and implement risk mitigation measures and operational improvements.

• Collaborate with operations, environmental, project, and engineering teams to support tailings and dam safety objectives.

• Ensure compliance through technical documentation, reporting, and participation in audits and reviews.

• Manage and review consultant and contractor deliverables.

• Support incident investigations, dam safety reviews, emergency preparedness, and change management processes.

• Drive continuous improvement in geotechnical practices, monitoring programs, and tailings governance.

• Communicate technical findings and recommendations to stakeholders.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## About You

## Education:

• Undergraduate degree in Engineering in appropriate discipline.

• Professional engineering designation (P.Eng) required.

## Experience:

• 10-15 years of relevant experience preferred.

• Experience managing FEL studies, as well as supporting or leading pre-feasibility, feasibility, and large-scale project execution within mining, extractive, or infrastructure industries.

• Operational and site-based experience in mining environments, including underground operations, with technical exposure to open pits, stockpiles, and dams.

• Experience working on brownfield projects, operations, or maintenance activities, with knowledge of project delivery systems and associated deliverables.

• Broad industry experience and networks across mining and geotechnical disciplines, with exposure to multiple commodities considered an asset.

## Skills:

• Strong commitment to safety, technical excellence, and delivering results.

• Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to convey complex technical concepts and work effectively within multidisciplinary teams.

• Proven ability to analyze alternatives, assess risks and opportunities, and recommend practical solutions.

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are required for modern technologies such as AI and defence. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

title: Director of Registration & Licensure
description:
## Director of Registration & Licensure

## Moncton, New Brunswick

## Reference #JL-NBCP-10163

The New Brunswick College of Pharmacists (NBCP) is the regulatory body responsible for protecting the public and advancing excellence in the practice of pharmacy throughout New Brunswick. The College licenses and regulates pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, and pharmacies in support of safe, ethical, and competent pharmacy practice across the province.

NBCP is entering an exciting period of transformation. As the regulatory environment continues to evolve through labour mobility initiatives, registration modernization, legislative reform, and workforce development, the College is building its leadership capacity to help shape the future of pharmacy regulation in New Brunswick.

On behalf of NBCP, Meridia Recruitment Solutions is seeking a Director of Registration & Licensure to join the organization in a newly established leadership role.

## The Role

Reporting to the Deputy Registrar, the Director of Registration & Licensure will provide strategic leadership for the College's registration and licensure portfolio, overseeing regulatory processes that ensure registration and licensing decisions are fair, transparent, efficient, and aligned with the College's public protection mandate.

This is a unique opportunity to lead modernization initiatives that will help shape the future of pharmacy regulation in New Brunswick. The successful candidate will support critical priorities including registration system modernization, labour mobility initiatives, licensure pathway development, educational partnerships, workforce planning, and future legislative reform.

Working closely with College leadership, staff, government partners, educational institutions, and national regulatory organizations, the Director will serve as a key contributor to strategic decision-making and organizational growth.

## Why Join NBCP?

This is a rare opportunity to join a progressive regulator at a pivotal point in its evolution. As the College advances labour mobility initiatives, modernizes registration and licensure systems, develops innovative pathways for internationally educated pharmacy professionals, and supports future pharmacy workforce development, the successful candidate will play a central role in shaping the future of pharmacy regulation in New Brunswick. This role offers the opportunity to influence policy, support legislative reform, build strategic partnerships, and leave a lasting impact on the profession.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Provide strategic leadership for the College's registration and licensure functions, including departmental planning, priorities, service standards, and performance outcomes.

• Lead the ongoing modernization of registration and licensure processes, systems, policies, and regulatory frameworks.

• Oversee registration, licensure, renewal, reinstatement, applicant assessment, and related regulatory activities.

• Lead the review and modernization of registrant and pharmacy registers, ensuring data quality, consistency, and regulatory compliance.

• Define and support the implementation of business and regulatory requirements for enhancements to registration systems, databases, and applicant-facing technology platforms.

• Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to identify opportunities for regulatory improvement and operational efficiency.

• Provide leadership on policy development, process reviews, and regulatory initiatives that support public protection while reducing unnecessary barriers to registration.

• Support educational and practice-readiness initiatives, including partnerships with educational institutions, workforce development programs, and credential recognition processes.

• Support the development and implementation of innovative registration, education, assessment, and licensure pathways for internationally educated pharmacy professionals, while advancing labour mobility and workforce development initiatives.

• Contribute to legislative and regulatory reform initiatives, including future amendments to the Pharmacy Act and related regulations.

• Prepare briefing materials, reports, recommendations, and presentations for senior leadership, Council, and committees.

• Build strong relationships with registrants, applicants, educational institutions, government partners, national assessment organizations, and other regulatory bodies.

• Provide leadership, coaching, and support to direct reports while fostering a collaborative and high-performing team culture.

• Represent the College on provincial, regional, and national working groups and committees as required.

• Monitor emerging regulatory, educational, and workforce trends and provide recommendations to support the College's strategic priorities.

## Qualifications & Experience:

• Bachelor's degree in public administration, education, health administration, business, law, or another relevant discipline.

• 5-10 years of progressive leadership experience within professional regulation, credentialing, licensing, higher education administration, healthcare, certification, public administration, or a related field.

• Experience leading complex projects, organizational change initiatives, policy development, or process modernization efforts.

• Experience interpreting legislation, regulations, policies, or governance frameworks.

• Demonstrated success building relationships and collaborating with diverse stakeholders.

• Experience working with professional regulatory bodies, licensing organizations, educational institutions, credentialing agencies, or public sector organizations is considered an asset.

• Experience leading modernization, digital transformation, process improvement, or organizational change initiatives is highly desirable.

• Knowledge of healthcare regulation, professional regulation, credential assessment, workforce planning, or adult education is considered an asset.

• Bilingualism (English and French) is considered a strong asset.

## Skills & Attributes:

• Strategic thinker with strong planning and organizational skills.

• Ability to lead and influence through change.

• Strong judgment and decision-making capabilities.

• Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.

• Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills.

• Ability to navigate complex regulatory and stakeholder environments.

• Strong relationship-building and collaboration skills.

• High level of professionalism, integrity, and discretion.

• Digital acumen and an interest in process and systems modernization.

## What NBCP Offers:

• Competitive compensation within an established salary band, starting at $125,800, based on qualifications and experience.

• Employer-paid health and dental benefits.

• RRSP contribution program of 6.5% of salary up to $6,500 annually.

• Professional membership and licensing fee reimbursement.

• Professional development and conference support.

• Flexible hybrid work environment.

• Office closure between Christmas and New Year's.

title: Technical Service Representative – Part-time
description:
Join Our Team as a Part-time Technical Service Representative at Atlantic Lottery!

Are you a tech-savvy problem solver with a passion for customer service? Atlantic Lottery is seeking a Technical Service Representative to support a service territory spanning across Happy Valley Goose-Bay, Newfoundland. This field-based role requires regular travel throughout the assigned territory. In this hands-on role, you'll be responsible for servicing and maintaining lottery terminals and related equipment across Video Lottery and Retail Lottery sites, ensuring maximum uptime and compliance with service standards.

You'll work independently, traveling extensively within your territory, and play a key role in preventative maintenance and servicing/repairing equipment at retailer locations while maintaining positive relations. You will ensure maximum up time of all assets delivering on key performance metrics while meeting our Service Level Agreements (SLA's).

## Why Join Our Team?

• Work with innovative gaming technology in a hands-on role that combines technical problem-solving and customer service.

• Enjoy the freedom and variety of a field-based position where you'll manage your day and make a visible impact.

• Join a supportive team that values learning, collaboration, and delivering exceptional experiences for our customers and communities.

Hours: 23 hours per week.

Application Deadline: October 13, 2026

Qualifications
Education and Experience:

• Educational Requirements: An Electronics diploma or a certified Engineering Technology diploma from a recognized post-secondary institution.

• Experience: 1 to 3 years of experience in Technical and Customer Service roles.

• Physical Requirements: Ability to lift and move weights up to 50 pounds.

• Driving Requirements:
• A clean and valid driver's abstract.

• A valid driver's license as required by law.

• Access to a reliable vehicle with valid registration and insurance certificates, maintained in a clean and safe operating condition.

• Travel Requirements: Ability to travel up to 90% of the time within the designated service territories.

• Work Schedule: Willingness to work shifts, including evenings and weekends, as needed.

• Age Requirement: Must be 19 years of age or older.

Professional Skills:

• Ability to resolve technical issues efficiently by applying critical thinking and using available resources.

• Excellent listening, communication, and collaboration skills.

• Strong motivation and eagerness to learn new technologies, applications, and tools relevant to the role.

• Proficiency in MS Office.

• Ability to multi-task, problem-solve, prioritize and competently handle a variety of activities with a high degree of accuracy in a fast paced, customer-driven environment.

Assets:

• Gaming experience

• Troubleshooting experience

• A+ and Network+

• Service Now

• Cisco Meraki

Special Condition of Employment for Field Employees:

• Must be able to successfully complete First Aid/CPR training within provincial requirements.

• Steel toe boots/shoes are a requirement

• Must complete Defensive Driving course

## Work Location & Flexibility

• Field-based remote position supporting a service territory across Newfoundland (Happy Valley-Goose Bay region). Extensive daily travel throughout the territory is required.

## Compensation

• Salary: Starting at $34.00/hourly (based on experience, skills, market conditions, and internal equity.

## AL Benefits

Casual or Part-time employees may be eligible to participate in our life insurance plans, medical, dental, optional life, and dependent life coverage upon qualification which is one year of service with Atlantic Lottery and have worked a minimum of 630 hours in that same year.

## Recruitment Process

We've made meaningful enhancements to our hiring practices in recent years. Our typical recruitment process includes:

• Two virtual interviews (due to the location of the role)

• An assignment and/or scenario‑based questions

• Behavioral or cognitive assessments

• Verification of relevant certifications (as applicable)

All interviews are conducted in English, our primary working language, unless otherwise specified.

Only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Successful candidates will undergo reference checks and a mandatory criminal background check. Additional financial, educational, or credential verifications may be required depending on the role.

## Role Commitment

To support employee development, business continuity, and knowledge transfer, individuals who accept this position are expected to remain in the role for a minimum of 18 months before being eligible to apply for or transfer to another position within Atlantic Lottery.

This expectation applies to both external hires and employees moving into the role from another position.

## Internal Candidates

Internal applicants must be in good standing, including meeting expectations on their most recent performance review, and must not be on probation. Consideration may also include factors such as performance improvement plans, disciplinary actions, attendance, and completion of mandatory training.

A Predictive Index (PI) assessment will be completed or shared with the hiring leader as part of the evaluation process.

## Internal Recruitment Considerations

For internal recruitment processes, preference may be given to employees currently occupying regular or term positions with AL. Selection decisions will consider business needs, approved staffing requirements, organizational headcount parameters, qualifications, and overall fit for the role.

## Eligibility to Work in Canada

Candidates must have all required work permits, visas, and authorizations and be eligible to work in Canada at the time an offer is made. It is the candidate's responsibility to secure these requirements.

Atlantic Lottery welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada. Atlantic Lottery is not participating in the Temporary Foreign Worker (Labour Market Impact Assessment) Program, Provincial Nominee Programs, or the Atlantic Immigration Program at this time. Support for any other immigration programs for new hires is subject to internal policies, operational needs, and program restrictions and is not guaranteed.

Responsibilities
What You'll Do:

• Provide exceptional technical support by diagnosing and resolving issues with gaming technology to keep equipment operating reliably

• Maintain and install gaming equipment at retail and destination locations, ensuring a seamless experience for customers and players

• Build strong customer relationships by delivering professional, responsive service and clear communication in the field

• Support operational success by helping meet service commitments and minimizing equipment downtime across your service territory

• Collaborate with internal teams to troubleshoot complex issues, share insights, and support new initiatives and product launches

• Promote safe and compliant operations by following established standards, policies, and regulatory requirements

We are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees and customers feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers and communities in which we live and serve. If you require an accommodation for the recruitment/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, or accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations), please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

description:
## Family Law Mediator

## Two-year term, with possibility of extension

## Fredericton

## Open Competition

The New Brunswick Legal Aid Services Commission (NBLASC) is seeking an individual to fill a key role as Mediator to support the Family Law Services Mediation Pilot Project in Fredericton and Woodstock.

## Who we are

The NBLASC is a team of professionals advocating with compassion. We provide legal assistance to low-income individuals and are a crucial part of a fair and equitable justice system. We are committed to access to justice, and we advocate for our clients' rights.

Compassion, Accountability, Professionalism, and Excellence: These are our values, and are at the heart of everything we do.

## What you will do

The Mediator will serve as a vital component of the Mediation Pilot Project under the New Brunswick Legal Aid Services Commission. This role demands impartiality, exceptional negotiation skills, and a commitment to enhancing access to justice for families.

Reporting to the Director of Family Law Services, the Mediator will be responsible for:

• Facilitating Mediation Sessions
Conducting mediation sessions to facilitate constructive dialogue, identify areas of agreement and support parties in working toward mutually acceptable resolutions as a result of a marital or common law separation.

• Conflict Resolution and Agreement Drafting
Assisting parties in identifying key issues, potential solutions, and working toward mutually acceptable resolutions including parenting arrangements, child support and spousal support as well as other related issues where appropriate to support a comprehensive resolution. The goal is to arrive at a written agreement for the parties.

• Coordination with Stakeholders
Collaborating with the Mediation Coordinator to schedule sessions and align the mediation process with project's objectives.
Preparing appropriate mediation documentation to clearly record areas of agreement and any outstanding issues and coordinating with private bar counsel, ensuring both parties receive independent legal advice before finalizing outcomes.

• Program Development and Evaluation
Contributing to the development, implementation and ongoing refinement of the pilot project, including providing practical input on policies, procedures and service delivery.
Supporting the program's evaluation by maintaining records of mediation outcomes and providing feedback to improve service delivery.
Assisting in the evaluation of project success metrics, such as case resolution rates and client satisfaction.

## • Other related duties as assigned.

## Who you are

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

## Need to have (Essential qualifications and skills)

• Bachelor of Law Degree

• Membership in good standing or eligibility for membership with the Law Society of New Brunswick

• Recognized family mediation training and/or certification, or a commitment to complete required mediation training and pursue an approved certification or accreditation pathway as part of the pilot.

• Minimum of 5 years experience in Family Law

• Please state your date of admission to a Canadian Law Society.

• Written and spoken competence in English and French is required. Please state your language capability.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please ensure that preferred language for assessment is identified on your resume.

## Nice to have (Asset qualifications):

• Demonstrated negotiation skills.

• Experience in conflict resolution.

• Experience working with families experiencing conflict, maintaining sensitivity to emotional and relational dynamics.

• Virtual platforms and technology such as TEAMS.

## You possess the following behavioural competencies:

• Creative Thinking

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Client Service Orientation

• Initiative

• Flexibility

$95,550 - $115,622 - Pay Band 7, Management

## How to apply

We encourage you to apply by email at HR-NBLASC.RH-CSAJNB@GNB.CA stating "2026-25Mediation Pilot" in your email subject line on or before October 23, 2026.

title: Early Childhood Educator, Child Study Centre
description:
The Child Study Centre at Mount Saint Vincent University invites applications for the position of Early Childhood Educator.

## MSVU Child Study Centre - Who We Are & What We Care About

Mount Saint Vincent University's Child Study Centre is entering an exciting new chapter as we prepare to open the expanded and new child care facility in early Spring 2027.

Founded in 1976, the Child Study Centre is a licensed, not-for-profit early learning and child care centre committed to providing high-quality, inclusive, accessible, and culturally responsive programming for young children. We create environments where children and educators are inspired to explore, create, and grow, while honouring diverse identities, experiences and ways of knowing.

As a university-based child care centre, we work closely with the MSVU community and the Child and Youth Study program. Our educators have unique opportunities to mentor students, engage with research, contribute to innovative practice, and help shape the future of early childhood education and care in Nova Scotia.

We are inspired by the Reggio Emilia Approach, and our work is guided by the Nova Scotia Early Learning Curriculum Framework and a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, belonging, social justice, and environmental responsibility. We recognize that creating equitable and inclusive environments requires ongoing reflection, learning, and action. We are committed to the ongoing work of decolonization, and believe that reflective practice, curiosity, and lifelong learning strengthen both individuals and communities.

We strive to create a workplace and space where educators feel supported, respected, and inspired to continue learning throughout their careers.

## About the Opportunity

Reporting to the Director, Child Study Centre, the Early Childhood Educator contributes to a safe, inclusive, and responsive environment where children are recognized as capable, curious, and active participants in their learning and experiences. The Early Childhood Educator works collaboratively with children, families, and colleagues to observe, document, and develop responsive curriculum that emerges from children's interests, ideas, relationships, and experiences. The role includes supporting children's well-being, belonging, and participation; creating thoughtful indoor and outdoor environments; and engaging in reflective pedagogical practice and collaborative inquiry.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will bring a minimum of 3 years of experience working with children in an ECE classroom and an ECE Level 2 or higher. The candidate will need to be familiar with the Nova Scotia Early Learning Curriculum Framework and have experience working with children using an emergent curriculum approach. They will be familiar with observing children and recording these observations to create relevant curriculum experiences in the classroom. The candidate will have excellent written and verbal communication skills and should be proficient in the use of Microsoft Office Suite.

The candidate will demonstrate a genuine appreciation for children and their abilities. The candidate must be able to work as part of a team of educators and work cooperatively with families. Willingness to continue with professional development and education is a must. First Aid and CPR certification is required.

Experience with pedagogical documentation would be an asset. Specific work experience with children below three years of age is an asset.

The successful candidate will be required to undergo a Child Abuse Registry check, Vulnerable Sector check, and Criminal Records check.

Responsibilities
• Co-create, implement, and reflect on responsive curriculum and learning experiences.

• Create safe, inclusive, and engaging indoor and outdoor environments.

• Observe and document children's interests, ideas, experiences, and participation.

• Build respectful, reciprocal relationships with children, families, and colleagues.

• Mentor and support practicum students and volunteers.

• Engage in ongoing professional learning, reflective practice, and quality improvement initiatives.

## Salary

In accordance with the Nova Scotia Early Childhood Educator Wage Scale.

## Start Date

Winter 2027 - exact date will be determined by the Child Study Centre opening timeline.

## Application Process

Applications should include a cover letter and a resume. The position will remain open until filled; however, applications will start being reviewed on October 28, 2026.

title: Corporate Controller
description:
## Corporate Controller
Halifax, NS
Reference # HL-PMS-10213

Since 1999, Premiere Suites has been one of Canada's most recognized and trusted providers of high-quality temporary residences for professionals and families. Offering furnished apartments, condominiums, and townhomes for extended stays of 30 days or more, Premiere Suites serves guests across Canada with a focus on quality, consistency, and exceptional service.

We are excited to partner with Premiere Suites in the recruitment of a Corporate Controller to join their team in Halifax, Nova Scotia.

Reporting to the Vice President of Finance and Technology, the Corporate Controller will play a key leadership role in overseeing the organization's accounting operations, financial reporting, planning, forecasting, and performance analysis. This position will provide meaningful financial and operational insights to support decision-making while strengthening financial discipline, controls, processes, and reporting across the organization.

## Key responsibilities include:

Financial Reporting & Planning

• Lead accurate and timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close and reporting processes

• Prepare and review financial statements, management reporting, and detailed variance analysis

• Own the annual budgeting and rolling forecasting processes, including financial models, assumptions, and scenario analysis

• Partner with department leaders to align financial plans with business priorities and recommend actions based on performance against plan

Financial Analysis & Business Insights

• Analyze profitability across suites, customers, regions, and strategic initiatives

• Develop and maintain operational dashboards and KPIs, including occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, and cost trends

• Identify trends, risks, and opportunities and clearly communicate the story behind the numbers to leadership

• Incorporate relevant external data to support benchmarking, competitive analysis, and informed decision-making

• Support strategic initiatives, investment analysis, and growth planning across the organization

Cash Flow & Financial Controls

• Manage daily liquidity, working capital, and short- and long-term cash flow forecasting

• Support banking relationships and organizational financing requirements

• Maintain a strong internal control environment and ensure financial processes and procedures are appropriately documented

• Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, organizational policies, and regulatory requirements

• Serve as the primary liaison with external auditors

Data Systems & Process Improvement

• Integrate financial and operational data from QuickBooks, CRM, and other business systems to strengthen reporting and analysis

• Ensure accuracy and consistency across financial and operational data sources

• Leverage advanced Excel, Power BI, and other technology to automate and enhance reporting

• Identify opportunities to streamline processes, reduce manual work, standardize reporting, and improve scalability

• Support data centralization and systems initiatives that enhance financial visibility across the business

Cross-Functional Leadership

• Act as a trusted financial partner to Operations, Sales, Marketing, and other functional leaders

• Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders, banks, auditors, and external partners

• Promote accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and data-driven decision-making throughout the organization

## The ideal candidate will possess:

• CPA designation is required

• 7+ years of progressive accounting, controllership, and financial planning and analysis experience

• Strong expertise in financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, and performance analysis

• Advanced Excel skills; experience with Power BI or similar tools is preferred

• Strong knowledge of QuickBooks Online and experience working with CRM and operational data

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex data into meaningful business insights

• Excellent communication and business partnership skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions and with senior leadership

• Demonstrated experience driving process improvement, automation, and operational efficiencies

• A proactive, hands-on approach with strong attention to detail and the ability to operate effectively in a growing environment

This is an exciting opportunity to join an established organization and play a key role in strengthening its finance function during a period of continued growth. The Corporate Controller will have broad exposure across the business, with the opportunity to influence financial strategy, enhance reporting and analytics, and support key operational and strategic decisions.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online at: https://meridiarecruitment.ca/Career/17909665625480000008fgb

For more information about this exciting opportunity please contact Heather Labucki, Partner, or Sara Morey, Senior Consultant at smorey@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let Sara know.

title: Maintenance Training Instructor (CAT E)
description:
## Purpose of position

Develop and deliver technical training with respect to aircraft systems, run up and taxi, troubleshooting, inspection techniques, refueling, etc. and company policy and procedures to all company CAT M & E employees, external customers and Aircraft on Ground (AOG) Contractors as required.

## Key responsibilities

• Evaluate as necessary, whether the students have achieved the desired level of knowledge as stated in the course objectives/lesson plans.

• Ensure standards for student safety are followed during any training including practical drills or work.

• Delivery of other training programs when required.

• Develop company Approved Training Organization (ATO) aircraft type courses (ATA Spec 104 Level 3) to meet Transport Canada and company approval requirements.

• Develop aircraft type familiarization courses (ATA Spec 104, Level I).

• Develop aircraft tow training, aircraft ground runs & taxi training, avionics systems training, diagnostics training and specialized tooling training such as borescope inspection.

• Develop new courses as directed by the Maintenance Training Manager.

• Develop Maintenance Control Manual / Maintenance Production Manual (MCM/MPM) Standards and Update courses.

• Respond to and report back on daily operational issues.

• Ensure training location and equipment are arranged for the training, and any equipment issues are reported back through the Maintenance Training Manager or 3rd party person responsible.

• Administration of any required course examinations including completing forms and reports.

• Ensure course attendance records are completed and forwarded to the Maintenance Training Coordinator when required. Provide support, coaching and training material to line trainers as required.

## Required qualifications

• Minimum of 5 years experience in the maintenance of aircraft.

• Ability to successfully complete the "Train the Trainer course".

• Excellent English communication skills, both written and oral (as all training is done in English).

• Previous experience as an Aircraft Maintenance Trainer.

• Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams).

• Transport Canada endorsements on current company aircraft types (E175, CRJ900, Dash 8-400).

title: Senior Buyer
description:
