## Key Responsibilities:

• Lead strategic sourcing initiatives, supplier evaluations, commercial negotiations, and procurement support for capital projects, including the execution of purchase orders, contracts, and supplier deliverables..

• Manage critical supplier relationships and supplier performance to ensure compliance with contractual agreements, terms, conditions, schedules, quality, safety, deliverables, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement expectations.

• Provide expediting support as needed to maintain operational goals.

• Lead RFI/RFP/RFQ processes, analyze supplier proposals, negotiate commercial terms and conditions, and support drafting, negotiation, and administration of commercial agreements in collaboration with Operations, Finance, Legal, and suppliers.

• Provide occasional after-hours and on-call procurement support for critical operational needs, emergency purchases, supply disruptions, and urgent business requirements.

• Experience with capital asset acquisition programs in a fast-paced, highly technical industry/environment, including supplier selection, equipment sourcing, commercial evaluations, and project implementation support.

• Clear understanding and experience working with INCOTERMS, international logistics, supplier contracts, and commercial risk management.

• Working knowledge with MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) is required.

• Ability and willingness to travel occasionally within Canada, the United States, and other international locations as required for supplier visits, project implementation, factory acceptance testing (FAT), negotiations, audits, and operational initiatives.

• Organizational Leadership: Able to lead the organization and supply base to maximize results.

• Collaboration: Regarded as a constructive team player and have a strong sense of partnership behavior

• Analytical thinking: Disciplined and data oriented to gain competitive advantage.

• Communication: Ability to communicate objectives clearly both in writing and orally

• Creative & Flexible: Able to evaluate opportunities and respond to changing requirements.

• Ability to work independently when needed, to make sound business decisions, and can accurately balance risks with business needs.

• Adaptability to work in developing environments.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness, and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

School of Ocean Technology/Centre for Applied Ocean Technology

Marine Institute

(Contractual On-Call Positions)

A campus of Memorial University, the Fisheries and Marine Institute (MI) is North America's most comprehensive marine institute dedicated to education, training, applied research, industrial response, and technology transfer supporting ocean industries. The School of Ocean Technology (SOT) promotes the growth of the ocean technology sector through education, training, applied research, technology transfer, and community engagement. The school delivers diploma, bachelor's, and graduate programs to meet this sector's needs, with an underlying focus on key ocean technologies. Operating within MI's School of Ocean Technology, the Centre for Applied Ocean Technology (CTec) provides research and development support, industry outreach, and scientific and technical advisory services to clients and partners, with expertise spanning ocean observation, ocean mapping, remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), aerial drones, autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). The Centre is based at The Launch, MI's ocean innovation centre and a cornerstone facility in Canada's ocean innovation ecosystem, located in Holyrood, Newfoundland and Labrador, approximately 35 minutes from St. John's. This team works at the cutting edge of ocean technology, in collaboration with a wide range of marine sectors locally, nationally, and internationally, to enhance the safety, efficiency, sustainability, and profitability of maritime pursuits through the application of technology.

## DUTIES

Research & Technical Personnel (RTP) duties include marine and administrative project assistance, operating vessels, ensuring passenger safety, and compliance with Transport Canada and Marine Institute seafarer's regulations. RTP must understand navigation techniques, including reading charts, using GPS systems, and understanding hydrographic equipment.

The scope of the position will include vessel operation and basic maintenance tasks such as checking fluid levels and inspecting equipment. They may also be required to assist with mechanical issues and ensure reporting to maintenance staff. RTP may be required to create and maintain records such as passenger manifests, work procedures, maintenance logs, fuel consumption records, and incident reports.

Opportunities exist to contribute to research and project work with industrial clients or other academic partners through SOT/CTec, MI International, or collaboration with other schools. The School of Ocean Technology is actively involved in community engagement activities, and members are expected to participate in this very important aspect of our mandate. As the institute's representative, the personnel must be able to foster appropriate working relationships with stakeholders and management. Conducting themselves professionally and demonstrating a safety-minded approach to all activities is imperative.

This position will require working outdoors, over/near water, and on a boat; wearing appropriate PPE (PFD, safety shoes, eye protection, hard hat, etc.); and lifting objects (minimum 50 lbs. requirement).

## QUALIFICATIONS

Considerable (3-5 years) related experience; at minimum, Small Vessel Operator Proficiency Training Course, Restricted Operator Certificate, and a valid First Aid Certificate. ## Advancing New Brunswick's defence sector

Opportunities New Brunswick (ONB) is New Brunswick's lead business development corporation, a provincial Crown corporation dedicated to accelerating private sector growth, creating high-value jobs, and helping companies succeed locally and globally. Guided by its core values of Professionalism, Integrity, and Excellence, ONB supports businesses as they navigate challenges, improve productivity, strengthen supply chains, and expand into national and international markets. Since its inception in 2015, ONB has served as a catalyst for economic growth and job creation. ONB was recognized as one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures in 2025, named one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers for nine consecutive years from 2017 to 2025, and received Atlantic Business Magazine's Employers of Diversity award in 2022.

ONB is seeking an accomplished defence professional for a two-year contract to support the province's growing defence and security portfolio. The Senior Lead, Defence Investments will position New Brunswick as a credible partner within the national and global defence industry. Working with senior decision-makers, the Senior Lead will identify and advance investment opportunities that contribute to New Brunswick's economic growth, strengthen the province's defence sector, and support Canada's sovereignty objectives. Success in the role will depend on strong connections and an established network across Canada's defence ecosystem, with connections to organizations such as the Canadian Armed Forces, the Department of National Defence, the Defence Industrial Agency, and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.

The Senior Lead will advise ONB's senior leadership on opportunities to strengthen and grow New Brunswick's defence industry. They will build and maintain collaborative relationships with military leaders, industry stakeholders, federal departments, and national defence organizations while using ONB's customer relationship management system to ensure visibility and coordination across opportunities and company accounts. The role will identify and develop opportunities in investment, procurement, innovation, supply chains, defence logistics, and in-service support that align with provincial priorities. The Senior Lead will also monitor emerging trends, legislation, and developments in the defence and security environment, assess their potential effects on ONB's operations and strategic objectives, and prepare reports and briefings for senior leadership.

The successful candidate has a relevant post-secondary degree and progressively responsible experience in the public or private sector, including at least 10 years in defence and security.They bring in-depth knowledge of the Canadian and global defence industry, including key organizations, supply chains, procurement processes, governance frameworks, and emerging market opportunities. They have an established network across industry, government, and the military, along with demonstrated experience engaging partners andadvancing business development opportunities. Effective advisory,influencing, consultation, and relationship-building skills are essential. The successful candidate is collaborative, adaptable, and focused on achieving results. ## EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

## Confederacy of Mi'kmaw Nations

## Payroll Clerk

## About CMN

Confederacy of Mi'kmaw Nations (CMN) is a Tribal Council representing the eight Mi'kmaq communities of mainland Nova Scotia. Our mission is to proactively promote and assist Mi'kmaq communities' initiatives towards self-determination and enhancement of community. CMN's Department of Finance (DF) is currently looking for a motivated and knowledgeable candidate to fill the role of Payroll Clerk.

## Position Overview

Under the direction of the Chief Financial Officer, and reporting to the Controller, the Payroll Clerk is responsible for the day-to-day processing and updating of payroll information for all CMM and affiliates. This includes data entry, transaction review, filing, employee follow up, and clerical services to ensure effective, efficient, and accurate payroll processing operations.

## Overview of Responsibilities:

• Provide payroll support to all business areas.

• Ensure all payroll transactions are accurate and timely.

• Comply with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), financial and all CMM policies and procedures.

• Process and distribute T4's, Records of Employment, and any other mandatory payroll related information according to CMM guidelines.

• Process updates with group insurance provider Chamber of Commerce.

• Process payroll direct deposits and cheques.

• Maintain the filing system for all the payroll documentation.

• Respond to payroll-related queries from our auditors.

• Address requests from Operational managers regarding payroll transactions.

• Reconcile and update payroll related balance sheet accounts.

• Coordinate with A/P to ensure travel and workshop advances to employees are reconciled and cleared properly and efficiently.

• Participate in relevant professional development opportunities provided by CMM.

• Fluent Mi'kmaw speaker and writer is an asset.

## Position Requirements:

• Ability to manage multiple lines of business, including the balance of working with the needs and requirements of many stakeholders.

• Ability to work effectively with other departments, levels of government, industry, and the public.

• Demonstrated ability to work on multi-discipline teams, or independently, and meet deadlines.

• Excellent communication skills, written and spoken.

• Strong work ethic and ability to work in an environment requiring discretion and confidentiality.

• Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and accounting software, such as Sage etc.).

• High levels of teamwork, client service and professionalism.

• Ability to apply creativity and innovative thinking to community focused solutions.

• Demonstrated strong initiative, motivation, conscientiousness, and dedication.

• Ability to work unsupervised with a high level of productivity with the ability to seek and take direction.

• Ability to be adaptable, flexible, manage multiple priorities to ensure fellow employees are well served and relationships are developed and maintained.

• Ability to think analytically and critically while problem solving to identify specific needs and potential solutions.

• Ability to manage time and various activities effectively and efficiently while providing quality customer service.

• Able to develop relationships and this will include strong interpersonal and communication skills, both written and verbal, collaboration, conflict resolution, and active listening.

## Why work with us?

Confederacy of Mi'kmaw Nations (CMN) is well known throughout Canada as a professional organization that is committed to providing a pleasant and healthy working environment for all its employees. As an organization, we understand that a great work/life balance is essential to success. As a full-time employee you can expect:

• An atmosphere that is both professional and family oriented.

• Enrollment in the organization's benefits packages on your first day of employment with no waiting period, which includes Health & Dental, and Employee & Family Assistance Program (EFAP).

• Generous amounts of paid time off (Paid Statutory Holidays plus St. Anne's Day and Aboriginal Day, Summer Shutdown (2 weeks), Christmas Shutdown (roughly 2 weeks), plus 1 week of discretionary vacation time (up to 2 weeks with 10 years of service).

title: Construction Foreman
description:
CONSTRUCTION FOREMAN
Russon Construction | Fredericton, NB

## The Company

Russon Construction is a well-established construction company serving commercial and residential clients throughout Fredericton and the surrounding area. Since 2008, we have built our reputation on quality workmanship, attention to detail, and delivering projects that exceed our clients' expectations.

## The Opportunity

This is an opportunity for an experienced construction professional who takes pride in their work and enjoys leading a team. At Russon Construction, we believe carpentry is more than a trade-it's a profession. We are looking for someone who shares that mindset and understands that a successful project requires quality workmanship, good communication, organization, and leadership.

As a Construction Foreman, you will oversee day-to-day activities on site, coordinate employees and subcontractors, maintain our quality standards, and help ensure projects stay on schedule. This is a hands-on position. Our foremen lead from the front and work alongside the crew when required.

Our normal work hours are 7:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday, and we generally finish our work week at noon on Fridays. Occasionally, evening or weekend work may be required to accommodate project or client needs.

Pay: $27.00 to $35.00 per hour, based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated leadership ability.

## Responsibilities

• Lead and supervise employees on commercial and residential construction projects.

• Plan and coordinate daily site activities.

• Read and interpret construction drawings and specifications.

• Coordinate subcontractors, suppliers, deliveries, and materials.

• Assign work and provide direction to crew members.

• Maintain high standards for workmanship and productivity.

• Monitor project schedules and communicate progress or concerns.

• Identify site issues and help develop practical solutions.

• Maintain a clean, organized, and professional job site.

• Promote and maintain safe work practices.

• Communicate professionally with clients, subcontractors, suppliers.

• Perform hands-on carpentry and construction work as required.

## The Person

The successful candidate will be an experienced construction professional who is comfortable taking responsibility for a project and leading a crew. The ideal candidate will have:

• Red Seal Carpenter certification, or an equivalent combination of training and experience.

• A minimum of five years of construction experience.

• Strong experience in residential and/or commercial construction.

• Previous experience supervising or leading a construction crew.

• Strong knowledge of construction methods, materials, and sequencing.

• Ability to read and understand construction drawings.

• Ability to plan ahead, organize work, and keep projects moving.

• Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

• Ability to work independently with limited supervision.

• A professional attitude and strong commitment to quality workmanship.

• A valid driver's license with a clean driver's abstract.

We are looking for someone who takes ownership of their work, leads by example, and understands the importance of doing the job properly.

## To Apply

Please send your resume to jason@russonconstruction.com

We appreciate everyone who takes the time to apply. Candidates whose experience and qualifications are a good fit for the position will be contacted for an interview. References are not required with your initial application; however, references may be requested prior to an offer of employment.

At Dr. Karine Spence's Family Medical Practice, we believe our dedicated team plays a vital role in our patients' healthcare journey. We are committed to delivering an exceptional experience for every patient who walks through our doors.

## The opportunity:

Our team, located in Dieppe, NB, is offering an opportunity for a dedicated Registered Nurse to join our team on a full-time, permanent basis. We are seeking a friendly, approachable, self-motivated individual with a positive attitude who is adaptable, organized, and able to successfully balance multiple tasks in a fast-paced clinical environment. As a vital member of the team, the Registered Nurse is responsible for delivering quality nursing care to patients. The ideal candidate demonstrates strong time management skills, works efficiently in a dynamic setting, and approaches patient care with empathy and professionalism. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, are passionate about healthcare, and enjoy collaborating within a supportive team setting, we would love to hear from you!

## Key Responsibilities, as required/applicable:

The Registered Nurse (RN) will play a vital role in delivering comprehensive health care services. This role involves (but is not limited to):

• Coordinating patient care by assessing, planning, evaluating and discussing/reviewing with the physician.

• The RN will be responsible for immunizations, well baby care, pap tests, and will evaluate patients with a variety of health issues.

• Maintaining patient files, encounter information, clinical data, and other information in a careful and confidential manner via EMR Software.

• Answering inquiries in a helpful, respectful and efficient manner.

• Reviewing and processing faxes electronically, including patient referrals.

• Educating, advising, and empowering patients on preventive healthcare and disease prevention.

• Liaising between clinic, hospital, specialists, home care and community agencies to ensure integrated, continuous care.

• Staying up to date with medical advancements to provide high-quality care.

• Performing all other related clinical, administrative or special tasks as needed.

## Experience & Education Required:

• The applicant must have successfully completed a Bachelor of Science in Nursing.

• The applicant must be currently registered and in good standing with the Nurses Association of New Brunswick (NANB).

• Experience in primary care, community health, or other areas of medicine is considered a strong asset. We encourage applications from nurses with diverse backgrounds and levels of experience who are eager to join a patient-focused team.

Job Description: The Mi'kmaq Language Coordinator will assist with the on-going development, planning and implementation of the Qalipu First Nation (QFN) Mi'kmaw Language Revival project, assist QFN staff across the organization with Mi'kmaq Language translation and support and assist with the inclusion of Mi'kmaw language in other QFN initiatives where appropriate.

Responsibilities:

Plan and schedule all language classes associated with QFN's Language revival program, across various levels of Mi'kmaw instruction.

Update QFN's language resources as needed

Assist with QFN's internal and external communications that involve Mi'kmaw Language or promotion of language programs

Work alongside QFN's various departments, Chief and Council to provide organizational wide language support

When appropriate, work with QFN's external partners to provide language support as is outlined in QFN's language policy

Develop language materials and compile resources to be used in various outreach initiatives

Monitor the project budget, scope and schedule

Support the continuation of QFN's language programs and initiatives through research, proposal writing and networking

Reporting on programming progress and success

Support participants in the QFN language program through scheduling and coordination of one-on-one mentoring with the language facilitator

Promote, maintain, and advance QFN's Language Policy

Continuation of Mi'kmaw language education to ensure personal advancement toward fluency

Other duties as directed by supervisor

Qualifications:

Education: Completion of a minimum 2-year diploma level program within a field of study related to Social Sciences, Community Studies, Education, an Arts discipline such as History or Anthropology. Consideration will be given to those applicants who possess equivalent training and experience training and experience. Some knowledge of the Smith Francis Orthography would be considered an asset.

Experience: A minimum of one (1) year of experience teaching or delivering programs for adults, children and/or youth, including experience teaching the Mi'kmaw Language. Demonstrated experience in coordinating and facilitating programs and events. Experience in community engagement and working with the Mi'kmaw population in a culturally respectful and community-centered manner. Experience in

reading, writing, and speaking Mi'kmaw, with demonstrated ability to incorporate language and culture into programming. Proficiency in Microsoft operating systems and common online communication, registration, and feedback platforms.

Working Conditions: This position primarily involves office-based duties during regular working hours. However, the successful candidate will be required to work before or after regular business hours, some weekends, and in various locations for some programs and events. A portion of the work could take place in outdoor environments with variable weather conditions, based on the programming, events and initiatives undertaken. Including but not limited to working in both indoor and outdoor environments, travelling to remote communities or within Mi'kma'ki, which could require overnight stays. Physical activity is required, including walking up to 5 kilometers per day, hiking, bending, crouching and lifting to a maximum of 30 pounds.

Employee Benefits:

Statutory and Non-Statutory Holidays: Employees are entitled to 13 days off to cover Statutory and Non-statutory holidays per year.

Office Hours: Office hours during are from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm Monday to Thursday, Friday 8:30 am to 12:30 pm.

Christmas Break: the office closes during the Christmas break, this is an added bonus that employees are entitled to.

Under 2 hours Medical Appointment: Employees may attend an appointment of less than 2 hours with no deductions to Sick and Family Medical.

Discretionary Bereavement: One day off per year for the death of a relative not included as immediate family, a close friend or neighbour.

Vacation Pay: 6% paid out bi-weekly.

Apply: If you are interested in this position, please apply online with resume, covering letter, and three professional references to: https://qalipu.bamboohr.com/jobs/ with subject line: "Mi'kmaw Language Coordinator" Submissions are to be addressed to:

Mrs. Janet McAuley, Human Resources Manager

Qalipu Mi'kmaq First Nation

3 Church Street
Corner Brook, NL A2H 2Z4

The successful applicant must have a valid driver's license, and access to a reliable vehicle.

description:

## Position Summary:

The Executive Officer is the chief administrative leader of the Association, responsible for implementing the strategic direction established by the Board of Directors while overseeing all aspects of the Association's operations. Reporting directly to the Board, the Executive Officer provides leadership in governance, financial management, membership engagement, advocacy, communications, events, and organizational development to ensure the Association delivers exceptional value to its members and advances the residential construction industry. This role is a 6month contract with the possibility of permanent hire.

• Provide strategic and operational leadership to achieve the Association's mission, goals, and strategic priorities.

• Serve as the primary liaison between the Board of Directors, members, committees, government, industry partners, sponsors, and stakeholders.

• Lead governance activities by supporting Board and committee meetings, implementing Board decisions, maintaining corporate records, and ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, bylaws, and policies.

• Oversee the Association's financial operations, including budgeting, financial reporting, cash flow management, audits, and sound financial controls.

• Develop and implement strategies to recruit, retain, and engage members while delivering high-quality member services and support.

• Lead government relations and advocacy initiatives by monitoring industry issues, building relationships with elected officials, and representing the Association on matters affecting the residential construction sector.

• Direct all communications, marketing, public relations, website content, social media, newsletters, and member communications to strengthen the Association's profile and engagement.

• Provide leadership and oversight for Association events, sponsorships, programs, and the successful delivery of the annual Home Show and other signature initiatives.

• Recruit, mentor, supervise, and develop staff and contractors while fostering a collaborative, high-performing workplace culture.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with industry partners, community organizations, sponsors, and affiliated associations.

• Support long-term organizational sustainability through strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, operational improvements, and succession planning.

• Prepare reports, presentations, recommendations, and correspondence while maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, confidentiality, and member service.

## Qualifications:

The ideal candidate is a collaborative and strategic leader with experience in association management, business administration, nonprofit leadership, or a related field. They possess strong financial acumen, governance knowledge, relationship-building skills, and exceptional communication abilities. Experience working with Boards of Directors, government stakeholders, and member-based organizations is considered an asset.

• Executive leadership and organizational management

• Governance and Board relations

• Financial planning and fiscal stewardship

• Strategic planning and execution

• Membership engagement and stakeholder relations

• Government relations and advocacy

• Communications, marketing, and public relations

• Event and program management

• Human resource leadership

• Strong interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills

This is a dynamic leadership opportunity for an experienced professional who is passionate about serving members, building industry partnerships, and leading a respected organization that supports and advocates for the residential construction industry. The role combines strategic leadership with hands-on operational management and requires a collaborative, results-oriented approach.

title: Security Guard (Casual)
description:
## The organization

At Events East Group, we proudly manage and operate the Halifax Convention Centre, Scotiabank Centre and Scotiabank Centre Box Office. Our people and our community make us the favoured event destination for our guests. Whether we are attracting large delegations or hosting an elite group of athletes for an international competition, we are a catalyst for new opportunities and connections between Nova Scotia and the world.

## The position

Events East Group is now inviting applications for the position of Security Guard (casual) within our Security team.

Reporting to the Manager, Security Services, the Security Guard plays a vital role in maintaining a safe and secure environment across Events East Group facilities. This position ensures effective access management, continuous monitoring, and timely response to any security or safety concerns, supporting overall operational integrity and the well-being of all occupants. Flexibility is essential, as shift scheduling is based on events and operational needs.

Qualifications

## Qualifications and Experience

• Completion of high school or equivalent secondary school.
• Post-secondary education preferred.

• 1 year experience in a relevant, security-related role.

Responsibilities

## Key Responsibilities

## Operations:

• Directly administer and manage security access control platform (Kantech):
• Control access to facility meeting room doors as well as service corridors and stairwells, including pre-programming based on event requirements (Momentus).

• Pre-program passenger elevator requirements on a case-by-case basis; managing on-site changes and requests.

• Monitor cameras for event and facility concerns, threats, or other situations.

• Actively monitor Active Threat System (ATS); manually activating the system as required.

• Manage Intrusion Detection and Fire System at Scotiabank Centre (Simplex).

• Perform regular facility inspections including front-of-house spaces, back-of-house spaces, emergency exit routes, and limited exterior areas, noting and - where possible mitigating - safety, security, or property risks. Escalate concerns as necessary.

• Support Incident Command System (CACF platform operation during fire alarms, personnel and guest evacuations, medical emergency responses, etc.) in accordance with Events East policies, procedures, and SDS's.

• Answer incoming calls to Security Operations Centre, including facility emergency phones.

• Respond swiftly to calls for deployment or other support calls from front-of-house staff.

• Investigate alarm trips (e.g.: fire alarm activation points, one-off activation of a Nightlock, etc.) as required.

• Support facility policies and procedures during move-in and move-out's (e.g.: enforcement of non-use of passenger elevators, escalators, or Argyle Entrance).

• Review event programming regularly for changes; manage work orders including updating actuals and closing orders.

• Maintain positive working relationships with official security partner staff.

• Act as a positive role model for all staff members in job performance, work ethic, and disposition.

• Foster positive relationships with all teams, championing organizational values and recognizing colleagues who demonstrate supporting behaviors.

• Actively, constructively participate in meetings, projects, and working groups as assigned and directed.

• Participate actively in all training and development initiatives.

• Support adoption of new technologies and technical skills as they are introduced to the department.

• Accept constructive performance feedback and coaching; independently apply self-improvement actions as appropriate.

• Other duties as required.

## Administration:

• Adhere to all Events East Group policies, procedures, and guidelines

• Complete a shift report for each scheduled shift.

• Complete or gather all applicable documents (key sign-outs, event staff sign-ins, etc.).

• Manage the respective security office e-mails.

• Act decisively in challenging or stressful situations; problem-solving in the moment.

• Report any faulty or defective equipment or system to the Manager, Security Services.

• Report any supply shortage or deficiency to the Manager, Security Services.

• Report any facility or infrastructure damage or deficiency to Manager, Security Services and the respective Property Services Building Manager.

## Health & Safety:

• Adhere to all departmental standards, guidelines, and procedures to ensure the safety of oneself, team members, and guests.

• Report safety hazards, near misses, and incidents promptly, taking appropriate action to address hazards when safe, and actively participating in the investigation process.

• Wear, use, and ensure the appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) as required, re-porting any violations or damaged PPE within the team or onsite.

• Achieve and maintain first aid certification at SFA CPR C level.

• Take a lead role in facility response to fire alarms and medical emergencies during non-critical times.

• Identify and mitigate any event-related health and safety concerns, both property-related and security-related, protecting Events East Group against losses, penalties, damages, settlements, or other expenses or liabilities.

title: Executive Director
description:
CAREER OPPORTUNITY

Mainland NS Building Trades: Executive Director

## Position Overview

The Mainland Nova Scotia Building Trades is a council of construction industry Trade Unions. Our affiliated Unions provide highly trained, safe working trade professionals to the Nova Scotia construction industry. Our mandate includes promoting and developing business for our 12,000 members and providing a united voice on issues affecting the professional trades.

The Executive Director of the Mainland Nova Scotia Building Trades Council is a pivotal leadership role responsible for supporting the 13 affiliated unions and guiding the organization towards its mission and goals. This role requires a dynamic leader capable of managing complex relationships with affiliated unions, government, industry and community partners while ensuring the Council's objectives are effectively communicated and advanced. The Executive Director also oversees the administration and supports the activities of the Building Trades Advancement College.

## Key Competencies

## Government Relations

• Support the Council's government relations and advocacy priorities at the provincial level.

• Monitor legislative, regulatory and policy developments that affect affiliated unions and provide timely updates and briefing materials to union leadership.

• Maintain relationships with elected officials, government agencies and other relevant stakeholders; represent the Council in consultations and meetings as directed by the Executive.

## Industry and Labour Relations

• Establish and nurture partnerships with government, industry leaders and key industry stakeholders, Indigenous leaders and leaders of underrepresented groups to promote the interests of Unionized labour.

• Provide organizational leadership and foster inclusive working relationships among the Council, Executive and affiliated unions, promoting collaboration, transparency and accountability.

• Stay informed about industry trends and developments that impact Unionized labour.

• Collaborate with owners and employers to develop fair labour practices and policies.

• Collaborate with Union leaders to address provincial workplace issues and improve labour conditions.

• Coordinate collective bargaining efforts among the affiliated Unions.

## Public Relations

• Develop and oversee communication strategies for Construction Industry Trade Unions.

• Coordinate public campaigns to raise awareness regarding Union initiatives and achievements.

• Serve as a spokesperson for the Unions, representing their positions and interests to the government, media, public, and other key industry stakeholders.

## Additional Responsibilities

• Leadership - Provide strong leadership on behalf of the Council and the 13 affiliated Unions, promoting a culture of collaboration, transparency, and accountability.

• Prepare reports, recommendations, briefing materials to support Executive decision making; provide regular updates on operations, finances, relationships, communications and emerging issues.

• Strategic planning - Develop and implement long-term strategic growth and success plans.

• Budgeting - Oversee the Council's financial operations, including budgeting, and financial planning.

• Administrative Oversight - Oversee the day-to-day operations of the Council and the Trades College, ensuring compliance with accreditation and regulatory requirements, as well as the efficiency and effectiveness of all programs and activities.

## Qualifications

All candidates must have proven leadership and strong communication skills. Knowledge of the Unionized construction industry is essential. The position requires an individual with energy, presence, integrity and the ability to seize opportunities and be a strong advocate for Unionized Labour.

Additional criteria that will be considered in the selection process includes:

• A minimum of 10 years experience in a leadership role within a Union, government, or related organization.

• Proven track record in government relations, labour relations, industry relations, and public relations.

• Strong analytical and strategic abilities.

• Experience in financial management and budgeting.

• Post-secondary education in labour relations, business, or a related field.

## Compensation

The Executive Director position offers a competitive salary based on experience, plus comprehensive benefits, including health insurance, a retirement plan, paid time off, and professional development opportunities.

## Application Process

To apply, submit your resume, cover letter, and references to Jonathan Gaul, President of the Mainland Nova Scotia Building Trades Council, at jgaul@dc39.ca by 4pm on October 16, 2026. Use "MLNS Building Trades Executive Director Application" in the subject line.

Please note that this position requires travel within Nova Scotia and occasional travel outside the province. We thank all applicants; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Bryony House is seeking an experienced Programs and Operations Manager to join our leadership team and play an important role in supporting our mission to provide a safe haven for women and their children experiencing intimate partner violence.

If you are a strong people leader who can balance staff leadership, program oversight and the day-to-day operational demands of a busy organization, we would love to hear from you! This role is well suited to someone who is comfortable making decisions, navigating competing priorities and supporting teams doing meaningful work.

Qualifications
• Degree or diploma in Social Work, Women's Studies, Sociology, Psychology, nonprofit management, business administration or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• At least five years of relevant experience, including three years of management experience with responsibility for supervising staff.

• Strong experience in people leadership, performance management and conflict resolution.

• Experience coordinating staff schedules and timesheets, along with budget management and financial reporting.

• Experience with facilities, maintenance or other operational responsibilities.

• Knowledge of intimate partner violence, trauma-informed practice, crisis intervention, harm reduction and the systemic barriers affecting marginalized communities.

• Strong organizational, communication and decision-making skills with a commitment to confidentiality.

• Proficiency with common workplace technology, with the ability to learn and use PayWorks and HIFIS.

• Experience in a unionized workplace and/or IPV shelter, housing, outreach or children's services is considered an asset.

Responsibilities
Reporting to the Executive Director, the Programs and Operations Manager provides leadership to assigned teams and oversees programs, shelter operations, building maintenance, budgets and payroll administration. Specific responsibilities include:

## Team Leadership & Supervision

• Provide direct supervision and leadership to Outreach, Housing Support, Children's Counsellors and household staff, including regular individual and team meetings.

• Lead recruitment, onboarding, training and performance management for assigned teams in consultation with the Executive Director.

• Coordinate schedules, leave and coverage while balancing operational needs, approved budgets and collective agreement requirements.

• Set clear expectations, address workplace concerns and conflict constructively, and support a respectful and inclusive workplace.

• Apply organizational policies and the collective agreement consistently and support labour relations matters involving assigned teams.

## Program Oversight

• Oversee outreach, housing support and children's programming, ensuring services are coordinated, accessible and responsive to client needs.

• Work collaboratively with the Shelter Manager to coordinate support across shelter and community services and address service gaps.

• Review program documentation and support staff in navigating complex situations, escalating significant concerns when appropriate.

• Oversee the Reaching Home housing project, including its budget, activities, outcomes, funder relationships and reporting requirements.

## Shelter Operations & Building Maintenance

• Oversee the daily functioning of the shelter building and household services, including cleaning, food services, supplies, household, and maintenance coordination.

• Monitor building access, security, emergency readiness and operational risks in collaboration with the Shelter Manager and Executive Director.

• Participate in the Joint Occupational Health and Safety Committee and support the development and implementation of operational and safety procedures.

## Budget, Scheduling, & Administration

• Manage assigned program, household and operational budgets, monitor monthly spending and take action to address variances or emerging cost pressures.

• Coordinate schedules, leave requests and coverage for assigned teams while balancing operational needs, approved budgets and collective agreement requirements.

• Manage and approve staff timesheets in PayWorks, reviewing hours worked, overtime, premiums and leave for accuracy and resolving discrepancies before approval deadlines.

• Maintain accurate purchasing and expense records and support annual budgeting and forecasting.

• Oversee timely and accurate HIFIS documentation for assigned programs, including supporting staff training, data quality and reporting.

This role provides the right candidate with the opportunity to work with an amazing team of people dedicated to providing women and children a safe haven away from violence. Our team members also enjoy:

• Comprehensive benefits plan, 50% of premiums covered by Bryony House

• An RRSP matching program

• Full-time hours

• Paid time off

description:
## JOB PURPOSE

The Trauma Nurse is an RNCA position within the DECH Emergency Department that provides experienced clinical support and leadership in the assessment and management of trauma and other high­acuity patients. Working as part of the multidisciplinary team, the Trauma Nurse coordinates care from initial presentation through stabilization, treatment, and final disposition or transfer, ensuring safe, timely, and evidence-informed care.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Current registration with the College of Nursing of New Brunswick (CNNB).

• Current BCLS certification/ RQI certification.

• Current ACLS certification/ Current PALS certification.

• Completion of Trauma Nursing Core Course (TNCC), Emergency Nurse Pediatric Course (ENPC)

• Completion of EPICC foundations, Pediatrics and Trauma or willingness to obtain.

• Current advanced care nursing competencies.

• Demonstrated experience caring for high-acuity and trauma patients.

• Strong clinical assessment, critical-thinking and decision-making skills.

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and unpredictable environment.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

• INFO debrief certification or willingness to obtain.

• Minimum 5 years Emergency Department experience or 2 years with the completion of the Critical Care Course.

• Demonstrated knowledge and skills in the competencies of BCLS, ACLS, PALS, CTAS, Advanced Nursing Competencies, Emergency Pediatric Nursing (ENPC}, Trauma Nursing (TNCC}, and Basic 12 lead ECG interpretation as demonstrated by certification and/or written and practical testing.

• Demonstrated assessment skills and ability to function independently with minimal supervision.

• Good work record and ability to attend work on a regular basis.

• Ability to perform the duties of the position.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

In addition to the responsibilities of an Emergency Department RN, the Trauma Nurse will:

• Participate in trauma activations and assume an appropriate role within the trauma team.

• Provide comprehensive and timely assessment of trauma patients.

• Support the stabilization and resuscitation of critically injured patients.

• Assist with the coordination of nursing care during trauma activations.

• Anticipate patient and team needs during high-acuity trauma events.

• Prepare and assist with trauma procedures, needed departmental procedures, equipment, medications and blood products, including mass transfusion protocol.

• Collaborate closely with the Emergency Department physician and multidisciplinary team.

• Monitor patient response to interventions and communicate changes in condition promptly.

• Support the coordination of diagnostic investigations, consultations and patient transfers.

• Ensure accurate and timely documentation of trauma care.

• Assist with the safe transition of patients to inpatient units, critical care or receiving facilities.

• Participate in trauma debriefings following significant events.

• Maintains strict confidentiality regarding all aspects of work.

• Provide support and guidance to nurses developing their trauma knowledge and skills.

• Identify and communicate opportunities to improve trauma care and patient safety.

• Completes annual advanced nursing competencies related to emergency care.

• Maintains strict confidentiality regarding all aspects of work.

## COMPETENCIES

Competencies Identified by Horizon Health Network:

• Emergency Nursing Assessment.

• Trauma Assessment and Management.

• Clinical Judgment and Decision-Making.

• Triage and Prioritization.

• Resuscitation and Stabilization.

• Recognition of Clinical Deterioration.

• Patient- and Family-Centered Care.

• interprofessional Collaboration.

• Communication and Handover.

• Patient Safety and Quality Improvement.

• Professional Accountability.

• Leadership, Education and Knowledge Sharing.

• Communication and Interpersonal Skills.

• Decision making.

• Critical thinking.

• Professionalism.

• Patient/Client Focus

If a candidate's primary language of communication is not English, an English Language Proficiency Evaluation is required for all postings (Reading, Writing and Oral).

title: Fish Handling Labourer
description:
Hermitage Processing Inc., a Division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, is offering a unique opportunity for the right individual to join the Processing Team as Fish Handling Labourer.

Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly-skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## Position Summary

The Fish Handling Labourer is responsible for receiving, handling, sorting, grading, weighing, transferring, and preparing fish and seafood products for storage, processing, and shipment. The position supports daily seafood operations by moving products between receiving, holding, processing, storage, and loading areas; operating material handling equipment; loading and unloading transportation vehicles; and maintaining product quality and food safety standards. Employees may also assist with fish processing, packaging, and production activities as operational requirements dictate.

## Duties and Responsibilities

The employee will perform some or all of the following duties:

• Receive fish and seafood products from holding tanks, receiving areas, and other designated work areas.

• Transfer fish and seafood products between holding tanks, coolers, storage facilities, processing areas, and loading areas.

• Assist with the transfer and handling of fish and seafood products from vessels when operationally required.

• Sort, grade, weigh, inspect, and record fish and seafood products according to species, size, quality standards, and destination requirements.

• Prepare fish and seafood products for storage and shipment by icing, packing, palletizing, and staging products for transport.

• Load and unload trucks and other transportation vehicles for the movement and shipment of fish and seafood products.

• Operate forklifts, pallet jacks, and other material handling equipment to move products, packaging materials, and supplies throughout the facility.

• Assist with shipping, receiving, inventory control, and product traceability activities.

• Clean and sanitize tanks, equipment, work areas, coolers, loading areas, and storage facilities

• Follow all food safety, quality assurance, biosecurity, occupational health and safety, and company policies and procedures.

• Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work environment.

Secondary Duties and Responsibilities

(Performed as required based on operational needs)

• Assist fish processing operations, including cleaning, trimming, grading, filleting, packaging, and preparing fish and seafood products for further processing or shipment.

• Support production-line operations during periods of increased production demand.

## Employment Requirements

• No formal education required.

• Previous fish processing, seafood handling, warehouse, shipping/receiving, wharf operations, or general labour experience is considered an asset.

• Forklift experience is considered an asset.

• Ability to work in a physically demanding environment.

• Ability to work effectively as part of a team.

• Ability to follow workplace safety procedures and operational instructions.

## Work Conditions and Physical Capabilities

• Repetitive tasks.

• Physically demanding work.

• Frequent lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling of products and materials.

• Standing and walking for extended periods.

• Bending, crouching, and reaching.

• Exposure to wet, cold, humid, and outdoor conditions.

• Overtime and weekend work may be required based on operational needs.

## The Opportunity

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to work within the parameters of the role but to reach your fullest potential. We are a team that is driven to succeed. We count performance, we reward contribution, and we recognize talent. It is about being at the center of a global leader in seafood and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

Why Cooke ? Simple, because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

We appreciate all resumes; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: AI Solutions Architect
description:
## Purpose of position

The AI Solutions Architect designs, governs, develops and delivers enterprise AI solutions aligned with Jazz architecture, security, compliance, data governance requirements and ensures deployed AI solutions remain secure, reliable, compliant, supportable, and effective throughout their operational lifecycle. The role actively builds critical solution components in conjunction with the Software Development team and AI Analysts, translating business needs into secure, supportable and measurable production capabilities.

## Key responsibilities

• Lead end-to-end solution architecture for AI initiatives from discovery through production.

• Define integration patterns, security requirements, data flows, deployment models and operational support requirements.

• Establish reusable architecture patterns, implementation standards and technical roadmaps.

• Lead technical design reviews and coordinate delivery across business, data, software development and infrastructure stakeholders.

• Design, build, test and deploy AI-enabled applications, services and integrations.

• Develop proofs of concept, prototypes, accelerators, reference implementations and critical production components.

## Required qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or diploma in Computer Science, Information Systems or a related discipline; equivalent education and experience may be considered.

• 5+ years working in IT, designing and developing enterprise solutions.

• Experience with Generative AI, Machine Learning or Advanced Analytics.

• Knowledge of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI Agents, Prompt Engineering or Responsible AI principles.

• Experience in API design, Enterprise Integration.

• Experience with DevOps, CI/CD, testing and monitoring practices.

• Knowledge of secure development, privacy and data governance practices.

• Strong business analysis, facilitation, technical writing, stakeholder communication skills, strategic relationship-building and change leadership skills.

• Advanced experience in Enterprise Solution Architecture, Software Development, Data Architecture or Cloud Architecture.

• Experience collaborating with multidisciplinary development and business teams and moving solutions from concept to production.

• Strategic and systems thinking skills.

• Ability to present technical concepts and recommendations to business and technology leaders.

title: Aircraft Maintenance Auditor
description:
## Join a Team That Keeps Aircraft Safe, Compliant, and Mission Ready!

PAL Technical Services is a leader in full-service aircraft maintenance, providing a comprehensive range of aviation services including aircraft modifications, line maintenance, maintenance repair and overhaul (MRO), and engineering support. As the maintenance division of the PAL Group of Companies, we support both domestic and international operations while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, and regulatory compliance.

We are currently seeking an Aircraft Maintenance Auditor to join our team in St. John's, NL.

In this role, you will provide independent oversight of maintenance operations, technical records, airworthiness programs, and quality systems to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, company procedures, and industry standards. You will play a key role in supporting our Safety Management System (SMS), Quality Management System (QMS), and continuous improvement initiatives across the organization.

## What You'll Do

## Audit & Compliance

• Conduct audits of aircraft maintenance operations, airworthiness activities, maintenance planning, technical records, supply chain, stores, and maintenance control functions.

• Assess compliance with Canadian Aviation Regulations (CARs), company manuals, SMS requirements, and applicable industry standards.

• Monitor ongoing compliance with Transport Canada requirements and organizational procedures.

• Support regulatory inspections, certification audits, and customer oversight activities.

## Audit Reporting & Corrective Actions

• Prepare detailed audit reports and document findings, observations, and non-conformances.

• Support root cause analysis and corrective action development.

• Track corrective actions through to completion and verify effectiveness.

## Continuous Improvement & Risk Management

• Identify quality, safety, and airworthiness risks.

• Analyze trends and recurring audit findings.

• Recommend improvements that enhance compliance, operational effectiveness, and overall system performance.

## Supplier & Contractor Oversight

• Conduct supplier and vendor audits.

• Assess contracted maintenance providers for regulatory and contractual compliance.

• Evaluate supplier quality systems and corrective action effectiveness.

## Records & Documentation Review

• Review maintenance records and documentation for accuracy, completeness, and traceability.

• Verify compliance with document control and record retention requirements.

## What You'll Bring

## Required Qualifications

• Diploma or Degree in Aviation Maintenance, Aerospace, Engineering, Quality Assurance, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Minimum 5 years of aviation maintenance experience.

• Strong knowledge of:
• Canadian Aviation Regulations (CARs)

• Continuing Airworthiness requirements

• Maintenance Control Systems

• Safety Management Systems (SMS)

• Quality Management Systems (QMS)

## Preferred Qualifications

• Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME) Licence.

• Minimum 3 years of experience in quality assurance, auditing, regulatory compliance, airworthiness, or maintenance management.

• AS9110, ISO 9001, Internal Auditor, or Lead Auditor certification.

• SMS Auditor Training.

• Human Factors Training.

• Experience working within a Transport Canada-regulated environment.

## Skills & Competencies

• Strong analytical and investigative abilities.

• Excellent communication and report-writing skills.

• Root cause analysis and corrective action management experience.

• Exceptional attention to detail.

• Ability to work independently while maintaining auditor objectivity.

• Strong organizational and time-management skills.

## Working Conditions

• Travel to maintenance bases, hangars, operational facilities, and supplier locations will be required.

• Combination of office, hangar, and field-based work environments.

• Occasional evening and weekend work to support audits, inspections, and operational requirements.

## Why Work for PAL?

At PAL, we recognize that our people are our greatest asset. That's why we offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support you both professionally and personally.

## The Perks of Being One of Our PALs

• Personal travel privileges with PAL and interline agreements with multiple airlines

• Industry and partner discounts

• Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and life insurance coverage

• Pension Plan with Employer Matching

• Employee Stock Purchase Plan

• Employee Tuition Assistance Program

• Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP)

## Ready to Apply?

If you're passionate about aviation safety, quality assurance, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement, we'd love to hear from you.

PAL Technical Services is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diversity, equity, and inclusion are valued and celebrated. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences.

title: Compliance & Enforcement Coordinator (Program Admin Officer 1-2)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50024

Department: Justice

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 18-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Nova Scotia Accessibility Directorate is a dynamic and committed team that is leading and coordinating Nova Scotia's work towards the goal to become an accessible province by 2030. We work together with persons with disabilities, community organizations, businesses, municipalities, post-secondary institutions and other partners to advance the cultural shift needed.
The Accessibility Directorate has built strong relationships across government and with public sector and community partners to support their efforts to improve accessibility, including the Government's accessibility plan. We lead the development of accessibility standards in the areas of education, employment, service delivery, public transportation, and information and communication. The Directorate also leads the implementation and enforcement of the Built Environment Accessibility Standard Regulation. Additionally, we develop accessibility awareness resources, tools and awareness activities to help create more accessible and inclusive communities.

About Our Opportunity
As Compliance and Enforcement Coordinator, you will support the Accessibility Directorate's compliance and enforcement activities. You will track compliance inquiries, coordinate compliance monitoring and reporting, and conduct inspection and enforcement activities as needed. You will work with public sector bodies, government departments, businesses, and the public to advance understanding and compliance with the legislation. You will work with Directorate staff to develop and implement compliance strategies, processes, resources.
The Compliance and Enforcement Coordinator reports to the Manager of Compliance and Capacity Building.

Primary Accountabilities
In this role, you will regularly:
• Receive and respond to general inquiries related to accessibility and application of the Accessibility Act (Act) and Accessibility Standard Regulations. This includes triaging inquiries and preparing responses, that are accurate, clear, and consistent.
• Monitor prescribed public sector bodies' compliance with accessibility plan and accessibility advisory committee requirements and provide guidance and identify available supports.
• Receive and respond to complaints of non-compliance in relation to the Act and regulations, under the supervision and guidance of the Manager of Compliance and Capacity Building.
• Maintain and manage the compliance and enforcement database.
• Support the collection and reporting of data related to compliance and enforcement activities.

You will occasionally:
• Conduct inspections and document findings in relation to non-compliance and issue compliance orders as needed, under the supervision and direction of the Manager of Compliance and Capacity Building.
• Assist in developing, implementing, and improving processes and guidelines to support effective compliance and enforcement program delivery and implementation.
• Contribute to the development and facilitation of information and educational materials related to compliance and enforcement.
• Support public events and conferences regarding outreach and education presentations to prescribed public sector bodies and other organizations.
• Liaise with partners across government, public sector bodies, businesses, community organizations and others on compliance and enforcement issues and activities.

Qualifications and Experience
Competencies assessed for the position include:
• A bachelor's degree and a minimum of 1 year in a related field. An equivalent combination of training and experience will be considered.
• Experience conducting inspections, auditing or other compliance and enforcement activities to support regulatory programs.

DIRECTOR OF FACILITIES

JOB SUMMARY:

This position reports to the General Manager - Operations Services.

The incumbent is accountable for providing leadership in the planning, design, construction, management, operations and maintenance of all City facilities to ensure they are sustainable and efficiently operated. This position works closely with other department heads by providing expertise and support with regards to the operation and maintenance of physical structures in which other departments operate. This position will also implement appropriate facility management information technology solutions to assist in the management of city facilities over the entire life cycle. The incumbent will lead priority capital projects dealing with new city facilities and historic preservation projects (i.e. Treitz House and Fire facilities, etc.) that will enhance the physical character of Moncton and serve the City well into the future .

EDUCATION:

• Completion of a post secondary degree or diploma in Engineering or related field associated with facility management, building construction, architecture etc.

• A P. Eng. Designation would be a definite asset.

• LEED professional accreditation is considered an asset.

EXPERIENCE:

• Must have a minimum of five (5) years experience in a senior management role with direct responsibility for managing staff and resources.

• Must have experience in technical systems related to facility management, building construction, etc.

• Must be willing to maintain and/or undertake professional development as the department directs, following industry norms.

• Professional experience in energy management planning, energy auditing and green building design will be considered an asset.

LANGUAGE:

• English essential. The ability to function in both official languages is an asset, but not a requirement.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

• Must have above average communication skills, both orally and in writing.

• Must have demonstrated leadership, relationship management and negotiation skills.

• Must be a team player.

• Must have the ability to write, interpret and understand construction specifications including blueprints, as-builts, and technical reports for various building components and functions.

• Must have the ability to multi-task, prioritize and meet deadlines.

• Must be self-motivated and highly capable of solving problems.

• Must be knowledgeable of the New Brunswick Occupational Health and Safety Act and other relevant legislation as it relates to facility management.

• Must be familiar with green building design standards including LEED and Green Globes.

• Knowledge of current building codes and other relevant regulations is considered an asset.

• Ability to effectively utilize various administrative programs (Office 365), including strong skills in data collection and analysis, as well as implementation of modern technologies.

OTHER:

• Must possess and maintain a valid Class 5 Driver's License.

CONTACT:

• Must have the ability to establish and maintain effective internal and external working relationships at all levels. The work requires contact with the general public, vendors, employees of various departments, members of City Council, other levels of government and outside contractors, developers and all facility stakeholders.

• This position requires an individual with a strong customer service approach to their work, a positive attitude that reflects the best interests of the corporation and the community at large and a strong, team player.

SUPERVISION:

• This position leads and manages a diverse group of staff responsible for project management, operations and maintenance, and all aspects of facility management.

• The work requires supervising, coaching, and mentoring employees, allocating staff to projects, reviewing and evaluating the quality and quantity of work, and formally evaluating staff performance and manages issues related to performance and attendance.

CONDITIONS OF WORK:

• This position requires minimal physical effort with minimal exposure to disagreeable conditions. The majority of work is performed in a professional office setting with frequent visits to various buildings, facilities, structures or construction sites.

• Work is at times intense requiring an individual with the ability to work under pressure within tight time frames for project completion.

• Work may be required on weekends, evenings and holidays.

conversations.

• Work collaboratively with stakeholders to provide support and subject matter expertise on the identification and development of KPI’s and assist in enabling value for money and risk mitigation.

• Analyze internal and third-party data to identify risks related to supply chain sustainability including potential disruptions in the current and projected future supply chain, and monitor threats to supply availability and NLHS operations.

• Evaluate and promote Environmental Social Governance (ESG) initiatives in NLHS in relation to supply chain and SRM including collaborating with suppliers to implement sustainable practices and monitor their progress, and promote diversity and inclusion within the supply chain;

• Promote the Supplier Relationship Management function and associated customer/end user satisfaction goals internally.

• Assist with the management and coordination of product recalls, warranties and supplier complaints.

success.
* Minimum 2 years experience in managing suppliers, leading difficult conversations, navigating amongst multiple parties with differing perspectives, decision making, and project management.
* Minimum 2 years specific supply chain experience in: business and supply chain strategy; contract and formal legal document writing and management, supplier engagement, performance monitoring, execution management; supplier relationship management, and risk management.
* Experience in working within the ESG space particularly in monitoring impacts on supplier relationships.
* Very proficient in preparing electronic reports, analysis, data management, and communications.
* Strong writing and formatting skills to develop, proof-read, edit, and format legally binding content is required. And, must have the ability to communicate, both orally and written, with internal customers, departments, vendors, and other external stakeholders such as Public Procurement Agency and legal counsel to ensure there is a clear understanding of the requirements.
