title: Civil Engineer
description:
Located in Oxford, NS
Application Deadline: October 28, 2026

Oxford Frozen Foods Ltd, a member of the Bragg Group of Companies, is a family-owned international business that has over 1,200 employees, eight manufacturing facilities and two large farming operations within Atlantic Canada and the United States. Oxford Frozen Foods is the world's largest provider of Wild Blueberries, one of North America's largest producers of premium frozen carrots and one of Canada's premier manufacturers of onion rings and battered appetizers.

## Benefits of being an Oxford Frozen Foods Employee:

• Comprehensive benefit package including a matching contribution pension plan.

• Employee Housing Loan program provides a forgivable loan up to $40,000.

• Vacation PLUS we offer a vacation purchase plan allowing for additional time off.

• Employee Discount Program offering discounts at various businesses and industries.

## Position Scope:

We are seeking an experienced and solutions-driven Civil Engineer to oversee the structural integrity, facility expansion, and site infrastructure of our food processing operations. In this critical role, you will bridge the gap between heavy civil infrastructure and strict food safety standards. You will manage capital construction projects, oversee wastewater treatment systems, and ensure our facilities are engineered to support cutting-edge processing equipment while maintaining compliance with environmental and hygienic design regulations.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Lead civil and structural design efforts for plant expansions, retrofits, and new facility construction, managing projects from conceptual design through commissioning.

• Design and oversee the installation of critical plant infrastructure, including sanitary flooring, drainage systems, utility piping, and structural supports for heavy processing equipment and silos.

• Manage and upgrade site wastewater treatment facilities, ensuring optimal capacity and strict compliance with local, provincial/state, and federal environmental regulations.

• Prepare bid documents, select contractors, and oversee on-site construction to ensure work is completed safely, on time, within budget, and without disrupting ongoing plant production.

• Work closely with Process Engineers, Quality Assurance, and Maintenance teams to ensure all structural and civil modifications align with Lean manufacturing principles and food safety standards (GMP, HACCP, SQF).

• Conduct regular structural assessments of the plant, roof systems, and site grounds (paving, storm water management) to identify and address maintenance needs proactively.

## Work Environment & Physical Requirements:

• On-site in a manufacturing environment with exposure to plant operations.

• Exposure to external climate conditions.

• Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as required.

## Qualification & Experience:

• Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering or a closely related discipline.

• Professional Engineer (P.Eng. / PE) designation is highly preferred (or eligible for registration).

• Minimum of 5 years of civil or structural engineering experience in an industrial manufacturing environment. Direct experience in the food and beverage processing industry is highly desirable.

• Strong understanding of industrial wastewater management, hygienic facility design, structural load analysis, and construction management.

• Knowledge of building codes, environmental regulations, and food safety standards (CFIA, FDA, HACCP) as they pertain to facility design.

• Proficiency in AutoCAD, Civil 3D, Revit, or similar drafting and design software.

• Criminal Record Checks are required for successful applicants.

• Valid Driver's License is required.

Oxford Frozen Foods is searching for someone who demonstrates professionalism and integrity, and who is committed to following company policies, procedures, and all applicable regulations.

The successful candidate demonstrates a strong commitment to safety, maintains organized and clean work areas, and effectively manages time in a fast-paced environment. They possess solid organizational skills, a strong sense of urgency, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team.

Oxford Frozen Foods is committed to providing a safe, respectful, inclusive workplace free from discrimination, harassment, and workplace violence and welcome applications from all qualified individuals.

Applications can be made by visiting www.oxfordfrozenfoods.com/opportunity and applying through our career center.

title: Senior Machine Learning Developer I
description:
Req Id: 433050

At Bell, we do more than build world-class networks, develop innovative services and create original multiplatform media content – we advance how Canadians connect with each other and the world.

If you're ready to bring game-changing ideas to life and join a community that values, professional growth and employee wellness, we want you on the Bell team.

The Bell Mobility team offers the best and latest mobile devices, wireless services and Internet of Things solutions to consumer and business customers, with the top speeds, coverage and reliability on Canada's Best National Network. We love to innovate, embrace big challenges, and live for the newest technology

Summary
We're looking for a Senior ML Developer to join our AIOps Platform team. In this role, you will work closely with Data Scientists to take AI/ML solutions to production. You will accelerate the delivery of our core AI services from proof-of-concept to highly available, production-grade. You will bridge the gap between data science and platform operations, applying robust software engineering practices, intent-driven development, and MLOps best practices to ensure our systems are scalable, reliable, and performant.

Key Responsibilities
• Production ML Engineering: Collaborate with data science, platform developers and architects, and other teams to operationalize ML models, LLM / Agentic workflows, and advanced analytics.

• MLOps & Lifecycle Management: Own the end-to-end ML lifecycle (feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment). Enforce MLOps best practices including CI/CD, model versioning, reproducibility, and rollout controls.

• Pipeline & Architecture Design: Build real-time streaming pipelines using Apache Beam/Dataflow and design robust event-driven architectures (Kafka/PubSub patterns).

• Design and build high-throughput, low-latency system architectures with strict idempotency and deduplication.

• API & Service Delivery: Lead API and schema design for complex ML-enabled services.

• Quality & Reliability: Instill a strong testing and quality mindset across the team (test-driven development, unit/integration tests, code reviews, security checks). Debug and optimize distributed systems for maximum performance.

• Infrastructure Management: Implement Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/CDKTF) to manage scalable, cloud-native deployments.

Critical Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science or Computer Engineering or a related field. Relevant experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

• 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, specifically focused on production-grade AI/ML systems.

• Expert-level proficiency in Python software engineering.

• Strong experience with the GCP stack (Vertex AI, BigQuery, Spanner, GKE, GCS, Pub/Sub).

• Deep practical knowledge of MLOps best practices and taking models from proof-of-concept to highly available production services.

• Hands-on experience with real-time data processing (Apache Beam, Dataflow) and event-driven architecture (Kafka, PubSub).

• Proven ability in Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/CDKTF) and cloud-native orchestration (Kubernetes).

• Strong software-testing and quality discipline (unit/integration/end-to-end/functional testing, code review, security checks)

• Hands-on experience with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, scikit-learn, XGBoost, or TensorFlow.

• Experience with graph databases / Spanner Graph and Graph Neural Networks (GNN)

• Strong communication, analytical, debugging, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Ability to write clean, efficient, and reusable code.

• Plus if you have experience with distributed / federated query engines such as Trino.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with telecom industry data and network architecture.

• Post-secondary degrees or certificates in Statistics, Mathematics, and Data Science.

• Experience deploying secure agentic workflows with cost management and decision traceability.

title: Director, Marine Engineering
description:
Port Saint John is seeking a Marine Engineer to join its Infrastructure, Assets and Engineering team. This role leads and supports marine infrastructure projects that enable safe, efficient and sustainable port operations.

The Marine Engineer provides technical and project management expertise for piers, berths, wharves, navigation channels, turning basins, dredging and other marine assets. The position is the Port's technical lead for capital dredging and supports the operational dredging program while collaborating with internal teams, consultants, contractors, regulators and port users.

Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in civil, marine, coastal, ocean, geotechnical or structural engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

• Seven to ten years of progressive engineering experience, preferably involving marine or port infrastructure, dredging, coastal works, heavy civil infrastructure or major capital projects.

• Demonstrated experience with project delivery, procurement, construction, contract administration, consultant management and contractor oversight.

• Strong technical judgment, project management, communication, collaboration and problem-solving skills.

• Registration as a Professional Engineer, or eligibility for registration, with the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of New Brunswick.

• Eligibility to obtain the required Transport Canada security clearance and possession of a valid Class 5 New Brunswick driver's license, or equivalent.

• Project management or related marine construction, dredging, environmental, safety or asset management credentials are considered assets.

You will thrive in this role if you:

• Put safety and wellness first, using a safety-first approach to guide your decisions.

• Show initiative, embrace innovation and persevere when facing obstacles.

• Treat others with respect and build trust through honesty, openness and accountability.

• Commit to continuous learning and support the development of your colleagues.

• Include others by building strong relationships and engaging meaningfully with

Responsibilities
• Plan and deliver marine infrastructure projects from scope development and procurement through construction and close-out.

• Lead the capital dredging program and support operational dredging, including technical review, permitting, budgets, schedules, risk and stakeholder coordination.

• Review engineering drawings, specifications, studies, estimates, tender documents and contractor deliverables.

• Assess navigation channels, vessel accommodation, under-keel clearance, mooring systems, berth loading and related operational requirements.

• Support inspections, condition assessments and lifecycle planning for Port-owned marine assets.

• Coordinate consultants, contractors, regulators, terminal operators and other stakeholders while ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, contractual and regulatory requirements.

• Prepare project updates, reports, recommendations, funding documentation and organized technical records.

Port Saint John operates on the traditional and unceded territory of the Wolastoqey, Mi'Kmaq, and Peskotomuhkati Nations. Our commitment to truth and reconciliation is grounded in respect for Indigenous cultures and heritage and in building meaningful relationships.

Port Saint John connects people and markets by building partnerships and developing innovative solutions that create economic and social value. With links to more than 350 ports worldwide and direct access to central Canadian markets through Canadian National and Canadian Pacific rail networks and the Trans-Canada Highway, the Port is a key facilitator of trade within Canada's Atlantic Gateway. Our transportation infrastructure provides a marine gateway to global markets while supporting prosperity and sustainability.

Help shape the future of marine infrastructure at Port Saint John. If your experience and values align with this opportunity, we invite you to apply.

The application deadline is October 19th.

title: Town Manager
description:
Employment Opportunity- Town Manager

The Town of Deer Lake is perfectly located within the province of Newfoundland and Labrador as it serves as the central hub between Labrador and the Island of Newfoundland. Beautifully situated at the top of the Humber Valley, Deer Lake serves as the gateway to Gros Morne National Park, Northern Peninsula and Labrador. Home to approximately 5,000 residents, our thriving Town of Deer Lake offers endless freshwater beaches, a thriving regional airport, and is commonly affirmed as the snowmobile hub of the island.

The Town Council of Deer Lake is pursuing to hire a Town Manager to provide leadership and direction and shall bear the responsibility for the overall administration of the Town's organization including labour relations, risk management; budgeting; financial analysis and executing all municipal policies and bylaws set forth by Council. In addition, the manager shall provide broad policy and general guidance to department heads related to operations, fiscal and general management function; and to provide close general supervision to personnel within the administrative department.

Reporting to Council, this position is responsible for:

• Delivering a safe, respectful and welcoming workplace by providing leadership and direction for all staff, departments and divisions.

• Providing advice to Council regarding policy, governance and operational matters.

• Developing and managing annual budgets and financial plans including capital works.

• Serving as a strong liaison between Deer Lake Search and Rescue, and Deer Lake Airport Authority.

• Ensuring staff remain motivated and committed to delivering a high level of public service while overseeing human resources and staff performance.

• Ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, regulations and Town bylaws.

• Building and maintaining a positive relationship with residents, businesses, community groups and government agencies.

• Coordinating all special projects for the Town including capital infrastructure projects, management studies, new initiatives, programming and various professional services; and

• Developing a respectful relationship with Union representation of the Town's employees by overseeing negotiations and executing existing collective agreements in a fair and unbiased manner.

The Ideal candidate shall possess:

• A bachelor's degree in business administration, commerce, public administration, engineering or related field with minimum of five (5) years progressive senior managerial expertise in the public-sector

• Consideration will be given to candidates with a combination of education and experience acceptable to the Town;

• Professional, ethical with good character and integrity;

• Strong planning and economic development skills;

• Strong financial management and budgeting skills;

• Sound understanding of municipal governance, legislation and administration.

• Effective interpersonal, written and oral communication skills;

• An ability to manage a diverse team of subordinates and department heads;

• Proficient knowledge of with Microsoft Suite programs.

Hours of Work:

This is a salaried position. The incumbent will be expected to attend all scheduled council meeting (public or non-public) which regularly occur within the evening hours. In addition, the incumbent shall be in a rotation with department managers for on-call for emergency services to relieve all other departmental managers.

Salary:

Salary shall be commensurate based on experience and qualifications. A competitive benefits package shall compliment the commensurate package.

title: Senior Business Analyst – Pension Transformation
description:
## WHO WE ARE:

Mariner innovates always and everywhere, turning novel ideas into practical solutions. From products and services to venture creation, we build better futures powered by people. We partner with people embracing change, leveraging data, cybersecurity, cloud, and change management to drive successful business outcomes that matter to our customers.

Mariners build for change. Like SHIFT Energy, our energy management and decarbonization company. Or East Valley, created to scale social economic impact in our communities through investment and mentorship of emerging change-makers and their companies.

• We care about the impact we have on our community.

• We serve by solving complex problems.

• We grow because growth fuels opportunities.

• We innovate always and everywhere.

• We build a business that lasts.

## OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE:

We are seeking a Senior Business Analyst to support a complex Pension Transformation initiative on a short-term client project, with an immediate start preferred. This role will work across business, operations, finance, compliance, technology, and external vendors to bring structure and clarity to a highly complex transformation environment

The ideal candidate will bring strong senior-level transformation experience, with direct pensions experience highly preferred. Experience with pension administration, pension operations, pension platform migration/replacement, recordkeeping transformation, or pension administration outsourcing would be particularly relevant. Strong Financial Services or Insurance transformation experience may also be considered.

## WHAT YOU LL BE DOING IN THE ROLE:

• Review and clarify the existing requirements backlog, identifying gaps, duplication, inconsistencies, and unresolved decisions.

• Map and validate current-state and future-state business processes, including roles, handoffs, dependencies, controls, and process gaps.

• Facilitate working sessions with business stakeholders, SMEs, project teams, technology teams, and external vendors to clarify requirements and drive decisions.

• Translate business requirements into clear deliverables, dependencies, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, and requirements traceability.

• Support data migration, system integration, reconciliation, testing/UAT, and operational readiness activities.

• Work across business and technology teams to ensure requirements are understood, validated, and aligned throughout the transformation lifecycle.

• Identify and escalate risks, dependencies, requirement gaps, and outstanding decisions that could impact the program critical path or go-live.

• Bring structure to ambiguous or incomplete requirements and independently drive analysis through to resolution.

## WHAT SKILLS / QUALIFICATIONS YOU LL NEED TO DO THE JOB:

• Senior Business Analyst experience supporting complex transformation programs.

• Strong experience with business process mapping, requirements elicitation, requirements documentation, and stakeholder facilitation.

• Experience supporting data migration, integrations, testing/UAT, reconciliation, and requirements traceability.

• Strong preference for pensions experience, particularly within pension administration, pension operations, or pension transformation.

• Experience with pension administration outsourcing, pension platform migration/replacement, or recordkeeping transformation is highly desirable.

• Strong Financial Services or Insurance transformation experience may be considered where direct pensions experience is limited.

• Experience working within regulated or highly controlled environments.

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively across business, finance, operations, compliance, technology, and external vendor teams.

• Strong facilitation and decision-support skills, with the ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments.

• Ability to work independently, learn quickly, and bring structure and clarity to ambiguous or incomplete requirements.

## AND YOU ARE...

• Always improving your skills and knowledge: you want to be the best at what you do

• Curious and creative; comfortable taking on new problems and challenges

• A self-starter with the ability to recommend priorities to the project leader

• Comfortable working through problems and figuring things out with minimal supervision

• Great problem-solving skills: thorough and reliable

• Able to work in a team: share knowledge and assist other team members

• A good communicator: able to explain your ideas and recommendations

• Well organized and dependable under pressure: you manage your time effectively

• Energized by our company values!

## WHY MARINER?

We believe in making a positive impact in the communities where we live and work! Not only are we passionate about nurturing a thriving technology sector here in Atlantic Canada, but we are also committed to solving technology challenges that will make an impact worldwide. Technology is everlasting, and we take pride in connecting world class talent to world class projects and business solutions.

If you are an IT Professional, Software Professional, or Management Consultant, that is passionate about career development, data, and problem solving, we want to hear from you! If this sounds like someone you know, share this with them so they do not miss the opportunity to experience Mariner!

To achieve this, we know we need to be all in on training and development of our team so we can continue to move the needle in the technology sector together. Of course, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to our team, but our competitive edge is the development and training that our team experiences every day.

Be part of our vibrant community that values diversity and embraces inclusion at every level. We are committed to fostering a culture where individuals from all backgrounds and walks of life feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. Our collaborative environment celebrates the richness of ideas and experiences, and we believe that by embracing diversity, we can achieve greater innovation and excellence together. Come and help us create a workplace that reflects the beautiful tapestry of our global community.

## Join our growing team!

title: Chemical Engineer (or equivalent)

Oxford Frozen Foods Ltd, a member of the Bragg Group of Companies, is a family-owned international business that has over 1,200 employees, eight manufacturing facilities and two large farming operations within Atlantic Canada and the United States. Oxford Frozen Foods is the world's largest provider of Wild Blueberries, one of North America's largest producers of premium frozen carrots and one of Canada's premier manufacturers of onion rings and battered appetizers.

## Benefits of being an Oxford Frozen Foods Employee:

• Comprehensive benefit package including a matching contribution pension plan.

• Employee Housing Loan program provides a forgivable loan up to $40,000.

• Vacation PLUS we offer a vacation purchase plan allowing for additional time off.

• Employee Discount Program offering discounts at various businesses and industries.

We are seeking a proactive, self-directed Process Engineer to drive process optimization, cost-effectiveness, and continuous improvement across our production environments. In this hands-on role, you will evaluate internal procedures, equipment capabilities, and supplier networks to build safe, high-quality manufacturing workflows. You will lead projects from concept through launch and into full production, ensuring all systems operate with maximum efficiency and strict quality standards.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Conduct workflow and shop layout analyses to improve material handling, boost productivity, and establish accurate work standards for product costing.

• Lead Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (PFMEA) and Control Plan development with suppliers; apply Lean principles (VSM, 5S, Kanban, Poka-Yoke) across all assembly lines.

• Identify and implement process upgrades for internal lines and supplier bases, framing proposals with clear cost-benefit analyses for executive approval.

• Support Quality teams in evaluating new tiered suppliers' manufacturing capabilities, strengths, and operational risks.

• Manage project timelines, resolve complex technical issues through root cause analysis, and report status updates to cross-functional stakeholders.

## Work Environment & Physical Requirements:

• On-site in a manufacturing environment with exposure to plant operations.

• Exposure to external climate conditions.

• Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as required.

• Lifting up to 50 lbs. and standing for extended periods is required.

## Qualification & Experience:

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Mechanical Engineering or equivalent discipline).

• Professional Engineer (P.Eng. / PE) designation or EIT path preferred.

• Track record of bringing at least one project from inception through launch, followed by at least one year of ongoing production support.

• Deep expertise in Lean Manufacturing and Quality Control techniques; working knowledge of HACCP and BRC requirements.

• Strong root cause analysis skills, logical deductive reasoning, and proficiency in creating actionable project plans.

• Highly organized, tenacious problem-solver, effective communicator, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment with minimal supervision.

• Must be willing and able to travel as needed.

• Criminal Record Checks are required for successful applicants.

Oxford Frozen Foods is searching for someone who demonstrates professionalism and integrity, and who is committed to following company policies, procedures, and all applicable regulations.

The successful candidate demonstrates a strong commitment to safety, maintains organized and clean work areas, and effectively manages time in a fast-paced environment. They possess solid organizational skills, a strong sense of urgency, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team.

title: Wildlife Park Attendant (Visitor Services) (Casual Vacancies)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50063

Department: Natural Resources

Location: SHUBENACADIE

Type of Employment: Casual

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 15-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
Nova Scotia is rich in natural resources including biodiversity, forests, provincial parks, and the land we manage. The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for the development, management, conservation and protection of forest, parks and wildlife resources and the administration of Crown land. Together we are working with Nova Scotians to build a better future through sustainable natural resource management as we all benefit from the natural health and wealth of the province.

The Shubenacadie Wildlife Park is one of Nova Scotia's top tourist destinations and has attracted millions of visitors over the past 72 years. The 331-hectare park provides unique recreational and educational opportunities while showcasing native wildlife and conservation initiatives.

About Our Opportunity
Do you enjoy working with people while also supporting wildlife conservation and outdoor operations?

The Shubenacadie Wildlife Park is seeking Wildlife Park Attendants with a strong visitor experience focus. As a key member of our team, you will help create a welcoming, safe, and educational experience for visitors while supporting the day-to-day operations of the park.

Primary Accountabilities
• Welcoming visitors and providing exceptional customer service

• Processing admissions and retail transactions

• Providing information about wildlife, exhibits, programs, trails, and local attractions

• Responding to visitor inquiries and resolving customer concerns

• Supporting special events, education programs, and visitor engagement activities

• Maintaining clean, safe, and welcoming public spaces (should be specific about cleaning public washrooms.)

Secondary responsibilities may include:

• Conducting routine observations of animals and reporting concerns to Animal Care staff

• Monitoring wildlife exhibits and assisting with public safety around animal enclosures

• Performing inspections of trails, boardwalks, fences, signage, and visitor infrastructure

• Light maintenance and housekeeping of the Wildlife Station and public-use facilities

• Assisting Animal Care and Maintenance teams with operational requirements as needed

• Supporting emergency response and severe weather preparations when required

As a Wildlife Park Attendant, you will work closely with the Visitor Experience, Animal Care and Maintenance teams to deliver a positive experience for both visitors and wildlife.

Qualifications and Experience
To be considered for this opportunity, you've completed high school or have an equivalent combination of training and experience.

To be successful in this role, you should possess, confirm in your cover letter, and be prepared to demonstrate:

• Strong customer service and communication skills

• Experience handling cash and processing financial transactions

• Experience operating point-of-sale systems and basic computer software

• Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail

• Interest in wildlife, conservation, environmental education, or outdoor recreation

• Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions

• Ability to perform light physical labour including walking, lifting, cleaning, and trail inspections

• Valid Nova Scotia Class 5 Driver's License or equivalent

The following will be considered assets:

• Visitor services, tourism, retail, hospitality, admissions, or recreation experience

• Experience working in parks, zoos, museums, aquariums, nature centres, or similar attractions

• Knowledge of Nova Scotia wildlife and conservation issues

• Experience conducting facility inspections or maintenance activities

• First Aid/CPR certification

• Knowledge of Occupational Health and Safety and WHMIS requirements

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Working Conditions
• Work is performed both indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.

• Shifts may include weekends, holidays, evenings, and special events.

• Frequent interaction with visitors during periods of high attendance.

• Significant walking throughout the park and trail systems is required.

• Routine inspections of trails, exhibits, and visitor facilities are required.

• The ability to adapt quickly to changing operational priorities is essential.

• Staff may be required to support emergency operations, weather events, or visitor incidents.

Additional Information
This is a Wildlife Park Attendant position with a primary focus on visitor services and park operations. Successful candidates will receive training related to visitor services, wildlife observation and reporting, public safety, and facility inspections.

This competition is being leveraged to fill 2 casual hourly vacancies.

What We Offer
• Meaningful work contributing to one of Nova Scotia's premier wildlife and tourism destinations.

• Opportunities to gain experience in visitor services, wildlife conservation, and outdoor recreation.

• A supportive and collaborative team environment.

• Valuable experience within the Provincial Government.

• Opportunities for future permanent, seasonal, term, temporary, and casual employment.

title: Marketing and Events Coordinator
employer: Chartered Professionals in Human Resources New Brunswick
description:
Marketing and Events Coordinator

Full-Time / Remote

Based in New Brunswick with Travel Requirements

Salary: $55,000-$62,000 Annually Based on Experience, Qualifications and Skills

CPHR New Brunswick is seeking a Marketing and Events Coordinator to help grow our reach, strengthen relationships with members and partners, and create experiences that bring New Brunswick's HR and business communities together. This role brings together marketing strategy, sponsorship development and hands-on event delivery. The coordinator will have the independence to lead projects from planning through execution while working closely with colleagues, volunteers and partners. This role will suit someone who enjoys meeting people, building relationships and bringing energy to in-person events. While much of the planning and marketing work happens remotely, the coordinator will regularly connect with members, sponsors and partners and be on-site to deliver events throughout New Brunswick.

## What We offer

Flexibility is one of the things we value most. We offer remote work and flexibility in organizing the workday, with the trust to manage responsibilities while making room for life outside work. Events and meetings require availability at set times, but outside those commitments, there is room to establish a working rhythm that supports both professional responsibilities and personal life.

Our small, collaborative team provides an environment where everyone has a voice. The coordinator will have ownership of their portfolio and the independence to lead it, with colleagues who share ideas, offer support and figure things out together. We also offer a competitive compensation package and benefits that support employee well-being. As CPHR New Brunswick grows, the coordinator will have opportunities to shape the role and see the impact of their work on our members and workplaces across the province.

## Responsibilities

• The coordinator will develop and lead a marketing strategy that identifies key audiences, sets clear priorities and supports CPHR New Brunswick's goals. This includes creating campaigns for membership, professional development, partnerships and events, and coordinating content in English and French across email, social media, the website and other channels.

• The role includes establishing and managing marketing KPIs, tracking progress and using findings to guide decisions.

• Business development is an important part of this position. The coordinator will proactively identify and pursue new sponsorship opportunities while also growing relationships and opportunities with existing partners. This includes identifying prospective sponsors, conducting outreach, developing proposals, securing commitments and cultivating strong, long-term partner relationships.

• Throughout the year, the coordinator will plan and deliver multiple events, managing everything from budgets and suppliers to promotion and the on-site experience, while building connections across New Brunswick's HR and business communities.

## Qualifications & Skills required

• Experience developing and implementing successful marketing strategies that support organizational business goals.

• Experience creating content for and managing organizational social media accounts, including planning, publishing, community engagement and performance tracking.

• Demonstrated success proactively securing new sales, sponsorships or comparable partnerships, as well as growing existing partner relationships.

• Experience planning and delivering events, including managing competing priorities and responding to changes on event day.

• Advanced written and spoken communication skills in both English and French. These skills will be assessed during the selection process.

• Strong organizational skills and the ability to make decisions and move work forward independently.

• A collaborative approach and demonstrated ability to build strong professional relationships.

Applicants whose experience has provided the skills to succeed in this role are encouraged to apply.

## Location, Travel and Work Authorization

This is a remote position based in New Brunswick, with regular travel throughout the province and occasional travel outside New Brunswick. Occasional evening and weekend work is required to support events, with scheduling adjusted accordingly. The coordinator will need to be available to attend and deliver events as planned. Reasonable work-related travel expenses will be reimbursed in accordance with CPHR New Brunswick's travel and expense policy.

The ability to travel throughout New Brunswick, including to locations that may not be accessible by public transportation, is required. The role requires the ability to carry out the physical requirements associated with event setup and teardown, with accommodation where required. This includes transporting and carrying marketing materials to and from events, lifting, bending and assembling pop-up marketing displays and other event materials.

The successful candidate must be legally authorized to work in Canada and reside in New Brunswick by the start date of the role. CPHR New Brunswick is unable to provide immigration sponsorship for this position.

## How to Apply

Please submit a résumé to tina@cphrnb.ca by October 15, 2026.

CPHR New Brunswick welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds and identities and is committed to an accessible and inclusive hiring process. Accommodations are available at any stage of recruitment. Applicants are encouraged to let us know what would support their participation.

title: Electrical Drafting Technologist
description:
At CBCL Limited, we are a successful, dynamic, and growing engineering and environmental consulting firm. As a leader in renewable energy integration in the Atlantic region, we have many exciting projects forecasted in the coming years. With the growth of our service offerings, we are seeking enthusiastic individuals who want to contribute to the expansion of clean energy and the resulting positive impact on our environment.

We currently have an exciting opportunity for an Electrical Drafting Technologist to join our Electrical Utilities & Renewables design team in our Halifax, Nova Scotia office. Bring your passion and skills to a collaborative team that thrives on delivering innovative solutions for our clients in the electrical utilities and renewable energy sectors. You'll play a pivotal role in advancing clean energy initiatives that power our communities and contribute to a more sustainable future.

All experience levels are encouraged to apply! Whether you're just starting your career or you're a seasoned professional, this is an opportunity to be part of exciting projects and grow alongside a team of skilled engineers and technologists dedicated to making a positive impact.

Your Key Responsibilities:

• Contribute to the Future of Clean Energy: Contribute to the drafting design of electrical systems, including power transmission and distribution, substation layouts, protection and control systems, and SCADA systems;

• Craft with Precision: Perform accurate and detailed drafting work, including drawings, specifications, and technical documentation using AutoCAD and Revit for both 2D drafting and 3D modelling;

• Collaborate and Innovate: Work with senior engineers and multidisciplinary teams to refine design concepts, perform engineering calculations, and ensure project specifications meet client needs and regulatory standards;

• Support Project Success: Prepare technical reports and tender documents.

Your Capabilities and Credentials:

• Educational Background: A diploma in Electrical Engineering Technology is preferred. Candidates with diplomas in CAD-related fields such as Civil or Structural Engineering Technology, Architectural Engineering Technology, Architectural Drafting, or similar programs will also be considered;

• Experience: 2 to 5 years of relevant experience in electrical CAD drafting is preferred, but we are open to candidates with less experience who are eager to learn and grow;

• Technical Expertise: Proficiency in AutoCAD/Civil3D, MicroStation, and Revit, as well as 3D component modelling software with ability to create and edit electrical designs and equipment;

• Team Player: A collaborative mindset to work effectively within a team environment; and

• Organized and Detail-Oriented: Ability to multi-task, manage time effectively, and pay attention to detail through the coordination of complex design packages.

What will Make You Stand Out:

• Previous experience in a consulting engineering environment is highly desirable;

• Certification as a Certified Engineering Technologist (CET) or the ability to become registered is preferred;

• Experience with Autodesk Revit, AGI32 lighting simulation software, and SKM Power*Tools or other electrical simulation software is a plus; and

• Past use of Bluebeam Revu for collaboration and review of drawings is beneficial;

• Experience in graphic design with ability to generate aesthetic drawings is considered a strong asset.

You are welcome to apply even if you do not meet all of the requirements.

What we can offer you:

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• CAAT Defined Benefit Pension Plan with employer contributions

• Generous vacation allowance commensurate with experience

• Maternity or Parental leave top-up

• Health spending account

• Wellness incentive

• Membership dues reimbursement

• Education and lifelong learning subsidization

• Community volunteering incentive

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Public transit subsidy

In addition to the above benefits, we offer:

• Flexible hours and locations to support work/life balance, including hybrid solutions;

• Ability to work paid overtime and bank time-in-lieu for future use;

• Diverse team with a wide range of experience and expertise;

• Exposure to a variety of projects;

• Support to develop skills and pursue projects related to your own interests;

• Collaboration between multiple disciplines and levels of expertise;

• Mentoring opportunities to foster your personal and professional development;

• Accessible and central offices in Atlantic Canada and Ottawa; and

• Access to training opportunities in areas ranging from technical development to leadership skills.

• CBCL is employee-owned, with ownership opportunities available to eligible staff.

About Us

At CBCL our purpose is to create a positive and lasting impact on people and our planet. As an employee-owned firm, at CBCL, our people are everything. We are committed to promoting inclusivity and diversity for a workplace where everyone can thrive, and we build long-term relationships with our clients while providing them with innovative solutions.

We have earned recognition as one of Canada's Top 100 Employers and one of Canada's Best Managed Companies. Our multitalented group of professionals offer consulting in the Infrastructure, Water and Wastewater, Buildings, Industrial, and Earth and Environment sectors. We value our people, our communities, and our history and look forward to continuing our steady growth.

Along with our commitment to reducing our carbon footprint corporately, CBCL develops and implements sustainable engineering solutions that respect the current social and environmental impacts, as well as future implications of our designs.

CBCL operates from its offices in Halifax and Sydney, NS; Charlottetown, PE; Saint John, Fredericton and Moncton, NB; St. John's, NL, and Ottawa, ON.

CBCL Limited strives to provide a diverse workplace that is inclusive, accessible and celebrates individuals and what makes us unique. We are proud to be an employer partner with the Canadian Centre for Diversity and Inclusion and Pride at Work.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace for all. If you require accommodations at any stage of the recruitment or interview process, or while working with us, please email hr@cbcl.ca. We will work with you to meet your needs in a respectful and timely manner.

Our goal is to ensure every candidate has a fair opportunity to demonstrate their abilities. We value diverse perspectives and are dedicated to removing barriers that may prevent individuals from thriving in their roles.

title: Draftsperson
description:
Located in Oxford, NS

Application Deadline: October 28, 2026

Oxford Frozen Foods Ltd, a member of the Bragg Group of Companies, is a family-owned international business that has over 1,200 employees, eight manufacturing facilities and two large farming operations within Atlantic Canada and the United States. Oxford Frozen Foods is the world's largest provider of Wild Blueberries, one of North America's largest producers of premium frozen carrots and one of Canada's premier manufacturers of onion rings and battered appetizers.

## Benefits of being an Oxford Frozen Foods Employee:

• Comprehensive benefit package including a matching contribution pension plan.

• Employee Housing Loan program provides a forgivable loan up to $40,000.

• Vacation PLUS we offer a vacation purchase plan allowing for additional time off.

• Employee Discount Program offering discounts at various businesses and industries.

## Position Scope:

We are seeking a detail-oriented Draftsperson to transform design concepts, rough sketches, and engineering specifications into precise technical drawings and schematics. Working closely with the engineers, you will ensure every plan is accurate, clear, and compliant with relevant industry standards and building codes.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Prepare detailed 2D layouts and 3D models using software such as AutoCAD, Revit, or SolidWorks.

• Coordinate with design leads, engineers, and project managers to resolve design ambiguities, clarify tolerances, and specify material requirements.

• Modify existing drawings based on engineering change orders, site measurements, or feedback.

• Verify that all drawings comply with company formatting protocols, safety requirements, and local regulations.

• Organize and archive digital drawing files, project logs, and revision histories for internal and external team access.

## Work Environment & Physical Requirements:

• On-site in a manufacturing environment with exposure to plant operations.

• Exposure to external climate conditions.

• Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as required.

## Qualification & Experience:

• Associate degree, diploma, or technical certification in Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Drafting Technology, or a related discipline.

• Demonstrated proficiency with standard CAD software (e.g., AutoCAD, Revit, Inventor, or SolidWorks).

title: (Senior Financial Analyst) Program Admin Officer 3
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50000

Department: Finance and Treasury Board

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 15-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Nova Scotia Department of Finance and Treasury Board, we provide financial leadership, analysis, and policy support that helps strengthen Nova Scotia. As stewards of the province's financial affairs, we deliver a broad range of corporate fiscal and management services.

Our eight Financial Advisory Services (FAS) units work directly with departments, Crown corporations, and other public service entities, providing support in budgeting, forecasting, and program-related financial advice. We are continuously seeking new and innovative ways to improve how we plan, manage, budget, and invest.

About Our Opportunity
As the Program Administration Officer 3 (Senior Financial Analyst), you provide specialized financial expertise and strategic advice to senior management and program areas. You will play a key role in supporting the financial management and delivery of government programs and funded external agencies, while contributing to sound decision-making, financial oversight, and the evaluation of new and existing initiatives.

This competition may be used to fill multiple Permanent, Term, Temporary and Casual Senior Financial Analyst opportunities over the next several months.

Primary Accountabilities
Some of the primary accountabilities of the role will include:

• Provide specialized financial advice and analysis to support the administration, delivery, and oversight of government programs and funded external agencies.

• Prepare and analyze financial information related to budgets, forecasts, agreements, contracts, program costing, payment disbursements, and exception reporting.

• Interpret and apply financial and program policies, guidelines, and legislation, while monitoring financial accountability, audit requirements, and risk management processes.

• Contribute to annual budget development, business planning, and Estimates support materials, and assess the fiscal impacts of program and budget initiatives.

• Support accurate and timely month-end and year-end processes, including financial statements, audit files, and the reconciliation of recovery claims for cost-shared programs and capital projects.

• Analyze financial trends and program data, identify opportunities for process and systems improvements, and build strong working relationships with clients, partners, and service providers.

Qualifications and Experience
This may be the right opportunity for you if you have a bachelor's degree plus 5 years of related experience; or an equivalent combination of training and experience. You also possess knowledge of Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS) and other relevant CPA Canada standards and requirements.

You have experience providing financial analysis, advice, and support in a complex program, public sector, or government environment. You are comfortable interpreting and applying financial policies, guidelines, agreements, and legislation, and have experience preparing or reviewing budgets, forecasts, financial reports, and supporting analysis to inform decision-making. You bring strong analytical, organizational, communication, and relationship-building skills, along with the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and respond effectively to complex stakeholder issues.

Experience supporting month-end or year-end processes, audit activities, recovery claims, contract or agreement administration, and financial systems or reporting improvements will be considered assets. Experience supervising staff, or providing guidance and support to junior team members, is also considered an asset.

While not required, the following would be considered assets:

• A Canadian CPA accounting designation or enrolment in a recognized CPA accounting program

• Knowledge and experience using SAP/S4HANA or a similar ERP system

• Knowledge and experience in the delivery of a broad spectrum of financial services to a varied client group

• Knowledge and experience in the performance of auditing procedures

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
This is an excellent career opportunity for many, and we do consider an equivalent combination of training, education, and experience. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Your normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day. You may be required to work overtime on occasion.

The majority of your work is conducted in a comfortable office environment.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

• A dynamic, client-focused office environment where service excellence and teamwork are our focus

Pay Grade: PR 13

Salary Range: $2,805.63 - $3,410.48 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. EMP makes a difference in the lives of those it serves by drastically reducing hospital admissions and greatly increasing patient satisfaction with its level of health care.

To holistically coordinate the care of each patient, incorporating the nursing profession's values of knowledge, theory and practice. • Diploma in Nursing or a Bachelor's Degree in Nursing;

• Currently registered and in good standing, or eligible for registration, with the College of Nursing of New Brunswick (CNNB);

• A good driving record with a valid New Brunswick Class 5 Driver's License;

• Have a current CPR Level C certification or be prepared to obtain within 3 months;

• Support student placement initiatives;

• Able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record;

• A high regard for confidentiality; and

About Us
Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services (NL Health Services) integrates five former health entities into a unified provincial authority. This transformation follows recommendations from Health Accord NL to improve healthcare delivery for the province’s 510,550 residents. NL Health Services employs over 22,000 people, delivering care across the continuum and embracing senior-friendly care as a foundational approach to meet the unique needs of older adults.

The Senior-Friendly Manager - Acute is a transformational leadership position focused on advancing care for older adults within their zone. Reporting to the Director of X in collaboration with the Strategic Health Network- Health of Older Adults, this role is responsible for leading the integration of senior-friendly care practices and implementing evidence-based initiatives such as Acute Care of the Elderly, Senior-Friendly Emergency Departments, and Senior-Friendly Hospitals to support the establishment of Centres of Excellence in Aging in line with recommendations from Health Accord NL and the vision of the Strategic Health Network for Health of Older Adults.

A key aspect of this role is the establishment and leadership of zone-based working groups to operationalize senior-friendly care priorities. By bringing together key stakeholders and partners, the manager will ensure the effective implementation of initiatives that improve outcomes for older adults. This will require networking and partnering with various programs across the continuum of care including but not limited to: Medicine, Surgery, Emergency Services, Rehabilitation, Primary Health Care, Community Supports, Professional Practice, Clinical Efficiency, Quality, Research and Innovation, Digital Health, as well as various health system partners to advance senior-friendly initiatives.

Additionally, the Senior-Friendly Manager - Acute will lead and/or participate in provincial working groups and contribute insights from their zone to inform provincial strategies and align local efforts with broader system-wide improvements. They will also need to work in close partnership with the Senior-Friendly Manager- Community to support seamless care delivery across the continuum of care for older adults.

The Senior-Friendly Manager - Acute oversees the planning, implementation, and evaluation of senior-friendly care initiatives within their zone. This includes collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to develop standardized care pathways, enhance patient flow, and ensure smooth transitions between acute care and community-based services, long-term care, and personal care homes. As a change management expert, the manager will design and implement strategies to engage stakeholders, mitigate risks, and foster the seamless integration of evidence-based practices. This role also involves developing education materials and providing coaching/ mentoring support to staff to build capacity for delivering high-quality, senior-friendly care.

Resource planning and budgeting are integral to the position. The manager will identify resource requirements, prepare budget submissions, and support recruitment and retention for senior-friendly initiatives/ programs. The manager will also supervise/ manage staff to ensure effective operation and outcomes. They will establish performance indicators and lead the collection, analysis, and reporting of data to evaluate the effectiveness of these initiatives. Insights from these evaluations will be shared with the SHN- Health of Older Adults and provincial leadership to guide decision-making and ensure alignment with provincial priorities. Responsibilities of this position may also include developing and delivering presentations for relevant audiences which may include executive, leadership, providers, and/or patients and families.

By driving innovation, fostering collaboration, and advancing evidence-based practices, the Senior-Friendly Manager - Acute will play a pivotal role in transforming care for older adults and ensuring their zone contributes meaningfully to the provincial vision for Centres of Excellence in Aging and enhanced care delivery for older adults in Newfoundland and Labrador.

Job Qualifications
Education
A baccalaureate degree in a health-related discipline or social sciences is required.
A master's degree is preferred.
Education and training in project management, change management, and quality improvement is an asset.

Experience
A minimum of three years' experience with older adults in acute care required.
Experience in project management and change management.
Experience with quality improvement and/or process improvement.
Previous leadership experience is an asset.
Recent management experience is an asset.

Competencies (Knowledge, Skills & Abilities)
You demonstrate knowledge of the breadth and complexity of the care of older adults during hospitalization. To have good understanding of quality improvement principles, resource/capacity management, and pathway planning.

You possess a dynamic leadership style focused on:
• Leading yourself by having self-awareness, managing your performance and health, developing yourself, and demonstrating character that is in line with NLHS’s values of respect, integrity, fairness, organizational connectedness and excellence;
• Engaging others through fostering development of others, contributing to the creation of a healthy organization, communicating effectively, and building effective teams;
• Achieving results by setting direction, strategically aligning decisions with vision, values, and evidence, taking action to implement decisions, and assessing and evaluating outcomes;
• Developing coalitions through purposefully building partnerships and networks to create results, demonstrating a commitment to customers and service, mobilizing knowledge, and navigating socio-political environments;
• Transforming systems by thinking analytically and critically and questioning and challenging the status quo, encouraging and supporting innovation, orienting yourself strategically to the future, and championing and orchestrating change.

Other
Current registration with a professional association is required.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

Please submit your resume/cover letter, clearly demonstrating how you meet the required qualifications.

Job Summary
The Laboratory Assistant performs a variety of duties associated with laboratory tests and analyses. Work can involve collecting blood and other specimens from patients; delivering specimens to the laboratory; sorting, recording, centrifuging and preparing specimens for analysis; packaging specimens for transport to other testing locations; receiving testing results; and performing a variety of routine, automated and manual tests.

Phlebotomists are an integral part of our healthcare team and are responsible for the collection of specimens for laboratory analysis. Phlebotomists are responsible for collecting blood from patients through venipuncture, instructing patients on proper collection techniques of urine and other specialized samples, properly labelling specimens, and other general duties as required.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that the regular physical and psychological demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Occasionally lifts or moves supplies generally not weighing in excess of 25 lbs. and occasional carrying, pushing/pulling and lifting between 25-50 lbs.
Constantly stands, walks and bends or stretches into awkward positions when performing specimen collection procedures with patients.
Constantly there is a requirement for fine finger and precision work when using needles to extract specimens, and when palpating for veins, when entering data into the computer, and preparing specimen labels.

Laboratory Assistant
- Graduation from a recognized program in Phlebotomy or Medical Laboratory Assistant is required.
- Training or experience in basic laboratory techniques.
- Successful completion of the Medical Laboratory Assistant national examination as recognized in Canada is required.

Customer Service Specialist

You'll answer questions, solve problems, and help customers find products and services that fit their needs. No two calls are the same, so every day brings something different.

What You'll Be Doing

As a Customer Service Specialist, you'll support customers through inbound calls while balancing exceptional service with sales opportunities. In this role, you'll:

• Answer customer questions about accounts, billing, products, and services

• Take the time to understand customer needs and recommend the right solutions

We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. • Opportunities for internal growth and promotion

• Paid vacation and holidays

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• Pension plan

We are committed to building a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We embrace diversity, inclusion, equity, and accessibility throughout all levels of the organization and encourage members of equity groups to self-identify during the application process.

title: Office Manager, Payroll & Accounting
description:
Office Manager, Payroll & Accounting
Location: Edwardsville, Nova Scotia
Work Arrangement: In person
Position: Full-time, permanent
Salary: $58,000 to $65,000, depending on experience
Reports to: Director of Finance

## The Opportunity

Cape Breton Beverages and Trans-Atlantic Preforms are seeking a careful, dependable and highly organized Office Manager, Payroll & Accounting. This is a role for someone who takes their work seriously and takes pride in getting the details right. You will be responsible for payroll, benefits and pension administration, core accounting processes and day-to-day office administration for both companies. You will also lead a small, established team, currently made up of four administrative support staff.

The role also supports our sister companies, Nova Scotia Spirit Co./Blue Lobster and Annapolis Cider Company, with a second review of payments and transfers, banking and cash management support, and backup coverage when needed. The work follows a well-defined cycle with firm deadlines: regular payroll runs, month-end and year-end accounting, and scheduled government remittances.

Reporting to the Director of Finance, you will have clear responsibilities, clear lines of approval and the support you need to do the work accurately and well. You will be the trusted point of contact for employees and managers on payroll, benefit and pension questions. You will also work with our external accountants, auditors, financial institutions and benefit providers.

## What You'll Do

## Payroll, Benefits & Pension

• Process payroll accurately and on schedule for employees across both companies.

• Maintain payroll records and process changes related to compensation, deductions, vacation and other payroll matters.

• Prepare payroll reconciliations, source deduction remittances and related reporting.

• Prepare and issue Records of Employment.

• Administer employee benefit and pension plans, including enrolments, changes, terminations and contributions.

• Work directly with benefit and pension providers to resolve issues and ensure accurate administration.

• Answer employee questions on payroll, benefits and pension clearly and accurately.

• Maintain accurate and confidential employee records.

## Accounting & Financial Administration

• Complete assigned month-end accounting processes and procedures.

• Prepare and post recurring and other required journal entries.

• Assist with general ledger reconciliations and account analysis.

• Prepare and submit HST returns and other required government remittances.

• Oversee accounts payable and support other accounting functions as required.

• Prepare financial and administrative reports for management.

• Maintain complete and accurate accounting records and supporting documentation.

## Banking & Cash Management

• Oversee company deposits and day-to-day banking activities.

• Review and process EFT transactions, with final approval by finance leadership, in accordance with company procedures.

• Support banking administration and correspondence.

• Ensure banking transactions and records are accurately maintained and reconciled.

• Provide a second review of payments and transfers for Nova Scotia Spirit Co./Blue Lobster and Annapolis Cider Company before they are released, in accordance with company procedures.

• Support the Director of Finance with banking and cash management for Nova Scotia Spirit Co./Blue Lobster and Annapolis Cider Company, including tracking balances and preparing banking information and reports.

## Year-End & Audit

• Support and coordinate the annual year-end accounting and financial reporting process.

• Prepare year-end schedules, reconciliations and supporting documentation.

• Work closely with the Director of Finance and external accountants and auditors to provide required information.

• Respond to audit requests and assist in resolving issues identified through the year-end process.

• Support other financial reporting and compliance requirements as needed.

## Team & Office Administration

• Lead a team (currently comprised of four administrative support staff) by example, as the technical expert in payroll and administration, providing clear direction, training and regular feedback.

• Make sure the team's work is completed accurately, on schedule and in line with company procedures.

• Provide administrative support to managers and employees on payroll, benefits and other employment-related matters.

• Coordinate day-to-day administrative requirements and maintain organized company records.

• Keep accounting and administrative procedures documented and up to date, and recommend improvements.

• Assist the Director of Finance with defined projects as needed.

• Provide backup coverage for payroll, accounting and administrative functions at Nova Scotia Spirit Co./Blue Lobster and Annapolis Cider Company when needed, as assigned by the Director of Finance.

## What You Bring

We are looking for someone who is thorough, disciplined and reliable, with strong knowledge of payroll and accounting and a commitment to doing things properly. The ideal candidate will have:

• At least 5 years of relevant experience in payroll, accounting, financial administration or a combination of these areas.

• Hands-on payroll processing experience, with a sound understanding of payroll rules and remittance requirements.

• Experience supervising or leading a small team.

• Experience with month-end accounting processes, reconciliations and financial reporting.

• Experience preparing government remittances, including payroll source deductions and HST.

• Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.

• A methodical, organized approach, with the ability to plan work around recurring deadlines.

• Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

• Respect for procedures, controls and confidentiality, and sound judgment about when to ask a question or raise a concern.

• A professional, respectful and factual manner with employees and colleagues.

• The confidence to follow up, uphold standards and see that procedures are followed.

• The ability to work independently within clear guidelines.

Experience with Sage 300 and Paymate is considered an asset. Post-secondary education in accounting, business administration, payroll or a related field is also considered an asset.

## Confidentiality

This position requires signing a confidentiality agreement, and the successful candidate will be subject to a criminal background check. You will have access to financial information, payroll and compensation details, and sensitive personnel and business matters. In a community where many of our employees are neighbours, discretion is not a formality. It is the foundation of the role.

## Why Cape Breton Beverages and Trans-Atlantic Preforms?

• Stability. Cape Breton Beverages has operated in Cape Breton for 77 years under multiple generations of the same family, and Trans-Atlantic Preforms has been manufacturing for more than 35 years.

• Clarity. Clearly defined tasks, duties and reporting relationships, with established procedures and approval processes.

• A professional work environment. We take quality and accuracy seriously, in our products and in how we run our business.

• Accountability. You will be accountable for accurate payroll, records and administration for both companies, with ownership of your area of expertise.

• Training and support. A structured handover, thorough training on our systems and a Director of Finance who is available for direction.

• A consistent schedule. In-person work at our Edwardsville office.

• Compensation. A salary of $58,000 to $65,000, depending on experience, plus health and dental benefits, and pension.

• A long-term home. A role you can grow in as the companies grow, with a team that has deep roots in Cape Breton and a genuine commitment to its employees, customers and community.

## About Us

We are a group of four Nova Scotia companies with a shared ambition: from Nova Scotia to the world. Cape Breton Beverages has been bottling Pepsi products in Cape Breton for 77 years, across multiple generations of the same family. Trans-Atlantic Preforms has manufactured PET preforms for customers across Canada and internationally for more than 35 years. Nova Scotia Spirit Co. produces Blue Lobster spirits and ready-to-drink beverages, now expanding distribution nationally. Annapolis Cider Company is an award-winning craft cidery in the Annapolis Valley, recognized internationally for its cider. Together we employ more than 170 people across the province. We are growing, and we are building the systems and leadership infrastructure to support our next stage of growth.

This position is based with Cape Breton Beverages and Trans-Atlantic Preforms, with defined banking, payment review and backup support responsibilities for Nova Scotia Spirit Co./Blue Lobster and Annapolis Cider Company. At Cape Breton Beverages, we locally produce Pepsi, 7-Up, Schweppes, and Crush soft-drink products and distribute a wide range of other beverages across Cape Breton Island. Cape Breton Beverages also provides Full Service Beverage and Snack vending throughout Cape Breton Island through its subsidiary Downeast Vending.

All of our companies are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture and share the same core values: quality and reliability in everything we produce, disciplined execution, long-term relationships with customers and partners, continuous improvement, and a strong sense of responsibility to our employees and communities. When you work at Cape Breton Beverages and Trans-Atlantic Preforms, you are part of a team that helps make this Island a better place to live through our active support of fundraisers, community organizations and special events in Cape Breton.

## How to Apply

Please submit your resume and cover letter through CareerBeacon. Applications will be reviewed as they are received and this posting will close once the position is filled, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We thank all applicants for their interest; only those selected for the next round, Predictive Index assessments, will be contacted.

Cape Breton Beverages and Trans-Atlantic Preforms are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcome applications from qualified candidates of all backgrounds.

title: Development Officer
description:
Employment Opportunity: Development Officer - a full-time (35 hours per week) one-year contract position (renewable) | Subject to a probationary period.

Established in 1789, the University of King's College is Canada's oldest chartered university and is associated with Dalhousie University. A small and extraordinarily lively academic community located in Halifax (Kjipuktuk), Nova Scotia, King's is known nationally and internationally for its interdisciplinary programs in the humanities, including its first-year Foundation Year Program, its professional programs in journalism and its fine arts programs in creative writing. King's is a community in which students, faculty, alumni, and staff work to bring greater understanding, creativity, and compassion to the world.

King's owns a unique niche in Canadian higher education. It is the university for thinkers and creators who are lovers of ideas, books, writing, scholarly conversations, the fine arts and learning in community. It is a university that aims to open doors to the transformative education it provides to students from all backgrounds and communities by opening itself to being transformed by what inclusivity brings to the college. It is an exciting time in the University's history, with a high-profile capital project in its infancy, a new president to be formally installed in October, and a college wide effort underway to review, rejuvenate and reinvest in our outstanding academic programs. This timing creates an exceptional opportunity for the successful candidate to join a collaborative, service-oriented team in the King's Advancement Office.

The University's Office of Advancement is responsible for fundraising, communications and alumni impact and engagement activities. Advancement professionals cultivate relationships with alumni, parents and friends and work with them to help them achieve their philanthropic goals, which support student success, academic excellence, and have community impact.

The King's Advancement Office accomplishes a lot with a very small team. The Development Officer position, which is the first designated position of its kind at King's, is designed to increase fundraising revenue for King's priorities, helping to positively position the University within the broader community and, along with Advancement colleagues, to foster an environment that encourages and enables donor engagement, volunteerism and financial support.

Reporting to the Director of Advancement, the Development Officer is responsible for helping to implement the University's Three-Year Fundraising Strategy. The position is aimed at attracting mid-level gifts ($10-50k) through individual donor giving. Using Advancement's database and research tools, the Development Officer is responsible for relationship management through identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of a portfolio of donor prospects. From time to time, the Development Officer may also play a role in assisting the office with its requests to foundations.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Work with the Director (and others) to increase mid-range gifts in support of the University's priorities.

• Work with the Director (and others) to become familiar with and comfortable conversing about the University's needs and aspirations.

• Help to prepare compelling funding proposals and align projects and budgets with philanthropic interests.

• Manage a portfolio of suspects, prospects and donors, advancing their relationship and engagement with King's through personalized strategies, reporting, and acknowledgement activities.

• Track fundraising activities and track proposals, manage related budgets, and balance competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Provide fundraising leadership by briefing and collaborating with Advancement colleagues and their key stakeholders.

## Additional Responsibilities:

• When needed, possible, and presumed beneficial, research foundation priorities, help to prepare compelling funding proposals and align projects and budgets with philanthropic interests.

This position involves local travel, travel throughout the Maritimes and Ontario, and less frequently potential travel elsewhere in Canada for donor meetings. It may also require attendance at some evening events. The successful candidate must hold a current driver's license and be legally allowed to drive in Canada (need not own a vehicle).

## Required Qualifications:

• Undergraduate degree or diploma preferably in Fundraising or Non-Profit Management, Marketing, Communications, English, Journalism, or a humanities-focused area of study. CFRE designation will be considered an asset.

• Minimum five years' experience in fundraising or other relationship-intensive work (or an equivalent combination of training and experience).

• Demonstrated experience of leading small-scale projects.

• Ability to handle confidential matters with a high level of integrity.

• Demonstrated experience developing and writing both summary and comprehensive funding proposals, including positioning projects and budgets, to highlight the strongest possible alignment between a project's impact and an individual donor's philanthropic interests. Similar experience with developing and writing summary and comprehensive project management documents will also be considered.

• Experience with fund development software or similar customer relationship management software. Experience with Raiser's Edge will be considered an asset.

## Closing Date: October 15, 2026

Salary will be commensurate with level of education and experience. The salary range for this position is: $60,762 -$68,595 including a benefits plan with medical, dental and travel.
