6350 Coburg Road
Halifax, Nova Scotia B3H 2A1
pethrona.russell@ukings.ca

Are you seeking meaningful work in a fast-paced environment? Do you have a passion for health and wellness? Do others come to you for guidance and support? Are you looking for a career that directly impacts your community region?

If yes, apply for this Live Well | Bien Vivre Health Coach position with the Heart and Stroke Foundation of New Brunswick and help our mission to Promote Health, Save Lives and Enhance Recovery.

## Job Overview:

The Heart & Stroke Foundation of New Brunswick is seeking a Health Coach to work with our Live Well | Bien Vivre (LW|BV) program in the Miramichi region of the province. The Live Well | Bien Vivre Program (LW|BV) is an exciting partnership between the Heart and Stroke Foundation of New Brunswick and the Government of New Brunswick. This unique initiative utilizes a community-based approach to support the prevention and management of chronic disease. As a health coach, you will have the opportunity to work with clients to support individual wellness with a focus on active living, healthy eating, mental fitness, and tobacco-free living.

The health coach works as a non-clinical professional who uses a combination of health promotion techniques, individualized guidance, and community resources to enhance the quality of life for their clients. The health coach motivates and supports individual health and wellness goals while building confidence and promoting positive healthy behavior change.

## Health Coach role includes:

• Providing personalized coaching to participants of the Live Well | Bien Vivre program to help identify and achieve client's health and wellness goals.

• Utilizing behavior change strategies to assist clients to set actionable goals and develop a personal health plan; encourage and motivate lifestyle change; navigate to local resources; and ongoing review of clients' progress to help achieve goals.

• Building relationships and expanding networks with stakeholders, partners, and organizations to enhance community connections and to increase program participation.

• Providing verbal and written reports as required to management, including expenses.

• Promoting and maintaining the vision, mission, and policies of the Heart and Stroke Foundation of New Brunswick and the people it serves and supports.

## Candidates should possess the following:

## Education

• Post-secondary education in health or wellness, kinesiology, social sciences, adult education, community development, and/or 3+ years experience in a related field.

## Ideal Qualifications

• Experience in working with health-related or non-profit groups.

• Experience in working with individuals, working within teams, and engaging groups.

• Qualifications in areas such as nutrition, mental wellness, coaching and/or health behaviours would be an asset.

• Fluent in spoken & written English is required, and fluency in French is an asset.

• Practical knowledge of MS Office Suite, email, Facebook, Google Suite, etc.

title: Site Superintendent
description:
At Acadian Construction, we don't just build projects. We build relationships, strengthen communities, and create spaces that leave a lasting impact across Atlantic Canada.

We're looking for a Site Superintendent in the Halifax Regional Municipality (HRM) who's ready for more than just managing a construction site. This is an opportunity for someone who wants to lead meaningful commercial projects, work alongside experienced construction professionals, and be part of a growing company where leadership, accountability, and teamwork matter.

Qualifications
• Minimum 5 years of experience in commercial construction site supervision.

• Must be based in or near the Halifax Regional Municipality (HRM) and willing to travel throughout the Maritimes as required.

• Strong understanding of commercial construction processes, scheduling, and subcontractor coordination.

• Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications.

• Strong organizational and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong communication and relationship-building abilities.

• Experience with Microsoft Office Suite and construction reporting tools.

• Experience with Procore is considered an asset.

Responsibilities

## What You'll Do:

As a Site Superintendent, you'll oversee daily site operations from project start-up through closeout while working closely with Project Managers, clients, consultants, subcontractors, and field teams.

## You'll be trusted to:

• Lead and coordinate all on-site construction activities.

• Manage subcontractors, site crews, schedules, and daily workflow.

• Maintain project quality, safety, and productivity standards.

• Review project drawings, specifications, and schedules to ensure work is executed correctly.

• Identify and resolve on-site issues proactively to keep projects moving forward.

• Conduct site inspections and ensure compliance with safety requirements and company standards.

• Coordinate material deliveries, equipment, and site logistics.

• Communicate regularly with Project Managers regarding progress, risks, and site updates.

• Build strong working relationships with clients, consultants, and trade partners.

• Lead project closeout activities, including deficiencies and final site turnover.

## Why Acadian Construction?

At Acadian Construction, you're not just overseeing projects, you're helping deliver them the right way.

## What We Offer:

• Competitive compensation package.

• Group benefits program, including health, dental, vision, and an Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP).

• Company RRSP program.

• Professional development and career growth opportunities.

• A collaborative, team-oriented culture built on our core values: Evolve, Lead, Own It, Collaborate, and Move Forward.

• Employee events, recognition initiatives, and opportunities to get involved.

## Ready to Join Our Team?

If you're looking for a company that values leadership, growth, accountability, and teamwork, we'd love to hear from you.

## Apply by October 16, 2026.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

## Job Summary:

The Director of Business Operations will oversee business functions and lead the business operations, identify opportunities for growth and development, and provide accountability. The role will be responsible for leading the office, administrative, and sales sides of the business. This position will work closely with the General Manager on staffing requirements, capacity planning, job readiness, operational performance, customer concerns, and company-wide initiatives. The Director of Business Operations will have broader responsibility for the business, including oversight of sales, marketing, accounting, purchasing, staffing, planning, and profitability. description:
Title: Learning Ecosystem Support Specialist

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Temporary Full-time (12 months)

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

Reporting to the Director of Product Management, the Learning Ecosystem Support Specialist provides advanced technical support for the Canadian Red Cross Learning Ecosystem, including the external administration portal, eCommerce platform, Brightspace LMS, CRM integrations, identity services, and related applications. The role serves as the primary technical escalation point for cross-platform issues, integration failures, and end-to-end transaction troubleshooting across the learning technology ecosystem.

## In this role, you will :

• Investigate, diagnose, and resolve web-layer technical issues within D2L Brightspace, admin portal and eCommerce platform including HTTP errors, rendering glitches, and application timeouts.

• Review browser developer tools, console logs, network payloads, and application logs to identify front-end and back-end performance bottlenecks.

• Investigate authentication and access issues, including Single Sign-On (SSO) and integration access problems.

• Review application logs, integration logs and API transactions to determine if an issue is internal or vendor related.

• Collaborate closely with development team and vendors to gather technical details required to resolve complex issues.

• Spot check high-level HTML, CSS, and JavaScript issues logged in console or custom widgets that impact accessibility or mobile responsiveness.

• Diagnose and resolve issues reported by customer service related to system configurations.

• Coordinate with internal Technology Group and D2L support to ensure issues are assigned to the appropriate support group.

• Maintain clear and concise case notes documenting the issue, investigation, actions taken and resolution details for each support ticket.

• Ensure internal stakeholder are informed of the ticket status, progress, and resolution activities while coordinating with the Customer Service Escalation Specialist to maintain macros/scripts.

• Document system configurations, troubleshooting playbooks, and root-cause analyses for the internal knowledge base.

• Develop a strong understanding of the Prevention& Safety business and delivery service model.

• Ensure all established processes and quality controls have been completed prior to ticket closures.

• Interact with Product Owner, D2L Technical Advisor Manager (TAM) and internal Technology Group team to validate product software issues and assist in their resolution.

• Take ownership of the support tickets assigned and be responsible for them until resolution and for communication with internal staff.

• Maintain a current skill set on third Party D2L applications used by external customers and internal staff.

• Train Tier 2 staff on high-level troubleshooting steps to provide sufficient details in support ticket.

## What we are looking for:

• College degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or related field or 2 + years of previous technical support experience or equivalent experience.

• 7 + years of experience administering, configuring or supporting web eCommerce, admin portals or D2L Brightspace platform.

• Strong technical understanding of web infrastructure, including HTTP/S protocols, web servers, DNS, and SSL/TLS certificates

• Proficiency in using web browser debugging tools (Chrome DevTools) to analyze network traffic and console errors.

• Experience with Microsoft D365 (e.g. CRM & F&O) or related is required.

• Practical knowledge of web standards and coding in (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) and API integrations (REST, JSON, LTI 1.3).

• Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities with demonstrated comprehensive troubleshooting tactics.

• Ability to tailor explanations of technical concepts to the end user audience.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are a must.

• Proficiency in English oral and written, is required.

• Familiarity with Vue.js is preferred but not required.

## Working Conditions:

• Ability to work from home as the primary workspace.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Able to communicate effectively with operations and maintenance personnel while carrying out duties.

• Familiar with operating a computer and running Windows-driven applications.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where our operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from the Voisey's Bay mine into finished nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. • Minimum of 3 years of operating experience in a mineral processing plant with experience in 4 of the following circuits: crushing, grinding, flotation, dewatering, reagents, paste plant, tailings and water management, concentrator central control room, or paste plant control room.

• Experience operating a forklift and/or overhead cranes would be considered an asset.

## Skills:

• Basic understanding of mineral processing theory and practice.

• Familiar with the process flowsheet and with the equipment and its function.

• Familiar with the safe work practices and standard operating procedures of the concentrator.

• Able to recognize hazards in an industrial workplace and understands his or her role in assessing and managing risk.

• Able to apply logical thinking to solve problems and "trouble-shoot" abnormal situations to correct mechanical or process problems.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Indigenous Employment Coordinator.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Apply by: Friday, October 16th, 2026

About Us
The Safety Branch of the Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration delivers regulatory programs that protect workers and the public. Through education and outreach, inspection and enforcement, equipment registration, permits and licences, more than 130 employees located across Nova Scotia support compliance with provincial safety requirements. The Branch uses a compliance pathway that includes setting and promoting requirements, verifying compliance and taking enforcement action when necessary.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Executive Director, Occupational Health and Safety, the Senior Director Compliance and Inspection provides strategic direction, quality-management oversight, operational planning expertise and leadership for the provincial delivery of workplace occupational health and safety compliance, inspection, enforcement and investigation programs and regulatory activities.
The Senior Director provides timely, informed advice to senior leadership and Regional Directors, leads major province-wide compliance and inspection initiatives, supports continuous improvement, and contributes to legislative and regulatory reform in response to emerging workplace-safety issues. The role may exercise authorities delegated under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, as determined by the Executive Director.

Primary Accountabilities
• Lead the development, execution and continuous improvement of comprehensive regional operational plans, performance measures and service-delivery frameworks that meet legislative requirements and align with departmental priorities.

• Provide provincial oversight of inspections, investigations, enforcement actions, administrative penalties, prosecutions and case management to support the clear, consistent and fair application of occupational health and safety legislation, policies and procedures.

• Monitor regional performance, inspection and enforcement practices, emerging risks and service-delivery gaps, and provide strategic direction and decision support to Regional Directors and compliance and inspection staff.

• Review files, make recommendations on enforcement actions and intervene when appropriate enforcement action has not been taken or requires correction.

• Lead change initiatives for province-wide regional inspection and compliance operations, including the development and implementation of standards, programs, processes and service-delivery improvements.

• Represent Nova Scotia on provincial, regional and national working groups concerned with regulatory harmonization, labour mobility, emerging issues, regulatory development and compliance planning.

• Build and maintain strategic relationships across the Safety Branch, government departments and agencies, other levels of government, professional associations, communities, the Workers' Compensation Board and the private sector.

• Provide advice and background information to senior and elected officials and, when required, respond to media inquiries concerning occupational health and safety inspections, investigations and serious incidents.

• Lead the effective planning and management of human and financial resources, including performance objectives, coaching, succession planning, employee development, respectful workplace practices, procurement and budget forecasting.

Qualifications and Experience
This may be the right opportunity for you if you have a university degree relevant to occupational health and safety, coupled with several years of leadership experience in a related field. An acceptable combination of education, training and experience may be considered.
You have demonstrated knowledge and experience in occupational health and safety compliance, inspection, enforcement, investigation, program delivery and the development of solutions that affect workplace health and safety. Experience working with various levels of government and diverse partners is required.
You possess exceptional interpersonal, written and verbal communication, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills. You can provide clear strategic advice, manage sensitive and high-profile issues, and establish effective relationships with a diverse range of individuals and organizations. Experience responding to media inquiries on sensitive matters is considered a strong asset.
You are proficient in Microsoft Office applications and possess strong organizational and analytical skills. You work accurately, pay close attention to detail and balance competing priorities in a fast-paced environment. You quickly synthesize new information and provide advice grounded in sound judgment and professional expertise.
A valid driver's licence is required.
Leadership competencies required at this level include Decisiveness, Strategic Orientation, Developing Others, Team Leadership, Self-Awareness and Personal Impact, Effective Interactive Communication, Partnering and Relationship Building, and Intercultural and Diversity Proficiency.
We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interviews and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

• Field visits may involve exposure to dust, dirt or noise and walking over rough terrain or obstacles.

• The role manages sensitive and time-critical matters, competing demands, serious-incident response and regulatory deadlines.

Additional Information
This position leads a province-wide management and inspection organization, including Regional Directors and specialized investigation and inspection functions.
Offer of employment is conditional upon completion of all applicable background checks and confirmation of credentials, with results satisfactory to the employer.

What We Offer

• Countless career paths

description:
## Provincial Trails Coordinator

## Department of Natural Resources

## Pay Band 5

## Fredericton

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are:

The Department of Natural Resources is seeking an individual to join the Crown Lands Branch, as the Provincial Trails Coordinator, located in Fredericton.

The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for protecting and managing the forests, fish, and wildlife, and for overseeing the development of mineral resources in New Brunswick. The Crown Lands Branch is responsible for the administration and management of Crown lands across New Brunswick, ensuring responsible use and sustainable development. The branch oversees land tenure and land use authorizations supporting a wide range of commercial, recreational, and resource-based activities on Crown lands, including the management of the Former Railway Line and other corridors for the development and management of a recreational trail network.

## What you will do:

As a member of the Approvals Section and reporting to the section Manager, the selected candidate will be responsible for coordinating the development of both motorized and non-motorized trails on Crown lands with the objective to ensure the safe, sustainable and strategically located public recreational trail opportunities that maximizes the economic, social and environmental benefits to the province.

## Key responsibilities:

• Developing and maintaining a positive working relationship with the main trail user groups and relevant staff from other departments with similar trail mandates;

• Creating and maintaining Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data to support activities related to motorized trail applications;

• Participating as Chairperson of the Provincial Trail Planning Committee, with responsibility for agendas and minutes and related liaison functions, including trail application processes for development, use and maintenance of all trail networks;

• Providing functions associated with the operation of the Trail Management Trust Fund including all processes and protocols as established by the Minister, necessary for the disbursement of funds in accordance with the Off-Road Vehicle Act;

• Participating in process improvement related initiatives;

• Working with project managers and other branch staff to ensure trail priorities are met and clients receive timely responses to trail applications, including making recommendations with respect to policies, procedures, regulation and/or legislation, as they relate to Crown land use and trails;

• Performing other related duties as required.

## Who you are:

• You have excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• You excel at providing high-quality client services.

• You are at your best when challenged and thrive on getting results.

title: Case Managers
description:
## Work Remotely Anywhere in the Province of New Brunswick.

Looking to make a meaningful impact in the lives of injured workers and employers across New Brunswick?

WorkSafeNB is hiring a Bilingual written and spoken Case Manager for a permanent position within our Claims Management team. We're also creating a talent pool of qualified Bilingual written and spoken candidates for future permanent and term opportunities. When you apply, you'll be considered not only for the current opening but also for upcoming bilingual Case Manager roles over the next year.

Reporting to a dedicated Claims Management leader, you are responsible for a broad range of responsibilities including assessing the needs of individual workers and administering the benefit provisions of the Workers' Compensation Act. They also exercise leadership in the development of a goal-oriented return-to-work plan; liaising with employers, health-care providers, unions, and other service providers to ensure access to appropriate medical and vocational rehabilitation services. Other responsibilities include managing assigned caseloads, preparing reasoned plain language decisions, adhering to procedures for return-to-work management and approving/authorizing services and benefits for injured workers on an ongoing basis.

## Salary And Hours Of Work:

• Hours of work are those required to perform the assigned tasks but shall not be less than 35 hours per week, 7 per day. Monday to Friday between 8:00-5:00 PM.
• The pay scale for this position is $92,248.80 to $108,528.00 annually.

## Responsibilities

• Experience in building strong trusting relationships with clients and external service providers to promote early and safe return to work outcomes.
• Exercise leadership in the development of a goal-oriented return-to-work case plan, by proactively managing a timely and safe return-to-work process through the active participation of the injured worker and employer.
• Work in a high pace environment without losing sight of the Safe and Early Return to Work Goal.
• Work collaboratively with injured workers, employers, and health-care professionals, in the development of the return-to-work plan.
• Manage, organize, and prioritize a high-volume workload; deal with changing and conflicting priorities and deadlines, remain professional and maintain resiliency when confronted with challenging circumstances.
• Prepare written decisions that contain the issue in review, the policy tests, the evidence, the weighing of evidence, the rationale for the decision and conclusion that supports WorkSafeNB's position.
• Act as principal decision maker on assigned claims and effectively communicate decisions both verbally and in writing when determining entitlement to compensation, services, and medical aid.
• Make decisions in a fiscally responsible manner including verification and authorization of benefit entitlements and to defend these decisions in writing, both when approving and denying entitlement to compensation.

## Qualifications

• A University Degree is required. A degree in the field of health-related sciences or Social Sciences (e.g., Psychology or Social Work) would be considered an asset.
• Five years of experience in the field of medical management, disability management, vocational counseling, vocational rehabilitation, or other related work experience.
• Either have, or be willing to obtain, certification in disability management within two years of employment.
• Knowledge of social agencies and the services/benefits available such as Social Assistance, Employment insurance, Canada Pension Plan Disability.
• Knowledge of or experience with the following acts would be an asset: Workers' Compensation Act, Workplace Health Safety, Compensation Commission Act, Firefighters Act, Occupational Health and Safety Act, Human Rights Act, Privacy of Information Act, Employment Standards Act and Employment Insurance Act.
• Demonstrate critical thinking and reasoning for decision-making and writing is considered an asset.
• Experience in interpreting and implementing legislation and policy is considered an asset.

## Competencies:

• Ensuring Accountability
• Teamwork and Collaboration
• Decision Making
• Adaptability
• Client-focused Service
• Enabling Communication
• Planning and Organizing
• Problem Solving
• Written Communication
• Legislation and Compliance

You'll enjoy a range of valuable benefits designed to support your well?being and success. Below is an overview of what we're pleased to offer you:

The team at WorkSafeNB is passionate about promoting health and safety in New Brunswick workplaces. We strive to make New Brunswick the safest place to work. However, injuries do occur, and when they do, we are committed to providing caring recovery and return to work services, benefits, and compensation to injured workers and their families. title: Education Consultant (Education Officer 3)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 49976

Department: Labour, Skills and Immigration

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 13-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration works to provide fairness, safety and prosperity for all Nova Scotians by helping them live, learn and work to their highest potential. Together, we support workplace safety, apprenticeship, adult education, workforce development and other services that affect everyday life in Nova Scotia.
The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency supports and advances apprenticeship training and certification across the province. Working with industry, training providers, communities, regulatory authorities and provincial, territorial and federal partners, the Agency develops and maintains occupational standards, curriculum standards, examinations, training pathways and policies that contribute to a highly skilled workforce.
We are seeking an innovative, collaborative and highly skilled education professional to join the Standards and Examinations team as Education Consultant, Apprenticeship Agency.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Manager, Program Standards, the Education Consultant provides leadership and direction for the development, implementation and continuous improvement of a portfolio of skilled trades training and certification products. You will design, develop and maintain occupational and curriculum standards, assessments, examinations and flexible training pathways that respond to industry needs and support quality apprenticeship programming across Nova Scotia.
You will work with business, industry, labour, education providers, communities, equity groups and government partners to identify emerging needs and develop new programs and initiatives. You will also provide evidence-informed advice on whether proposed training pathways or initiatives should proceed and may contribute to workforce development initiatives aligned with Government and Agency priorities.

Primary Accountabilities
As the Education Consultant, you will:

• Write, review, edit and validate occupational standards, curriculum standards, competencies, learning outcomes, assessments and examinations for assigned skilled trades.

• Determine short- and long-term priorities for the development, review and revision of trades training and certification products.

• Design innovative, flexible and accessible training pathways and resources for in-person, online and other delivery models, including pathways for new trades or trades without established training options.

• Apply expertise in curriculum development, adult education, Universal Design for Learning, cultural responsiveness, equitable learning principles, assessment design and examination-item development.

• Recruit, screen and support subject matter experts, instructors and industry practitioners participating in development and validation activities.

• Plan and facilitate provincial, Atlantic and national workshops involving subject matter experts, instructors and apprenticeship representatives.

• Chair or support committees, task teams and steering committees, and represent the Agency on provincial, regional and national initiatives, including work undertaken through the Atlantic Apprenticeship Council and the Canadian Council of Directors of Apprenticeship.

• Build and maintain effective partnerships with business, industry, labour, education providers, youth and equity groups, communities, and federal, provincial and territorial governments.

• Ensure published standards, examinations and communications meet applicable Atlantic and national standards and comply with government legislation, regulations, policies and quality requirements.

• Maintain alignment and consistency among occupational standards, curriculum documents, assessments and examinations.

• Monitor occupational, technological, industry and labour market trends; research policies, programs and leading practices in Canada and internationally; and recommend new or revised programming.

.
• Conduct examination-item and statistical analyses to support the validity, reliability and continuous improvement of assessments and programs.

• Support the development, annual review and evaluation of transfer-credit agreements with secondary and post-secondary education providers, including approximately 50 external certificate and diploma programs.

• Provide expert guidance on recognition of prior learning, transfer credit, cross-trade credit and credential-recognition matters.

• Lead or support policy development related to apprenticeship training and certification, including consultation and jurisdictional research.

• Prepare proposals, reports, briefing notes, issue papers, surveys, presentations and other internal and external communications, and present information to diverse audiences.

• Monitor project expenditures, follow procurement requirements, manage contracts with technical writers or development consultants, and coach contracted resources.

• Contribute to labour market and workforce planning initiatives, including analysis related to education and training programs, recruitment, retention, succession planning and workplace culture.

• Perform other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Experience
As the successful candidate you have a master's degree in education, as well as 8 years of experience in the design, development, implementation and evaluation/monitoring of training standards, curriculum, examinations, policies and/or programs, or an equivalent combination of training and experience. Experience in online course development and delivery is required.
You also have:

• Significant experience developing, reviewing or implementing curriculum, occupational standards, competency frameworks, assessments or examinations.

• Demonstrated knowledge of adult learning, Universal Design for Learning, culturally responsive and equitable education practices, and valid and reliable assessment principles.

• Experience leading complex projects involving multiple partners, competing priorities and firm timelines.

title: Data Analyst
description:
The Opportunity

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Customer & Grid Intelligence

Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia

Type of Employment: Permanent, Full-Time

Closing Date: October 13, 2026

Are you passionate about transforming data into meaningful insights that drive business decisions? As a Data Analyst on the Data Insights & Analytics team within Customer & Grid Intelligence, you'll play a key role in helping the organization leverage data to improve operational performance, enhance customer outcomes, and support strategic decision-making.

In this role, you will work with a wide range of data sources, including smart meter, asset, customer, among others, turning complex information into actionable intelligence. You'll collaborate with business and technical teams to develop dashboards, reports, and analytical solutions that support operational efficiency, data quality, and continuous improvement.

This is an excellent opportunity for a curious and analytical professional who enjoys solving problems, working with large datasets, and translating business needs into impactful data-driven solutions. You'll have the chance to influence decision-making across the organization while expanding your technical, analytical, and stakeholder engagement skills.

Key elements of this role include:

• Develop dashboards and visualizations that provide meaningful insights and support business decision-making.

• Create, maintain, and enhance reports using large and complex datasets to address operational and strategic needs.

• Analyze data sources, workflows, and business processes to identify trends, opportunities, and actionable recommendations.

• Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and availability of critical business and smart meter data.

• Develop and maintain data models, data dictionaries, and data catalogs that improve data accessibility and governance.

• Perform data validation, testing, and quality assurance activities to support reliable reporting and analytics.

• Write and optimize complex SQL queries across multiple data sources to support analysis and reporting requirements.

• Partner with stakeholders to understand business challenges and translate requirements into effective data solutions.

• Create ad hoc reports to address emerging business needs.

• Support data transformation activities and the development of data-driven solutions.

• Contribute to requirements gathering, data modelling, and workflow development aligned with business processes.

• Communicate analytical findings and technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance reporting capabilities, business processes, and operational performance.

These skills will make you successful:

• Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Business Analytics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 2-4 years of experience in data analysis, reporting, data modelling, business intelligence, or a related analytical role.

• Advanced experience working with SQL and relational databases.

• Experience developing dashboards and reports using Tableau and working with large, complex datasets.

• Knowledge of data modelling, data transformation, data quality management, and data validation methodologies.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify trends and translate data into actionable insights.

• Experience gathering and interpreting business requirements to develop practical, data-driven solutions.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences.

• Familiarity with Python, statistical analysis, machine learning concepts, or similar analytical tools is considered an asset.

• Experience working with smart meter technologies, customer information systems, work management systems, ServiceNow, ITIL, or ITSM processes is considered an asset.

If you're excited by the opportunity to work with complex data, build impactful analytics solutions, and help drive informed business decisions, we'd love to hear from you.

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by Tuesday, October 13, 2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

• Competitive Compensation: Short-term incentive plan and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

## Full careers. Full lives.

## Join the Medavie Health NL Team

Are you looking for a fulfilling career that makes a meaningful impact on your life, and the lives of others? As the provider of emergency medical services and medical communications operations across Newfoundland and Labrador, Medavie Health NL (MHNL) is proud to offer career opportunities for professionals who share our strong commitment to delivering healthcare to communities throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.

If you're a passionate professional seeking a unique and meaningful career, MHNL is your destination. Join our team and achieve your full potential in a supportive and dynamic environment.

As an Application Specialist, you will work as part of the Provincial Medical Communications Centre (PMCC) team, with a primary focus on the administration, support, optimization, and ongoing development of applications and technologies that support PMCC operations.

The Application Specialist will be the primary PMCC resource for the Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) system and will serve as the go-to contact for CAD and PMCC technology-related matters. This includes the day-to-day administration and configuration of the CAD system, identifying opportunities to improve functionality, supporting system changes, and working directly with the CAD vendor to troubleshoot issues and develop and implement enhancements that meet the operational needs of PMCC.

The position will work closely with Medavie IT and other technical resources to support PMCC applications, integrations, access, system issues, and technology initiatives. The Application Specialist will also work collaboratively with System Performance on data, CAD reporting, dashboards, system performance information, and other reporting requirements to ensure PMCC has accurate and meaningful information to support operational decision-making.

Responsibilities Include:

• Administer, configure, maintain, and support the PMCC Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) system and other PMCC applications and technologies.

• Act as the primary PMCC subject matter expert and point of contact for CAD functionality, configuration, workflows, integrations, and system-related issues.

• Work directly with the CAD vendor to identify opportunities for enhancement, troubleshoot issues, test solutions, and implement system changes that support PMCC operational requirements.

• Coordinate and participate in the testing and implementation of application changes, upgrades, enhancements, and new functionality.

• Maintain accurate technical documentation related to application configuration, workflows, system functionality, processes, and user support.

• Contribute to application and technology roadmaps for PMCC systems and identify future technology requirements.

• Support application administration activities including configuration, user access, version control, and system changes.

• Participate in workflow and security reviews and ensure application changes support organizational and PMCC requirements.

• Provide technical and application support to PMCC operational groups and assist with the timely resolution of system-related issues.

• Work collaboratively with other Medavie programs and departments on shared applications, technology, data, and system initiatives.

• Support PMCC projects involving application development, system enhancements, data, reporting, workflow changes, and technology implementation.

Professional Qualifications & Competencies:

• Related EMS, emergency communications, healthcare, or equivalent operational experience considered an asset.

• Experience working with Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) systems, emergency communications systems, or other operational applications considered an asset.

• Experience in application administration, system configuration, business analysis, technical support, or a related field.

• Experience working directly with software vendors and IT teams to troubleshoot issues and implement system enhancements.

• Experience working with data, reporting, dashboards, or system performance information considered an asset.

• Experience with SQL, reporting tools, or data analysis considered an asset.

• Strong knowledge of application configuration, system administration, workflow development, and version control.

• Strong technical aptitude with the ability to analyze, troubleshoot, problem-solve, and make sound decisions.

• Ability to understand operational requirements and translate them into practical application and technology solutions.

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy when working with system configuration, data, reporting, and operational workflows.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, service requests, projects, and deadlines.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information clearly to both technical and operational audiences.

• Demonstrated ability to build strong working relationships and collaborate effectively with operational teams, IT, vendors, System Performance, and other programs.

• Ability to work independently while recognizing when issues require collaboration or escalation.

• Demonstrated commitment to continuous improvement and the effective use of technology to support PMCC operations.

## Salary Range

• $64,000 to $71,000 annually.

The Base Pay range may vary depending on the successful candidate or other relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience and education/training. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Medavie employees may participate in various performance-based incentive programs. Payments under these programs are discretionary and subject to both individual and organizational results.

MHNL is the selected proponent to design, manage and operate a single, integrated road and air ambulance service in Newfoundland and Labrador. We are an incorporated, wholly owned NL-based subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS), the largest contracted provider of emergency management services in Canada and a national leader in primary health care solutions, including mobile integrated health and community paramedicine programs.

Together with Medavie Blue Cross, MHS is part of Medavie, a national health solutions partner and innovative leader in benefits management, health management, and healthcare delivery. Backed by our team of over 8,200 dedicated professionals, we exist to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest.

If you share our mission of improving the wellbeing of Canadians, join our team.

We are more than just a workplace - we are a people-focused, visionary organization dedicated to fostering well-being and making a meaningful impact on the lives of our employees and the Communities we serve.

We celebrate individuality and value the diverse perspectives and skills our employees contribute. We go beyond providing competitive pay and comprehensive benefits by offering opportunities for personal and professional growth, meaningful experiences, and supportive leadership. description:

Company: Nova Scotia Power

Department: Work in Asset Management - Customer & Grid Intelligence

Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia

Closing Date: October 13, 2026

Are you passionate about improving business processes, solving operational challenges, and delivering technology solutions that make a real impact? As the Product Owner, Work and Asset Management (WAM), you will play a key role in shaping and enhancing the systems that support Regional Operations teams and field work execution.

In this role, you'll serve as the bridge between operational users, business stakeholders, and technical teams, ensuring that WAM solutions evolve to meet changing business needs while delivering maximum value to the organization. You'll have the opportunity to influence how work is planned, scheduled, and managed, driving initiatives that improve efficiency, strengthen user experience, and support operational excellence.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys combining business analysis, product ownership, stakeholder engagement, and continuous improvement. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams, lead meaningful change, and help translate complex operational needs into practical technology solutions that support employees, contractors, and customers alike.

Key elements of this role include:

• Champion the end-user experience for Regional Operations teams by optimizing WAM solutions and related business processes.

• Partner with operational stakeholders, subject matter experts, and technical teams to identify needs and develop effective solutions.

• Gather, analyze, and translate business requirements into system enhancements, configurations, and solution designs.

• Prioritize initiatives and product improvements that deliver the greatest operational and business value.

• Lead workshops, discussions, and working sessions to uncover opportunities for process improvement and innovation.

• Assess business impacts, troubleshoot system challenges, and recommend solutions that improve operational effectiveness.

• Support solution delivery through user acceptance testing, validation activities, and issue resolution.

• Conduct business impact assessments related to system and process changes.

• Develop and contribute to training, user support materials, and change adoption activities that help teams successfully embrace new processes and technologies.

• Build strong relationships across the organization, facilitating collaboration, alignment, and informed decision-making.

• Manage stakeholder expectations and provide updates on initiatives and outcomes.

• Apply project management principles to plan, coordinate, track, and deliver initiatives.

• Coordinate and support cross-functional projects, providing progress updates, managing priorities, and helping deliver successful outcomes.

These skills will make you successful:

• Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Minimum 6 years of relevant experience in product management, business analysis, and product ownership role, with experience supporting Energy Delivery processes within an electric utility environment.

• Experience working with Agile and Scrum methodologies, with the ability to gather requirements, analyze business processes, and translate business needs into effective technology solutions.

• Experience with Work and Asset Management (WAM) solutions and related technologies such as Maximo, CIS, Salesforce/Field Service, particularly within utility or field operations environments is considered an asset.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and collaboration platforms.

• Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and applying project management practices to drive results.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills with the ability to evaluate information from multiple sources.

• Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build consensus among diverse groups.

• Experience supporting organizational change, user training, and solution adoption initiatives.

• Ability to facilitate workshops and build collaborative relationships across teams.

• Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

If you're energized by improving operational performance, influencing technology strategy, and partnering with teams to create better ways of working, we'd love to hear from you. This is an opportunity to make a visible impact while helping shape the future of Work and Asset Management solutions across the organization.

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers.

If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by Tuesday, October 13, 2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

About Us
Nova Scotia is rich in natural resources, including biodiversity, forests, provincial parks, and the land we manage. The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for the development, management, conservation and protection of forest, parks and wildlife resources, and the administration of the province's Crown land. Together we are working with Nova Scotians to build a better future through sustainable natural resource management as we all benefit from the natural health and wealth of the province.

The Shubenacadie Wildlife Park is one of Nova Scotia's top tourist destinations and has attracted millions of visitors over the past 72 years. The 331-hectare park has enchanted Nova Scotians and visitors alike and provides a wide range of outdoor recreational and educational opportunities.

About Our Opportunity
Do you enjoy working with people and creating positive visitor experiences? The Shubenacadie Wildlife Park is seeking Visitor Experience Clerks to serve as the first point of contact for visitors and help ensure every guest receives exceptional customer service.

## Visitor Experience Clerks take pride in:

• Professionally welcoming visitors and processing admissions
• Providing information about the Wildlife Park, programs, exhibits and surrounding area
• Operating point-of-sale systems and processing sales transactions
• Answering questions and resolving customer concerns
• Maintaining a clean, safe and welcoming admissions area for staff and

## Secondary duties may include:

• Balancing cash and preparing daily deposits
• Cleaning and maintaining admissions facilities and public washrooms
• Assisting with inventory control and merchandise displays
• Supporting special events and visitor programs
• Assisting with weather-related activities including sweeping, sanding and snow removal as required

As a Visitor Experience Clerk, you will work under the supervision of the Visitor Experience Supervisor.

Primary Accountabilities
As the first staff member many visitors interact with, you will set the tone for their visit. You will utilize excellent customer service, communication, and problem-solving skills to address visitor inquiries, difficult customer situations, unexpected visitor volumes, and booking issues.

You will be responsible for:

• Processing admissions, merchandise sales and other financial transactions
• Maintaining accurate cash handling and accounting records
• Balancing and preparing daily revenue deposits
• Providing accurate information regarding the Wildlife Park and local attractions
• Maintaining a safe, clean and welcoming visitor environment
• Working independently while prioritizing tasks and responding to operational requirements as they arise

Qualifications and Experience
You've completed Grade 12 or have an equivalent combination of training and experience.

To be successful in this role, you should possess, confirm in your cover letter, and be prepared to demonstrate:

• Experience working with cash transactions, balancing, deposits, and basic accounting procedures
• Experience operating cash registers and point-of-sale systems
• Excellent customer service and communication skills
• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
• Strong problem-solving abilities and sound judgment
• Ability to stand for extended periods and work in a fast-paced environment.

The following are considered assets:

• Previous tourism, hospitality, retail, admissions, or visitor services experience
• Knowledge of the Shubenacadie Wildlife Park and local tourism attractions
• Knowledge of park directives, departmental policies and procedures
• Knowledge of Occupational Health and Safety requirements
• Experience working with public education or recreation facilities

We will assess the above qualifications using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Working Conditions
• Weekend, and evening work is required, often outside in all weather conditions.
• Work is primarily conducted in a small admissions office with frequent interaction with the public.
• Periods of high visitor volume require sustained concentration, accuracy and customer service excellence.
• Employees may occasionally be required to perform light groundskeeping, cleaning and weather-related duties.
• Ability to work independently while maintaining a high level of professionalism is essential.

Additional Information
Currently, there is a casual position available from October to May, primarily as weekend and evening shifts, often outdoors in all weather conditions.

The Wildlife Park welcomes approximately 100,000 visitors annually, making the Visitor Experience Clerk an important ambassador for both the Park and the Department.

What We Offer
• Meaningful work contributing to one of Nova Scotia's most visited attractions.

• Opportunities to develop customer service, communication, and administrative skills.

• A supportive team environment.

• Valuable experience within the Provincial Government.
• Opportunities for future seasonal and casual employment.

Medavie Health Services New Brunswick (MHSNB) is the subsidiary of Medavie Health Services responsible for the optimal operation and management of EM/ANB, an integrated organization specializing in the delivery of primary health care services with the goal of facilitating access to quality care so that patients can achieve better health outcomes. Our company is currently looking for new team members to support its mission of providing excellence in emergency and community care within our various programs, namely Ambulance New Brunswick, the Extra-Mural Program and NB Health Link. As a not-for-profit organization, Medavie is proud to commit an annual social dividend to the Medavie Health Foundation to support programs and initiatives aimed at addressing some of our country's most pressing physical and mental health care challenges.

We are looking for a Facilities Technician to help support our growing operation which provides exemplary, highly coordinated primary health care in the right place, from the right provider, at the right time .

Reporting to the Manager, Facilities, the Facilities Technician will be responsible for upkeep and repair tasks of all EM/ANB Facilities in the Province. One of your main responsibilities will be to maintain our Facilities to ensure the buildings are safe for building occupants and properly maintained.

## In this role, you will be responsible for:

description:
## Inclusion Coach

## Annapolis Valley Region – Lawrencetown Location

NS Early Childhood Development Intervention Services (NSECDIS) provide province-wide specialized services to families of young children between birth and school entry, who either have a biological risk for or a diagnosis of, developmental delay in NS. Consultation, information, support and services designed to meet the individual needs of each child and family are delivered in the child's home and may extend to community based programs. Services emphasize the enhancement of skills and ability through planned interactions to promote child development and family capacity.

Early Childhood Development Intervention Services (ECDIS) also facilitate early childhood educator capacity building through the delivery of inclusion coaching to childcare and pre-primary program settings, utilizing the Pyramid Model. The Pyramid Model for Supporting Social Emotional Competence in Infants and Young Children is a conceptual framework of evidence-based practices for promoting young children's healthy social and emotional development.

## Requiring: 1 Full Time Inclusion Coach

## Annapolis Valley Region – Lawrencetown Office

Through the implementation of Pyramid Model evidence-based practices, the Inclusion Coach provides professional development and program coaching to build the capacity of early childhood educators and childcare centres to support young children's social emotional and behavioural competency.

Coaching definition: Coaching is an interactive process based on a collaborative relationship. It is intentionally designed to promote sustainable growth in attitudes, skills and knowledge to effectively implement best practices for optimal development of young children and their families. Through observation, discussion, reflection and collaborative planning the coach promotes the early childhood educator's abilities to grow toward their identified goals.

## Duties and Responsibilities

## Program Planning

• build relationships and establish an environment and culture of best practices

• observe coachee and program to gather information for the coachee's profile and coaching and development plan

• assist coachees and programs to identify priorities and functional/meaningful outcomes based on their identified needs

• respond sensitively to the coachee's cultural diversity and individual preferences

• provide guidance and support to the program data coordinator on measures, collecting data, and using data for making decisions

• provide ongoing support to program leadership teams by attending their meetings and assisting with data-use and decision making as required

## Program Delivery

• provide training and support to early childhood educators and other staff on Pyramid Model and inclusive practices

• identify resources and supports in accordance with individual coaching plans

• plan, implement and document regularly scheduled coaching visits/consultations and meetings

• inform coachees of available options to support their professional growth and development in accordance with their own styles and preferences, including preferred levels of involvement in the intervention process

• organize and conduct regular reviews and revisions of the coaching and development plan with coachee and program

• support the implementation of individualized strategies and supports based on the coachee's and program's identified strengths, resources, priorities and concerns

• support the coachee and program to reflect on observations of their progress and to connect child development theories to practice in a clear, meaningful and practical manner

• assist the coachee and program in critically evaluating services and supports that are best for their program

• provide guidance, development and support to the program's internal coaches on practice-based coaching and tools for assessing a classroom implementation strengths and needs

• provide data, information and documentation to the Provincial Leadership team as required

• participate in training (in person/online), research and program evaluations as required

• maintain an on-going commitment to learning and professional development

## Community Connection

• provide support to other Inclusion Coaches and Developmental Interventionists as needed

• maintain knowledge base of community-based services, resources, and programs

• facilitate and maintain partnerships with local service providers to create networks of community supports for early childhood educators and families

• make recommendations for referrals to appropriate services/programs, as needed

• assist the coachee and program to find and access community resources to support their program

• attend community events and meetings with community partners as required

• communicate with other intervention, education and health professionals in order to

learn of emerging professional consensus and approaches

• participate in NSECDIS centre-based programming

• participate on community-based committees where appropriate

## Administration

• support/mentor other Inclusion Coaches and Developmental Interventionists, regarding service delivery and caseload problem solving

• continue/maintain own professional development (e.g., goal setting, reading, course work, sharing information with other professionals in the field)

• expand professional knowledge base through ongoing education and the critical evaluation of emerging research and professional literature

• participate in the preparation and presentation of public relations materials as required.

• participate in program development and evaluation

• maintain and report any statistics, records, data, etc. required by the organization and leadership team

• collect and maintain data on each coachee and child care/pre-primary program's progress and prepare written reports as needed

## Required Qualifications and Skills

## Education

• a minimum Bachelor's degree in early childhood development or the equivalent combination of training and experience

## Work Experience

• experience working with children from birth to school age and their families is essential

• experience within early childhood education settings and a knowledge of policies and systems that affect early childhood services

## Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• competency and knowledge in early childhood development, social emotional learning, family-centred practice, and family systems theory

• demonstrated ability to implement developmentally appropriate practices, use adult

education principles, and deliver community-based programming

• strong planning, organizational, and time-management abilities

• knowledge/experience using observational assessment tools

• excellent communication (oral and written) and interpersonal skills, with the demonstrated ability to create and maintain effective relationships with children, families, early childhood educators and other community partners

• demonstrated knowledge of current trends, best practices, and research regarding early childhood development, and ability to apply theory to practice

• experience with underserved communities in the region (e.g., African Nova Scotian, First

Nations, new immigrant, Francophone/Acadian) and ability to communicate in other

languages an asset

• proficiency in the use of computers including word processing, e-mail, internet, digital calendars, file sharing programs, online data entry and video conferencing

• obtain valid First Aid Certification (Standard Child Care First Aid & CPR)

## Personal Attributes

• empathic, sensitive approach in communicating with children and families

• highly motivated and organized

• professional with the highest ethical standards

• able to work independently and within a team

• strong communicator verbally and in writing

• commitment to family-centred practice

• awareness of professional boundaries in working with families

## Working Conditions

• flexibility for some evening and weekend work when required

• regular travel (to childcare and pre-primary programs, other service provider locations, etc.) and access to own vehicle and valid driver's license is required

Salary: $34.20/hour plus Benefit Package

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the families we serve. We welcome applications from Acadian Francophones, Aboriginal People, African Nova Scotians, new immigrants and other racially visible persons and persons with disabilities. If you are a member of one of the equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your cover letter or resume.

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
Reporting to the Aerospace Procurement Manager, the successful candidate will integrate with the existing procurement team in providing timely and cost-effective procurement, including value added sourcing and ordering of parts, materials, equipment and services by applying and adhering to best supply chain practices.

What You Will Do:
• Source parts, materials, equipment and services from established vendors as well as establish new vendors as required

• Implement and execute commodity strategy to support cost, quality, supplier reduction, and delivery sourcing goals

• Review internal requests, prepare and release requests for quote (RFQ), and negotiate pricing with suppliers

• Create purchase orders with approved suppliers in accordance with Standard Plant Procedures (SPP's) and Administrative Directives (AD's)

• Responsible for the management of purchase orders in the MRP system (JD Edwards)

• Develop supplier relationships to ensure all parts & materials meet the requirements of internal and external customers

• Action discrepant, defective or unacceptable products/services with Receiving Inspection, Receiving and Quality Assurance departments, end users, vendors and others to determine the source and root cause of the problem and action the necessary corrective / preventative actions as required

• Resolve invoice discrepancies accurately and in a timely manner

• Interface with key stakeholders in a proactive manner to obtain and provide information, including procurement technical advice in support of overall operations

• Recommend and implement cost reduction initiatives

• Work within and promote Lean practices to meet departmental and divisional goals

• Meet industry representatives on behalf of the company

• Carry out special assignments as required

What You Will Bring:
• Preference given to candidate with post-secondary education with 4 to 7 years' experience in supply chain ideally in the aerospace and/or aviation industries; or same level of experience in a similar type of complex and dynamic technical environment

• Supply Management Training (SMT) Program, Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMP) Designation, P.Log. or equivalent

• Skill in using MRP system; knowledge of JD Edwards would be considered an asset

• Intermediate to advanced computer skills – Emphasis on MS Office and use of MRP/ERP systems

• Experience in aerospace purchasing an asset

• Dynamic and have the ability to multi-task and shift priorities in a very demanding work environment while maintaining a high level of accuracy and detail

• Strong communication skills

• Incumbents must be able to pass and maintain (PSPC) Public Services and Procurement Canada and Transport Canada security clearances

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment policies. Continually focusing on your individual safety and the safety of others who may be affected by your work and to fully comply with all Federal Health and Safety Legislation.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), Secret Level II Security Clearance through PSPC - Contract Security Program, and Transport Canada RAIC clearance.

What We Will Do For You:
• All of IMP's benefits become effective on your first day of work, regardless of your position.

• We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RSP Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Long Service Awards, Volunteer Grant Program, Scholarship Program, and more!

IMP is committed to Employment Equity and our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative at all job levels. We welcome applicants from Indigenous People, Visible Minority Groups, Persons with Disabilities and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self identify on either your cover letter or resume.

VON Canada is a not-for-profit organization providing home and community care services for over 125 years. Focusing on person-centred care, we provide the support people need and want, at home and in the community, so they can live healthier, happier lives surrounded by loved ones.

As a VON nurse, you'll deliver holistic person-centred care to children, youth, adults, seniors, and support their families. • Rehabilitative programs
