title: General Manager & Regional Governance Modernization Lead
description:
General Manager & Regional Governance Modernization Lead
Yarmouth, Nova Scotia
Reference #JL-MDY-9785

The Yarmouth Area Industrial Commission (YAIC) is a regional economic development organization focused on supporting sustainable growth and prosperity throughout the Yarmouth region. Through strategic management of key assets, stakeholder partnerships, and economic development initiatives, YAIC plays an important role in advancing opportunities that benefit businesses, residents, and communities.

YAIC is seeking a collaborative and strategic leader to serve as General Manager & Regional Governance Modernization Lead. This unique position combines operational leadership of the Commission with a regional mandate to coordinate governance modernization initiatives across three municipal partners.

## The Role

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the General Manager & Regional Governance Modernization Lead is responsible for the overall management and strategic direction of YAIC. The role provides leadership in operational planning, financial stewardship, stakeholder relations, contract management, and governance support while ensuring the organization achieves its strategic objectives.

Approximately 70% of the role is dedicated to General Manager responsibilities, including oversight of port operations, leases, financial management, and organizational performance. The remaining 30% is focused on advancing a regional governance modernization initiative, supporting municipal partners as they explore opportunities to strengthen collaboration, service delivery, and regional governance models.

This position operates within a service delivery model that utilizes contracted and outsourced expertise for selected administrative, financial, legal, engineering, and technical services. The General Manager maintains accountability for oversight, performance management, and coordination of all external service providers.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Provide strategic advice and operational leadership to the Board of Directors.

• Oversee port operations, leases, tenant relationships, and related business activities.

• Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, contractual, and governance requirements.

• Lead organizational financial planning, budgeting, reporting, and risk management activities.

• Manage relationships with government partners, tenants, community stakeholders, and industry representatives.

• Represent YAIC in meetings, public engagements, and regional initiatives.

• Develop and manage service agreements with contracted providers and consultants.

• Monitor outsourced services to ensure quality, timeliness, cost-effectiveness, and compliance with organizational expectations.

• Oversee contract administration and performance management of external service providers.

• Identify opportunities to optimize service delivery through a balance of internal and outsourced resources.

• Coordinate and advance regional governance modernization initiatives involving multiple municipal partners.

• Support research, analysis, policy development, and implementation planning related to governance modernization.

• Prepare reports, recommendations, and presentations for municipal and organizational stakeholders.

• Coordinate consultants, funding opportunities, project timelines, and stakeholder engagement activities.

• Support change management efforts and facilitate collaboration among participating organizations.

• Track progress toward strategic objectives and modernization milestones.

## Qualifications & Experience:

• Degree in public administration, business administration, finance, economics, governance, or a related discipline. Equivalent experience will also be considered.

• Progressive leadership experience within municipal government, economic development, public sector organizations, not-for-profit entities, or related environments.

• Experience in governance, financial management, contract administration, and strategic planning.

• Demonstrated success managing outsourced or vendor-delivered service models.

• Strong understanding of public sector governance, stakeholder engagement, and organizational accountability.

• Experience leading projects that involve multiple organizations, partners, or levels of government.

• Strong financial and analytical skills with experience interpreting budgets, reports, and performance metrics.

• Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and facilitation skills.

• Political acumen and the ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments.

• Proven ability to manage competing priorities and deliver results in a dynamic environment.

## What Success Looks Like:

• Effective oversight and delivery of outsourced services within budget and established performance expectations.

• Advancement and achievement of regional governance modernization milestones.

• Strong financial stewardship and operational performance.

• Positive stakeholder relationships and successful regional collaboration.

• High levels of Board confidence and satisfaction with organizational leadership and strategic direction.

title: Maintenance Operations Supervisor
description:
## Job Title: Maintenance Operations Supervisor

## Location: Petit-De-Grat, Nova Scotia

## TP-SME-9687

Samson Industrial is a family-owned marine service company based in Petit-De-Grat, Nova Scotia, specializing in high-quality boat repair, maintenance, and refit services. With roots dating back to 1987, the company has built a reputation for technical expertise, craftsmanship, and a customer-focused approach to servicing vessels. Their experienced team supports a wide range of marine needs, including mechanical systems, hydraulic and propulsion systems, structural fabrication, welding, fiberglass repair, machining, and vessel inspections.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with Samson Industrial in the search for a Maintenance Operations Supervisor to join their team. This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for an experienced operations professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys leading from the front.

## Role Description

Reporting to the Operations Manager, the Maintenance Operations Supervisor will play a critical role in overseeing daily operations within Samson Industrial's boat repair facility. This is a highly visible, hands-on leadership position responsible for coordinating workflow, supporting employees, maintaining productivity, and ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.

This role is ideal for an operations-focused leader who enjoys working in an active environment and being directly involved with employees, equipment, subcontractors, and ongoing projects. The successful candidate will spend the majority of their time in the yard, providing direction, solving problems, and ensuring the operation runs smoothly.

## Key Responsibilities:

## Operations & Team Leadership

• Work closely with the Operations Manager to plan upcoming work and coordinate weekly priorities.

• Assign daily tasks to yard employees and ensure work progresses according to schedule.

• Provide day-to-day leadership, guidance, and support to a team of skilled tradespeople.

• Monitor progress, identify challenges, and address issues before they impact timelines.

• Act as a key communication link between employees and the Operations Manager.

## Marine Repair Coordination

• Support the coordination of vessel repair and maintenance projects from arrival through completion.

• Help identify operational issues and determine the best approach for resolution.

• Work alongside mechanics and tradespeople to understand project requirements and priorities.

• Ensure equipment, tools, and materials are available to support ongoing work.

• Coordinate subcontractors and external service providers as required.

## Materials, Equipment & Yard Management

• Order materials and supplies required for upcoming projects.

• Ensure employees have the resources needed to complete work efficiently.

• Maintain an organized and productive yard environment.

• Support proper use and maintenance of equipment and tools.

## Safety & Quality

• Promote safe work practices and ensure company safety expectations are followed.

• Monitor work quality and support a culture of attention to detail and craftsmanship.

• Identify potential safety or operational concerns and address them promptly.

## Qualifications

The ideal candidate will be a hands-on leader with experience in a mechanical or industrial environment. They will have the technical understanding needed to work effectively with tradespeople while also bringing strong organizational and leadership skills.

## Ideal Qualifications include:

• 5+ years of experience in a mechanical, marine, industrial, construction, or similar environment.

• Strong mechanical aptitude and previous experience working with tools, equipment, or mechanical systems.

• Previous supervisory or team leadership experience.

• Ability to understand repair processes, troubleshoot issues, and make practical decisions.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

• Excellent communication and problem-solving abilities.

• Experience in the marine industry would be considered a strong asset.

Candidates with backgrounds in heavy equipment, automotive, industrial maintenance, fabrication, or other skilled trades environments are encouraged to apply.

## What Success Looks Like

• Employees having clear priorities and the support needed to complete their work.

• Projects moving forward efficiently with minimal delays.

• Materials, tools, and equipment being available when required.

• Strong communication between the yard team and Operations Manager.

• A safe, organized, and productive repair facility.

• Increased operational efficiency and reduced day-to-day involvement required from ownership.

## Why Join Samson Industrial?

• Take on a key leadership role within a respected marine repair operation.

• Work alongside experienced tradespeople in a hands-on environment.

• Make a direct impact on daily operations and customer service.

• Enjoy a diverse role where no two days are the same.

• Build a long-term career with a growing local organization.

description:

Position Type: Regular

Location: Any NBCC campus

Salary Range: $53,794 to $63,674 Annually

Qualifications

## Education & Experience:

• Diploma or Degree in a relevant field with related years of experience.

• Designation in Public Service Procurement Program would be considered an asset.

• Knowledge of Oracle fusion, eBS would be considered an asset.

• Strong working knowledge in Microsoft office applications - Excel, word documents and email (office suite), Power Point.

• Strong oral and written communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively at all levels of the organization.

• Experience in handling large amounts of data for reconciliation and reporting.

## Professional Skills:

• Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Results Oriented, able to prioritize and consistently deliver on -time and accurate results.

• Highly flexible with excellent interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to navigate and build relationships effectively throughout the organization.

• Ability to maintain a high degree of professionalism and confidentiality.

• Demonstrated problem-solving skills, analytical ability, and innovative thinking.

• Self-motivated, service and results oriented.

• Ability to work under pressure in a fast-paced environment.

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively independently and within a team.

• A desire for continuous learning and growth.

• Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.

Preference may be given to candidates who have experience working in a post-secondary environment.

Candidates must clearly demonstrate how they meet these qualifications on their resumes.

Other combinations of education and experience may be considered as equivalent. Subject to competition response, the minimum qualifications may be raised.

All applicants must be eligible to work in Canada at the time of application. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

Responsibilities
The Procurement to Pay Agent (P2P), reporting to the Manager, Procure to Pay, is responsible for managing purchasing requests in collaboration with internal stakeholders and suppliers. This role handles tactical sourcing activities and is accountable for the P2P process including ensuring that NBCC receives quality products and services in an efficient and effective manner.

## Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

## PROCUREMENT

• Manage end-to-end Procure-to-Pay (P2P) activities, including requisitions, purchase orders, receiving, invoicing, payment, and supplier issue resolution in Oracle Fusion.

• Support and administer competitive procurement processes, including Tenders, RFPs, RFQs, and RFIs, ensuring compliance with procurement policies, trade agreements, contractual requirements, and organizational procedures.

• Coordinate with stakeholders and suppliers to define requirements, develop procurement strategies, evaluate submissions, negotiate commercial terms, and support supplier selection and contract award.

• Provide procurement support for IT goods and services, including hardware, software, SaaS/cloud solutions, software licensing, IT consulting, cybersecurity services, telecommunications, and other technology-related requirements.

• Review and manage purchase requisitions and POs to ensure accurate pricing, quantities, approvals, contractual terms, supporting documentation, and compliance with procurement requirements.

• Support contract lifecycle management, including contract development, amendments, extensions, renewals, change orders, pricing, deliverables, service levels, expiry dates, and supplier performance.

• Monitor supplier performance and coordinate with stakeholders to resolve contractual, service, purchasing, receiving, invoicing, and payment issues.

• Provide guidance to business partners on procurement policies, competitive bidding, contract compliance, P2P processes, PO management, and procurement best practices.

• Maintain complete procurement and contract records and ensure appropriate documentation, approvals, and audit trails are retained.

• Identify cost-saving opportunities, process improvements, risk mitigation measures, and efficiency improvements across procurement and P2P operations.

• Supporting the development, review, and implementation of procurement contract terms and conditions, and monitoring contracts to ensure compliance with contractual requirements, pricing, deliverables, service levels, renewal dates, and other obligations.

• Reviewing competitive proposals and procurement submissions against established evaluation criteria and requirements and supporting the selection and recommendation of appropriate suppliers in accordance with procurement policies and procedures.

• Posting and amending Tenders, RFPs, RFIs, and RFQs on NBON, including issuing addenda, responding to administrative procurement requirements, and coordinating updates throughout the solicitation process.

• Supporting the preparation and administration of contract amendments, extensions, renewals, and change orders, ensuring appropriate approvals and documentation are obtained before changes are implemented.

## ACCOUNTS PAYABLE

• Regulating payments including invoices, credit notes, i-Expense (travel claims), Student Refunds (domestic and International), Purchase Card transactions, Salary/Travel and Retirement advance requests, Requisitions for Payment (employee work related purchases, donations, etc.), reimbursement Expense requests, and the preparation and application of journal entries, and digital records management.

• Manage and process invoices, credit notes, iExpense claims, student refunds, P-Card transactions, employee reimbursements, payment requests, advances, and journal entries in accordance with NBCC policies and legislative requirements.

title: Graphic Design Co-op
description:

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Corporate Communications
Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia
Type of Employment: Temporary, Full-Time (Winter 2027 Co-op Term: January - April 2027)

Are you passionate about visual storytelling, creative design, and bringing ideas to life through engaging communications?

As a Graphic Design Co-op, you'll gain hands-on experience supporting creative design projects and communication initiatives that help strengthen Nova Scotia Power's brand and business objectives.

Working with our team during the Winter 2027 Co-op Term, you'll contribute to a variety of digital and print design projects while collaborating with creative professionals, communications specialists, and stakeholders across the organization. You'll help create, adapt, and maintain visual assets that support marketing, internal communications, customer-facing initiatives, and corporate campaigns, while ensuring alignment with established brand standards.

This is an excellent opportunity for students who enjoy a mix of graphic design, visual communications, multimedia content creation, and stakeholder collaboration. You'll contribute to real projects, expand your creative and technical skills, and gain valuable experience that can help launch a career in graphic design, digital media, marketing, communications, or brand management.

## What you'll do:

• Support the production of creative assets across digital and print channels, including marketing materials, internal communications, and customer-facing content.

• Create and update branded materials such as social media graphics, PowerPoint presentations, fact sheets, posters, and event collateral.

• Resize, adapt, and format campaign materials for various platforms while ensuring compliance with established brand standards and design guidelines.

• Assist with video editing activities, including trimming footage, formatting content for different channels, and incorporating revisions based on stakeholder feedback.

• Collaborate with creative and communications team members to support ongoing campaigns, initiatives, and projects across the organization.

## Who you are:

• Hands-On Learning & Development: Gain practical experience in graphic design, visual communications, brand management, multimedia content creation, creative workflows, asset management, and stakeholder review processes while receiving mentorship from experienced graphic designers and communications professionals.

title: Vice President Operations and Business Development
description:
IMP Group is a privately-held investment corporation, working to support our diverse business divisions to develop and deliver substantial value and growth in industries ranging from aerospace to healthcare. At IMP, we know our employees are central to our business success and so we cultivate and support our teams to be strategic, competitive, forward-thinking, resilient and innovative. If you are searching for a distinctive professional challenge, the exciting next step in your career is here at IMP.

The Opportunity:
Truro Cannabis, a member of IMP Group's investment portfolio, is currently seeking a highly motivated individual to join our team in the role of Vice President Operations and Business Development.

As a federally licensed producer of medical and recreational cannabis products, Truro Cannabis is proud to call Truro, Nova Scotia home. Through the operation of our 45,000 sq ft cultivation facility, we are dedicated to producing outstanding quality cannabis products in a professional and highly controlled environment. Exceptional products, practices, and policies are the backbone of Truro Cannabis, and that commitment to quality is evident in all aspects of our organization.

## Overview

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Vice President will provide enterprise-level leadership across Truro Cannabis, with accountability for strategic direction, operational performance, regulatory compliance, financial stewardship, and sustainable growth. This role will translate Board-approved objectives into clear business priorities, lead the development and execution of effective growth strategies, and ensure the Company's operations, controls, and procedures support quality, compliance, profitability, and long-term success. Working closely with department heads and internal stakeholders, the Vice President will foster alignment, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization while identifying opportunities to strengthen performance, expand commercial channels, and position the Company for future growth.

Accountabilities:
• Develop and execute the Company's mission, vision, strategic plan, and growth priorities for Board review and approval.

• Lead enterprise-wide operational performance, ensuring activities, resources, and results are aligned with Company strategy, quality standards, and business objectives.

• Ensure organizational compliance with the Cannabis Act and Regulations, including timely responses to regulatory requests, audits, examinations, and emerging regulatory developments.

• Provide financial leadership through operating budgets, capital expenditure planning, business cases, financial reporting oversight, and performance analysis to support profitability and sustainable growth.

• Review financial and non-financial performance reporting to identify risks, opportunities, solutions, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Lead commercial strategy by identifying new sales channels, strengthening customer and partner relationships, and assessing domestic and international market opportunities, including the United Kingdom, Australia, and Germany.

• Oversee production planning, inventory levels, forecasting, and corrective action to ensure operational plans support business objectives.

• Work cross-functionally with senior management, department heads, and internal stakeholders to align priorities, manage risk, improve efficiency, and drive key initiatives to completion.

• Build, lead, and develop a high-performing management team by setting clear expectations, supporting accountability, providing constructive feedback, and promoting professional development.

• Prepare timely materials, updates, and recommendations for the Board of Directors to support informed decision-making, governance responsibilities, and statutory obligations.

• Maintain current knowledge of cannabis markets, industry trends, competitive dynamics, and regulatory requirements to inform strategy and decision-making.

• Perform other responsibilities as operationally required.

Experience and Education:
• 3+ years of proven experience as a Vice President or in another senior management role with enterprise-level accountability.

• Demonstrated experience developing business strategy, translating vision into executable plans, and delivering profitable growth.

• Senior executive experience in manufacturing or consumer packaged goods is required; cannabis experience would be considered an asset but is not required.

• Strong understanding of corporate governance, financial stewardship, operational leadership, and general management best practices.

• Experience working across diverse business functions, including operations, quality assurance, finance, sales, and marketing.

• Entrepreneurial mindset with outstanding organizational, leadership, analytical, and decision-making skills.

• MBA, CPA, or other relevant advanced education or professional designation would be considered an asset.

Competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities):
• Demonstrates strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand operational performance, manage budgets, and align decisions with organizational objectives

• Excellent analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities, coupled with strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.

• Solid understanding of facility operations and associated systems.

• Proven ability to coordinate cross-functional teams, manage priorities, and communicate effectively with employees at all organizational levels.

• Exceptional organizational, planning, and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

## Requirements

The Cannabis Act requires this position to undergo security/background checks, and the individual must be approved by Health Canada as suitable (able to obtain a Health Canada Security Clearance for the role of RPIC-Responsible Person In Charge).

If you are interested in joining our exceptional team and think you have what it takes to be a pioneer in a new industry, submit your resume to us in confidence along with a cover letter to careers@trurocannabis.ca or Nick.Rowe@trurocannabis.ca .

IMP Group is committed to Employment Equity and our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative at all job levels. We welcome applicants from Aboriginal people, visible minority groups, persons with disabilities and women in occupations and positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of the equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on either your cover letter or resume.

title: Quality Assurance Analyst
description:
## Service New Brunswick

## Quality Assurance Analyst

## Pay Band 4

## Open Competition

## Multiple positions

## Flexible location within New Brunswick

## About the team

Service New Brunswick (SNB) is building a new, dynamic team to transform how we deliver IT services across the province. As one of the largest IT employers in New Brunswick, with over 700 technology professionals located across the province, we are dedicated to having an agile, client-focused approach, acting as a strategic partner to government departments, health authorities, schools, and other public sector organizations.

As one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers, we offer flexible work options—including remote, hybrid, and in-office roles—in most major cities across New Brunswick. In this role, you will play a critical part in helping us design and implement technology solutions that drive efficiency, innovation, and better service for New Brunswickers.

## Who are you?

• Client-centric and passionate about delivering exceptional service.

• Demonstrate initiative and are adaptable, organized and solution-oriented.

• Effective communicator and collaborator, and you enjoy sharing your knowledge and expertise with others.

• A strong relationship builder who genuinely cares about your clients' priorities and goals.

## What will you be doing?

The Quality Assurance Analyst will play a key role in ensuring the quality, stability, and reliability of applications. You will work closely with development, business, and support teams to provide quality assurance services. You will also actively participate in requirement reviews to identify potential defects early in the development lifecycle.

## Key Responsibilities include:

• Lead test planning and execution for projects in both Waterfall and Agile methodologies.

• Perform manual testing, including functional, regression, integration, and exploratory testing.

• Develop, execute, and maintain automated test scripts using (Ex.) Selenium and Cucumber for web and API testing.

• Ensure 100% test coverage by creating, executing, and maintaining comprehensive test cases for both manual and automated testing.

• Participate in requirement reviews to identify potential defects and ambiguities early in the project lifecycle.

• Assist with production issues by reproducing and validating reported defects and completing fix validation testing before release.

• Conduct bug triaging, working closely with developers, business analysts, and stakeholders to prioritize and resolve issues.

• Create, organize, and maintain test cases using HP Quality Center, Azure Test Plans or Zephyr Scale within Jira, ensuring full requirement traceability and structured execution cycles.

• Utilize Jira or Azure DevOps for user story and defect management, sprint tracking, reporting and cross-functional collaboration.

• Identify, log, track, and validate defects while working proactively with development teams to resolve issues.

• Execute testing activities in preparation for project releases and upgrades.

• Participate in change management reviews and approvals.

• Adhere to QA policies, procedures, and SNB methodologies to ensure software quality.

• Attend team status meetings and working group meetings as required.

• Work closely with the Quality Assurance team, Project leads, and Business leads to meet project deadlines.

## Why join SNB?

You'll have an excellent opportunity to grow, learn and make an impact as we tackle some of our client's biggest IT business challenges. Our core goals are to identify relevant and transformative digital IT solutions to support our clients in delivering business value to their customers.

At SNB, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are:

• Human-Centered: We prioritize well-being and flexibility for our employees.

• Driven by Growth: We invest in your professional development and career advancement.

• Celebrating Excellence: We recognize and reward outstanding contributions.

• United by Purpose: Every project you work on makes a real difference for New Brunswickers.

• Empowered to Decide: We trust our teams to make decisions and innovate boldly.

Join us and be part of transformational initiatives shaping the future of IT and Health services in New Brunswick.

## What do you need to be successful?

## ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS:

• A university degree in Computer Science or an equivalent field.

• At least 4 years of QA testing experience in software development environment. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

Written and spoken competence in English is required. Please state your language capability.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please state your language capability on your application and ensure that the preferred language for assessment is clearly identified.

## What qualifications can set you apart from other candidates?

ASSET QUALIFICATIONS: Preference may be given to candidates who demonstrate they have training or experience in one or more of the following areas:

• Experience as a QA Test Lead

• Experience in data confidentiality and client privacy as it pertains to application design and development.

• Experience with Structured Query Language (SQL) in a QA environment.

• Experience with HP Quality Center, Azure Test Plans or similar testing tools.

• Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and best practices.

• Experience with Azure DevOps for test case management and defect tracking.

• Experience with Selenium and Cucumber or similar tools for test automation.

• Experience with Jira or Azure Boards for user story and bug management and sprint tracking

• Experience with API testing tools such as Postman.

• Experience with performance testing and tools like LoadRunner and/or Jmeter.

• Experience with the Salesforce platform and related modules (such as Health Cloud and Community Cloud).

• Experience working with Health Care and Electronic Health Records applications.

• Completion of a Quality Assurance certification (e.g., ISTQB). Please provide proof of relevant certifications.

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

## OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Some weekday evenings and weekend work hours may be required.

• Candidates will be required to undergo Criminal History Clearance prior to appointment.

BEHAVIOURAL COMPETENCIES: The successful candidate will possess the following behavioral competencies:

• Analytical Thinking & Judgment

• Client Service Orientation

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Results Orientation

• Teamwork & Cooperation

TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES: The successful candidate will possess the following technical competencies:

• Strong leading, planning and organizing skills.

• Expertise in manual testing and test automation.

• Excellent spoken and written communication skills.

Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

Salary: $59,644 - $83,408 annually – Pay Band 4 - Management and Non-Union Pay Plan

We encourage applicants to apply online by clicking here before December 31, 2026, indicating competition number R85-2025/26-699. We will review applications periodically and candidates are encouraged to apply without delay. In the unlikely event that you experience technical difficulties or are unable to complete your application online, contact pc@snb.ca.

We thank all those who apply, however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level within the same work location.

Veterans who demonstrate they are among the most qualified, shall be given preference at the time of appointment.

title: Supervisor Court Administration & Judicial Support
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 49994

Department: Justice

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 12-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Court Services Division of the Nova Scotia Department of Justice is dedicated to excellent service and the provision of fair and accessible administration of justice, including court administration and security.
The Division provides administrative support to the courts listed: Nova Scotia Court of Appeal, Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (including Family Division), Provincial Court, Family Court, Small Claims Court, Probate Court and Bankruptcy Court. The courts act independently from the government to address individual cases.
For more information on the Department of Justice Court Services please visit our website: https://novascotia.ca/just/Court_Services/

About Our Opportunity
The Supervisor is responsible for the overall management and operation of the Court Administration Office and Judicial Support. Management and operational responsibilities in this role include effective and efficient control of human and technical resources while adhering to the applications of relevant laws, policies and procedures. As the Supervisor, you are accountable for general accounting principles, and will maintain control of accounting and banking practices used in collecting monies paid into court.
In consultation with the Court Administrator and Policy Team the Supervisor will assesses and manage staff training and career development needs. Respond to new and changing legislative, policy and operational requirements by adjusting the plan to reflect new training priorities.
The Supervisor provides technical and procedural direction in the day to day operations of a Justice Centre.
The Supervisor is responsible for providing legal information and assistance to a diverse client group, performing quasi-judicial functions as authorized by legislation, and playing a lead role in the development of policies and procedures.
In this role, you will also liaise with judges and the legal community to ensure the delivery of superior quality client service.

Primary Accountabilities
• Provide technical and procedural direction to court administration and judicial support staff

• Oversee the management and training of staff and promote a positive, healthy, safe, and secure work environment

• Make recommendations for improvements and enhancements to polices, procedures, and guidelines

• Ensure that the public and other participants in the justice system receive current and accurate legal information and assistance

• Account properly for money received into court, ensure that fees are charged in accordance with the Costs and Fees Act,

• Ensure that Occupational Health and Safety programs are followed in accordance with OH&S statues, regulations, policies and procedures, Corporate OH&S Policy and other legislative requirements

• That office areas are safe and secure, proper records classification and retention policies are followed

Qualifications and Experience
You will possess an undergraduate degree in a related discipline plus several years of related experience which includes directly managing front line staff. An equivalent combination of education/experience may be acceptable.
As the successful candidate, you will demonstrate excellent leadership skills and the ability to problem-solve using a flexible and creative approach. You will be an experienced team builder who facilitates timely service through the motivation of staff. In this fast-paced role, your ability to meet deadlines and balance priorities through careful time management is essential. Your high level of diplomacy, tact, professionalism and the ability to deal with difficult and demanding situations is key. Knowledge of an automated environment and accounting skills are essential in this role.
Familiarity with all aspects and procedures of the court systems and a thorough working knowledge of the legislation, jurisdiction and operations of the various levels of court in Nova Scotia are considered important assets.
The successful applicant must be eligible to be appointed as a staff Justice of the Peace. A valid Nova Scotia drivers' license is required.
The Government of Nova Scotia has adopted the LEADS Leadership Framework. During the interview, candidates will be expected to express how they have demonstrated the key behaviours and capabilities required to effectively lead in a caring and inclusive environment. LEADS Domains includes Leads Self, Engage Others, Achieve Results, Develop Coalitions and Systems Transformation. Please follow LEADS (novascotia.ca) for more information.
We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• May be required to work overtime and/or travel

• The courthouse is extremely busy with exposure to clients facing stressful circumstances, who may become verbally or physically abusive

• Considerable concentration is required to read, listen, interpret, and communicate information relating to court proceedings, policies, and procedures

• Considerable pressure to meet deadlines, ensure the efficient functioning of the court, as well as balancing the expectations in serving the needs of the judiciary, legal profession, public and other justice sector participants

• There is a need for constant awareness of the law and legislation policies and procedures

Additional Information
This is a permanent employment opportunity, located at the Halifax Law Courts.
An enhanced security screening may be required.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless career paths.

• A dynamic, client-focused office environment where service excellence and teamwork are our focus.

title: Director of Financial Reporting
description:
Director of Financial Reporting
Halifax, NS
Reference # HL-CLI-10199
Our client, Clarke Inc. is a leading real estate company engaged in the development, ownership, and management of a diversified portfolio of commercial, hospitality, residential, and mixed-use properties Clarke's objective is to maximize shareholder value through disciplined capital allocation, identifying undervalued or underperforming assets, and driving long-term value creation.
Clarke's real estate portfolio continues to evolve and includes significant holdings across multiple asset classes, including hotels, residential developments, office and commercial properties, and a growing investment portfolio, including:

• Over 1,400 residential units in both construction and development.

• Over 50 office and commercial properties throughout Canada, the United States and Ireland.

• 22 hotels across Canada owned or managed.

• Residential and transportation operating businesses.

• Commercial to residential conversions.

• $130M+ investment portfolio (active and passive).

We are excited to be partnering with Clarke in the search for a Director of Financial Reporting to join their team in Halifax, NS. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director of Financial Reporting will provide leadership and oversight for the Company's financial accounting and public-company financial reporting, ensuring compliance with IFRS, securities regulations, and internal control requirements.
This role is heavily focused on external financial reporting, including financial statements, disclosures, and audit coordination. Working within a lean and collaborative finance team, the Director will also contribute to valuation work, technical accounting matters, internal controls, and special projects. Candidates with an entrepreneurial, flexible mindset who are comfortable operating in a dynamic environment will be well suited to this role.
This position is full time in-office and is based out of the Bayers Lake office in Halifax, NS.
Key responsibilities include:

• Ownership of the preparation, review, and finalization of quarterly and annual financial statements, MD&A and press releases.

• Lead and manage various projects.

• Lead and mentor corporate finance and accounting personnel within a team environment.

• Responsible for all financial reporting requirements.

• Preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual Board reporting, including managing the process for preparation of board binders for the quarterly meetings.

• Review and oversee the 52-109 certification process and testing.

• Review and oversee property-level accounting across office, hotel, and residential real estate assets.

• Assistance with other value-add projects and initiatives.

• Responsible for coordination with external auditors.

• Preparation and review of various corporate department budgets and annual consolidated budgets and business plan.

• Lead complex fair value analyses on a quarterly basis, including valuation methodologies, key assumptions, third-party valuation coordination, and related disclosures.

• Lead technical accounting research and preparation of memos for complex transactions.

• Assist with business combinations, including purchase price allocations and business acquisition reports.

• Preparation, review, and finalization of the Annual Information Form (AIF).

• Other duties as required.

## The ideal candidate will possess:

• Strong financial reporting and accounting skills, with a strong knowledge of IFRS, consolidations, and public company reporting requirements, with a genuine interest in financial reporting.

• Public-company experience, or current experience in an assurance firm with a strong public-company client portfolio, strongly preferred.

• Experience in real estate or asset-intensive businesses considered a strong asset.

• Ability and desire to work autonomously on some projects while collaborating with a team on others.

• Proven leadership, forward-thinking, and decision-making skills.

• Ability to manage people, provide performance reviews, and mentor staff.

• Strong communication skills, including the ability to present insight and actionable recommendations in a concise and confident manner.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Experience with leading projects.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel.

• CPA designation required.

This is an exciting opportunity for a financial reporting professional seeking a senior, hands-on role within a growing and dynamic public company!

title: Manager Cash Management and Banking Services
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia

Department: Finance and Treasury Board

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 12-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Department of Finance and Treasury Board we strive to provide financial leadership, analysis and policies that strengthen Nova Scotia. As stewards of the province's financial affairs, we deliver a wide range of corporate fiscal and management services – including the preparation of the provincial budget, forecast updates, fiscal and tax policy, cash and debt management and administration – as well as ensure government plans are coordinated and fiscally responsible.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Director of Cash Management & Banking Services, the Manager of Cash Management & Banking Services prepares and maintains a cash forecasting system for the General Revenue Fund. They assist in the daily activities of the Cash Management section such as short-term borrowing as well as investing of surplus funds for the General Revenue Fund via the capital markets and are responsible for managing the excess funds in the Province's Public Debt Management Fund and other miscellaneous fund accounts as applicable. This position will also provide support working closely with the Cash Management Officer to identify and create efficiencies.

This position also assists with the Banking function of the Province including the review of Banking and Merchant Contracts, setup and closure of required bank and merchant accounts, coordinate to ensure all merchant account setups are PCI Compliant, facilitation of the administration of banking services for the Province of Nova Scotia, and providing support and working closely with the Banking Administrator to identify and create efficiencies.

The incumbent will be expected to keep abreast of changing financial market conditions and work with senior management for both short-term and long-term forecasting requirements, and for the maintenance of capital markets relationships. Another important function of the Manager, Cash Management and Banking Services role is to conduct ongoing credit analysis of counterparties and the monitoring of potential financial exposures of the Province of Nova Scotia as it relates to cash management and banking services. The Manager Cash Management & Banking Services is expected to perform the duties of the Director, Cash Management & Banking Services as operational requirements dictate.

The Manager Cash Management & Banking Services is also expected to contribute to the development, review, and presentation of strategic document reports, briefing materials, business cases, and executive-level presentations to support senior management decision-making and departmental priorities, when necessary.

It is also expected that the Manager provides supervision and leadership along with the Director to the Banking and Cash Management Officers.

Qualifications and Experience

They will also have at least five (5) years of experience working in the financial service industry. Experience in forecasting, financial securities, cash management and corporate banking is preferred. Knowledge of Corporate Treasury products and solutions would be considered an asset.
The Manager Cash Management and Banking Services will have advanced computer skills, strong analytical skills, prior experience with accounting principles and advanced skills with Excel and Word are essential. Advanced knowledge in Power Point and SAP also desired. Knowledge in or a strong willingness to learn Visual Basic for Application "VBA" programming is a requirement. Candidate must demonstrate how they have exercised initiative and good judgement.
Excellent interpersonal skills, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills are required. Candidates need to have high standards in accuracy, communication and the ability to prioritize tasks with minimal supervision.

title: Director of Nursing
description:
Director of Nursing $110,840-$122,372 annually, based on experience + Signing Incentive | Full-Time

Lincourt Manor Inc. | St. Stephen, New Brunswick

## About Lincourt Manor

Lincourt Manor Inc. is a 60-bed licensed nursing home serving seniors and adults with disabilities in St. Stephen, New Brunswick, conveniently located on Chipman Street next to Charlotte County Hospital. With planning underway for a new nursing home, this is an exciting time to join Lincourt Manor and contribute to the future of long-term care in the St. Stephen community. We are seeking an experienced nursing leader who excels in interpersonal relations and can successfully bridge a management role in a unionized environment.

## The Opportunity

The Director of Nursing is accountable for planning, organizing, directing, and participating in the Home's care services and for ensuring the delivery and management of high-quality nursing care to all residents in alignment with Lincourt Manor Inc.'s vision and mission. As a key member of the interdisciplinary management team, the Director of Nursing provides consistent, transparent leadership while building respectful and fair relationships between management and frontline staff.

The role requires knowledgeable stewardship within two collective agreements and compliance with applicable legislation, the Management Directives Manual, the Nurses Act (N.B.), Nursing Home Standards, and the Canadian Nurses Association Code of Ethics. The Director promotes collaborative decision-making, resident safety, staff development, and continuous improvement across the Home.

## Key Responsibilities

• Provide clinical leadership and oversight for the delivery of safe, resident-centred nursing and care services.

• Lead, support, and supervise nursing and care staff, including performance management, coaching, staff development, and competency support.

• Provide respectful, timely, and transparent clinical communication with residents, families, and Powers of Attorney (POAs), ensuring changes in health status, care needs, treatment recommendations, risks and outcomes are communicated clearly and appropriately.

• Respond to resident, family and POA concerns within the scope of the DON's authority, ensuring appropriate documentation, follow-up and timely escalation of unresolved, recurring or significant concerns to management.

• Support staffing, scheduling, and workforce planning to maintain appropriate care coverage and operational continuity.

• Ensure compliance with applicable legislation, Nursing Home Standards, professional standards, policies, and regulatory requirements.

• Lead and support quality improvement, risk management, infection prevention and control, incident review, and corrective action processes.

• Oversee clinical documentation, care practices, policies, procedures, and related nursing standards.

• Work effectively within two collective agreements and support fair, consistent labour and employee relations practices.

• Collaborate with residents, families, physicians, pharmacy, allied health professionals, government partners, and other service providers.

• Participate as a key member of the management team and contribute to organizational planning, problem-solving, and continuous improvement.

## Qualifications

• Baccalaureate degree in Nursing, or an equivalent combination of nursing education and relevant experience. Additional education or training in administration and/or health care management is considered an asset.

• Minimum of three years of relevant supervisory experience.

• Current registration, or eligibility for registration, with the Nurses Association of New Brunswick (NANB).

• Strong leadership, communication, interpersonal, and conflict-resolution skills, with a high level of emotional intelligence.

• Demonstrated ability to lead collaboratively and make fair, consistent, and well-informed decisions.

• Experience in long-term care, gerontology, and/or a unionized health care environment is considered an asset.

• Demonstrated ability to interpret and apply legislation, regulatory requirements, standards, and organizational policies within a health care environment.

## Conditions of Employment

• Satisfactory criminal record check clearance.

• Satisfactory Social Development check.

• Maintain current registration and good standing with the Nurses Association of New Brunswick (NANB) throughout employment.

## What We Offer

Lincourt Manor Inc. offers a competitive total rewards package and a signing incentive, including:

• Dental care

• Extended health care

• Life insurance

• Vision care

• Paid time off

• New Brunswick Nursing Home Management Pension Plan

• Wellness program

• On-site parking

• Professional development opportunities, subject to availability and funding

## Why Lincourt Manor

This is an opportunity for an experienced nursing leader to make a meaningful impact in a close-knit long-term care environment, working alongside an established management team to support quality resident care, staff development and continuous improvement. With planning underway for a new nursing home, the successful candidate will also join Lincourt Manor at an exciting time in its continued growth and service to the St. Stephen community.

## How to Apply

Interested and qualified candidates are invited to submit a resume and cover letter to shatt@practicalhrs.com by Friday, October 30, 2026.

We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from all qualified candidates. We are committed to employment practices that are free from discrimination and consistent with the New Brunswick Human Rights Act.

title: Physiotherapist
description:
About the Windsor Elms Village (Falmouth, NS): Windsor Elms Village is an Eden Registered Home with a resident-directed philosophy of care. It builds on a rich history and reflects our commitment to continue to evolve to meet the emerging needs of seniors in Nova Scotia. We will continue to embrace life, provide compassionate support and encourage meaningful relationships with residents, families, staff and the community. We are creating a home environment, which is eco-friendly and lowering our carbon footprint, where residents can continue to grow and experience the fullness of life.

Creating a Sense of Home: We are home to 108 residents. At Windsor Elms Village there are three distinct neighbourhoods. Each neighbourhood has four houses of nine residents. With such a diverse group of residents, you will find each house has its own character. At WEV, we strive to create flexibility that mirrors life in the communities and homes our residents have known.

Physiotherapist:

We are seeking a full time Physiotherapist to work in our home located in Falmouth, NS

As our Physiotherapist, you will be assessing and treating residents who are referred to PT for care and establishing a treatment program and/or recommendations. Key functions of the role include the following:

· Maintaining communication with the care team, attending physician and other health disciplines.

· Educating residents and their families and the care team with regards to the condition and the PT intervention.

· Perform clinical assessments, set goals and provide treatment plans for Residents.

· Initiate appropriate treatment intervention based on clinical assessment.

· Provide on-going evaluation of resident progress. Administer and collect outcome measurement information.

· Participate in orientating new care partners and students and be a mentor/preceptor for therapy students.

· Deliver interventions for individual residents , or groups of residents, in areas of physical or functional skills such as carrying our mobility and strengthening exercises.

· Exercises sound judgement in the delivery of prescribed treatments to the residents

· Request and accommodate resident's individual choices whenever possible .

· Encourage and support residents to maintain or regain their independence

· Provide explanations to residents. Negotiate with residents when requests cannot be met.

· Support relationships that are central to the residents.

· Work to create a culture of safety for all.

As a Physiotherapist within our team, you are committed to alleviating the three plagues of loneliness, helplessness, and boredom. This is based on the Eden philosophy, our Guiding Principles, and our established policies and procedures. You will strive to create a positive and pleasant environment in the Resident's home by working collaboratively and respectfully with all care partners including residents, co-workers, families, physicians, community and professional agencies. Being a resilient team player with strong leadership/mentoring skills, you will strive to enhance and strengthen the groups and individuals who live and work at the Windsor Elms Village.

As an important member of our team -- working with all care partners - you do what it takes to enrich relationships and well-being for residents.

Qualifications:

· Degree in Physiotherapy or equivalent from a recognized school of Physiotherapy.

· Current registration with the Nova Scotia College of Physiotherapy and eligibility for membership in the Canadian Physiotherapy Association.

· Ability to communicate well with Residents , their families and care partners.

· Preferred experience with geriatrics as well as working with physically and/cognitively impaired residents

· Preferred Alzheimer's Course & PIECES Training considered an asset

· Current First Aid & CPR Certification

· Clear Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check

Special Notices regarding Pension Plan

The Windsor Elms is an active participating employer with Nova Scotia Employees' Pension Plan (NSHEPP). If you are a member of NSHEPP, your pension is portable to Windsor Elms Village.

Interested in applying?

Windsor Elms offers a competitive compensation package and a work environment where teamwork and individual contributions are valued. Submit a resume to Tanya.carey@winelms.ca or fax 902-798-3302.

title: Senior Manager, Organizational Change Management
description:

This role sets the vision, strategy, methodology, and standards for how change is led, governed, and embedded into the organization—advancing readiness, adoption, and long?term cultural and behavioral shifts.

As a Senior Manager within Business Transformation, you will oversee a high?performing OCM team, influence executive decision?making, and shape how employees and leaders navigate change. You will strengthen organizational change capability, drive alignment across business functions, and ensure transformation initiatives deliver measurable business value.

## OCM Excellence & Service Delivery

• Experience developing strategies, managing budgets, and leading teams.

• Exceptional communication skills, including facilitation and executive presentations.

• Professional certifications such as; Prosci, Certified Change Management Professional (CCMP), Project Management Professional (PMP), Agile, Lean, Human Centered Design, Adult Education are highly desirable.

We understand that experience comes in many forms, and we're dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we've listed above, please consider applying. Have a question or want to learn more about this opportunity? Contact Danielle.Boutilier@emera.com.

title: Product Manager, Destination
description:
## Join Our Team as a Product Manager, Destination at Atlantic Lottery!

In this role, you'll lead the strategy, roadmap, and performance of products and experiences within Atlantic Lottery's Destination portfolio. You'll leverage customer insights, player behaviour, market trends, operational knowledge, and data-driven decision making to identify opportunities, enhance player experiences, optimize portfolio performance and deliver meaningful customer and business outcomes.

Working closely with teams across Product, Marketing, Technology, Analytics, Operations, and external partners, you'll guide products through their full lifecycle, from concept and planning to launch and ongoing optimization. This role is ideal for a strategic, collaborative, and results-oriented professional who enjoys solving complex challenges, aligning diverse stakeholders, and delivering value through strategic product leadership.

## Why Join Our Team?

• Shape the future of Atlantic Lottery's Destination product experience through strategic product leadership.

• Influence business decisions using customer insights, analytics, and market intelligence.

• Collaborate with diverse teams across the organization to bring innovative ideas to life.

• Make a meaningful impact by delivering products and experiences that drive value for players and Atlantic Canadians.

Application Deadline: October 20, 2026.

Qualifications
Education and Experience:

• Bachelor's degree or diploma in Business, Marketing, or a related field. Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.

• 5+ years of experience in product management, brand management, digital product delivery, gaming, eCommerce, or another customer-focused environment.

• Demonstrated experience developing product strategies, roadmaps, and business plans while delivering measurable business results.

• Experience using customer insights, data, and analytics to make strategic business decisions.

• Experience leading multiple initiatives and influencing outcomes across cross-functional teams.

• Must be 19 years of age or older and reside in Atlantic Canada.

Professional Skills:

• Strategic thinking and strong business acumen.

• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management abilities.

• Ability to influence and build relationships across multiple functions and levels of an organization.

• Strong planning and prioritization skills with the ability to manage competing demands.

• Comfortable navigating ambiguity and driving clarity in evolving environments.

Assets:

• Experience working with digital platforms, customer experience initiatives, or omnichannel products.

• Experience in gaming, hospitality, entertainment, retail, financial services, or other regulated industries.

• Familiarity with Agile delivery practices and technology-enabled product development.

## Work Location & Flexibility

This role may be based out of one of our Atlantic Canadian offices: Moncton, NB; Halifax, NS; or St. John's, NL. Moncton is preferred for onboarding.

• During probation: Full-time, in-office (Moncton preferred for onboarding)

• After probation: Choice of full-time in-office or hybrid (2-3 days per week onsite)

## Compensation

• Salary Band: $75,200 - $122,200

• Candidates can expect to start around $79,900, with placement dependent on experience, skills, market conditions, and internal equity

## AL Benefits

• Extended health coverage (medical, dental, vision)

• Basic life insurance and disability coverage

• Defined Benefit Pension Plan

• Three weeks' vacation annually (pro‑rated), 13 paid statutory holidays, and a vacation purchase program

• Wellness support, including wellness programs, 3 personal care days, and a 24/7 Employee & Family Assistance Program

• Two paid volunteer days per year

• Career advancement opportunities

## Recruitment Process

We've made meaningful enhancements to our hiring practices in recent years. Our typical recruitment process includes:

• Two in‑person interviews

• An assignment and/or scenario‑based questions

• Behavioral or cognitive assessments

• Verification of relevant certifications (as applicable)

All interviews are conducted in English, our primary working language, unless otherwise specified.

Only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Successful candidates will undergo reference checks and a mandatory criminal background check. Additional financial, educational, or credential verifications may be required depending on the role.

## Role Commitment

To support employee development, business continuity, and knowledge transfer, individuals who accept this position are expected to remain in the role for a minimum of 18 months before being eligible to apply for or transfer to another position within Atlantic Lottery.

This expectation applies to both external hires and employees moving into the role from another position.

## Internal Candidates

Internal applicants must be in good standing, including meeting expectations on their most recent performance review, and must not be on probation. Consideration may also include factors such as performance improvement plans, disciplinary actions, attendance, and completion of mandatory training.

A Predictive Index (PI) assessment will be completed or shared with the hiring leader as part of the evaluation process.

## Internal Recruitment Considerations

For internal recruitment processes, preference may be given to employees currently occupying regular or term positions with AL. Selection decisions will consider business needs, approved staffing requirements, organizational headcount parameters, qualifications, and overall fit for the role.

## Eligibility to Work in Canada

Candidates must have all required work permits, visas, and authorizations and be eligible to work in Canada at the time an offer is made. It is the candidate's responsibility to secure these requirements.

Atlantic Lottery welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada. Atlantic Lottery is not participating in the Temporary Foreign Worker (Labour Market Impact Assessment) Program, Provincial Nominee Programs, or the Atlantic Immigration Program at this time. Support for any other immigration programs for new hires is subject to internal policies, operational needs, and program restrictions and is not guaranteed.

Responsibilities
What You'll Do:

• Develop and execute product strategies, roadmaps, and plans that support player engagement, business growth, and organizational objectives.

• Own the full product lifecycle, from opportunity identification and planning through launch, optimization, and ongoing performance evaluation.

• Use customer insights, player data, industry trends, and market research to identify opportunities and inform product decisions.

• Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including product and financial performance, using data and analytics to measure success, identify opportunities, and prioritize improvements.

• Develop business cases and recommendations for product, technology, and capital investments based on expected customer and business outcomes.

• Lead cross-functional initiatives by partnering with Technology, Marketing, Analytics, Operations, vendors, and external stakeholders to deliver product outcomes.

• Balance customer needs, business objectives, operational considerations, Healthy Play, and regulatory requirements when making product recommendations and prioritization decisions.

• Build alignment across business, technology, operations, marketing, analytics, and external partners by communicating product priorities, performance, opportunities, and strategic direction.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees and customers feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers and communities in which we live and serve. If you require an accommodation for the recruitment/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, or accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations), please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

title: Accounting Clerk II
employer: Newfoundland and Labrador Legal Aid Commission
description:
Legal Aid NL is an innovative legal aid plan that responds to the needs of low income persons by promoting access to justice through the provision of quality legal assistance for criminal, family and some administrative law matters. Services are provided through a staff based delivery model via the twelve full service offices and five project offices in the province.

We are currently seeking an Accounting Clerk II to fill a contractual position with our accounting team in the Provincial Director's Office. The successful candidate will report to the Finance Manager and will be a member of a team responsible for performing a number of legal, administrative and human resources support functions within in the Accounting Department.

The Accounting Clerk II is responsible for a variety of financial accounting work in relation to Legal Aid's financial management system (Sage) including entering and editing a high level of invoices ensuring policies, procedures, and controls are followed; preparing payments for release as required; preparing journal entries and accruals as necessary; reconciling and verifying invoices for payment; procurement and purchasing; administrative work for human resources and establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with co-workers, regulatory agencies, suppliers, vendors, clients, and the general public; assisting with knowledge sharing, mentoring and training of co-workers and new employees as requested; preparing reports for management as needed. Other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications for this position are normally acquired through completion of two-year Business Diploma Program combined with 2 - 4 years of relevant experience in an accounting role. Other combinations of related experience and training in financial accounting may be considered. Proficiency with Sage 300 or other accounting software and a general knowledge and understanding of accepted accounting principles is required. Candidates must be proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Power Point. The successful candidate must also have the ability to process a large volume of transactions with excellent attention to detail, and a high degree of accuracy. Experience in payroll processing would be as asset. Candidates should also have demonstrated ability to organize work, set priorities and meet deadlines is a must as well as the ability to work well under pressure and adapt to changing work environments and competing demands.

The successful applicant will be required to provide a Certificate of Conduct with Vulnerable Sector Check prior to commencement of employment.

Employees of the Newfoundland and Labrador Legal Aid Commission are covered under the Provincial Government Pension Plan and Health Plan. An optional Dental Plan and Disability Plan are also available. The salary range for this position is $45,554.60 to $50,414.00.

Interested candidates should submit cover letter and resumes no later than 4pm on Friday October 9th, 2026 to HumanResources@legalaid.nl.ca.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Applicants may be considered for similar openings that arise within 6 months of the closing date.

title: Team Lead, Disability Support Program
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50038

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

Location: SYDNEY

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 12-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services (ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and Disability Support Program(DSP).
The Disability Support Program (DSP) is committed to fostering innovative ways to empower individuals with disabilities to pursue their vision of a fulfilling life. We are on a journey to implement international best practices that uphold human rights and choice to enhance the way people engage with their communities. We envision Nova Scotia as a place where people with disabilities can choose the life they want to live, in communities that are welcoming, inclusive, and supportive. A life where individuals can build authentic relationships, explore their interests, and achieve their full potential as valued citizens in their community.

About Our Opportunity
We're hiring a DSP Team Lead to lead their team in day-to-day operations and support the implementation of the new community-based program. This new framework is a critical aspect of the Human Rights Remedy, addressing systemic discrimination against persons with disabilities.
Reporting to the Regional HUB Manager within DSP, the Team Leads are responsible for supporting DSP Programs, recruiting, managing, and partnering with community members to maximize opportunities for inclusion. Many aspects of this community-based framework are new and as Team Lead, you must be adept at guiding teams through ambiguity, creating safe spaces, and excel in developing effective partnerships.

Primary Accountabilities
As Team Lead, you will be responsible for leading a dedicated team and ensuring the delivery of high-quality, inclusive, and human-centred programs within their region, including:

• Managing the delivery of Disability Support Programs; ensuring regional needs are met

• Providing recommendations for program improvements and monitoring their delivery and evaluation.

• Full responsibility for the recruitment, selection, and onboarding of their team members, as well as the discipline, performance management and grievance procedures.

• Leading your team through change, providing coaching, performance management, conflict resolution, and professional development.

• Mentoring your team to achieve the short-term and long-term priorities of the department.

• Building and nurturing partnerships within communities including leading the promotion of local and people-centre services and developing leadership of persons with disabilities in the ongoing improvement of DSP Programs.

• Championing inclusivity and a human-centred approaches in all aspects of your work.

• Fostering authentic professional relationships in both the workplace and within community.

Qualifications and Experience
Completed post-secondary education in Management, Social Sciences, Disability Supports, Human/ Social Services or Health Care Related fields, plus several years of related experience. An equivalent combination of training and experience will be considered.
You possess a genuine passion for people and human rights, fostering a positive, strengths-based, person-centered culture. You have several years of related experience in the implementation of disability services and programs, combined with team leadership experience.
You must also demonstrate:

• Strong relationship management skills to partner with the community members and within your local area to develop and implement individual-specific services.

• Leadership skills to help your team navigate through changes aligning with the new DSP framework.

• Collaborative work experience to work alongside other Team Leads in maintaining equitable and standardized process for selection, onboarding, coaching and management of team members.

• Skills in interpreting information, particularly pertaining to the DSP remedy, and providing expert guidance for program delivery and compliance.

• Excellent interpersonal skills and empathy for conflict resolution and navigation in ambiguous situations.

• Understanding of the challenging circumstances faced by individuals with disabilities and mental health conditions, and an awareness of the compounded impact of intersectionality on their experiences.

While not required, the following are considered assets:

• experience in leading teams through change

• management experience in a unionized environment

• experience in grievance procedures

• certification in Project Management

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Most of your work is in a central office environment with frequently required travel to various locations across the province. You will work in Sydney, but you will also be expected to travel to Port Hawkesbury to support staff there as well.

This role places considerable mental pressure on the individual, requiring high personal resiliency to meet emotional demands. You will navigate complex situations, working with individuals through potentially emotional or stressful times in their lives. This environment underscores the importance of adaptability and emotional resilience.

Additional Information
You must have the ability to travel frequently within and occasionally outside of your region.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace: our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless career paths.

Pay Grade: EC 10

Salary Range: $3,247.28 - $4,059.12 Bi-Weekly

The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your electronic application.
