If you require an accommodation throughout the recruitment process, please contact us at competitions@novascotia.ca.

The Court Services Division of the Nova Scotia Department of Justice is dedicated to excellent service and the provision of fair and accessible administration of justice, including court administration and security.
The Division provides administrative support to the courts listed: Nova Scotia Court of Appeal, Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (including Family Division), Provincial Court, Family Court, Small Claims Court, Probate Court and Bankruptcy Court. The Justice Officer 4 case manages high-volume and often high conflict cases and performs the quasi-judicial functions of a Prothonotary or Registrar of Probate as set out in the legislation and rules that govern the Courts, including, but not limited to the Civil Procedure Rules, Probate Act and Court Officials Act. title: Project Manager
description:
Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, South America and Australia. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

Cooke is continuing to deliver technology-enabled change across its global operations, supporting growth, efficiency, and operational excellence. As a Project Manager, you play a key role in translating business priorities into well-executed initiatives that deliver measurable outcomes.

## The Role

As a Project Manager, you independently manage IT initiatives from initiation through close-out. You apply Agile, Waterfall, or Hybrid delivery approaches as appropriate and work closely with Business Analysts, IT delivery teams, business stakeholders, and vendors to ensure projects are delivered within scope, schedule, and budget. This role is well-suited to an emerging project management professional looking to deepen their delivery skills within a structured PMO environment.

## Key Responsibilities

• Plan and manage small-to-medium projects, including scope, schedules, resources, budgets, and forecasts.

• Apply Agile, Waterfall, or Hybrid delivery methods with confidence, adapting approach to project needs.

• Facilitate requirements clarification and delivery planning with Business Systems Analysts and stakeholders.

• Monitor and manage risks, issues, dependencies, and change activities throughout the project lifecycle.

• Track project financials, monitor variances, and support forecasting and budget alignment.

• Coordinate delivery across IT teams, business partners, and third-party vendors.

• Prepare and deliver clear project status updates, dashboards, and reports for stakeholders and leadership.

• Ensure project documentation meets PMO governance and quality standards.

• Support benefits tracking and ensure alignment to business objectives.

• Contribute to PMO continuous improvement through lessons learned and process refinement.

## What Success Looks Like

• Projects are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned to business outcomes.

• Risks and issues are identified early and managed proactively.

• Stakeholders are well-informed and engaged throughout delivery.

• Project data, schedules, and documentation are accurate and reliable.

• You demonstrate growth toward proficient project leadership.

## Core Skills & Competencies

• Project planning, execution, and delivery fundamentals.

• Agile, Waterfall, and Hybrid delivery methodologies.

• Risk, issue, dependency, and change management.

• Project financial tracking and forecasting.

• Stakeholder communication and facilitation.

• Strong organization, prioritization, and time management.

## Behaviors That Drive Success

• Accountability - Take ownership of delivery outcomes.

• Collaboration - Work effectively across cross-functional teams.

• Adaptability - Adjust delivery approach to project needs.

• Outcome Driven - Focus on delivering measurable value.

• Growth Mindset - Actively develop project management skills.

## Experience & Qualifications

• 2-4 years of experience coordinating or managing projects in an IT or business environment.

• Practical experience applying Agile, Waterfall, or Hybrid methodologies.

• Working knowledge of budgeting, forecasting, and resource planning at the project level.

• Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience).

• Hands-on experience with project management and collaboration tools such as Monday.com, MS Project, Excel, Microsoft Teams, and SharePoint.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

## Benefits Package:

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• Support Services: Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Time Off: Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave for work-life balance.

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

• Convenience: On-site parking or parking allowance.

If you're looking to join a supportive team environment with opportunities for personal and professional development, apply now and become part of our dynamic team.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness, and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

title: Human Trafficking Navigator (Victim Services Navigator) (Designated)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50020

Department: Justice

Location: SYDNEY

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 12-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

Designation Status
This opportunity is designated to applicants that are or identify as Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Inuit, or Métis).
See the Nova Scotia Government's Employment Equity Policy for more information, including additional details on the designated groups.

About Us
The Justice Supports and Services Division of the Department of Justice consists of three programs: each providing Nova Scotians access to critical programming and support. The Maintenance Enforcement Program helps to facilitate the payment of court-ordered child and spousal support; the NS Restorative Justice Program provides opportunities for those harmed by crime, the person who caused the harm and the communities affected to communicate (directly or indirectly) about the causes, circumstances, and impact of that crime, and to address their related needs. Victim Services offers support to victims of crime as their case moves through the justice system.
Within Victim Services we offer a range of services to help victims of crime, promote victims' rights and interests and advise government on issues relating to victims of crime; and work with justice partners and the community to develop policies and programs that address the needs of crime victims. We can help provide the victim, spouse, or relative, with information, support and assistance as their case moves through the criminal justice system. When criminal charges are laid, victims and family members can contact us directly for help. We provide the following programs: Provincial Victim Services Program, Child Victim/Witness Program, Criminal Injuries Counselling Program, Victim Impact Statement Program, Restitution Program and the Sexual Offense Legal Representation Program.

About Our Opportunity
The Victim Services Officer is responsible for delivering the Provincial Victim Services Program, in accordance with the rights of victims of crime as outlined in the Victim's Rights and Services Act, the Criminal Code of Canada and the victim-related provisions of other federal and provincial statutes, including the Victim Bill of Rights.
In this position, you support survivors and families of human trafficking and sexual exploitation. Responsibilities include: maintaining an effective communication network with Justice, community and government officials at the regional level, coordinating services for victims of crime within the criminal justice system and the community, monitoring and recommending intervention strategies to address identified gaps in service at the community level, supporting victims for access to justice, and providing referrals to culturally appropriate resources.

Primary Accountabilities
• You will ensure the confidentiality of client information and maintain a caseload of highly sensitive files and provide support to help meet clients needs and provide referrals to specialists as needed.

• Ensure client service information is accurately entered in the Victim Services case management system

• Assess risk and communicates information in accordance with the High-Risk Domestic Violence Case Coordination Protocol framework and program policy and procedures.

• Collaborate with other government and community organizations, community outreach, navigation, and support.

• Work with other organizations to provide culturally specific supports and services that meet the needs of survivors and families of human trafficking and sexual exploitation.

• Collaborate with African Nova Scotian and Indigenous communities to understand the historic complexities of sexual violence within marginalized and other vulnerable communities and survivors of human trafficking.

• Maintain knowledge of all relevant legislation, and applicable policies and procedures.

• Promote diversity through ongoing education, communication and support to colleagues, victims, and families.

• Participate in human trafficking and sexual exploitation initiatives, committees, training and outreach.

Qualifications and Experience
You possess a bachelor's degree (typically in the Social Sciences) and three years' related experience. An equivalent combination of education, training and experience will be considered. Related experience includes (but is not limited to) providing client services in the community.
In this role, you are required to have experience in client assessment and interviewing techniques, as well as case management and computer skills. Your knowledge of the criminal justice system and community resources, the Victims' Rights and Services Act, the Criminal Code of Canada, and the Canadian Victims Bill of Rights is essential.
In addition, you understand the complexities of human trafficking and sexual exploitation and the traumatic impacts of both survivors and families of those who have experienced human trafficking and sexual exploitation. You have experience in working with individuals who have been human trafficked/ sexually exploited and with vulnerable populations.
Furthermore, you have excellent oral and written communication skills, good organizational ability and strong interpersonal skills including the ability to work as part of a team. You demonstrate empathy, warmth and tact along with an in-depth understanding of human dynamics and the effects of victimization. Sound judgment and the ability to work with self-confidence and decisiveness are also important in this role.
A high level of judgement, independent decision-making and discretion is required, in accordance with the policies and procedures and best practices set out by the division.
Access to reliable transportation is required as you will be responsible for travel to multiple locations in your coverage area.
The ability to speak French would be considered an asset.
The above qualifications will be assessed using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Include, but are not limited to:

• A Bachelor's degree in a related field and a Master's degree in a related field and one year of related experience

• A two-year certificate/diploma in a related field plus five year's related experience

• A one-year certificate/diploma in a related field plus six year's related experience

• Seven year's experience working in a related field with no formal training

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• There will be a need for flexibility in working hours.

• May be required to work overtime on occasion.

• Stressful work environment given extensive exposure to human trafficking and sexual exploitation cases.

• Sitting at a computer for long periods of time.

• Mentally challenging due to a high demand for accuracy and attention to detail with a high volume of work.

• Potential for both physical and non-physical violence from hostile clients and offenders.

• Possible exposure to domestic disturbances and aggressive attitudes towards government officials.

• Travel is required to attend meetings and offer services in courts and clients' communities.

Additional Information
This is a permanent employment opportunity, located in Sydney, NS.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

Pay Grade: PR 12

Salary Range: $2,698.22 - $3,273.84 Bi-Weekly

title: Certified Mobile Crane Operator
description:
## About the Role:

As a Certified Mobile Hoist/Mobile Crane Operator in the aquaculture support industry, you will play a critical role in the safe and efficient handling of heavy materials and equipment essential to our marine operations team. Your expertise will ensure that large components and commodities are moved, lifted, and positioned with precision, directly impacting the quality and timeliness of our marine operations. You will collaborate closely with dispatch, site managers and personnel, vessel captains, and safety personnel to coordinate lifts and maintain compliance with all safety regulations and company policies. This role demands a high level of technical skill, situational awareness, and adherence to safety standards to prevent accidents and equipment damage. Ultimately, your work will contribute to maintaining a smooth workflow and supporting the overall productivity and success of our marine sites in the southern NB area.

## Minimum Qualifications:

• Valid certification as a Mobile Crane/Mobile Hoist Operator recognized in NB.

• Minimum of 3 years of experience operating mobile hoists and/or mobile cranes independently.

• Comprehensive knowledge of hoist/crane operation safety standards and regulations.

• Ability to read and interpret load charts and rigging requirements.

• Physical ability to perform the duties of the role, including climbing, lifting, and working in various weather conditions.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience working in the aquaculture industry and in particular on wharves

• Additional certifications related to rigging or heavy equipment operation.

• Familiarity with computerized crane control systems and telematics.

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment.

## Responsibilities:

• Operate mobile hoists/cranes to lift, move, and position heavy materials and equipment in various situations and locations.

• Conduct pre-operation inspections and routine maintenance checks on hoist/crane equipment to ensure safety and functionality.

• Collaborate with riggers and ground personnel to plan and execute lifts safely and efficiently.

• Adhere strictly to all safety protocols, industry regulations, and company policies during crane operations.

• Maintain accurate records of crane usage, inspections, and any incidents or maintenance performed.

• Respond promptly to operational needs and adjust crane positioning as required to support operational processes.

• Participate in safety meetings and training sessions to stay current with best practices and regulatory changes.

## Skills:

The required skills enable the operator to safely and efficiently maneuver heavy loads, ensuring precise placement that supports operational workflows. Strong communication and teamwork skills are essential for coordinating with riggers and other personnel to execute lifts without incident. The ability to interpret technical documents such as load charts and rigging plans ensures that lifts are planned and conducted within safe operational limits. Preferred skills, such as familiarity with aquaculture-based needs and challenges, enhance operational efficiency and safety. Additionally, safety certifications and experience in the Heavy lift environment contribute to a proactive approach to hazard identification and mitigation, fostering a culture of safety and reliability.

title: Administrative Support - Health Services
description:
## Work Remotely Anywhere in the Province of New Brunswick

WorkSafeNB is seeking to fill a one-year full-time casual assignment of Administrative Support – Health Services.

Reporting to the Manager, Business Operations, the Administrative Support – Health Services coordinates prescription requests across New Brunswick, acting as a liaison between clients, pharmacies, and Nurse Consultants. They gather medication details, process special authorizations, and issue drug rejection letters, ensuring compliance with policies and Nurse Consultant guidance.
Administrative Support – Health Services oversee Independent Medical Examination (IME) referrals, managing provider allocations and ensuring compliance with procurement guidelines. They handle client communications, assist with Long-Term Disability (LTD) questionnaires, process Age 65 notifications, and follow up on medical information requests from healthcare providers. The role also involves coordinating travel for medical appointments, booking transportation and accommodations, and submitting travel advance requests. Through efficient communication and administrative support, they help case managers and teams deliver exceptional client service.

## Salary and Hours of Work:

• Hours of work are those required to perform the assigned tasks but shall not be less than 35 hours per week, 7 hours per day. Monday to Friday between 8:00-5:00 PM.

• The hourly rate for this position is $28.53 to $32.49. CUPE 1866 employees receive Step 1 of the pay band for the position appointment.

## Responsibilities

• Handle incoming and outgoing calls to assist clients, service providers, pharmacies, co-workers, and case managers with administrative and medical-related requests. Gather client information for medications and medical reports to ensure accurate and up-to-date file management.

• Prepare and send drug rejection letters on behalf of the claim owner, ensuring all relevant policies, legislation, and supporting rationale provided by a Nurse Consultant are included. Act as the primary liaison between clients, pharmacies, service providers, and Nurse Consultants, ensuring clear and timely communication regarding prescription requests, drug authorizations, rejections, and medical information updates.

• Oversee and track the Independent Medical Examination (IME) referral process, including handling service provider invitations, tracking awards, and ensuring accurate document uploads. Maintain detailed records in a complex Excel spreadsheet while serving as the liaison between case managers, clients, and service providers.

• Engage with a roster of potential service providers and allocate referrals in accordance with procurement processes and the master service agreement. Administer and monitor the two-stage competitive process for fairly awarding IME referrals, ensuring compliance with procurement guidelines and selection criteria.

• Assist clients with completing LTD questionnaires and respond to their inquiries. Send Age 65 letters three months before benefits cease, reviewing prescription lists to determine if funding requests should be forwarded to Nurse Consultants. Conduct SF-36 and QPD questionnaires verbally with clients and submit them for review to assess medication funding eligibility.

• Responsible for sending medical information requests to Service Providers (e.g., Physicians, Hospitals, Chiropractors, Physiotherapists) and following up to ensure timely receipt of the required documentation.

• Arrange travel logistics for clients attending medical appointments, including hotel reservations, taxi services, flights, and ferry arrangements. Communicate with clients and service providers to finalize plans and submit travel advance requests to the Benefits Payments Department. Ensure case managers and clients receive timely updates on travel arrangements.

• Other duties may be assigned as needed or based on operational requirements

## Qualifications

• A one (1) year post-secondary diploma or certificate in medical health services, office administration, business, health services or a related field.

• Minimum of one (1) year of experience in a clerical, administrative, or customer service role, preferably within healthcare, insurance, or a workers' compensation environment. Proven experience delivering client-focused support, including clear communication, problem-solving, and coordination with pharmacies, healthcare providers, or insurance representatives for prescription requests and special authorizations. Familiarity with claims processing, case management support, workforce re-entry, and pensions or long-term disability (LTD) programs, including knowledge of relevant policies, procedures, and applicable legislation.

• Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams), SharePoint, Adobe Acrobat Pro, Case Management systems, and the Automated Benefits Claims Center (ABCC) to support documentation, communication, and workflow coordination.

• Knowledgeable in Claims Management processes, including Workforce Re-entry, Pensions, and Long-Term Disability, with a strong understanding of related systems, policies, and applicable legislation.

• Familiar with medication approvals, special authorizations, and collaboration with pharmacies and healthcare providers.

• Understanding of Independent Medical Examination (IME) referral processes, compliance standards, and accurate record-keeping protocols.

An equivalent combination of greater education, combined with less work experience may be considered.

## Competencies:

• Adaptability

• Ensuring Accountability

• Teamwork and Collaboration

• Client-focused Service

• Information Gathering and Processing

• Digital Literacy

• Resilience

• Information Management

• Problem Solving

• Analytical Thinking

## Written and spoken competence in English and French is required.

Your primary workspace will be from your in-home office, with the occasional expectation of in person meetings, for that reason, working from outside the province or country is not permissible.

If you are interested in pursuing this opportunity with WorkSafeNB, please apply online at www.worksafenb.ca by October 14, 2026.

We thank all those who apply however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

For more information about WorkSafeNB, or this and other employment opportunities, please visit our website at worksafenb.ca.

## About Us

The team at WorkSafeNB is passionate about promoting health and safety in New Brunswick workplaces. We strive to make New Brunswick the safest place to work. However, injuries do occur, and when they do, we are committed to providing caring recovery and return to work services, benefits, and compensation to injured workers and their families. Culture is the heartbeat of the organization. The stronger it is, the further we go! Selected by our employees, our WorkSafeNB values shape our culture. We put our values of Accountability, Collaboration and Trust into ACTion. We demonstrate accountability by taking pride in and ownership of our work so we can take care of our clients and other New Brunswickers. Through collaboration, we build strong partnerships and innovate to achieve better outcomes. Trust guides our organization; we lead and listen with empathy and embrace diversity, inclusion and belonging. These ACTions shape us.

Closing Date: Open until filled.

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

We are currently seeking an IT Systems Analyst to join our Information Technology team based in the Firm's Halifax, NS office.

Type of Position: Full-Time, Permanent

Closing Date: Monday, October 12th, 2026

## The Opportunity:

An integral member of the Firm's Information Technology Team, the IT Systems Analyst will be responsible for administering, analyzing, and testing various IT technologies and solutions. This role requires a curious, inquisitive, and proactive IT professional who shows initiative and seeks opportunities to expand their area of understanding within the field.

In particular, the IT Systems Analyst will provide administration & support for various systems, applications, and cloud solutions including the Firm's document management system, and Office 365, as well as create and administer servers in a virtual environment. Additionally, they will manage document security utilizing ethical wall platforms, and will participate in monthly maintenance outside of standard working hours.

The successful candidate will perform analysis and administration of Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services including AD objects, permissions, authorization / authentication, domain controllers, security, DNS and DHCP services, and Group Policy testing, deployment, and troubleshooting.

The IT Systems Analyst will take ownership of system support tickets, and assist in vetting, researching, resolving, or escalating them as appropriate. Using monitoring tools to ensure ongoing health of IT systems, they will act on service-affecting notifications in a timely fashion. This role will also work with vendors on projects deploying and supporting new solutions. Additional responsibilities of the IT Systems Analyst include assisting with IT security-related tasks, client audits and RFPs, as well as various other projects and duties as assigned - all while ensuring adherence to the Firm's Administrative IT Security Policy and User & Network Security Policy.

If you are a results-driven IT professional with a passion for analyzing and optimizing systems to enhance organizational efficiency, we want to hear from you! The successful candidate will have a degree or diploma in Information Technology and 2+ years of experience administering Windows servers, Active Directory, Office 365, network applications, and virtualized environments, with knowledge of VMware, including Vcenter, VM Lifecycle, ESXi, Snapshots and Vmotion technologies.

The successful candidate is required to work predominantly in-person at our Halifax, NS office during their first couple of months with the Firm. Afterwards, the IT Systems Analyst will be eligible to apply for a flexible working arrangement, which allows for a mix of in-office & remote work options.

Standard Work Hours: Mon - Fri | 8:15 am - 4:30 pm | 36.25 hours per week

Salary Range: $80,898 - $110,256 per annum

## YOUR FOCUS

Reporting to the Director, DataNB, the Research Scientist initiates, designs, leads, and contributes to large-scale mixed methods and quantitative research and/or evaluation projects across a range of areas relevant to the DataNB mandate. The Research Scientist provides senior leadership within the unit and shares in the responsibility of ensuring DataNB's long-term sustainability. This position is also expected to design and lead other activities relevant to DataNB that advance DataNB's mission and objectives.

The primary focus of this role will be to support the capacity of the Institute specifically in the areas of workforce and occupational health research, including workers compensation claims data and chronic disease data sets. This role is to facilitate further engagement in research grants and contracts and overall research productivity in the field of occupational medicine and workforce health. Depending on the needs of the Institute, the position may also entail scientific leadership of quantitative administrative data studies.

• Design and lead large-scale research projects, evaluations, and related initiatives using administrative data sets housed at DataNB.

• Supervise the work teams of research and/or evaluation staff on specific projects.

• Conduct statistically analysis and produce tables and figures suitable for publication.

• Provide leadership and direction to specific research projects and initiatives that are led or supported by DataNB staff.

• Oversee and lead the creation of research reports and scientific manuscripts for academic publication.

• Participate and lead in the planning, development, and implementation of new research initiatives.

• Lead the output, interpretation, and communication of statistical results with internal and external stakeholders.

• Provide mentorship and supervision to database analysts, research assistants, administrative staff, and junior colleagues, including graduate students and postdoctoral fellows.

• Contribute substantially to the development and production of the DataNB strategic plan.

• Develop research and training collaborations with faculty members at UNB and other universities as well as other research partners and organizations.

• Secure competitive funding to help sustain the ongoing operation of DataNB.

• Build effective relationships and partnerships within and outside the organization.

• Manage complex, multi-faceted projects with multiple internal/external stakeholders.

## WHAT YOU BRING

• A PhD in health, epidemiology, biostatistics or a related field.

• A minimum of 2 years full-time experience in a highly autonomous research role (not including work completed as part of graduate studies).

• Experience with evaluation projects, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, quantitative research projects, particularly using administrative data, claims data, and data set linkage.

• Experience or active interest in workplace/ occupational health, claims data, chronic disease, health data, epidemiology.

• Experience mentoring and/or supervising.

## Additional Strengths

• A track record of scholarly achievement such as peer-reviewed publications, conference proceedings and invited presentations of scholarly work is considered a strong asset.

• Experience working with administrative data/large data sets is considered a strong asset.

• Experience writing and submitting applications for Tri-Council funding is considered a strong asset.

• Experience or training with research-based software such as SPSS, Overview, R, SAS, Python, SQL, Stata, NVivo, JMP, REDCap, etc. considered an asset.

• Experience collaborating across and within various faculties and disciplines is considered an asset.

• Strong conceptual and analytical skills.

• Strong knowledge of quantitative methods relevant to public policy and evaluation.

• Excellent written and verbal interpersonal communication skills.

• Effective problem-solving and decision-making skills.

• Ability to work well independently as well as within a team environment.

• Ability to address and interact with a wide variety of audiences and personalities professionally.

## WHY CHOOSE UNB?

UNB offers a large variety of benefits for employees, including a full pension, a minimum of three weeks of vacation annually, the Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP), and dental, life, and health insurance.

title: Sunnyside Property Coordinator
description:
Type of Employment: Full-time, permanent, unionized (CUPE Local 5048)

Work Location: Saint John, NB (On-site work environment)

Application Deadline: October 9, 2026

United Way Maritimes - with teams located in and serving the regions of Central New Brunswick, Colchester & Cumberland Counties, Halifax, Lunenburg County, Pictou County, Prince Edward Island, and Saint John, Kings & Charlotte - is a for-impact organization that brings donors, volunteers, and partners together to create lasting social change. We believe everyone matters and deserves to belong, be safe, and live a life of their choosing. To help, United Way Maritimes alleviates and reduces local poverty by funding, partnering, convening, and advocating for solutions. United Way Maritimes is part of a federated movement of 50+ United Ways across the country.

The staff at United Way Maritimes takes pride in bringing together people who have a range of experience, talents, and backgrounds. We share a passion for each of the places we call home and bring many different skills and strengths to the work we do. Our community and social change priorities include poverty, social isolation, affordable housing, people experiencing marginalization and vulnerability, and recovery and resilience to environmental, mass casualty and public health emergencies. We provide a supportive and flexible work environment filled with opportunity, balance, and laughter.

The Housing Team is focused on creating and stewarding a sustainable, equitable, and community-driven parallel housing system that provides opportunities unavailable in the general market. This includes supportive housing, affordable rental, and attainable homeownership models that support people exiting homelessness, strengthen housing stability, and address gaps such as missing-middle housing.

The Sunnyside Community is a new supportive affordable housing community project in Saint John, New Brunswick owned and operated by United Way. This community will offer up to 70 high-quality, deeply affordable modular home units, with wrap around supports to ensure residents can remain safely housed.

Reporting to the Property Manager, Affordable Housing, the Sunnyside Property Coordinator is a hands-on and resident-focused professional who can effectively balance day-to-day property operations with building positive, respectful relationships with residents and community partners. They are skilled at coordinating maintenance, repairs, contractors, and tenancy-related matters while taking initiative to ensure the property is safe, well-maintained, and welcoming. Guided by strong values and a compassionate approach, they understand that successful affordable housing management requires both caring for the physical property and supporting residents with dignity, respect, and consistency through collaborative relationships with onsite support providers and team members.

## The key responsibilities of the role include:

• Resident & Tenancy Relations: Acts as the primary on-site contact for residents for property-related matters. Supports move-ins, move-outs, tenancy administration, rent collection processes, and property-related concerns while maintaining accurate records and professional resident relationships. Works collaboratively with residents, support providers, and community partners to promote successful tenancies, address emerging concerns, and ensure residents understand their responsibilities, available supports, and community expectations.

• Property Operations & Maintenance: Serves as the primary on-site coordinator for property operations, ensuring the housing community is safe, well-maintained, and responsive to resident needs through regular inspections, preventative maintenance, timely repairs, and oversight of property assets. Coordinates contractors, suppliers, and maintenance activities, maintains accurate records, supports procurement and emergency preparedness efforts, and works closely with the Property Manager to identify and address ongoing maintenance, safety, and capital improvement needs.

• Administration & Reporting: Maintains accurate operational, financial, and property records while providing regular updates to the Property Manager on property conditions, resident matters, maintenance needs, and emerging risks. Supports reporting, budgeting, audits, inspections, and compliance activities, while identifying opportunities to strengthen policies, procedures, and overall site operations.

• Compliance & Risk Management: Support housing operations in compliance with Residential Tenancy legislation, Occupational Health & Safety requirements, fire and accessibility standards, insurance obligations, and other regulatory requirements. This includes supporting or conducting inspections and reporting, managing insurance claims, and proactively identifying and mitigating operational risks.

## Qualifications

• Minimum three years of relevant experience in property operations, residential housing, facilities maintenance, affordable housing, community-based services, or a related field.

• Demonstrated practical skills in basic property maintenance and minor repairs.

• Ability to assess maintenance requirements and determine when work can be completed directly and when a qualified contractor is required.

• Experience coordinating contractors, suppliers, and service providers.

• Knowledge of, or ability to quickly develop strong working knowledge of New Brunswick residential tenancy legislation and processes.

• Understanding of Occupational Health & Safety requirements and safe work practices.

• Demonstrated ability to work respectfully and effectively with residents from diverse backgrounds, including individuals who may have complex needs.

• Strong interpersonal, communication, and active listening skills.

• Ability to establish positive resident relationships while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries.

• Demonstrated ability to organize and prioritize work based on importance, urgency, safety, and resident impact.

• Ability to work independently with minimal day-to-day supervision while knowing when to escalate matters to the Property Manager.

• Strong written communication and record-keeping skills with excellent attention to detail.

• Ability to appropriately manage confidential resident information.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 (e.g., Word, Outlook, SharePoint) and the ability to learn property management and organizational information systems (i.e., Yardi).

• Comfortable using common property maintenance, landscaping, and grounds-care tools and equipment.

• WHMIS certification, or willingness to obtain certification.

• Valid driver's licence and access to reliable transportation.

• Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning relevant to the position.

The ideal candidate is a values-driven and resident-focused professional with experience in affordable or supportive housing, homelessness services, or the nonprofit sector. They are organized, accountable, and proactive, with a hands-on, solutions-focused approach to managing operational and resident needs while building positive relationships with residents, colleagues, and community partners. Committed to Housing First, harm reduction, and trauma-informed practices, they remain calm and adaptable in changing environments and work collaboratively to support a safe, respectful, and well-managed residential community. Certifications in areas such as First Aid, crisis intervention, conflict resolution, suicide prevention, and overdose prevention are considered strong assets.

United Way Maritimes is committed to a comprehensive compensation package including salary, group retirement savings plan contribution, health and dental benefits, generous vacation time, additional time-off during the December holiday period, and professional development and training opportunities. The salary for this position is $56,650 per year.

Interested candidates are encouraged to reach out to our Administrative & HR Assistant, Aleks Wilson, for a conversation about the role, salary range, and total compensation package. To contact Aleks, please email: jobs@unitedwaymaritimes.ca or 902-298-3702.

If this sounds like you, let us know by sharing your resume and cover letter outlining why you could be the right fit for United Way Maritimes and this role. Submit your application to jobs@unitedwaymaritimes.ca by October 9, 2026 at 11:59 PM (AST).

United Way Maritimes deeply values equity and is committed to ensuring our staff community reflects the diversity of the wider community. We welcome applications from African Nova Scotian people, people of African descent, Indigenous peoples, racialized people, women, people with disabilities, people of varied sexual and gender identities, and others with the skills and knowledge to productively engage with diverse communities. United Way Maritimes seeks to maintain its commitment to inclusion and equity and recognizes that increasing the diversity of our staff supports this objective.

title: Director of Planning and Development Services
description:
## ABOUT US

Bridgewater, Nova Scotia, Canada is a town of approximately 9,000 residents, nestled in the heart of the LaHave River Valley on the province's South Shore.

Located within an hour of Halifax, Bridgewater's reputation as the Main Street of the South Shore is well-deserved -- the community is the service centre for more than 60,000 residents within a 30-minute drive in Lunenburg and Queens counties.
Bridgewater boasts all the service you would expect from a modern location and couples it with the charm and feel of a tightly knit community, the kind where neighbours know each other and everyone greets you with a smile.

The Town of Bridgewater is currently seeking a Director of Planning and Development Services to join our team.

The Town of Bridgewater is committed to offering equal employment opportunities based on qualifications and performance, and free from discrimination because of age, race or ethnic origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, disability, family status, gender identity, or other protected characteristics, in accordance with the Nova Scotia Human Rights Act. At the Town of Bridgewater, we strive to make our recruitment, assessment, and selection processes as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for applicants with disabilities.

If you require any accommodations at any point during the application and hiring process, please contact Human Resources at employment@mjsb.ca or call 902-543-4651.

## ABOUT THE ROLE

The Director of Planning and Development Services is responsible for the overall management of the Town's Planning, Sustainability, and Development Services which includes strategic and long-term community and land use planning, project management, development review and control, building and fire inspection services, sustainability, special projects and GIS services.

The position is responsible to ensure the Department is aligned with Council and Organizational Priorities, developmental and capacity building of departmental staff, and financial management of the department budgets and plans.

## ABOUT YOU

You are naturally collaborative and know how to pull people together to accomplish goals. You are able to see the big picture which will allows you to make valuable contributions to grow the Town with the help of your planning and development service team. You lead by example in aligning with your team's goals with the goals of the organization and Council. Teamwork and collaboration are important to you, and you recognize the value of working with other departments to achieve Council's vision. You understand the importance of community, and with your leadership you will enable the recreation and culture team to offer programs and services to serve our diverse community. Do you see yourself in this description?

## PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

## Planning

• Acts as a subject matter expert on Land Use and Community Planning.

• Working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders, research, report and make recommendations to Town Council on planning related studies, land use matters, policy and by-law amendments, and development agreements.

• Working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders, prepare Municipal Planning Strategy and Land Use By-law, Subdivision By-law and Development Agreements, including amendments to these documents.

## Development Services

• Perform the duties of Acting Deputy Development Officer for the Towns' Subdivision By-law and interprets and administers the Subdivision By-law and Subdivision Regulations, including the processing and approval of subdivision applications in the absence of the Municipal Development Officer.

• Assist the Development Officer in interpretation and administration of Municipal Planning Strategy and Land Use By-law, when required. Acts as Acting Development Officer for the Town's Land Use By-law in the absence of the Development Officer.

## Sustainability

• Working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to oversee the development and implementation of the Town of Bridgewater's:

• Community Energy Investment Plan and revisions there to.

• Integrated Community Sustainability Plan, and revisions thereto.

• Municipal Climate Change Action Plan and revisions thereto.

## Building/Fire Inspection

Through an Inter-Municipal Shared Services Agreement with neighboring municipal units, is responsible for:

• Overseeing the delivery of Building Inspection Services.

• Overseeing the administration of the Dangerous and Unsightly Inspection Policy and MGA provisions.

• Overseeing the administration of the Minimum Standards By-law.

• Overseeing the delivery of Fire Inspection Services in accordance with the Towns Policy Re: System of Fire Inspections, Fire Safety Act and Regulations.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• Degree in Planning or a field closely related to planning,

• Eligibility for membership in C.I.P.

• A valid Nova Scotia driver's license.

• A minimum of ten (10) years of previous employment experience as a planner, or a combination of suitable training and experience; and

• A minimum of five (5) years of previous leadership and /or management experience

• Thorough knowledge of the Municipal Government Act (MGA), with emphasis on content and procedures for adoption, amendment, and administration of Municipal Planning Strategy, Subdivision By -law, Land Use By-law and Development Agreements.

• Excellent knowledge of local government responsibility, organization and procedures.

• Program delivery and Project Management.

• Knowledge of the application of Geographic Information Systems and spatial analysis.

• Proficiency in MS Office, Permit Tracking systems and a general knowledge of GIS.

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT

• Permanent, full-time, non-union position.

• Annual Salary (Grade 8): $116,546 - $149,845, commensurate with experience.

• Competitive group benefits and group insurance package.

• Defined Benefit Pension Plan - PSSP

• Regular hours - Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm (35 hours per week). This position is required to attend evening meetings.

• Position operates out of the Town's Administration Department (60 Pleasant Street).

Please submit your application no later than October 30, 2026 @ 11:59 p.m. at: https://Bridgewater.scouterecruit.net/jobs/TOB2026019

title: Manager of Planning Services
description:
Job Title: Manager of Planning Services
Location: Truro, Nova Scotia
TP - MCC - 10174

Centrally located within Nova Scotia between two extraordinary coastlines, The Municipality of Colchester is a progressive rural municipality that offers an unparalleled work-life balance. It is a place that is affordable, welcoming, family focused, rich in diverse culture and natural beauty with thriving businesses and access to all the modern amenities typically found in an urban setting, without the common stresses of urban living.

The Municipality is experiencing significant growth and transformation, creating exciting opportunities to influence the future of communities across the region. From affordable housing initiatives and active transportation planning to infrastructure investments and the modernization of municipal services, Colchester is committed to building vibrant, sustainable communities while continuously improving how services are delivered.

Meridia Recruitment is pleased to partner with the Municipality of the County of Colchester in the recruitment of a Manager of Planning Services, a key leadership role responsible for overseeing planning operations, supporting a growing team, and helping guide the Municipality through an exciting period of growth, innovation, and change.

## Role Description

Reporting to the Director of Community Development, the Manager of Planning Services provides strategic leadership for the Municipality's planning function, overseeing land use planning, development review, policy development, sustainability initiatives, and long-range growth planning.

Leading one of the Municipality's larger teams, including planning, development, and sustainability professionals, you will play a critical role in advancing strategic priorities, supporting organizational modernization, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing culture. While providing guidance on complex planning matters, your primary focus will be on leadership, team development, process improvement, and ensuring the department is positioned to effectively support the Municipality's continued growth and evolution.

As a trusted advisor to senior leadership and Council, you will help shape policy, guide planning initiatives, and balance community interests, development opportunities, legislative requirements, and long-term municipal objectives.

## Key Responsibilities:

Planning Leadership & Development Oversight

• Lead and oversee the Municipality's planning services function, providing strategic direction to planning, development, and sustainability staff.

• Oversee the review and evaluation of rezoning applications, development agreements, subdivision applications, and amendments to planning documents.

• Ensure the effective administration of the Municipal Planning Strategy, Land Use By-law, and Subdivision By-law.

• Guide the development, review, and implementation of planning policies, regulations, and procedures in accordance with municipal priorities and provincial legislation.

• Provide expertise and support on complex planning matters, emerging issues, and development opportunities.

Team Leadership & Organizational Development

• Lead, mentor, and support a multidisciplinary team through a period of growth, modernization, and organizational change.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, and customer-focused service delivery.

• Coach staff through complex planning, development, stakeholder, and public engagement matters.

• Support employee growth and development by establishing clear expectations, encouraging professional development, and building team capacity.

• Empower staff to take ownership of their work while providing leadership, guidance, and strategic oversight.

Strategic Planning & Community Growth

• Lead long-range planning initiatives that support sustainable growth, infrastructure planning, housing, community development, and Council's strategic priorities.

• Research demographic, economic, environmental, and development trends to inform future planning decisions.

• Develop and implement community planning goals, policies, and programs that support the Municipality's vision and long-term objectives.

• Lead and support major planning projects, studies, and initiatives that address emerging opportunities and community needs.

• Champion innovative approaches to planning challenges and opportunities.

Stakeholder Engagement & Community Relations

• Build and maintain positive relationships with residents, property owners, developers, community organizations, government agencies, and other stakeholders.

• Provide professional planning advice regarding municipal policies, regulations, standards, and development processes.

• Support public consultation and community engagement initiatives related to planning projects and policy development.

• Respond to public inquiries and planning matters with professionalism, transparency, and a strong customer service focus.

Council & Corporate Support

• Serve as a trusted planning advisor to senior leadership and Council by providing strategic expertise and evidence-based recommendations.

• Prepare reports, recommendations, policy documents, and presentations for senior leadership, committees, and Council.

• Present planning proposals, studies, and policy recommendations to Council and advisory committees.

• Collaborate with municipal departments to ensure planning considerations are integrated into corporate projects and initiatives.

• Support the ongoing development and implementation of Community Development Department goals and priorities.

Financial & Operational Management

• Prepare and manage Planning Services budgets, ensuring responsible stewardship of municipal resources.

• Support modernization initiatives, process improvements, and the continued transition toward digital service delivery.

• Monitor departmental performance, service delivery standards, and operational effectiveness, identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.

• Ensure resources are effectively aligned with departmental priorities and service objectives.

## Your Qualifications:

• Degree in Planning from an accredited university program.

• Full membership, or eligibility to become a full member within three months of hire, with the Licensed Professional Planners Association of Nova Scotia.

• 5+ years of progressive planning experience, preferably within a municipal environment.

• Strong knowledge of municipal planning principles, land use planning, subdivision regulations, planning legislation, and policy development.

• Experience managing planning projects, development applications, and regulatory review processes.

• Experience preparing reports, policy recommendations, and presentations for senior leadership and elected officials.

• Strong financial acumen, including budget preparation and resource management.

• Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder engagement skills.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines.

## Assets include:

• Master's Degree in Planning.

• Demonstrated supervisory experience with the ability to mentor, motivate, and develop teams.

• Experience working within a Nova Scotia municipal planning environment is an asset.

• Familiarity with the history, geography, and development trends of Colchester County.

• Experience leading major policy reviews, growth management initiatives, housing strategies, infrastructure planning, or community development projects.

• Experience supporting technology adoption, digital transformation, or organizational modernization initiatives.

## Why Colchester?

This is an exciting opportunity to play a leading role in shaping the future of one of Nova Scotia's growing municipalities. As Manager of Planning Services, you will influence land use policy, guide community growth, support major development initiatives, and contribute to projects that have a lasting impact on residents, businesses, and communities throughout Colchester County.

Colchester offers a collaborative and supportive work environment, competitive compensation, a defined benefit pension plan, comprehensive benefits, professional development opportunities, and the chance to make a meaningful contribution to the region's long-term success.

The Municipality of Colchester is committed to treating people fairly, with respect and dignity. Their goal is to continue to move forward as a diverse and inclusive community representative of the citizens they serve by offering equal opportunities free of biases. They have formed an Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Accessibility Committee to keep them accountable and to help them reach this goal.

The Municipality encourages all qualified applicants who self-identify as Indigenous, Black/African Nova Scotian, Persons of Colour, Newcomers, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ to apply and self-identify on their applications.

title: Financial Services Officer - Accounts Payable
description:
Reporting to the Controller, the Financial Services Officer - Accounts Payable is responsible for the processing, balancing and payment of all invoices and payments owed by NSCAD University. This position is a key component of our internal control structure. The FSO - AP issues weekly cheques, ensures that all purchase orders are up-to-date, posts all invoices and determines when to pay bills and whether or not spending is properly authorized.

Qualifications
Completion of Grade 12 and a one-year diploma in accounting combined with at least three (3) years of related experience or equivalent education and experience is required.

Proficiency in typing, business machines (fax, photocopiers, and calculator) and computer is necessary.

Accuracy and the ability to adhere to strict deadlines are required. Very good interpersonal skills, an ability to communicate effectively, and well developed organizational and time management skills are required.

The incumbent must be able to work with frequent interruptions and be capable of handling and maintaining concentration on several different duties at one time

Responsibilities
• Process and audit accounts payable transactions, including invoices, honorariums, travel claims, reimbursements, petty cash, and other payment requests, ensuring appropriate approvals, documentation, tax treatment, and compliance with University policies.

• Manage the Accounts Payable subledger, including vendor statement reconciliation, timely payment processing, cheque runs, outstanding cheque monitoring, and reconciliation of the subledger to the General Ledger.

• Administer the University's purchase order process, including PO encumbrances, approvals, receipts, outstanding and cancelled POs, troubleshooting, distribution, and follow-up with departments and purchasers.

• Monitor and administer employee allowances, travel and cash advances, grants, and other expenditures to ensure accurate tracking and compliance with University policies and collective agreements.

• Prepare monthly financial reconciliations and reports, including Facilities expenditures, petty cash, prepaid accounts, and other General Ledger accounts.

• Prepare and submit the University's monthly HST returns and CRA remittances, and process foreign exchange drafts, wire transfers, manual cheques, and other banking transactions.

• Maintain accurate vendor, student, and employee financial information within Colleague and related systems, including establishing and updating vendor accounts and banking-related information.

• Maintain capital asset records and supporting documentation, and provide financial records, reconciliations, trial balances, and other documentation required for internal and external audits.

• Coordinate banking and cash-handling activities, including deposits, money orders, petty cash, cheque distribution, and related documentation.

• Provide financial and purchasing support across the University, including training users on purchasing processes, resolving procurement and vendor issues, supporting customs clearances, reviewing telecommunications expenditures, and preparing ad hoc financial reports and projects.

Note: These are the primary duties of the position; duties related to this job may be assigned from time to time as may become necessary to the operation of NSCAD University. Changing circumstances for the university may require modifications to positions and position descriptions in the future.

title: Senior Policy Analyst
description:
The Senior Policy Analyst will provide policy analysis and strategic advice to senior leadership of Build NS to promote effective planning, policy development, implementation and evaluation of programs and policies related to projects, programs and priorities to ensure evidence-based decision making.

Reporting to the Director, Policy and Research, the Senior Policy Analyst will lead projects and participate in multi-disciplinary, interdepartmental and intergovernmental teams of senior staff in the identification and analysis of options and recommendations to respond to abroad range of policy and corporate issues. This position will play a major role in supporting informed, effective decision-making within the organization and coordinate and participate extensively in areas of policy development and legislative change. In addition, this role will support in the business planning process and accountability requirements to assure satisfactory governance.

Qualifications
Minimum of a bachelor's degree (business, public administration) with 5 years of experience in policy analysis, strategic and business planning, project management, legislative planning/analysis, and management of submissions to Executive Council Office.

Proven management and leadership skills; are able to demonstrate excellent verbal and written communication skills; and have extensive experience with presentations/facilitation.

Highly motivated, flexible and demonstrate expertise when dealing with complex situations requiring innovative and proactive solutions. Experience working with internal and external stakeholders is required. As a dynamic leader, you possess the ability to lead change, move forward new initiatives and overcome ongoing challenges. An excellent understanding of current departmental legislation, programs, and policies is a definite asset. A proven ability to make decisions and provide advice/recommendations in ambiguous situations using sound judgment and monitoring risk is required.

This competition will remain open until filled.

Responsibilities

## Informed and evidenced based decision making:

Undertakes research, develops and analyzes policy options and makes recommendations on a broad range of complex and sometimes conflicting issues in order to inform the decision-making process by senior management. This involves knowledge of research methods, coordination of multi-disciplinary teams to assist in the identification and analysis of policy options, drafting of policy papers and recommendations, development of policy instruments, and consultation with internal and external stakeholders.

Works collaboratively on submissions to Executive Council and Treasury and Policy Board (e.g., Memorandums to Executive Council, Reports & Recommendations to Executive Council, Requests for Legislation).

Consults with Treasury and Policy Board, Finance CSU, and Justice to ensure sound policy development. Participates in briefings and presentations to support the President/CEO, VP's and Senior Directors in appearances at Executive Council, Public Accounts, etc.

Alignment of corporation's priorities with government objectives and commitments:

The Senior Policy Analyst is required to manage a broad range of corporation-wide policy initiatives that are at a high level of complexity and require significant leadership and understanding of corporate and government issues and priorities. The Senior Policy Analyst has a solid understanding of and plays a key role in addressing major policy issues and will build and maintain a strong network of colleagues throughout the corporation and across Government.

Represents the Division/Corporation on task forces, work groups, project teams and advisory bodies to ensure that departmental priorities are considered in government policies and decision-making. A broad corporate understanding and extensive participation in senior cross-sector/department activity is essential.

## Corporation goals are realized:

Provides leadership within the corporation in the development of long-term strategic plans to address critical issues.

Ensure that strategies are consistent with and support Government's vision and priorities. This responsibility is addressed by promoting broad dialogue among stakeholders to address key issues; undertaking environmental scanning to identify emerging trends; researching best practices; and promoting involvement by staff at all levels of the corporation in identification of strategies to ensure the corporation's goals are realized.

## Good governance and accountability:

title: Managing Director - Marketing Agency
description:
Higher Talent Inc. has partnered with Pilot° in their search for a Managing Director reporting to their St. John's, NL office.

## ABOUT THE ROLE:

Reporting to the President & Executive Chair, the Managing Director (MD) is the senior operational and leadership executive responsible for the day-to-day performance, stability, and growth of Pilot°. The MD translates vision into execution, ensuring the agency operates profitably, efficiently, and with strategic clarity.

This role is ideal for a seasoned leader who combines business acumen, people leadership, and operational discipline, and who thrives in a creative, client-driven environment. The MD must be a confident, credible leader internally and with senior clients.

The Managing Director is central to Pilot's next chapter-ensuring the agency is strong, stable, scalable, and future-ready, while preserving the values, reputation, and creative excellence that define the brand for more than three decades.

## WHO THEY ARE:

Pilot° is a full-service marketing and communications agency with more than 30 years of experience supporting long-standing clients across the private, public and non-profit sectors. Small by design, Pilot° brings together a tight-knit team of uniquely talented and experienced professionals who leverage their individual expertise, networks, and trusted relationships to deliver exceptional value and meaningful results for clients.

With a strong, respected brand and a reputation for quality, collaboration, and impact, Pilot° is known not only for outstanding client work but also for treating employees exceptionally well, offering a supportive culture and highly competitive benefits.

Located in the heart of downtown St. John's, NL, the role offers an inspiring work environment surrounded by historic charm, vibrant streets, and the perfect setting for scenic lunchtime strolls and local shopping.

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

## 1. Agency Leadership & Management

• Provide strong, steady leadership to the leadership team and staff.

• Set clear priorities, expectations, and accountability across the agency.

• Foster a high-performance culture grounded in respect, collaboration, and excellence.

• Act as a trusted partner to the President & Executive Chair in decision-making and execution.

## 2. Operations & Workflow Oversight

• Own the operational rhythm of the agency: resourcing, scheduling, workflow, and delivery.

• Ensure projects and retainers are delivered on time, on budget, and to scope.

• Oversee project management systems, internal workflows, and process improvement.

• Champion consistency and discipline across tools, templates, and reporting (e.g., project management, time tracking, financial reporting).

## 3. Financial Performance & Profitability

• Be accountable for agency financial health, including:

• Revenue targets

• Gross margin

• Utilization and recoverability

• Cost control

• Work closely with finance/accounting to review monthly financials and forecasts.

• Identify risks and opportunities early and take corrective action as needed.

• Ensure pricing, resourcing, and scope decisions support long-term sustainability.

## 4. Client Leadership & Relationship Management

• Provide senior oversight on key client accounts.

• Step in as an escalation point when needed to protect relationships and outcomes.

• Ensure client work aligns with Pilot's strategic and creative standards.

• Support account leaders in managing scope, expectations, and value delivery.

## 5. Business Development & Growth Support

• Support new business development efforts alongside senior leadership.

• Help evaluate opportunities for strategic fit, capacity, and profitability.

• Contribute to proposals, pitches, and pricing strategies as required.

• Strengthen Pilot's reputation as a trusted, high-calibre agency partner.

## 6. People Leadership & Talent Development

• Has direct leadership responsibility for senior operational and client-facing roles.

• Lead, coach, and support the leadership team (Account, Strategy, Creative, Operations).

• Ensure clear role definitions, performance expectations, and development plans.

• Support recruitment, onboarding, and retention of high-quality talent.

• Champion succession planning and leadership development within the agency.

## 7. Governance & Strategic Alignment

• Execute against the strategic direction set by the President & Executive Chair.

• Ensure decisions align with Pilot's values, brand, and long-term vision.

• Prepare briefing materials, operational updates, and performance reporting as required.

• Contribute to strategic planning and annual goal-setting.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Senior leadership experience in a professional services, agency, consulting, or complex client-service environment.

• Demonstrated success managing teams, budgets, and operational performance.

• Experience working with founders, boards, or executive leadership is an asset.

• Exposure to marketing, communications, creative, or adjacent industries preferred (but not mandatory).

## Skills & Attributes

• Strong operational and financial acumen.

• Excellent people leadership and communication skills.

• Calm, decisive, and credible under pressure.

• Strategic thinker who can also execute at a detailed level.

• High emotional intelligence and sound judgment.

• Comfortable navigating complexity, ambiguity, and competing priorities.

## Mindset

• Values collaboration over ego.

• Comfortable leading in a smaller market with big-market standards.

• Motivated by building something enduring, not just personal advancement.

• Respects creative cultures while bringing structure and discipline.
