If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services(ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and Disability Support Program(DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
The Central Registry Clerk provides administrative and clerical records services that support the Department's Central Registry daily operations under the direction of the Records Analyst 2. The role helps maintain integrity, accessibility, security, and accurate tracking of physical and electronic records while delivering responsive service to departmental clients.

Working within established legislation, policies, procedures, and records schedules, the Clerk creates, retrieves, returns, files, inventories, scans, and tracks records; supports storage, reactivation, disposition, litigation and information-access searches; and contributes operational knowledge and supports records digitization projects and FileNet initiatives.

Primary Accountabilities
• Monitor the Central Registry shared email account and respond to routine records enquiries and service requests from Head Office and regional offices.

• Create new physical record folders and update record categories, metadata, descriptions, locations, status, and other authorized information in FileNet or related tracking tools.

• Process file retrieval, search, charge-out, return, check-in, filing, and reactivation requests, maintaining accurate tracking information at each stage.

• Conduct assigned records searches, prepare search reports, and retrieve records in support of FOIPOP, litigation, discovery, Adoption Disclosure, and other authorized business requests.

• Prepare records for off-site storage by assigning box numbers, reviewing inventory information, supporting transmittal documentation, and updating databases and box lists.

• Assist with records disposition activities by identifying eligible files, pulling records, checking inventories, and preparing supporting administrative documentation for Records Analyst review.

• Inventory physical records, enter folder descriptions, replace damaged folders, complete shelf checks, reorganize files, and help maintain orderly and accessible storage areas.

• Scan and transcribe historical, fragile, or requested records; perform quality checks; apply approved naming practices; and maintain security during digitization work.

• Maintain routine access lists, program contacts, supply stocks, and other operational records used to deliver Central Registry services.

• Participate in cross-training, procedure updates, FileNet or electronic records management projects, and other assigned Central Registry initiatives.

• Provide backup support to other Records Clerks and perform related duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Experience
To be successful in this role, the applicant will have at least three years of related administrative, clerical, records, registry, filing, or information-management experience. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

You also have:

- Experience working with physical and electronic records management systems such as FileNet.

- Experience in applying records classification and retention schedules, such as STAR/STOR.

- Experience maintaining records inventories, databases, and spreadsheets using records management tracking tools.

- Experience using office scanning equipment.

- Proficiency using Microsoft Office Suite applications and other Records Management tools, such as MS Access, Excel, Word, Outlook, SharePoint; and Adobe Acrobat.

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to enter, verify, organize, and retrieve information accurately using records management principles and best practices.

- Knowledge of records management principles and of records management lifecycles.

- Good judgement and understanding of the need to protect confidential, sensitive, and historical information.

- Exceptional customer service and communication skills for supporting staff across Head Office and regional locations.

- Organizational and time-management skills, including the ability to manage frequent interruptions and changing priorities.

- The ability to follow legislation, policies, schedules, procedures, and established work processes while identifying discrepancies for supervisor review.

- The ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.

- The ability to regularly work with boxes weighing 40-45 pounds.

Assets include:

- Familiarity with the Government Records Act, FOIPOP Act, Public Archives Act, or related privacy and information-management requirements.

- Applying records digitization workflows.

- Experience performing records searches, records storage transfers, reactivations, dispositions, litigation holds and discovery support.

- Experience handling historical, archival, fragile, personal, confidential, or sensitive records.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include, but are not limited to:

• Completion of a related 2-year diploma and 1 year of related experience

• Completion of a related 1-year diploma and 2 years of related experience

• Completion of a related Bachelor's degree

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day.

• Work is primarily in the Central Registry.

• Ability to review documents or files for hours is required.

• Must be able to lift and carry boxes weighing up to 40-45 pounds and climb step ladders.

• Requires working in file rooms with records that may be dusty.

• Occasional travel to regional offices or off-site storage as required, as such a Driver's license is an asset.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless Career Paths.

## Position description

Reporting to the Dean of Libraries and Archives, the Library Resources and Access Manager leads a team of staff responsible for technical services, access services, & resource sharing. This position oversees the acquisitions budget, has five direct reports, and manages a portfolio of ~13 individuals. The LRAM is responsible for developing and sustaining a unified approach to resource management, access, and patron services, ensuring collaboration, coordination, and communication across library departments. This position works closely with the Collections Librarian, ordering librarians, and other partners inside and outside the library. The incumbent is a member of the leadership team and serves as the staff supervisor-in-charge in the absence of the Dean.

## Responsibilities

• Under direction from the Dean of Libraries & Archives, is an active member of the leadership team and serve as the staff supervisor-in-charge in their absence

• Contribute to a positive organizational culture, facilitating collaboration, coordination, and communication within and across departments

• Hire, train, coach, and mentor supervisees, assisting the Head of Access Services & Resource sharing with the same; set goals, track progress, monitor results, and provide feedback and guidance to ensure success

• Support the Head of Access Services & Resource Sharing to ensure efficient and effective workflows and outstanding patron-oriented services

• Under direction from the Dean, oversee the library acquisitions budget and related financial processes and practices; create, input, roll-over and manage the budget (~$1mill in operating and endowments) in the library LSP (Alma); approve fund codes and expenditures; reconcile accounts, track balances, and prepare budget projections

• Oversee print and electronic resource acquisitions staff and operations, ensuring adherence to established procedures that facilitate efficient processes, responsible financial practices, and accessible library resources; ensure maintenance of up-to-date vendor files

• Supervise cataloguing and metadata technician; ensure high-quality records that facilitate access and discoverability as determined by the Collections Librarian; support librarians with digital and other special projects as requested; facilitate effective and timely workflows

• Serve as a member of the electronic resource troubleshooting team; assists with triaging, resolving, and delegating support tickets; communicate professionally with patrons to resolve issues and ensure access

• In collaboration with Novanet and internal team, configure the acquisitions and fulfillment modules in Alma; maintain expert knowledge of Alma functions and analytics; identify and ensure task cleanup for acquisitions and cataloguing functions

• Develop procedures and documentation to support departmental operations and make recommendations for improvement

• Run reports, gather statistics, and communicate frequently with library administration, financial services, librarians, vendors, and others; support librarians' collection and electronic resource assessment and evaluation processes as needed

• Identify, recommend, and assist with implementation and training for new systems, services, processes and skills for continuous improvement in consultation with appropriate colleagues

• Coordinate, provide, or support training for staff and student workers; supervise student workers as needed; provide backup to departmental operations as needed.

## Other Duties

• Electronic resource management

• Budget management and accounting

• Experience with creating and maintaining catalogue and metadata records

Our vision is to be a recognized leader in service and public protection that delivers trusted, accessible, modern programs, and contributes to Nova Scotia as a safe and desirable place to live, work and do business.

The Alcohol, Gaming, Fuel and Tobacco (AGFT) Division of Service Nova Scotia is the regulatory body charged with administering Part II of the Gaming Control Act, parts of the Liquor Control Act, and the Theatres and Amusements Act. The AGFT issues approximately 13,000 licenses annually, and provides in counter service to approximately 3,100 annually.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Director of Investigation and Enforcement, the Senior Gaming Analyst provides operational leadership, technical expertise, and regulatory oversight for gaming investigations, compliance activities, and gaming technology within the province. The Senior Gaming Analyst supports the planning, development, implementation, and ongoing enhancement of policies, procedures, standards, and regulatory frameworks related to lottery schemes and gaming operations.

The Senior Gaming Analyst is responsible for supervising analytical and investigative staff, coordinating complex regulatory and technical activities, and providing subject matter expertise related to gaming systems, gaming integrity, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies. The role contributes to divisional planning, operational priorities, risk management, and strategic decision-making.

Lottery schemes include, but are not limited to, casinos, slot machines, Video Lottery Terminals, online gaming systems, electronic raffle systems, bingo, table games, lotteries, games of chance, and associated hardware, software, networks, and cloud-based technologies that may impact the integrity of gaming within the province.

Primary Accountabilities
Provide leadership for the division's gaming compliance, investigative, and technical oversight programs to ensure lottery schemes within the province operate in accordance with legislation, regulatory standards, and integrity requirements. Support divisional planning, operational priorities, resource allocation, and continuous improvement initiatives related to gaming regulation and enforcement.

Lead, supervise, and mentor staff engaged in regulatory, investigative, analytical, and technical activities. Establish operational priorities, assign work, monitor performance, provide technical direction, support staff development, and ensure consistency in investigative practices, inspections, reporting and regulatory decision-making.

Provide senior expertise and decision-making support related complex gaming investigations, integrity concerns, compliance matters, enforcement actions and emerging regulatory risks.

Lead and develop, implementation and ongoing enhancement of policies, procedures, technical standards and regulatory frameworks related to gaming systems, lottery schemes, investigations, compliance activities, and gaming integrity within the province.

Provide strategic oversight of compliance monitoring, audits, inspections and technical reviews related to casinos, video lottery terminals, online gaming systems, charitable gaming, electronic raffle systems, and other regulated lottery schemes. Identify emerging trends, integrity concerns, and operational risks requiring regulatory response or enhanced oversight.

Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with gaming operators, independent testing laboratories, law enforcement agencies, financial institutions, regulatory organizations, vendors, and other government agencies to support information sharing, regulatory consistency, compliance activities, and investigations involving gaming integrity or emerging technologies.

Prepare and present technical reports, briefing materials, risk assessments, recommendations, and policy analysis for senior management related to gaming integrity, regulatory compliance, operational risks, enforcement matters, and emerging gaming technologies.

Represent the division on internal and external committees, working groups and interjurisdictional initiatives related to gaming regulation, investigations, cybersecurity, compliance monitoring and technical standards.

Qualifications and Experience
To be considered for this opportunity, you are registered as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) and hold membership in good standing with Engineers Nova Scotia. You hold a Bachelor of Engineering in addition to a minimum of 6 years of related experience. You are registered with Engineers Nova Scotia as Licensed to Practice.

In addition, you hold extensive experience providing operational leadership, technical expertise, and regulatory oversight for investigations, and compliance activities. You also have experience in planning, developing, implementing, and enhancing policies, procedures, standards, and regulatory frameworks. .

In addition, you demonstrate:

· Strong leadership and communications skills

· Experience supervising staff

· A high degree of judgment and accuracy

· Strong interpersonal and relationship building skills

· Diplomacy, resourcefulness with a focus on clients

· Strong organizational skills and the ability to work with minimum supervision

· A professional attitude at all times.

The following would be considered assets: experience within the regulated areas of Liquor, Gaming, Smoke, Theatres and Amusement, and a good working knowledge of data spreadsheet and work processing software.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
The primary hours of work will be determined by the employer and the hours of operation of premises and events licensed by the Alcohol Gaming Fuel & Tobacco Division. Will include varied hours of shift work to include evenings, nights and weekends.

Posted Date: 2026-09-11

Closing Date: Open until filled.

If there are no Primary Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Primary Care Paramedic, then Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to an EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

description:
At Hydro we work to foster positive work-life balance and offer remote or hybrid working arrangements for some positions based on the nature of work being performed and an assessment of other relevant factors.

## Opportunities, Growth, Job Satisfaction...Join the Hydro Team.

­Hydro Plant Operator
Competition #: NLH-RE-26-144
Status: Permanent
Location: Bay D'Espoir

Our employees are at the heart of what we do. We're looking for passionate and performance focused people - people who want to make a difference for our customers and who share our values.

## GENERAL DUTIES:

description:

## Position Summary

Reporting to the Administrator, the Dietitian is responsible for defining and for the direction, coordination, quality, safety, planning and delivery of all matters related to Nutritional Services for the facility. As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Dietitian assists in the development, administration and coordination of the departmental policies and procedures and makes reports and recommendations to the Administrator regarding the function of the Nutritional Services Department.

The Dietitian is responsible for assessing the Clinical Nutritional needs of all residents of Glen Haven Manor upon admission and complete assessment follow up annually and as required. The Dietitian is also responsible for the planning, organizing of the menu and then reviewing or making changes based on the Nutritional Guide of Canada and all therapeutic diet programs. The Dietitian collaborates with all departments to ensure activities are planned and coordinated appropriately, integrates suggestions identified through Resident and Family Council, participates in all planning related to the priorities of the facility and the needs of residents.

The Dietitian conducts periodic evaluations and survey inspections to identify deficiencies and develops and implements a corrective action plan. The Dietitian ensures all information related to nutritional service requirements and keeping a resident's environment safe and clean are implemented in accordance with the commitment to providing exceptional individualized quality care.

## Duties & Responsibilities

## Management and Leadership:

• Assesses the Clinical Nutritional needs of all residents of Glen Haven Manor upon admission and complete assessment follow up annually and as required. The Dietitian is also responsible for the planning, organizing of the menu and then reviewing or making changes based on the Nutritional Guide of Canada and all therapeutic diet programs.

• Recommends therapeutic diets, oral nutritional supplements, and texture modifications.

• Participates in resident care conferences and contributing to interdisciplinary care planning.

• Works closely with the nursing staff, including Director of Care; nurses and additional members of the care team, using an interdisciplinary approach to ensure coordinated nutritional support for residents.

• Educates residents, families, and staff on nutrition-related topics.

• Establishes and maintains high standards for employee performance and conducts performance reviews.

• Participates in the development and coordination of strategic planning.

• Provides effective leadership by ensuring that best practices protocols are implemented, practiced, upgraded, and maintained by duly qualified and licensed professionals.

• Responsible for the direction of site-based operations staff. This includes responsibilities regarding disciplinary matters, training, retraining, quality assurance and client satisfaction.

• Coordinates and provides accountabilities for all departmental activities to insure the effective and efficient delivery of services of the department including matters related client admissions, client service, family liaison, governmental liaison, accreditation, licensing, professional standards, and professional outsourcing of services required by the department.

• Accounts for the smooth, effective, and efficient operation of the department, and more particularly, to create and support a work environment conducive to a positive staff morale and a profession staff approach in all their interactions with clients, client families, co-workers, and the public at large.

• Facilitates coordination and communication of matters that have inter-departmental implication or impact.

• Provides leadership and participates in the various standing or ad hoc committees and teams with a commitment to continuously improve the standard of care or the general environment conducive to the delivery of quality care.

• Actively participates in the planning, organizing, and directing of the activities in Departments within the designated span of control. Observe all by-laws, rules, and regulations and the Facility's compliance with federal and provincial statutes and regulations.

• Communication on a routine basis with Senior Leaders/Managers, to advise the Administrator on matters pertinent to services and care within the organization.

• Participate in the public relations programs within the facility and community, with other facilities and community agencies.

• Participate in personal professional development.

• Develops, implements, and modifies policies and procedures.

• Instills a positive service-minded attitude and feeling of pride and responsibility in the Support Services staff by demonstrating a personal enthusiasm and team spirit.

• Accounts for the overall comfort and satisfaction of residents as it relates to departmental services.

## Quality Assurance and Compliance:

• Ensures departmental compliance with all requirements imposed including matters related to information management, policies, procedures, statutory requirements, and professional standards.

• Establish and maintain the standards of the Canadian Council on Accreditation for Health Care Facilities that are relevant to the profession for which there is line authority and ensures active participation in the Quality Assurance Programs of the facility.

• Performs an important role in the quality assurance process by performing inspections of all Nutritional services provided, and ensure compliance with all applicable statutory, regulatory or industry standards and codes. Reporting responsibilities include inspection reports, client satisfaction surveys, equipment inspections, daily team reports, project completion reports, and other quality assurance tasks.

## Safety Health & Environmental Affairs

• Complete all job tasks in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedures and Safe Work Practices and acknowledge health and safety as everyone's responsibility.

• Active participation in activities associated with the management of workplace safety, health and environmental affairs as endorsement of a progressive safety culture.

• Applies infection control practices and standards precautions, as required.

## Working Conditions

• Hours of Work - Monday to Friday (including evenings, weekends and holidays as determined by department & organizational need)

• Lead staff corrective action and disciplinary processes.

• Interface with residents, families, and visitors

• Report and respond to emergency situations.

## Physical Requirements

• Light to moderate working conditions

## Direct Reports

• Support Services Supervisor, Support Services Team consisting of Cooks and Nutritional Services Workers.

It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to the role.

Please quote the competition number and the Zone you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Us
The Fleet Services Division of the Department of Public Works is recruiting for a Mechanic II (Automotive Repair Technician) to join the Fleet Services team in Miller Lake.

This is your opportunity to become part of the team who are pivotal in ensuring the Public Works Fleet is running smoothly and safely. Without our Automotive Repair Technician's proactive measures, equipment issues or failures could lead to an interruption of services provided. As the Technician, you are one of our key team players who support the overall safety and efficiency of our provincial road network.

About Our Opportunity
Under the general supervision of the Shop Supervisor (Miller Lake), the Mechanic diagnoses equipment failure, repairs, rebuilds and makes adjustments to a variety of department vehicles.

Primary Accountabilities
The Mechanic uses specialized tools and equipment located in government facilities designed and equipped for mechanical work and assists with field repairs as required. The Mechanic may do any one or a combination of the following or other related duties as required to complete vehicle repairs, modifications and/or preventative maintenance. Some duties will consist of Mechanical Repairs, Internal Combustion / Diesel Engines, Fuel Systems, Engine Management Systems, Electrical, Electronic and Vacuum Control Systems, Power Train Systems, Anti-lock Braking Systems, Steering and Suspension Systems and Heating and Cooling Systems.

Qualifications and Experience
High School Diploma or GED and an Inter-Provincial Red Seal Certificate in the Automotive Service Trade plus a minimum of five (5) years diversified mechanical experience is required. A valid Nova Scotia's driver's license and mechanic tools are required upon hire. Provincial Red Seal Certificate of Qualification in Truck and Transport Repair, or Air Conditioning Certification would be considered assets.

A knowledge of computer-controlled engine diagnostic technology and competency as well as a general knowledge for determining paint codes and parts would be considered an asset along with demonstrated oral and written communication skills and the ability to work in a team environment.

A valid Nova Scotia driver's license and mechanic tools are required.

Upon hire, applicants will be required to successfully complete Nova Scotia Motor Vehicle Inspection (MVI) training as part of their probationary requirements.

Additional certification and skills considered an asset include:
• Provincial Certificate of Qualification in Truck and Transport, Autobody or Mechanical Trade;

• WHMIS;

• St. John Ambulance First Aid certification;

• Driver's License with Air Brake endorsement certificate;

• Knowledge of the Occupational Health & Safety Act;

• Knowledge of MVI regulations;

• Wheel Installation;

• I-Car (specific training unitized bodies); and

• Training in welding, pipe fitting, wiring and new paint types/application Forklift course.

In this role you consistently demonstrate initiative, remaining up to date in changes to equipment, methods and technology within the mechanical field. Strong communication skills are necessary for the times when you will be helping staff diagnose and resolve equipment issues. You must also be able to work effectively with minimal supervision as most of your time will be spent working independently. Professionalism and a high standard for client and customer service is required.

You will be assessed on the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: practical driving test, written examination, interview, and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

This position is based at the Miller Lake mechanical branch and does not typically require travel. Occasional travel for training or support at other branches may be required.

Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by noise, fumes, dust, grease/oil, used oil, chemical/cleaning substances such as brake cleaner and solvents; vibration from impact tools; extreme working temperatures related to work with engine coolants and torches; and at times adverse weather conditions while operating in a field environment.

description:
Employment Opportunity

## Community Healing Coordinator

Position Title
Community Healing Coordinator

Department
Health

Salary
$70,000 per annum

Term
Full-Time/Term Position/1 Year

Location
Dependant on the successful candidate's location

Estimated Start Date
November 2026

Wasoqopa'q First Nation (formerly Acadia First Nation) is governed as a custom band under the provisions of the Indian Act with established bylaws, policies and procedures. The First Nation's electoral system constitutes an election once every five (5) years with positions for one Chief and eight (8) councillors. Chief and Council elect, are the governing body responsible for making decisions for the overall health and well-being of communities, Elders, youth and families.

Wasoqopa'q First Nation is unique in its geographical composition, spread throughout the Southwestern regions of Nova Scotia spanning five counties from Yarmouth to Halifax, encompassing six (6) reserves - Yarmouth, Ponhook, Medway, Wildcat, Gold River, and Hammonds Plains, in both rural and urban settings. To support administration and business operations, Wasoqopa'q First Nation, with supporting staff, provides programs and services within two (2) Health Centres, a Youth Centre, two (2) Community Centres, six (6) administration offices, and six (6) business establishments, including economic development, education, employment, fishing, forestry, health, housing & maintenance, human resources, and social.

## Position Overview and Objective

WFN is currently recruiting for a Community Healing Coordinator, reporting to the Health Director, responsible for fostering culturally safe, strength-based community led initiatives that build capacity, resilience, wellness and crisis readiness, through the facilitation of engagement, coordinating resources, supporting shared learning through a Community of Practice. Working collaboratively with community leadership, Health Director, wellness teams, Elders, Knowledge Keepers, service partners, and the Tajikeim Mental Wellness Team, the Coordinator contributes and advances the Healing Through Loss Framework development work.

## Essential Functions and Duties

• Coordinate access to information, resources, and culturally safe supports during crisis situations

• Promote culturally grounded approaches to grief, loss, traditional healing, resilience, and shared access to Mi'kmaw resources

• Act as a primary point of contact for employees requesting support related to addressing client crisis, grief, loss, trauma, and wellness concerns

• Support WFN in identifying immediate needs, long-term wellness and crisis response goals for healing

• Work with the Healing Through Loss Tajikeim'k Lead to support WFN community engagement, implementation, and evaluation of the Healing Through Loss Framework

• Facilitate engagement sessions, plan meetings, follow-up activities, and implementation plans that reflect community priorities

• Build relationships with wellness teams, community organizations, service providers, and external partners.

• Serve as a liaison between WFN, Tajikeim'k, and regional service providers

• Support knowledge sharing, collaboration, and ongoing Community of Practice meetings focused on crisis response, healing, and mental wellness

• Work with community, and other Community Healing Coordinators in the development of community support mapping work

• Identify training, education, coaching, mentorship, and resource-sharing opportunities that strengthen community wellness and crisis response

• Assist in co-developing culturally relevant tools, resources, and educational materials

• Promote trauma-informed, culturally safe, and community-led practices for loss, grief, crisis, and healing to support front line teams in their wellness

• Maintain records of engagement activities, implementation progress, outcomes, and identifying emerging community needs

• Collect feedback to support continuous improvement and identify service gaps

• Prepare reports, briefing materials, recommendations, and updates for leadership and partners

• Work with the Tajikeim'k Mental Wellness Team to plan, implement, and evaluate workforce wellness initiatives

• Foster peer learning, mentorship, collaboration, and strategies to address vicarious trauma impacts, compassion fatigue, psychological safety and workplace stress

• Work with community partners, Elders, and Knowledge Keepers to strengthen staff wellness, self-care, reflective practice, resilience, and crisis preparedness

• Adhere to all Wasoqopa'q First Nation (WFN) Policies, Procedures and necessary procedures, as required

• Working in a team environment, other duties, training and activities, as required

## Qualifications

• Degree in Social Work, Public Health, Community Development, Indigenous Studies, Mental Health and Addictions, or a related field

• Minimum 2-3 years' experience in community mental wellness, crisis response, Indigenous health, or community development

• Experience working respectfully with Elders, Knowledge Keepers, community members, and partners

• Strong understanding of mental wellness, grief, loss, trauma-informed care, suicide intervention principles, crisis response, and community healing practices

• Knowledge of L'nu culture, traditions, healing practices, and culturally safe service delivery

• Knowledge of the Mi'kmaw language is an asset

• First Aid CPR, WHMIS and OHS are considered an asset

• Criminal Record Check and Vulnerable Sector Check required

• Child Abuse Registry Check required

## Required Abilities, Skills and Competencies

• Strong interpersonal, facilitation, and communication skills

• Ability to collaborate with communities, health teams, educators, service providers, and external partners

• Ability to evaluate programs and activities and adjust approaches to support positive outcomes

• A commitment to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of diversity, equity and inclusion

## Working Conditions

• Office Hours of work occur 8:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Thursday, inclusive, circumstances may arise that require evenings and or weekends, altering weekly work schedules

• Travel may be required to attend meetings

• A valid driver's license is required, as is access to a vehicle

• Occasionally, travel and meetings may fall outside of the regular office hours

• Travel to the other location requires driving for significant periods of time

## Application Requirements

Submit Cover Letter and Resume to resumes@wasoqopaq.ca

**Please quote #COMMUNITYHEALINGCOORDINATOR on your cover letter and indicate your salary expectations for this position.

WFN appreciates the interest of all applicants, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. WFN does not assume candidate expenses related to this recruitment process.

In accordance with the Aboriginal Employment Preference Policy of the Canadian Human Rights Commission, if all qualifications are equal, preference will be given to persons of Aboriginal ancestry and if a Wasoqopa'q First Nation Band member.

Deadline to Apply: OCTOBER 22, 2026

We value the contributions that each person brings, and are committed to ensuring equal opportunity and participation as part of the WFN team.

title: Expression of Interest: Pay Band 4/5 - Federal-Provincial-Territorial Secretariat Opportunity
description:
NEW BRUNSWICK HOUSING CORPORATION

EXPRESSION OF INTEREST: Pay Band 4/5
Open Competition - Temporary Opportunity
Federal-Provincial-Territorial Secretariat Opportunity

Housing New Brunswick (HNB) is seeking expressions of interest from Pay Band 4 and 5 employees for roles in contributing to the development of an FPT Secretariat. Over the next few years, HNB will be preparing to assume a stronger leadership role in FPT housing collaboration, requiring strong coordination, policy analysis, strategic advice, and relationship management across many levels of government. This initiative aims to identify employees for temporary assignments, projects, development opportunities, or future roles within the evolving Secretariat.

## About the Opportunity:

The FPT Secretariat will help advance New Brunswick's housing priorities through effective intergovernmental coordination, clear advice to senior leaders, and timely support for national and regional housing discussions. The Secretariat will work closely with HNB teams, partners across the Government of New Brunswick, federal departments and other provinces and territories. This is an opportunity to gain exposure to high-priority intergovernmental work, strengthen briefing and policy skills, and contribute directly to Housing New Brunswick's readiness for future FPT leadership responsibilities while helping to shape a team that will become increasingly important to the organization over the coming years.

## Key Areas of Work:

• Support preparation for FPT, Provinces and Territories (PT), Assistant Deputy Minister (ADM), Deputy Minister and Minister-level meetings, including briefing notes, speaking notes, agendas, decision materials, and follow-up summaries.

• Leadership and collaboration on national working groups, including organizing facilitating and driving the agenda for multi-jurisdictional meetings to align strategic housing initiatives across regions.

• Development and delivery of high impact presentations for senior executives, intergovernmental partners, and stakeholder forums. Presentations must effectively communicate key insights, progress metrics, and strategic opportunities, and should reflect a high standard of analytical and visual clarity.

• Track federal, provincial and territorial housing developments, commitments, risks and opportunities relevant to New Brunswick.

• Coordinate input from HNB divisions and other departments to support clear and consistent provincial positions.

• Assist with federal agreement management, action plans, reporting, claims, performance tracking and related governance materials.

• Cross-jurisdictional analysis and reporting: includes performing in-depth jurisdictional analysis of housing policies, funding allocations, and performance outcomes and will involve synthesizing complex data sets to provide evidence-based insights and recommendations to senior leadership and working groups.

• Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal and external partners.

## Need to have:

• A bachelor's degree in business, sociology, or a related field and four (4) or five (5) years of related work experience. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

• Written and spoken competence in English and French is required. Some positions only require English. Please state your language capability.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please ensure that preferred language for assessment is identified on your resume.

## Behavioral Competencies:

The successful candidate will possess the following leadership competencies:

• Strategic Thinking

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Relationship / Network Building

• Analytical Thinking/Judgment

• Organizational Awareness

## Technical Competencies:

The successful candidate will possess the following technical competencies:

• Policy and Research Analysis

• Planning and Organizing Skills

• Written Communication

• Consulting Skills

• Project Management

## Who Should Apply

This opportunity may be a good fit for employees who are curious, organized, collaborative and interested in housing policy, federal funding programs and intergovernmental work, even if they do not have direct FPT experience. Candidates should be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, managing competing deadlines, synthesizing information, and preparing clear written materials for senior decision-makers.

Ideal candidates will bring some combination of the following:

• Strong writing, research and analytical skills with good judgment, discretion and attention to detail.

• Experience preparing briefing notes, decision documents, meeting materials or policy advice.

• Ability to work across teams and build effective relationships.

• Intergovernmental relations or corporate coordination.

• Ability to organize information, track commitments and support follow-up on complex files.

• Comfort working with ambiguity and helping build new processes as the Secretariat develops.

Employees are encouraged to discuss their interest with their manager before applying.

Submitting an expression of interest does not ensure placement but may identify employees for future opportunities based on organizational needs and feasibility.

Interested employees are asked to submit a brief expression of interest outlining:

• Why you are interested in supporting the FPT Secretariat.

• Relevant experience, skills or strengths you would bring to the work.

• Any areas of development you are hoping to strengthen through this opportunity.

## Wage:

Pay Band 4 - $ 59, 644 - $ 83, 408 annually.
Pay Band 4 - $ 68, 276 - $ 95, 342 annually.

## How to apply:

We encourage applicants to apply online at www.ere.gnb.ca, by mail at the following address, or by email at HumanResources.sd@gnb.ca by October 9, 2026, indicating competition number R37-2026-27-20. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

title: Director, Public Transit
description:
Job Title: Director, Public Transit
Location: Moncton, New Brunswick
TP - CMC - 10143

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is proud to partner with the City of Moncton in the search for a Director, Public Transit to lead Codiac Transpo through an exciting period of growth, modernization, and regional collaboration.

Serving the communities of Moncton, Dieppe, and Riverview, Codiac Transpo is a vital public service that connects residents to employment, education, healthcare, recreation, and community life. As one of Atlantic Canada's leading transit systems, Codiac Transpo is focused on delivering safe, reliable, accessible, and customer-focused transportation services while advancing a Council-approved Transit Growth Strategy that will shape the future of mobility across the region.

This is a unique leadership opportunity to guide a growing transit organization through significant operational, technological, and infrastructure investments, including service expansion, fleet modernization, and the development of future transit facilities.

Role Description
The Director of Public Transit provides strategic and operational leadership for Codiac Transpo. You will oversee all aspects of transit operations including service delivery, fleet and infrastructure management, financial planning, administration, customer service, safety, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Leading a team of approximately 120 employees, including five direct-report managers, you will be responsible for ensuring the delivery of high-quality transit services while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and service excellence. This role requires a leader who can balance long-term strategic priorities with day-to-day operational demands while building strong relationships with municipal leaders, elected officials, employees, union representatives, and community stakeholders.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Provide overall strategic and operational leadership for Codiac Transpo and its people, services, assets, and budgets.

• Lead the implementation of the Transit Growth Strategy, including route expansion, service enhancements, and operational improvements.

• Oversee all transit functions including operations, finance, fleet management, infrastructure, technology, administration, and customer service.

• Manage operating and capital budgets while ensuring effective stewardship of public resources.

• Lead major capital projects, including fleet expansion and replacement initiatives, transit technology investments, and future transit facility development.

• Develop, mentor, and support a high-performing leadership team while fostering a positive and inclusive workplace culture.

• Promote strong labour-management relationships and provide leadership within a unionized working environment.

• Monitor operational performance, safety, customer experience, and service reliability while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.

• Collaborate with municipal partners in Moncton, Dieppe, and Riverview on service planning, governance matters, cost-sharing discussions, and regional transit initiatives.

• Provide recommendations and presentations to senior leadership, municipal councils, and the Public Transit Governance Committee.

• Build strong relationships with community partners, elected officials, regulators, and industry stakeholders.

• Support the adoption of innovative technologies, systems, and best practices to improve operational effectiveness and customer service.

## Your Qualifications:

The ideal candidate is a collaborative and forward-thinking leader who is passionate about public service and committed to delivering safe, reliable, and sustainable transit solutions. You have demonstrated success leading complex operations while motivating teams through growth and change.

## Your qualifications will include:

• A post-secondary degree in business administration, public administration, transportation, engineering, planning, or a related discipline. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.

• 10+ years of progressive leadership experience within public transit, transportation, municipal operations, or a similarly complex service environment.

• Direct experience within public transit operations, transit planning, or transportation services.

• Experience managing large teams and developing high-performing leaders.

• Demonstrated success operating within a unionized environment.

• Strong financial acumen with experience overseeing operating and capital budgets.

• Experience leading organizational change, service improvements, and strategic initiatives.

• Exceptional interpersonal, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.

• Strong problem-solving, negotiation, and decision-making abilities.

• The ability to balance competing priorities while maintaining a focus on customer service, safety, and operational excellence.

• Valid driver's licence.

## Assets include:

• Senior leadership experience within a municipal transit organization.

• Experience implementing transit growth strategies or major service expansion initiatives.

• Experience overseeing fleet modernization, fleet replacement, or transit infrastructure projects.

• Knowledge of emerging transit technologies and industry best practices.

• Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset.

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a critical public service during a transformative period of growth and investment. You will play a key role in shaping the future of public transportation across Greater Moncton while working alongside dedicated employees, municipal leaders, and community partners committed to building a more connected region.

Competition # : 49992

Department: Public Works

Location: MILLER LAKE

Zone: Miller Lake Mechanical Branch

Type of Employment: Year Round

Union Status: CUPE - NSPG

Closing Date: 08-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

Under Article 13 of the Collective Agreement between the Nova Scotia Department of Public Works and the Canadian Union of Public Employees, Local 1867, the following opportunity is being posted.

Please quote the competition number and the Zone you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Us
At the Department of Public Works we are responsible for building and maintaining a sustainable provincial infrastructure for Nova Scotians. From highways and bridges to government buildings and registration of vehicles, safety and quality of life are top of mind. We support Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways, 4,100 bridges, and 9 provincial ferries.
Our Fleet Services Division is pivotal in ensuring Public Work's Fleet is running smoothly; ensuring the safety of our provincial road network.

About Our Opportunity
We will ensure you have the right tools to do the job, and there is nothing more important than your safety. You have a clean workspace, and your ideas and input are valued and considered. Your coveralls and other personal protective equipment (PPE) are provided, as are the larger shared tools available in our fully stocked inventory tool room. We also have an annual footwear and tool reimbursement allowance; as you must bring your own mechanical tools.

Primary Accountabilities
Under the general supervision of the Fleet Service Coordinator, the Mechanic II diagnoses equipment failure, repairs, rebuilds and adjusts a variety of government mobile machinery and equipment used to perform road maintenance activities for both summer and winter operations. You will use specialized tools and equipment located at a government facility designed and equipped for mechanical work, assist with field repairs as required, and other related duties as required to complete equipment repairs, modifications and/or preventative maintenance.

Qualifications and Experience
Some high school and an Inter-Provincial Red Seal Certificate of Qualification in Truck and Transport plus a minimum of five (5) years of diversified mechanical experience.
Upon hire, applicants will be required to successfully complete Nova Scotia Motor Vehicle Inspection (MVI) training as part of their probationary requirements.

A valid Class 5 drivers' license is a condition of employment, and an acceptable driver abstract must be submitted before employment begins. Air Brake endorsement is an asset.

Knowledge of computer-controlled engine diagnostic technology and competency as well as general knowledge of computers is required. Demonstrated oral and written communication skills and the ability to work in a team environment.

An Inter-Provincial Red Seal Certificate of Qualification in (Heavy Duty) Equipment, Air Conditioning Certification and Air Brake Endorsement would be considered assets. Completion of training and knowledge of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, First Aid and WHMIS are further assets to be considered.
You consistently demonstrate initiative in your role; remaining up to date in changes to equipment, methods and technology within the mechanical field. Your exceptional communication skills will assist you when working with staff to help diagnose and resolve equipment issues. You are a self-motivated individual who works both independently with minimal supervision and participates fully as an effective team player. You consistently maintain a professional and courteous disposition and hold a high standard for clients.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
This position is based at the Miller Lake mechanical branch and does not typically require travel. Occasional travel for training or support at other branches may be required.

Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by noise, smoke and gas fumes and at times adverse weather conditions while operating in a field environment. Considerable standing, lifting, carrying and moving about is a requirement of this position.

Additional Information
These two (2) opportunities are for Year-Round positions based out of the Miller Lake mechanical branch.

These opportunities are for 52-week Year-Round positions – the duties of which are full time and continuous in nature.

You must bring your own mechanical tools.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless Career Paths.

title: Team Lead Drop-in- 6 Month Term Opportunity
description:
## Full Time Term: Team Lead Drop-in

## About the Opportunity

Shelter Nova Scotia is offering employment for a 6 month project to expand our walk- in service at The Hub, located at 101-5506 Cunard Street, to 5 days of service per week. The project will run with an emphasis on collecting data on client needs, program usage and trends for the purpose of informing the business case to expand The Hub program permanently.

## This is a 6 month term opportunity

## Requirements

• Post secondary experience or degree in Social Sciences, Social Work, Human Services or a Diploma from a recognized educational institution with relevant experience such as human services, social services, healthcare, or a combination of education and experience is required

• Certification in the following or the ability to obtain: Standard First Aid/CPR Level "C"; Non-Violent Crisis Intervention; Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (ASIST); Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS); Safe Food Handlers certification

• Successfully obtain Child Abuse Registry check and/or Government of Canada Personnel Screening or Criminal Record Check

## About the Facility

The Hub supports people who are experiencing homelessness through a connection to Coordinated Access System (CAS), support with housing applications, and provides food, clothing, shower, and laundry access (laundry and shower are intended for those who sleep outside). It also serves as a space to build connection and belonging among those who are housed but experiencing isolation and loneliness. The Hub also administers a fund to disperse to people in need of non-recurring prevention and diversion funds.

## Compensation: $36 an hour + 4% vacation

## Hours of Work

40 hours per week, includes days, evenings, weekends.

Tentative schedule- Sun/Mon 09:00-17:00 and Tues/Wed/Thurs 12:30-20:30

## Deadline to apply: Thursday October 8th 2026 at 8:00am.

Shelter Nova Scotia is committed to building a diverse and inclusive community without judgement. We value people for who they are, the uniqueness they bring and the opportunities to learn from our differences. We welcome applications from members of diverse communities.

description:

2025532

Canadian Union of Public Employees

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

Salary: As per collective agreement.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Emergency Medical Technicians are based on the current Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements for Emergency Medical Technician as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our emergency medical technicians provide transportation and patient care for non-urgent low acuity patients and are expected to maintain and operate ambulances and related equipment in accordance with patient needs and public safety.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in emergency medical technology or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• High school graduation plus an Emergency Medical Technician program/course

• Must meet all legislated requirements for Emergency Medical Technician in New Brunswick

• Must be registered, active Emergency Medical Technician with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

• Written & Spoken competency in one of the two official languages (English or French) is required and spoken competency in the other official language is preferred.

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your EMT certificate from a recognized institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as an Emergency Medical Technician within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR Level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community submit your application.

title: Director, Operational Services
description:
Job Title: Director, Operational Services
Location: Truro, Nova Scotia
TP - CHI - 10141

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with Chignecto-Central Regional Centre for Education (CCRCE) in the recruitment of a Director, Operational Services to join their Executive Leadership Team in Truro, Nova Scotia.

CCRCE serves approximately 20,000 students and employs more than 4,000 staff across 65 schools throughout central and northern Nova Scotia. As one of the province's largest public education organizations, CCRCE is committed to providing inclusive, safe, healthy, and supportive learning environments that enable student success. The Operational Services Department oversees a diverse operational portfolio that includes school facilities, student transportation, health and safety, capital projects, infrastructure planning, and responsibilities as landlord for several leaseholds, in support of schools and communities across the region.

## Role Description

Reporting to the Regional Executive Director, the Director, Operational Services provides strategic leadership and oversight for Property Services, Student Transportation, infrastructure, and Health & Safety across the region. Leading a team of approximately 500 employees and overseeing an operational budget of approximately $60 million, the Director is responsible for ensuring the effective delivery of operational services that support schools, students, staff, and communities.

This role serves as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team and requires a leader who can balance strategic planning with a visible, hands-on approach to leadership. Working closely with senior administrators, school leaders, government partners, contractors, consultants, and community stakeholders, the Director will help shape the future of CCRCE.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Providing leadership and oversight for Property Services, Student Transportation, and Health & Safety.

• Serving as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, contributing to organizational planning and decision-making across the Regional Centre.

• Leading and developing multidisciplinary operational teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.

• Overseeing transportation services supporting more than 13,000 students daily through a fleet of approximately 200 buses.

• Directing facilities operations, maintenance programs, custodial services, and infrastructure investments across more than 3.8 million square feet of educational and support facilities.

• Developing and managing significant operational and capital budgets while ensuring responsible stewardship of public resources.

• Leading long-range capital planning, major repairs, renovations, construction projects, and infrastructure renewal initiatives.

• Monitoring operational performance, service levels, and departmental effectiveness to ensure high-quality service delivery.

• Ensuring compliance with procurement requirements, purchasing policies, tendering processes, regulatory obligations, and health and safety standards.

• Building strong relationships with principals, school communities, contractors, municipalities, consultants, government agencies, and other stakeholders.

• Providing leadership within a unionized environment, including labour relations matters and participation in collective bargaining activities.

• Supporting emergency management planning, operational continuity, school closure decisions, and transportation service interruption protocols across the region.

## Your Qualifications

As the ideal candidate, you are a collaborative and highly visible operational leader who combines strategic thinking with a practical, solutions-oriented approach. You have experience leading large teams, managing complex operations, and building strong relationships within public-facing organizations.

## Your qualifications include:

• Post-secondary education in engineering, operations management, facilities management, business, public administration, or another discipline relevant to operational leadership.

• 5+ years of management experience, combined with 5+ years of experience overseeing large-scale operations, infrastructure, facilities, transportation, fleet management, public works, healthcare operations, education operations, or similar complex environments.

• Demonstrated success leading large, diverse teams and managing significant operational budgets.

• Experience working within a unionized environment and a strong understanding of labour relations and collective agreements.

• Working knowledge of provincial building and fire code requirements, accessibility standards, environmental and regulatory compliance, and the Occupational Health and Safety Act.

• Experience with procurement, purchasing policies, tendering processes, contract administration, and supplier management.

• Strong project management, strategic planning, and organizational leadership capabilities.

• Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement, and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to lead organizational change while maintaining a strong focus on service delivery and operational excellence.

• Valid driver's licence and ability to travel throughout the region.

## Assets include:

• Engineering background.

• A professional designation, such as P.Eng., CPMM, FMP or PMP, or eligibility for professional registration, is an asset.

• Experience in public education, municipal government, public works, healthcare, transportation, fleet management, facilities management, or other large public-sector organizations.

• Experience leading major capital construction, infrastructure renewal, or asset management programs.

## Why CCRCE?

This is a unique opportunity to lead one of the largest operational portfolios in Nova Scotia's public education sector. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, you will help shape the infrastructure, transportation systems, and operational services that support approximately 20,000 students and 4,000 employees across the region.

CCRCE offers a comprehensive total rewards package, including a competitive salary, defined benefit pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, generous vacation entitlement, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a values-driven public service organization.

title: Senior Analyst, Market Intelligence
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Senior Analyst,Market Intelligence, to join our Commercial Team in Toronto, Ontario.

This is a permanent hybrid position.

As a Senior Market Analyst, you will provide market intelligence and strategic insights across Vale Base Metals' portfolio. You will conduct macroeconomic, commodity, and pricing analysis, develop market supply and demand forecasts, and assess competitive dynamics to support business planning and commercial decision-making.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Market, you will play a key role in identifying market opportunities and risks while helping shape strategic initiatives through data-driven analysis and research.

## Key Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain commodity market supply and demand models, including market balances, market segments and regional trends.

• Analyze macroeconomic indicators, commodity prices, premiums, derivatives, and policy developments impacting global markets.

• Conduct competitive intelligence research on industry participants, projects, and market developments.
