Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) for a full-time position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants/Emergency Medical Responder (EMR). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR).

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) until the ACP position is filled.

Job Summary
The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of Paramedicine. The base for this service is located at Witless Bay AB Base.

Duties/Job Demands
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications
• Graduation from High School or equivalent;
• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

The primary purpose of the Nurse Practitioner (NP) is to provide comprehensive healthcare, as a member of a collaborative team to our Oncology patients. title: Integration Specialist
description:
Bluedrop Training & Simulation Inc. (BTSI) develops advanced training and simulation solutions for the aerospace and defense industry. Our team designs and delivers high-performance virtual and mixed reality training systems used by front-line operators in complex and demanding environments.

As an Integration Specialist, you will play a key role in integrating, configuring, testing, and supporting advanced simulation and training systems throughout the product lifecycle. You will work closely with systems engineering, software development, and production teams to incorporate a variety of third-party hardware and software technologies into our simulation products.

This role combines hands-on technical integration work with customer-facing field support responsibilities and requires occasional travel to customer and test sites.

Qualifications
• Minimum of 2 years of relevant industry experience

• Bachelor's degree in a technical field is preferred

• Strong working knowledge of Windows operating systems, system configuration, and troubleshooting

• Familiarity with software and system concepts including operating systems, networking, and system performance metrics such as CPU usage, memory utilization, network throughput, and bottleneck analysis

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues

• Strong attention to detail and ability to manage timelines and expectations

• Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment

• Comfortable working in customer-facing environments and travelling to remote customer sites as required

## Nice to Have:

• Familiarity with networking concepts including TCP/IP, switching, routing, and network troubleshooting

• Experience with software and system testing

• Experience with scripting or software development (e.g. Python, PowerShell, C++, C#)

• IT support or systems administration experience

• Experience working with Virtual Reality (VR) or Mixed Reality (MR) hardware and tracking systems

• Experience with military simulation platforms such as VBS3/VBS4 or Arma, including mission creation, terrain modification, or basic scripting

• Experience integrating third-party hardware and software systems

Responsibilities
• Configure and integrate hardware and software components using vendor-provided documentation and internal procedures

• Develop and maintain system setup, configuration, and support documentation

• Troubleshoot system-level hardware, software, networking, and integration issues

• Perform root cause analysis and develop corrective solutions for identified problems

• Collaborate with software, systems, and production teams during integration and product development activities

• Participate in system architecture discussions, design reviews, and technical documentation activities

• Conduct feature, regression, and integration testing across simulation products

• Evaluate and recommend hardware and software technologies based on system requirements

• Work directly with third-party technology vendors to resolve integration and support issues

• Provide remote and on-site support for deployed customer systems

• Deliver customer training, field support, and product demonstrations

• Travel to customer and test sites as required

## What's in it For You?

• Work on advanced VR/MR simulation and training systems used in demanding operational environments

• Collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams across software, systems, and production

• Exposure to cutting-edge simulation, visualization, and training technologies

• Opportunities for hands-on field support, customer interaction, and technical growth

• Competitive compensation, benefits, and career development opportunities

• Flexible work arrangements and a collaborative team environment

• Opportunity to contribute directly to products used by global aerospace and defense customers

Posted Date: 2024-12-20

Closing Date: Open until filled.

## Definition of Work:

This position will support the Primary Care Neighborhood (PCN) in the Coast of Bays. A Primary Care Neighborhood is a geographic area where all community based primary healthcare providers function as an interconnected team in delivering the care patients require. As a member of the PCN, the successful candidate will work collaboratively to provide team based comprehensive, patient centered, and culturally safe healthcare to meet the needs of patients and communities. PCNs will enable the delivery of a range of quality care for patients within their own communities while facilitating interdisciplinary work amongst healthcare providers.
The philosophy of a Primary Care Neighborhood is to deliver care that is patient-centered, comprehensive, team-based, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety. This philosophy of health care encourages providers and care teams to meet patients where they are. The Primary Care Neighborhood is a place where patients are treated with respect, dignity, and compassion, and enable strong and trusting relationships with providers and staff. This is a model for achieving primary care excellence so that care is received in the right place, at the right time, and in the manner that best suits a patient's needs.
Definition of Work:
This physiotherapy position is a highly independent clinical position with the primary purpose of facilitating optimal physical performance of clients with a wide variety of physical, or environmentally induced impairments utilizing the models of best practice and developed pathways. Proficiency in all practice areas will be required as this is a multifaceted position. In consultation with the primary care team, clinical work involves screening of referrals, client assessment, development of client centered goals and intervention plans, coordination of other services and completion of all required documentation. This position may also require travel and the utilization of virtual technologies in supporting the clientele within the neighborhood.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care; demonstrate a commitment to continuous quality improvement and demonstrate a commitment to safety partnering with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Required qualifications:
• Graduated from a School of Physiotherapy approved by Central Health.
• Current registration with the Canadian Physiotherapy Association and the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Physiotherapists.
• A minimum of 3 years (within the last 5 years) of Physiotherapy.
• Demonstrated experience and knowledge of development and program evaluation.
• Demonstrated research, analytical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
• Consistent demonstration of NLHS core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence (I CARE)
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

title: Senior Legislative Policy Analyst (Planning & Development Officer 3)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 49914

Department: Health and Wellness

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 14-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Department of Health and Wellness offers opportunities to grow and advance in a dynamic sector that touches the lives of all Nova Scotians. Along with our partners, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority and the IWK Health Centre, we are committed to continually improving our health care system. With a focus on collaborative primary health care, continuing care, improved supports for mental health and addictions, digital health, capital infrastructure, and more, the department is thinking differently about how to plan, fund, legislate and monitor to improve access and service delivery. To do this, we're recruiting leaders at all levels of the organization who embrace a challenge and believe in their ability to make a difference.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Manager, Health Profession Regulation, the Senior Legislative Policy Analyst works within the Health Workforce Policy and Partnerships team, providing legislative and policy expertise and oversight related to best practices in regulating health professions. The position supports the design, development, and implementation of legislation, regulations, and policies that strengthen the health workforce, including implementation of the Regulated Health Professions Act (2023).
Your work plan will include managing projects to develop new regulations; building relationships with external stakeholders, such as health profession regulatory bodies, employers—including NSH, IWK, and continuing care organizations—educational institutions, and professional associations; and conducting strategic analysis and developing policy options to support the government's health-system transformation priorities related to health profession oversight. This work will include updating scopes of practice and improving licensing and professional conduct frameworks.
As the Senior Legislative Policy Analyst, you will play a critical role in supporting senior leaders through process-driven, evidence-informed decision-making. At times, you will work closely with government colleagues on intersecting health profession initiatives and may be required to engage in departmental, interdepartmental, and/or federal-provincial-territorial working groups.
Your expertise and ability to adapt quickly within a highly complex system will be essential to navigating detailed regulatory and consultative processes.

Primary Accountabilities
In this role you will make a significant contribution to the organization. Key responsibilities of this role include:

• Researching best practices in health profession regulation and government oversight of regulatory bodies.

• Liaising with Nova Scotia's 19 health profession regulatory bodies on emerging issues and government initiatives.

• Preparing briefing notes and correspondence for senior officials on a broad range of health profession regulation matters.

• Collaborating with internal and external partners to develop and evaluate policy options and provide strategic recommendations on health profession legislation and regulations, including through reports, briefing materials, and submissions to Executive Council.

• Providing advice to colleagues on health profession regulation and stakeholder relations.

• Leading and/or participating in working groups focused on health profession policy issues and supporting consultation activities as required.

• Monitoring the introduction and passage of legislation affecting health profession regulation.

Qualifications and Experience
To be considered for this opportunity, you must hold a bachelor's degree in public policy, political science, law, a health-related field, or a related discipline, plus eight years of experience designing, developing, reviewing, and/or implementing policies or programs.
Legal education and registration as a regulated health professional are considered assets.
As part of your application, you must demonstrate experience in the following areas:

• Progressive position responsibility.

• Superior verbal and written communication skills, with experience preparing reports and briefing materials.

• Strong leadership skills, sound judgement, initiative and an ability to build collaborative working relationships.

• Experience working with multiple internal and/or external stakeholders to advance shared priorities.

• Extensive experience in public policy development, including conducting complex research, policy analysis, and implementation.

• Strong interpersonal and negotiation skills, with the ability to work collaboratively in a dynamic team environment.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

You must be highly organized and able to manage change, competing priorities, and tight deadlines while working collaboratively and completing complex assignments with minimal supervision.

The following will be considered assets:

• Knowledge of government structures, legislative processes, public policy principles, health profession regulation, and the health care system.

• Knowledge of or experience in professional regulation or government regulatory oversight.

• Experience planning or leading complex consultations.

• Experience working in the health care system.

• Experience developing and monitoring business or strategic plans.

We will assess these qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following methods: a written examination, standardized testing, an oral presentation, an interview, and reference checks.

Equivalency
An equivalent combination of training, education and experience will be considered. Equivalencies may include, but are not limited to:

• A completed Masters degree and 6 years of related experience

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Most of your work is in a comfortable office environment. You may be required to travel. There is a need for you to balance competing priorities and meet strict deadlines. Your normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day. You may be required to work overtime on occasion. Regularly reads and interprets multiple sources of information, regular requirement to type, read and work on a computer.

Additional Information
This is a TERM employment opportunity with anticipated end date of May 31, 2028. The appointment status ('term', 'temporary' or 'casual') is dependent on the start date of the successful candidate.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

• A dynamic, client-focused office environment where service excellence and teamwork are our focus.

Pay Grade: PR 17

title: Electrical Engineering Technologist
description:
## About Novate

We are a specialized electrical engineering consulting firm focused on delivering high quality design, analysis, and technical support for municipal, industrial, and infrastructure projects. Our work includes control systems, power distribution, automation, instrumentation, and commissioning support for clients across Nova Scotia. We are growing and looking to add a motivated Electrical Engineering Technologist to support our design team.

This role is ideal for graduates of the NSCC Electrical Engineering Technology program (or similar programs) with relevant industry experience being an asset.

## Position Overview

The Electrical Engineering Technologist will work closely with our engineers and designers to support the development of electrical control and power system designs, technical documentation, and field activities. This position includes both office-based/remote design work and occasional site visits.

## Key Responsibilities

Design & Drafting

• Prepare and update AutoCAD electrical drawings, including:
• Single-line diagrams

• Control schematics

• Wiring diagrams

• Panel layouts

• I/O lists and cable schedules

• Assist with electrical control system design, including control panel layouts, instrumentation integration, and motor control systems.

• Support power distribution design, including load calculations, equipment selection, and coordination with utilities.

Technical Analysis & Documentation

• Perform electrical studies, such as:
• Short-circuit analysis

• Arc flash calculations

• Load flow and voltage drop analysis

• Assist in preparing:
• Technical reports

• Specifications

• Bill of materials

• Submittal packages

• As-built documentation

• Cost estimates

• Maintain project documentation and ensure compliance with applicable codes and standards (CEC, CSA, utility requirements).

Project & Site Support

• Participate in site visits for data collection, inspections, and verification of existing conditions.

• Provide site administration support, including:
• Reviewing contractor work

• Responding to RFIs

• Tracking deficiencies

• Documenting progress

• Support commissioning activities, including:
• Equipment functional testing

• Control system verification

• Field troubleshooting

• Coordination with contractors and clients

Collaboration & Communication

• Work closely with engineers, project managers, and external stakeholders.

• Communicate clearly and professionally with clients, contractors, and suppliers.

• Contribute to internal design standards, templates, and continuous improvement initiatives.

## Qualifications

Required:

• Diploma in Electrical Engineering Technology (NSCC or equivalent).

• Strong proficiency with AutoCAD (AutoCAD Electrical experience considered an asset).

• Understanding of electrical control systems, power distribution, and industrial equipment.

• Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and technical documents.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Valid Nova Scotia driver's license and ability to travel to project sites.

Conditional Employment: The successful candidate may be required to provide a satisfactory criminal record check as a condition of employment, where required for client, project, or site access. Any information obtained will be considered confidentially and assessed in relation to the requirements of the position.

Assets:

• Experience in consulting engineering or industrial electrical environments.

• Familiarity with PLCs, SCADA systems, and instrumentation.

• Experience with electrical analysis software (e.g., ETAP, SKM, EasyPower).

• Knowledge of municipal or industrial project environments.

• CSA/CEC code knowledge and practical application experience.

## What We Offer

• Competitive salary based on experience.

• Health and benefits package.

• Opportunities for professional development, training, and certification.

• Flexible work environment with a mix of office, remote and field work.

• Exposure to a wide range of municipal and industrial projects.

• Supportive, collaborative team culture.

The philosophy of a Family Care Team (FCT) is to deliver care that is patient-centered, comprehensive, team-based, culturally safe, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety. This philosophy supports providers and care teams to meet clients where they are using an inter-professional collaborative approach where care is provided in the right place, at the right time, by the right provider in a manner that best suits the client’s need. The team will ensure clients are treated with respect, dignity, and compassion, and enable strong and trusting relationships with providers and staff. FCT’s will enable the delivery of a range of quality care for clients within their own communities while facilitating interdisciplinary work amongst healthcare providers. The FCT for the Baie Verte/ Springdale Family Care Team will cover both communities and the surrounding areas. This position will be based in Springdale.

There may also be a requirement to support services such as, but not limited to, Acute Care Services, Long Term Care, and Emergency Services which may include the Fast Track Stream of Care and Virtual Care Stream, and community teams.

Definition of work:
As part of the collaborative team, the Nurse Practitioner will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice in order to provide comprehensive assessment and care to clients and provide clinic leadership. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and quality of life through client attachment and client paneling to clinic providers, with the support and wrap around services of the full team. The successful applicant works independently in diagnosing conditions, prescribing medications, performing or ordering diagnostic tests and treatments, evaluating treatments and providing follow-up care in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team. The Nurse Practitioner provides comprehensive and holistic nursing care to clients including health promotion, injury and illness treatment and prevention, supportive, curative and rehabilitative care in a primary care practice setting. The Nurse Practitioner will document using the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). In this leadership role, the Nurse Practitioner will contribute to the ongoing program development, implementation, and evaluation of the FCT including client and clinician engagement. The role will encompass participating in clinic evaluations and continuous quality improvement processes based upon current best practice guidelines. Flexible hours are required (combination of days, evenings, and weekends required). The Nurse Practitioner will report to the Regional Director of Primary Health Care & Community Nursing in the Central Zone.
As an advanced practitioner, the Nurse Practitioner functions in the roles of practitioner, educator and leader. As governed by provincial regulations, he/she practices independently, collaborating with the primary care physicians in the area for issues outside the Nurse Practitioner scope of practice. Travel throughout the region may be required. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Required qualifications:
• Graduation from a Nurse Practitioner program approved by Central Health.
• Current registration as a Nurse Practitioner with the Association of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.
• Current BLS certification.
• Demonstrated knowledge of home and community health services.
• Demonstrated exceptional leadership qualities and problem-solving skills as well as oral and written communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to work well independently and in an interdisciplinary team environment.
• A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 5 Driver’s License.
• Consistent demonstration of the core values of NL Health Services: Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence (I CARE)
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory Certificate of Conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Demonstrated skill in using health care-based computer systems (CRMS, Meditech, EMR).
• Experience in the care and management of patients with diabetes, COPD, heart failure, and/or mental health disorders is an asset.
• Experience working in a Primary Health Care setting is an asset.

*Electronic Medical Records (EMR) training is required and will be provided upon hire.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services (NL Health Services) brings together five former separate health entities - Eastern Health, Central Health, Western Health, Labrador-Grenfell Health, and the Newfoundland and Labrador Centre for Health Information. The creation of a provincial health authority was announced following recommendations from Health Accord NL.

NL Health Services is responsible for delivering health and community services to more than 528,000 people living in Newfoundland and Labrador and employs over 21,000 people. NLHealthServices.ca

Definition of Work:
This is a clinical position in which the Social Worker II will work within the Bishop’s Falls Correctional Centre to provide individual and group counselling and work with the community mental health and addictions team in central zone. The incumbent will be expected to liaise with other team members within the community and other correctional facilities within the province, as required. The Social Worker II will collaborate with Corrections staff (i.e. Classification Officers) on referrals for community health services upon release.

The Social Worker II is expected to have strong decision-making abilities, and to function with a considerable degree of autonomy. As an integral member of the interdisciplinary team, the Social Worker II completes comprehensive psychosocial assessments, formulates treatment plans, provides therapeutic interventions and coordinates treatment with relevant community agencies. This involves working with clients, their families, team members, and community resources. Also integral to this position is the provision of psycho-education and therapeutic group programs related to sexual offences and other offences, including impaired driving. Funding to support additional training will be provided.

In addition to clinical responsibilities, the Social Worker II participates in a variety of administrative and community development activities with a focus on developing services for Correctional Health clients. Accountability is established through ongoing clinical recording and an annual peer audit.

The Social Worker II will also be expected to provide field instruction for Social Work students.

This position reports to the Program Coordinator for Correctional Health Services, and the Program Manager for Community Mental Health and Addictions Services in Central zone.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

description:
## Office Operations Manager
Halifax, NS
HL-NSSA-10176

The Nova Scotia Association of Architects (NSAA) is the self-governing professional association that is responsible for licensing and regulating the practice of architecture in Nova Scotia. Established in 1932 and mandated under The Architects Act, the NSAA protects the public interest through the regulation of architects and architectural firms across the province. The Association oversees licensure, professional standards, continuing professional development requirements, and regulatory compliance to protect the public and advance the professional practice of architecture.

We are pleased to be partnered with them to bring an Office Operations Manager to their team in Halifax, NS. Reporting to the Executive Director, the Office Operations Manager is responsible for the seamless administration and operation of the organization. This position provides executive support to the Executive Director while overseeing administrative systems, volunteer and committee support, member service administration, communications, records management, and special events.

The successful candidate will be a key operational resource, ensuring organizational effectiveness through strong planning, process improvement, support for partners and third-party collaborators of the organization, and demonstrating strong attention to detail. Working in a fast-paced environment, this role requires exceptional judgment, discretion, initiative, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high standard of professionalism and confidentiality.

## Responsibilities in this role will include:

• Coordinate administrative activities to ensure smooth day-to-day operations including responding to inquiries, triaging communications, replenishing all office supplies.

• Identify opportunities to improve office systems, processes, and administrative procedures to increase efficiency and service delivery.

Under Article 13 of the Collective Agreement between the Nova Scotia Department of Public Works and the Canadian Union of Public Employees, Local 1867, the following opportunity is being posted.

Please quote the competition number and the Zone you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Us
Maintaining our Provincial Infrastructure is no small job.

The Department of Public Works supports Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways and 4,100 bridges.

If you enjoy operating Heavy Equipment, and seeking your next opportunity where you will directly contribute to the safety of our province, we want to hear from you.

About Our Opportunity
Under the supervision of the Area Manager, the Equipment Operator Trainer supports the development of Equipment Operators. This role plays an essential part in Equipment Operator onboarding, seasonal preparation, documentation quality, and ensuring procedures are followed correctly.

Trainers are expected to work proactively and independently, using structured work plans aligned with operational priorities and seasonal demands. They collaborate closely with Area Managers, Operations Supervisors, Equipment Operators, and Equipment Instructors/Inspectors (EQIIs) to ensure training and documentation efforts are consistent, useful, and responsive to District needs.

This position provides structured and assigned training support and does not replace supervisory functions or routine peer-to-peer coaching that occurs among Equipment Operators as part of normal operations.

Primary Accountabilities
As an Equipment Operator Trainer, your role is pivotal in helping the public arrive safely at their destination. The main responsibilities of this position include:

• Actively monitoring and supporting Equipment Operator development, documenting progress and offering feedback to Supervisors

• Supporting the coaching of new and existing Equipment Operators on the safe performance of tasks such as plowing, ditching, ice blading, grading, and other equipment operations. Tracking progress of new Equipment Operators and supporting scheduling OPTP testing with EQII when Equipment Operators have achieved sufficient experience

• Ensuring Equipment Operators are following safety protocols while operating, including trip inspections, hazard assessments, protective equipment, and safe use of attachments

• Reporting serious or repeated performance concerns to the Operations Supervisor for action

• Preparing equipment for training, including ensuring it is operationally fit, trip inspections are complete, equipment is fuelled, attachments installed, etc.

• Providing hands-on instruction and demonstrations to ensure Equipment Operators are proficient in the safe and effective operation of machinery

Qualifications and Experience
To be eligible, you must have a High school diploma or GED equivalent and minimum 5 years of experience operating relevant equipment.

You must have access to a reliable motor vehicle and a class 3 Driver's License with Air Brake Endorsement and Condition 15 is required. Applicants must possess this license at the time of hire. A Class 1 license is considered an asset.

You must be able to demonstrate the ability to operate a wide variety of heavy equipment in all seasons and to work independently and manage priorities using structured task planning.

As the ideal candidate, you are flexible, self-motivated, and comfortable working in adverse weather conditions. As part of our team, you bring professionalism and hold a high standard for client service with proven organizational skills, including tracking training-related records and reviewing documentation such as logs and inspection forms and Computer literacy (e.g., digital forms, spreadsheets, email).

You will be assessed on the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: practical driving test on a tandem truck, written examination, interview, and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
You will be working in a range of weather conditions, from extreme heat to cold, and managing environmental hazards such as uneven terrain and slippery surfaces. The Equipment Operator Trainer may also need to work near moving traffic, which presents safety risks.

Occasionally, work may take place in areas with machinery, resulting in exposure to smoke and fumes. The role also involves environments with elevated levels of noise, dust, and vibration. These conditions require a high level of adaptability and situational awareness to ensure safety and efficiency.

Additional InformationYour designated work location is 18 Hardscratch Road, Yarmouth. Based on operational requirements, you may be required to travel to and work from locations within Shelburne (Zone 32), Yarmouth (Zone 34), and Saulnierville (Zone 35).

• Zone 34 (Yarmouth)

This opportunity is for a 52-week, Year-Round position – the duties of which are full time and continuous in nature.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

## Definition of work:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) performs professional work in the provision of emergency and medical care to clients in a variety of settings. This position will play a key role in supporting the Virtual ER model in Central Zone’s rural facilities, working very closely with the Virtual ER team and will travel throughout the region as needed. Work involves performing independent advanced medical care and intervention to clients at pre-hospital scene settings, during transport and within healthcare facilities. The ACP conducts physical examinations; performs comprehensive assessments and tests; interprets a variety of tests and procedures; and initiates a variety of advanced interventions. The successful candidate provides primary client care by surveying the emergency situation and taking any necessary action. The ACP is an integral team member of facility-based response teams including but not limited to the Code Blue Response team and the Code White Response team. The ACP also functions as a leader and a mentor within the paramedicine program, as well as a preceptor for advanced and primary care paramedic students. The Paramedic is an integral member of the Emergency Department team, providing care, based on their scope of practice to patients in the ER, in collaboration with nursing staff and physicians. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centred care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

• Graduation from high school with a diploma recognized by the Newfoundland and Labrador Department of Education and Early Childhood Development.

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association.

• BLS Certification.

• OPMD Certification (including all current courses/modules).

• Current physical capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimal standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy.

• A valid Class IV driver’s license issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Preferred qualifications:

• Experience as an Advanced Care Paramedic.

Title: Senior Program Coordinator, Social Emergencies

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2024, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Social Emergencies (SE) Program responds to an event or situation that exceeds the health and wellness resources and capacities of a community. The goal of the SE Program, in collaboration with the impacted community, is to provide stabilization, psychosocial support, resource mobilization, and support capacity building. The SE Program is guided by several complementary evidence-based frameworks, such as the CRC Indigenous Peoples and Community Engagement Pathway Frameworks and the Creating Safe Environments (CSE) Strategy, stewarded by Indigenous Programs. These frameworks align Risk Reduction and Resilience initiatives with principles for respectful engagement through all phases of a SE response to emphasize a community-driven, sustainable, and equitable recovery.

The Senior Program Coordinator, under the direction of the Senior Manager, will support the planning, coordination, and implementation of social emergency response initiatives. This role is responsible for ensuring rapid mobilization of resources through developing response protocols, supporting logistical coordination, and providing direct service delivery, including training and social emergency response. The Sr. Program Coordinator will play a key role in supporting program monitoring, evaluation, and continuous improvement, ensuring that activities are contextually relevant, evidence-informed, and aligned with organizational standards and community priorities.

## In this role, you will :

• Support the planning and implementation of the SE response strategy and ensure service delivery activities reflect cultural inclusion and safety.

• Support the planning and monitoring of the SE response structure, ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, and quality standards.

• Assist with logistics, procurement, and administrative needs to facilitate successful SE responses.

• Coordinate technical support requests and ensure access to necessary resources.

• Organize and facilitate meetings, briefings, and key response activities, ensuring proper documentation and follow-up.

• Develop and maintain documentation to ensure consistency across SE processes and procedures

• Maintain and update SE response trackers, databases, and monitoring systems for real-time data tracking.

• Collect, analyze, and report on SE key program indicators to support decision-making and continuous improvement.

• Ensure proper documentation, storage, and accessibility of SE response data for compliance and future reference.

• Facilitate communication and collaboration with internal teams, external partners, and stakeholders to ensure alignment, support SE objectives, and enhance overall effectiveness.

## What we are looking for :

• Qualifications include a minimum of 4-5 years' experience and a 1-2 year post-secondary certification/diploma and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) and SharePoint is required.

• Lived and/or has professional experience with First Nations, Inuit and/or Métis Nations or communities.

• Demonstrated experience working directly with Indigenous communities, organizations, or governments in a culturally safe, respectful, and reciprocal manner.

• Ability to identify, investigate and analyze problems, identify root causes and risks, and apply technical, functional and organizational knowledge to develop solutions.

• Ability to identify opportunities for process creation and/or improvement to enhance efficiency and effectiveness in service delivery.

• Ability to understand data analytics to assess performance metrics and generate reports for management.

• Communication skills, diplomacy and empathy to interpret information and deliver advice, clarify client or stakeholder needs, offer solutions, and resolve escalations in new or somewhat sensitive situations.

## Working Conditions :

title: General Manager
description:
General Manager

Portland Custom Millwork Ltd.

## Position Summary

Portland Custom Millwork is seeking an experienced General Manager to oversee the day-to-day operations of its custom millwork projects. The General Manager will coordinate projects from estimating through production, installation, and completion, ensuring work is properly planned, accurately priced, completed on schedule, and delivered to a high standard.

## Key Responsibilities

## Estimating and Project Planning

• Review drawings, specifications, site conditions, and customer requirements.

• Prepare accurate estimates for materials, labour, subcontractors, and installation.

• Develop project scopes, budgets, timelines, and production requirements.

• Identify potential design, pricing, scheduling, or installation issues before work begins.

• Coordinate changes to project scope and prepare change-order pricing.

## Project Management

• Manage multiple millwork projects from award through final completion.

• Coordinate with customers, contractors, designers, architects, suppliers, and installers.

• Monitor project costs, progress, deadlines, and quality.

• Ensure drawings, approvals, measurements, materials, and site conditions are ready before production or installation.

• Resolve project issues promptly and keep customers informed.

• Review completed work and ensure deficiencies are addressed.

## Scheduling and Production

• Develop and maintain the overall production and installation schedule.

• Prioritize projects based on customer deadlines, available labour, material lead times, and shop capacity.

• Assign work and provide clear direction to shop and installation employees.

• Hold regular scheduling meetings and communicate changes to the team.

• Monitor workflow and adjust schedules when delays or conflicts arise.

## Purchasing and Materials

• Determine material and hardware requirements for each project.

• Order materials accurately and on time.

• Monitor supplier pricing, availability, and lead times.

• Confirm materials are received, inspected, and allocated to the correct projects.

• Minimize waste, rush orders, and excess inventory.

## Operations and Leadership

• Oversee the daily activities of the shop and installation teams.

• Set clear expectations for productivity, workmanship, safety, and professionalism.

• Support, coach, and hold employees accountable for performance.

• Help recruit, train, and retain skilled employees.

• Maintain organized and efficient shop and project-management processes.

• Promote a positive, respectful, and solutions-focused work environment.

## Financial and Business Management

• Monitor estimated versus actual labour and material costs.

• Identify and address project overruns.

• Support project billing by confirming progress, completed work, and approved changes.

• Review project profitability and recommend operational improvements.

• Provide regular updates to the Owner on schedules, project risks, staffing, cash-flow requirements, and overall performance.

• Help develop pricing standards, operational procedures, and growth plans.

## Qualifications

• Experience managing custom millwork, cabinetry, construction, or a related manufacturing operation.

• Strong estimating and project-management experience.

• Ability to read architectural drawings, shop drawings, and specifications.

• Knowledge of millwork materials, hardware, manufacturing, finishing, and installation.

• Strong organizational and scheduling skills.

• Ability to manage several projects and competing deadlines.

• Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.

• Comfortable working with estimating, scheduling, and accounting software.

• Valid driver's licence.

## Key Measures of Success

• Projects are accurately estimated and profitable.

• Materials are ordered correctly and available when required.

• Production and installations are completed on schedule.

• Labour and material overruns are minimized.

• Customers receive consistent communication and quality workmanship.

• Employees understand priorities and are held accountable.

• The shop operates safely, efficiently, and with minimal downtime.

## Position Details

• Reports to: Owner/President

• Employment: Full-time

• Location: Portland Custom Millwork Ltd.

• Compensation: Based on experience

Posted Date: 2026-06-18

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.
If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.
The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required. \

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Technologist, Medical Radiation (MRT)
description:
Title : Technologist, Medical Radiation (MRT)

Employee Working Location : In-person (Canada)

Employment status : Deployed 3-4 weeks working full-time hours when deployed

Salary band : $41.23 / hour (eligible for pier diems, travel and accommodation covered by CRC)

The Canadian Red Cross (CRC) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2024, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

## In this role, you will :

• Perform, monitor, and report radiographic investigations and services as per medical orders, delivering safe, high-quality care in accordance with professional standards, clinical guidelines, and medical directives.

• Ensure the quality and safety of all radiographic services by operating equipment correctly and maintaining compliance with national standards, regulations, and health authority requirements throughout deployment.

• Conduct and contribute to clinical assessments of radiographic services, monitor patient outcomes, and support the continuous improvement of imaging protocols and operational practices.

• Collaborate with the multidisciplinary team, on-site clinical leads, local health authorities, and partner agencies to promote efficient patient care and maintain effective communication channels during deployment.

• Manage, monitor, and ensure the safe, correct use and function of radiography equipment and associated medical supplies in line with operational and partner requirements.

• Maintain accurate documentation, data collection, and reporting that meets local legal requirements, regulatory standards, and organizational obligations.

• Support planning and delivery of radiography services as requested by the partner, including active participation in service monitoring and the implementation of new procedures or protocols.

• Mentor and build the capacity of clinical, non-clinical, and auxiliary personnel in radiographic practices as appropriate.

• Adhere to all deployment requirements, including flexibility across assigned shifts, completion of the CRC Learning Pathway and site-specific training, currency of certifications and licensures, maintenance of professional indemnity coverage, and compliance with medical, safety, and infection prevention protocols.

• Work independently and responsibly in mobile or dynamic settings, upholding organizational and partner standards at all times.

## What we are looking for :

• Academic qualification in Medical Radiation Technology (minimum 3-year college diploma or university degree) or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• CAMRT certificate required and collected as a part of the process..

• Current Professional Registration in good standing in at least one province in Canada.

• Professional certification or post-graduate qualification in trauma/emergency radiation technology, humanitarian affairs, or a related field is an asset.

• Minimum 4-7 years of professional experience in medical radiation technology.

• Experience in a radiology department using hard copy films and analogue equipment.

• Experience operating portable X-ray machines and other radiographic equipment in clinical or field settings.

• Experience monitoring equipment performance and conducting basic verification and quality control checks.

• Experience working in emergency, humanitarian, or resource-limited contexts.

• Experience living or working in a cultural context other than their own, including Indigenous, remote, or isolated communities, is an asset.

• Ability to identify, investigate, and analyze equipment or service problems, determine root causes and risks, and apply technical knowledge to develop practical solutions.

• Proficiency in standard computer applications (Microsoft Office Suite).

• Experience in health needs assessment and the design or adaptation of radiographic service protocols in dynamic or non-standard settings.

• Training, facilitation, coaching, and capacity-building skills applicable to clinical, non-clinical, and auxiliary personnel.

• Ability to coordinate with health authorities and foster effective working relationships with multidisciplinary teams and partner stakeholders at various levels.

• Strong communication skills, diplomacy, and empathy to interpret and deliver clinical information, clarify stakeholder needs, and resolve issues in sensitive or complex situations.

• Ability to adapt to changing circumstances and work independently in fast-paced, mobile, or dynamic environments.

• Flexibility to travel on short notice to various destinations for periods of several weeks as required.

• Fluency in English is required; French is an asset.

• Maintenance of current professional indemnity coverage and compliance with all medical, safety, and certification prerequisites for deployment.

## Working conditions :

• Difficult and demanding -both physically and psychologically-working conditions are expected.

• Due to dynamic nature of an emergency and proximity to epidemic/ pandemic affected area, issues with access and mobility and strict protocols and procedures.

• Possible long hours of work in demanding context with limited resources

• Potential for exposure to communicable disease (TB, Covid, etc.), bodily fluid, and hazardous materials that can result in potential health risks to the incumbent.

• Living conditions vary by deployment. When deployed to remote, northern nursing stations, the following can be expected: very basic living conditions including group living and shared accommodations ,potential for placement in community with non-potable water, potential for placement in community with water shortages and/or frozen plumbing for days at a time.

• If requested by CRC clinical support team, must complete any pre or post deployment screening ( i.e.. TB screening, Covid testing)

• Must ensure all prescription medications are up to date and supply will be sufficient for duration of deployment.

• A valid provincial driver's licenceis an asset

• As a health care provider, you may be required to provide a health attestation regarding vaccination history depending on deployment/partner requests.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

• Full vaccination against COVID-19 is mandatory for this position and operation.

Before you apply, please watch this video to learn more about a casual position with the Canadian Red Cross.

title: Investigator
description:
The Financial and Consumer Services Commission (Commission) is a leader in integrated financial and consumer services regulation. The Commission's mandate is to protect consumers and enhance public confidence in the financial and consumer marketplace through the provision of regulatory and educational services. With offices in both Fredericton and Saint John, it is responsible for the administration and enforcement of provincial legislation regulating mortgage brokers, payday lenders, real estate, securities, insurance, pensions, credit unions, trust and loan companies, cooperatives, unclaimed property, and a wide range of consumer legislation. The Commission is a self funded Crown corporation responsible for the administration and enforcement of financial consumer services legislation.

We offer opportunities for dedicated professionals to play a vital role in carrying out our mandate.

## Investigator - Enforcement Division (Fredericton or Saint John Office)

We are seeking an experienced Investigator to join our Enforcement Division. Reporting to the Director of Enforcement, this position is responsible for investigating suspected breaches of New Brunswick Financial and Consumer Services legislation through the application of investigative, intelligence gathering, digital evidence analysis, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) techniques.

The successful candidate will assess complaints and referrals, develop investigative strategies, gather and analyze evidence, conduct interviews, support enforcement proceedings, and collaborate with regulatory and law enforcement partners. This role also contributes to identifying emerging risks and protecting New Brunswick consumers and investors.

## Your Focus:

• Assessing complaints, referrals, and intelligence, and developing investigative strategies;

• Conducting investigations into potential violations of financial and consumer services legislation;

• Gathering, analyzing, and preserving documentary, digital, and testimonial evidence;

• Conducting OSINT and digital investigations to identify evidence, intelligence, and emerging risks;

• Support enforcement proceedings through the preparation of reports, evidence, and testimony;

• Building relationships with regulators, law enforcement agencies, and other stakeholders to support investigations and intelligence sharing; and

• Monitoring emerging trends, technologies, and investigative practices to strengthen enforcement activities and regulatory outcomes.

## What you Bring

• Community College diploma and/or certificate in Criminology, Specialized training in Commerce, Accounting, Finance, Economics, Law, Data Analytics, or Intelligence Studies.

• Professional certification or specialized training in investigations, intelligence analysis, digital forensics, OSINT, fraud examination, compliance, or financial crime investigations is an asset.

• 3-5 years investigative experience in a regulatory, law enforcement, compliance, financial services or consumer protection environment.

• Good working knowledge of financial and consumer protection legislation.

• Experience conducting complex investigations, assessing evidence, and preparing investigative reports and recommendations.

• Demonstrated experience conducting investigative interviews and collecting, documenting and preserving evidence;

• Knowledge of internet and social media investigations, digital evidence handling, and; OSINT tools and techniques;

• Strong written and oral communication skills in both official languages are required.

## Additional Strengths

• Knowledge of AI-assisted research and investigative technologies, experience with cryptocurrency, blockchain analysis, digital asset or forensic investigations, and experience using case management systems is an asset.

The Financial and Consumer Services Commission offers a competitive salary and benefit package as well as excellent opportunities for personal growth and challenge. Salary will be commensurate with experience. If you are interested in being a key part of this team, please forward your résumé and covering letter.

Salary Range: $75,482 to $103,787 (annual compensation)

As a condition of employment, the successful candidate will be required to undergo a pre-employment background check in accordance with the Commission's Pre-Employment Background Checks Directive. This may include criminal record checks, credential verification, and reference checks.

For more information about this position please visit our website at www.fcnb.ca or call the Talent Acquisition Specialist at (506) 643-7790.

Please note that only candidates selected for further evaluation will be contacted.

## In this role, you will :

• Provide subject matter expertise and strategic and technical guidance to strengthen program/service effectiveness, ensuring alignment with best practices, organizational priorities, and national society needs.

• Assess program/service gaps, analyze trends, and provide recommendations for operational enhancements to improve service delivery, accessibility, and impact.

• Serve as a key advisor to internal teams at national and provincial levels, fostering collaboration and knowledge-sharing.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with government agencies, nonprofits, national societies, Indigenous organizations, and other key stakeholders to support service delivery.

• Provide technical expertise, training, and mentorship to internal teams and external partners to enhance their capacity in program delivery.

• Contribute to financial reporting and compliance with funding requirements, while ensuring transparency and accountability to partners.

• Develop and implement training materials, toolkits, and resources to support program effectiveness and knowledge transfer.

• Advise on culturally safe and inclusive approaches to ensure equitable program/service access for diverse communities.

• Lead program/service evaluation efforts by analyzing performance metrics, community feedback, and impact assessments to inform decision-making.

• Ensure compliance with funding agreements, regulatory requirements, and organizational policies, providing advisory support to mitigate risks and improve accountability.

• Contribute to the development of performance reports, dashboards, and impact narratives for leadership and external stakeholders.

• Guide the development and execution of relevant strategies that foster meaningful participation, co-design, and inclusive decision-making.

• Work with communities to identify evolving needs, emerging challenges, and opportunities for program/service enhancement.

• Advocate for community-driven solutions, ensuring program strategies reflect cultural, social, and economic considerations.

## What we are looking for :

• Qualifications include a 3-year college diploma or university degree in social sciences, community development, Indigenous studies, Gender and Social Justice, Feminist studies or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience related to protection, diversity and inclusion, child protection, gender equality, anti-racism and decolonial approaches, and/or SGBV programming would be an asset.

• A minimum of 6-9 years' experience in humanitarian assistance, international or community development, public administration or other related field.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) and SharePoint.

• Ability to identify complex problems, analyze interrelated factors, assess and mitigate risks, and develop solutions using specialized skills.

• Communication and influence skills to gather perspectives, understand needs, and present information to reach consensus, often in somewhat sensitive situations.

• Knowledge of community engagement principles, participatory approaches, and capacity-building techniques.

• Experience working with diverse communities, including Indigenous, rural, and underserved populations.

• Fluency in English is required; Fluency in French and or Spanish is considered a strong asset. Additional languages relevant to the communities and regions served by the organization are considered an asset.

## Working Conditions :

• The majority of the work is conducted virtually, with possibility of deployment and on-site meetings.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.
