title: Lead Electrical Engineer/Partner
description:
Job Title: Lead Electrical Engineer/Partner
Location: Bedford, Nova Scotia
TP - MLE - 10142

Since 2012, MLE Consulting Engineers has provided mechanical building systems design and consulting services for commercial, healthcare, long-term care, and multi-unit residential projects. Known for their technical expertise, collaborative approach, and commitment to delivering practical solutions, MLE has built a strong reputation among clients, contractors, and industry partners across Atlantic Canada.

As the firm continues to grow, MLE is making a strategic investment in its future by establishing an in-house electrical engineering division. This exciting expansion represents a unique opportunity to build upon the strength of an established engineering practice while helping shape a new area of the business. This opportunity offers the successful candidate the ability to build and lead an electrical division while benefiting from an existing client base, active project pipeline, operational support, and established engineering infrastructure.

People are at the center of everything MLE does. Their culture is built on collaboration, integrity, continuous improvement, and a commitment to delivering high-quality solutions while fostering a supportive and inclusive workplace.

Meridia Recruitment is excited to partner with MLE Consulting Engineers in the search for a Lead Electrical Engineer/Partner to join their team in Bedford, Nova Scotia.

## Role Description

As the Lead Electrical Engineer/Partner, you will contribute to the establishment and growth of MLE's electrical engineering division while serving as a key member of the firm's leadership team. This role is ideal for an experienced engineer who is interested in combining technical expertise and project leadership with client development, team building, and business strategy.

Working alongside MLE's existing partners and project teams, you will oversee electrical engineering projects from concept through construction. You will work together to develop client relationships, identify new opportunities, and build the team and capabilities required to support the practice as it grows.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Provide technical leadership in the design and consulting of electrical building systems.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, contractors, architects, consultants, and industry partners.

• Identify new business opportunities through client engagement, professional networks, and industry involvement.

• Contribute to strategic planning and decision-making as a member of the partnership team.

• Develop and evaluate design solutions that balance reliability, energy efficiency, operational performance, and cost-effectiveness.

• Manage multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring quality, budget, and schedule expectations are achieved.

• Collaborate with various engineering disciplines on multidisciplinary projects.

• Coordinate project activities with clients, contractors, architects, consultants, and internal project teams.

• Respond to RFIs, prepare CCOs, and develop electrical sketches and supporting construction documentation.

• Review contractor progress claims, change orders, and extra costs related to electrical work.

• Conduct periodic site reviews and prepare reports documenting construction progress and compliance with project requirements.

• Participate in project meetings with clients, contractors, vendors, manufacturers, and consulting partners.

• Review commissioning documentation, operation and maintenance manuals, testing reports, and project close-out materials.

• Adhere to MLE's established office and design processes while developing and implementing quality standards specific to the electrical engineering practice.

• Foster a culture that aligns with MLE's core values, collaborative environment, and commitment to excellence.

## Your Qualifications

The ideal candidate is an experienced electrical engineering professional with strong technical expertise and proven project leadership capabilities. You are comfortable being part of an ownership team responsible for both project and business outcomes and are motivated by the opportunity to develop a growing engineering practice.

## Your qualifications include:

• Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation, or eligibility for registration with Engineers Nova Scotia.

• 8+ years of experience in electrical building systems design, including leading projects through design, construction, and project delivery.

• Demonstrated ability to manage projects independently and serve as a trusted technical advisor to clients and project stakeholders.

• Strong understanding of electrical systems within commercial, residential, institutional, healthcare, and/or long-term care facilities.

• Experience working with AutoCAD.

• Strong project management, organizational, and time-management skills.

• Strong client-facing and relationship-building skills, with the ability to serve as a trusted technical advisor, communicate effectively with clients and stakeholders, understand their needs, and build lasting relationships throughout the project lifecycle.

• Interest in business development, client engagement, and contributing to the growth of an engineering practice.

• Self-motivated, independent, and comfortable taking ownership of business and project outcomes.

## Considered an asset:

• Experience working with Revit.

• Previous leadership, mentoring, or team-building experience.

• Demonstrated success developing client relationships and generating new business opportunities.

• Experience growing or helping establish a professional practice.

## Why join MLE?

This is a rare opportunity to build and lead an electrical engineering division within an established and respected consulting engineering firm, where people are at the center of everything they do.
This opportunity offers:

• Optional, no-cost ownership potential through shareholder participation in the newly established electrical engineering company.

• A ground-floor leadership role with meaningful influence over the practice's direction and growth.

• An established pipeline of work generated through MLE's existing client relationships and mechanical engineering practice.

• Operational and leadership support, including administrative resources and established engineering infrastructure.

• A collaborative, people-first culture that values flexibility, professional development, and long-term success.

• A bright and welcoming office environment, conveniently located in Bedford, with free on-site parking.

• The opportunity to expand MLE's multidisciplinary capabilities and contribute to the continued evolution of a growing Atlantic Canadian engineering firm.

You'll lead a skilled estimating team supporting projects across the commercial, government, industrial, utility, and institutional sectors while contributing to bid strategy, risk assessment, operational planning, and long-term business success.

The successful candidate will balance strong estimating expertise with people leadership, business judgment, and relationship management. You'll be responsible for ensuring estimates are accurate, competitive, and complete while developing the team, strengthening processes, and supporting Black & McDonald's continued growth in Atlantic Canada.

Team Leadership & Development: Lead, coach, and mentor a team of Estimators, assign work, support professional development, and foster accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Estimating Oversight: Oversee and, where required, prepare estimates for labour, materials, equipment, and subcontracted work based on drawings, specifications, tender documents, and contract requirements.

Bid Strategy & Risk Assessment: Review estimates, assess project risks and opportunities, support bid strategy, and ensure final submissions are accurate, competitive, and commercially sound.

Supplier & Subcontractor Engagement: Work closely with suppliers, subcontractors, owners, consultants, designers, and architects to develop pricing, clarify scope, and support successful tender submissions.

The Rehabilitation Assistant reports to the Manager of Patient Services with NL Health Services and provides physiotherapist support and occupational therapist support in the treatment of residents, patients, and clients.

Under the clinical direction and supervision of Clinical Physiotherapists, Physiotherapy services will focus on assisting patients/residents/clients to reach functional goals; this may involve carrying out assigned exercise programs, individual/caregiver education and plans of care related to range of motion, strengthening, balance and mobility. Under the direction of the Physiotherapist, the Rehabilitation Assistant will be responsible for tracking assistive mobility equipment and patient/resident/client follow-up as assigned.

Under the clinical direction and supervision of Clinical Occupational Therapists, Occupational Therapy services will focus on enhancing patients/residents/clients’ participation to meet occupational goals; this may involve self care, individual/caregiver education, and community participation. Under the direction of the Occupational Therapist, the Rehabilitation Assistant will be responsible for patient/client/resident care follow up, assistive device provision, care, and training; maintaining equipment and adaptive aid inventories; and ordering equipment/supplies.

The Rehabilitation Assistant?will carry out individual and group interventions with patient/resident/clients as directed by the Physiotherapist and/or Occupational Therapists. Other assigned tasks from Physiotherapists and Occupational Therapists may be required.

The Rehabilitation Assistant will be responsible to precept Rehabilitation and OTA/PTA students and offer other clinical education experience to students within NL Health Services.

This Rehabilitation Assistant maintains accountability to the Regional Professional Practice Consultants for Occupational Therapy and Physiotherapy for professional integrity and practice issues.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

Regularly lifts or moves objects less than 10 lbs., up to 25 lbs. and lifts and moves patients, limbs (or may utilize a mechanical lift) for exercises. Regularly, there is a requirement to physically handle materials for the set up and running of activities. Regularly required to stand or walk for extended periods and occasionally required to drive to clients’ homes or community buildings to assist with therapy or to facilitate activities. Regularly a variety of body postures including working in awkward or cramped positions, bending, kneeling and stretching and sometimes strength and endurance is required. Occasionally operates machinery, equipment, and hand tools that require controlled fine finger work and precision.

Visual and Auditory concentration is required.

Demonstrated ability to follow ethical guidelines, function within scope of practice responsibilities, and comply with legal requirements.

Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with others to meet patient goals and overall delivery of physiotherapy and occupational therapy services.

Demonstrated ability to utilize clinical judgment, problem-solving and decision-making skills.

A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

description:
Position Title Manager, Finance and Corporate Services

Department Name Corporate Services

Reports to CEO

Version Dated September 21, 2026

## About Advantage St. John's Inc.

Advantage St. John's is the investment attraction agency established by the City of St. John's, the Town of Conception Bay South, and the Town of Paradise. Its mission is to amplify economic growth by enhancing investment and talent attraction, supporting business retention and expansion, and advancing economic development opportunities in Newfoundland and Labrador's capital region.

## Position Summary

The Manager, Finance and Corporate Services provides financial management, corporate services, and operational oversight to support the effective administration and long-term sustainability of Advantage St. John's. The Manager leads budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, payroll coordination, procurement controls, contribution agreement administration, funding research, grant applications, internal controls, and the preparation of quarterly and year-end financial statements for the CEO and Board of Directors. This position ensures the Agency's financial resources, systems, records, policies, and processes are managed with accuracy, accountability, compliance, and sound judgment.

In addition to leading the finance and corporate services portfolio, the Manager supervises the Executive Assistant and provides oversight across human resources, governance, risk management, information systems, property management, records management, privacy, and administrative functions. The Manager also contributes directly to Advantage St. John's investment attraction mandate by providing financial intelligence related to taxes, incentives, funding programs, and business conditions in Canada and Newfoundland and Labrador, and working collaboratively with the CEO, staff, partners, funders, and stakeholders to advance organizational and regional economic development priorities.

## Key Responsibilities

## Financial Management and Accountability

• Lead the Agency's financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, monitoring, reporting, and year-end processes in accordance with accounting standards, funding agreements, government requirements, and organizational policies.

• Prepare quarterly and year-end financial statements, reports, and supporting analysis for review by the CEO and presentation to the Board of Directors.

• Provide financial advice, analysis, and guidance to the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board of Directors, to support informed decision-making

• Coordinate the development, approval, and ongoing monitoring of annual operating and project budgets in collaboration with directors, funding partners, and the Board.

• Oversee day-to-day financial administration, including invoicing, accounts receivable, payment tracking, collections, deposits, and related follow-up to support timely and accurate cash flow management.

• Coordinate payroll administration and employee-related financial processes, including payroll inputs, benefits remittances, vacation or leave tracking inputs, expense claims, and liaison with external payroll or benefits providers as required.

• Administer procurement and purchasing controls by supporting requisitions, purchase approvals, vendor set-up, purchase orders, invoice verification, contract documentation, and compliance with organizational policies and funding requirements.

• Maintain complete, accurate, and secure financial records, including filing, document retention, audit support materials, banking records, remittance documentation, and confidential financial information.

• Ensure effective internal controls, financial policies, and processes are established, documented, consistently applied, and regularly reviewed.

## Grant and Funding Management

• Research and monitor municipal, provincial, federal, and partner funding programs to identify opportunities that align with the Agency's mandate, strategic priorities, operations, and project needs.

• Prepare and coordinate funding applications, proposals, business cases, supporting budgets, workplans, cash flow projections, and required documentation in collaboration with internal staff, funding agencies, and organizational partners.

• Maintain awareness of eligibility criteria, program deadlines, application requirements, reporting obligations, and funding conditions to support timely and compliant submissions.

• Administer contribution agreements and related project files, including tracking approved activities, eligible expenditures, milestones, deliverables, amendments, payments, and compliance requirements.

• Support project reporting, reimbursement claims, financial reconciliations, variance explanations, and funder communications to ensure obligations are met accurately and on schedule.

## Governance, Risk, and Human Resources

• Provide advice on financial, operational, human resource, governance, and risk matters.

• Serve as Advantage St. John's designated ATIPPA Coordinator, leading compliance with the Access to Information and Protection of Privacy Act, managing access requests, privacy matters, and serving as the primary liaison with the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner.

• Develop and oversee policies, procedures, and best practices related to privacy, records management, information governance, retention schedules, and the protection of confidential information.

• Prepare policies, and recommendations for the CEO and Board of Directors regarding access, privacy, records management, and information governance matter.

• Manage the Agency's insurance requirements and related risk management practices, ensuring appropriate coverage, regulatory compliance, and organizational safeguards are maintained

• Promptly communicate significant, contentious, or emerging financial, operational, human resource, legal, or reputational issues to the CEO.

• Ensure human resource practices are consistent with organizational policies, employment legislation, occupational health and safety requirements, and best practices.

• Supervise, support, and provide direction to the Executive Assistant, including work planning, priority setting, coaching, performance management, and professional development.

• Maintain appropriate personnel policies, procedures, records, and confidentiality safeguards.

• Foster a respectful, collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing workplace culture.

## Property Management and Information Systems

• Ensure compliance with lease obligations and serve as the primary liaison with property management representatives regarding lease renewals, facility operations, maintenance, and office upkeep.

• Oversee office accommodation, equipment, services, safety, security, and business continuity requirements in collaboration with the Executive Assistant.

• Oversee information technology, telecommunications, software, cybersecurity, data protection, and related vendor relationships to ensure systems are reliable, secure, and appropriate for the Agency's needs.

• Plan and coordinate technology improvements that strengthen administrative efficiency, collaboration, business continuity, and information security.

• Ensure appropriate access controls, backup practices, equipment management, and technology-related policies are maintained.

## Investment Attraction Support

• Collaborate with the CEO, the Director of Economic Growth, and other team members to advance qualified investment leads, provide responsive investor support, prepare for investment attraction events, and execute investment attraction projects.

• Apply financial expertise to support investor and business client inquiries by providing research, analysis, and intelligence on relevant tax considerations, incentive programs, funding supports, and financial advantages available in Canada and Newfoundland and Labrador.

• Support the procurement processes and coordination of cross-functional project teams and external consultants to ensure deliverables are completed on time, within budget, and in accordance with funding and organizational requirements.

## Education and Experience

• A university degree in business, commerce, finance, accounting, public administration, or a related discipline from a recognized institution.

• A recognized professional accounting designation, such as CPA, is preferred.

• A minimum of five years of progressive management or leadership experience, including responsibility for financial management and staff supervision.

• Experience managing annual operating and project budgets exceeding $1 million.

• Experience with non-profit, public-sector, or government-funded financial reporting and contribution agreements is considered an asset.

• Experience in finance, human resources, privacy, information technology, risk management, governance, and policy development.

## Additional Requirements and Competencies

• Strong financial acumen, judgment, analytical ability, and attention to detail.

• Demonstrated ability to lead staff, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

• Excellent written, verbal, presentation, relationship-management, and stakeholder-engagement skills.

• Ability to exercise discretion and maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive financial, personnel, client, and organizational information.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and financial, payroll, client relationship management, and information management systems.

• Commitment to the vision, mission, values, and regional mandate of Advantage St. John's.

• A valid driver's licence.

## Compensation

Advantage St. John's offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including group health, life and dental coverage, a matching group retirement savings program, and professional development. The office is located in downtown St. John's and includes parking. Advantage St. John's is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from all qualified individuals.

## Apply

Applications should be emailed to info@advantagestjohns.ca with the subject line Application - Manager, Finance and Corporate Services. Thank you to all that apply. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Executive Chef
description:
Executive Chef

Breton Crafthouse | Downtown Sydney, Nova Scotia

Breton Crafthouse is seeking an experienced and motivated Executive Chef to lead our culinary program and kitchen operations in downtown Sydney.

Born from Breton Brewing Co., Breton Crafthouse brings the culture, hospitality and community focus of Breton Brewing into a unique downtown setting. The Crafthouse combines a full-service restaurant featuring elevated brewpub fare and brick-oven pizza, an onsite microbrewery, retail shop, and private event space.

We are looking for a strong culinary leader who can build on the foundation we have established while continuing to evolve the food program, develop our kitchen team and deliver an experience that complements the quality and character of the Breton brand.

## The Role

The Executive Chef is responsible for the overall leadership, performance and development of the culinary operation at Breton Crafthouse.

Reporting directly to the General Manager, the Executive Chef will work directly with the Crafthouse kitchen team to oversee food quality, menu development, kitchen operations, food costs, labour, purchasing, training and the development of the culinary team.

This is a senior leadership position requiring someone who is equally comfortable developing great food, leading people and managing the financial performance of a busy kitchen.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to shape the future of the Crafthouse food program while having the support and resources of the broader Breton Brewing organization.

## Key Responsibilities

## Culinary Leadership & Menu Development

• Provide overall leadership and direction for the Crafthouse culinary program

• Maintain consistently high standards for food quality, presentation and execution

• Lead the continued development and evolution of the Crafthouse menu

• Maintain and develop our focus on brick-oven pizza and elevated brewpub fare

• Create dishes that are approachable, distinctive and appropriate for the Crafthouse concept

• Develop seasonal features and new menu offerings

• Ensure menu decisions balance creativity, guest appeal, operational execution and profitability

• Look for opportunities to incorporate and complement Breton beers throughout the food program

## Kitchen Leadership & Team Development

• Lead, coach and develop the kitchen management and culinary teams

• Recruit, train and retain talented kitchen employees

• Build a professional, positive and accountable kitchen culture

• Establish clear expectations for quality, preparation, cleanliness and execution

• Develop strong kitchen leaders who can successfully manage day-to-day operations

• Create effective training and development programs for culinary employees

• Foster an environment built around teamwork, respect and continuous improvement

• Work closely with the General Manager to create strong alignment between front-of-house and back-of-house teams

## Kitchen Operations

• Oversee all aspects of daily kitchen operations

• Establish and maintain effective systems for preparation, production, service and closing

• Ensure consistency in recipes, portions and presentation

• Maintain food inventory levels and monitor waste

• Maintain appropriate staffing levels based on business volumes

• Develop efficient kitchen schedules and deployment strategies

• Ensure equipment and facilities are properly maintained

• Identify opportunities to improve kitchen efficiency and workflow

• Maintain high standards for cleanliness, organization and food safety

• Ensure compliance with all applicable health, safety and regulatory

## Financial Performance

• Take responsibility for the financial performance of the culinary operation

• Develop and manage kitchen budgets in collaboration with the General Manager and senior leadership

• Monitor and manage food cost, kitchen labour, waste and other key operating metrics

• Maintain accurate recipe costing and appropriate menu pricing

• Analyze menu performance and identify opportunities to improve profitability

• Establish effective inventory, receiving and purchasing controls

• Manage supplier relationships and product purchasing

• Minimize waste while maintaining quality and appropriate inventory levels

• Participate in regular financial and operational reviews with the General Manager and senior leadership

## Events & Business Development

• Lead the culinary execution of private events and special functions

• Work with the General Manager and events team to develop menus and experiences for private bookings

• Support brewery events, beer releases and other Breton initiatives

• Develop food concepts that create additional reasons for guests to visit Crafthouse

• Identify opportunities to grow food sales and strengthen the overall Crafthouse offering

• Collaborate with marketing on seasonal menus, promotions and special events

## The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced culinary professional who combines creativity and a passion for food with strong leadership and business judgment.

The successful candidate will ideally have:

• Significant culinary leadership experience in a high-volume restaurant, brewpub, hotel, resort or comparable hospitality environment for a minimum of 5 years

• Demonstrated experience leading and developing kitchen teams

• Strong menu development and recipe costing experience

• A solid understanding of food cost, kitchen labour, inventory management and restaurant profitability

• Experience managing purchasing and supplier relationships

• Strong organizational and problem-solving skills

• The ability to maintain high standards in a fast-paced environment

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills

• A collaborative leadership style and the ability to work effectively with front-of-house management

• Experience with brick-oven pizza considered an asset

• Experience with private events and functions considered an asset

• An appreciation for craft beer, locally inspired food and the role hospitality businesses play within their communities

## What Success Looks Like

The Executive Chef will be expected to build and maintain a culinary operation that delivers:

• Consistently excellent food

• A distinctive and evolving Crafthouse menu

• A strong and well-developed kitchen leadership team

• An engaged, professional and accountable kitchen culture

• Effective food and labour cost management

• Strong menu profitability

• Efficient and organized kitchen operations

title: General Manager
description:
## General Manager

## Breton Crafthouse | Downtown Sydney, Nova Scotia

Breton Crafthouse is seeking an experienced and motivated General Manager to lead our downtown Sydney operation.

Born from Breton Brewing Co., Breton Crafthouse brings the culture, hospitality and community focus of Breton Brewing into a unique downtown setting. The Crafthouse combines a full-service restaurant featuring elevated brewpub fare and brick-oven pizza, an onsite microbrewery, retail shop, and private event space.

We are looking for a strong hospitality leader who can bring these elements together and take overall responsibility for the operation, performance and continued development of Breton Crafthouse.

## The Role

The General Manager is responsible for the overall leadership and day-to-day operation of Breton Crafthouse.

Working closely with the Executive Chef, Crafthouse supervising team and reporting to Breton Brewing's senior leadership, the General Manager will oversee the people, systems and financial performance of the business while ensuring a consistently high standard of hospitality.

This is a senior leadership position requiring someone who can balance the demands of a busy hospitality operation with the broader responsibility of developing people, improving systems, managing financial performance and planning for continued growth.

The successful candidate will have the autonomy to lead the operation while having the support and resources of the broader Breton Brewing organization.

## Key Responsibilities

## Leadership & Team Development

• Provide overall leadership to the Crafthouse team

• Lead, coach and develop managers and supervisors

• Foster a positive, professional and accountable workplace culture

• Oversee recruitment, onboarding, training and employee development

• Establish clear expectations and standards across the operation

• Work closely with the Executive Chef to ensure strong alignment between front-of-house and back-of-house operations

• Identify and develop future leaders within the organization

## Operations & Guest Experience

• Oversee of daily Crafthouse of food & beverage and retail operations.

• Maintain high standards for hospitality, food, beverage, cleanliness and overall guest experience

• Ensure operational systems, policies and procedures are consistently followed

• Maintain an active presence throughout the operation and support Crafthouse team members during key service periods. Key service periods include but are not limited to lunch and dinner services.

• Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, service and the overall guest experience

• Ensure compliance with licensing, health and safety, employment and other regulatory requirements

## Financial Performance

• Take responsibility for the overall financial performance of Breton Crafthouse

• Develop and manage annual operating budgets in collaboration with senior leadership

• Monitor revenue, labour, food cost, beverage cost and other key operating metrics

• Review financial and operational results and take action where required

• Work with CFO & Operations Manager to develop strong financial and operational controls

• Develop strategies to increase revenue and improve profitability

• Ensure scheduling and staffing levels are appropriate for business volumes

## Food & Beverage

• Partner with the Executive Chef on menu development, food quality, pricing and profitability

• Support a strong working relationship between kitchen and front-of-house leadership

• Work with Breton Crafthouse's brewing team to showcase Breton beer and Good News products

• Support the development and promotion of beers produced through the onsite microbrewery

• Work with the marketing team to ensure beverage programming reflects the quality and identity of the Breton & Good News brands

## Events, Retail & Business Development

• Oversee the successful operation and continued development of Crafthouse's private event business

• Support the growth of retail sales and other revenue opportunities within the location

• Work with the Breton Brewing marketing team on promotions, events and community initiatives

• Identify new opportunities to increase traffic, sales and engagement

• Build relationships with local organizations, businesses and community partners

## The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced hospitality professional who combines strong operational leadership with sound business judgment.

The successful candidate will ideally have:

• Significant management experience in a restaurant, brewpub, hotel, resort or comparable hospitality environment

• Demonstrated experience leading and developing teams

• Strong understanding of restaurant financials, including labour, COGS, budgeting and profitability

• Experience managing a high-volume operation

• Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills

• The ability to establish standards and hold teams accountable while maintaining a positive workplace culture

• Experience with events, beverage programs or multi-revenue-stream hospitality operations considered an asset

• An appreciation for craft beer, food and the role hospitality businesses play within their communities

• Experience with Toast POS & WISK considered an asset

## What Success Looks Like

The General Manager will be expected to build a strong, sustainable operation that delivers:

• An exceptional and consistent guest experience

• A highly engaged and well-developed team

• Strong collaboration between front-of-house and kitchen operations

• Effective labour and cost management

• Continued revenue growth and improved profitability

• Successful events and community partnerships

• Strong operational systems and accountability

• A workplace culture that reflects the values of Breton Brewing

Most importantly, the General Manager will ensure that as Crafthouse continues to grow and evolve, it remains distinctly Breton - welcoming, community-focused, quality-driven and a place where both guests and employees want to be.

## What We Offer

• Competitive salary based on experience

• Performance-based incentive opportunity

• Medical & Dental benefits

• Healthy Living Stipend

• Employee Discounts

• Senior leadership responsibility within a growing local company

• Support from an established management and ownership team

• The opportunity to have a meaningful impact on the community through the continued development of Breton Crafthouse

## About Breton Crafthouse

Breton Crafthouse represents an extension of what Breton Brewing has built in Cape Breton - bringing together locally brewed beer, quality food, hospitality and community in the heart of downtown Sydney.

With a full-service restaurant, brick-oven pizza, onsite microbrewery, retail shop and private event space, Crafthouse offers a diverse hospitality experience and an exciting opportunity for an experienced General Manager to lead its next stage of growth.

Interested candidates are invited to submit a resume and cover letter outlining their experience and interest in leading Breton Crafthouse to: careers@bretonbrewing.ca

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

Salary: As per collective agreement.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Emergency Medical Technicians are based on the current Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements for Emergency Medical Technician as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our emergency medical technicians provide transportation and patient care for non-urgent low acuity patients and are expected to maintain and operate ambulances and related equipment in accordance with patient needs and public safety.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in emergency medical technology or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• High school graduation plus an Emergency Medical Technician program/course

• Must meet all legislated requirements for Emergency Medical Technician in New Brunswick

• Must be registered, active Emergency Medical Technician with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

• Written & Spoken competency in one of the two official languages (English or French) is required and spoken competency in the other official language is preferred.

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your EMT certificate from a recognized institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as an Emergency Medical Technician within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR Level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

Also other competencies related to changes in PANB Scope of Practice guidelines and approved by the Provincial Medical Director may also be added to the duties and responsibilities of this classification.

Responsibilities will include:

• Support month-end accounting activities, including journal entries, prepaid accounts, intercompany chargebacks, and recurring entries.

• Prepare supporting documentation for accounting entries and financial reporting for review and approval.

• Complete overhead analysis, bank transaction clearing, and related accounting entries.

• Reconcile, analyze, and maintain general ledger accounts and sub-ledgers, investigating and resolving discrepancies as required.

• Assist with the preparation and review of monthly financial statements, reporting packages, schedules, and supporting data.

• Prepare account analysis and reconciliations to support accurate and timely financial results.

• Provide financial information and analysis to operational teams to support business needs and decision-making.

• Prepare and submit account reconciliations with clear supporting documentation to validate balances.

• Support compliance audits, financial reviews, and monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting requirements.

• Contribute to accounting projects, process improvements, and reporting initiatives.

• Respond to inquiries from internal stakeholders in a timely and professional manner.

• Develop ad hoc financial reports and analysis as required.

• Strong experience with account reconciliations, financial analysis, general ledger maintenance, and month-end accounting.

• Excellent organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage competing deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders.

• A proactive and self-motivated approach, with the ability to take ownership of processes and identify opportunities for improvement.

• A collaborative mindset and ability to work effectively as part of a team.

title: Waterfront Operations Coordinator
description:
The Waterfront Operations Coordinator supports the safe, efficient, and customer-focused operation of marina facilities across the waterfront portfolio. Reporting to the Area Manager, this position coordinates daily operational activities, provides frontline tenant and stakeholder support, conducts routine inspections, assists with maintenance, and supports compliance with organizational, safety, and environmental standards. The Waterfront Operations Coordinator escalates issues appropriately and contributes to a positive and professional marina environment. The Waterfront Operations Coordinator will supervise and manage our frontline operations summer students who occupy the roles of Property Attendant, Marina Attendant and Waterfront Ambassadors.

Qualifications
• High School Diploma or equivalent;

• Strong customer service, communication, and interpersonal skills.

• Certification in a licensed trade is an asset, such as welding, plumbing, electrical, or carpentry;

• Experience leading and directing staff in a team environment;

• Experience in marine infrastructure maintenance and repair;

• Experience with building systems, including HVAC, security, electrical, and plumbing, is considered an asset;

• Experience with procurement-related activities is an asset;

• Considerable experience using power tools for landscaping, construction, maintenance, and repair;

• Experience working at high-profile properties with significant public visitation is an asset;

• Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with team members;

• Ability to schedule work, prioritize tasks, and manage competing deadlines;

• Ability to triage requirements based on internal capacities and or external support need, particularly with respect to the timely repair of emergency and or priority issues;

• Ability to effectively communicate with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.

• A passion for working with your hands and a drive to learn new things.

• Critical thinking along with strong problem-solving skills;

• Considerable use of the Microsoft Office Suite, specifically, Outlook, Teams, Excel, and Word;

• Valid Class 5 drivers' license;

• Possession of or willingness to attain a Forklift Operator's License and Fall Arrest Training;

• Possession of, or willingness to obtain, a Pleasure Craft Operator Card and Restricted Operator Certificate (Maritime);

• Possession of, or willingness to obtain, First Aid and WHMIS certification;

• Demonstrated initiative and a consistently positive, professional attitude.

• Ability to work outdoors in variable weather conditions.

• Physically capable of climbing docks, walking on uneven surfaces, lifting and carrying moderate loads, and performing hands-on operational tasks.

• Ability and willingness to travel between marina sites; valid driver's license and access to a reliable vehicle required.

This competition will remain open until filled.

Responsibilities

## Operations & Customer Service

• Serve as the primary point of contact for customer complaints, inquiries, and service concerns; provide courteous assistance, address matters within scope, and escalate unresolved or complex issues through the appropriate channels.

• Coordinate daily marina activities and manage customer communications in accordance with established procedures.

• Coordinate super yacht berth requests and related communications, ensuring all booking details requiring operational decisions are directed to management for approval.

• Serve as the primary user of the marina booking software by maintaining proficiency in system functions, troubleshooting user issues within scope, and providing guidance to staff on standard system use.

• Assist with the coordination of marine-related event bookings by providing required information, documenting basic event requirements, directing detailed planning needs to management, and completing related tasks as directed by management.

• Maintain organized storage of operational information, forms, and booking records within the designated SharePoint Blueprint folders.

• Oversee litter collection and waste-management data collection, analyze results, and recommend operational improvements.

• Support planning and operational readiness for the Bedford Mill Cove Marina and any future marine developments in the central zone.

## Safety, Compliance & Inspections

• Follow all marina safety procedures and organizational policies at all times.

• Support compliance with Occupational Health & Safety Committee (OHSC) requirements, marine regulations, and environmental standards by following established procedures and promptly escalating concerns.

• Lead Blue Flag certification requirements and environmental compliance initiatives.

## Leadership, Coordination & Reporting

• Support seasonal staff by providing day-to-day guidance and leadership on basic procedures and site practices in alignment with management direction.

• Coordinate, develop, and deliver seasonal staff training in accordance with established procedures and operational requirements.

• Ensure seasonal staff are following required safety procedures and applicable regulations by monitoring work practices, addressing and documenting instances of non‑compliance, and escalating repeated or serious concerns to management.

• Coordinate and carry out assigned work activities in accordance with operational priorities and the established chain of command.

• Escalate issues related to safety, maintenance, operational risk, missed deadlines, tenant concerns, or other operational challenges to management in accordance with established procedures.

• Support revenue tracking, reporting, and general operational data collection as required by management.

• Complete operational logs, inspection records, and other documentation accurately and within required timelines.

• Maintain accurate records of berth assignments, bookings, and visitor information as directed to support management oversight.

• Conduct routine audits of seasonal staff duties to verify work is performed to required standards and report findings to management for follow‑up.

• Follow the established chain of command and direct internal communications through the appropriate supervisory levels.

• Obtain management approval before initiating communication with contractors, and provide all instructions, updates, and site-access details in accordance with management direction.

• Ensure all communications with tenants are routed through management, refrain from providing operational decisions or commitments directly to tenants, and avoid initiating contact or outreach to tenants without prior authorization from management.

• Complete summer student performance reviews in a well-documented and thoughtful manner.

## Travel & Site Support

• Travel between marina sites as required, using a personal vehicle in accordance with organizational policies and procedures.

• Provide on-site presence and support at various marina locations to assist with operations, inspections, and events as directed.

• Additional duties may be assigned to support marina operations and organizational needs.

Competition Number: VAC0022750

Posted Date: 2026-03-19

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Job Summary:
The Advanced Care Paramedic works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.
The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Current ACLS certification;
• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;
• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

title: Community Coordinator
employer: The Canadian Mental Health Association of New Brunswick
description:
Acadie-Bathurst region

French language proficiency is a mandatory requirement for this position, in addition to English proficiency, as some individuals accessing CMHA of NB services communicate primarily in French. Therefore, candidates must possess the necessary French and English language skills to perform the role effectively.

## About CMHA of NB

The Canadian Mental Health Association of New Brunswick Inc. (CMHA of NB) is part of a nationwide, voluntary organization that that envisions a country where mental health is a universal human right. CMHA of NB work is guided by the mission of ensuring that all people in New Brunswick experience good mental health and well-being.

CMHA of NB is STEADFAST and has long fought to improve the state of mental health in New Brunswick, yet acknowledges that the work is ongoing and remains committed to this important task. CMHA of NB is INCLUSIVE and strives for all people in New Brunswick to see themselves represented and served by CMHA of NB. The organization values the voice of those who have experienced mental illness and recognize a diverse range of mental health approaches.

CMHA of NB is PROACTIVE, with leaders who value action over mere talk, and is committed to innovation and forward-thinking to continually address and improve mental health in New Brunswick. Furthermore, CMHA of NB is COMPASSIONATE, approaching its mission with empathy, care, love, and kindness.

CMHA of NB, being COLLABORATIVE, mobilizes and marshals resources, partners, and people to come together to realize necessary changes in our communities and in the mental health system in New Brunswick. CMHA of NB provides a wide range of services and supports to people who are experiencing mental illness, their families, friends, and the public. One of the core goals of these services is to help people with mental illness develop the personal tools to lead meaningful and productive lives.

## Position Description:

The Community Coordinator is the face of the Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA) of New Brunswick in the communities they serve. This role is essential in promoting mental health awareness, reducing stigma, and connecting individuals to valuable mental health resources. The Community Coordinator will act as a primary connector of service providers in their health zone to ensure collaboration and connection, deliver informative presentations, advocate for mental health, and assist individuals in navigating available services. This position is community-based, involving frequent interaction with the public, local organizations, and community groups.

## Key Responsibilities:

Program and Service Delivery:

• Deliver CMHA-approved presentations on mental health, mental illness, and wellness to diverse community groups.

• Coordinate and manage logistics for community-based programs, including venue selection, registration, participant communication, and evaluation.

• Facilitate self-help/support groups or provide support for existing groups in the region.

• Serve as a regional resource navigator, assisting individuals with accessing services and resources such as mental health, addictions services, and community programs.

• Identify education opportunities and promote the services of CMHANB to individuals and organizations in the relevant health zone.

Program Development, Quality, and Monitoring:

• Ensure regional programs meet established standards, quality, safety, and confidentiality requirements, including adherence to PHIPPA regulations.

• Collaborate with the team to assess and improve existing programs and services.

• Administer and evaluate programs to measure their impact and outcomes, and report findings to the direct supervisor.

• Regularly review program effectiveness with the Manager and group facilitators, addressing any challenges and proposing solutions.

Public Awareness:

• Assist in raising awareness of CMHANB programs and services through methods and processes established by CMHA of NB.

• Networking and Partnerships:

• Represent CMHANB on community and provincial committees, promoting mental health initiatives and building partnerships with relevant organizations.

• Collaborate with community agencies to ensure CMHANB services are well-integrated and avoid duplication of efforts.

• Establish and maintain partnerships with public and private sector organizations to meet the specific needs of the local community.

Administration:

• Maintain accurate records and databases, ensuring confidentiality and adherence to data management policies.

• Submit mandatory reports, case updates, and other documentation on time using appropriate systems such as Teams and caseWORKS.

• Attend scheduled team meetings and contribute to collaborative decision-making.

## Qualifications:

• A diploma or degree in social work, psychology, health promotion, education, community development, or a related field.

• Minimum of 2-3 years of experience in a related field such as mental health support, community engagement, public health education, non-profit program delivery, or other related fields.

• A combination of related work experience and education may be considered.

• Proficiency in both English and French is mandatory.

• Excellent working knowledge and skills in MS Office 365 and digital database systems is required.

• Exceptional interpersonal, networking, and relationship-building abilities.

• Strong presentation and public speaking skills tailored to diverse audiences.

• A valid Work Permit is mandatory for temporary residents.

• Residency in New Brunswick (NB) or willingness to relocate is mandatory.

• A new Criminal Record and Vulnerable Sector Check is mandatory.

## Core Competencies:

• Interpersonal Relationship

• Networking

• Communication

• Service Orientation

• Self-Development

• Accountability

• Values, Ethics, Integrity

• Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging (EDI)

• Financial Acumen

• Flexibility

• Self-Management and Resilience

• Teamwork and Collaboration

• Leadership and developing others

• Strategic Thinking

• Project Management

• Change Management

• Creative Problem Solving & Decision Making

## Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:

• Strong understanding of mental health and wellness concepts, including mental illness, stigma reduction, and recovery-oriented practice.

• Familiarity with New Brunswick's mental health and addictions services, community-based programs, and health zone structures.

• Knowledge of relevant privacy and confidentiality legislation (e.g., PHIPAA - Personal Health Information Privacy and Access Act).

• Awareness of principles of equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging (EDIB) in service delivery.

• Understanding of group facilitation practices and adult learning principles.

• Strong presentation and public speaking skills tailored to diverse audiences.

• Exceptional interpersonal, networking, and relationship-building abilities.

• Demonstrated planning, coordination, and organizational skills for program and event logistics.

• Effective written and verbal communication in English and French.

• Accurate documentation and reporting skills in line with case management or program evaluation tools (e.g., caseWORKS).

• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while being a strong team collaborator.

• Ability to adapt to shifting priorities and respond to emerging community needs.

• Capacity to navigate community resources and support individuals in accessing appropriate services.

• Ability to handle sensitive topics and maintain confidentiality and ethical standards.

## Other Attributes:

Passionate about mental health advocacy and community well-being.

High emotional intelligence and empathy in leadership.

Commitment to ethical and evidence-based practices.

## Working Conditions:

## · Work Environment:

o Primarily based in an office setting with flexibility for remote work as needed.

o Occasional travel within New Brunswick to attend meetings, community events, and Community Partners engagements.

o Collaborative and team-oriented work culture, with engagement across multiple departments and external partners.

## · Work Hours:

o Full-time position with a standard workweek of 37.5 hours.

o Occasional evening and weekend work may be required.

o Flexibility in schedule to balance organizational needs with work-life balance.

## · Physical & Mental Demands:

o Requires sustained periods of sitting, working at a computer, and attending virtual or in-person meetings.

o Fast-paced environment with multiple priorities, requiring strong time management and decision-making skills.

o Emotional resilience needed when handling sensitive mental health-related topics and high-stakes advocacy.

o High level of accountability, requiring creative thinking and problem-solving.

## Health & Safety Considerations:

o Regular adherence to occupational health and safety policies, especially when attending community sites or working with vulnerable populations.

o Exposure to emotionally charged situations and discussions, requiring strong self-care practices and support mechanisms.

## How To Apply:

· Please submit your resume and cover letter in one PDF file to careers@cmhanb-acsmnb.ca.

· CMHA of NB is committed to building a skilled and diverse workforce that reflects the New Brunswickers we serve. As an equal opportunity employer, we actively support workplace equity for all persons, and are committed to including and reflecting the population we serve. CMHA of NB encourages applicants to identify as belonging to one of the designated groups of the Employment Equity Act. Preference shall be given to those who demonstrate they are among the most qualified as stated above. Employment Equity Act

We thank all those who apply; however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

title: Director, Financial Services
description:
Director, Financial Services
Truro, NS
Reference # HL-CHI-10138
At Meridia Recruitment Solutions, we are proud to partner with the Chignecto-Central Regional Centre for Education (CCRCE) in the recruitment of a Director, Financial Services. Reporting directly to the Regional Executive Director, this executive leadership opportunity will play a pivotal role in shaping the financial strategy, stewardship, and operational excellence of one of Nova Scotia's largest Regional Centres for Education.
Serving diverse communities across central and northern Nova Scotia, CCRCE is committed to providing high-quality educational experiences that support student success and organizational excellence. As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Director, Financial Services will provide strategic financial leadership, oversee a broad finance function encompassing budgeting, financial reporting, payroll, procurement, financial planning, accounting services, and financial systems. You will lead a talented team of finance professionals while serving as a trusted advisor to the Regional Executive Director and senior leadership team.
The successful candidate will drive financial planning and business strategy, ensuring compliance with public-sector financial standards while supporting operational excellence and continuous improvement across the organization. You will also maintain strong relationships with the Department of Education, auditors, financial institutions, and other key stakeholders.
Responsibilities include:

• Lead the development and execution of regional financial strategies, annual budgets, and long-term business plans.

• Provide leadership and oversight for accounting, payroll, procurement, budgeting, and financial reporting functions.

• Establish and maintain effective financial controls, policies, and procedures that support accountability and compliance.

• Partner with senior leadership to ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities and educational objectives.

• Oversee the implementation and optimization of financial systems and technologies.

• Ensure the delivery of timely, accurate, and meaningful financial reports to support decision-making.

• Serve as the primary liaison with external auditors and regulatory bodies, ensuring compliance with statutory and reporting requirements or facilitate external audits and regulatory reviews, ensuring timely provision of information and compliance with applicable requirements.

• Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing finance team.

• Provide guidance on contracts, financial risk management, and matters requiring legal or regulatory consideration.

• Foster a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and service excellence throughout the organization.

## The ideal candidate will possess:

• A university degree with a concentration in Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.

• A Canadian CPA is a must.

• 5+ years of management experience coupled with 5+ years experience leading budget and financial management in a large organization.

• Demonstrated success overseeing complex budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting functions.

• Strong knowledge of accounting standards, financial controls, governance, and risk management practices.

• Exceptional analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

• Experience driving process improvements, system implementations, and organizational change initiatives.

• The ability to build trusted relationships with senior leaders, government stakeholders, auditors, and external partners.

description:
## Take the Next Step in Your Public Practice Career

What if your next career move gave you the opportunity to do more than manage engagements?

Jump Recruitment is excited to conduct a search for an experienced and driven Senior Manager on behalf of our client, located in St. John's, NL.

## WHO WE ARE:

Our client is an established and growing accounting firm seeking an experienced Senior Manager to join its team. This opportunity is ideal for a CPA or experienced accounting professional currently working in a public accounting environment who is ready for greater ownership, stronger client relationships, and a broader role in the success of the business.

You may have built a strong technical foundation at a national or large regional accounting firm. Now, you may be looking for an environment where your experience is more visible, your client relationships are deeper, and your contributions can have a more direct impact.

• Take greater ownership of client relationships and engagements.

• Have greater visibility and influence within the organization.

• Build a career path toward increased leadership and management responsibility.

You will take ownership of client engagements, work directly with clients to understand their businesses and challenges, and provide practical recommendations that support their continued growth and success.

description:
Competition # : 48849

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Permanent

Closing Date: 13-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Department of Seniors and Long-Term Care offers opportunities to grow and advance in a dynamic sector that touches the lives of many Nova Scotians. Along with our partners, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority, the Department of Health and Wellness, long-term care facilities, home care agencies, training institutions and other sector leaders, we're committed to continually improving the support system for seniors and others requiring home care, long-term care and other community-based supports.
In addition, the department supports the social and economic well-being of older adults ensuring policy formulation and effective decision-making as well as policy coherence across government departments as it relates to aging. The department is thinking differently about how to plan, fund, legislate and monitor to improve access and service delivery for Nova Scotia's senior population. To do this, we need leaders at all levels of the organization who embrace a challenge and believe in their ability to make a difference.

About Our Opportunity
Reporting to the Executive Director, Continuing Care, as the Director of Long Term Care (LTC), you will play a key leadership role in the Branch leadership team whose mandate is to lead, prioritize and drive Continuing Care initiatives that lead to better resident/client care outcomes, stronger system performance across the broader health system, and timely advice to senior leadership on sector priorities, risks, and emerging issues.
You will provide both operational and strategic leadership. Specifically, you are accountable for advancing program excellence and system change through strategic partnerships, and for overseeing programs, initiatives and projects that are governed by multiple pieces of provincial legislation, regulations, policies, and standards. You will maintain a strong connection to the sector, monitor performance and emerging pressures, identify and assess risks, and provide timely, evidence-informed advice to senior leadership on policy, investment, operational priorities, and mitigation strategies. You will also work collaboratively with multiple and diverse stakeholders to strengthen the continuing care system and improve access to quality care.

Primary Accountabilities
More specifically, in this role you will:

• Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Continuing Care sector, ensuring alignment with government priorities, departmental direction, and broader health system objectives.

• Maintain an ongoing understanding of sector pressures, performance, emerging issues, and system risks, and translate this intelligence into timely advice and action.

• Advise senior leadership on Continuing Care sector policy, investment considerations, operational pressures, and risk mitigation strategies.

• Identify, assess, and escalate emerging issues and risks, and lead or support coordinated responses as appropriate.

• Lead the implementation of programs, initiatives, and system improvement efforts within a complex legislative, regulatory, and policy environment.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with operators, service providers, health system partners, and other stakeholders to understand impacts, inform decisions, and support system performance.

• Support policy and program development by bringing operational insight, sector intelligence, and practical implementation considerations into decision-making.

• Influence and contribute to strategic planning, priority setting, and resource discussions related to Continuing Care services in Nova Scotia.

• Demonstrate sound fiscal oversight paired with an understanding of complex funding environments.

Will be required to support the broader continuing care/department programs as needed.

Qualifications and Experience
You have experience in complex, multi-faceted environments where understanding interdependencies across program areas, sectors, and systems is critical to success, and you apply this understanding in your everyday work.
You are strategic and adaptive, enjoy collaborative planning, and are able to meet the challenges inherent in a fast pace complex system. You are skilled at synthesizing information from multiple sources, assessing impacts, and recommending practical, timely courses of action.
You are resourceful and influential in your ability to secure buy-in through written materials and presentation, build capacity, optimize provincial resources and demonstrate public accountability. You have demonstrated experience identifying emerging operational, strategic, and reputational risks, and providing advice to senior leaders on policy, program, operational, and investment matters. You think outside the box, and you have the confidence and conviction to introduce innovative concepts and solutions founded on sound reason, judgment, experience, and expertise.
You are a leader who has extensive experience leading teams to achieve results in a fast-paced, changing environment. You bring strong judgment, professionalism, and the ability to navigate sensitive issues with discretion while building trusted relationships across government, the health system, and external partners.
You possess a Bachelor's Degree in a related field and several years of progressive leadership experience. The possession of a Master's Degree, a background in Nursing and/or leadership experience in Continuing Care are considered an asset. An equivalent combination of related training and experience may be acceptable.
Leadership competencies required at this level of work are Decisiveness; Strategic Orientation; Developing Others; Team Leadership; Self-Awareness & Personal Impact; Effective Interactive Communication; Partnering & Relationship Building; and Intercultural Diversity Proficiency.
We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
An equivalent combination of training, education and experience will be considered. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day

• Will be required to work overtime on occasion

• Travel will be required

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

• A dynamic, client-focused office environment where service excellence and teamwork are our focus.

description:
## WHO WE ARE

Mariner innovates always and everywhere, turning novel ideas into practical solutions. From products and services to venture creation, we build better futures powered by people. Our purpose has always been to be a great, everlasting technology company for those who make an impact - elevating people, data, and technology in the best way to solve hard problems. Mariners build for change. Like SHIFT Energy, our energy management and decarbonization company. Or East Valley Ventures, created to scale social economic impact in our communities through investment and mentorship of emerging change-makers and their companies.

Mariner s purpose has always been to be a great, everlasting technology company and the core values that guide us every day are:

## OUR VALUES

• We care for our team.

• We care about the impact we have on our community.

• We serve by solving complex problems.

• We grow because growth fuels opportunities.

• We innovate always and everywhere.

• We build a business that lasts.

OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE: We are seeking a Senior OT Control Systems Engineer to join a critical industrial operations environment in Saint John, New Brunswick. In this role, you will be responsible for the design, support, optimization, and security of Operational Technology (OT) and industrial automation systems that enable safe and reliable operations. The successful candidate will bring extensive experience in process control, industrial networking, distributed control systems, and automation technologies within complex industrial settings such as refining, manufacturing, utilities, or other process-driven environments.
This is an on-site position in Saint John, NB.

## WHAT YOU LL BE DOING IN THE ROLE:

• Lead the design, implementation, and enhancement of OT and industrial control system solutions to support operational and business objectives.

• Configure, maintain, and troubleshoot automation systems, including DCS, PLC, HMI, SIS, and asset monitoring platforms.

• Develop and maintain control strategies, system configurations, and automation standards to improve performance, reliability, and safety.

• Design and support industrial networks, ensuring high availability, cybersecurity compliance, and secure system integration.

• Plan and execute system upgrades, patching, lifecycle management activities, and technology modernization initiatives.
