Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic to this position. If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.
If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

Job Summary:
The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.
The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;
• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

## Dietitian

## New Glasgow, Nova Scotia

## Reference #JL-GHM-9799

Glen Haven Manor Corporation is a trusted long-term care provider in Pictou Conty dedicated to enhancing the health, well-being, and quality of life of its residents. With a strong commitment to resident-centered care, the organization fosters a culture of compassion, respect, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Through the efforts of an engaged interdisciplinary team, they deliver high-quality services that support residents' physical, emotional, and social well-being while creating a positive and rewarding environment for employees.

## The Opportunity

Glen Haven Manor Corporation is seeking a Dietitian to join its leadership team. Reporting to the Administrator, the Dietitian provides clinical nutrition leadership and oversight for all aspects of Nutritional Services within the facility. This role is responsible for assessing resident nutritional needs, developing and monitoring nutrition care plans, overseeing menu planning and therapeutic diets, ensuring regulatory compliance, and supporting high-quality resident-centered care. The Dietitian collaborates closely with nursing, support services, residents, families, and interdisciplinary team members to promote optimal nutritional health and resident satisfaction.

As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the successful candidate will contribute to strategic planning initiatives, quality improvement programs, departmental leadership, and organizational objectives while fostering a positive and collaborative culture focused on excellence in care.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Assess the clinical nutritional needs of residents upon admission and complete ongoing evaluations, annual reviews, and reassessments as required.

• Develop, implement, and monitor individualized nutrition care plans.

• Recommend therapeutic diets, oral nutritional supplements, texture modifications, and other nutrition interventions as appropriate.

• Plan, organize, review, and revise menus to ensure compliance with Canada's Food Guide and therapeutic diet requirements.

• Participate in resident care conferences and contribute to interdisciplinary care planning.

• Collaborate with nursing staff, physicians, and other healthcare professionals to ensure coordinated nutritional support for residents.

• Educate residents, families, and staff on nutrition-related topics and best practices.

• Provide leadership and oversight to Nutritional Services staff and departmental operations.

• Establish performance expectations, conduct evaluations, and support staff development through coaching and mentorship.

• Participate in strategic planning initiatives and organizational improvement projects.

• Develop, implement, and maintain departmental policies, procedures, and best practices.

• Monitor departmental compliance with professional, regulatory, accreditation, and organizational standards.

• Conduct audits, inspections, and quality assurance activities to identify opportunities for improvement and implement corrective actions when required.

• Foster collaborative relationships across departments to support resident care and operational effectiveness.

• Participate in committees, quality initiatives, and organizational projects aimed at enhancing resident outcomes and service delivery.

• Support public relations and community engagement activities as required.

• Promote a positive, resident-focused culture and ensure exceptional service delivery within Nutritional Services.

• Ensure safe work practices and infection prevention and control standards are consistently maintained.

## Qualifications & Experience:

• Bachelor of Science in Applied Human Nutrition (Dietetics) or Nutrition Major.

• Completion of an approved Dietetic Internship Program.

• Professional registration with the Nova Scotia Regulator of Dietetics (NSRD) and/or membership in a recognized professional dietetic association.

• Management or Leadership Certificate considered an asset.

• Minimum three years of senior leadership experience in a healthcare environment, preferably within long-term care, or five years of nutrition management experience leading medium to large teams.

• Demonstrated experience in labour relations and applying collective agreements.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

• Experience with strategic planning considered an asset.

• Strong knowledge of clinical nutrition, therapeutic diets, food service operations, quality improvement, and healthcare regulations.

• Excellent communication, leadership, coaching, conflict resolution, and relationship-building skills.

• Strong organizational, time management, decision-making, and problem-solving abilities.

• Ability to work collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team environment.

• Demonstrated commitment to professionalism, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

## Position Overview:

The Saint John Police Force is now accepting applications for experienced Police Officers.

Police officers are an integral part of the community, responsible for maintaining law and order and protecting members of the public. Police officers build relationships with community members and work collaboratively with them to solve problems and enhance the wellbeing of the people they serve with self-confidence, analytical thinking, while always acting at a high moral standard with honesty and integrity.

## Minimum Requirements:

To become a Sworn Police Officer, as outlined in the New Brunswick Police Act, applicants must:

• Have reached the full age of nineteen years.

• Be a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident of Canada.

• Be a graduate of the Police Science Program at the Atlantic Police Academy OR

• Be a graduate of a comparable training course offered at a police training institute approved by the Minister OR

• Have a minimum of three years of satisfactory full-time service as a member of any police force in Canada.

• Not have been convicted of an offence under the Criminal Code (Canada), the Narcotic Control Act (Canada), or the Food and Drugs Act (Canada), or if convicted, shall have received a pardon.

• Have a valid driver's license.

The Youth Outreach Worker (YOW) is a frontline prevention and early intervention position within Mental Health & Addictions. Working with youth and young adults up to age 29, the Youth Outreach Worker provides community-based outreach, brief intervention, mental health promotion, addictions prevention, system navigation, and connection to services.

This position focuses on building trusting relationships with youth where they live, learn, work, and gather. Services are delivered through schools, community organizations, recreation settings, virtual platforms, and other community locations. title: Specialist Auditor
description:
## Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are seeking a Specialist Auditor

This is a permanent position with a global scope supporting Vale Base Metals operations in Canada, Brazil, and other international locations based in Toronto.

## About You

The Auditor is responsible for conducting independent and objective audit examinations to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management, and governance processes across Vale's operations in Canada and globally. The role involves performing audits in accordance with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) International Standards, Vale's Internal Audit Policy, and the highest ethical and professional standards.

This position supports the Board of Directors, Audit Committee, Fiscal Council, Executive Leadership, and Management by providing assurance and insights regarding the effectiveness of operational, financial, compliance, environmental, and governance controls. The Auditor contributes to improving business performance while safeguarding Vale's assets, people, reputation, and environment.

## In this role, you will:

• Conduct risk-based audits of operational, financial, compliance, and governance processes across Vale's business operations.

• Lead audit engagements, when required.

• Assess the effectiveness and efficiency of internal controls, risk management practices, and governance frameworks to identify opportunities for improvement.

• Evaluate compliance with applicable laws, regulations, policies, procedures, contracts, and internal standards.

• Verify the integrity, reliability, and accuracy of operational and financial information used for decision-making.

• Contribute to the protection and preservation of Vale's assets, employees, and environmental resources through comprehensive audit assessments.

• Execute audit engagements in accordance with established audit programs, professional auditing standards, internal methodologies, and ethical principles.

• Prepare clear, concise, and well-supported audit reports that accurately communicate observations, risks, recommendations, and conclusions.

• Present audit findings and recommendations to management and senior leadership.

• Maintain complete and accurate audit documentation and working papers while ensuring appropriate confidentiality and information security.

• Support investigations related to allegations received through the Whistleblower and Reporting Channels, including suspected fraud, misconduct, or internal control deficiencies.

• Collaborate with stakeholders across the organization's three lines of defense to strengthen risk management and control processes.

• Support internal audit activities related to Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance testing and certification requirements.

• Participate in departmental initiatives, including the development and enhancement of audit methodologies, procedures, work programs, reporting tools, analytics, and performance indicators.

• Provide advisory and consulting services when appropriate, while maintaining the independence required of the Internal Audit function.

• Stay informed of evolving audit standards, industry best practices, regulations, and emerging risks relevant to Vale's operations.

## Experience

• Minimum 5+ years of experience in Internal Audit.

• Professional certifications such as CIA, CPA, CISA, CRMA, CFA, or equivalent are preferred.

• Fluent in Portuguese language is considered an asset.

• Bachelor's degree in accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.

• Advanced education such as an MBA, Postgraduate Degree, Master's Degree is considered an asset.

• Strong knowledge of internal auditing standards, internal controls, enterprise risk management, corporate governance, SOX compliance, and fraud investigations.

• Experience conducting operational, financial, compliance, and risk-based audits in complex organizations.

• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, report-writing, and stakeholder management skills.

• Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively with diverse teams across multiple geographies and time zones.

• Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally, including remote operational sites, as required.

## What we Offer

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans, and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## Why Toronto

Toronto, Canada's largest city and financial hub, is a center of innovation, commerce, and culture. Known for its diverse economy and vibrant urban environment, Toronto offers unparalleled access to talent, technology, and global connectivity.

Our Toronto office serves as a strategic hub for corporate functions, technology development, and business operations. Here, we drive initiatives that support Vale Base Metals' global operations, leveraging advanced analytics, digital transformation, and strategic planning to ensure operational excellence across all regions.

Toronto's dynamic ecosystem enables collaboration with leading technology partners, universities, and research institutions, fostering innovation in mining and metals processing. This location is integral to shaping the future of sustainable mining and advancing our commitment to responsible resource development.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all.

We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success.

We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Pay Grade: F4T

Minimum Starting Salary: $100,000

Apply by: Friday, October 2, 2026

The Atlantic Hockey Group (AHG) is seeking an experienced and motivated hockey professional to serve as Director of Hockey Operations - New Brunswick. This leadership position will be responsible for the planning, management, delivery, and growth of AHG's youth and adult hockey programming throughout New Brunswick.

The successful candidate will be highly organized, development-focused, and well connected within the New Brunswick hockey community. This individual must be comfortable leading both on-ice programming and off-ice operations, while identifying opportunities to strengthen and expand AHG programming across the province. Candidates with recognized off-ice training certifications and relevant experience will also be considered for this position.

The Director of Hockey Operations will work closely with the AHG President and management team to oversee and grow the organization's New Brunswick operations.

• Provide leadership and oversight for AHG hockey programming throughout New Brunswick.

• Plan, organize, and deliver high-quality on-ice training and development programs.

• Lead coach recruitment and selection, ensuring coaching positions are filled with qualified, reliable, and appropriately experienced individuals.

• Coordinate tournaments, showcases, camps, leagues, and other seasonal programming.

• Work closely with AHG staff, coaches, instructors, and coordinators to maintain consistent program standards.

• Manage scheduling, staffing, logistics, and day-to-day program operations with strong attention to detail.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with coaches, facilities, associations, partners, and members of the New Brunswick hockey community.

• Identify opportunities to develop new programs and expand existing AHG programming throughout the province.

• Extensive background and experience within the hockey industry.

• Strong knowledge of the New Brunswick hockey landscape and established relationships within the hockey community.

• Proven ability to develop, organize, and manage multiple hockey programs simultaneously.

• Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.

description:
## COMPETITION NUMBER

## 202600416

## POSITION TITLE

Primary Care Paramedic

## LOCATION

Port Elgin, NB

## BARGAINING UNIT

NB Union – Specialized Health Care Professionals

## STATUS

Full time permanent

## HOURS OF WORK

Rotating days and nights, weekends, and statutory holidays. Subject to change due to operational requirements.

## ANTICIPATED START DATE

As soon as possible

## ANTICIPATED END DATE

Not applicable

## SALARY RANGE

As per collective agreement

## LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT

Written and spoken competency in one of the two official languages (English or French) is required and spoken competency in the other official language is preferred.

## CLOSING DATE

This competition will remain open until filled.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community, submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

title: Receptionist
description:
The Receptionist ensures the smooth running of the office they support while being the friendly first point of contact for those visiting the office and often for in-office staff.

## Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

• Handling all day-to-day, task-oriented activities for the office, including:
• Welcoming guests and visitors; offering refreshments.

• Managing inbound/outgoing calls.

• Managing incoming and outgoing mail and courier deliveries.

• Coordinating support for virtual and in-person meetings including catering, as required.

• Ensuring the boardroom is in order and that technology like microphone and speakers are switched on before and after meetings.

• Ensuring the boardroom is neat including wiping down the table and kitchenette area and maintaining the coffee/tea facilities in a neat and orderly fashion.

• Maintaining the kitchen in a clean and orderly manner: In particular, filling the dishwasher at the end of the day and emptying it at the beginning of each day including wiping down the counter if required.

• Maintaining the public and shared spaces in the office ensuring they are neat and orderly.

• Ensuring healthy and local (where possible) snacks and coffee are refreshed daily.

• Ensure that refuse bins in shared spaces, including the boardroom and kitchen, are regularly emptied and kept neat.

• Other tasks as they evolve.

## Qualifications/Skills

• Reliable, punctual, and professional.

• Experience working with Microsoft Office specifically Word, Excel, PowerPoint.

• Excellent verbal and oral communication skills, interpersonal skills.

## About the m5 Group of Companies:

Group m5 is one of Atlantic Canada's largest independent collectives of industry-leading communications firms, including m5 the agency, MQO Research, and Group ATN Consulting.

We recognize that to build an excellent team, we need to provide an excellent place to work. m5 is an employer of choice in Atlantic Canada. We offer a work-life balance uncommon in the industry and the opportunity to work with some of the best and brightest minds locally and nationally. Every day, you will collaborate with a talented team to help us help our clients make meaningful changes in their communities and in their industries. At m5, variety is abundant, and if you seek it, there is endless opportunity. Regardless of your role or career level, you will learn from your colleagues and clients. We support staff through courses, webinars, and mentoring to keep everyone current in our dynamic industry. We help our team balance work and life with summer hours, and a generous annual vacation break. We offer health insurance, a corporate gym membership, and retirement savings plans. We've even created a "curiosity credit" to ensure staff can refill their creative cups outside our walls. We take care of our team, so they can bring their best selves to work-ready to collaborate and innovate. Your team can't wait to welcome you!

Don't meet every single requirement? Studies show equity-deserving individuals often apply only if they meet every qualification. The m5 group of companies is an equal-opportunity employer and is dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. So, if you are excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may just be the right candidate for this or other roles. If you require accommodation to participate in this recruitment, please get in touch with join-our-team-accommodations@m5.ca (accommodation requests only; other emails will not be read).

This position is based in St. John's, NL and is being offered on a 1-year contractual, part-time basis. Please e-mail your application by October 9, 2026 stating the position title "Receptionist - St. John's" to Human Resources at join-our-team@m5.ca.

For further information on m5, please visit our website at www.m5.ca.

title: Licensed Practical Nurse (L.P.N.)
description:
## Join Our Nursing Team as a Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)

Location: Berwick, Nova Scotia
Department: Nursing
Reports to: Nurse Manager / Shift Supervisor

Union: CUPE
Job Type: Full-Time / Part-Time (based on operational need)

## Pay Rate

• Hourly Rate of Pay: $30.3493 - $34,2443

• Plus: Shift premiums for evenings and weekends

• Good News: Wages are expected to increase within the year-with retroactive pay

## Why Choose Grandview Manor?

At Grandview Manor, every nurse is part of a compassionate, team-oriented environment where your expertise truly makes a difference. As a not-for-profit long-term care home in the heart of the Annapolis Valley, we are committed to providing high-quality, person-centered care that supports the well-being of our residents, families, and community.

You'll work in a collaborative, respectful, and supportive setting that values your skills, experience, and dedication.

## Perks & Benefits

We take care of our team the same way we take care of our residents:

• Comprehensive Health Benefits (medical, dental, vision)

• Lumino Virtual Health Care - convenient access to healthcare professionals

• NSHEPP Pension Plan - secure and reliable retirement savings

• $5.00 Staff Lunches - healthy, affordable meals on-site

• Health & Wellness Committee - wellness initiatives, activities, and staff recognition

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP) - confidential support for you and your family

• 10% Off at Larry's Pharmacy - exclusive savings for staff

• Paid Vacation and Sick Time - balance work and personal life

## What You'll Do

As an LPN, you'll provide compassionate, resident-focused care while supporting the nursing team and mentoring staff. Your responsibilities include:

• Supervising and guiding Continuing Care Assistants (CCAs) and Long Term Care Assistants (LTCAs)

• Providing physical, emotional, and spiritual care to residents

• Administering medications, injections, venipuncture, and treatments per physician orders

• Communicating effectively with residents, families, staff, and interdisciplinary teams

• Assisting in staffing, scheduling, and orientation of new staff

• Participating in care planning, assessment, and ongoing review of resident needs

• Maintaining accurate documentation and records

• Providing outreach services to affiliated facilities as assigned

• Responding to emergencies with sound clinical judgment and critical thinking

## What We're Looking For

• Current license with the College of Licensed Practical Nurses of Nova Scotia (CLPNNS)

• Ability to practice full scope of LPN duties

• Strong leadership, organizational, and communication skills

• Ability to collaborate effectively and delegate appropriately

• Compassionate, conscientious, and resident-focused

• Skilled in critical thinking, clinical judgment, and emergency response

## Why You'll Love Working Here

• Join a supportive, team-oriented work environment

• Make a meaningful difference in the lives of residents and their families every day

• Access opportunities for professional growth and development

## How to Apply

If you're passionate about nursing and want to be part of a compassionate, values-driven team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today through our Career Centre at https://workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/mdf/recruitment/recruitment.html?cid=e8d43e97-d93e-42e8-9137-aa945a354f23&ccId=19000101_000001?=en_CA

Join Grandview Manor-and help us deliver care, comfort, and compassion every day.

The Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Program of NL Health Services – Eastern Urban Zone is seeking a qualified and highly motivated Hematopathologist to join the Hematopathology Division at Health Sciences Centre in St. John's, NL.

The successful candidate will join three (3) other Hematopathologists and work in collaboration with molecular and diagnostic pathologists, clinical and medical microbiologists, genetics scientists, and clinical chemists, providing the province with tertiary and quaternary laboratory care.

The Division of Hematopathology offers transfusion medicine, bone marrow pathology, flow cytometry, hematology core lab, coagulation, and hemoglobinopathy services. It also provides training to medical laboratory technology students, medical students, anatomic pathology, and other medical residents. Hematopathologists are supported by molecular pathology and cytogenetics laboratories providing testing for various myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms, and by immunohistochemistry laboratories.

This full-time position will also share responsibilities in providing medical oversight in hematopathology and transfusion medicine to rural hospitals and community health centres across NL, offering basic hematology, coagulation, and transfusion medicine testing and transfusion services. The position will provide consultative services for a wide variety of patient programs including hematology, bleeding and coagulation disorders, bone marrow transplantation, and blood transfusion.

Through strong formal affiliations with Memorial University, and on the recommendation of the Discipline Chair, the successful candidate will be eligible for a clinical faculty appointment in the Academic Discipline of Laboratory Medicine and will be expected to participate in collaborative research activities and scholarship including teaching, research, and other academic pursuits.

Work Environment

St. John's is a vibrant, historic city on the eastern tip of North America, offering a warm and welcoming community, a thriving arts and culture scene, and easy access to the stunning natural landscapes of the Avalon Peninsula — including whale watching, hiking, and some of the most dramatic coastlines in Canada.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

Montana Consulting Group is a human resources consulting firm with a difference. Besides consulting, we have developed a reputation for high quality customized and standard management development programs that make a tangible difference in workplaces across Canada.

Our approach is practical and down to earth, and your style will need to reflect that. Even if you are not deeply experienced in these areas today, this is an opportunity for someone who wants to learn from industry experts.

Ideally, you would be based at our office in Moncton, but you will be required to travel regularly within and occasionally outside New-Brunswick. title: Director of Finance
description:
Higher Talent is excited to conduct an executive search for a strategic, hands-on, entrepreneurial Director of Finance for Fort Amherst Healthcare, in St. John's, NL.

## WHO WE ARE:

Fort Amherst Healthcare, a subsidiary of Fort Amherst Properties, is an investment company headquartered in St. John's focused on the development of high-quality seniors housing and health care services. The company currently owns and operates approximately 400 personal care home suites across the province, consisting of both licensed personal care homes and independent living seniors' apartments. Facilities under management include Bishops Gardens (St John's), Westbury Estates (Southlands), Mountain View Retirement Centre (Corner Brook), Cambridge Estates (St. John's).

With happiness, health and wellness as top priorities, we strive to offer an extensive range of services, living options, and lifestyle choices to meet individual needs - whether highly active, needing a little assistance day-to-day, or requiring a custom-designed care plan.

To learn more about us, please visit Fort Amherst Healthcare.

## THE ROLE:

The Director of Finance is a strategic, hands-on finance leader with a strong accounting foundation and demonstrated experience managing the financial operations of a complex, people-focused organization. The successful candidate will build and professionalize the finance function, establish scalable corporate systems and partner closely with the President, Director of Operations, site leadership, the Board, lenders and external advisors.

## RESPONSIBILITIES:

Reporting to the President, the Director of Finance will lead accounting, financial reporting, planning and analysis, treasury, banking, tax, audit coordination, lender and Board reporting and financial controls. The role will also oversee defined corporate-support functions including information technology, insurance, contracting, procurement, supply-chain governance, vendor administration and shared-service coordination.

## Financial Leadership & Reporting

• Lead accounting and financial reporting across all properties and legal entities.

• Own monthly close, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, financial controls and scenario analysis.

• Standardize accounting practices, policies, controls and reporting processes.

• Translate financial results, risks and opportunities into actionable recommendations for the President and Board.

## Treasury, Tax & Risk

• Oversee cash management, banking, treasury, tax, audit coordination and lender reporting.

• Support financing, lender diligence, covenant compliance and transaction requirements.

• Oversee insurance, risk management and related regulatory requirements.

## Systems & Business Operations

• Modernize financial systems, reporting and workflow automation.

• Oversee technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, continuity and third-party providers.

• Establish scalable processes for contracts, procurement, vendors and shared services

## Systems & Business Operations

• Modernize financial systems, reporting and workflow automation.

• Oversee technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, continuity and third-party providers.

• Establish scalable processes for contracts, procurement, vendors and shared services.

## Growth & Integration

• Support M&A diligence, financing and transaction execution.

• Lead finance, banking, insurance, systems and vendor integration for acquisitions and new entities.

• Build scalable shared-service processes as the organization grows.

## Leadership & Partnership

• Serve as a trusted financial and business advisor to the President.

• Partner closely with the Director of Operations and site leadership.

• Strengthen financial understanding and accountability across the organization.

• Lead and develop finance and business-support personnel as the function grows.

## ABOUT YOU:

• CPA designation.

• 7+ years of progressive financial leadership experience; experience in healthcare, long-term care, seniors living, or another regulated, multi-site environment is an asset.

• Degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

• Strong experience in budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, and financial controls.

• Strong business acumen with the ability to connect financial performance to operational realities.

• Exceptional analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail.

• Proven leadership experience with the ability to mentor, develop, and motivate a team.

• Experience with accounting/ERP systems and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.

• Proactive, hands-on approach with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

• Knowledge of government funding programs and regulatory requirements is an asset.

## WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT:

An attractive total compensation package, including a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, employer matched RRSP, personal time off, professional development and growth opportunities.

## HOW TO APPLY:

If you are financially rigorous, commercially minded, and comfortable moving seamlessly between detailed execution and executive-level decision-making, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact. Bring your sound financial judgment, integrity, accountability, and leadership to Fort Amherst Healthcare-and take the next step in your career.

NL Health Services – Eastern Rural Zone invites applications for three (3) permanent full-time Hospitalist Physicians at Dr. G.B. Cross Memorial Hospital in Clarenville, NL.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. Competition No. 2627-074

The salary scale for NSCC Faculty is based on steps that range from $81,760.18 - $104,267.58. Faculty may receive up to a maximum of five steps for full-time equivalent years of instructional experience (instructional experience is defined as teaching high school Grade 10 and above) and may receive up to an additional four steps for the relevant occupational experience. The maximum a new Faculty can expect to receive is nine steps or $97,388.02.

This is a designated competition open to individuals who self-identify as Mi'kmaq.

Qualifications

## Qualifications and Occupational Experience:

• The minimum educational qualification for this position is a Bachelor/Master of Education and/or a relevant university degree in Math, Social Sciences, or the Sciences (e.g., Biology, Physics, Chemistry), or Bachelor of Engineering (or other Engineering credential), or an undergraduate degree in a field related to the subjects to be taught.

• You have a minimum of five years (full-time equivalent) of recent and related occupational experience teaching at the High School or post-secondary level.

• Experience in a team teaching environment and a strong track record of working collaboratively.

• Experience in curriculum and resource development.

• Experience teaching online and/or using e-learning technology in a blended format is an asset.

• A strong working understanding of Universal Design for Learning is an asset.

• You are familiar with and comfortable using computer applications such as the Microsoft Office Suite, e-mail and Learning Management Systems.

• You have demonstrated experience liaising with business and industry in your field.

• You are comfortable working in a digital environment; you take responsibility for acquiring knowledge about advancing technology; and you are committed to using technology in support of an exceptional student experience, including multi-media technologies and a variety of platforms that will engage students in online and blended learning.

• Ideally, you have related experience in delivery of educational programs or training to adults.

• Occupational experience that includes experience in providing performance feedback will be considered an asset.

• You have knowledge and experience in applying WHMIS, Occupational Health and Safety and occupation-specific safety practices.

• You are comfortable using multi-media technologies and a variety of platforms that will serve to engage students in online and blended learning capacities. The ability to teach effectively in an online/blended environment which includes building knowledge of best practices for the delivery and management of courses delivered whole or in part online, using a course management system to communicate with students and to foster and support a collaborative online learning community with and between students will be an important factor in your success. Candidates who do not have previous online/blended teaching experience must be open to and willing to participate in training for this delivery model.

## Relevant Skills and Knowledge:

• You demonstrate a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, accessibility, and anti-racism

• You possess excellent presentation skills and can facilitate content effectively and engagingly to a variety of audiences

• You are known for your superior interpersonal skills and can manage interpersonal relationships and issues effectively

• Your superb team building skills will enable you to develop a positive classroom dynamic and productive collegial relationships

• Your commitment to excellence, to life-long learning and to community involvement make you an ideal candidate for Faculty at NSCC

Responsibilities
As a member of the School of Access, Business, Creative Industries and Education faculty team, you will:

• Provide theoretical and practical instruction in the Adult Learning Program (ALP) primarily in the areas of Science and Math and potentially Social Studies. This role will involve in-person delivery during the daytime and may include synchronous online delivery in the evening.

• Collaboratively design and deliver educational experiences for a diverse group of learners. This will include preparation, instruction, assessment, and evaluation of students using a broad range of flexible teaching and learning practices and technologies such as Learning Management Systems (e.g., Brightspace) and classroom technology.

• Ensure health and safety practices and procedures are followed in your classroom, shops, and labs.

• Maintain currency with the latest industry practices relevant to your program and to continually develop your understanding of 21st century teaching and learning practices. This position may involve different delivery modalities (e.g., in-class, online, blended online/in-class), off-site instruction and alternate work hours such as weekends and evenings.

• Related duties include but are not limited to academic and career advisement, participating on committees, program marketing, curriculum revision/development through collaborative practice within faculty working groups, supporting, and monitoring work placements, liaising with business and industry, representing the College as required and upholding NSCC policies and procedures.

As a condition of employment, Faculty at NSCC must complete a part-time adult education program delivered by NSCC. This adult education program is a significant investment on the part of NSCC in the learning and development of new employees. To achieve regular status, all probationary, full or part-time Faculty of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Faculty whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

Candidates selected for interviews will be expected to provide at least three recent occupational references. The successful candidate will be expected to provide official transcripts to show proof of academic achievements.

NSCC is committed to the full inclusion of all applicants. As part of this commitment, NSCC will ensure that applicants are provided reasonable accommodations, as required. If accommodation is needed to participate in the job application process, please contact Jaclynn Kelly, HR Generalist, at jaclynn.kelly@nscc.ca. description:
## Head of Communications
Halifax, Nova Scotia
Reference #JL-PSA-10132

PSA Halifax is Atlantic Canada's leading container terminal operator and an integral gateway for global trade. As part of the PSA International network, one of the world's largest port groups, PSA Halifax connects international supply chains through two container terminals and a corporate office in Halifax, Nova Scotia. Through strategic investments, operational excellence, and a commitment to people, PSA Halifax plays a vital role in supporting economic growth across the region and beyond.

As the organization navigates significant transformation across the shipping and logistics industry, PSA Halifax is seeking a Head of Communications to help shape and strengthen communications across the business. This newly created role will be instrumental in driving employee engagement, supporting organizational change, strengthening stakeholder relationships, and ensuring clear, consistent communication during a period of growth and evolution. As PSA Halifax continues to evolve in response to industry transformation, workforce change, technology adoption, and significant growth opportunities, the Head of Communications will play a key role in helping employees, leaders, and stakeholders navigate change with confidence.

## The Role

Reporting to the Managing Director, with a close working relationship with Human Resources and regional communications leadership, the Head of Communications will serve as PSA Halifax's principal communications resource. This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role responsible for establishing and leading the organization's communications function while supporting a diverse workforce of salaried and unionized employees. This is an ideal opportunity for a communications leader who thrives in building, shaping, and executing communications strategies from the ground up. As a team of one, the successful candidate will be equally comfortable developing strategy and rolling up their sleeves to write, plan, and deliver communications across the organization.

The successful candidate will partner with senior leaders to translate business priorities, operational developments, organizational change initiatives, and industry developments into clear, engaging, and effective communications. They will play a critical role in fostering alignment, trust, transparency, and engagement across multiple employee groups while supporting the organization's reputation among key external stakeholders.

Working within a dynamic and evolving industry environment, the Head of Communications will help strengthen connections between leadership and employees, support employee and labour-relations communication initiatives, enhance employer branding efforts, and contribute to PSA Halifax's long-term culture and business objectives.

## Key Responsibilities:

## Internal Communications & Employee Engagement

• Develop and execute a comprehensive internal communications and employee engagement strategy aligned with organizational priorities.

• Translate corporate strategy, business objectives, operational updates, and transformation initiatives into meaningful communications for employees.

description:
Labour Relations Lawyer - Association of University of New Brunswick Teachers (AUNBT)

The Association of University of New Brunswick Teachers (AUNBT) invites applications for the position of Labour Relations Lawyer.

AUNBT (a union under the NB Industrial Relations Act) represents approximately 600 full-time and 350 contract academic staff located primarily on UNB's Fredericton and Saint John campuses.

## Key Responsibilities

Subject to the direction of the President and Executive Committee, the Professional OfficerLabour Relations Lawyer will perform the following representative duties:

• Provide substantial professional support to the Grievance Committee in all aspects of the grievance process, including case management, grievance hearings and arbitrations, and research.

• Assist the President and various AUNBT committees.

• Support negotiation teams in the collective bargaining process.

• Be involved in communicating with and offering support services to AUNBT members.

• Promote good working relations with various levels of UNB's administration and with other UNB employee groups. The successful candidate may have a role in relations with other local, provincial and national associations with similar interests.

• Undertake other strategic, legal, or policy initiatives as requested to support the objectives of AUNBT and its membership.

## Qualifications

Applicants will have a law degree and preferably postgraduate training in a labour-related area. The successful candidate will have experience working in academic and/or unionized environments. Experience with interpreting collective agreements, the grievance and arbitration processes, and facility with legal/contract drafting is essential. The successful candidate must possess strong analytical, communication and interpersonal skills. They must be flexible and able to work collegially. They will work from UNB's Fredericton campus and must be able to travel to the Saint John (and, occasionally, Moncton) campus as needed.

AUNBT is an equal opportunity employer, committed to principles of equity and diversity in the workplace. The applications of Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.

## Salary Range

$105,540 - $167,243 (Effective July 1, 2026). Compensation is governed by AUNBT's established salary grid, with starting placement on the grid calculated strictly by years of directly relevant experience (0 to 27 years).

## Deadline

Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Please submit a letter of application and a detailed résumé to Adam Wilson, President, AUNBT at aunbt@aunbt.ca.

description:
## COMPETITION NUMBER

202600431

## POSITION TITLE

Emergency Medical Technician

## LOCATION

Moncton, NB

## BARGAINING UNIT

Canadian Union of Public Employees

## STATUS

Full time permanent

## HOURS OF WORK

Rotating days, weekends, and statutory holidays. Subject to change due to operational requirements.

## ANTICIPATED START DATE

As soon as possible

## ANTICIPATED END DATE

Not applicable

## SALARY RANGE

As per collective agreement

## LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT

Written and spoken competency in one of the two official languages (English or French) is required and spoken competency in the other official language is preferred.

## CLOSING DATE

This competition will remain open until filled.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

Salary: As per collective agreement.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Emergency Medical Technicians are based on the current Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements for Emergency Medical Technician as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our emergency medical technicians provide transportation and patient care for non-urgent low acuity patients and are expected to maintain and operate ambulances and related equipment in accordance with patient needs and public safety.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in emergency medical technology or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• High school graduation plus an Emergency Medical Technician program/course

• Must meet all legislated requirements for Emergency Medical Technician in New Brunswick

• Must be registered, active Emergency Medical Technician with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

• Written & Spoken competency in one of the two official languages (English or French) is required and spoken competency in the other official language is preferred.

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your EMT certificate from a recognized institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as an Emergency Medical Technician within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR Level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

Please note: Related and allied duties may be assigned from time to time as may become necessary to the operation of Ambulance NB. Also other competencies related to changes in PANB Scope of Practice guidelines and approved by the Provincial Medical Director may also be added to the duties and responsibilities of this classification.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

title: Warehouse Shipper/Receiver
description:
Jump Recruitment, on behalf of our client, Nu-Quest Distribution Inc., are seeking a Warehouse Shipper/Receiver to join their team in Mount Pearl, NL.

## Position Summary:

The Warehouse Shipper/Receiver is responsible for the accurate receiving, storage, handling, and shipping of products within the warehouse. This role supports inventory control, order fulfillment, warehouse organization, and occasional delivery services while ensuring compliance with company procedures, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), and product handling requirements.

## Key Responsibilities:

Receiving Operations

• Receive incoming shipments and verify products against shipping documentation.

• Inspect all deliveries for damage and report discrepancies or shortages.

• Use handheld scanning equipment to receive inventory into the warehouse management system.

• Accurately stock products in designated locations and rotate inventory according to expiry dates, ensuring older stock is positioned for first use.

• Reconcile receiving discrepancies and communicate issues to the Warehouse Supervisor.

Shipping Operations

• Verify customer orders against invoices to ensure accuracy and completeness.

• Pick, pack, and prepare orders for shipment using appropriate packaging materials and containers.

• Apply shipping labels, identifying information, and special handling instructions as required.

• Select the most cost-effective shipping methods while maintaining service requirements.

• Obtain management approval for any additional shipping costs before releasing shipments.

Warehouse Maintenance and Inventory Support

• Assist in maintaining a clean, organized, and safe warehouse environment.

• Perform shelf organization and inventory housekeeping activities.

• Identify and remove expired, damaged, or outdated products and transfer them to the Returns Department according to company procedures.

• Support inventory accuracy through proper product handling and storage practices.

Delivery Responsibilities

• Perform occasional deliveries and pickups as required.

• Deliver products to hospitals, pharmacies, and other customers throughout the Metro area, CBS, Avondale, Pouch Cove, and the Southern Shore.

• Collect and return signed documentation, including Proof of Delivery forms and COS slips, when required.

• Ensure all products are transported safely and securely.

• Return all customer product returns, packaging, and documentation to the warehouse or office upon completion of deliveries.

• Ensure no products, returns, or packaging materials remain in company vehicles after deliveries are completed.

## Qualifications & Skills:

• Previous warehouse experience is required.

• Valid driver's license with a satisfactory driving record is preferred for delivery duties.

• Experience with inventory management systems and handheld scanners is considered an asset.

## Job Details:

• Comprehensive benefits package provided.

• Fast-paced warehouse environment.

• Frequent standing, walking, bending, and lifting.

• Ability to lift and move products weighing up to 50 lbs.

• Exposure to varying warehouse temperatures and shipping activities.

• Training provided for Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), product storage and handling, temperature-controlled shipping procedures, damaged products receiving and reporting and company warehouse policies and procedures.

title: Registered Nurse (RN), SANE - Casual
description:
## ## Requisition Details:

Employment Status: Casual
Program Name: Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner
Work Schedule: Days, Evenings, Nights, Weekends
Union/Bargaining Unit: NSNU
On Call: Yes
Location Coverage: SANEs must be able to respond to a case in all 3 designated emergency departments (Truro, Amherst, Musquodoboit Valley) within 1.5 hours.
Existing Vacancy: Yes - we're currently hiring candidates for an existing vacancy in this position.

If External candidates are interested in working concurrently as a visiting nurse with VON, please indicate your interest on your cover letter.

The SANE course is 6 days long in the classroom, often in Truro, with a 2-day Skills Lab usually in Halifax on a weekend. VON orientation and e-learning are also required with a date to be determined.

Hired nurses will be trained to work in a support role with fully trained SANEs, with plans to take the next SANE course offered. Questions can be directed to the Manager at SANE@von.ca

## Job Summary:

The Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) program is a provincial, community-based intervention service that is provided, in this region, to Colchester and Cumberland counties and the Eastern Shore area. It is managed/administrated by the VON Colchester East Hants site. Specially trained RNs and NPs provide timely, professional, confidential, trauma-informed medical and forensic care and referrals for aftercare to post-pubescent victims of sexual assault and domestic violence, of all genders and orientations, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

SANE nurses report to the Manager of the SANE program. SANE nurses will be hired as an employee of VON and all training will be provided. The SANE nurse role may include, but is not limited to medical and forensic examinations, evidence collection, documentation, education, providing referrals, collection of statistical data, and providing testimony in court. On-call SANEs must attend scheduled monthly meetings and training sessions as necessary. On-call SANEs must have access to reliable transportation and be able to respond to a call to the designated emergency department (Truro, Amherst, Musquodoboit Valley) within 1.5 hours.

*Current VON nurses are encouraged to apply and may hold positions in both the visiting nurse program and the SANE program. External candidates with a primary job elsewhere will be assigned on-call hours based on the availability provided to us. Available hours must be provided 6 weeks in advance for each month. If External candidates are interested in working concurrently as a visiting nurse with VON, please indicate your interest on your cover letter.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Function as part of the on-call SANE response team, which may include:
• Available for approximately 96 hours a month (divided into blocks of 12–48-hour blocks of time)

• Respond to calls at designated site within 1.5 hours.

• Triage clients to determine if any necessary medical treatment is needed before forensic exam.

• Conduct medical-forensic exams including proper collection of photographic and other evidence, accurately conducting sexual assault medical forensic interviews, and maintaining chain of evidence.

• Testing for and administering prophylactic medications including emergency contraception.

• Document all aspects of the encounter with the victim as per regulatory requirements, including mandatory duty to report as appropriate.

• Awareness of other community programs related to sexual assault.

• Testify in legal proceedings as necessary.

• Maintain confidentiality.

• Use a trauma-informed approach when caring for victims/survivors.

• Provide client-centered and culturally competent care.

• Maintain accountability based on the standards established by the Nova Scotia College of Nursing, policies and protocols of the individual healthcare facilities and the SANE program, and ethical and legal requirements of professional practice.

• Maintain competency through regular practice, attending monthly staff meetings, and professional development opportunities.

• Access confidential debriefing services as needed to maintain emotional and physical wellness

• Optional opportunities to teach or present information to schools and community organizations

## External and Internal Relationships:

• Engages clients with a trauma-informed approach, allowing clients to choose options and treatments best suited to their preferences.

• Knowledge of community services related to sexual assault response and care at all stages, and understands the importance of maintaining good relationships with these partners.

## Education, Designations and Experience:

• Must be licensed as a RN or NP in the province of Nova Scotia.

• Current CPR required.

• Must be available to complete NS community-based SANE training upon hire with commitment to complete full SANE certification at a later date.

• Previous SANE experience a strong asset.

• Three (3) years of experience in the community, women's health, or acute care preferred.

• Experience in forensic or emergency nursing, mental health, women's health, sexual health, crisis response, counseling, or trauma-informed care, is an asset.

• Knowledge of the criminal justice system is an asset.

## Skill Requirements:

• Ability to observe and make effective assessment of clinical and forensic issues.

• Strong attention to detail.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills that allow for effective engagement with victims/survivors of sexual assault, staff, SANE team, community partners, and the public.

• Strong interpersonal relationship building skills.

• Ability to be independent with decision-making

• Ability to work collaboratively as a member of an interdisciplinary team, with SANE partner, and community partners.

• The capacity to adhere to strict confidentiality.

• Able to articulate effectively knowledge of components of quality and risk management principles as they relate to clinical practices.

• Effective time management skills

## Other:

• Access to reliable transportation

• Current and original copies of satisfactory Criminal Record/Vulnerable Sector check and Child Abuse Registry check.

• Available to work flexible hours.

• The use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) will be required

Working conditions and physical demands: This role requires a detail-oriented approach in a dynamic environment, with physical activity including lifting, carrying (using proper techniques), bending, reaching, kneeling, and other movements that emphasize good body mechanics. Individuals in the role are required to walk, sit, stand, and climb stairs throughout the day, with some tasks requiring fine hand movements.

Attention Current Employees (Internal Applicants): If you are applying to a unionized position and you are a member of its bargaining unit, please be aware that this posting may remain open beyond the deadline if there are not enough applicants to fill the position(s). If the posting remains open after the initial deadline, VON may close the posting at its' discretion or a rolling deadline equivalent to the posting period specified in your Collective Agreement will be deemed, and each successive period will be treated as a separate posting for purposes of comparing seniority between candidates.

• Support resident-centered dining practices and respond respectfully to resident needs and preferences, while promoting dignity and choice.

• Dispose of waste and recycling according to organizational procedures.

• Record daily temperatures of all dishwashers; wash and rinse cycles.

• Maintain monthly cleaning and kitchen duties schedules; sign off when completed.

## Inventory and Supply Support

• Stock shelves, refrigerators, and storage areas as required.

• Assist with receiving, storing, rotating, and organizing food and supplies.

• Report shortages, damaged products, or equipment concerns to the appropriate supervisor.

• Support efforts to minimize waste and ensure proper food handling practices.

• Ensure correct labeling of food items and leftovers.

• Follow the first-in-first-out rule to ensure correct rotation of food items.

• Document spoiled foods and wastage to monitor inventory.

## Teamwork and Collaboration

• Work collaboratively with Food Services Department team members and other departments.

• Follow oral and written instructions accurately and efficiently.

• Demonstrate flexibility in performing assigned duties and learning new tasks.

• Participate in orientation, training, and educational opportunities as required.

• Report equipment concerns, food shortages, safety hazards, and incidents promptly.

• Be respectful of your fellow workers.

• Take part in department quality control audits and procedures.

• Assist in the training of department staff and students.

• Perform other related duties as assigned.

## Required:

• Grade 12 education or equivalent.

• First aid in choking (obtained internally within organizational timelines).

## Preferred:

• Recent Food Safety Training or equivalent food safety certification.

## Experience

## Preferred:
