## Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• Ability to read, write, and follow oral and written instructions.

• Ability to complete routine written documentation and records.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

• Commitment to excellent customer service and resident satisfaction.

• Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

• Willingness to learn new skills and tasks.

• Ability to maintain confidentiality regarding residents and organizational information.

• Knowledge of safe food handling and sanitation practices is considered an asset.

• Knowledge of dementia care principles and the ability to use respectful, person-centred approaches when communicating and supporting residents during meal service.

## Working Conditions

## Physical Demands

• Shift work, including days, evenings, weekends, and holidays.

• Frequent standing and walking throughout the shift.

• Ability to safely handle and transport food service supplies, meal trays, and equipment using appropriate lifting techniques and assistive devices as required.

• Frequent reaching, bending, stooping, pushing, pulling, and repetitive movements.

• Ability to prioritize tasks and complete work within established timelines.

• Ability to follow detailed instructions and maintain accuracy.

• Ability to adapt to changing priorities and operational needs.

• Professionalism.

title: Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)
description:
The Maritime Odd Fellows Home is a 47 Bed Long Term Care Facility located in the town of Pictou, overlooking picturesque Pictou Harbour. The Odd Fellows Home has a long history providing quality care to our valued Residents and is in need of a Full-time LPN to join our care team.

The Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) utilizes the nursing process, critical thinking and problem solving skills to provide holistic care to individuals, families, and groups. The LPN is responsible for planning nursing care in an assigned area as required by individualized Resident needs and according to dependent and independent nursing functions while adhering to recognized nursing techniques, procedures, and established standards based on the scope of practical nursing, under the direction of the Registered Nurse.

The LPN contributes to the efficient and effective functioning of the Home, coordination of Resident care and staffing. The LPN accepts responsibility for maintaining and continually enhancing competencies through ongoing professional development including participation in education programs, research and continuous quality activities. The LPN practices according to the College of Licensed Practical Nurses of Nova Scotia Code of Ethics for Licensed Practical Nurses, Standards of Nursing Practice, specialty standards as applicable and the policies and procedures of the Maritime Odd Fellows Home. Working collaboratively as a member of the health care team by respecting and acknowledging the roles of all those within the healthcare system in contributing to safe, competent and ethical care, the LPN provides Resident-centred care that responds appropriately to the physiological, psychological, social, cultural, and spiritual needs.

The Opportunity We are currently seeking Maintenance Technicians – Heavy Duty Equipment Technicians to join our Surface and Underground Mobile Maintenance Team in Voisey's Bay, Labrador, a fly-in fly-out operation. These are permanent on-site positions, working a 2 weeks on, 2 weeks off rotational schedule. Relocation to the province of Newfoundland and Labrador is required for this position. As a Maintenance Technician – Heavy Duty Equipment Technician you will be responsible for repairing, troubleshooting, adjusting, overhauling, servicing, and maintaining mobile heavy-duty mining equipment. Additionally, in this position you will:
• Inspect Bolters, Jumbo Drills, Haul Trucks, Graders, Bulldozers, Excavators, Shovels, Loaders and other surface and underground equipment for proper performance and troubleshoot equipment to detect faults and malfunctions.

• Inspect, examine and test parts in order to recommend the extent and nature of the work to be done then test the final repair.

• Service attachments and working tools as required.

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodations are equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• Experience with the repair and maintenance of CAT, Epiroc, Hitachi, Sandvik and Maclean Mining Equipment would be considered an asset.

• Previous mining experience would be considered an asset but transferable skills from other industries are encouraged to apply.

• Ability to work through troubleshooting charts and reading schematics would be considered an asset.

• Knowledge of and interest in computerized diagnostic tools and equipment would be considered an asset.

• Ability to troubleshoot Heavy Duty hydraulic systems, electrical systems and powertrains would be considered an asset.

Skills:
• Demonstrated willingness to learn and develop new skills.

• Passion to learn and grow while taking on new challenges.

• Reliable and dependable mechanic with a strong team player attitude.

Why Newfoundland and LabradorNewfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role. At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada. title: General Surgeon
description:
Horizon Health Network is seeking a General Surgeon to join our collegial and collaborative team in beautiful Upper River Valley, New Brunswick.

## Why you should work here

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

Situated west-centrally in New Brunswick, the Upper River Valley area, including the Town of Woodstock and the Town of Hartland, Horizon's Upper River Valley Hospital serves a catchment population of 45,000. Many sites in this region are situated along the majestic St. John River valley and all sites are within driving distance of the province's historic capital, Fredericton.

The hospital provides services to the Town of Woodstock, Town of Hartland several villages and other surrounding communities. The community's economy is mainly based on natural resources and farming industries. The area has a diverse population distribution that is 60% rural and 40% urban.

The Upper River Valley Hospital is the newest hospital in New Brunswick. It has been designated as the first full-service hospital in Canada to be recognized as a leader in energy and environmental design.

## Incentives & Remuneration

Remuneration is via an alternative funding plan (AFP) arrangement.

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Rural recruitment incentive of $100,000.00 with a 4-year return of service.

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

## What you will do

• Perform both elective and emergency general surgical operations.

• Provide outpatient services for the assessment and management of patients including clinics and minor OR cases.

• Provide inpatient care including daily rounds on patients.

• Provide consultations to hospital-based patients as requested by medical or hospital staff.

• Maintain a private office for elective consultations and visits.

• Teaching responsibilities for residents, medical students, and others as appropriate.

• Collaborate with the interdisciplinary team to address staff and patient education needs.

• Participate in the use of departmental and corporate evidence-based rules of practice to ensure that expected standards of care are achieved.

• Participate in the on-call rota of the Division of General Surgery.

• Within the confines of this scope of practice and position description, provide other duties that may arise by circumstance and may be assigned by the Chief of the Department of Surgery, the Chief of Staff, Medical Director and/or Vice President of Medical Affairs.

## Who you are

• Must be eligible for license to practice medicine in the Province of New Brunswick.

• Must be eligible for membership with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick.

• Must be eligible for malpractice insurance from the Canadian Medical Protective Association (CMPA), or equivalent, appropriate to the category of practice.

• Excellent communication, interpersonal and team-building skills.

• Good attendance and work record.

## Interested? Apply Today!

If you have questions, please email physiciancareers@horizonnb.ca with the subject "Application for General Surgery, Upper River Valley".

description:
html
Competition number: PF 26-004

Salary: $68,309.00 - $68,309.00/Year

Job Type: Temporary Full Time

Closing Date: April 12, 2026

## Position Overview:

Under the direction of the Director of Human Resources, this position will proactively coordinate disability management files, assessing any barriers to ensure timely, effective, and successful return-to-work plans. The Disability and Wellness Coordinator will collaborate with internal and external partners to ensure compliance with applicable legislation while promoting a culture of health and wellness in coordinating Workplace Wellness programs.

The incumbent requires a high level of energy, organizational skills, initiative, and independent judgment in the performance of varied wellness and disability management duties that are highly confidential in nature.

As a member of the Saint John Police administration team, this member must understand the vision, mission, and leadership principles of the Saint John Police and promote our organizational values of leadership, accountability, professionalism, inclusiveness, integrity, and valour.

Successful completion of the security clearance and integrity interview are requirements of the Saint John Police.

## Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Disability Management:

• Administer and coordinate non-occupational and occupational claims, ensuring timely and accurate processing as part of a return-to-work or duty-to-accommodate program.

• Serve as a liaison between employees, managers, healthcare providers, and insurance partners to support return-to-work plans.

• Ensure compliance with applicable legislation, policies, standard operating procedures, and reporting requirements.

• Assist employees when they are off work or at risk of being off work for health reasons; provide direction in completion of required documentation.

• Ensure employees' disability management files are maintained, stored securely, and remain confidential.

• Educate employees and management on disability inclusion, reasonable accommodations, and best practices.

• Respond to numerous daily inquiries either by walk-in, telephone, and/or email.

• Conduct timely assessments, schedule, and attend return-to-work meetings with employees, managers, and external stakeholders to facilitate discussions, ensuring accommodations are effective.

• Prepare and maintain monthly and quarterly reports, tracking types of leaves and return-to-work programs.

• Attend and participate in discussions on various return-to-work committees.

Wellness:

• Foster a culture of health and well-being across the organization by coordinating wellness days, incentive challenges, and educational campaigns.

• Be an active member of committees (e.g., wellness and fit for duty).

• Deliver wellness educational sessions for new and current employees.

• Collaborate with the City of Saint John Human Resources department related to wellness initiatives.

• Coordinate and be present for all required ergonomic assessments in the workplace.

• Perform other related duties as required.

## This is the life-changing opportunity you've been looking for.

Imagine a playground in Atlantic Canada

surrounded by fresh waterways on one side and the ocean on the other.

Horizon Health Network is currently seeking Geriatricians to join the Division of Geriatric Medicine
in beautiful Fredericton, New Brunswick.

## Why you should work here

New Brunswick offers a safe and welcoming community with a relaxed lifestyle and a true work-life balance, enriched by its diverse Indigenous, Anglophone, and Francophone heritage.

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

Horizon's Dr. Everett Chalmers Regional Hospital (DECRH) is located in Fredericton, the capital city of New Brunswick. The DECRH is partnered with Dalhousie University and is a teaching site for Family Medicine residents, as well as medical students in an innovative longitudinal clerkship program. The Geriatric Medicine outpatient clinic is based at the nearby Woodbridge Centre facility. You'd be joining a dynamic team of three internist Geriatricians in a collegial environment which supports your flexibility to pursue clinical, educational, quality improvement and administrative interests.

## Incentives & Remuneration:

This is a salaried position with a base range of $273,962 - $302,796. Participation in the General Internal Medicine on-call service is optional and is remunerated additionally in a fee-for-service model.

Salaried physicians enjoy vacation and medical education leave, paid overhead expenses including administrative support, extended health benefits, and unparalleled work-life balance.

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Urban recruitment incentive of $50,000.00 with a 2-year return of service.

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

## Who you are

• Geriatric Medicine specialist (Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or equivalent).

• Must hold a valid license to practice medicine in the Province of New Brunswick.

• A member in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick and the Atlantic Registry.

• Must have current malpractice insurance from the Canadian Medical Protective Association (CMPA) appropriate to the category of practice.

• Bilingualism (French/English) would be considered an asset.

## What you will do

As a Geriatrician, you will establish a full-time practice offering both inpatient and outpatient services:

• Provide assessment and management of both new and follow-up outpatients through the Geriatric Medicine Clinic at the Woodbridge Centre in Fredericton.

• Provide inpatient consultations upon request in Fredericton and Oromocto hospitals.

• Provide consultations to local nursing home residents at the request of the primary care provider.

• Provide consultations at home, if desired.

• Collaborate in the care of older adults admitted to the inpatient rehabilitation unit at the DECRH, including attending weekly interdisciplinary team meetings.

• Engage in clinical teaching for resident physicians and medical students. Didactic and small-group teaching opportunities are also available.

• There are numerous opportunities to participate in administrative roles for those who wish.

## Interested? Apply Today!

To learn more, visit https://myhorizoncareer.ca/

If you have questions, please email physiciancareers@horizonnb.ca.

## For more information about our community, please see below:

Fredericton Region - Horizon Health Network

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. title: Senior Marine Structural Engineer
employer: GEMTEC Consulting Engineers and Scientists Limited
description:
Are you an experienced Marine Structural Engineer looking to progress your career? We're looking for a Senior Marine Structural Engineer to join our growing team. We are open to filling this position in any of our Atlantic Canada offices including Fredericton, Moncton, Saint John, Grand Falls, Bathurst, Halifax or St. John's.

At GEMTEC, we offer something different. We're an employee-owned, 400-person multidisciplinary consulting firm—not too big, not too small. We're large enough to compete head-to-head with publicly traded engineering giants, but still small enough to maintain the culture and flexibility of a close-knit team.

Our size and hands-on management style let us move quickly, embrace new opportunities, and empower our people to shape their own careers—without getting lost in corporate bureaucracy.

A typical day on the job might look like:

• Providing engineering designs for civil infrastructure projects (ports, harbours and bridges)

• Working with diverse teams of discipline managers, engineers, designers and technicians

• Managing projects and being responsible for completion on schedule and financial performance

• Acting as a technical resource and as a mentor to junior/intermediate staff

• Writing, compiling and reviewing technical reports

• Preparing fee proposals

• Being a member of site visit teams, gathering information as required to complement design activities

• Maintaining quality throughout a project and implement improvements when determined

• Preparing regular project summary reports

• Encouraging growth within the group and increasing the general knowledge base throughout the company

• Developing and sustaining long-lasting business relationships with clients

• Identifying and mitigating potential hazards in the field or onsite, promoting a safe working environment.

• Employee owned company with future potential to be a shareholder

• Year end profit sharing bonus

• Health and dental benefits

• Matching RRSP employer contributions up to 5%

• Office year-end closure (paid time off between Christmas and New Years)

• Work/life balance including a 37.5 hour work week and flexible working arrangements including hybrid options.

• Growth and development opportunities as we work on a large variety of projects so you can build your skills and experience.

Your qualifications and what you bring:

• Bachelor's degree in civil engineering from an accredited University

• Minimum of 12 years of experience in civil engineering including specific expertise in marine structures.

• Adaptability to represent GEMTEC professionally with clients, developers, or contractors

• Strong written and verbal communication skills needed to convey technical ideas clearly

• Eligibility to register or are currently registered as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) with one or more of the Atlantic provinces

• Proven ability to manage projects

• Ability to obtain security clearance

• Valid driver's license

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a temporary call-in position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics and Ambulance Operators/Attendants. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
* Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

## Salary:

* Advanced Care Paramedic - CGHSA-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $39.14 to $46.27 per hour
* Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour
* Ambulance Operator/Attendant – CG-25 of the NAPE HS salary scale $23.78 to $26.19 per hour
* A financial recruitment incentive may apply to this position for new hires in exchange for a return in service. If so, the recruiter will discuss with you.

The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for main-taining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and sup-porting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine. The base for this service is located at Green Bay Health Centre, Springdale.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lift-ing/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
• Graduation from High School or equivalent;
• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

Salary:
• Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour
• Ambulance Operator/Attendant – CG-25 of the NAPE HS salary scale $23.78 to $26.19 per hour

A financial recruitment incentive may apply to this position for new hires in exchange for a return in service. If so the recruiter will discuss with you.

title: Commercial Assessor
description:
## Commercial Assessor
Public / Two Permanent / Full Time

The Municipal Assessment Agency is required to provide municipalities with real property values (or assessments) in accordance with the terms and conditions of the province's Assessment Act, 2006. We are responsible for providing a fair and effective property assessment service to 244 municipalities within Newfoundland & Labrador.

LOCATION: Any Regional Office (St. John's, Gander, or Corner Brook)

The Municipal Assessment Agency is committed to providing its employees with training and overall professional growth. We provide great rewards including, but not limited to, comprehensive health benefits, flexible working arrangements, leave benefits, a continuous learning environment, employee & family assistance program, and challenging work.

## THE ROLE:

The Valuation Services Division of the Municipal Assessment Agency is offering a great opportunity for a Commercial Assessor. The successful candidate will ensure accurate valuation of property and outstanding customer service to our clients throughout Newfoundland & Labrador.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Analyse market data and assign value to all properties in a portfolio of real property including but not limited to commercial, industrial, institutional, and resource-based properties.

• Collaborate with field employees to set priorities and ensure timelines are met.

• Ensure the quality of the valuation and equity of assessment through application of accepted methods and performance of prescribed quality control functions (i.e. ratio studies, equalization process, etc.).

• Review property data and inspect properties in support of the appeal process.

• Represent the agency at tribunal hearings and appear as a witness in Supreme Court to provide evidence for verification of data and valuation.

• Conduct market research on real property to keep abreast of market trends within regions.

• Investigate property transactions to determine and verify consideration, influences on price, and qualification as an open market transaction.

• Provide opinions and estimates of condition, age, and functionality of improvements using a review of maps, deeds, and surveys.

• Determine and record ownership, boundary, dimensional, topographical, and location details.

• Verify legal descriptions of properties by comparing them to current assessment records.

• Confirm building codes and zoning by-laws to determine any effects on the appraised property.

• Interview individuals familiar with the property as required.

• Provide valuation and consulting services outside the assessment function to municipalities in the form of a letter of opinion or brief narrative work.

## SCREENING CRITERIA:

• Completion of a diploma in appraisal, assessment, or a related field (equivalencies will be considered)

• Certification or designation in good standing in one of the following:
• Accredited Appraiser or Certified Residential Appraiser of the Appraisal Institute of Canada, (A.A.C.I. or C.R.A)

• Certified Assessment Evaluator of the International Association of Assessing Officers (C.A.E.)

• Residential Evaluation Specialist (R.E.S)

• Associate or Accredited (M.I.M.A. or A.I.M.A) designation through the Institute of Municipal Assessors

• Eligible for membership in the International Association of Assessing Officers, Institute of Municipal Assessors, or the Appraisal Institute of Canada

• Experience in real estate valuation, including commercial, industrial, institutional, or resource-based properties

• Experience using computer software (i.e. Microsoft Excel & Word, databases, etc.)

• Experience with related legislation (i.e. Assessment Act, 2006) (asset)

• Experience with iasWorld or similar software (asset)

• Experience in a Computer-Assisted Mass Appraisal (CAMA) environment (asset)

## ASSESSMENT CRITERIA:

• Knowledge of real commercial property assessment practices

• Knowledge of related legislation (asset)

• Proficiency with related computer programs and software

• Ability to effectively exchange information

• Ability to independently manage time and tasks

• Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships

• Problem-solving skills

• Leadership skills

• Analytical skills with attention to detail

• Client service orientation

## CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT:

## CONDITIONS OF OFFER

• Valid class 5 NL Driver's Licence

SALARY: CG-37 ($65,756.60 - $73,473.40) as per the NAPE Collective Agreement.
Effective September 1, 2026 until August 31, 2027, a market adjustment of $13,700 as per the Market Adjustment Policy will be in effect.

Applications, quoting reference MAA.CA.07.2026, must be submitted to careers@maa.ca

Medavie Health Services is a national leader in primary health care solutions and the largest contracted provider of emergency management services in Canada. Together with Medavie Blue Cross, we are part of Medavie, a health solutions partner committed to improving the wellbeing of Canadians.

With a growing network of 5,400 health care professionals in six provinces, Medavie Health Services has a long history of operating ground and air ambulance services, medical communications, Mobile Integrated Health/Community Paramedicine programs, 911 Public Safety, 811 Telehealth, home health care, as well as clinical training.

We are proud to invest in communities to help address some of Canada's most pressing physical and mental health care challenges.

As an employee of Medavie Health Services, we are accountable to our patients and coworkers by participating in and supporting all safety related initiatives, as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture that focuses on patient safety and a safe and respectful workplace.

As a HPEI employee, and as part of the Mobile Mental Health Team, operated by Medavie, this position responds to individuals in crisis requiring de-escalation, mental health and risk assessments, and coordination of care and support in the community. The Registered Nurse works collaboratively with other interdisciplinary service providers such as, but not limited to, Community Mental Health and Addictions, Primary Care, Psychiatry, EMS, justice, victim services, child and family services, and police services.

## Duties:

• Complete initial and on-going client assessments including substance use history, suicide risk assessment and Best Possible Medication History (BPMH).

• Assess client for most appropriate service

• Provide education and support to clients in individual and group format.

• Develop case management planning in collaboration with the client.

• Communicate with interdisciplinary services as required.

• Provide Recovery Based, Client/Family Focused, Trauma Informed Care.

• Educate clients on harm reduction strategies.

• Perform other duties as required.

## Minimum Qualifications:

• Baccalaureate Degree in Nursing or Psychiatric Nursing or Diploma in Nursing with extensive experience in clinical area may be considered

• Some nursing experience (1-3 yrs) with a combination of hospital and/or community setting

• Obtain and maintain education credentials and certifications specific to practice area

• Active or eligible for registration with the College of Registered Nurses and Midwives of Prince Edward Island

• Possess a solid knowledge of chemical dependency and substance use.

• Strong interpersonal, problem solving, and individual and group communication skills.

• Have good previous work and attendance record.

• Knowledge of the Provincial Mental Health Act

• Additional relevant education and experience will be considered an asset.

• Knowledge and experience using the Telus EMR would be considered an asset.

description:
Requisition ID: 2081

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. Position Overview:
Planners provide process planning, material requirements, labour estimates and tooling requirements for aircraft programs and component manufacture.

What You Will Do:
• Plan detail manufacture, process and assembly sequences of production work.

• Play an active role in the staging of work. Involved in detail review and assessment, interdepartmental coordination, issue resolution and deployment of work to the floor.

• Research and review technical data for accuracy and completeness.

• Ensure correct and approved maintenance program data is called out within the Process Planning documentation and that this data is maintained.

• Ensure correct product conformance procedures, including the handling of non-conforming material are followed and adequately recorded.

• Ensure appropriate level of AMO authority is advised of any deficiency noted in any practice or procedure, which may compromise the airworthiness of an aeronautical product.

• Determine and initiate provisioning requirements for all projects/programs.

• Assist Production, Purchasing and Sub-Contractors with technical data interpretation and liaise with the Engineering Department to resolve problems.

• Initiate and action requests for Engineering Services (RES).

• Prepare labour and material cost estimates for proposals and Request For Employees.

• Provide guidance and assistance to other personnel as required.

• Additional duties as assigned by supervisor.

MUNN Insurance has been protecting Atlantic Canadians for more than 100 years and is one of the region's leading independent insurance brokerages. With offices across Newfoundland and Labrador and Nova Scotia, MUNN is committed to delivering exceptional insurance solutions and personalized service to individuals, families, and businesses.

This role combines consultative selling, insurance expertise, and relationship management to help businesses make informed insurance decisions. As the primary advisor throughout the client lifecycle, you will manage opportunities from initial consultation through binding and renewal, while developing long-term client relationships that contribute to portfolio growth and retention.

Posted Date: 2026-07-15

Closing Date: Open until filled.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

Competition Number: VAC0012039

Posted Date: 2025-05-29

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Job Summary
The Clinical Psychologist III provides advanced clinical leadership, as well as administration and supervision of psychology services, in the interprofessional, Collaborative Care Neuropsychiatry Program within the Mental Health and Addictions Program at Newfoundland & Labrador Health Services. This program is focused on provision of community-based consultation, assessment, and intervention to folks with developmental disability and acquired brain injury who experience a co-occurring mental health concern, or psychiatric illness. The incumbent will provide and supervise Clinical Psychology services to clients and families referred to the program, with a focus on meeting individuals’ needs in a holistic, flexible, client-centered approach.

The Clinical Psychologist III will be responsible for completing psycho-diagnostic assessments with responsibilities including conducting advanced, independent diagnostic interviews, formulating and communicating diagnoses using DSM-V-TR, selecting and administrating comprehensive psychometric tests, supervising psychometrist(s) in test administration. Additionally, the Clinical Psychologist III will be involved in consultation with Behaviour Management Specialists and other interdisciplinary team members in the integration of assessment results within treatment/support plans.

This position will be expected to apply psychological principles and knowledge according to best practice for the provision of intervention services for individuals with dual diagnosis. The incumbent will also be responsible for implementing and evaluating the psychological interventions provided to clients and their families, providing individual and family treatment for patients with dual diagnosis, provide comprehensive training in evidence-based practice for individuals living with dual diagnosis and neurological conditions/major neurocognitive injuries and concurrent mental health disorder, or psychiatric illness.

The Clinical Psychologist III is considered an integral part of the interdisciplinary team and regular attendance of clinical rounds will be expected. The Clinical Psychologist III will act as a resource for other health care professionals and will advise on and participate in the development, implementation and evaluation of policies and procedures (e.g., quality improvement, workload management). The Psychologist will engage in program evaluation, and may be involved in conducting research, publishing research findings, as well as applying for research and operating grants.

The Clinical Psychologist III will be required to uphold the standards of professional practice set forth by their licensing board. They will provide supervision for provisionally registered psychologists, psychology residents, and clinical psychology doctoral students. They will also provide consultation to fully registered psychologists, and other allied health professionals across the health authority. They may also be involved in the teaching and support of psychiatry residents, and medical students.

This position reports to the Program Manager for Mental Health and Addictions Tertiary Services and maintains accountability to the Psychology Professional Practice Consultant for professional integrity and practice issues.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Occasionally, there is lifting or physical strength required, less than 10 lbs for files, boxes, or equipment.
Regularly sits; occasionally works in awkward/cramped positions, and stands to facilitate or teach groups.
Uses fine finger/precision work when on the computer and visual concentration is required when in sessions with patients (i.e. reviewing patient charts/notes, tests and for documenting work, and when reading or researching information).
Visual concentration is required to interpret patient observations and integrate into patient evaluation.
Auditory concentration is constantly required in sessions with patients to listen attentively, to be alert and to obtain and interpret information correctly.
A higher than normal level of attentiveness is required when assessing high risk patients

Job Qualifications
Graduation with an approved/recognized Doctorate Degree in Clinical Psychology is required.
Registration or provisional registration with Newfoundland and Labrador Psychology Board is required.
Graduate course work and supervised experience in psychological assessment including cognitive and diagnostic assessment with adults is required.
Graduate course work and supervised experience in evidence based therapy with individuals and groups with a specific focus on mental health issues is required.
Previous experience supervising Doctoral level residents is preferred.
Exhibited strong communication, program development and evaluation skills.
Possessed strong leadership and supervisory skills that are focused on engaging others and developing coalitions.
Demonstrated ability to provide strong and comprehensive clinical support, training and mentorship to Clinical Psychologists II's and other supervisees.
Possessed strong analytical, critical reasoning, collaboration, problem solving, decision-making and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to effectively translate and communicate knowledge in the specialized area of psychology practice to others.
Demonstrated ability to conduct research, deliver lectures/clinical education sessions and provide clinical direction and consultation within an interprofessional environment.
Ability to work autonomously, prioritizing caseloads and client needs.
Demonstrated ability and willingness to participle in the clinical training activities of the psychology discipline.
Demonstrated strong awareness of ethical principles and standards of professional conduct.
Use of a personal vehicle is a condition of employment.
A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

In the absence of previous experience, the successful candidate will be required to complete a specialized training course in Winter/Spring 2025. The course could be up to approximately one week in length. Participation may include travel for in-person training and/or virtual (online) training. Financial assistance will be provided to cover the cost of the training program. A return-in-service agreement will be required, and the length will depend on the total amount of funding provided. The service obligation will begin once the candidate has successfully completed the education program.

Posted Date: 2026-06-12

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients.

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

• Bachelor's degree in one of Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline.

• Registered as an Engineer-in-Training, or eligible for registration with APEGNB or

• 2–4 years of experience in industrial process specifically in Pulp and Paper processes.

• Foundational understanding of process design concepts, including process flow diagrams (PFDs), P&IDs, mass and energy balances, process calculations, and equipment selection.

• Interest in supporting feasibility studies, plant assessments, process optimization initiatives, and capital improvement projects.

The PHC Family Care Team (FCT) mandate is to provide patients without a primary care provider of the Central region with access to primary health care services. Services will be provided using an inter-professional collaborative approach where patients will see the right provider at the right time and right place. The team includes physicians, NPs, RNs including diabetic nurse educator, clerical supports, LPNs, pharmacists, social workers, dietitian, physiotherapist and occupational therapist. All health care providers, including physicians, will be expected to practice to their full scope of practice to meet patient needs and requirements. The FCT aims to provide continuity of care to improve health outcomes and patients quality of life.

We are seeking physicians to manage a roster of patients. There are other services in the area of the FCT which the physician is encouraged to consider participating in including: Hospitalist Services, Emergency Department Services, Long-Term Care, Palliative Care, and other opportunities. ## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

## ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The Surgical Services Perioperative Program of NL Health Services – Eastern Urban Zone invites applications for a full-time Cardiac Anesthesiologist at Health Sciences Centre in St. John's, NL, with a start date of June 20, 2026.

The successful candidate will join a group of six (6) Cardiac Anesthesiologists at HSC, working with the entire group of 22 Anesthesiologists including cardiac. The Anesthesiologist will function as a key member of the perioperative team, responsible for the provision of anesthetic services to surgical patients. Practice will be at least 50% in the provision of cardiovascular anesthesia, with direct involvement in the care of patients pre- and post-operatively, including responsibility for pre-admission anesthesia clinics and post-operative pain management.

Health Sciences Centre runs 14–16 operating rooms per day across the following surgical specialties: General, Cardiac, Neuro-Surgery, Plastic, Orthopedic, Gynecology/Gyne-ONC, Cath Lab, Neuro-Interventional Radiology, Ophthalmology, and Urology. Anesthesiologists also provide support to ECT, Endovascular Treatment of Stroke, and Acute Pain Services.

On-call coverage averages two (2) times per month, with additional second-call coverage for APS, EVT, and second team averaging one to two times per month. Members of the Cardiac Anesthesia group provide specific coverage for cardiovascular anesthesia on call and transesophageal echocardiography for the perioperative program on call.

Health Sciences Centre is a teaching hospital affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine at Memorial University of Newfoundland and Labrador, providing opportunities to engage in educational experiences with anesthesia residents and undergraduate medical students.

St. John's is a vibrant, historic city on the eastern tip of North America, offering a warm and welcoming community, a thriving arts and culture scene, and easy access to the stunning natural landscapes of the Avalon Peninsula — including whale watching, hiking, and some of the most dramatic coastlines in Canada.

CarteNav Solutions, a PAL company, is an international leader in situational awareness solutions for the maritime, land, and air environments. As a Technical Project Manager, you'll be the bridge between our software engineering teams and our customers, translating technical progress into business confidence and business requirements into technical plans. You'll own the planning, coordination, and execution of complex software delivery projects. You'll also influence delivery best practices and help shape the future of how we scale and operate.

## What You'll Do

• Own end-to-end delivery of complex, technical projects from kickoff through deployment and acceptance

• Develop project plans, risks, budgets, and deliverables, while managing the formal schedules, budgets, and reporting requirements

• Translate customer and contractual requirements into clear technical specifications and actionable plans that engineering teams can execute against

• Ensure deliverables meet contractual, security, and compliance requirements, including export control, documentation, and acceptance testing obligations

• Represent the project delivery function in leadership planning and customer engagements

• Serve as the primary point of contact as a trusted advisor to customers and senior stakeholders

• Coordinate efforts across engineering, QA, product, and support teams to keep priorities aligned and dependencies visible

• Drive continuous improvement of delivery practices, tooling, and templates across the project management function

• Support proposal development and project estimation for new opportunities

## What We're Looking For

• 7+ years of experience in project management, with meaningful time spent managing software delivery

• Experience managing projects for government, defense, or other highly regulated customers

• Technical fluency — comfortable in conversations about architecture, integrations, and the software development lifecycle, even without a hands-on engineering background

• Proven ability to manage large-scale software initiatives, within a multi-stakeholder technical environment

• Proficiency with project management delivery tools like Jira, Microsoft Planner, Azure DevOps, or similar

• Clear, precise written and verbal communication, including formal status reporting and documentation

• Eligible to obtain and maintain a government security clearance, or ability to meet applicable export control and citizenship requirements

• PMP, Agile, or similar certifications are preferred

## Nice to Have

• Experience with defense, aerospace, or public sector procurement processes

• Familiarity with regulatory or safety-critical software standards

• Experience mentoring or leading other project managers

## Why Join Us?

• Work on software that supports real, high-stakes missions for government and defense customers

• Sit at the intersection of technical delivery and customer strategy, with real influence over how projects get built

• Join a global team that values clarity, ownership, and getting the details right

• Advance your career in a forward-thinking environment

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is passionate about creating great software, cares about client engagements, and takes pride in successful project delivery. If you're an experienced project leader ready to help deliver mission-critical software and shape how we work—let's talk.

• Pension Plan with employer matching

title: Junior Industrial Process Engineer / EIT
description:
We are seeking an Engineer-in-Training or Junior Industrial Process Engineer to join our growing Industrial team in either Halifax, NS or Fredericton, NB. This role is ideal for an early-career engineer who is interested in developing practical process engineering experience within industrial facilities, including pulp and paper, forestry, tissue manufacturing, and related process sectors.

As an Engineer-in-Training or Junior Industrial Process Engineer, you will work under the guidance of experienced engineers and project managers to support process engineering assignments through each stage of project delivery, from data collection and preliminary design through detailed engineering, construction support, and commissioning.

Your key responsibilities:

• Support process engineering assignments for pulp and paper, forestry, tissue manufacturing, and other industrial process facilities.

• Assist with the preparation of process engineering deliverables including process flow diagrams (PFDs), P&IDs, mass and energy balances, process calculations, and technical reports.

• Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams including mechanical, electrical, structural, civil, and automation specialists to support coordinated project delivery.

• Support feasibility studies, process optimization initiatives, facility expansions, modernization projects, and operational improvement assignments.

• Participate in process assessments, field reviews, data collection, equipment evaluations, and plant performance reviews.

• Assist with technical documentation, proposal inputs, cost estimates, and project coordination activities as required.

• Provide support during construction, commissioning, and startup activities under the direction of senior technical staff.

• Build your technical skills through hands-on project experience, mentoring, and exposure to a broad range of industrial process engineering work.

Your capabilities and credentials:

• Bachelor's degree in one of Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline.

• Registered as an Engineer-in-Training, or eligible for registration with APEGNB or

• 2–4 years of experience in industrial process specifically in Pulp and Paper processes.

• Foundational understanding of process design concepts, including process flow diagrams (PFDs), P&IDs, mass and energy balances, process calculations, and equipment selection.

• Interest in supporting feasibility studies, plant assessments, process optimization initiatives, and capital improvement projects.

• Strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team environment.

• Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn from experienced engineers while developing technical knowledge and consulting skills.

What we can offer you:

• A competitive compensation package effective on your first day of employment:
• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• CAAT Defined Benefit Pension Plan with employer contributions

• Generous vacation allowance commensurate with experience

• Maternity or Parental leave top-up

• Health spending account

• Wellness incentive

• Membership dues reimbursement

• Education and lifelong learning subsidization

• Community volunteering incentive

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Public transit subsidy

In addition to the above benefits, we offer:

• Diverse team with a wide range of experience and expertise.

• Exposure to a variety of projects.

• Support to develop skills and pursue projects related to your own interests.

• Collaboration between multiple disciplines and levels of expertise.

• Mentoring opportunities to foster your personal and professional development.

• Accessible and central offices in Atlantic Canada and Ottawa.

• Access to training opportunities in areas ranging from technical development to leadership skills.

• Competitive salary: $65,000 - $80,000 annually, depending on experience.

To meet pay transparency requirements, compensation ranges are included for roles in locations where required by law. The salary range listed for this position represents the expected hiring range; actual starting compensation will vary based on factors such as professional experience, technical expertise, credentials, and alignment with the role's requirements, as well as internal compensation structures and market data. Beyond base salary, CBCL provides a comprehensive total rewards package that includes health and dental benefits and a pension program from your first day of employment, along with eligibility for an annual discretionary bonus.

About Us

At CBCL our purpose is to create a positive and lasting impact on people and planet. As an employee-owned firm, at CBCL, our people are everything. We are committed to promoting inclusivity and diversity for a workplace where everyone can thrive, and we build long-term relationships with our clients while providing them with innovative solutions.

We have earned recognition as one of Canada's Top 100 Employers and one of Canada's Best Managed Companies. Our multitalented group of professionals offer consulting in the Infrastructure, Water and Wastewater, Buildings, Industrial, and Earth and Environment sectors. We value our people, our communities, and our history and look forward to continuing our steady growth.

Along with our commitment to reducing our carbon footprint corporately, CBCL develops and implements sustainable engineering solutions that respect the current social and environmental impacts, as well as future implications of our designs.

CBCL operates from its offices in Halifax and Sydney, NS; Charlottetown, PE; Saint John, Fredericton and Moncton, NB; St. John's, NL, and Ottawa, ON.

CBCL Limited strives to provide a diverse workplace that is inclusive, accessible and celebrates individuals and what makes us unique. We are proud to be an employer partner with the Canadian Centre for Diversity and Inclusion and Pride at Work.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

Job Summary:
The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

Qualifications:
• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;
• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

Office Operations

Preferred Qualifications

• Familiarity with ERP systems and document management platforms.

• Additional language skills would be an asset.

• Opportunities for professional development and career growth.
