Job Summary
The Occupational Therapist II (OT II) will work in an inter-professional collaborative team environment, to provide person and family-centered care that is evidence-based, comprehensive and compassionate, with a focus on improving access, optimal health outcomes and quality of life. The Occupational Therapist II is a leadership role responsible for coordination of clinical client care as well as assisting clients and their families to navigate family care teams and community services. The Occupational Therapist II will practice to their full scope in order to meet client needs; participate in direct care of clients and provide clinical leadership, including:

• Utilizing a collaborative, shared-care approach, works in partnership with clients, families, caregivers, team members and community partners, to support individuals and communities to achieve optimal health, wellness, functional independence and physical performance.

• Providing direct client care including comprehensive assessment, diagnostic and therapeutic services; planning, implementation and evaluation of treatment plans, incorporating the Determinants of Health.

• Health promotion and education for individuals, families, caregivers, collaborative teams, community groups, external agencies with a focus on promoting health and recovery, mental health support, falls prevention, home safety assessments, equipment assessment/prescription, self-management, community mobility and ‘Ageing in Place’ initiatives

• Facilitation of group sessions to promote wellness, support chronic disease prevention and management and improve quality of life.

• Facilitation of integrated virtual care options to increase access for individual and group sessions.

• Acting as a liaison with community wellness groups and initiatives to assist in program planning, development, implementation and support.

• Providing professional and clinical leadership, education, mentorship and support to the inter-professional collaborative team, occupational therapy support staff, and students/learners.

• Recognizing cultural diversity and practicing culturally safe care.

• Practicing age-friendly care in a collaborative care team setting.

• Work closely with the manager and other team members to:

• Assist in program development,

• Achieve client, community and clinician engagement

• Improve care coordination among team members across the continuum of care, from hospital to community to home, ensuring coordinated, seamless transitions of care and timely access to improve health outcomes and optimize quality of life.

• Participate in evaluation and continuous quality improvement processes based upon current evidence-based practices.

• Use assessment to assist patients to navigate care pathways by communicating with the team and advocating for the client.

• Engage in continuous education relevant to the position and provide guidance and support to Rehabilitation Assistants, students and other health professionals in the team.

• The OT II position offers an excellent opportunity to apply advanced clinical, theoretical and decision-making skills through comprehensive clinical knowledge and an interdisciplinary collaborative team approach to primary health care.
Required Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved recognized school of occupational therapy with a Master’s Degree in Occupational therapy.

• Active membership with the Canadian Association of Occupational Therapy (CAOT).

• Current registration & licensed (or eligible for licensure) with the Newfoundland and Labrador Occupational Therapy Board (NLOTB).

• A minimum of three years’ experience within the last five working as a Clinical Occupational Therapist with an adult outpatient population is preferred.

• Current BLS certification or willingness to complete on hire

• Demonstrated progressive leadership, organizational, interpersonal and decision-making skills.

• Demonstrated effective oral and written communication skills.

• Demonstrated strong collaboration skills and the ability to create and maintain successful working relationships.

• Ability to self-direct and work independently and collaborate with team members

## Additional Qualifications/ Assets:

• Completion of a post entry education courses in suicide intervention (ASIST), non-violent crisis intervention (CPI) considered an asset

• Proficiency with TELUS Med Access EMR, Meditech , CRMS, and Microsoft Office tools

• Previous experience in adult education

• Knowledge in change leadership and quality improvement methodologies

• Experience in a collaborative team model

• Experience working in and understanding of the unique challenges and opportunities of rural health care services delivery

• Understands systemic racism and applies concepts of cultural safety in engaging with First Nations, Inuit and Metis communities

## Job Demands

• By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts or moves objects up to 30 lbs. and assists, supports, pushes or pulls clients and equipment up to and over 50 lbs.

• Regularly stands and walks, and drives to and from sites/homes within the region.

• Occasionally uses hand tools and equipment that requires rapid physical movement and reflexes and controlled movement.

About Us
At the Safety Branch of the Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (LSI), we are responsible for delivering effective and efficient regulatory management for the protection of the public and workers' safety through education, outreach, inspection and enforcement, equipment registration, permits, and licenses. Our staff of over 115 employees, located throughout Nova Scotia, do this by using the Pathways to Compliance to enhance compliance through setting, promoting, verifying and enforcing requirements under various pieces of legislation.
LSI works to provide fairness, safety, and prosperity for all Nova Scotians by helping them live, learn and work to their highest potential. We have a staff of more than 500 employees working from offices throughout Nova Scotia. Together we are responsible for safety, labour standards, apprenticeship, immigration and population growth, and many other facets of everyday life.
If you are searching for a rewarding career, we have an exciting opportunity for you to explore as a Technical Safety Officer.

About Our Opportunity
The Inspector works independently and is responsible for the enforcement of the Boiler and Pressure Equipment Regulations, as well as the Power Engineer's Regulations, in your assigned territory. This is done through on-site inspection, providing information, advice and technical direction and interpretation of applicable American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler and Pressure Vessel Codes and the Canadian Standards Association (CSA) Codes and Standards to owners, operators, employers and employees, contractors, suppliers, consultants, power engineers, etc.
As the Inspector you will conduct a wide variety of specialized, related technical inspections as well as investigations of accidents and fatalities and alleged violations under the legislation. The Inspector conducts qualification testing of pressure welders and brazers, invigilating exams under the Power Engineers Regulations and ensure compliance with these regulations by issuing orders, including immediate stop work orders as well as initiating prosecution action.
As the Officer, you will work under the general supervision of the Chief Inspector/ Manager, Boiler & Pressure Equipment Section of the Technical Safety Division.

Primary Accountabilities
• Conducts reviews of welding procedures, design drawings and specifications for boilers, pressure vessels and associated fittings to ensure compliance with applicable Codes and Standards.

• Prepare monthly activity and status reports as well as attending meetings and preparing associated correspondence.

• Provide input to the technical development of the relevant ASME and CSA codes and standards

• Conduct reviews of quality control systems of ASME Code shops and CSA B51 Code Shops involved in the manufacture of ASME and CSA B51 Code stamped boilers and pressure vessels, to satisfy the requirements set out by ASME and the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors.

Qualifications and Experience
This may be the right opportunity for you if you have completed high school as well as a related trade or technical training in the area of specialty plus 7 years of related experience after the course completion; an equivalent combination of training and experience may be considered.
Relevant trade or technical training includes any of the following:

• Certified Engineering Technologist or Technician with a background in the mechanical engineering field;

• Power Engineer, First or Second Class;

• Journeyman Boilermaker,

• Quality Control/Welding Engineering Technology with experience in pressure welding, pressure equipment manufacturing, construction, repair or maintenance.

You have knowledge and experience in the use of non-destructive testing equipment and methodologies and the requirements of applicable ASME Code Sections, interpretation of mechanical drawings, boiler and pressure vessel design, piping design, welding, refrigeration, metallurgy, feed water conditioning, instrumentation, fuels and fuels gases as well as combustion principles, thermodynamics, pumps, turbines, compressors and air conditioning.
You must be able to work in tight confined spaces and heights
You possess the following:

• Exceptional communication (written and verbal);

• Computer skills including management of electronic files;

• Proficiency in word processing and spreadsheets such as Microsoft Word and Excel and the ability to operate customized computer applications;

• Interpersonal, relationship building, and public speaking skills; and

• Strong problem solving and decision making skills.

Equivalency
Certifications Required
You passed an examination and hold or are willing to obtain within 1 year of appointment, a Commission from the National Board of Boiler Pressure Inspectors and shall have been engaged in ASME boiler and pressure vessel code related work such as inspection or design under the provisions of the ASME code, or administration of shop inspections services under the ASME Code.
You must also have passed an examination, and hold or obtain within 2 years of appointment, the Authorized Inspector AI Commission, issued by the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors, which verifies the candidate's ability to ascertain the validity and quality of the fabrication, welding, non-destructive examination and other quality control requirements of the ASME Code. You may be required to complete Modules 1 though 13 of the Welding Inspection Technology Program offered through the Canadian Welding Bureau.
You must have, or be able to obtain and maintain, a security clearance certificate issued through the Safety and Security Office of Public Works and Government Services Canada (or its equivalent) and be able to be designated as a Safety Inspector under the Treasury Board of Canada Safety Standards.
You must have the following:

• A valid Class 5 Driver's License along with access to a reliable vehicle; and

• A current certificate in Emergency First Aid (or the ability to obtain one within 6 months of appointment).

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day

• May be required to work overtime on occasion

• Travel within your region and throughout the province

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

• A dynamic, client-focused office environment where service excellence and teamwork are our focus.

Pay Grade: TEBP 27

title: Quality Assurance Assistant
description:
Company: Shediac Lobster Shop Ltd.
Department: Quality Assurance / Quality Control
Reports To: Quality Assurance Manager
Industry: Seafood / Lobster Processing

The Quality Assurance Assistant position is responsible for overseeing the monitoring of product and production activities to ensure lobster products meet established food safety, quality, regulatory and customer requirements. Assist the Quality Assurance Manager with reviews, audits, verification and trend analysis, CAPA preparation, coordinating implementation and verification activities associated with implemented CAPA plans.

The QA employee performs verification on routine inspections, checks, monitoring and documentation throughout production and identifies product or process issues requiring attention, correction or escalation. QA Assistant also works closely with QC technicians and leads to ensure accuracy and compliance. The position works closely with all departments, reports quality or food safety concerns to the Quality Assurance Manager and assists in the resolution of those concerns.

## Key Responsibilities

## Production & Product Monitoring

• Conduct routine verifications of quality checks throughout production.

• Inspect raw materials, work-in-process and finished products for compliance with established specifications.

• Monitor product quality, condition, appearance and other required product characteristics.

• Verify that products meet applicable customer and company specifications.

• Review defects, deviations or unacceptable product for compliance corrective actions.

• Communicate quality concerns immediately to Production and/or the QA Manager.

• Assist in preventing non-conforming product from being released.

## Food Safety & Process Controls

• Review and verify food safety and process monitoring activities.

• Temperatures and other established process controls.

• Verify that required production and food safety checks are completed at the required frequency against records and recording activities.

• Observe employee compliance with GMPs, hygiene and food-handling requirements.

• Report food safety concerns or deviations immediately.

• Assist and oversee verification of sanitation processes and results.

## Product Specifications & Label Verification

• Verify product against applicable specifications.

• Ensure labels and packaging for accuracy.

• Identify incorrect or non-compliant labels or packaging before product is released.

• Correct and report specification or labeling discrepancies to the QA Manager.

## Non-Conforming Product

• Assist in controls of non-conforming products and equipment.

• Place or assist in placing affected product on HOLD according to company procedures.

• Clearly identify and segregate held or non-conforming products.

• Control deviations and notify the QA Manager and Production.

• Assist with product evaluation, reinspection and corrective actions as directed.

• Verify corrections when assigned before affected production continues or product is released.

## Records & Documentation

• Accurately complete assigned QC monitoring forms and records.

• Record inspection results, temperatures, product checks and deviations.

• Ensure records are completed at the time monitoring occurs.

• Document corrective actions taken when required.

• Maintain clear, accurate and legible records.

• Submit completed records to the QA Manager according to established procedures.

• Review, organize and when required verify documents and records.

## Traceability & Product Control

• Assist with traceability activities and product identification.

• Support product hold, release and recall activities when required.

• Assist the QA Manager with traceability exercises and product investigations.

## Communication

• Communicate quality and food safety concerns promptly and professionally.

• Work cooperatively with all departments in addressing, and implementing corrective and preventative actions.

• Escalate significant or repeated deviations to the QA Manager.

• Provide factual information regarding quality findings and production observations.

## Authority

Quality Assurance Assistant personnel have authority and responsibility to:

• Identify and report food safety or quality concerns.

• Request correction of identified product or process deviations.

• Place or recommend product be placed on HOLD when requirements are not met.

• Escalate unresolved or significant issues to the QA Manager.

• Stop or request the stopping of an affected process when there is an immediate food safety or serious product compliance concern.

Final disposition of significant non-conforming product and decisions involving regulatory compliance, program changes or customer requirements remain under the authority of the QA Manager and/or designated management.

## Skills & Qualifications

The QA Assistant employee should demonstrate:

• Strong attention to detail.

• Ability to follow written procedures and product specifications.

• Ability to accurately complete records and documentation.

• Good communication and organizational skills.

• Ability to identify, report and correct product defects or deviations.

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced seafood production environment.

• Understanding of GMPs, food safety and quality requirements.

• Ability to work independently while escalating issues appropriately.

• Competent in Microsoft Word and Excel.

• Understanding of food safety fundamentals, HACCP and GFSI standards.

Training will be provided on applicable company food safety programs, product specifications, monitoring procedures, documentation requirements and responsibilities.

English Language Requirement: Strong written and verbal English skills are required, with the ability to read and write clearly accurately.

## Overall Responsibility

The primary responsibility of QA Assistant is to oversee inspection and monitoring activities, identify and document product and process deviations so that problems are addressed before non-conforming product is released. The QA Manager manages the quality system; QA Assistant verifies the continual day to day implementation of the program along with the QC technicians to ensure continuing compliance.

title: Chemical Engineering/Engineering Science/Chemical Engineering Technology Co-op Student
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking two Chemical Engineering/Engineering Science/Chemical Engineering Technology co-op students to join our Technology & Innovation team in Mississauga.

The role is on-site and a 16 month fixed term position starting in January 2027. This posting is for an existing position vacancy.

As a Chemical Engineering/Engineering Science/Chemical Engineering Technology student, you will have the opportunity to further your development, gaining practical knowledge and experience working closely within the Hydrometallurgy group on a range of processes related to nickel, copper and cobalt processing. You will also gain a deeper understanding of our company and our sustainable approach to mining via exposure to other Vale operations in Canada and abroad.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Conduct literature search and document reviews on research papers and patents relative to undertaken projects

• Assist in the design, implementation and safe execution of chemical laboratory and miniplant testwork programs

## Governance Specialist & Executive Assistant to the Executive Director

## Nova Scotia Barristers' Society

Strong governance depends on someone who is highly organized and applies sound judgement. You anticipate what the Executive Director, Council members and senior leaders will need, bring order to complex meeting cycles, and follow through until decisions and commitments are documented and advanced. You build trust through thoughtful prioritization, clear communication and careful handling of confidential information. If you are an experienced governance and executive support professional who takes pride in making leaders and governing bodies more effective, the Nova Scotia Barristers' Society offers an opportunity to put that expertise to work in service of the public interest.

As Governance Specialist & Executive Assistant to the Executive Director, you will sit at the centre of the Society's governance and executive operations. You will connect the ED's office, Board and Council, committees and senior leadership team, prepare leaders to make informed decisions, and keep actions, records and governance processes moving forward with precision. This is a visible and trusted role for a professional who understands that effective governance is built through disciplined preparation, strong relationships and reliable follow-through.

The Nova Scotia Barristers' Society regulates Nova Scotia's legal profession in the public interest. With more than 3,700 members, the Society is responsible for accreditation, ethical standards, professional responsibility, complaints and practice standards. It also works to improve the administration of justice. Through this mandate, the Society helps maintain public trust in the legal profession and the rule of law.

The Society is focused on strengthening public trust through modern, effective regulation. Its priorities include modernizing governance, policies and processes; improving communication and engagement with members and the public; supporting a competent and inclusive profession; advancing access to justice; collaborating with justice system partners; and addressing systemic barriers. Respect, transparency and accountability guide how the Society works and serves Nova Scotians.

Recent work to review Board and Council policies has created a strong foundation for the next phase of governance maturity. You will help complete that work, keep governance documents current, strengthen meeting and decision processes, and establish practical systems that support compliance, transparency and continuity.

Reporting to the Executive Director and with accountability to the Board and Council, you will be a critical liaison among the governing body, its committees, the ED's office and the senior leadership team. You will build trusted relationships with the Chair and Council members, keep people informed and aligned, and provide the organization and context leaders need to carry out their responsibilities effectively.

Your governance responsibilities will include preparing agendas, minutes, briefing notes, presentations and committee chair reports; coordinating Board and Council meeting materials; maintaining policies, terms of reference, gap analysis, succession and board development documents; tracking actions to completion; and supporting nominations, orientation and onboarding for Council members, Officers and independent committee members. You will also provide technical and administrative support during leadership and strategy meetings and keep planning documents accurate and current.

Alongside the governance portfolio, you will provide high-touch executive support to the Executive Director. You will manage a busy calendar, coordinate meetings and travel, prepare correspondence and documents, process expenses and facilitate communication with employees, members, partners and other external stakeholders. Your ability to set priorities, anticipate needs and protect the ED's time will create space for the Executive Director to focus on the Society's mandate and strategic priorities.

The ideal candidate will have post-secondary education and at least 10 years of experience in board governance and executive support. Direct, hands-on experience supporting a board or governing council is essential. You bring excellent writing, editing, presentation and interpersonal skills, along with sound judgment, discretion and the emotional maturity to work confidently with senior leaders and Council members.

You are organized, proactive and comfortable managing several priorities and deadlines in an environment where plans can change. You value thoughtful process and know how to improve workflows gradually, balancing structure with adaptability. You work independently, collaborate naturally and approach sensitive situations with tact. Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office and web-based platforms is required, as is the ability to learn new technology quickly. Most importantly, you are motivated by the Society's public-interest mandate and the opportunity to strengthen the legal profession in Nova Scotia.

Please submit your resume online by clicking "Apply." For more information, contact Greg Dickie confidentially at gdickie@royerthompson.com. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please contact Susan Brimble at sbrimble@facetconnect.com.

Facet is committed to presenting a diverse and inclusive roster of candidates to our clients. We welcome and encourage applications from Indigenous persons, African Nova Scotians, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, women, members of the 2SLGBTIQIA+ community and newcomers to Canada. Candidates from equity-deserving groups are invited to self-identify in their cover letter or resume.

Facet is a recruitment firm with an unshakeable belief that change is a good thing. People are not only our purpose, they are also our passion. Facet recruits talented professionals who aspire to impact organizations and the communities they serve. We are inspired by these individuals and believe they are at the core of building purpose-driven, dynamic, and forward-thinking workplaces.

title: Controller
description:
Controller
Yarmouth, NS
HL-WIG-10124
The Wilson Group is a fourth-generation, family-owned business with over 100 years of earning the trust of communities across southwest Nova Scotia. What started as a general store has evolved into a dynamic, multi-location retail group operating under national banners including Home Hardware Building Centre, The Brick, and Bell, with a diversified portfolio spanning home improvement, building materials, furniture, appliances, electronics, floral, and property management.
Over the last five years, The Wilson Group has entered a significant new chapter of growth. Definition of work:
The Nurse Practitioner (NP) is responsible to provide comprehensive assessment and care to clients. This is an advance practice role providing professional, analytical and an autonomous, comprehensive range of health services to clients and patients including but not limited to health assessments and diagnosis of diseases, disorders, injuries and conditions; treating and managing acute and chronic illnesses and identifying health risks and needs within the Dr. Huge Twomey Health Centre. This position will be a blended role, supporting Acute Care Services, Primary Health Care, Long Term Care and Emergency Services which may include the Fast Track Stream of Care and Virtual Care Stream. Optimizing alternate care modalities such as virtual technology will be an option to increase accessibility to primary health care in the region.
The NP will provide advanced nursing care including health promotion and prevention and chronic disease management for common resident health issues in collaboration with physicians and other members of the multidisciplinary team. The NP will work in partnership with the multidisciplinary team to develop, lead, implement and evaluate best practice. The NP will work with the Clinical Nurse Educator/Facilitator in the development and evaluation of policies, standards of care and clinical services for residents at the Dr. Huge Twomey Health Centre. The NP will assume a leadership role in influencing clinical practice and patient outcomes and collaborate with the broader healthcare team and community partners regarding complex and challenging care situations. The NP will promote a person and family centered philosophy to care and establish a preventative, integrated, approach that is driven by individualized assessment of needs and individual choice. The successful candidate must demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Required qualifications:
• Graduation from a nurse practitioner program approved by Central Health.
• Current registration as a nurse practitioner with the Association of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.
• Current BLS certification.
• Airway Management training or willingness to complete next available training opportunity.
• Completion or willingness to complete next available course in ACLS, PALS, TNCC and NRP.
• Gentle Persuasive Approach or willingness to complete next available course.
• CNA certification in Gerontology or willingness to complete next available course.
• Demonstrated exceptional leadership qualities and problem-solving skills as well as oral and written communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to work well independently and in an interdisciplinary team environment.
• Consistent demonstration of NLHS corporate values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, Excellence.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory Certificate of Conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Demonstrated skill in using health care-based computer systems such as Meditech.

Closing Date: Open Until Filled

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a temporary position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from High School or equivalent;

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance is required;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

## Salary:

• Advanced Care Paramedic - CG-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $39.14 to $46.27 per hour

• Primary Care Paramedic – CG-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour

• A financial recruitment incentive may apply to this position for new hires in exchange for a return in service. If so, the recruiter will discuss with you.

title: Project Coordinator
description:
As a Project Coordinator, you will support Project Managers in the delivery of complex simulation and training solutions, including helicopter rear-crew training devices and other advanced training systems. Working with multidisciplinary teams, you will coordinate project activities, maintain accurate project financial information, and support planning, reporting, and project controls. This role is well suited to an organized, analytical, and detail-oriented individual who enjoys working on technically complex projects and helping teams deliver successfully.

Qualifications
• Minimum three (3) years of experience in project coordination, project administration, project controls, financial administration, PMO support, or a similar project-based role.

• Diploma or bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Project Management, Accounting, or a related discipline; equivalent experience will also be considered.

• Project Management Professional (PMP) and/or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification would be considered an asset.

• Demonstrated experience supporting multiple projects in a project-based, matrixed, or PMO environment.

• Strong analytical skills and demonstrated experience working with project budgets, forecasts, expenditures, schedules, and performance information.

• Experience preparing or supporting project forecasts, month-end reporting, project performance reporting, or similar management information.

• Strong Microsoft Excel skills and confidence working with detailed project and financial data.

• Experience with ERP or project management systems such as NetSuite, or equivalent systems, would be considered an asset.

• Experience with Microsoft Project or similar project scheduling software would be considered an asset.

• Experience with Jira, Confluence, Power BI, or other project reporting and production-management tools would be considered an asset.

• Knowledge of project forecasting, earned value management, project controls, or Estimate at Completion methodologies would be considered an asset.

• Excellent organizational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects.

• Strong attention to detail and a demonstrated commitment to data accuracy.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with Project Managers, Finance, functional teams, and other cross-functional stakeholders.

• Experience working within Aerospace & Defence or with Canadian military programs would be considered an asset.

• Must be eligible to obtain and maintain Government of Canada Security Clearance.

Responsibilities
• Support Project Managers with the day-to-day coordination and administration of assigned projects, as directed by the Project Manager, to help ensure project activities, deliverables, schedules, and budgets remain on track.

• Coordinate project activities, resources, meetings, communications, documentation, client deliverables, and other project logistics across internal and external stakeholders, as directed by Project Managers.

• Assist Project Managers in maintaining project plans, schedules, resource allocations, budgets, expenditures, forecasts, Estimate at Completion (EAC) information, and percent-complete data within NetSuite and other applicable project systems.

• Monitor and compile project cost, schedule, resource, and performance information; prepare project status reports, forecasts, month-end information, and other project reporting for review by Project Managers and management.

• Support project procurement and financial administration activities, including purchase order coordination, supplier invoice review, cost allocation, invoice tracking, and resolution of discrepancies.

• Prepare and maintain project documentation and contractual deliverables, including project plans, status reports, risk registers, meeting records, CDRLs, and other project records.

• Perform other project coordination, reporting, and administrative activities as directed by Project Managers to support successful project delivery.

title: Instructional Designer
description:
As an Instructional Designer (ID), you will be responsible for the analysis, design and development of face-to-face and online training. Working closely with Project Managers, Instructional Designers, Subject Matter Experts and Developers, you will design creative instructional strategies.

Qualifications
Candidates must possess the following qualifications:

• Must have a college diploma or degree in any field.

• Must have a minimum of five (5) years' experience within the last ten (10) years in instructional design.

• Must have a minimum of three (3) years' experience within the last ten (10) years in the instructional design of eLearning products.

• Must be able to obtain Government of Canada Secret security clearance

• Must be proficient in English.

Responsibilities
• Use process and standards, storyboard EL/DL products as prioritized by leadership in terms of content, media, learner profiles, instructional methods and levels of knowledge.

• Liaise with courseware project Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and Offices of Primary Interest (OPIs) for content acquisition, clarification, and overall alignment of EL/DL content to the desired performance objectives (POs) in accordance with the mandated Training Plan (TP).

• Advise and liaise with the production and quality assurance teams during product design, development, release and evaluation phases, including but not limited to contributing to learner assessment products, QC checks complete with verifications, and peer review.

• Assist in conducting QC reviews if required.

• Synthesize content into creative, sound instructional design that is cognitively engaging.

• Write assessment questions appropriate to the level of learning, matching the learning objectives.

• Work cooperatively with multi-disciplinary project teams consisting of DND civilian and military personnel, interns and other contractors.

• Participate in appropriate planning processes, meeting and working groups dealing primarily with the overall project, the project team and matters pertaining to general courseware production and the content review and revision cycles.

• Ensure consistency and maintain documentation for specific style guidelines (i.e., project specific or school specific style guides).

• Prepare courseware text documents to be sent to translation.

• Support development of the project plan and schedule.

• Assist in the design of the learning solution and prepare both high level and detailed design documents.

• Assist in the design and support the development of prototypes and beta test products and ensure compliance with specifications and standards.

• Liaise with development staff as needed prior to and during production (ie. to refine media specifications, to clarify storyboards and to share updates or changes).

• Identify potential obstacles, scope changes or impact on deliverables.

• Other duties as required.

## About Us

NL Health Services offers the full continuum of health and community services including public health, long-term care, community services, hospital care and unique provincial programs and services. NL Health Services prides ourselves on providing the highest quality care and service possible to the people in our communities, in our region, and in the province. To do that, we employ qualified, competent, and caring individuals who are dedicated to their professions and to our vision of Healthy People, Healthy Communities.

## About the Opportunity

We are seeking a compassionate and skilled Pediatrician to join our healthcare team. The ideal candidate will provide comprehensive medical care to infants, children, and adolescents, ensuring their physical, emotional, and developmental health. The physician will share the workload and on-call duties within the department. Pediatric services at our regional hospital include outpatient clinics, Emergency Department call coverage, inpatient coverage, routine neonatal care and attendance at difficult deliveries. We offer the opportunity for interdisciplinary clinics in the areas of development, behavior, obesity and chronic disease; opportunity to diversify based on physicians' interest. The position offers a vigorous and varied caseload, and the fulfillment of serving the needs of families in this rural part of the province. The applicant must be willing to work within a regional team with a focus on person-and-family-centered care. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

## Compensation & Incentives

Pediatrics compensation is competitive and varies based on the nature of your work and location. Your total renumeration is influenced by many things including whether you choose to work part-time vs. full-time, your experience and the community you practice in. Remuneration payment model is salaried.

Your experience is valued and recognized in Newfoundland and Labrador. We offer competitive incentives of up to $275,000 CAD for Pediatricians that recognize your passion, dedication and all that you will bring to our communities. Many incentives are stackable. We encourage you to chat with a physician recruiter to learn more. We also support a site visit for those who are curious about our province and provide relocation reimbursement.

## Qualifications

Eligible for registration and licensure as a Pediatrician with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Newfoundland and Labrador (CPSNL).

Recent changes to registration and licensure have reduced barriers and allow doctors with comparable credentials to work in our province faster. The College of Physicians and Surgeons of Newfoundland and Labrador regulates the practice of medicine in the public interest. Newfoundland and Labrador have been diligently working to reduce barriers and to allow doctors with comparable credentials to work in our province more quickly.

New approved licensure jurisdiction pathways for Specialists from Ireland, U.K., United States of America (USA), New Zealand, Australia and South Africa, as well as others approved by the CPSNL. Individuals must be trained and certified from these countries.

The successful candidate must also satisfy credentialing requirements of Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services.

To determine your eligibility, apply for registration and review licensure policies, please visit CPSNL website for complete information: https://cpsnl.ca/licensing-and-registration/licence-eligibility/

For more information about these incentives and physician opportunities in our province please visit https://www.workinhealthnl.ca or email Physician.Recruitment@nlhealthservices.ca.

## About Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, is the most easterly place in North America. A vast land, with a relatively small population, we have some of the friendliest people you’ll ever meet. Here, you can experience a solitary wilderness one day and immerse yourself in a vibrant culture the next. This is a land of rich history and natural wonders: stunning coastlines, breaching whales, icebergs, and some of the most incredible skyscapes you’ll ever see.

title: Saltwater Aquaculture Worker
description:

Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly-skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

As a result of our robust growth, we are hiring Saltwater Aquaculture Workers to join our team. The ideal candidates will be self-motivated team players willing to work flexible work hours and schedules.

The primary duties include, but are not limited to:

• Monitoring and operating the feeding systems.

• Report any observed irregularities in stocks.

• Grid installation and inspection/repair.

• Marine cage and net installation and removal.

• Operate, maintain, and clean aquaculture equipment and enclosures.

• General site maintenance including net washing.

• Operation of boats for aquaculture operations.

• Grade and weigh aquaculture stock.

• Harvest assistance as required.

*Applicants must hold or be willing to obtain a Marine Emergency Duties (MED) certificate .

This is a labour-intensive position, requires standing for long periods of time; applicants must be comfortable working in outside weather conditions on both aquaculture sites and aboard maintenance vessels.

Experience within the aquaculture field would be considered an asset but not required as on the job training is provided.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

## Benefits Package

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• Support Services: Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Wellness: Wellness programs.

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

*As per company policy, a criminal background check is required.

## The Opportunity

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to work within the parameters of the role but to reach your fullest potential. We are a team that is driven to succeed. We count performance, we reward contribution, and we recognize talent. It is about being at the center of a growing, global leader in seafood and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

Job Summary:
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.
The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.
The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;
• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
* Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
* Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
* Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
* Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
* Graduation from High School or equivalent;
* Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
* Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
* Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
* Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
* Current certification in Basic Life Support;
* Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
* Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
* Effective oral and written communication skills;
* Critical and sound decision making skills;
* Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
* For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
* A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
* A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

## Salary:

* Advanced Care Paramedic - CGHSA-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $39.14 to $46.27 per hour
* Primary Care Paramedic – CGHSA-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $32.71 to $37.40 per hour
* Ambulance Operator/Attendant – CG-25 of the NAPE HS salary scale $23.78 to $26.19 per hour

description:

## JOB SUMMARY:

The Edmundston Regional Hospital, New Brunswick, is seeking full-time pediatricians. Successful candidates will perform their duties, including the diagnosis, care and treatment of medical disorders within their specialty, with considerable clinical independence.?The pediatrician exercises independent medical judgment in performing their duties, delivers services to inpatients and outpatients, and acts as a consultant to other physicians.?The pediatrician will be responsible for delivering pediatric care to patients in Zones 5 and 6, with the support of affiliated tertiary centres.

This position involves professional medical work performed by a certified specialist (a physician with a specialty certification recognized by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick). Functions relating to the diagnosis, care and treatment of medical problems within the scope of the pediatrician's specialty are performed with a high degree of autonomy, but findings and observations may be subject to supervision and evaluation by the Department (program) Head / Program Director in which the physician works. Work may also be reviewed by Local and Regional Chiefs of Staff and the Medical Director for the zone. The physician works in accordance with the By-Laws of Vitalité Health Network.

## REQUIREMENTS:

• Degree from a recognized medical school and residency granting a licence in pediatrics;

• Certification from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (FRCPC) or equivalent;

• Eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick;

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team;

• Physical ability to perform the assigned work;

• Good work history (performance and attendance);

• Adherence to professional ethics principles, the Network's management philosophy, and organizational values;

• Compliance with the rules of confidentiality set by Vitalité Health Network.

Knowledge of French, spoken and written, is an asset.

About Us
Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services (NL Health Services) brings together five former separate health entities - Eastern Health, Central Health, Western Health, Labrador-Grenfell Health, and the Newfoundland and Labrador Centre for Health Information. The creation of a provincial health authority was announced following recommendations from Health Accord NL.

NL Health Services is responsible for delivering health and community services to more than 528,000 people living in Newfoundland and Labrador and employs over 21,000 people. NLHealthServices.ca

Job Summary
The Clinical Dietitian II is part of an inter-disciplinary team responsible for the monitoring and licensing of Personal Care Homes. This includes the monitoring of activities and reports related to nutrition and food service for assigned Personal Care Homes to ensure compliance to the Personal Care Home Program Operational Standards and the Personal Care Home Regulations 2001. There is a possibility of after-hours/weekend monitoring that may be required as part of the monitoring process. The Clinical Dietitian II collaborates with the inter-professional health care team in the provision of nutrition care; provides counselling/education to residents and staff of Personal Care Homes; participates in interdisciplinary team meetings, annual review meetings and investigations of complaints and completion of inspections which may require visits after hours and on weekends; and completes monthly statistical reports as required. The Clinical Dietitian II will engage in practice, program and quality improvement initiatives. The incumbent is required to support NL Health Service's Dietetic Internship Program through contribution of clinical practice expertise and/or preceptorship of dietetic interns.

This position reports to the Manager of the Personal Care Home Program and maintains accountability to the Provincial Professional Practice Consultant for Dietitians for integrity and professional practice.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Occasionally lifts objects up to 15 lbs. (e.g. oral nutrition supplements).
Regularly requires alertness to the health and safety of others (i.e. tube fed patients, clients with swallowing issues, etc.
Advice provided to clients impacts the health and safety of a client in regard to reactions to food allergies or blood glucose levels).
Regularly there are time pressures and deadlines and often there is lack of control over work pace.
Regularly requires a high level of attentiveness for exact results and precision for renal calculations, tube feeding and calculating nutrition prescriptions.

Job Qualifications
Bachelor of Science Degree in Nutrition/Dietetics or equivalent from a nationally accredited university program and successful completion of an accredited dietetic internship program is required.
Current Registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Dietitians is required.
Previous Clinical Dietitian experience in geriatric nutrition would be considered an asset.
Effective communication skills and the ability to work independently and as part of an interdisciplinary team would be considered an asset.
A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class 5 Driver's License and the use of a private vehicle are conditions of employment.
A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

title: CP140 OWSS Lead Asset Manager
description:
Requisition ID: 2586

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
Responsible to IMP CP140 OWSS Deputy Program Manager, and or his delegate, the successful candidate will be the primary point of contact for the Asset Management Group and be responsible for the direct supervision of a team of Asset Management Specialists (AMS). The successful candidate will be required to provide leadership, oversight, and expert level consultative advice in assigned areas of the CP140 Aircraft, including the provision of technical information and analysis, monitoring performance and maintenance requirements, and recommending improvements to optimize life-cycle costs, equipment availability and maintainability. The successful candidate will also be required to review, recommend, amend, and maintain Standard Plant Procedures (SPPs) and work instructions affecting areas within the AMS scope of responsibility.

What You Will Do:
• Supervise the CP140 AMS group, providing guidance, direction, mentorship, and support.

• Monitor AMS timekeeping, including timesheets, vacation, overtime, workload distribution, and departmental resource requirements.

• Monitor AMS hours and material budgets on behalf of the CP140 OWSS D/PM, adjusting resources as required to meet workload demands.

• Act as a liaison with DND customers and coordinate with Engineering, Production, Material, and Program departments to ensure task continuity, teamwork, and CP140 fleet operational availability.

• Contribute to program optimization, annual and long-term planning, special projects, aircraft modifications, and budget alignment.

• Ensure AMS key performance indicators are met and provide input to monthly activity reports.

• Attend and support required OWSS, review, and DND Change Control Board meetings.

• Develop and maintain SPPs and work instructions, monitor AF9000 procedures, and review procedure changes for AMS impacts.

• Assess and manage risks through the IMP Risk Management System and ensure appropriate action on technical notices.

• Review AMS and Engineering reports for quality, compliance, and airworthiness requirements, coordinating recommendations with the appropriate authorities.

• Assist with annual performance appraisals and promote a safe, respectful, and collaborative workplace.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

What You Will Bring:
• Ten years of aircraft and aircraft systems experience is required, of which five years should be hands-on work exposure to aircraft type (preferably heavy multi-engine) including supervision of others and release to flight certification authorization.

• Three years or more of experience in DND aircraft engineering administration or project management is desirable.

• Strong organizational and communication skills are essential.

• The position requires a comprehensive knowledge of the process of aircraft engineering and maintenance management.

• Familiarity with DND AF9000 series process is highly desirable.

• Good technical writing skills, the ability to read and interpret aircraft drawings and knowledge of related CFTOs (including IETMs) would be a significant advantage.

• Formal training in the CP140 Primary Air Vehicle (PAV) and related systems would be ideal; however, similar experience on another aircraft would be considered and asset.

• Training in Logistics support, Reliability Centered Maintenance and/or asset management would be considered and asset.

• Familiarity with the use of computers and MS Office software with abilities in Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, Power Point, and access are required.

• DND experience as an aircraft release authority (ARA) would be considered an asset.

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupation Health and Safety and Environment policies. Continually focusing on individual safety and the safety of others who may be affected by the sections work and to fully comply with all federal Health and Safety Legislation. Participate in Continuous Improvement, Lean & 5S activities as applicable in the department.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Canadian Government Security Clearances.

What We Will Do For You:
• All IMP's benefits become effective on your first day of work, regardless of your position.

• Employees are entitled to 3 paid personal days and 12 statutory holidays per year.

• We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RRSP Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Long Service Awards, Volunteer Grant Program, Scholarship Program, and more!

IMP is committed to Employment Equity and our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative at all job levels. We welcome applicants from Indigenous People, Visible Minority Groups, Persons with Disabilities and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self identify on either your cover letter or resume.

Job Summary:
The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;
• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)
