title: Architectural Technologist & Design Lead
description:
Job Title: Architectural Technologist & Design Lead
Location: Lower Sackville, Nova Scotia
TP-SBG-10014
For over 50 years, Sealand Building Group (Sealand) has been more than a construction company. They are dedicated partners in progress, creating controlled environments that help shape a better future for their customers, employees, and communities. Specializing in food processing, cold storage, agribusiness, distribution, and advanced manufacturing facilities, Sealand designs and builds reliable, high-performance environments that support some of Canada's most essential industries.
Sealand approaches every project with a foundation of strong values: humility in their work, honesty in their partnerships, a focus on results, kindness in their actions, and honor in their commitments. This philosophy enables them to deliver not only technically sound facilities, but also lasting relationships built on trust and shared success.
Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with Sealand Building Group in the recruitment of an Architectural Technologist & Design Lead to join their team located in Lower Sackville, Nova Scotia.
Role Description
As the Architectural Technologist & Design Lead, you will develop accurate and coordinated technical drawings as well as lead the coordination of the design process from initial project concept through construction and project closeout. Working closely with clients, consultants, project team, field team, and the internal design team, you will help transform conceptual ideas into functional facility layouts and ensure designs are coordinated, constructible, and aligned with project scope, schedule, and budget.
This is a hands-on role that combines technical design expertise with design coordination. While much of your time will be spent drawing, you will also manage consultants, facilitate design meetings, review drawings, and keep projects moving forward. Success in this role requires strong architectural knowledge, excellent communication skills, and the ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders throughout the design process.
Your responsibilities will include:

• Work with clients to understand operational requirements and develop functional building layouts and design concepts.

• Prepare conceptual layouts, design-development drawings, permit packages, and construction documents using AutoCAD, and other applicable design software.

• Develop floor plans, elevations, sections, details, schedules, and building-envelope assemblies.

• Produce accurate as-built drawings and updated drawings at project completion.

• Coordinate the design process from project initiation through construction and project closeout.

• Lead the coordination of architectural, structural, civil, mechanical, electrical and refrigeration disciplines.

• Manage external consultants and facilitate design coordination meetings throughout the project.

• Review drawings, specifications, schedules, and technical documentation for completeness, coordination, constructability, and compliance with project requirements.

• Ensure designs remain aligned with project scope, budget, schedule, and operational objectives.

• Identify design conflicts, missing information, and coordination issues and work with project stakeholders to resolve them.

• Track design decisions, revisions, approvals, and outstanding items throughout the project lifecycle.

• Work closely with design, project and site teams to support the successful transition from design into construction.

• Review RFIs, shop drawings, samples, and other construction submittals for design coordination purposes.

• Participate in site visits to review existing conditions, construction progress, and design-related issues.

• Maintain organized design records, drawing registers, meeting minutes, revision logs, and project documentation.

• Support permit submissions, regulatory approvals, and project closeout activities.

• Promote practical and constructible design solutions that support project quality, safety, schedule, and budget objectives.

Your Qualifications
The ideal candidate is an experienced Architectural Technologist who enjoys bringing people, information, and projects together. You are confident working with multiple stakeholders, comfortable asking questions and challenging assumptions, and thrive in environments where communication, coordination, and problem-solving are critical to success.
Your qualifications include:

• A degree or diploma in Architectural Technology, Structural Engineering Technology, Architecture, Engineering, or a related field.

• 7+ years of experience in architectural design, drafting, design coordination, or construction project delivery.

• Strong proficiency in AutoCAD and the ability to prepare and modify drawings when required.

• Strong working knowledge of applicable building codes and construction standards.

• Ability to read, interpret, and review construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and technical documentation.

• Experience coordinating external consultants and design disciplines throughout the project lifecycle.

• Strong understanding of building construction methods, systems, and design coordination processes.

• Working knowledge of Bluebeam and Microsoft Office.

• Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain project momentum in a fast-paced environment.

• Valid driver's license and ability to visit project sites is required.

## Assets include:

• Experience working on industrial, food processing, cold storage, manufacturing, distribution, or other specialized construction projects.

• Experience within a design-build construction environment.

• Site experience and exposure to active construction environments.

## Why Join Sealand Building Group?

• Professional development, education, and training opportunities.

• A collaborative and supportive team environment.

• The opportunity to work on specialized projects that help build Canada's food industry.

• Competitive compensation and benefits.

• Quality vehicles, accommodations, and technology resources.

• Travel per diem, where applicable.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.
For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Heather Simmons, Consultant at 902-421-2335 and hsimmons@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.
Meridia Recruitment Solutions connects leading organizations with top talent by building strong relationships and creating ideal matches with candidates because we are only successful when you are. We appreciate your interest in this opportunity.
To learn more about Meridia Recruitment Solutions, our job opportunities, and career advice we invite you to explore our site and subscribe for career alerts.

title: Communications & Engagement Lead (Future Opportunities)
description:
WHO WE ARE:
Mariner innovates always and everywhere, turning novel ideas into practical solutions. From products and services to venture creation, we build better futures powered by people. Our purpose has always been to be a great, everlasting technology company for those who make an impact - elevating people, data, and technology in the best way to solve hard problems. We partner with people embracing change, leveraging data, cybersecurity, cloud, and change management to drive successful business outcomes that matter to our customers.

Mariners build for change. Like SHIFT Energy, our energy management and decarbonization company. Or East Valley created to scale social economic impact in our communities through investment and mentorship of emerging change-makers and their companies.

Mariner s purpose has always been to be a great, everlasting technology company and the core values that guide us every day are:

## OUR VALUES

• We care for our team.

• We care about the impact we have on our community.

• We serve by solving complex problems.

• We grow because growth fuels opportunities.

• We innovate always and everywhere.

• We build a business that lasts.

## OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE:

We are looking for an experienced Change Management Consultant to join a client engagement focused on a large-scale transformation. In this role, you will lead strategic communications and stakeholder engagement, creating a clear and consistent narrative that connects complex transformation efforts, builds understanding, reduces uncertainty, and supports adoption.

## WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING IN THE ROLE:

• Develop and execute strategic communications and stakeholder engagement plans for complex transformation initiatives.

• Create a clear, consistent transformation narrative that connects related projects, changes, and implementation activities.

• Develop targeted communications for diverse audiences, including key messages, executive materials, FAQs, toolkits, bulletins, digital content, and information packages.

• Lead and support stakeholder engagement through town halls, forums, advisory groups, workshops, consultations, and surveys.

• Translate complex policy, technical, and operational information into clear, audience-appropriate communications.

• Establish communications roadmaps and governance to ensure coordinated messaging, executive alignment, and effective risk management.

• Partner with leaders and project teams to identify stakeholder concerns, manage competing priorities, and support successful adoption.

## WHAT SKILLS/QUALIFICATIONS YOU'LL NEED:

• Demonstrated experience leading communications and stakeholder engagement for large-scale transformation initiatives.

• Experience supporting complex transformation programs involving significant policy, technology, or operational changes.

• Proven ability to develop strategic communications and cohesive messaging for diverse and geographically dispersed stakeholder groups.

• Exceptional writing skills, with the ability to simplify complex policy, technical, and operational information.

• Strong executive communications, stakeholder management, facilitation, and influencing skills.

• Experience with stakeholder consultations, workshops, forums, surveys, and other engagement activities.

• Ability to think strategically, navigate competing stakeholder priorities, and manage multiple communications needs in a complex transformation environment.

• Experience supporting complex public-sector environments, such as government, healthcare, or education is highly preferred.

## WHY MARINER?

We believe in making a positive impact in the communities where we live and work! Not only are we passionate about nurturing a thriving technology sector here in Atlantic Canada, but we are also committed to solving technology challenges that will make an impact worldwide. Technology is everlasting, and we take pride in connecting world class talent to world class projects and business solutions.

If you are an IT Professional, Software Professional, or Management Consultant, that is passionate about career development, data, and problem solving, we want to hear from you! If this sounds like someone you know, share this with them so they do not miss the opportunity to experience Mariner!

To achieve this, we know we need to be all in on training and development of our team so we can continue to move the needle in the technology sector together. Of course, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to our team, but our competitive edge is the development and training that our team experiences every day.

Be part of our vibrant community that values diversity and embraces inclusion at every level. We are committed to fostering a culture where individuals from all backgrounds and walks of life feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. Our collaborative environment celebrates the richness of ideas and experiences, and we believe that by embracing diversity, we can achieve greater innovation and excellence together. Come and help us create a workplace that reflects the beautiful tapestry of our global community.

## Join our growing team!

title: New Brunswick IAC Sales Representative
description:
EDDY GROUP LIMITED "Maritime Owned and Operated"

Eddy Group Limited is a Maritime-based wholesale distributor and proud member of "Canada's Best Managed Companies". Eddy Group Limited has been a trusted partner in the construction industry for over a century. As a family business now in its fifth generation, we are all about providing top-notch products, personalized solutions, and great service to our industrial, commercial, and residential customers.

As part of our Head Office Sales team, the New Brunswick IAC Sales Representative will be responsible for developing and supporting Eddy Group Limited's Industrial Automation and Controls (IAC) business throughout New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island. This position serves as a resource for Eddy Group's branch sales teams and customers, providing product expertise, solution support, opportunity development and technical guidance.

Working collaboratively with the Branch sales teams, the IAC Specialist will help identify IAC opportunities, develop customer relationships, support quotations and product selections, and assist in converting opportunities into profitable sales.

The successful candidate will build strong relationships with customers, suppliers and Eddy Group employees while developing a strong understanding of the IAC product portfolio and the applications in which those products are used.

## What you'll do:

• Develop and grow IAC sales throughout New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island in alignment with Eddy Group's sales and business objectives.

• Identify, qualify and pursue new IAC business opportunities with existing and prospective customers.

• Develop and maintain strong, profitable customer relationships.

• Work with customers to understand their applications, challenges and requirements and recommend appropriate IAC products and solutions.

• Conduct customer visits, site visits and sales calls throughout New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island as required.

• Maintain regular contact with key IAC customers and identify opportunities for additional products and services.

• Prepare for and conduct customer presentations, product demonstrations and meetings.

• Develop opportunities from initial inquiry through quotation, follow-up and successful sale.

• Work with suppliers and manufacturers to identify products, pricing, technical information and solutions for customer requirements.

• Assist branch salespeople with IAC product selection, applications, specifications and customer requirements.

• Assist with complex IAC quotations, product recommendations and solution development.

• Participate in customer calls with branch salespeople where specialized IAC knowledge would add value.

• Provide guidance to branch employees without taking ownership of the customer relationship away from the branch salesperson.

• Help branch sales teams become more knowledgeable and confident in selling IAC products.

## Qualifications and key competencies:

• Post-secondary education in business, sales, engineering technology, electrical, automation, controls or a related field is considered an asset.

• Minimum five years of experience in wholesale distribution, electrical, automation, controls, industrial or related industries.

• Strong knowledge of IAC products, applications and solutions.

• Previous experience in a sales, technical sales, applications or customer-support capacity.

• Experience working with industrial customers and understanding their operational requirements.

• Strong ability to develop and maintain customer relationships.

• Demonstrated ability to identify sales opportunities and convert them into profitable business.

• Strong product knowledge combined with the ability to understand and communicate technical information.

• Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills.

• Ability to work effectively with both customers and internal sales teams.

• Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

• Self-motivated and capable of working independently while remaining highly collaborative.

• Strong business acumen, including an understanding of pricing, gross profit and customer profitability.

• Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

## Why join the Eddy Group?

• Health, drug, dental, life insurance, dependent life insurance, AD&D, EFAP and LTD Benefits.

• Vehicle allowance and gas cards for business purposes.

• Defined Contribution Pension Plan (4% Employee and 2% Employer Match).

• Earn quarterly and annual commissions for your hard work.

• Join a dynamic, results-driven team where collaboration is key, and success is the norm.

• Experience a winning culture that makes you proud.

• Eddy Group has family values and treats its employees that way.

This is a full-time position that may be located anywhere in New Brunswick with preference for individuals located near Eddy Group Ltd locations. Regular business hours are from 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Friday, however, occasional work outside these hours should be expected.

Annual base salary will be commensurate with your experience.

About Us
The Public Prosecution Service (PPS) offers a unique and meaningful opportunity to contribute to justice and public safety. Established in 1990 as the first statutorily based independent prosecution service in Canada, the mandate of the PPS is rooted in its commitment to ensuring fair and equal treatment in the prosecution of criminal and provincial offences.
We are looking for the brightest legal minds, who also reflect the rich diversity of our province! We don't just accept difference – we celebrate a supportive culture of diversity and belonging. We strive to create an environment where different perspectives and experiences are welcomed and valued. We encourage applications from those that equally value and champion equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility (EDIA).

Why Choose Us?
A career with the Public Prosecution Service in Nova Scotia provides a unique opportunity to contribute to justice, public safety, and the overall well-being of the community while working in a professional, inclusive, and ethical environment.
We are a dedicated and passionate team with a determination to make a difference in the society we serve, utilizing our expertise and recognizing and applying an equity and inclusion lens to our work, in our training and development, workplace culture, communications, partnering and engagement to ensure we protect and reflect the communities we live in and serve.

What We Offer
1. Commitment to Justice and Public Interest:
This is achieved by performing prosecution duties with fairness, professionalism, and integrity. Employees actively contribute to upholding the principles of justice in Nova Scotia.
2. Mission and Goals:
Aligning with the Government of Nova Scotia's priority of fulfilling social responsibility for public safety, the PPS' mission and goals include providing excellence in public service, identifying, and managing resources effectively, applying best business practices, and fostering an environment for independent prosecutorial discretion that recognizes the importance of diversity and inclusion in ensuring representation reflective of the community.
3. Core Business Functions:
Employees at the PPS engage in core business functions that play a crucial role in the legal landscape of Nova Scotia. These functions include representing the Crown in criminal and quasi-criminal matters at all levels of court, handling appeals, providing legal advice and assistance to law enforcement, and actively participating in the development of criminal law and prosecutions policy.
4. Professional Development and High Ethical Standards:
The PPS is committed to maintaining a diverse team that reflects excellence, dedication to public service, and high ethical standards. Employees have the opportunity for professional development in a welcoming environment that values continuous improvement and recognizes diversity and inclusion contributes to a healthy and thriving workplace culture that allows team members to be their full selves at work, while upholding the highest ethical principles.
5. Community Engagement:
The PPS is focused on providing a service that is reflective of the community it serves. By fostering diversity and inclusivity, employees contribute to building a legal system that understands and respects the needs and perspectives of the broader community.
6. Impactful Contribution to Society:
Working for the PPS allows individuals to make a direct and meaningful impact on society by upholding the rule of law, protecting the safety and well-being of the community, and ensuring the fair treatment of those accused of prohibited conduct.
For more information on the Public Prosecution Service please visit the following link: https://novascotia.ca/pps/

This position is based in Cape Breton Region will report to the Chief Crown Attorney, Cape Breton Region, to whom the incumbent is accountable for the provision of competent prosecution services. The Crown Attorney will advise law enforcement agencies when requested. Other key responsibilities include conducting the prosecution of charges resulting from matters within the Public Prosecution Service mandate that result from law enforcement agency investigations and other prosecutions and duties as directed by the Chief Crown Attorney, Cape Breton.

Qualifications and Experience
You are a practicing member of the Nova Scotia Barristers' Society (or eligible to become so) and have a thorough understanding of the prosecution process, and competence in the areas of criminal procedures, evidence, and substantive criminal law. Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

title: Continuous Improvement Engineer
description:
Requisition ID: 2518

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. The Continuous Improvement Engineer will analyze business processes and identify opportunities for improvement across aircraft and component maintenance/modification/repair/overhaul, aircraft part manufacture, engineering, supply chain, and project portfolio management activities. Develop and implement improvement initiatives using continuous improvement tools & techniques, working closely with diverse stakeholder groups, often including IT. Measure improvements, set them up to be sustained, communicate results, celebrate successes, and share lessons learned. Promote and develop continuous improvement knowledge and thinking throughout the organization.

What You Will Do:
• Review existing processes, facilities, systems, etc. for potential productivity improvements.

• Use standard lean, six sigma, and industrial engineering tools/techniques to analyze existing processes and suggest improvements.

• Training and experience in process improvement techniques such as lean manufacturing, six sigma, and continuous improvement

• Ability to successfully work and communicate with all levels of employees and management

• Strong MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, MS Project, MS Word, MS Power BI, & SQL skills preferred

title: Administrative Support (Clinical) (1025)

employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 49374

Department: Justice

Location: Dartmouth, New Glasgow, Sydney and Yarmouth

Type of Employment: Relief

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 18-Jul-27 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Correctional Services division of the Department of Justice is responsible for the administration and operation of community and custody-based programs and services for adults and young persons. Within the Correctional Services core business area there are two programs: community corrections & correctional facilities. Each of these program areas is broken down into closely related activities that have a specific impact on the program's target group.
Four (4) adult correctional facilities and one (1) youth centre provide the safety and security of person in custody while providing programs that address dynamic criminogenic factors to assist with their successful, reintegration back into the community.
Nova Scotia Correctional Services utilizes an evidence-based approach in both Community Corrections and custodial facilities. Core Correctional Practices (CCP) is the foundational practice that drives reintegration and rehabilitation practices deployed within Correctional Services. Utilizing CCP, Correctional Services staff can effectively interact, manage behavior, and help facilitate change, within target populations.
For more information on the Department of Justice Correctional Services please visit our website.

About Our Opportunity
As a Correctional Officer, you are responsible for the safe secure custody, control and supervision of sentence and remand persons in custody in an adult correctional facility on a rotating shift basis. Our Correctional Officer undertakes duties associated with your shift assignment in various areas of the facility. These areas include persons in custody Living Units, Admission and Discharge, Reception/Visitation, Recreation, Laundry, and Canteen Services. In this role, you will have regular and ongoing interaction with persons in custody, while encouraging pro-social behaviour. You are also responsible for administrative functions related to the case management database (JEIN) and the Offender Behavioural Management System. Correctional Officers work with a diverse person in custody population and are accountable for promoting and adhering to policy and procedures, standard operating procedures, post orders and directives.
As part of this role, you will be involved with conducting persons in custody counts and searches, writing reports, ensuring persons in custody security and safety, and compiling tasks related to physical plant cleanliness and maintenance requirements.

Primary Accountabilities
Facility Security
Provides dynamic supervision of persons in custody and safe secure custody, control, and supervision of the persons in custody
Persons in Custody Supervision
Includes, but not limited to participate in the case management of persons in custody; approve and arrange professional and personal visits and professional persons in custody phone calls, and escort persons in custody within the facility; respond to persons in custody complaints and requests; assist in the completion of forms (e.g. requests, complaints); supervise persons in custody work activity inside and outside the facility
Physical Plant Maintenance
Supervise facility cleaning by persons in custody, supervise persons in custody trustees on outside work detail, submit maintenance work orders when required
Programs
Advise persons in custody of available programs and referring and adhering to the posted program schedule and support persons in custody program work in the living units
Administration & Communication
Record and communicate information through reports, forms, logbooks, email and JEIN documentation and participate in committees or meetings as requested by the Superintendent or designate
Communicate in a timely, transparent, and effective manner and participate in workplace wellness initiatives by promoting teamwork, leadership, diversity, and a healthy workplace

Qualifications and Experience
You possess a High School diploma and 2 years of related experience. An equivalent combination of training and experience will be considered. Typical equivalencies include: a certificate/diploma from an accredited Correctional Officer program or a university degree in a related field of study (Criminology, Psychology or other Social Science programs).
Your experience and knowledge in the following areas are considered assets in this role:

• Previous employment as a Correctional Officer, or within Adult/Youth Custody

• Experience in law enforcement (Police, Sheriffs, Border Services, Military Police)

• Experience in the following areas may also be given consideration towards an equivalency: Security, Military, Firefighting, Social Workers, Residential Counsellors/Caseworkers/Support Workers, Occupational Health & Safety.

• Leadership experience (i.e. leading youth programs, groups, or committees, working with vulnerable populations)

• Experience working with diverse communities, including Elders, knowledge keepers, cultural leaders, and community organizations, is considered an asset.

Equivalency
Include, but not limited to:

• A related 2 year post secondary diploma

• A related 1 year post secondary diploma and 1 year of related experience

• 5 years of employment in a related field, for example Social Work; Residential Counselling, working with vulnerable populations

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Working Conditions
• Required to work shiftwork which can be physically, mentally, and emotionally demanding

• Must be constantly alert when in contact with facility population

• Required to perform person and area searches and use restraint equipment which is physically demanding

• Potential for disruption to personal and family life when there is a disturbance at the facility

• The position requires the ability to work effectively in a facility setting that may be noisy during periods of peak operational and resident activity.

• Regularly interact with persons in custody and manage challenging behaviours in a professional and respectful manner.

• Perform searches, security checks, escorts, and respond to emergencies and critical incidents as required.

• Work collaboratively as part of a team while maintaining professional boundaries and adhering to established policies, procedures, and security protocols.

• Must maintain constant awareness and professionalism while engaging with facility populations, including individuals who may have difficulty controlling emotional responses.

Additional Information
Relief employees fill gaps in the schedule and replace full time employees when operational requirements demand as determined by the Employer – as a relief employee there is no guarantee of hours.
Relief correctional officers are required to work shift work (day shift, night shifts, holidays, weekends on short notice)
The facility is a 24-hour operation and is a tobacco-free/vape-free environment, and is not permitted on the property.
This position requires a valid Driver's License, a Driver's Abstract, Standard First Aid/CPR Certificate, and proof of all stated education and training. This should be uploaded to your profile at the time of application.
Assessment Process

## Join Us in Creating the Best Places to Live, Shop, Work & Play

As Commercial Leasing Manager, you will be responsible for the strategic leasing, financial performance, tenant relations, and operational oversight of Southwest Properties' commercial portfolio.

We believe in going beyond the necessary to create inspiring environments. To us, a building is so much more than just a collection of walls under a single roof. At Southwest, we believe an innovative, exceptional, thoughtfully designed building can inspire great things to happen inside and around it.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## Here's a Few Reasons Why We Love Where We Work

• Customizable Plan Options for Health & Dental Coverage (Single/Family Plan Options)

• Annual Health and Wellness Incentives

## What Your Day Will Look Like

You will lead all commercial leasing activities, including lease negotiations, tenant retention, portfolio optimization, landlord representation, and commercial property performance. You will work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders, tenants, property management providers, legal counsel, and service providers to maximize occupancy, revenue, tenant satisfaction, and long-term asset value.

This position will work with members of the senior management team and property operations to support the strategic objectives and performance of the commercial portfolio.

Hours of Work: Full-time day hours Monday to Friday, with occasional evening and after-hours commitments.

Work Location: Southwest Properties Main Office (1315 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS), with regular visits to commercial properties and tenant locations.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## Compensation

In addition to a competitive base salary, the successful candidate will participate in a performance-based commission program tied to commercial leasing activities and the achievement of established leasing objectives. This incentive structure is designed to reward strong performance in areas including business development, tenant acquisition, lease negotiations, and occupancy growth.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## What You'll be Responsible For

## Commercial Leasing & Tenant Relations

• Develop and implement leasing strategies that maximize occupancy, revenue, tenant retention, and long-term portfolio value.

• Lead the negotiation and administration of all commercial leasing transactions, including new lease agreements, licenses, amendments, renewals, extensions, assignments, and terminations.

• Act as the primary point of contact for commercial tenants, ensuring a high standard of customer service and tenant satisfaction.

• Review, negotiate, and finalize leasing documentation in collaboration with legal counsel.

• Proactively prospect for new tenants and leasing opportunities to minimize vacancy and maximize portfolio performance.

• Establish and maintain strong relationships with existing tenants, prospective tenants, brokers, and industry stakeholders.

• Conduct market research and provide subject matter expertise on commercial leasing trends, market conditions, and competitive positioning.

• Provide advice and recommendations regarding tenant mix, tenant quality, customer experience, and overall commercial property performance.

• Manage and resolve conflicts of interest between tenants, landlords, and other stakeholders while maintaining positive business relationships.

• Represent Southwest Properties at industry events, networking functions, and professional associations.

## Portfolio Performance & Financial Management

• Establish leasing and financial performance objectives for commercial properties.

• Set and manage market rents, discounted rents, license fees, operating costs, recoveries, and other lease-related financial terms.

• Oversee rent collection, accounts receivable, arrears management, tenant defaults, and collection processes.

• Monitor budgets and prepare financial and operational reports.

• Analyze leasing performance, occupancy trends, market activity, and revenue opportunities.

• Prepare rent rolls, tenant abstracts, leasing forecasts, budget inputs, and portfolio performance analyses.

## Property Operations & Landlord Representation

• Work collaboratively with the Operations team to ensure commercial properties are maintained and operated to a high standard.

• Act on behalf of the ownership group to provide guidance, support, and oversight to third-party property management providers.

• Manage landlord relationships and ensure landlord obligations under lease agreements are fulfilled.

• Procure, negotiate, and manage third-party vendor contracts.

• Manage external service providers and contractors.

• Monitor tenant compliance with lease obligations and building requirements.

## Strategic Planning & Reporting

• Monitor market conditions, competitor activity, and emerging trends.

• Provide strategic recommendations regarding portfolio performance and asset optimization opportunities.

• Support acquisitions, development projects, redevelopment initiatives, and other strategic projects.

• Collaborate with Finance, Construction & Development, Operations, and Market teams.

• Prepare and present leasing, financial, and operational reports to leadership and committees.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## Your Environment

This role operates across a variety of settings, including the Southwest Properties Main Office, on-site property locations, and tenant-facing environments. Southwest Properties Main Office is located at 1315 Lower Water Street, Halifax, Nova Scotia.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## What Will Help You Succeed

You don't require all the listed qualifications to add incredible value to our team. If you feel energized thinking about what you could accomplish at Southwest, we would love to hear from you.

Our ideal candidate has a Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Real Estate, Finance, Property Management, or a related discipline, combined with 5-7 years of progressively senior experience in commercial leasing, real estate asset management, commercial property management, or a comparable field.

• CPM, RPA, CCIM, or equivalent designations are considered an asset.

• Ability to build strong, professional relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

• Professional written and verbal communication.

• Highly organized, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.

• Proactive and solutions-oriented mindset.

• Strong negotiation and influencing skills.

• Customer-focused approach with a commitment to service excellence.

Position requires: Criminal Records Check Completion.

____________________________________________________________________________________

## People are at the Heart of Everything We Do

Southwest Properties is committed to attracting and retaining a diverse team, who values your experiences, perspectives, and unique identity. We are committed to creating and maintaining an environment that is inclusive, equitable, and welcoming.

____________________________________________________________________________________

Thank you for your interest in Southwest Properties. Those chosen for an interview will be contacted.

We are a team of individuals who get joy from bringing joy to others.

## Senior Client Service Manager
Halifax, Nova Scotia
Reference #JL-BLW-10035

Bloom Wealth Inc. is a boutique wealth management firm serving clients throughout Atlantic Canada and across Canada. Built on long-term relationships, trust, and exceptional client service, Bloom Wealth provides comprehensive investment, insurance, and financial planning solutions tailored to each client's unique goals. The firm takes pride in delivering a highly personalized experience, combining professional expertise with a warm, family-oriented culture where clients feel valued and supported.

As Bloom Wealth continues to grow, they are seeking a highly organized, client-focused, and experienced Senior Client Service Manager to join their team in Halifax, Nova Scotia.

## The Role

The Senior Client Service Manager is a key member of the Bloom Wealth team and plays a critical role in ensuring a seamless client experience across investment and insurance services. Supporting advisors in all aspects of client onboarding, account maintenance, service delivery, and ongoing relationship management, this individual serves as a trusted operational partner and an important point of contact for clients.

This is an ideal opportunity for an experienced wealth management professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys juggling multiple priorities, and takes pride in delivering exceptional service. The successful candidate will bring strong industry knowledge, meticulous attention to detail, and a proactive approach to managing complex client needs and administrative processes.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Provide administrative and operational support to Bloom Wealth advisors throughout the client lifecycle.

• Process new investment accounts, transfers, and trades while ensuring all documentation is complete and compliant.

• Manage and follow insurance applications and in-force business through every stage of the process.

• Maintain accurate client records, documentation, and activities within the firm's CRM and associated systems.

• Serve as a primary point of contact for client inquiries and requests, providing prompt and professional service.

• Coordinate with investment dealers, insurance carriers, service providers, and head office teams to ensure client needs are met efficiently.

• Prepare and support annual client reviews, meeting materials, account documentation, and DocuSign workflows.

• Monitor outstanding client matters, ensuring all follow-ups are tracked, documented, and completed in a timely manner.

• Maintain compliance standards and procedures across all investment and insurance business activities.

• Collaborate closely with advisors and team members to ensure visibility on client activity, upcoming business, and outstanding requirements.

• Assist with marketing initiatives, client communications, newsletters, and office administration as required.

• Provide guidance and support to newer team members, including junior Client Service Managers, co-op students, and new advisors when appropriate.

• Attend industry training sessions, provider seminars, and complete required continuing education requirements.

## Qualifications & Experience:

• Mutual Fund Licensed (required).

• Life Insurance License considered an asset but not required.

• Minimum 7-10 years of experience in a client service, wealth management, investment administration, or financial services environment; 10+ years is considered ideal.

• Experience supporting investment and insurance business, including account processing, trades, transfers, and client documentation.

• Strong understanding of compliance requirements and industry best practices within the financial services sector.

• Proficiency with CRM platforms and Microsoft Office applications.

• Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and shifting deadlines simultaneously.

• Outstanding attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Professional, client-focused demeanor with strong relationship-building capabilities.

## The Ideal Candidate

Bloom Wealth is seeking an individual who is proactive, engaged, and highly accountable. The successful candidate will take ownership of their work, anticipate client and team needs, and consistently follow through on commitments. They will excel in a collaborative environment where communication, teamwork, and client care are essential to success. This person is naturally curious, enjoys improving processes, and understands that delivering an exceptional client experience often requires flexibility, initiative, and a willingness to adapt to changing priorities throughout the day.

title: General Manager
description:
General Manager - Northeast Nutrition Inc.
Location: Truro, Nova Scotia
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
Work Setting: On-site
Experience Level: Senior Leadership

## About Cooke Aquaculture

Cooke Aquaculture is a global seafood company with operations across North America, Europe, South America, and Australia. Our success is driven by a dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative team supported by dedicated employees who live and work in coastal communities and contribute to the strength of the local economy. As an integrated seafood company, Cooke is committed to delivering high-quality, responsibly produced seafood while continually investing in our people, operations, and communities.

## About Northeast Nutrition Inc.

Northeast Nutrition Inc., a member of the Cooke family of companies, operates an integrated feed manufacturing facility in Truro, Nova Scotia. The facility produces high-quality, nutritionally optimized aquaculture feed that supports Cooke farming operations in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Newfoundland and Labrador, and Maine. We are seeking an experienced and results-oriented General Manager to provide strategic and operational leadership for the facility. This is a key leadership position responsible for ensuring safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective operations while delivering consistent feed quality and performance to support Cooke's farming operations.

## The Opportunity

As General Manager, you will have overall responsibility for the performance of the Northeast Nutrition facility. You will lead a multidisciplinary team, establish operational priorities, drive continuous improvement, manage costs, and ensure the highest standards of safety, quality, regulatory compliance, and customer service. This is a highly visible leadership role with significant influence on operational performance and the broader success of Cooke's integrated aquaculture business.

## Key Responsibilities

• Lead Plant Operations
• Provide overall leadership and accountability for day-to-day plant operations.

• Oversee production, quality, maintenance, shipping and receiving, health and safety, labour management, training, and operational planning.

• Develop and execute production plans to meet the needs of Cooke's farming operations while maximizing plant capacity and efficiency.

• Establish performance objectives, monitor key operating metrics, and take decisive action to address gaps.

• Ensure effective coordination between production, maintenance, quality, logistics, and other functional areas.

• Drive Operational Excellence
• Lead a culture of continuous improvement across the facility.

• Champion Lean Manufacturing principles and identify opportunities to improve throughput, productivity, reliability, and overall plant performance.

• Reduce waste, unplanned downtime, production losses, and operating costs.

• Partner closely with Maintenance to improve equipment reliability, preventative maintenance, and asset utilization.

• Use operational data and performance metrics to identify trends, solve problems, and drive sustainable improvements.

• Ensure Feed Quality, Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance
• Maintain the highest standards of feed quality, nutritional performance, and product consistency.

• Ensure compliance with applicable HACCP, CFIA, FDA, environmental, occupational health and safety, and other regulatory requirements.

• Lead the investigation and resolution of quality or feed-performance issues through effective root-cause analysis and corrective action.

• Promote a culture where quality and food safety are embedded in every aspect of the operation.

• Build and Lead High-Performing Teams
• Lead, coach, and develop managers, supervisors, and plant employees.

• Establish clear expectations and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, respect, and continuous improvement.

• Support workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, training, performance management, and succession planning.

• Develop strong relationships with employees, operational leaders, and key stakeholders across Cooke.

• Encourage employee engagement and participation in safety, quality, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Manage Financial & Business Performance
• Develop and manage operating budgets and financial targets.

• Maintain strong control over labour, raw materials, energy, maintenance, and other operating costs.

• Identify and implement initiatives that improve productivity and profitability without compromising safety or quality.

• Analyze operational and financial performance to support informed business decisions.

• Balance short-term operational requirements with long-term capacity, reliability, and business objectives.

• Champion Health & Safety
• Provide visible leadership in health and safety and ensure compliance with all applicable legislation and company standards.

• Establish and maintain a proactive, prevention-focused safety culture.

• Ensure employees are appropriately trained and equipped to perform their work safely.

• Lead by example and hold leaders and employees accountable for safe work practices.

## What You Bring

• 5+ years of progressive leadership experience in feed manufacturing, aquaculture, food manufacturing, or a closely related process-manufacturing environment.

• Previous experience leading a manufacturing facility or large-scale production operation.

• Strong knowledge of plant operations, production planning, maintenance, reliability, quality, and cost management.

• Demonstrated success leading teams and delivering measurable improvements in productivity, efficiency, safety, and financial performance.

• Experience with Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, root-cause analysis, and operational performance management.

• Strong understanding of HACCP, CFIA, FDA, and other applicable food/feed safety and regulatory requirements.

• Experience managing budgets, operating costs, capital requirements, and business performance.

• Excellent leadership, communication, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, highly integrated operating environment.

• Post-secondary education in business, engineering, manufacturing, food science, aquaculture, or a related discipline would be considered an asset.

## Working Environment

This is an on-site leadership position based at the Northeast Nutrition facility in Truro, Nova Scotia. The General Manager is expected to maintain a strong presence on the production floor and actively engage with employees and operational teams. The role involves working in a manufacturing environment that may be fast-paced, noisy, and subject to varying temperatures. Appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) is required in designated areas.

## Why Join Cooke?

At Cooke, we believe our success comes from people who take initiative, demonstrate resourcefulness, and are committed to getting the job done well. We provide our leaders with the opportunity to make meaningful decisions, solve complex challenges, develop high-performing teams, and build a career within a growing global seafood company. You'll be joining an organization where your leadership can have a direct impact-not only on the performance of a facility, but on an integrated aquaculture operation spanning multiple regions.

NOTE: The recruiter is reviewing and interviewing eligible applicants for this position as they are received. If you are interested in this posting, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

Company Website: https://www.cookeseafood.com

## PRODUCTION COORDINATOR

## (1 Year term position)

Northeast Nutrition Inc. is looking for a Production Coordinator (for a term of 1 year) to join our Team in Truro, Nova Scotia. Reporting to the Plant Manager, the Production Coordinator is a key role in supporting the production operations.

The Role
The Production Coordinator is responsible for planning and coordinating feed production and logistics to ensure timely delivery to aquaculture farms. This role acts as the primary liaison between internal teams, external customers, and transportation providers. Key responsibilities include production scheduling, documentation, inventory management, and maintaining strong communication channels to support continuous plant operations.

## Responsibilities

• Serve as the main contact with Regional Production Managers and Warehouse Managers to understand feed and warehousing requirements.

• Communicate with internal and external customers to manage immediate needs and long-term forecasts.

• Build and maintain the plant's production extruder list based on feed forecasts.

• Create shop orders and shipping documents, ensuring a minimum of 72 hours of production plans are in place.

• Prepare U.S. shipping and export documentation for cross-border shipments.

• Coordinate outbound logistics schedules and communicate weekly plans to carriers; update schedules as needed.

• Maintain continuous communication between truck carriers and plant production to ensure smooth flow and adequate warehouse space.

• Follow up on orders to confirm shipment, receipt, and billing accuracy.

• Conduct monthly finished feed inventory counts and collaborate with the Controller on adjustments.

• Order packaging supplies (empty totes, 25 KG bags, labels, pallets) to maintain production flow.

• Ensure timely feed delivery to farms-preventing any feed shortages.

## Qualifications

• Post-secondary education in logistics, supply chain, or a related field, or equivalent experience, is considered an asset.

• Minimum 2 years of experience in production coordination or logistics.

• Strong organizational and communication skills.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ERP systems.

• Knowledge of feed manufacturing or related industry preferred.

## Attributes

• High attention to detail and accuracy.

• Strong time management and organizational skills.

• Ability to work in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

• Good interpersonal skills for effective communication with internal and external stakeholders.

title: Civil Engineering Technologist
Treasury & Corporate Finance Co-op Student
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Treasury & Corporate Finance co-op student to join our Treasury team in Toronto.

The role is hybrid and an 8, 12, or 18 months fixed term position starting in January 2027. This posting is for an existing position vacancy.

As a Treasury & Corporate Finance student, you'll gain hands-on exposure to treasury operations, financial analysis, cash and liquidity management, corporate finance, and financial risk management within a global organization.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Support the preparation of recurring treasury and financial reports; analyze data to identify trends, variances, and potential issues; and assist with presentation materials for internal stakeholders.

• Help monitor daily cash positions, update short-term cash flow forecasts, support payment and receipt processes, and assist with bank account reconciliations and investigation of outstanding items.

• Support analyses of debt, liquidity, capital structure, funding alternatives, interest costs, and other corporate finance topics.

• Assist with data collection, reporting, and analysis related to foreign exchange, interest rate, counterparty credit, and liquidity risks, in accordance with established policies and controls.

• Help improve reports, controls, dashboards, and workflows using Excel, Microsoft Copilot, artificial intelligence, and other data-analysis or automation tools.

• Maintain accurate records and supporting documentation, follow internal policies and procedures, and assist with audit or compliance requests.

• Contribute to treasury projects and cross-functional initiatives, prepare meeting materials, track agreed actions, and perform other relevant assignments.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation

• Flexible work arrangements

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Opportunities to build your network and lots of fun!

## About You

## Education:

• Currently enrolled in your second year of a bachelor's degree program in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, Accounting, Engineering, Data Analytics, or a related field.

## Skills:

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to organize priorities, meet deadlines, work collaboratively, and handle confidential information responsibly.

• Proactive attitude, curiosity, sound judgment, and willingness to learn.

• Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; familiarity with Microsoft Copilot, artificial intelligence, data visualization, automation tools, or enterprise systems is an asset.

## Why Toronto

Vale Base Metals' Toronto office serves as a pivotal hub for the company's operations. This office is central to Vale Base Metals' finance, strategic planning, commercial (marketing and sales), and sustainability teams, driving key initiatives that support the company's global mission. Toronto's vibrant, diverse, and dynamic environment enhances Vale Base Metals' ability to innovate and excel in these critical areas, reflecting the city's status as a leading international business center.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry. In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the company must be lawfully able to work for the company in the country where the role is located. The company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

The Canadian Red Cross is looking for an analytical Senior Program Advisor who can turn research and emerging insights into useful guidance and concrete products. This role will help us understand what is changing, what it may mean, and where future risks and opportunities may emerge by bringing together data, operational insight, and diverse perspectives to support evidence-informed decisions, innovation, and organizational readiness.
The successful candidate will be comfortable working with ambiguity, exploring complex problems, testing assumptions, and translating a wide range of information into clear and useful insights. They will work collaboratively across teams and with external partners to identify emerging issues, strengthen analysis, and support the development of practical responses and new opportunities.

## In this role, you will :

• Implement and continuously improve a humanitarian foresight cycle, including the development of annual risk-based scenarios, to support operational and longer-term planning with evidence-based assumptions.

• Conduct research, environmental scanning, and analysis using internal and external sources to identify emerging humanitarian trends, risks, opportunities, and planning implications.

• Develop clear foresight products, scenarios, briefings, presentations, and recommendations that translate complex information into useful insights for planning and decision-making.

• Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to frame complex challenges, test assumptions, and identify practical options.

• Support the identification and assessment of innovative approaches, service improvements, partnerships, and future opportunities.

• Develop risk-based scenarios and assess potential humanitarian impacts, readiness, and capacity or capability needs to support strategic planning, program or service design, and organizational improvement.

• Build and maintain internal and external partnerships across public, private, academic, and humanitarian sectors to gather and validate insights, strengthen analysis, share relevant risk information and lessons learned, and support senior leaders' engagement in foresight and emergency-planning forums.

• Contribute subject matter expertise and advice to projects and initiatives that strengthen organizational readiness, effectiveness, and impact.

• Contribute effectively within project and matrix teams; support planning and reporting; maintain organized team documentation and records, including SharePoint filing; manage relevant subscriptions and information resources; and continuously improve foresight methods, tools, and products through research, learning, and collaboration.

## What we are looking for:

• A minimum of six to nine years of job-related experience and a three-year college diploma or university degree in social sciences, community development, Indigenous studies, public administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. A graduate diploma or degree, professional degree, certification, or designation in a related field may be required.

• Experience in research, strategic analysis, policy, program or service design, foresight, risk analysis, innovation, planning, emergency management, or a related field.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to gather, integrate, interpret, and assess complex information.

• The ability to identify patterns, trends, risks, opportunities, and connections across different issues and sources.

• Demonstrated problem-solving skills and comfort working on complex issues where the way forward may not be immediately apparent.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex information into concise and accessible insights.

• Experience preparing briefings, reports, presentations, recommendations, or other products for decision-makers and diverse audiences.

• Strong collaboration, facilitation, and stakeholder-engagement skills.

• Curiosity, sound judgment, initiative, and a willingness to explore new ideas and approaches.

• The ability to work independently under broad direction while contributing effectively within cross-functional or matrix teams.

• Experience with horizon scanning, forecasting, scenario planning, systems thinking, futures methods, or innovation methods would be an asset.

• English proficiency required, French is a strong asset.

## Working conditions:

• The work is primarily performed in an office or remote-work environment and requires sustained concentration and the ability to process significant amounts of information.

• The role may require occasional travel and flexibility during periods of heightened operational activity.

• Participation in emergency planning, preparedness, or response activities may be required.

Competition Number: VAC0028659

Posted Date: 2026-09-02

Closing Date: Open until filled.

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Junior Vessel Manager
description:
Junior Vessel Manager
St. John's, Maran Shuttle Tankers

Maran Shuttle Tankers (MST) is the shuttle tanker shipping unit of the Angelicoussis Group, a global leader in energy shipping with a proud history dating back to 1947. MST's story began with Statoil's first shuttle tanker loading in 1979 and has evolved through Navion, Teekay, and Altera Shuttle Tankers before joining the Angelicoussis family in 2025. Our vision is to be the Leader in Seaborne Solutions. We deliver world-class shipping services to our clients in a safe, reliable, and sustainable way, while embracing energy transition through innovative solutions for zero-carbon vessels. Our values guide everything we do: Integrity, Reliability, Innovation, Care, and Endurance.

## About the role

Maran has an office in St. John's Newfoundland, to manage the existing regional contracts. Maran provides shuttle tankers services for offshore crude oil loading and transportation from the offshore projects operating on the Grand Banks of Newfoundland and Labrador. The St. John's division operates under MST (Atlantic) Shipping Management ULC.

The Junior Vessel Manager is a development role designed to build the technical, operational, and commercial understanding required to progress toward full vessel management responsibilities. Working under the guidance and supervision of an experienced Vessel Manager, the role will support the safe, reliable, sustainable, and cost-efficient operation of assigned vessels while developing practical experience in shuttle tanker management.

The Junior Vessel Manager will assist the Vessel Manager and ship teams with day-to-day vessel follow-up, technical coordination, performance monitoring, and communication between the vessels, office, customers, and support functions. The position combines hands-on support, structured learning, and job shadowing, with increasing responsibility as capability and experience develop.

This opportunity is intended for a recent graduate or early-career professional with a relevant marine or technical background who is motivated to develop into a Vessel Manager role over time however, other candidates may be considered depending on qualifications and experience.

## Duties and responsibilities

Working under the guidance of the Vessel Manager, some of the areas you will support include:

• Treat safety and environmental compliance as a top priority.

• Support the safe and efficient operation of assigned shuttle tankers in accordance with internal and external requirements.

• Develop effective working relationships and communication with vessel staff, office support functions, customers, and other relevant internal and external stakeholders.

• Assist with planning, coordination, documentation, and follow-up of technical maintenance, inspections, dry-dockings, major repairs, and vessel performance activities.

• Contribute to financial follow-up, including budget input, forecasting, cost monitoring, and reporting.

• Support HSEQ initiatives, improvement actions, and follow-up activities in cooperation with relevant support functions.

• Participate in incident reviews, investigations, and corrective action follow-up, while learning the company's approach to safety, risk management, and continuous improvement.

• Participate as a member of the Emergency Response Team as training and competence develop.

## Qualifications

• Mechanical or electrical engineering or marine engineering background.

• Recent graduates are welcome to apply.

• Proficiency in written and oral English.

## Personal qualities

• Demonstrates teamwork, curiosity, initiative, and strong interpersonal and communication skills.

• Shows analytical ability, problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and willingness to learn in a complex operational environment.

The Company offers attractive compensation and benefits package and a friendly working environment. All applications will be treated as strictly confidential.

The position is based in St. John's, Canada.

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by September 30, 2026.

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

The region provides a wide range of services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations including eviction prevention, and monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance.
