title: Supply Chain Analyst Level 2
description:
Requisition ID: 2549

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
The primary responsibility will be to maximize the effectiveness and efficiency of Supply Chain Services in support of the CP140 Aurora Optimized Weapons Systems Management Program using the Canadian Forces Supply System (CFSS). The position will work in conjunction with Life Cycle Asset Managers as well as company and DND Technical Authorities (TA), to provide responsive procurement and supply support to the CP140 Fleet.

What You Will Do:
• Planning and preparation of documentation associated with the procurement and contracting of forecasted requirements in support of the CP 140 Aurora OWSS.

• Maintain efficient inventory control and management of assigned CP140 PAV materials.

• Advise Asset Managers on the procurement and distribution of goods and services necessary to support the fleet.

• Work effectively with parts buyers, Asset Managers, other Supply Chain Analysts, and material support representatives (internal and external) to ensure all assigned CFSS parts bins are responsively replenished to avoid High Priority Requirements (HPRs) and stock-out situations.

• Liaise effectively with Canadian Forces (CF) base/depot supply personnel, and on-site CF representatives.

• Prepare and maintain accurate HPR status reports for Asset Managers and for OWSS program management.

• Management of assigned stock codes and changes to the Procurement Authority list.

• Maintain efficient inventory control and management of assigned materials.

• Review / action / reconcile referred demands and recommended re-order buy requirements.

• Review / action / reorder point and reorder quantity information from the CFSS and adjust as required to ensure CF depot inventory levels for CP140 PAV items are adequate to ensure a high level of mission readiness.

• Carry out investigations to determine causes for repetitive material supply problems and initiate or recommend corrective actions.

• Be responsible for initial cataloguing support, preparing reports on parts replenishment, repair and overhaul and materials disposal.

• Read, understand, comply with, and suggest improvements for all inventory-related company procedures and directives.

• Satisfy customers in a professional manner and perform other functions as required.

What You Will Bring:
• Post-secondary education in Supply Chain Management/Logistics or equivalent experience in a technical or military environment.

• Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMP) or Professional Logistics (P. Log) designation would be beneficial.

• Proficient in MS Office Suite of applications and experience with ERP systems (e.g. JD Edwards, Peoplesoft, etc.)

• Excellent oral and written communication skills.

• Strong organizational ability and an aptitude for working with numbers.

• Proficient analytical skills and the ability to work independently.

• Time management and organizational skills.

• Strong influencing skills and the ability to meet objectives working with colleagues.

• Working knowledge of the Canadian Forces Supply System (CFSS) Defence Resource Management Information System (DRMIS) is preferred.

• Familiarity with the ISO 9000 quality environments.

• Incumbents must be able to pass and maintain Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) and Transport Canada security clearances.

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment policies. Continually focusing on your individual safety and the safety of others who may be affected by your work and to fully comply with all Federal Health and Safety Legislation.

• Participate in Continuous Improvement, Lean & 6S activities in your area.

• All successful applicants must be eligible to meet requirements for the U.S. International Traffic In Arms Regulations (ITAR), Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and Canadian government security clearance.

What We Will Do For You:
• All IMP's benefits become effective on your first day of work, regardless of your position.

• Employees are entitled to 3 paid personal days and 12 statutory holidays per year.

• We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RRSP Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Long Service Awards, Volunteer Grant Program, Scholarship Program, and more!

title: Director, Operational Policy & Market Operations
description:
## Director, Operational Policy & Market Operations
Halifax, NS
TP - IESO - 9311

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with IESO Nova Scotia to recruit a Director, Operational Policy & Market Operations. This is a critical executive leadership role that will shape the rules, systems, and services required to run Nova Scotia's electricity market.

IESO Nova Scotia is an independent not-for-profit organization created by the Province of Nova Scotia to change the way Nova Scotia's electricity system is managed, by assuming responsibility for managing the province's power system in real-time, supporting Nova Scotia's clean energy goals under the province's Clean Power Plan and planning for the province's future energy needs. The organization is guided by operating principles and values that include credibility, transparency, collaboration, independence, innovation, respect, public service, safety and security and reliability for electricity customers.

Role Description
As a member of the Executive Team initially reporting to the CEO, the Director, Operational Policy & Market Operations will play a foundational role in designing and overseeing operational policy, market rules, market services, and settlement processes required for a fair, transparent, and reliable electricity market.

In this role, you will build, lead, and oversee the rulebook, services, and administrative systems that govern Nova Scotia's electricity market. This includes designing operational policies, creating and maintaining market rules and manuals, overseeing settlement and financial calculations, ensuring market transparency, and leading compliance and stakeholder engagement efforts.

This is a highly strategic role that blends policy design, technical expertise, regulatory understanding, and organizational leadership.

Your responsibilities will include:

## Operational Policy & Market Rule Development

• Lead the creation and continuous improvement of operational policies, market rules, and market manuals that support reliable, fair system operations.

• Establish structured processes for rule development, consultation, approvals, and ongoing change management.

• Ensure rules align with regulatory expectations, reliability standards, and the evolving needs of a more renewable grid.

## Market Arrangements & Market Services Design

• Design participant requirements, registration processes, and the administrative frameworks that enable market participation.

• Develop market services that support system reliability and future market evolution.

• Adapt market services and arrangements as Nova Scotia transitions to higher levels of renewable energy.

## Settlement & Market Administration Oversight

• Oversee settlement processes, including charge types, calculation methods, reconciliations, and dispute management.

• Ensure all settlement systems are accurate, auditable, timely, and supported by strong internal controls.

• Lead the development of participant facing administrative processes that ensure fairness and clarity.

## Market Data Transparency & Reporting

• Establish transparent data publication practices, including dashboards, operational reports, and public facing information.

• Ensure data governance frameworks support integrity, confidentiality, and public transparency.

## Compliance, Enforcement & Market Integrity

• Build and oversee compliance and enforcement frameworks related to market rules and operational policies.

• Support investigations, escalation processes, and remediation activities.

• Work closely with Legal and Regulatory Affairs to ensure clarity, enforceability, and alignment with regulatory expectations.

## Stakeholder Engagement & Consultation

• Lead engagement with government, regulators, utilities, market participants, and customers.

• Facilitate consultations, working groups, and technical forums.

• Represent IESO NS as a senior spokesperson on market design, policy, and operational matters.

## Enterprise Leadership & Team Development

• Recruit, build, and lead a new team responsible for policy, market services, and administration.

• Contribute to organizational strategy, operational readiness, and cultural development.

• Champion diversity, equity, inclusion, and Truth & Reconciliation.

## Qualifications

You bring a depth of experience in electricity markets, operational policy, system operations, settlements, or regulatory environments. You thrive in high scrutiny, multi stakeholder settings and have the judgment, communication skills, and collaborative mindset required to design complex policies and build institutional credibility.

The ideal candidate will have:

• Minimum 10 years of experience in electricity markets, system operations, operational policy, market governance, settlements, or related fields.

• Strong knowledge of market rule development, market operations, and policy frameworks, ideally within an ISO/IESO, utility, regulator, or similar environment.

• Experience designing or administering settlement processes and cost allocation methodologies.

• Demonstrated success in stakeholder engagement, consultation, and public facing communication.

• Strategic thinker with strong analytical and governance capabilities.

• Proven ability to lead teams, build new functions, and thrive in environments with evolving mandates.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.

For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Rick Neima, Senior Consultant at 902-488-2534 and rneima@kbrs.ca, or please apply online by clicking the "Apply Now" button below. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

title: Logistics Coordinator
description:
## Job Title: Logistics Coordinator
Location: Bedford, Nova Scotia
TP - ATL - 10007

Meridia Recruitment is excited to partner with Alumitech Ltd. in the search for a Logistics Coordinator to join their Bedford-based team.
Founded in 1991 and proudly headquartered in Bedford, Nova Scotia, Alumitech is a recognized leader in the design, manufacture, and installation of custom-engineered curtain walls, architectural windows, skylights, storefronts, doors, metal cladding, and specialty glass systems. Known for precision, quality, and innovation, Alumitech is the trusted partner for Atlantic Canada's top construction companies, architects, and developers seeking complete building envelope solutions.

Role Description
As the Logistics Coordinator, you will be responsible for managing the flow of materials into and out of Alumitech's Bedford facility. Working closely with suppliers, transportation providers, project teams, and shop personnel, you will help ensure materials arrive on schedule, inventory remains accurate, and shipments are delivered efficiently to project sites and customers.

This newly created role combines logistics coordination, supplier follow-up, inventory management, shipping and receiving, and hands-on material handling responsibilities. Success in the role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to proactively manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. You will serve as a key point of contact for suppliers and freight providers, helping to ensure projects have the materials they need when they need them.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Coordinate inbound shipments from suppliers and track order progress, delivery schedules, and estimated arrival dates.

• Communicate directly with suppliers and transportation partners to ensure materials are delivered in accordance with project requirements and timelines.

• Plan and coordinate freight loads to maximize efficiency, reduce handling, and minimize the risk of damage.

• Receive and inspect inbound shipments, verifying the accuracy, completeness, and condition of materials.

• Investigate and resolve shipment issues, including shortages, damages, backorders, missing items, and supplier claims.

• Maintain and organize warehouse inventory, ensuring inventory transactions and material movements are accurately recorded.

• Coordinate outbound shipments to project sites and customers, including packaging materials and preparing shipping documentation.

• Maintain accurate records of all inbound and outbound shipments and provide regular updates on shipping activity.

• Operate material handling equipment, including forklifts and pallet jacks, as required.

• Support a safe, organized, and efficient warehouse environment.

Your Qualifications
The ideal candidate is organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can shift throughout the day. You enjoy solving problems, following up on details, and taking ownership of processes from start to finish.
Your qualifications include:

• Experience in shipping and receiving, warehousing, inventory control, logistics coordination, or a related field.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Experience tracking orders, coordinating deliveries, and communicating with suppliers or vendors.

• Strong computer skills and comfort working with email, spreadsheets, and inventory systems.

• Ability to work independently and take initiative.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills.

• Valid driver's licence with a clean driving record.

• Ability to safely lift up to 60 lbs when required.

• Commitment to workplace safety and safe material handling practices.

## Assets include:

• Experience in manufacturing, construction, glazing, fabrication, or industrial environments.

• Forklift certification or forklift operating experience.

• Experience operating scissor lifts.

• Experience working with inventory management systems.

• French language skills.

Your cover letter must demonstrate:

• relevant experience working, collaborating or representing organizations, institutions, networks or initiatives within Acadian and Francophone communities;

• practical knowledge of the realities, contemporary issues, institutions and networks regarding Francophonie affairs and Acadia in New Brunswick;

• the ability to apply this experience and knowledge to contribute effectively to the mandate of the City of Dieppe.

## SUMMARY

Reporting to the director responsible for Francophonie affairs, the incumbent provides strategic advice, represents the City at an institutional level, develops partnerships and coordinates municipal projects and initiatives. The incumbent contributes to integrating Francophonie affairs and Acadia priorities into the City's projects, programs and services, while promoting their visibility throughout the Dieppe community and among community partners.

The incumbent engages Acadian and Francophone communities, advises municipal departments and partners, and promotes the integration of Francophonie-related priorities into the City's projects, programs and services. The incumbent contributes to the profile and visibility of Francophonie affairs and Acadia through the development of strategic collaborations, municipal representation and the identification of opportunities that promote French-language vitality.

The scope of the position focuses on municipal directions, partnerships and strategic initiatives, rather than the direct delivery of services, individual intervention, teaching or client support.

## Advisory support and guidance

• Serve as a resource person for municipal departments on Francophonie, Acadia and linguistic vitality issues

• Advise and support departments in integrating practices that promote French-language vitality, active offer and bilingual services

• Contribute to the development of tools, resources and best practices in support of municipal priorities

## Partnerships and consultation

• Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with francophone and Acadian organizations, institutions and partners

• Coordinate consultation mechanisms related to municipal priorities concerning Francophonie affairs and the promotion of Acadia

• Represent the municipality in dealings with partners, networks and relevant bodies

## Promotion and development

• Coordinate activities, projects and initiatives that raise the profile of the Francophonie and Acadia

• Identify opportunities for collaboration, funding or development to support municipal objectives

• Help position the municipality as a dynamic, welcoming and inclusive francophone and Acadian community

• Demonstrated experience collaborating with organizations, institutions, networks or initiatives that support the promotion and vitality of New Brunswick's Francophone and Acadian communities

• Good understanding of the realities of francophone and Acadian communities, ideally in a minority context

• Ability to analyze, exercise judgment and solve problems

• Ability to engage partners and lead working groups, committees or consultation mechanisms

• Ability to establish and maintain collaborative relationships with various internal and external stakeholders

• Ability to communicate information clearly and adapt communications to different audiences

• Ability to work independently, take initiative and carry out assigned tasks in a thorough, highly organized manner

• Ability to handle sensitive or confidential matters with diplomacy, discretion and professionalism

• Ability to work effectively in a dynamic and changing environment

• Compliance with confidentiality and information management rules and policies

## Job Posting: Controller

Company: Prime Material Handling
Reports To: Director of Finance
Location: Dartmouth, NS
Position Type: Full-time, Permanent

## Job Summary

The Controller contributes to the overall success of Prime Material Handling by effectively managing our financial tasks, corporate budgets, and accounting operations. Reporting directly to the Director of Finance, you will maximize return on financial assets by maintaining a strong control environment that ensures compliance with company and legislative policies.

As a growing company, we need a hands-on leader who will manage and mentor an experienced team of three accounting professionals, with a heavy, direct focus on overseeing Accounts Receivable (AR), billing, and cash collections. Beyond team management, you will take ownership of reconciliations, cash flow projections, and budgeting, while partnering with the Director of Finance to provide strategic direction and guidance on key business decisions. This role is a true "player-coach" position-requiring someone who is equally comfortable shaping strategy and rolling up their sleeves to support frontline daily tasks.

## Key Duties and Responsibilities

## Strategic Financial Management & Controller Functions

· Strategy & Guidance: Provide the Management Team with accurate, timely financial data and recommendations to support growth and business decisions.

· Financial Reporting: Develop and maintain timely, accurate monthly financial statements and reports in accordance with GAAP.

· Budgeting & Variance Analysis: Partner with the Director of Finance and department heads (including Parts and Service) to establish annual budgets; deliver clear analysis of actual results vs. budgets.

· Cash Flow Optimization: Develop, manage, and monitor rigorous daily and weekly cash flow forecasting models.

· Compliance & Audits: Ensure all statutory requirements are met; prepare all supporting information for the annual accounting review, CRA, and Workers' Compensation Board.

· Continuous Improvement: Continually leverage available resources to improve operational efficiency across financial, customer, and internal processes.

## Team Leadership & Operational Focus

· Team Management: Supervise and mentor an experienced 3-person accounting team handling day-to-day transaction processing (AR and AP).

· Frontline Support: Demonstrate a genuine willingness to roll up your sleeves and assist the team with daily data entry, customer questions, and high-volume operations depending on the day's needs.

· Payroll Administration: Manage corporate payroll functions to ensure accurate and timely compensation.

## Skills and Qualifications

· Education: Post-Secondary degree in Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.

· Designation: A CPA professional designation is highly valued.

· Technical Skills: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel is strictly required for data manipulation, modeling, and financial analysis.

· Systems Adaptability: Strong technical aptitude with the ability to quickly master and navigate our industry-specific ERP system.

· Experience: 5+ years of progressive corporate accounting experience, including team management and direct exposure to budgeting/forecasting.

· Leadership Style: A flexible, collaborative leader who empowers others, listens to varied perspectives, and stays close to the frontline work rather than focusing solely on high-level delegation.

· Problem Solving: Ability to use complex reasoning, brainstorm creative solutions to immediate operational issues, and translate organizational strategies into actionable plans.

## Working Conditions

• Working in a climate-controlled office environment in Dartmouth, NS.

• Working in a fast-paced, growing business environment.

• Working overtime on occasion to meet month-end or budget deadlines.

Wasoqopa'q First Nation is "welcoming, inclusive and is a multigenerational Mi'kmaw Nation that is unique and successful at protecting its waterways and lands, and values the traditions, people, culture and spirituality, while carefully utilizing its assets and strengths for sustainability, jobs, culture and recreation."

Through community and economic development initiatives, programs and services, Wasoqopa'q First Nation continues to grow, enhancing the social and economic well-being of the Nation.

## Position Overview and Objective

WFN is currently recruiting for an Administrative Assistant, reporting to the Executive Director/Band Manager, responsible for providing supports to the overall functionality of the Medway office, with answering and fielding calls, addressing inquiries, scheduling, organizing events and activities, and maintaining the office budget, continually providing a welcoming environment for employees, WFN members and families and the general public.

• Maintain a monthly and or weekly schedule (calendar board) of all Medway Office employees.

• Assist in the planning and execution of community events, Elder and or youth trips and activities for Queens County members and families.

• Distribute, package, sort lobsters, scallops, moose meat for local WFN members, as required throughout the year.

• Establish and maintain an inventory of office supplies and maintenance of equipment.

• Maintain office accounting (writing cheques and balancing) for all purposes.

• Direct complaints, inquiries, and requests from WFN members to the appropriate person and or department.

• Keep the bulletin board up-to-date posting relevant material, such as job postings, notices, and newsletters.

• Maintain and up-to-date directory of frequently called numbers and addresses (including ALL WFN members in the area).

• Maintain confidentially of all records and files.

• Distribute via mail, email, social media Facebook page, or newsletters, notices to WFN members.

• Support the Health Department in organizing vaccination clinics, as needed.

• Maintain a schedule for VON appointments and client call reminders.

• Coordinate water testing for Medway Reserve residents as per Health Canada guidelines.

• Adhere to all Wasoqopa'q First Nation (WFN) Policies, Procedures, and necessary procedures, as required.

• Working in a team environment, other duties, training, and activities, as required.

## Qualifications

• Diploma in Office Administration or related field from a recognized institution and or equivalent experience.

• At least 1-year in working with the public in a customer service and/or office environment.

• Knowledge and experience working in a Mi'kmaw community is considered an asset.

• An understanding of Mi'kmaq culture and traditions is considered an asset.

• Demonstrated computer skills, e.g., Word, Excel, etc.

• Criminal Record/Vulnerable Sector Check and Child Abuse Registry Check are required upon hiring.

Submit Cover Letter and Resume to resumes@wasoqopaq.ca

WFN appreciates the interest of all applicants, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. WFN does not assume candidate expenses related to this recruitment process.

title: Site Controller
description:
## The Opportunity

This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast paced and growing environment in a key leadership role. The Site Controller reports to the General Manager and is a key member of the Red Shores Executive Team. The Site Controller is directly responsible for the Red Shores Audit and Shipping & receiving teams. This position will interact significantly with ALC Finance and Procurement teams.

The Site Controller is responsible for leading the day-to-day financial accounting, reporting, controls, and compliance functions for Red Shores Racetrack and Casino. This position ensures the accuracy, integrity, and timeliness of financial information while supporting operational decision-making across gaming, racing, food and beverage, facilities, and administrative business areas.

They play a key role in maintaining strong internal controls, safeguarding organizational assets, supporting audits, meeting regulatory and corporate reporting requirements, and providing budget leadership, forecasting, trend analysis, investment oversight, and financial insight that contributes to the ongoing success of the organization.

## Responsibilities:

• Oversee the preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, management reports, reconciliations, and supporting schedules.

• Maintain the general ledger and ensure accounting records are accurate, complete, and aligned with applicable accounting standards and corporate policies.

• Review financial results, investigate variances, and provide timely analysis and recommendations to management.

• Ensure accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, banking, cash management, and fixed asset records are processed accurately and on schedule.

• Leverage financial and operational data to proactively identify emerging risks and opportunities, provide strategic recommendations, and influence decisions that strengthen financial performance, optimize operations, and support organizational growth.

• Develop, maintain, and monitor internal control procedures that safeguard cash, gaming revenues, assets, records, and confidential information.

• Support internal and external audits by coordinating documentation, responding to inquiries, and implementing approved recommendations.

• Lead and coordinate the annual budgeting process in partnership with finance leadership and departmental managers, ensuring operating and capital budgets are accurate, realistic, and aligned with organizational priorities.

• Develop and maintain financial forecasts, rolling projections, and scenario analyses to support operational planning, labour planning, cash flow management, procurement planning, capital planning, and performance monitoring.

• Strengthening financial literacy and accountability across the organization by partnering with department leaders and managers to improve their understanding of financial results, budgets, forecasts, key performance indicators, cost drivers, and business performance.

• Lead, coach, and support finance team members by setting clear expectations, promoting accountability, and encouraging continuous improvement.

## Experience & Qualifications:

• Minimum 7 - 10 years Controller or senior level accounting experience.

• Post secondary degree or diploma in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related discipline.

• Charted Professional Accountant designation (CPA) or equivalent.

• Progressive experience in accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, budgeting, forecasting, trend analysis, investment analysis, capital planning, and audit coordination.

• Experience in gaming, hospitality, entertainment, or another highly regulated environment considered a strong asset.

description:

## Closing date:

Emergency Medical Care Inc. (EMC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS) that manages and operates ground ambulance, air medical transport and the medical communications operations in Nova Scotia through a performance-based contract with the provincial government's Emergency Health Services (EHS) Operations division and the Department of Health and Wellness. As well, EMC operates TeleHealth/811 medical communications for Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island for the Department of Health.

We access all communities in Nova Scotia in a timely and efficient manner with our fleet of more than 180 ambulances and support vehicles operating out of 60+ stations. We respond to 165,000+ calls annually across the province, which are actively managed through the EHS Operations Medical Communications Centre, the hub of all emergency (911) and non-emergency (hospital transfers) medical calls.

The EHS Operations LifeFlight program provides even greater accessibility by responding to patients on scene or through inter-facility transports by our critical care team via helicopter, fixed wing, or ground ambulance.

In addition, paramedics in Nova Scotia participate in various programs both urban and rural such as community-based paramedic programs, collaborative emergency centres, and emergency preparedness and special operations, to name a few.

There are lots of opportunities waiting for you in Nova Scotia. Apply now to learn more about our service and available positions.

## NATURE AND SCOPE:

Reporting to the SST Fleet Supervisor, the System Support Vehicle Transporter (Runner) is a key part of the System Support Team that provides vehicle movement pertaining to system vehicle repair, maintenance and other duties as assigned.

Responsible for ensuring operational readiness by safely transporting ambulances and system vehicles between fleet centers and stations. This role supports emergency service delivery through vehicle movement, readiness checks, and logistics support. It contributes directly to fleet availability, efficiency, and reliable frontline operations.

As a casual position, there are no scheduled hours, transporters are called in as necessary.

As an employee of EMC, we are accountable to our patients and coworkers by participating in and supporting all safety related initiatives, as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture that focuses on patient safety and a safe workplace.

## Duties & Responsibilities

The position entails, but is not limited to the following:

• Transport vehicles/equipment safely and efficiently between locations

• Conduct pre-trip inspections, cleaning, and readiness checks

• Ensure vehicles are washed down of heavy road debris upon delivery if required.

• Report vehicle defects or safety issues.

• Always interact professionally with EMC and EHS stakeholders.

• Support logistics including deliveries and special projects

• Communicate with internal teams and vendors

• Operate all system and company vehicles in accordance with Nova Scotia laws as well as all applicable policies and procedures and Safe Work Practices of EMC and EHS.

## Qualifications & Requirements:

• High school diploma or equivalent

• Retain a Nova Scotia Class 4 Driver's License/Obtain during 1st year

• 1-2 years driving or fleet-related experience preferred

• Ability to work, day, night, evening shifts including weekends

• Experience in operational or logistics environments is an asset

• First Aid an asset

• Effective oral and written communication skills.

• Displays good decision-making skills and takes initiative

## Knowledge & Skills:

• Strong time management and organizational skills

• Basic mechanical awareness

• Attention to detail and safety focus

• Effective oral and communication skills

• Ability to work independently and adapt to changing priorities

• Proficient in the use of computers and standard software applications

• Extended periods of driving, as well as frequent entry and exit from vehicles.

• Irregular work schedules

• Lifting and carrying within safe limits

• Exposure to varying weather conditions, including heat, cold, rain, snow, and ice.

Responsibilities include:

description:

TP - EFL - 8941

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is proud to partner with Emera Newfoundland & Labrador (Emera NL) in the search for a Senior Electrical Engineer to join their team. Emera NL is the owner and operator of the Maritime Link, one of Atlantic Canada's most complex and sophisticated electricity assets, enabling the interconnection between Newfoundland & Labrador and Nova Scotia through a high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system.

As a small, technically driven organization within the Emera family, Emera NL operates with a strong owner mindset. The team is lean, collaborative, and deeply invested in the long-term performance of its assets. This role offers a unique opportunity for an experienced electrical engineer to play a hands-on technical leadership role, gain deep exposure to HVDC systems, and help shape the future asset strategy of a nationally significant transmission link.

## Role Description:

As Senior Electrical Engineer, you will serve as the technical authority for Emera NL's HVDC transmission asset. Reporting to the Director of Engineering, you will provide electrical engineering leadership across operations, asset management, inspections, maintenance planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. The role goes well beyond traditional design work, as you will be relied upon to troubleshoot complex issues, work directly with operations and site teams, and help ensure the system continues to operate safely, efficiently, and reliably for decades to come.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Serving as the internal technical expert for the Maritime Link HVDC system, including transmission assets, converter stations, and control systems.

• Reviewing and interpreting vendor documentation, technical studies, reports, and operating procedures.

• Leading inspection strategies, condition assessments, and long-term maintenance planning as OEM support contracts wind down.

• Developing and maintaining risk-based asset management plans to ensure long-term reliability and performance.

• Supporting outage planning and execution, including participation in the annual planned outage and post-outage analysis.

• Working closely with operations teams to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues, providing sound judgement during abnormal or emergency conditions.

• Supporting protection, control, and automation activities in a controls-intensive operating environment.

• Collaborating with internal stakeholders, external contractors, OEMs, and consultants on ongoing operations and future initiatives.

• Contributing engineering input to capital planning, reliability improvements, and potential new infrastructure opportunities.

• Maintaining and enhancing engineering standards, documentation, and technical processes.

• Building internal technical capability and act as a trusted advisor within a lean, ownership-driven team.

• Participating in specialized training and industry forums, including international HVDC user conferences.

## Ideal Qualifications:

• Degree in Electrical Engineering with P.Eng. designation or eligibility for registration in Newfoundland & Labrador.

• Strong background in electrical power systems, ideally within utility operations, transmission, protection & controls, automation, or other complex industrial environments.

• Experience supporting operating assets, with a practical understanding of how systems perform in real-world, operational conditions.

• Comfortable working across disciplines, including controls, protection, automation, and systems integration.

• Exposure to HVDC systems is considered an asset; however, a strong electrical foundation is more important, and training will be provided for the right individual.

• Practical, solutions-oriented engineer with an ownership mindset and the ability to remain calm under pressure.

• Strong communicator who works effectively within a small, highly collaborative team.

• Motivated to build long-term technical depth in a unique and highly specialized power system environment.

## Why This Role Stands Out:

• Run a truly unique, complex asset that plays a vital role in Atlantic Canada's power system.

• Become a recognized HVDC expert through hands-on experience and global training opportunities.

• Work in a lean team where engineering judgement matters and your contributions are visible.

• Enjoy meaningful technical autonomy while being supported by experienced leaders and partners.

The Cherubini Group of Companies (Cherubini) is a Dartmouth-based leader in steel fabrication, widely recognized for delivering complex bridges, buildings, and infrastructure projects. As one of Canada's Best Managed Companies, Cherubini brings more than fifty years of expertise, modern fabrication facilities, and an unwavering commitment to quality, innovation, and safety. The organization plays a vital role in transportation, industrial, and renewable energy projects across Atlantic Canada and beyond.

## Role Description

The Project Manager is responsible for the technical, financial, and operational management of projects from contract award through completion. This role requires a thorough understanding of contractual and technical requirements and serves as the primary point of contact for clients. The Project Manager attends project meetings as required, leads internal coordination efforts, and builds strong, long-term customer relationships to ensure successful project outcomes.

## Your responsibilities will include:

Safety - Champion Cherubini's Safety Program by actively promoting the health and well-being of yourself and others in the office, on site, and in the shop. Lead by example and reinforce safety as a core value in all project activities.

Finance - Develop and manage project budgets based on estimates and oversee all fiscal aspects of projects from start to finish. Prepare financial reports as required. Manage contract changes, including cost and schedule impacts. Prepare progress billings, support collections as needed, issue purchasing requisitions, and approve invoices in accordance with budget and authorization levels.

Technical - Maintain a strong working knowledge of both contractual and technical project requirements. Oversee the preparation and review of shop drawings and erection plans. Review design documentation, prepare and submit requests for information, ensure timely follow-up, and issue clear work packages to the shop floor.

Leadership - Build and maintain strong customer relationships to support repeat business, reduce risk, and improve operational efficiency. Provide guidance and mentorship to Project Coordinators. Conduct regular visits to the shop and project sites to monitor progress and address issues proactively. Track and manage project status from initiation through closeout.

Administration - Prepare comprehensive technical and financial project debriefs. Solicit, evaluate, and coordinate sub-trade bids and supplier quotations for labour, materials, and equipment. Manage purchasing activities to ensure materials and services meet project specifications, schedules, and budget requirements.

## Your Qualifications

We are looking for a proactive and adaptable project management professional who can lead projects from planning through completion in a dynamic construction environment. The ideal candidate thrives in collaborative settings, building strong relationships with internal teams, clients, and vendors. Exceptional communication, organization, and problem-solving skills are essential, along with the ability to make informed decisions, manage competing priorities, and guide teams effectively. • Prior experience in steel fabrication is a strong asset.

• Post-secondary degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or equivalent technical training

• Strong knowledge of contracts, drawings, specifications, construction methods, and materials

• Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills

• Experience using web-based project management and collaboration tools to plan, manage, and track work.

• Knowledge of safety programs, regulatory requirements, and the Nova Scotia OH&S Act.

This is an opportunity to lead high-impact projects with one of Atlantic Canada's most respected structural steel fabricators. Position Overview:
The Production Supervisor position is a leadership position within a "Product" structured organization of the Fixed Wing and Rotary Wing programs. Production Supervisors are members of a dedicated team of multiple disciplined supervisor's whose roles are to lead teams of core employees augmented with additional employees as production requirements dictate. In particular, the Production Supervisor is charged with the progress of the aircraft production activities within established performance objectives and maintaining the well-being and development of their assigned employees.

What You Will Do:
• Responsible for the day to day management and performance of their employees.

• They are expected to lead, manage and carry out duties in accordance with Company policies, procedures, rules, and directives, and apply the same expectations to all IMP employees.

• Oversee the execution of staged work by drawing upon the available resource skills, disciplines and authorizations in order to complete the work in the most efficient manner possible.

• Participate in the staging of work and the identification and resolution of constraints. Responsible for productivity reports and to initiate action to correct errors.

• Enforce the requirement of strict clocking accuracy in terms of Cost, WIP management and AMO compliance.

• In compliance with the employees development plans, Production Foremen are expected to progress their employees to becoming qualified and authorized in their designated disciplines at the annual development rates set forth by the VP Production.

• Perform personnel and general administrative duties including preparation of performance appraisals, probation and training reports, maintenance of vacation/overtime. Etc.

• Ensure their employees receive regular objective and progress updates in relation to production plans, and employee development goals.

• Achieve the "No Fail Tasks and Priorities" that are set each year by their Production Director.

• Exercise due diligence in Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) related issues and promptly escalate in accordance with OHS policies and procedures.

• Other duties as required.

title: Manager, Finance Technology
description:
Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, South America and Australia. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

Cooke is continuing to mature its digital strategy through stronger demand capture, sharper business case discipline, and clearer accountability between business outcomes and technology delivery. As the Manager, Finance Technology, you lead the technology agenda for our Finance and Accounting functions turning finance priorities into a focused capability roadmap and delivery plan, and ensuring digital initiatives deliver measurable value across the core finance and accounting processes that keep the business running, anchored by record-to-report.

## The Role

As Manager, Finance Technology, you own both the near-term (typically 12-month) technology roadmap for Finance and Accounting and the delivery of that roadmap operating within Cooke's enterprise IT governance, architecture, and delivery frameworks. Finance and Accounting spans general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, treasury, tax, and financial planning & analysis. You translate finance priorities into sequenced, executable initiatives, define scope and success criteria, and lead the team that delivers capability-specific technology work. Delivery is coordinated through the Project Manager and within approved plans; you resolve domain-specific delivery issues, and you escalate risks, cross-capability trade-offs, and decisions beyond your authority through governance.

You partner closely with the Finance leadership team as your primary business stakeholders, the Digital Strategy Analyst, Solution Architect, Project Manager and Business Systems Analyst aligned to your capability areas. Enterprise Architecture governs technical standards and patterns and the PMO governs delivery. You report to the Director, Business Technology.

## Key Responsibilities:

## Team Leadership & Delivery Management

• Lead and develop the delivery team assigned to Finance Technology (e.g., Business Systems Analysts and Project Managers), with potential to scale as the portfolio grows

• Conduct regular 1:1s, set objectives, manage performance, and own development planning for your team

• Prioritize work, manage day-to-day execution decisions, and ensure quality, compliance, and timely delivery against defined standards and commitments

• Coordinate domain-specific resources and resolve delivery issues through the Project Manager, within approved plans

• Coach team members, build a learning culture, and mentor future team leads

## Finance & Accounting Capability Roadmap

• Own and maintain a 12-month technology roadmap for Finance and Accounting, aligned to enterprise sequencing set by the Director, Business Technology

• Translate finance and accounting priorities into sequenced, executable initiatives with measurable outcomes

• Define scope, constraints, and success criteria for initiatives within the capability

• Drive continuous improvement and capability maturity across finance and accounting processes - record-to-report (R2R), plus the finance side of procure-to-pay (accounts payable) and order-to-cash (billing, accounts receivable, and collections) that Finance shares with Procurement and Sales & Marketing

## Business Stakeholder Engagement

• Act as the primary technology partner for Finance and Accounting leaders, building trust and surfacing needs, pain points, and emerging demand into the intake process

• Represent the finance domain in intake triage, prioritization, and governance discussions

• Ensure requirements are clearly linked to business outcomes and that stakeholders are aligned on the baseline

## Initiative Quality & Business Case Discipline

• Ensure each initiative has a clear problem statement, a validated business case, a measurable objective, and a named business sponsor

• Support ROI validation and confirm scope, success criteria, and product fit before initiatives are submitted for prioritization or contract

• Provide inputs to budgeting and forecasting for the finance technology portfolio

## Delivery Readiness, Handoff & Benefits

• Confirm initiatives entering delivery have validated requirements, funded scope, and clear ownership, and provide a clean transition to implementation and then support

• Stay engaged through delivery to validate readiness, sign off on business outcomes, and support benefits realization

## Governance, Escalation & Decision-Making

• Participate in intake, architecture, and stage-gate reviews for initiatives impacting Finance and Accounting

• Provide clear recommendations and decisions within your authority and within agreed governance timelines

• Escalate cross-capability trade-offs and decisions beyond your authority through PMO or enterprise governance

• Remain accountable for delivery outcomes once initiatives are approved

## What Success Looks Like

• Finance and Accounting leaders have a clear, current, and trusted technology roadmap

• Initiatives entering delivery are well-framed, well-scoped, and ready for execution

• Core finance and accounting processes (record-to-report, and the finance side of procure-to-pay and order-to-cash) are measurably more efficient and better supported by technology over time

• The team is high-performing, well-developed, and operating to CookeIT standards

• The domain delivers measurable business outcomes, not just shipped projects

## Core Skills & Capabilities

• People leadership and coaching - able to lead, develop, and get results through a team

• Governance and quality assurance across delivery processes, frameworks, and standards

• Strong organizational, prioritization, and delivery management skills

• Stakeholder management and communication with finance and IT audiences

• Ability to translate strategy into team execution and connect initiatives to business outcomes

• Business case structuring, ROI validation, and outcome-based framing

• Understanding of IT financial management concepts (e.g., TBM taxonomy, cost categorization) is an asset

## Finance & Accounting Technology (Assets)

• Familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365 F&O) or Business Central would be an asset

• Familiarity with industry-standard finance processes - record-to-report (R2R), and the finance components of procure-to-pay and order-to-cash - would be an asset

• Understanding of core accounting and finance functions: general ledger, AP/AR, month-end and period-end close, consolidations, treasury, tax, and FP&A

• Awareness of finance data, reporting, and analytics needs (e.g., Power BI) and how they connect to ERP and master data

• Awareness of finance controls, audit, and compliance considerations

## Behaviors That Drive Success

• Adaptability - Anticipates change, guides the team through transitions, and adjusts plans to maintain momentum

• Collaboration & Synergy - Leads collaboration across functions; resolves conflicts constructively

• Outcome Driven - Sets stretch goals and ensures team alignment to business outcomes

• Growth Mindset - Builds a learning culture within the team and mentors others

• Business Acumen - Applies business insight to improve processes and make informed decisions

• Decisiveness - Makes timely, data-informed decisions within scope

• Digital Acumen - Applies digital insight to improve work quality and the finance user experience

• Political Savviness - Builds credibility and influence across departments

## Experience & Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Business, IT, Finance, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience)

• 5-8 years in IT or business roles, including 2-3 years in a supervisory or team lead capacity

• Demonstrated experience delivering technology for finance, accounting, or a comparable corporate function

• Experience leading BSAs and/or PMs and operating within a structured delivery and governance model

• Familiarity with capability-based planning, business case discipline, and vendor scope shaping

• Experience with project/portfolio management and reporting tools (e.g., Monday.com, MS Project) and governance frameworks

• Familiarity with D365 F&O or Business Central, and with finance processes such as record-to-report, an asset

• Comfortable engaging finance leadership and translating their priorities into technology outcomes

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

## Benefits Package:

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• Support Services: Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Time Off: Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave for work-life balance.

• Wellness: Wellness programs and access to on-site gym facilities (available in some locations).

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

• Convenience: On-site parking or parking allowance.

If you're looking to join a supportive team environment with opportunities for personal and professional development, apply now and become part of our dynamic team.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness, and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

NOTE: The recruiter is reviewing and interviewing eligible applicants for this position as they are received. If you are interested in this posting, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

• Energized by our company values!

• Comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans and access to e-health care

Not only are we passionate about nurturing a thriving technology sector here in Atlantic Canada, but we are also committed to solving technology challenges that will make an impact worldwide. title: Geology Co-Op Student
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking Geology Co-op Students to join our Geology team in Sudbury, Ontario.

This is a 4 to 16 month fixed term position starting in January 2027 or May 2027. Please be clear in your application which start date you are looking for.

As a Geology Co-op Student, you will provide geological service and be expected to travel underground and get exposed to beat geology work, including grade control practices, mapping, and mineability and dilution services to the mine operations. The student will also get exposure to core logging, including QAQC and geotechnical logging, and possible exposure to drill layout creation.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Attend and participate in daily safety line up meetings, and monthly safety meetings and required safety training.

• Communicate changes in ore interpretation to diamond drill geologists.

• Identify, analyze and recommend opportunities for safety, productivity and cost improvements.

• Current schedule is 5 days per week Monday to Friday 6:30am-3:00pm (excluding recognized holidays).

•

## About You

## Education:

• Currently enrolled in a Geology or Geological Engineering undergraduate program.

## Skills:

• Must be physically capable of handling 300'-500' of diamond drill core per day.

• Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 products; Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation.

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth.

• Online training and career development opportunities.

• Opportunities to build your network and lots of fun!

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses.

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are needed for the green economy. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Pay Grade: Student

Minimum Starting Salary: $23.75-$29.75

Apply by: October 15, 2026

title: Senior Specialist - Indigenous Health
description:
Title: Senior Specialist - Indigenous Health

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior Indigenous Health Specialist provides specialized Indigenous health and clinical expertise to support the planning, development and delivery of Health in Emergencies services within the Canadian Red Cross.
Working collaboratively with First Nations, Inuit and Métis Peoples, Indigenous Nations and communities, Indigenous leadership and organizations, health professionals, emergency management teams and partners, the Senior Specialist brings an Indigenous lens to public health, clinical services and emergency programming. The role supports culturally safe, respectful and responsive services that reflect Indigenous determinants of health, Indigenous knowledges, community priorities and relevant Indigenous rights frameworks.

The Senior Specialist also supports knowledge translation, health communication, relationship building, research and continuous improvement, helping teams apply clinical, public health and Indigenous health knowledge effectively across preparedness, response and recovery activities.

## In this role, you will:

• Provide Indigenous health and clinical subject-matter expertise to support the planning, development, implementation and evaluation of Health in Emergencies services.

• Contribute Indigenous health perspectives to preparedness, response, recovery and longer-term health programming, including clinical, public health and emergency management initiatives.

• Build and maintain respectful, reciprocal relationships with First Nations, Inuit and Métis Peoples, Indigenous Nations and communities, Indigenous leadership, health organizations and other partners.

• Engage with Indigenous communities and leadership to ensure programs and services reflect community-identified priorities, local context, Indigenous knowledges and culturally safe practices.

• Apply clinical and public health knowledge to support health assessments, service planning, continuity of care, health-needs analysis and appropriate referral/navigation pathways during emergencies.

• Develop and support knowledge translation and health communication approaches that make complex clinical, public health and emergency information accessible and relevant to diverse audiences.

• Facilitate reciprocal knowledge exchange between Indigenous communities, health professionals and emergency and humanitarian systems.

• Conduct research, environmental scans, assessments and analysis to inform program design, decision-making, monitoring and evaluation.

• Develop and contribute to learning resources, guidance, tools, briefings and other knowledge products that strengthen culturally safe practice across the Canadian Red Cross.

• Provide expert advice on Indigenous health, cultural safety, Indigenous rights, communication and community context to interdisciplinary teams, operational leaders and health professionals.

• Identify and support mitigation of cultural, communication, relational, clinical and operational risks that may affect program or service delivery.

• Represent Indigenous Health in internal and external working groups, partnerships and knowledge-sharing initiatives, and contribute to continuous improvement across Health in Emergencies.

## What we are looking for:

• Post-secondary education in a regulated health profession, health sciences, nursing, public health, medicine, dietetics, midwifery, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, pharmacy, paramedicine or another relevant clinical health profession is considered an asset.

• 6-9 years of relevant experience in Indigenous health, clinical services, public health, community health, health promotion or emergency health programming.

• Clinical experience in a healthcare, community health, public health or emergency health environment, with the ability to apply clinical knowledge to health service planning and delivery.

• Demonstrated experience working with First Nations, Inuit and/or Métis Peoples, Nations, communities, organizations or health systems in Canada.

• Strong understanding of Indigenous approaches to health and wellbeing, including the importance of community, culture, family, land, language and spirituality.

• Understanding of the impacts of colonization, systemic racism and jurisdictional barriers on Indigenous health and access to healthcare.

• Knowledge of cultural safety, cultural humility and Indigenous rights and health frameworks, including the Truth and Reconciliation Commission Calls to Action and the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.

• Demonstrated ability to work respectfully across Indigenous and Western health knowledge systems.

• Strong relationship-building, facilitation, communication, clinical reasoning and interdisciplinary collaboration skills.

• Demonstrated ability to translate complex clinical, public health or emergency information for different audiences and contexts.

• Ability to work effectively in complex, rapidly changing and high-pressure environments.

• Proficiency with standard computer applications and the ability to support research, analysis, reporting and knowledge-management activities.

## Working Conditions:

• The role includes fieldwork, deployment to emergency operations, and office-based work during non-deployment periods.

• Domestic or international travel to unsafe or high-stress environments; exposure to major adverse conditions requiring personal safety management.

• Work requires the ability to work to multiple, business critical, and conflicting deadlines.

• Work requires interactions in difficult, emotionally charged situations.

• Work requires interactions and support to clients who are experiencing traumatic situations.

• Field deployments may involve working in unstable environments with limited access to basic services, often in emergency and/or epidemic contexts. These settings require strict adherence to security protocols.

• Candidates must be medically cleared for travel in accordance with established Canadian Red Cross medical criteria, where applicable.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

title: Pricing Manager
description:
Pricing Manager

Designated office:

Eastlink

6080 Young Street

Halifax, NS

This position is:

On-site - working all 5 days per week in the Office

Our Revenue Management team is seeking a commercially minded and analytically strong Pricing Manager to lead the development and execution of pricing strategies across our Home Services portfolio (Internet, TV, and Home Phone). This role is ideal for a business or finance professional looking to become a key partner to Product, Sales, Marketing, and Finance. You will shape pricing decisions that balance revenue growth, margin, and customer value. You’ll also ensure we remain competitive in a fast-moving market.

What You'll Do

Drive Pricing Strategy, Revenue Management & Execution

• Lead end-to-end pricing strategy for all home services, including acquisition, retention, promotional, and in-market offers

• Optimize price structures to improve revenue growth, margin, customer lifetime value, and market competitiveness

• Evaluate trade-offs between growth, profitability, churn, and customer value using strong financial discipline

• Develop customer acquisition and loyalty pricing strategies that balance compelling market offers with sustainable commercial outcomes

Deliver Market & Financial Insights

• Analyze competitive trends, customer behavior, and regional performance

• Translate complex data into clear, actionable recommendations for leadership

• Identify risks and opportunities to enhance pricing effectiveness and market position

Partner Across the Business

• Collaborate with Product Management, Sales, Marketing, and Finance to align pricing with go-to-market and financial targets

• Act as a trusted advisor, influencing decisions that impact revenue, growth, and retention

Financial & Analytical Leadership

• Build models to assess pricing scenarios, elasticity, revenue impact, and profitability

• Track performance through KPIs and continuously refine pricing strategies

• Present insights in a clear, executive-ready format

What You Bring

• Degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field (MBA, CPA, CFA considered an asset)

• Experience in pricing, commercial finance, FP&A, or strategy, ideally in telecom, subscription-based services, or competitive consumer markets

• Strong financial modeling and analytical skills (revenue, margin, churn)

• Ability to turn data into practical, commercially sound recommendations

• Excellent communication skills and confidence working with senior leaders

• A collaborative, proactive mindset with strong business judgment

About Eastlink

Eastlink is proudly family-owned and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. After more than 50 years, we’ve grown from a small-town startup into one of Canada’s Best Managed companies without losing our entrepreneurial edge. We move fast. We try new things. We care about doing right by our customers, and we’re not afraid to take a different approach to make that happen.

Why Work With Us

We could say we’re not your typical telecom, but what makes us different is how we operate day to day. At Eastlink, we’re a tight-knit team all working toward common goals. We’re big enough to do meaningful work, but small enough that you can actually make your mark. You won’t get stuck waiting for layers of approval or years of tenure to make an impact! We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. And just like we invest in our network, we invest in you, with intention and for the long run.

We’re committed to building a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We embrace diversity, inclusion, equity, and accessibility throughout all levels of the organization and encourage members of equity groups to self-identify during the application process.

If you're looking for a place where you can grow your healthcare career while building a healthy, well-rounded life, look no further. A diverse range of opportunities in diagnostics, therapeutics and technical positions are available for qualified health professionals right now.

Working for Horizon gives you flexibility in your career, an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers. At Horizon, a rewarding opportunity is as close as the ocean!

Horizon is an equal opportunity employer that values and recognizes your contributions, is dedicated to patient safety and satisfaction, has competitive pay and benefits, and offers many opportunities for professional growth. With short commutes, the warmest ocean waters in Canada, and a rich and colourful cultural experience, New Brunswick is truly Canada's hidden gem. Situated on the Atlantic coast, the province boasts stunning landscapes ranging from pristine beaches to dense forests, providing endless opportunities for outdoor recreation such as hiking, camping, fishing, skiing and more.

Horizon is Atlantic Canada's second largest health authority servicing over a half a million people. We operate 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities, health care centres, clinics, and offices throughout New Brunswick. We offer services in both rural and urban areas.

Our people are the heart of our organization. We have more than 14,000 dedicated employees working with over 1,000 physicians, and play a major role in research, education, innovation and health and wellness.

title: Principal Engineer, Underground Mineral Reserves
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing? Who We AreWe are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future. With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia. Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals. Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career. The OpportunityWe are currently seeking a Principal Engineer, Underground Mineral Reserves to join our Mineral reserves team in Sudbury or Toronto, Ontario. This is a permanent position. As a Principal Engineer you will play a pivotal role in the development, estimation, and reporting of mineral reserves for Vale Base Metals. This position requires advising technical teams, ensuring compliance with industry standards, and providing strategic guidance to optimize resource extraction and management. The role involves overseeing MRMR governance, coordinating technical assurance programs, managing risks, and maintaining a secure database for mineral resources and reserves. The advisor also leads MRMR activities, assists in internal and external audits, and ensures accurate and compliant reporting, which has significant implications for the company's value and reputation In this position you will:
• Work closely with internal stakeholders to support Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves (MRMR) governance, reporting, and disclosure. Develop and maintain standardized internal reporting policies and processes, ensuring transparency and compliance with internal and external regulations.

• Coordinate the Technical Assurance program to review MRMR, identifying and communicating risks and opportunities. Conduct and facilitate internal and external MRMR audits to ensure compliance with established processes and procedures.

• Establish and enforce mining and MRMR standards and guidelines across operations and projects. Develop, maintain, and communicate guidelines and standards for mineral reserve and resource estimation and reporting.

• Manage the full set of risks associated with mineral resources and reserves. Maintain Resource Management risk registers for Base Metals using technical, regulatory, and short-term cash flow criteria.

• Provide expert technical input and reviews for reserve evaluation, reports, and project assessments. Oversee impairment and value-added analysis as part of the technical review activity. Act as a senior review assurance provider for mining and reserve estimation.

• Lead and provide strategic direction for MRMR activities, including setting business expectations and processes for the estimation, reporting, and disclosure of mineral resources and reserves. Align MRMR activities with the company's business objectives and long-term goals.

• Oversee the compilation, updating, and communication of consolidated mineral inventory, resource, and reserve estimates, including associated risks and opportunities. Assist to prepare and certify the annual Corporate MRMR Statement and validate mineral reserve estimates for inclusion in the Vale annual 20F filing.

• Oversee Vale Base Metals' central secure database for Mineral Resources and Reserves, ensuring data integrity, security, and accessibility for accurate reporting and strategic planning.

• Oversee the preparation and review of technical report summaries for each of Vale Base Metals operations, ensuring accuracy and compliance with industry standards.

• Approve and provide input into public and third-party disclosures related to Vale Base Metals mineral resource and reserve estimates.

• Review technical procedures impacting mineral reserve, resource, and exploration target estimation and reporting, recommending changes and best practices where appropriate

About You Education:
• Bachelor degree in Mining

• P. Eng (Canada) or CREA (Brazil)

Experience:
• 15+ years of post P.Eng experience

Skills
• Deep understanding of mining engineering principles and practices, with focus in underground operations and preferred experience in open pit operations.

• Familiarity with different types of commodities and mining settings, enhancing adaptability and expertise.

• Ability to act as a Qualified Person for mineral reserve and resources reporting (Cu, Ni and polymetallic mineralization)., ensuring compliance with regulatory standards.

• Knowledge of relevant regulations such as S-K 1300, NI 43-101, and standards such as CRIRSCO and CIM, ensuring adherence to industry norms.

• Demonstrated ability to accurately estimate and report mineral reserves, contributing to reliable and transparent disclosures.

• Ability to analyze complex data, identify issues, and develop effective solutions.

• Capability to lead teams, provide strategic direction, and align MRMR activities with business objectives.

• Proficiency in conveying technical information clearly and training team members effectively.

• Commitment to accuracy, thoroughness, and ethical conduct in all aspects of the role.

• Ability to adjust to changing industry conditions and requirements, maintaining effectiveness in a dynamic environment.

• Strong ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams, fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

• Expertise in coordinating technical assurance programs and managing risks associated with mineral resources and reserves.

• Skills in managing secure databases for MRMR, ensuring data integrity and accessibility.

• Experience in approving and providing input into public and third-party disclosures related to mineral resource and reserve estimates.

What We Offer You

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are needed for the green economy. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard.
