title: Horizon Communications Team General Application
description:
## Join Horizon Health Network's Communications and Marketing Team

Are you a storyteller at heart with a passion for strategic communications and/or marketing? Are you looking for meaningful work that allows you to make a real difference in the lives of New Brunswickers?

Horizon's Communications and Marketing portfolio is looking for talented and enthusiastic professionals to join our growing and fast-paced team!

If you're a communications and/or marketing professional who is energized by collaboration, motivated by purpose, and thrive on bringing clarity to complex issues, this is the opportunity you've been waiting for.

## About Us

The Communications team is responsible for internal and external strategic communications, digital channels, and media relations.

The Marketing team is responsible for brand management, campaigns, social media, creative services (design and videography), and translation services.

Together, we tell the stories of how Horizon staff, physicians, volunteers and patients, clients and family members are working to improve health care in our province and help ensure New Brunswickers have the information they need about their health care services.

Our team members have meaningful influence with health care leaders within Horizon, helping guide the organization through complex and challenging situations involving various internal and external stakeholders.

## About Our Opportunities

We're looking to meet with experienced communications and marketing professionals with a passion for sharing positive stories on numerous platforms with engaged and diverse audiences.

We have opportunities that will allow you to gain experience and expertise in a multitude of communications and marketing channels and work with health care providers, leadership and support personnel from across our organization.

Our work is fast-paced and rewarding, and every day on the job is different!

Working at Horizon provides you with a compensation package that is more than a base salary. You will be part of the public service, which provides access to health and dental, government pension, sick time, and vacation time, starting at three (3) weeks. Living outside the province? We offer a relocation allowance of up to $5,000.

## What You'll Do:

As a member of our collaborative team, you'll:

• Contribute to the planning and delivery of strategic communications and marketing projects that support Horizon's goals.

• Develop content and assets across multiple channels and formats, aligned with audience needs and Horizon's goals and brand standards.

• Collaborate with colleagues, leaders, and partners to deliver innovative, people-centred communication and marketing strategies.

• Manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment where no two days are the same.

• Help bring Horizon's stories to life – stories of innovation, care, research and the people behind them.

## What We're Looking For:

We're not looking for a perfect fit – we're looking for the right fit. If you bring some of the following skills and experience, we want to hear from you:

• Strategic thinker with at least 1 year of experience in communications, marketing, creative services, digital channels or a related field.

• Strong storytelling and content development skills, which may include writing, visual, digital, or multimedia formats, with a keen eye for detail and accuracy.

• Ability to juggle competing priorities and meet tight deadlines with professionalism and creativity.

• Experience using a wide range of tools, platforms, and channels, including digital, social media.

• Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills – a team player who thrives in a collaborative environment.

• Self-starter who takes initiative, follows through, and gets things done.

## Nice-to-haves

• Experience in health care, public sector, or a complex organization.

• Exposure to issues management, crisis response, or high-profile, time-sensitive work.

• Familiarity with analytics, performance measurement, and reporting related to communications, marketing or digital channels.

## Why Join Horizon?

Because what we do matters. As one of the largest health care organizations in Atlantic Canada, our communications team plays a critical role in informing, engaging and inspiring our communities, patients, staff and partners.

You'll join a highly supportive team that values creativity, collaboration and compassion, all while contributing to something bigger than yourself.

Ready to Apply?
Even if you're not sure you check every box – apply anyway. We want to hear from you.

Let's start a conversation.

Apply today and help shape the future of health care communications in New Brunswick.

## Diversity Statement

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care.

title: Electrical & Instrumentation Engineer
description:
Job Title: Electrical & Instrumentation Engineer
Location: Port Hawkesbury, NS
TP - AML - 9889

Port Hawkesbury Paper is Cape Breton's largest industrial employer and a leading manufacturer of paper products distributed across North America. Operating a large-scale, continuously running manufacturing facility, the company relies on a wide range of electrical, instrumentation, controls, and automation systems to support safe, efficient, and reliable production. Its operation combines modern automation technologies with established industrial equipment, creating an environment where engineers are involved in everything from day-to-day troubleshooting and reliability improvements to equipment modernization and capital projects.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with Port Hawkesbury Paper to recruit an Electrical & Instrumentation Engineer to join their team in Port Hawkesbury, Nova Scotia.

This is an opportunity to work closely with operations and maintenance teams in a highly integrated manufacturing environment, supporting critical production assets while contributing to system upgrades, process improvements, and long-term reliability initiatives.

Role Description
The Electrical & Instrumentation Engineer is a key technical resource within the Paper Machine Department, providing engineering support to Operations and Maintenance teams. Working closely with operators, electricians, instrumentation technicians, and maintenance personnel, you will troubleshoot electrical, instrumentation, controls, and automation systems while supporting the safe and reliable operation of critical production equipment. The successful candidate will help address equipment obsolescence, improve system performance, and support the ongoing evolution of a complex manufacturing operation.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Provide electrical and instrumentation engineering support to Operations and Maintenance teams.

• Participate in daily operations and maintenance meetings to support production and reliability objectives.

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, reliability, and operational performance

• Troubleshoot electrical, instrumentation, controls, and automation issues affecting equipment performance.

• Support PLC, VFD, instrumentation, control, and process automation systems.

• Collaborate with operators, electricians, instrumentation technicians, and maintenance personnel to resolve technical issues.

• Identify equipment obsolescence risks and support upgrade and modernization initiatives.

• Develop and implement solutions that improve reliability, performance, and operational efficiency.

• Support capital and maintenance projects as a technical lead or subject matter expert.

• Assist with project planning, equipment upgrades, and system improvement initiatives.

• Work with vendors, contractors, and external engineering resources on electrical and instrumentation projects.

• Participate in an on-call rotation and provide occasional after-hours support as required.

Your Qualifications
You are a hands-on engineering professional who enjoys solving technical problems, working closely with operations teams, and building practical solutions in an industrial environment. You are proactive, collaborative, and motivated to continuously develop your technical expertise. Recent graduates through to candidates with several years of relevant industrial experience are encouraged to apply.

Your qualifications include:
Recent graduates through to candidates with several years of relevant industrial experience are encouraged to apply.

• Degree in Electrical Engineering, Instrumentation Engineering, or a related discipline; Electrical Engineering Technology qualifications may also be considered.

• Engineer-in-Training (EIT) or Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation is an asset but not required.

• Commitment to workplace safety and continuous improvement.

• Exposure to industrial electrical systems, instrumentation, controls, automation, or manufacturing environments is preferred.

• Understanding of PLCs, VFDs, industrial controls, and process automation systems.

• Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities.

• Ability to work collaboratively with operations, maintenance, and technical teams.

• Self-motivated and curious, with a strong desire to learn, take initiative, and assume ownership of projects and challenges.

Why Join Port Hawkesbury Paper?
Port Hawkesbury Paper offers a unique opportunity to work within one of Atlantic Canada's most technically advanced industrial operations. Engineers gain exposure to complex electrical, instrumentation, controls, automation, reliability, and capital improvement initiatives while working alongside experienced operations and maintenance teams.

## Port Hawkesbury Paper offers:

• Exposure to large-scale, highly automated industrial equipment and systems

• Opportunities to work with electrical, instrumentation, controls, automation, and reliability initiatives

• Hands-on involvement in modernization and equipment upgrade projects

• Significant learning and professional development opportunities

• Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits

• Extended health and disability coverage

• Pension plan with a 5% employer contribution/matching program

• A strong commitment to safety, innovation, and continuous improvement

description:
## Faculty - Aviation

## Education

## Ivany Campus

## Dartmouth, Nova Scotia

## Applied Innovation and Technology

Three (3) Continuing Full-time Positions (one position in Mechanical, one position in Structures and one position in Avionics): Commencing approximately October 26, 2026

## Application deadline is 11:59PM, October 10, 2026

## Competition No. 2627-178

From Industry Expert to Instructor - Help Train the Next Generation of Skilled Aircraft Maintenance Engineers

Are you an experienced Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME) looking for a new challenge; one that keeps you connected to the work you love, while offering more balance, stability, and long-term security?

At Nova Scotia Community College, you can take the knowledge and experience you've built in industry and use it to mentor the next generation of AMEs, all while enjoying predictable hours, excellent benefits, and a career that's easier on the body.

**Secondment opportunities may be available, subject to approval from your current employer. This can be an excellent option for those interested in gaining teaching experience or exploring a new professional pathway while maintaining their existing employment and salary. If you are interested in exploring secondment options, please contact Jaclynn at jaclynn.kelly@nscc.ca.**

## Why Make the Move to Teaching?

This is an opportunity to stay hands-on in the trade without the physical demands, long shifts, emergency callouts, or unpredictable schedules that often come with industry work.

As a Faculty member with NSCC, you'll enjoy:

• The opportunity to share your industry expertise and help shape the next generation of AMEs

• Meaningful work that makes a lasting impact on students, industry, and communities

• A supportive team environment focused on collaboration, mentorship, and continuous learning

• The ability to stay connected to your trade while transitioning into teaching

• Predictable work hours that support work-life balance

• A stable and rewarding career in education with opportunities for professional growth

• Support and training to help transition successfully into teaching

Whether you're looking to slow down physically, spend more time with family, take your work experience in a new direction, or transition into a rewarding second phase of your career, this role offers the chance to do all of that while remaining deeply connected to the AME community.

Qualifications
We're seeking experienced tradespeople who are passionate about the industry and interested in helping others succeed.

Ideal candidates will have:

• Valid Transport Canada Aircraft Maintenance Engineers (AME) License: M1 or M2 or equivalent, AME-E and/or AME-S.

• A minimum of five years (full-time equivalent) of recent occupational experience.

• Clear understanding of Manufacturer's and Regulatory Documentation (CARS 566), including SRM, Service Bulletins, Engineering Drawings, etc.

• Comfortable using computer applications such as the Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

• A commitment to safety, mentorship, and lifelong learning

Previous teaching experience or related experience in the delivery of educational program or training adults would be an asset, but not required. If you've coached apprentices, trained coworkers, or shared your knowledge on the shop floor, you already have valuable experience to build on.

NOTE: Two years of your training will be counted towards the educational requirements and cannot be included as part of your occupational experience.

## Compensation & Benefits

The salary scale for NSCC Faculty is based on steps that range from $81,760.18 - $104,267.58 annually.

In addition to salary, NSCC offers:

• A defined benefit pension plan to support long-term financial security

• Comprehensive health and dental coverage, including vision, paramedical services, life insurance, Employee Family Assistance Program (EFAP), and more

• Up to 45+ days of paid vacation and recognized holidays, including paid time off between Christmas and New Year's

• Professional development and training opportunities to support ongoing learning and career growth

## Make an Impact

The aviation industry need experienced professionals willing to pass on their knowledge. This is your opportunity to shape the future of industry while building a healthier, more balanced future for yourself.

If you're ready to bring your experience into the classroom and help develop the next generation of AMEs, we'd love to hear from you.

Responsibilities
As part of the Applied Innovation & Technology faculty team in the Aircraft Maintenance Technology/Aircraft Maintenance Technician programs, you will:

• Deliver theoretical and hands on practical shop training along with classroom instruction

• Share real-life industry knowledge and troubleshooting experience

• Mentor and support students entering the trade

• Help students build the skills employers are looking for

• Promote and ensure health and safety practices and procedures are consistently followed in classrooms, shops, and labs

• Work collaboratively with fellow instructors and industry partners

• Stay current with evolving technology and industry practices

• Participate in student advising, curriculum development, program promotion, committee work, and work placement support

• You may also coordinate the aviation hangar and lab operations by setting up/taking down and maintaining the organization of the hangar and labs and its materials, equipment, and inventory

This role combines shop instruction with modern teaching tools and blended learning approaches, including in-class, online, and off-site instruction, as well as occasional evening and weekend sessions.

As a condition of employment, you are required to provide proof of a valid AME licence, prior to your start date.

As a condition of employment, Faculty at NSCC must complete a part-time adult education program delivered by NSCC. This adult education program is a significant investment on the part of NSCC in the learning and development of new employees. To achieve regular status, all probationary, full or part-time Faculty of the College must successfully complete the program within their probationary period. Term full-time Faculty whose term appointment is twelve or more months are also required to participate in this program.

Candidates selected for interviews will be expected to provide at least three recent occupational references. The successful candidate will be expected to provide official transcripts to show proof of academic achievements.

NSCC is committed to the full inclusion of all applicants. As part of this commitment, NSCC will ensure that applicants are provided reasonable accommodations, as required. If accommodation is needed to participate in the job application process, please contact Jaclynn Kelly, HR & Talent Consultant at jaclynn.kelly@nscc.ca. Our Employee Workplace Accommodation Policy can be found here: Employee Workplace Accommodations Policy | NSCC

title: Senior Manager, Marketing & Communications
description:
The Chalmers Foundation is seeking an experienced marketing and communications professional to lead the Foundation's marketing and communications function as Senior Manager, Marketing & Communications.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Senior Manager plays an important leadership role in strengthening the Foundation's reputation, community presence, donor engagement and fundraising success.

This is a broad marketing and communications leadership role. It requires someone who can understand organizational objectives, audiences, and community context; determine how the Foundation should communicate; and translate that strategy into relevant and effective content and campaigns.

The successful candidate will lead the Foundation's marketing and communications strategy, including brand, digital and social media, content, media relations, marketing analytics, and campaign communications. They will work closely with philanthropy and program teams, provide leadership to the Marketing Coordinator, and direct the Foundation's relationship with its external creative agency.

## The opportunity

At the Chalmers Foundation, marketing and communications are closely integrated with philanthropy.

Our work involves telling the stories of donors, healthcare professionals, patients, programs, and healthcare needs across our region. It requires understanding what our audiences need and want to hear, identifying the right stories and channels, and communicating the impact of philanthropy in ways that are credible, relevant, and engaging.

We are therefore looking for someone who brings strategic marketing judgment as well as strong execution capability.

The successful candidate will be expected to challenge assumptions when appropriate, make informed recommendations, use data to improve decisions, and help determine where the Foundation should focus its marketing resources.

## Key responsibilities

The Senior Manager will:

• Develop and lead the Foundation's integrated marketing and communications strategy, annual plan, priorities, budget and KPIs.

• Lead content and audience strategy across social media, digital channels, email, web, print, media and Foundation events.

• Guide the Foundation's social media and digital presence, ensuring content remains relevant to audiences and responsive to changing trends.

• Provide stewardship of the Chalmers Foundation brand and ensure consistency across public and donor communications.

• Work closely with philanthropy and program teams to develop marketing strategies supporting fundraising, stewardship, programs and community engagement.

• Use marketing, digital, social media, website and campaign data to identify insights and recommend changes.

• Lead media relations, news releases and significant public communications.

• Maintain effective communications relationships with Horizon Health Network and other healthcare and community stakeholders.

• Provide leadership, coaching and direction to the Marketing Coordinator.

• Direct the Foundation's relationship with its external creative agency and other marketing partners.

• Develop clear strategic briefs and provide informed direction and feedback on creative work.

• Support executive communications, including presentations, speaking notes and key messages as required.

• Represent the Foundation at appropriate donor, healthcare, community and networking activities.

• Manage marketing expenditures and ensure resources are aligned with organizational priorities.

## The person we are looking for

You will ideally have seven or more years of progressively responsible marketing, communications, or public relations experience.

More important than the number of years is the breadth of your experience.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

Our team is seeking an Advanced Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics and Ambulance Operators/Attendants. We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or Ambulance Operator/Attendant as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) for a period of one year, with possibility of extension.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine. The base for this service is located at Springdale Ambulance Base, Springdale

Duties/Job Demands:
The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will provide assistance to the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

Job Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;
• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.
• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.
• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

Qualifications:
• Graduation from High School or equivalent;
• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;
• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;
• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director
• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;
• Current certification in Basic Life Support;
• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);
• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)
• Effective oral and written communication skills;
• Critical and sound decision making skills;
• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;
• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.
• A satisfactory record of work performance is required;
• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

Salary:
• Advanced Care Paramedic - CG-37 of the NAPE HS salary scale $35.42 to $39.58 per hour
• Primary Care Paramedic – CG-29 of the NAPE HS salary scale $27.07 to $30.07 per hour
• Ambulance Operator/Attendant – CG-25 of the NAPE HS salary scale $23.78 to $26.19 per hour
• Applicable Labrador Allowance.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

title: Anatomical Pathologist
description:
Horizon Health Network is seeking a full-time Anatomical Pathologist to join the Department of Laboratory Medicine at Saint John Regional Hospital, the principal tertiary-care referral centre for southern New Brunswick and Atlantic Canada's leading centre for advanced care.

The successful candidate will join a collegial group of pathologists providing comprehensive diagnostic services to Saint John and the surrounding region. Saint John Regional Hospital is a major teaching hospital affiliated with Dalhousie University Medical School and supports undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, research, and quality improvement initiatives.

The Department of Laboratory Medicine provides a full range of anatomical pathology services, processing a diverse and complex spectrum of surgical pathology, cytopathology, and autopsy specimens from a tertiary-care referral population across southern New Brunswick. The department is supported by a state-of-the-art Molecular Diagnostics and Cytogenetics Program that delivers comprehensive testing across solid tumor oncology, hematologic malignancies, and inherited (germline) disorders.

While all qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, preference will be given to candidates with fellowship training and/or significant experience in one or more of the following areas:

• Renal Pathology

• Neuropathology

• Molecular Pathology

Candidates with expertise that complements existing departmental strengths and supports future program development are particularly encouraged to apply.

## Why you should work here

New Brunswick offers a safe and welcoming community with a relaxed lifestyle and a true work-life balance, enriched by its diverse Indigenous, Anglophone, and Francophone heritage.

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

Saint John is a vibrant coastal city located on the Bay of Fundy, offering an exceptional quality of life, affordable housing, excellent schools, outdoor recreation, and convenient access to Atlantic Canada's natural attractions. The city combines the amenities of an urban centre with the lifestyle advantages of a smaller community.

## Incentives & Remuneration

This position offers highly competitive remuneration for the position is based on New Brunswick Medicare's Alternate Funding Plan (AFP).

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Urban recruitment incentive of $50,000.00 with a 2-year return of service.

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

## What you will do

The physician will work collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team, adhere to evidence-based practices aligned with Horizon Health Network's mission.

• Provide diagnostic anatomical pathology services, including surgical pathology and intraoperative consultation

• Participate in subspecialty sign-out and multidisciplinary case conferences

• Contribute to quality assurance, accreditation, and laboratory improvement initiatives

• Participate in medical education for students, residents, and fellows

• Engage in clinical research and scholarly activities as desired

• Share in departmental on-call responsibilities

(Note: These responsibilities are the basic and prime duties associated with this position; other related and allied duties may be assigned from time to time as may be necessary to the operation of Horizon Health Network.)

## Who you are

Applicants must:

• Hold an MD degree (or equivalent)

• Be certified in Anatomical Pathology by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (or equivalent acceptable credentials)

• Be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick

• Demonstrate excellence in diagnostic surgical pathology

• Possess strong communication and teamwork skills

• Be committed to teaching, quality assurance, and continuous professional development

The physician must also meet continuing education requirements, adhere to departmental and health authority policies, comply with relevant legislation, and follow professional ethical standards set by regulatory bodies.

title: Nurse Practitioner (.5 FTE)
description:
Permanent Part Time
Nurse Practitioner (.5 FTE)

Saint Vincent's Nursing Home is an accredited not-for-profit home in the heart of Halifax, NS. We are a resident and family-centred community caring for each other. We are currently accepting applications for a part time Nurse Practitioner working 40 hours bi-weekly, day shift only.

The Nurse Practitioner (NP) partners with and complements other members of the health care team for the achievement of resident and family-centred care for long term care residents living with specialized and complex needs. The NP will have responsibility for one unit and will support other units as required. The NP provides clinical leadership for the Medical & Therapeutics Committee and integrates current scientific knowledge in geriatrics and best practice guidelines in decision-making based on critical appraisal and application of literature and research findings. The NP is an integral member of the team and collaborates with the Medical Director and unit physicians.

The ideal candidate will act as a resource, preceptor and mentor for nurses, students and other team members and will work with the interdisciplinary care team to develop and deliver services to residents.

The NP adheres to the Nova Scotia College of Nursing (NSCN) standards for Nursing Practice and Code of Ethics and is accountable for their own practice consistent with relevant legislation, professional and ethical standards.

## Qualifications / Education / Experience

• Master of Nursing: Advanced Nursing Practice stream or equivalent NP program,

• Current (or pending) registration as a Nurse Practitioner with CRNNS - Family/All Ages,

• Current BCLS Certification,

• Recent relevant experience working in a NP role within Long Term Care preferred.

## Required Skills:

• Assessment and Intervention: clinical/diagnostic reasoning, care planning, case management, evaluation of client self-care and related outcomes coupled with nursing care,

• Communication: builds positive and open relationships with residents, families, community partners, team members, and other professionals using verbal, written and electronic means,

• Critical Thinking: clinical judgment and problem-solving with the ability to integrate and evaluate pertinent data sources to problem-solve effectively within scope of practice,

• Resident and Family-Centered Practice: strong ethical standards and a commitment to professional development and life-long learning. Promotion of care for and with residents and significant others. Sensitive to client advocacy and social justice concerns,

• Teaching: ability to transmit information grounded in behavior change and principles of self-management intended to instruct residents and others about topics essential for health care and well-being. Application of innovative education and counselling technologies and strategies,

• Time and Resource Management: implementing activities to promote cooperation among relevant others, collaboration across disciplines and related activities,

• Leadership: promotes staff morale, cooperation, assertiveness and risk-taking, creative planning for change and innovation, implementation of policies or other protocols, and ongoing professional development,

• Language Competencies: ability to work with others to deliver care in other languages is an asset,

• Technology Literacy: experience with Microsoft Office and electronic health records,

• Attendance: must have the ability to maintain regular and consistent attendance.

## Salary & Benefits

We offer competitive salary and benefits, continuing education opportunities and flexible hours of work.

title: System Safety Engineer
description:
Job Title: System Safety Engineer
Location: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
TP - PPL- 10087

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with GeoSpectrum Technologies in search of a System Safety Engineer to join their growing team based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Founded in 1994, GeoSpectrum Technologies has built a strong reputation for designing and manufacturing advanced underwater acoustic systems and components used in the maritime surveillance, ocean science, defence, and energy sectors. Known for their innovation and collaborative culture, GeoSpectrum delivers highly customized, reliable technology solutions while fostering a workplace built on technical excellence, employee engagement, and continuous growth.

Role Description:
The System Safety Engineer serves as a key member of GeoSpectrum's Integrated Program Teams, acting as the focal point for system safety across complex development programs. This role leads and facilitates system safety activities to ensure risks are systematically identified, assessed, mitigated, and managed throughout the program lifecycle, from concept and design through testing, trials, and final delivery.

Working closely with multidisciplinary teams and subject matter experts, the System Safety Engineer leads System Safety Working Groups (SSWG), facilitates hazard analysis activities, and develops safety documentation in support of internal processes and customer requirements. The successful candidate will play a key role in shaping safety cases, supporting safe system design, and driving the continuous improvement of GeoSpectrum's system safety practices.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Act as Program Safety Manager within Integrated Program Teams, leading safety activities across the full program lifecycle.

• Facilitate System Safety Working Groups (SSWG) and collaborate with technical subject matter experts to identify, assess, and mitigate hazards.

• Lead and support Preliminary Hazard Analyses (PHA), Functional Hazard Analyses (FHA), Sub-System Hazard Analyses (SSHA), and other safety assessments.

• Develop and maintain safety documentation in accordance with internal processes, customer requirements, and applicable industry standards.

• Partner with Systems Engineers and product teams to define safety requirements and support verification and validation activities.

• Track hazards, mitigations, residual risks, and safety requirement verification activities throughout program execution.

• Support testing, field trials, and operational activities through hazard identification, risk assessment, and safety planning.

• Develop safety cases and supporting documentation for unique testing and operational scenarios.

• Contribute to the continuous improvement of GeoSpectrum's system safety processes, procedures, tools, and methodologies.

• Champion safety best practices and support the evolution of the organization's approach to System Safety Engineering.

Your Qualifications:
The ideal candidate is a collaborative and analytical engineering professional with experience identifying, assessing, and mitigating hazards within complex systems, processes, or operational environments. You are comfortable facilitating technical discussions, working with subject matter experts, and guiding cross-functional teams through safety and risk assessments.

## Key qualifications include:

• Post-secondary education in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Systems, Chemical, or a related discipline) or equivalent career experience.

• Experience conducting hazard analyses, risk assessments, or safety engineering activities within complex technical environments.

• Experience working with complex integrated systems across electrical, mechanical, software, and controls domains.

• Strong understanding of system safety principles, hazard analysis methodologies, and safety management frameworks.

• Demonstrated ability to facilitate technical discussions and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and subject matter experts.

• Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively in both technical and non-technical environments.

## Assets include:

• Experience with MIL-STD-882 and related system safety processes.

• Experience leading System Safety Working Groups (SSWG), safety reviews, or hazard analysis sessions.

• Experience as a Program Safety Manager or in a similar system safety role.

• Experience developing safety cases and supporting test or trial activities.

• Experience within defence, aerospace, marine, industrial, energy, or other highly regulated environments.

• Background in process safety, reliability engineering, or related disciplines.

title: Aircraft Structures Technician (AME - S or Military Equivalent)
description:
Requisition ID: 2612

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence's Canadian Search and Rescue Helicopter program has provided all aspects of support to Canada's fleet of Cormorant Search and Rescue (SAR) CH-149 helicopters for over twenty years. Operating from across Canada at three Main Operating Bases, Gander NL, Greenwood, NS, and Comox, BC and headquartered in the Cormorant Support Centre in Halifax, NS, the program provides comprehensive, turnkey In-Service Support to Canada's Cormorant helicopters. This unique program provides the RCAF with a full suite of all levels of support to this critical 24/7/365 mission.

Position Overview:
Perform First, Second and Third Level maintenance on aircraft mechanical, structural and electrical systems and components. This will include, but not be limited to, the servicing, inspection, removal, cleaning, repair, installation, adjustment, testing and certification (release) of aircraft mechanical, structural, avionic and electrical systems and components and ground support equipment.

What You Will Do:
• Perform structural inspections, repair, and maintenance procedures in support of both the line maintenance and scheduled maintenance teams.

• Complete aircraft maintenance documentation for the electronic record keeping system (ERKS).

• Perform aircraft release (ARA) when assigned, and trained, qualified and authorized.

• Ramp duties will include, but not be limited to, pre/post flight inspection and support, marshalling, parking, towing, fueling/defueling and installation/removal of required mission equipment and crash and emergency technical response.

• Perform ground runs of engines and auxiliary power units, where trained, qualified and authorised.

• Fly as necessary in support of maintenance, ferry and deployed operations.

• Deploy and work at other main operating bases and/or deploy in support of operations at remote sites, mobile repair parties and ferry flights.

• Work shift work, as required and/or assigned.

• Provide on-job-training to other employees, including task supervision.

• Attend training for trade and professional development and for qualification/certification purposes.

• Remove all debris accumulated by tasks performed and maintain a clean, safe work area. Carry out foreign object debris (FOD) inspections.

• Ensure hangar, shop, stores and office areas are clean and swept.

• Adhere to policies, procedures and directives established by the Company.

• Perform other tasks as may be required from time to time.

What You Will Bring:
• A minimum of 3 years experience in helicopter maintenance is required.

• Thorough knowledge of aircraft structures and structural components, inspection techniques, damage assessment, aircraft materials and hardware, use of special tools and equipment

• Ability to operate test equipment in support of aircraft maintenance.

• Knowledge of Electronic Record Keeping System (ERKS) procedures.

• Knowledge of Quality Systems.

• Knowledge of corrosion control techniques.

• Capable of reading and interpreting technical documentation such as maintenance manuals, work packages, drawings, blueprints and Standard Plant Procedures.

• Capable of performing Non-destructive Inspection, where trained, qualified and authorized.

• Ability to use standard computer programs and such specialized ones as may be necessary in the performances of the duties.

• Possess and maintain a valid driver s license to operate company vehicles and tow tractors.

• Graduate of a recognized aircraft maintenance course or apprenticeship program and hold a current Aircraft Maintenance Engineers license or be qualified as an aircraft aviation technician within the Canadian Armed Forces or equivalent commercial experience.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), and Secret Level II Security Clearance through PSPC- Contract Security Program.

title: Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME M1/M2 or Military equivalent)
description:
Requisition ID: 554

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence's Canadian Search and Rescue Helicopter program has provided all aspects of support to Canada's fleet of Cormorant Search and Rescue (SAR) CH-149 helicopters for over twenty years. Operating from across Canada at three Main Operating Bases, Gander NL, Greenwood, NS, and Comox, BC and headquartered in the Cormorant Support Centre in Halifax, NS, the program provides comprehensive, turnkey In-Service Support to Canada's Cormorant helicopters. This unique program provides the RCAF with a full suite of all levels of support to this critical 24/7/365 mission.

Position Overview:
The Aircraft Maintenance Engineer performs first and second line aircraft maintenance on the Cormorant Helicopter in support of our Canadian Search and Rescue operations. Duties include servicing, inspection, removal, cleaning, repair, installation, adjustment, flight testing and certification (release) of aircraft mechanical, structural and electrical systems and components and ground support equipment.

What You Will Do:
• Perform First and Second Level maintenance on aircraft mechanical, structural and electrical systems and components, and ground support equipment.

• Ramp duties will include but not be limited to pre/post flight inspection and support, marshalling, parking, towing, fueling/defueling and installation/removal of required mission equipment and crash and salvage response.

• Perform ground runs of auxiliary power units, where qualified and authorized.

• Fly as necessary in support of maintenance, ferry and deployment operations

• Travel and work at other main operating bases, deployments in support of operations at remote sites, mobile repair parties and ferry flights.

• Provide on-the-job-training to other employees.

• Attend training for trade and personnel development and for qualifications, recertification, and authorization purposes.

• Sweep and clean hangar, shop, stores and office areas, remove all debris accumulated by tasks performed and maintain a clean, safe work area.

• Adhere to policies, procedures and directives established by the Company.

• Provide supervision to other employees.

• Perform other tasks as may be required from time to time.

What You Will Bring:
• Graduate of a recognized aircraft maintenance course or apprenticeship program and hold a current Aircraft Maintenance Engineers license or be qualified as an aircraft aviation technician within the Canadian Armed Forces or equivalent commercial experience.

• A minimum of 3 years' experience in aviation maintenance is required.

• Thorough knowledge of aircraft systems, including, but not limited to, power plants, flight controls, dynamic systems, hydraulics, pneumatics, environmental, basic structures and power generation and distribution systems.

• Knowledge of use of special tools and equipment.

• Knowledge of corrosion control techniques.

• Capable of reading and interpreting technical documentation such as maintenance manuals, work packages, drawings, blueprints and Standard Plant Procedures.

• Capable of performing Non-destructive Inspection.

• Ability to use standard computer programs and such specialized ones as may be necessary in the performances of the duties.

• Valid Class 5 Drivers License, with the ability to drive vehicles, tow tractors and support vehicles.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), and Secret Level II Security Clearance through PSPC- Contract Security Program.

• Ensuring that orders leaving the kitchen are correct and accounted for in the Point of Sale system.

• Maintain a favorable working relationship with all other company employees and guests to foster and promote a working environment that maximizes morale, productivity and efficiency.

• 2 years experience as a cook

• Advanced knowledge of culinary techniques.

• Current knowledge of safe food handling requirements.

• Successful completion of a Culinary Diploma or Certification Program including Red Seal.

## Work Conditions:

title: Women's Counsellor (Relief/Casual)
description:
Bryony House is seeking a Relief or Casual Women's Counsellors to join our team and play an important role in supporting women and children experiencing intimate partner violence. If you are passionate about crisis intervention, trauma-informed support, and have a flexible schedule, we would love to hear from you.

We are currently hiring for both relief and casual positions:

• Relief: Relief staff are unionized and are eligible for an hourly wage of between $30.52 - $38.27/hour. Relief staff are the first to be scheduled in advance for vacation coverage and are on call first for emergency shift coverage. Hours of work can include days, evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays. Relief staff can be mandated to work certain shifts if there is no other casual coverage available.

• Casual: Casual staff are non-unionized and are eligible for an hourly wage of $29.50/hour. Casuals are scheduled if no other relief staff are available. Casual staff are not mandated to work if there is no other coverage available, it is based purely on their availability.

Neither position are guaranteed hours. Please specify in your application which role type you are interested in being considered for.

Qualifications
• Undergraduate degree in Social Work, Community Studies, Psychology, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

• Current First Aid, NVCI, and CPR certification.

• Experience and knowledge of working with women and children who have experienced violence and trauma.

• Demonstrated knowledge of crisis intervention and de-escalation strategies.

• Experience supporting individuals who use drugs and/or are in recovery from addiction.

• Experience supporting individuals living with mental illness and the impacts of trauma.

• Proven dependability, reliability, and professionalism in an employment setting.

• Demonstrated ability to manage workplace conflict professionally.

• Basic proficiency with Google Workspace and willingness to learn HIFIS case management software.

Responsibilities
Reporting to the Shelter Manager, the Women's Counsellor is responsible for providing crisis intervention, supportive counselling, advocacy, and shelter support services for women and children affected by intimate partner violence. Specific responsibilities include:

• Provide crisis intervention and support, safety planning and case management to residents.

• Advocate for clients and assist with referrals to community services and resources.

• Support women and children throughout their stay in shelter using a trauma-informed approach.

• Answer the 24-hour distress and crisis line and provide immediate support to callers.

• Complete intake assessments for women and children entering the shelter.

• Assist with household duties, and tasks to ensure the needs of the house and residents are met.

• Maintain accurate case documentation and statistics using organizational systems.

• Work collaboratively with colleagues while upholding organizational values and promoting a respectful workplace.

This role provides the right candidate with the opportunity to work with an amazing team of people dedicated to providing women and children a safe haven away from violence. If this sounds like the right fit for you, we'd love to hear from you!

Bryony House is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities.

Bryony House is an equal opportunity employer and a Unionized work environment: Public Service Alliance of Canada Local #80022.

The Continuing Care Assistant (CCA) is accountable to the residents' for providing quality care. They work under the direction of the Neighbourhood Manager and RN/LPN nursing staff. As a part of a multidisciplinary team the CCA meets the needs of the resident, while working within their scope of employment and within the framework, policies and objectives as set out by Tideview Terrace and the Department of Seniors and Long-Term Care.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Required:

· Approved Continuing Care Assistant Certification as per Department of Seniors and Long-Term Care.

· Medication module

· Active participation in learning opportunities of the Eden Alternative and organization

· Demonstrated ability to work as a team player in an Eden Alternative environment.

· Demonstrated commitment to excellence in resident centered care.

· The ability to balance tasks with residents' needs.

· Actively promotes activities that are meaningful to the residents' needs.

· Demonstrated interest in building resident relationships with a commitment in obtaining simple pleasures along with an active involvement to achieve simple pleasures.

· Adaptable, responsible and takes initiative.

· Excellent written and verbal communication skills and excellent interpersonal skills

· Must be able to perform duties that involve lifting, bending, and stretching and meet the overall physical and cognitive demands of the job.

· Outstanding work history inclusive of good attendance, demonstrated availability to work, available to work all shifts, weekends and holidays, and willingness to work all units in current and past employment.

Please submit application via this link: https://jbtmz.me/s/?e=4vddYpr2

Tideview Terrace is an EDEN Registered facility dedicated to eliminating the plagues of loneliness, helplessness, and boredom of our residents.

Creating Homes Where Life is Worth Living http://www.edenalt.org/

The Eden Alternative shows how companionship, the opportunity to give meaningful care to other living things, and the variety and spontaneity that mark an enlivened environment, can succeed where pills and therapies often fail. Places that have adopted the Eden Alternative typically are filled with plants, animals, and are regularly visited by children.

The Eden Alternative is also about changing the culture of long-term care organizations. The departmentalized, task-orientation of the current institutional model has created a culture that is characterized by pessimism, cynicism and stinginess. By moving away from the top-down bureaucratic approach to management and moving decision making closer to the Elders, Edenizing organizations are helping to support a meaningful life for their Elders.

The Advanced Care Paramedic works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. • Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Oncology Physician
description:
Imagine a playground in Atlantic Canada surrounded by fresh waterways on one side and the ocean on the other. Come live and belong to a community where families can raise their children in a safe, close-knit environment with a reasonable cost of living.

Horizon Health Network is seeking Oncology Physicians to join our collaborative teams in beautiful New Brunswick, Canada!

## Why you should work here

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

New Brunswick offers a safe, welcoming community and a relaxed lifestyle enriched by its Indigenous, Anglophone, and Francophone heritage. Whether by the ocean, a river, or a lake, you'll find an ideal place to call home—complete with short commutes, plenty of recreation, and space to enjoy with family and pets. At Horizon, you'll build a meaningful career that makes a difference while embracing the desirable East Coast lifestyle.

## Incentives & Remuneration

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Urban recruitment incentive of $50,000.00 with a return of service or Rural recruitment incentive of $100,000 with a return of service

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

Remuneration will be determined in accordance with the specific role and practice location. Additional details will be shared as the recruitment process progresses.

## What you will do

The Oncology Physician will join a well-established team of oncologists at one of our facilities. This full-time position offers an opportunity to provide high-quality, comprehensive medical care, with opportunities to participate in subspecialty activities catering to the applicant's interest. Opportunities and responsibilities may include:

• Provide high-quality care for patients with a range of oncological conditions across inpatient, outpatient, and emergency settings

• Collaborate closely with referring physicians and multidisciplinary care teams to ensure coordinated oncology care

• Participate in departmental quality improvement initiatives and service development

• Contribute to teaching, academic activities, and mentorship of medical learners

• Support the ongoing advancement of oncology services in New Brunswick.

## Who you are

• Medical degree from a recognized institution.

• Certification in Medical Oncology with the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (FRCPC) or equivalent.

• Candidates must be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of New Brunswick.

• Proficiency in English is required. Bilingual skills would be considered an asset.

• Interest in academic practice, teaching, or subspecialisation in oncology is considered an asset.

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care

## Interested? Apply Today!

If you have questions and/or to apply, please email physiciancareers@horizonnb.ca with the subject "Application for Oncology"

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). ASSISTANT REGIONAL DIRECTOR
Open Competition
