The Chaleur Library Regional Office provides administrative support to 12 public libraries within the Chaleur Library Region, as part of the New Brunswick Public Library Service. As a regional office, it serves the libraries located in the Restigouche and Gloucester counties of New Brunswick.

THE POSITION:
As the Assistant Regional Director, you will take part in the development, communication, and implementation of regional and provincial vision, as well as strategic and operational plans. You will be responsible for hiring, training, supervising, and evaluating managers of all small libraries in the region. You will also be responsible for the development and implementation of sound management practices. You will assume key responsibilities within the region in the absence of the Regional Director.

As Assistant Regional Director, you are a member of the Regional Management Team. In that role, you will be a key support in developing service in the region by coordinating provincial and regional programs and projects in your areas of responsibility; coordinating and supervising the development of library automation at the regional level; taking part in a variety of provincial, regional and community committees; assisting in the analysis of staff training needs and in the planning of appropriate training to meet them; assisting in the development of regional policies and procedures; assisting in the management of collections on a regional scale including selection and weeding; making presentations; supervising the compilation of regional statistics; researching and writing reports; and assuming other duties as assigned.

This is a Monday to Friday position; however, some evening and weekend work may be required. This position also involves travel. You will report to the Regional Director.

TO BE SUCCESSFUL:
We are looking for people with diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

• Behavioural competencies: Organizational Commitment; Effective Interactive Communication; Team Leadership; Developing Others; Results Orientation; Relationship / Network Building

• Technical competencies: Specialized Subject Matter Expertise and Knowledge

• Language: Written and spoken competence in English and French is required. Please state your language capability.

• Education: Master's degree in Library and/or Information Studies from an ALA accredited program and a minimum of four (4) years of related professional experience including one (1) year of management and supervision.

Experience working with library automation software, email, the Internet, and MS-Word is necessary.

Please ensure that your preferred language for assessment (English or French) is identified on your resume. You must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration.

Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

If we have difficulty recruiting for this position, you may be considered if you have less than four (4) years of experience at a salary commensurate with your experience.

SALARY: $66,924 to $93,470 per annum.

If you are eligible to work in Canada, apply online at eRecruitment, indicating competition number: 24-6236-001. This opportunity will remain open until the position is filled. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

title: Financial Controller
description:
## Financial Controller

Modern Construction, a subsidiary of the VINCI Group, was founded in 1945 and employs 160 people and operates across a range of activities, including construction and paving, asphalt production through a fixed plant, sale of aggregates with two operational quarries, trucking services and is an explosives distributor.

Modern Construction, located on the outskirts of Moncton, NB is currently looking for a financial controller. Reporting to the CFO, you will be tasked with preparing and reporting the financial data in compliance with the Group's fundamentals as well as accounting and management rules, all while meeting pre-determined deadlines.

Your main responsibilities will be as follows:

· Prepare monthly financial reports for management while analyzing and commenting on project and activity results in comparison to forecasts and operating budget.

· Prepare quarterly budgets for each center of operations with input from the management team.

· Ensure accurate and timely recording of revenues, expenses, accruals, and adjustments.

· Anticipate financial risks and proactively report budget overruns to decision-makers

· Ensure compliance with accounting standards and applicable tax and regulatory requirements.

· Prepare and coordinate year-end audit/review activities with external accountants and auditors.

· Oversee accounts receivable collections and monitor customer accounts.

· Oversee accounts payable to ensure invoices are properly approved, coded, and paid according to terms.

· Provide overall oversight of the payroll process, ensuring payroll is accurate and processed on time.

· Monitor cash position and forecast future cash requirements.

· Supervise and provide direction to the accounting staff.

· Support management with special projects and financial analysis as required.

· Assist with implementation and transition to new accounting systems (SAP).

Our ideal candidate is:

· An experienced professional with university studies in accounting (Bachelor's degree), finance or any other related field. A CPA designation would be considered an asset.

· 5+ years of similar experience in the accounting field.

· Bilingual (French and English).

· You must have a strong working knowledge of excel.

· Experience with SAP would be an advantage.

· Strong budgeting and forecasting skills, along with financial analysis.

· Have advisory skills and communication abilities that will enable you to support operational teams in achieving their budgetary objectives along with supporting your accounting team with their roles.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who takes pride in their work, enjoys being part of a team, and is interested in building a long-term career with Modern Construction.

We offer a comprehensive compensation package, including competitive salary, performance-based bonuses, a benefits package that also includes a pension plan, health benefits, and an employee share purchase program.

If you are interested in applying for the position, please forward your resume to Lise Dupuis at lise.dupuis@moderngroup.ca

## Entity

VINCI Construction is one of the world's leading construction companies, specializing in transport infrastructure, buildings, networks, and urban development. VINCI Construction leverages a network of local businesses, specialist networks, and specific expertise in major infrastructure projects. Operating in over 100 countries, its 1,300 companies employ more than 119,000 people and generated revenue of €31.5 billion.

title: Director, Project Delivery
employer: Build Nova Scotia Healthcare Infrastructure Division
description:
The Director, Project Delivery is accountable for leading the planning, execution, control, commissioning and operational turnover of assigned infrastructure projects. The position ensures projects are delivered safely, within approved scope, schedule and budget, and in accordance with Build Nova Scotia governance, quality and reporting requirements. The Director, Project Delivery provides day to day leadership to the assigned project delivery team and coordinates internal and external partners to achieve approved project and operational outcomes.

Located in Sydney, NS, this position reports to the Senior Director, Project Delivery and works collaboratively with our healthcare infrastructure division. This is a full-time five (5) year term position.

Qualifications
• As the ideal candidate, you have a post-secondary degree in Engineering, Construction Management or other relevant discipline, along with ten (10) plus years of progressive experience in a leadership role in construction operations or project management, preferably with a good understanding of healthcare or similar scale public infrastructure projects.

• A relevant professional designation or certification, such as P.Eng., Architect, C.E.T. or PMP, is considered an asset. An equivalent combination of education, professional credentials and directly related experience may be considered.

• You are a results-oriented leader with demonstrated success creating alignment across diverse organizations and leading high-performing teams of employees, consultants, specialists and contractors. You have a proven record in project governance, cost and schedule control, procurement, contract administration, risk management, change management, claims resolution and the implementation of effective project delivery practices. You understand the legislation, regulations, codes, standards and commercial considerations applicable to major public-sector construction.

• You can translate complex project information into concise, decision-ready reporting for senior leaders and government partners. You demonstrate sound judgment, strong written and verbal communication, disciplined prioritization and the ability to make timely decisions in a high-pressure, multi-project environment. You build trusted relationships while maintaining clear accountability for performance and results.

Responsibilities
• Leads projects to operational completion by leading both the internal and external parties to desired outcome.

• Develops and maintains project plans including scope, budget, and schedule to ensure project related policy objectives are realized as efficiently as possible.

• Supervises assigned project staff pursuant to Build NS human resource practices and oversees the works of contracted external resources to ensure the cost-effective delivery of work in accordance with the scope of negotiated contracts.

• Monitors project deliverables and provides direction to staff so that deliverables meet defined Build NS Healthcare quality standards.

• Manages project risk by prioritizing potential risk areas and recommending appropriate mitigation strategies to program management.

• Communicates regularly with sponsors and stakeholders to maintain positive working relationships, including participating in and leading federal/provincial/academic scientific, regulatory and technical advisory committees and community based committees and directing the development of Build NS program status reports consistent with organizational reporting processes and standards.

• Manages procurement of project resources according to Build NS procurement policy including contract management of Build NS project suppliers.

• Supports, or in the absence of the Senior Director acts as, spokesperson for the project with media and in public forum

• Provide leadership and direction to ensure the effective management of human and financial resources by setting and evaluating staff performance targets, promoting diversity and a healthy, respectful workplace, demonstrating the leadership competencies, respecting corporate human resources practices, promoting teamwork and individual development.

• Maintain internal communications, monitor revenues and expenditures, adhere to procurement guidelines, acquire goods and services in the most cost effective manner and accurately forecast budget requirements for the fiscal year.

• May perform other related duties as assigned.

Pay Grade: NSLHC-15

Salary Range: $4423.11 - $5528.89 Bi-Weekly

Salary Placement: The placement of a new hire into the salary range is based on an objective salary rating process. This process will assess the knowledge, skills, experiences and overall qualifications of a candidate to determine appropriate placement. Each pay grade has established steps, and new hires cannot exceed certain maximums which are outlined in the Compensation Framework.

• Defined Benefit Pension Plan

• Health, Dental and Life Insurance

• Paid Vacation and General Illness Leave

• Short- and Long-Term Disability

• Employee and Family Assistance Programs

• Professional Development Opportunities

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

title: Travel Consultant
description:
## Travel Consultant

On Site Training | Work From Home Opportunities | Starting at $21/hour + bonus potential

## Helping People Through the Moments That Matter

Travel doesn't always go according to plan.

Flights get cancelled. Weather disrupts plans. Connections are missed. Things don't always go as expected.

When that happens, our customers need more than someone to answer the call. They need someone who can listen, understand what matters most, and confidently guide them towards a solution.

As a Travel Consultant, you'll help our customers book, manage and modify their travel arrangements while delivering the exceptional service they expect. Whether you're helping a customer rebook a flight, adjust hotel reservations, navigate a travel disruption, or maximize the benefits available to them, you'll play an important role in turning stressful situations into positive experiences.

This isn't just about booking travel. It's about building trust, solving problems, and making customers feel genuinely supported when they need it most.

If you're someone who loves helping people, communicates naturally, and can stay focused when things get busy, we'd love to meet you!

## Why You'll Love Working Here

At Cloud5, we believe great customer experiences start with great people.

We'll provide the training, coaching, and support you need to succeed, even if you've never worked in travel before. You'll develop valuable customer service, communication, consulting, and problem-solving skills while working alongside a team that genuinely supports one another.

No two days are exactly the same. You'll tackle new challenges, connect with different customers, and continuously build skills that will benefit you throughout your career.

## No travel experience? No problem!

If you have strong customer service skills, enjoy helping people, and are passionate about creating positive customer experiences, we'll provide the training to help you succeed.

## Why Join Us?

· $21/hour starting wage with quarterly bonus potential

· Shift premiums across various hours/days

· Work from home opportunities following successful completion of training

· Employee referral bonus of up to $500 per successful candidate

· Medical & Vision benefits after 3 months

· Dental coverage after 6 months

· RRSP and TFSA options

· Company RRSP match up to 3 percent after 1 year

· Paid training and ongoing coaching to help you succeed

· Career growth opportunities within a growing organization

· Access to various travel perks and discounts

## What You'll Do

· Help customers book, manage, modify and troubleshoot travel arrangements

· Resolve travel-related issues and provide solutions during disruptions and unexpected situations

· Communicate with customers by phone to understand their needs and provide personalized support

· Demonstrate the value and benefits available to the customer

· Consult with customers to identify the best available options based on their unique circumstances

· Coordinate with travel suppliers and partners to secure travel arrangements and resolve issues

· Research solutions, troubleshoot challenges, and think creatively when standard options aren't available

· Maintain a calm, professional, and empathetic approach during complex or high-pressure situations

· Deliver a consistently exceptional customer experience while meeting service expectations

## What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

Success in this role isn't measured by how much you know about travel on day one. It's measured by how well you listen, solve problems, and create positive experiences for customers.

## You may be a great fit if you:

· Connect naturally with people and build rapport easily

· Are an active listener who takes the time to understand customer needs

· Lead conversations with empathy, professionalism, and confidence

· Enjoy troubleshooting and finding solutions to complex problems

· Can balance customer needs with program guidelines and available options

· Stay calm and resourceful when handling challenging situations

· Are highly organized and able to manage multiple tasks at once

· Communicate clearly and effectively, both verbally and in writing

· Are comfortable using technology and navigating multiple systems simultaneously

· Have a positive attitude, growth mindset and genuine desire to help others

Experience in customer service, hospitality, travel, contact center, or other service-focused environments is considered an asset, but we are equally interested in candidates who demonstrate strong communication skills, curiosity, and a customer first mindset.

Cloud5 Communications is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, disability status, age, or any other status protected by law. We will never request a fee or payment from candidates. Please do not provide any personal or financial information to anyone you suspect of recruitment fraud.

## How to Identify Recruitment Fraud:

• You receive a message on WhatsApp or another online messaging platform

• You are asked to provide a fee or payment (we will NEVER request payment from candidates)

• Our email communication will only ever come from a @Cloud5.com domain or @msg.paycomonline.com domain. We will never contact you through Gmail or any other free online mail service

• Cross reference the recruiter's name and contact information on LinkedIn or by contacting corphr@cloud5.com

• If you are still unsure call 1 (877) 241-2516

title: PAYROLL COORDINATOR
description:
Mount Saint Vincent University is strongly committed to fostering diversity and inclusion within our community and encourages applications from all qualified candidates including women, persons of any sexual orientations and gender identities and/or expressions, Indigenous persons, African Canadians, other racialized groups, persons with disabilities, and other groups that would contribute to the diversification of our campus. Candidates who identify as being from any of these groups are encouraged to voluntarily self-identify in their application materials. All qualified candidates are welcome to apply; however, priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents.

The Department of Financial Services at Mount Saint Vincent University invites applications for the position of Payroll Coordinator.

Classification: Permanent, Full-Time MPA Level 2 Position
Salary: $56,314 per annum [Step Progression: $56,314 to $68,515]
Start Date: ASAP

Application Process:

If you require an accommodation at any time during the application process, please let us know. Applications should include a cover letter and resume. This position will remain open until filled.

Qualifications
Candidates must have a payroll certification through the National Payroll Institute and a minimum of three years of progressive, related experience. Completion of a Bachelor of Business Administration/Commerce, or a related degree is considered as asset. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. The ideal candidate is a relationship builder who is able to interact with individuals with tact and diplomacy, and who has demonstrated strong problem-solving skills. Candidates must have demonstrated experience supervising others. This position requires the individual to have experience conducting financial analysis, be a self-starter, and have strong organizational and prioritization skills. Candidates must be proficient in the use of Microsoft Office Suite with advanced skills in Excel and use of technology to conduct analysis in the most efficient manner. Experience in using business enterprise systems for finance is required. Supporting all of these skills is a strong commitment to excellent customer service.

Responsibilities
Reporting to the Director of Finance and Administration, the Payroll Coordinator has overall responsibility for ensuring the timely, accurate, and confidential processing of the University's two bi-weekly Payrolls and one Monthly payroll, including the submission of all government remittances (in compliance with Canada Revenue Agency and other regulatory reporting requirements). Other responsibilities include preparation of monthly account reconciliations, supervision of one staff member (the Payroll Administrator), year-end payroll accruals, calendar year-end close/new calendar year preparations, and processing T4s. The Payroll Coordinator also provides ongoing policy and procedure recommendations aimed at increasing overall payroll effectiveness and efficiency. Other duties include:

• the verification, preparation, entering, checking and processing of payroll transactions

• the reporting, analysis, and oversight of Records of Employment and CRA remittances online

• oversees the implementation of changes or upgrades to the payroll module of the Colleague System including new functionality related to web applications for payroll

• performs other reconciliations or financial analysis as required

• oversees and participates in responding to requests for information

• monitors legislative requirements, updating the computerized payroll system as necessary

title: Accounts Payable Clerk
description:
Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, South America and Australia. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

The Accounts Payable Clerk (based out of Saint John, NB or Blacks Harbour, NB) is responsible for performing day-to-day accounting tasks related to the processing of invoices and expenses and maintaining accurate financial records. The role ensures that all vendor invoices and employee expenses are properly reviewed, approved, and adhere to company policies and accounting best practices.

## Responsibilities:

• Invoice / Expense Processing: Review and verify invoices and employee expenses for accuracy, completeness, and ensure proper approval and coding.

• Reconciliations: Reconcile vendor statements to ensure accurate record-keeping.

• Record Keeping: Maintain organized and up-to-date accounts payable files and records for audits and reporting purposes.

• Vendor Communication: Respond to vendor inquiries, resolve discrepancies, and maintain positive relationships with vendors.

• Vendor Maintenance: Co-ordinate and prepare documentation for vendor set up and maintenance. Set up as required.

• Expense Tracking: Assist with tracking and categorizing company expenses for accurate financial reporting.

• Month-End Close: Assist with month-end closing activities related to accounts payable and ensure financial records are updated.

• Compliance: Ensure compliance with company policies, tax regulations, and accounting standards. Escalate non-compliance.

• Process Improvement: Identify areas for improvement.

• Assist with other tasks and projects as required

## Requirements:

• High school diploma or equivalent; post-secondary education in accounting or administration is an asset.

• Proven experience as an accounts payable clerk or in a similar accounting role.

• Knowledge of basic accounting principles and accounts payable processes.

• Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel. Experience with accounting software (e.g., Dynamics GP, D365) is a plus.

• Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.

• Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work well in a team environment.

• Ability to handle sensitive financial information with confidentiality.

• An energetic, self-starter who works well in a deadline driven environment.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

## Benefits Package:

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• Support Services: Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Time Off: Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave for work-life balance.

• Wellness: Wellness programs and access to on-site gym facilities (available in some locations).

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

• Convenience: On-site parking or parking allowance.

If you're looking to join a supportive team environment with opportunities for personal and professional development, apply now and become part of our dynamic team.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness, and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centers around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's License (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community, submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

title: Analyst (Costing and Pricing) - PAL Aerospace
description:
PAL Aerospace is a leader in international aerospace and defence operations, delivering intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), training solutions, and in-service support worldwide. We are committed to delivering mission-critical capabilities through innovation, operational excellence, and a highly skilled workforce.

PAL Aerospace is seeking a motivated Analyst to support costing, pricing, and program risk and commercial management activities across our aerospace and defence portfolio.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional to build expertise in financial modelling, cost analysis, price strategy, and defence contracting, while working closely with experienced business development, program management, and technical teams. You will contribute to competitive bids, program financial planning, decision support for key strategic initiatives, and deal reviews, with opportunities for extensive C-suite and senior executive engagement.

## Key Responsibilities

## Financial Modelling & Costing

• Support the development of financial models and cost estimates, from detailed cost inputs through to pricing outputs

• Assist in maintaining and enhancing costing templates, tools, and financial models

• Perform basic to intermediate financial analysis, including scenario comparisons and sensitivity analysis

• Work with programs, engineering, and operations subject matter experts to gather and validate cost inputs

• Lead the preparation of costing and pricing materials for internal reviews

• Identify potential risks and inconsistencies in cost data and escalate appropriately

## Program Transition Support

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

Our team is seeking a Primary Care Paramedic for a full-time position. If no Primary Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Primary Care Paramedic, then Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to an EMR as the next highest classification, they will be awarded as temporary full time (TFT) and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful candidate will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;

• Current medical certification with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

title: Supply Chain Specialist
description:
Job Title: Supply Chain Specialist
Location: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
TP - PPT - 9688

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with Pure Paint Laboratories to recruit a Supply Chain Specialist for their Operations team based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Pure Paint Laboratories (Pure Paint) is committed to creating healthy spaces for a healthier planet. The company produces North America's only fully developed petroleum-free, plant-based architectural paint, made entirely from renewable agricultural ingredients. Inspired by ancient, time-tested formulas, Pure Paint's products are non-toxic, fully biodegradable, and designed to support healthier indoor environments while contributing to a renewable future.

Through a manufacturing process that begins with cold-pressed oilseed crops and other natural ingredients, Pure Paint creates durable, high-quality paint products while maintaining a commitment to sustainability and healthier spaces for generations to come.

Role Description
Reporting to the Operations Director, the Supply Chain Specialist develops and maintains practical, resource-loaded schedules that support the safe, efficient, and timely execution of production planning. Working closely with Sales, Operations, Maintenance, Project Teams, Procurement, and Stores, you will coordinate resources, identify risks and constraints, and align weekly and daily schedules with business priorities.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Building, maintaining, and communicating integrated schedules (daily, weekly, and rolling look-ahead) aligned to business priorities and available capacity.

• Converting approved work orders and scope into executable schedules by validating readiness requirements, including materials, tools, permits, access, labour skills, and durations.

• Facilitating weekly scheduling meetings with stakeholders and capturing decisions, constraints, and action items.

• Coordinating labour, equipment, and material planning while level-loading work to optimize utilization and reduce bottlenecks.

• Identifying critical path activities, dependencies, and schedule risks and proposing mitigation and scenario plans.

• Monitoring progress, updating schedules using actuals, and managing changes resulting from emergent work, outages, supply delays, or scope changes.

• Partnering with Procurement and Stores to confirm material availability, expedite shortages, and maintain a clear ready backlog.

• Maintaining scheduling standards, coding structures, and data quality within the ERP system.

• Producing routine schedule performance reports (planned vs. actual, compliance, backlog, resource loading) and presenting insights to leadership.

• Supporting shutdown and turnaround planning activities as required.

• Building long-range plans ranging from one to six months.

Your Qualifications
As the ideal candidate, you are highly organized and detail-oriented with strong planning, scheduling. analytical, and communication skills. You are capable of balancing competing priorities, facilitating stakeholder discussions, and adapting schedules as operational requirements change.

## Key qualifications include:

• Post-secondary education in Supply Chain, Business, Operations, Engineering or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 2+ years of experience in scheduling, production planning, and/or sales and operations planning (S&OP) and procurement.

• Working knowledge of scheduling principles, including dependencies, constraints, critical path methodology, and capacity/resource planning.

• Experience with scheduling and/or work management systems such as Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, SAP, Maximo, Katana, or similar planning systems.

• Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, pivot tables, data analysis, and data cleaning.

• Strong planning, prioritization, and stakeholder management abilities.

• Excellent communication, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

• A high level of attention to detail and commitment to schedule and data accuracy.

• Ability to adapt to changing priorities and re-plan effectively as constraints emerge.

• A continuous improvement mindset with the ability to identify root causes and recommend solutions.

• Strong understanding of the end-to-end supply chain, from raw material and packaging suppliers through to final delivery to the end customer.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.

For more information contact Thomas Pugh, Partner, at 902-818-4506 and tpugh@kbrs.ca or Rick Neima, Senior Consultant at 902-488-2534 and rneima@kbrs.ca, or please apply online by clicking the "Apply Now" button below. Horizon Health Network is seeking Cardiologists to join our collegial and collaborative team in beautiful New Brunswick.

## Why you should work here

New Brunswick offers a safe and welcoming community with a relaxed lifestyle and a true work-life balance, enriched by its diverse Indigenous, Anglophone, and Francophone heritage.

Horizon Health Network is the largest health authority in the region, employing dedicated professionals focused on delivering high-quality care. Our employees collaborate with community partners to provide accessible health programs and services to over half a million people through our 12 hospitals and more than 100 medical facilities and clinics.

## Incentives & Remuneration

Remuneration will be determined in accordance with the specific role and practice location. Additional details will be shared as the recruitment process progresses.

Successful applicants may be eligible to receive the following:

• Urban recruitment incentive of $50,000.00 with a 2-year return of service.

• Moving expense reimbursement is also available.

## What you will do

Responsibilities include inpatient and outpatient care, non-invasive diagnostics, and equal participation in echocardiography, ECG/Holter reporting, stress testing, CICU coverage, and on-call rotation. Outpatient volume beyond follow-up care is flexible. Leadership and professional development opportunities may be available. All cardiologists are part of the Division of Clinical Cardiology within the Departments of Cardiac Sciences and Medicine.

• Provide comprehensive inpatient and outpatient diagnostic services (e.g., echocardiography, ECG, Holter monitoring, stress tests, and other imaging modalities as qualified).

• Participate in CICU rotations, daily inpatient rounds on the cardiac stepdown unit, and provide inpatient consultations and care.

• Offer outpatient consultations and follow-up after inpatient/emergency care, as well as elective specialty consultations for the regional medical community (volume/scope customizable).

• Ensure coverage of your outpatient practice during absences; report all absences (planned/unforeseen) in writing to the Division Head.

• Participate in the cardiology on-call schedule, including weekdays, evenings, weekends, and holidays.

• Negotiate service gaps in advance to maintain coverage.

• Practice in alignment with Horizon Health's mission and values, in collaboration with interdisciplinary teams.

• Engage in teaching, quality improvement initiatives, and research supporting Horizon's clinical mandate.

(Note: These responsibilities are the basic and prime duties associated with this position; other related and allied duties may be assigned from time to time as may be necessary to the operation of Horizon Health Network.)

## Who you are

• Medical degree and Royal College certification in Cardiology.

• Licensed to practice in New Brunswick; in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of NB and the NB Medical Society.

• CMPA malpractice coverage appropriate to scope of practice.

• Proficient in inpatient and outpatient cardiology, including:
• Clinical cardiology consultation and longitudinal care

• CICU procedures (arterial/venous access, Swan-Ganz, IABP, temporary pacing, hemodynamic therapies)

• ECG, Holter, ABPM interpretation; comprehensive echocardiography (TTE, TEE, stress, 3D, contrast/bubble, strain)

• Strong communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills.

• Excellent attendance record and physical ability to perform duties.

• Proficiency in medical-level spoken and written English.

Preferred Assets:

• Fellowship training in a cardiology subspecialty.

• Experience with pacemaker/device interrogation and programming.

• Bilingualism (English/French) is a strong asset.

• Leadership experience in planning, strategy, and quality improvement.

• Experience in teaching and skill development for clinical teams.

• Interest in clinical or academic research welcomed.

The physician must also meet continuing education requirements, adhere to departmental and health authority policies, comply with relevant legislation, and follow professional ethical standards set by regulatory bodies.

## Interested? Apply Today!

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care

Job Summary
The Clinical Psychologist III provides an advanced and specialized psychology service to the clients of the Mental Health and Addictions Program in the Eastern Rural Zone in NLHS. This position acts on referrals from clients themselves, general practitioners, specialists and other healthcare providers. Standardized assessment and therapeutic interventions are provided to patients across the lifespan, with a wide range of complex needs including, but not limited to, anxiety, depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, eating disorders and personality disorders.

The responsibilities include designing, implementing and evaluating the psychological interventions provided to patients and families; conducting advanced, independent diagnostic interviews to expedite the formulation of an appropriate treatment approach; formulating and communicating psychiatric diagnosis using DSM-5-TR; selecting and administering comprehensive psychometric tests where appropriate, including but not limited to, intellectual assessment, personality assessment, neuropsychological screening, memory assessment and vocational/aptitude testing; interpreting psychological data for diagnostic purposes; conducting group facilitation; and monitoring/prioritizing patient wait lists according to clinical needs. The Clinical Psychologist may have involvement in DBT groups.

As a clinical leader, the Clinical Psychologist provides supervision to Psychology residents, Doctoral students and provisionally registered Psychologists. This position reports to the Division Manager and maintains accountability to the Professional Practice Consultant for Psychology for professional integrity issues.

Job Demands
Occasionally, there is lifting or physical strength required, less than 10 lbs. for files, boxes, or equipment.
Regularly sits; occasionally works in awkward/cramped positions, and stands to facilitate or teach groups.
Uses fine finger/precision work when on the computer and visual concentration is required when in sessions with patients (i.e. reviewing patient charts/notes, tests and for documenting work, and when reading or researching information).
Visual concentration is required to interpret patient observations and integrate into patient evaluation.
Auditory concentration is constantly required in sessions with patients to listen attentively, to be alert and to obtain and interpret information correctly.
A higher-than-normal level of attentiveness is required when assessing high risk patients.

Job Qualifications
Graduation with an approved/recognized Master's Degree in Clinical Psychology is required.
Graduation with an approved/recognized Doctorate Degree in Clinical Psychology is preferred.
Current and continuing registration or provisional registration with Newfoundland and Labrador Psychology Board is required.
Graduate course work and supervised experience in psychological assessment including cognitive and diagnostic assessment with children, adolescents and adults is required.
Graduate course work and supervised experience in evidence based therapy with individuals, families and groups with a specific focus on mental health issues is required.
Previous experience supervising Doctoral level residents is preferred.
Exhibited strong communication, program development and evaluation skills.
Possessed strong leadership and supervisory skills that are focused on engaging others and developing coalitions.
Demonstrated ability to provide strong and comprehensive clinical support, training and mentorship to other psychologists and supervisees.
Possessed strong analytical, critical reasoning, collaboration, problem solving, decision-making and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to effectively translate and communicate knowledge in the specialized area of psychology practice to others.
Demonstrated ability to conduct research, deliver lectures/clinical education sessions and provide clinical direction and consultation within an interprofessional environment.
Ability to work autonomously, prioritizing caseloads and client needs.
Demonstrated ability and willingness to participle in the clinical training activities of the psychology discipline.
Demonstrated strong awareness of ethical principles and standards of professional conduct.
Use of a personal vehicle is a condition of employment.
A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

Job Summary
This position works within the Nurse Practitioner's (NP) scope of practice in the category of practice of Family/All Ages. This is an advanced practice role providing professional, analytical and an autonomous comprehensive range of health services to clients and patients including but not limited to health assessments and diagnosis of diseases, disorders, injuries and conditions, treating and managing acute and chronic illnesses and identifying health risks and needs within a holistic model. In this role the nurse practitioner performs all activities utilizing a harm reduction approach within the primary health care framework.

The PHC Team mandate is to provide low barrier access to harm reduction focused, primary health care services for individuals who are homeless or precariously housed. Many of these individuals are navigating complex mental health and/or substance use conditions and often experience marginalization because of their circumstances; many have trouble accessing traditional health care services.

The NP will work to full scope of practice providing care to the vulnerable population through a walk-in clinic and/or outreach to various locations (Mobile Clinics, community partner locations etc.) They will also be involved in the Managed Alcohol Program (MAP) and a Palliative approach Care for vulnerable populations, in collaboration with other providers and team members.

The nurse practitioner is a member of the Downtown Healthcare Collaborative and harm reduction teams of health professionals including, but not limited to, registered nurses, pharmacist, occupational therapist, community outreach workers, social worker, peer support workers and others, working across programs and services to provide the best possible care. Health services in this context are provided in a variety of ways including street reach and mobile clinics, home visits, PHC walk-in clinics, community partnerships, and acute care partnerships.

The nurse practitioner, as a member of the team, provides for the presenting needs of the client and includes all routine primary health care and treatment as well as Hepatitis C, HIV, latent TB, STBBI testing and treatment, mental health single session counselling, client education, and is a satellite site for provision of SWAP supplies. All services are intended to reach the most vulnerable, underserved individuals in our community.

In keeping with NL Health Services Values, the harm reduction team members operate in an environment of mutual respect where the contribution of every team member, regardless of personal or professional background, is considered when providing care to clients. Team members are supported and encouraged to use their education, knowledge, strengths, experience, and expertise to practice to their full scope in the performance of their work, in support of the client, and in support of one another. Low barrier access to care is the foundation of service, meeting individuals wherever they are in their life journey and regardless of their personal circumstances. By working with the individual to address concerns impacting their personal health, the team endeavors to attach clients to permanent providers wherever possible and to connect them with long term services when necessary.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Constantly moves, lifts, or operates equipment/machinery up to 10 lbs. and regularly is required to lift/move equipment, books, supplies, and sometimes children up to 25 lbs. (may need to be deleted or added depending on the position). Occasionally, may have to reposition a patient over 50 lbs.
Physical effort also includes regular sitting to conduct patient histories, performing work on the computer and when assessing patients, regularly stands or walks.
When performing procedures, regularly uses fine finger/precision work and hand tools (i.e. medical instruments, computer mouse, stethoscope, etc.) requiring accurate control and steadiness.
Visual concentration is required when performing physical assessment and procedures, completing charts/reports, observing patients, reading equipment/monitors, and completing work-related correspondence on the computer.

Job Qualifications
Completion of an approved/recognized Nurse Practitioner program is required.
Current registration with the College of Registered Nurses of NL and Licensed (or eligible for licensure) as a Nurse Practitioner (Family/All Ages) with the CRNNL is required.
A minimum of five years clinical experience within the last seven in Primary Health Care is required.
Current BCLS Certification is required.

James Paton Memorial Regional Health Centre is seeking a skilled and patient-focused Anesthesiologist to provide comprehensive anesthesia care across surgical and procedural settings. Responsibilities include conducting thorough pre-operative evaluations, developing and implementing individualized anesthesia plans, and collaborating closely with surgeons, nurses, and other healthcare professionals to ensure optimal patient outcomes. The anesthesiologist will administer general, regional, and local anesthesia, continuously monitor patients’ vital signs during procedures, manage airways, and respond promptly to medical emergencies or complications. Post-operatively, the role involves overseeing patient recovery from anesthesia, managing pain and anesthesia-related side effects, and ensuring safe transitions of care. Additional duties may include participation in pain management services, emergency response, quality improvement initiatives, and teaching or mentoring, depending on department needs.

title: Senior Accountant
description:
## Senior Accountant
Saint John, NB
Reference # HL-OCA-10025

Our client, Ocean Capital Holdings Limited, is a privately held company with its head office located in Saint John, NB with interests in a number of businesses, including broadcasting, construction, energy, and real estate. Their purpose is to grow winning businesses with great people, which contribute to better communities. They unlock the potential of their businesses through imagination and a passion for winning, and they celebrate the uniqueness in each person. Their focus is on excellence and accomplishment.

We are excited to partner with them to bring an experienced Senior Accountant to their finance team in Saint John, NB. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Accounting, this position provides a broad range of accounting and financial support to Ocean Capital Holdings Limited and related companies. As an integral member of the accounting team, the Senior Accountant will play a key role in financial reporting, consolidated reporting, daily accounting activities, cash management, and process improvement initiatives across a diverse group of businesses.

## Responsibilities will include:

• Prepare monthly consolidated and non-consolidated financial statements and schedules, including journal entries, reconciliations, and variance analysis for multiple companies and present to Senior Leadership

• Coordinate with operational finance teams to prepare consolidated financial reports and analysis

• Prepare annual budgets and schedules including management reporting

• Assist in creation of annual management and shareholder reporting

• Manage day-to-day transactional processing: billing, cash forecasting

• Be a key resource to support and engage with audit processes - internal and external

• Assist with the development and implementation of formalized accounting and reporting policies and standards

• Assist in identifying and implementing process improvement initiatives within our team and cross functional teams

## The ideal candidate will possess:

• Chartered Professional Accounting (CPA) designation

• 5-7 years of progressive accounting experience post CPA completion

• Degree in Business Administration

• Experience with consolidated financial statements and US GAAP would be considered strong assets

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)

• Experience with mid-market to top tier ERP system

• Experience in applying foreign currency translation methods and managing exchange rate impacts in financial reporting and consolidations

• Strong presentation skills, capable of delivering complex financial information in an engaging and accessible manner

• Proven experience collaborating with and presenting to senior leadership

• Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

• Strong sense of ownership and accountability

• Industry experience considered an asset

• Managerial or supervisory experience considered an asset

• Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities

• Reliable self-starter with the ability to work independently and manage priorities

• Meticulous attention to detail and accuracy

title: Anesthesiology Physician
description:
Zone: Central Zone
Location: CNF - Central NL Regional Health Centre
Anesthesiology Physician
Central Zone - Physician
Permanent Full-time

Hours: 75 hours bi-weekly plus equal participation in call schedule

Salary: Alternate Billing Plan

Competition Number: VAC0021383

Posted Date: 2026-02-10

Closing Date: Open until filled.

## ABOUT NLHS

NL Health Services offers the full continuum of health and community services including public health, long-term care, community services, hospital care and unique provincial programs and services. NL Health Services prides ourselves on providing the highest quality care and service possible to the people in our communities, in our region, and in the province. To do that, we employ qualified, competent, and caring individuals who are dedicated to their professions and to our vision of Healthy People, Healthy Communities.

ABOUT CENTRAL ZONE
Central Zone is the second largest health zone in Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services, serving approximately 90,000 people (17 per cent of the province’s population) living in 176 communities. With a geographical area encompassing more than half the total land mass of the island, the Central region extends from Charlottetown in the east, Fogo Island in the north, Harbour Breton in the south, to Baie Verte in the west. Central Zone provides a variety of primary, secondary, long-term care, community health, and other enhanced secondary services.

Central NL Regional Health Centre is seeking a skilled and patient-focused Anesthesiologist to provide comprehensive anesthesia care across surgical and procedural settings. Responsibilities include conducting thorough pre-operative evaluations, developing and implementing individualized anesthesia plans, and collaborating closely with surgeons, nurses, and other healthcare professionals to ensure optimal patient outcomes. The anesthesiologist will administer general, regional, and local anesthesia, continuously monitor patients’ vital signs during procedures, manage airways, and respond promptly to medical emergencies or complications. Post-operatively, the role involves overseeing patient recovery from anesthesia, managing pain and anesthesia-related side effects, and ensuring safe transitions of care. Additional duties may include participation in pain management services, emergency response, quality improvement initiatives, and teaching or mentoring, depending on department needs.

Grand Falls-Windsor offers an excellent quality of life with short commutes, affordable housing, and strong schools, alongside year-round access to Newfoundland and Labrador’s outdoor lifestyle. This position is ideal for professionals seeking clinical breadth, professional autonomy, and a sustainable work–life balance within a welcoming community. Visit the following web site for information on the Community of Grand Falls-Windsor: Grand Falls-Windsor - Perfectly Centered

## QUALIFICATIONS

• MD from an accredited medical school

• Royal College certification (FRCSC) in Anesthesiology, or Board-eligible

• Eligible for Full or Provisional (non-restricted) licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Newfoundland and Labrador (CPSNL)

• Satisfy credentialing requirements of Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services including a satisfactory criminal record check and vulnerable sector check

REMUNERATION
Alternate Payment Plan Model. Alternate Payment Plan (APP) is a physician remuneration model in which compensation is not primarily based on fee-for-service billings. Instead, physicians are paid through a contractual arrangement that provides predictable income in exchange for the delivery of defined clinical and non-clinical services.

AVALIABLE INCENTIVES
Physician Signing Bonus $150,000
Come Home Incentive - $100,000 (if eligibility criteria are met)
**Contact Recruiter for further details

RECRUITER CONTACT
For specific inquiries please contact Hannah Bromley (hannah.bromley@nlhealthservices.ca)

A CV, supporting documentation and the names of three references are required. Applicants who do not provide the necessary documentation as outlined in this job posting will not be considered. In accordance with Canadian Employment and Immigration requirements, preference will be given to Canadian Citizens and Permanent Residents of Canada. NLHS hire on the basis of merit and are committed to employment equity. We thank everyone for their interest. Only those who are selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Diagnostic Imaging Technologist I
description:
Zone: Eastern Urban Zone
Location: St. Clare's Mercy Hospital
Diagnostic Imaging Technologist I
Medical Imaging - Radiology
Temporary Full-time (Until April 19, 2026, with the possibility of extension)
NAPE LX
00481RP1
Hours: 70 bi-weekly (8-hour rotating, shiftwork; days, evenings, nights, weekends)

Salary: LX-27 (CAD 32.16 - CAD 40.20 per hour)

Competition Number: VAC0018358

Posted Date: 2025-11-12

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Job Summary
The Diagnostic Imaging Technologist I in the Diagnostic Imaging Department performs a variety of diagnostic x-ray procedures. The work involves producing diagnostic images, which are interpreted by physicians and used in medical diagnosis; setting up, processing x-ray images, and positioning patients using standard anatomical positioning techniques; assisting senior technologists and radiologists to perform a variety of procedures; operating and caring for the x-ray equipment and in the production of diagnostic images; recognizing, reporting equipment malfunctions and completing routine preventative maintenance; and performing other related work as required.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Constantly lifts, moves objects, repositions, pushes and pulls objects and transports patients to and from testing area, less than 10 lbs. between 10-30 lbs.
Push/pull up to medium forces. Constantly stands and walks for extended periods.
Regularly requires repetitive movements of upper extremities.
A high level of alertness and attentiveness is required when performing x-rays when patients are critically ill, infectious, unstable or compromised in order to obtain accurate images as quickly as possible and ensure the patient's safety.

Job Qualifications
Graduation from a recognized (accredited) program in Medical Radiography Technology is required.
Current registration and member in good standing with the Canadian Association of Medical Radiation Technologists (CAMRT) is required.
Demonstrated strong communication skills are required in the day-to-day interaction with patients, co-workers and technologists.
A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

*Effective May 1, 2025, all Medical Radiation Technologists and X - Ray Health Professionals will require registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador Council of Health Professionals (NLCHP) in the appropriate discipline(s) in order to practice in Newfoundland and Labrador.

title: Fish Processing Plant Worker - DHON
description:
True North Salmon, a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program has opportunities for highly motivated individuals to join the Company's Processing Team based out of our facility located in St. George, New Brunswick.

Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly-skilled and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

As a result of our robust growth we are seeking Fish Processing Plant Workers to join our team.

Primary duties will include, but are not limited to:

• Unloading fish from fishing vessels and transporting to work area in the fish processing plant

• Cut and clean whole fish for further processing

• Set up and operate machines to box or package fish products

• Condition whole fish for shipping

• Weighing fish, recording weight and packing fish in ice.

• Cleaning work area and equipment

• Transporting supplies and packaging materials throughout plant and storage area manually or with power equipment.

*This position requires standing for long periods of time in a cold, wet environment and using hand tools including knives and pliers.

A general understanding of the processing line is considered an asset; however, on the job training is available.

Available Shifts/Hours are as follows:

• Continental night shift (6:00 pm-6:30 am) *night shift premium of $1.00/hour applies to this shift.

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to work within the parameters of the role but to reach your fullest potential. We are a team that is driven to succeed.

We count performance, we reward contribution and we recognize talent. It is about being at the center of a growing, global leader in seafood and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability
to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

At Ambulance New Brunswick, our team consists of talented emergency medical dispatchers, primary and advanced care paramedics, emergency medical technicians, and critical care flight nurses. Health care professionals who respond with their best in some of the most difficult situations imaginable.

As the provincial ambulance service provider, our dispatchers respond to calls from those in medical distress through the 911 system and send help within seconds. Our paramedics take over from there, responding to approximately 130,000 calls per year and transporting patients to hospital by ambulance. And, each year, our specialized air ambulance crew transfers hundreds of the most critically ill and injured patients to specialized medical centres around the Maritimes and beyond.

## Duties of Position:

Clinical expectations and responsibilities for Primary Care Paramedics are based on the current National Occupational Competency Profile (NOCP) for Primary Care Paramedics,Paramedic Association of New Brunswick registration requirements as well as Ambulance NB policies, procedures and protocols.

Our paramedics provide medical support to patients on scene and en route to hospitals. Given the unpredictability of clinical presentations in the field, they are skilled in emergency techniques and well-versed in various medical treatments. "First on scene" in times of crisis, they don't leave until the job's done.

If you're a new graduate from a post-secondary program in paramedicine or have working experience outside the province of New Brunswick, ANB has a standardized process for selecting top candidates to fill Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) positions. Conducted several times a year, the Selection Process consists of a comprehensive assessment to determine your level of qualification to work for our organization.

Required Qualifications:

• You are entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizenship, permanent resident status or work permit)

• Must demonstrate the ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record

• Must have a high regard for confidentiality and patient safety

• Primary Care Paramedic program/course of over six months; If you do not have one and are interested in this career, here is a list of paramedic programs in Atlantic Canada, click here

• Must be registered, active Paramedic with the Paramedic Association of New Brunswick; If you are not currently registered in New Brunswick, please visit PANB at www.panb.ca

• Must have a valid New Brunswick Class 4 Driver's Licence (or equivalent)

Additional requirements for your application:

• Current Resume and Cover Letter

• A copy of your PCP diploma from an accredited institution

• Proof of current registration with Paramedic Association of New Brunswick

• Proof of completion of a Physical Abilities Test (PAT) specific to working as a paramedic within the last 12 months

• Proof of valid CPR level C certification issued in the last 12 months

• Photocopy of front and back of valid Class 4 driver's license (or equivalent) with minimum one year driving experience

• Driver's abstract; issued within the last 30 days

• Copy of any valid Driver's course certificate i.e. CEVO, VFIS or NS VSP or equivalent issued within the last three years

• Criminal Record with Vulnerable Sector Check; issued within the last 30 days

• Immunization Record (Tetanus Tdap) within the last 10 years, 2 MMR vaccines (Measles, Mumps and Rubella) or lab evidenced immunity, 2 Varicella vaccines (Chicken Pox) or lab evidenced immunity, 3 Hepatitis B doses and Lab evidenced immunity, TB Skin Test (2 step) and a 1-step in the last 12 months; if reactive a follow up chest x-ray). Please note, a meeting with our Employee Health and Wellness Consultant can be scheduled, to ensure that all vaccinations are up to date by the time an offer is made

• Valid Official Language Assessments (oral assessment only) in both French and English from the Department of Post-secondary Education, Training and Labour. You can contact them at LS-SL@gnb.ca. Please take into account the additional time to receive your language assessment

• Additional training and/or education is highly valued.

For any questions for our HR team, please contact us at jobs-emplois@ambulancenb.ca

If you are looking for a career that will change lives and have a direct impact on the health of our community, submit your application.

Ambulance NB is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

title: Geotechnical Engineer
