description:
## Systems Engineer
Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
TP - GST - 9659

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with GeoSpectrum Technologies in search of Systems Engineers to join their growing team based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Founded in 1994, GeoSpectrum Technologies has built a strong reputation for designing and manufacturing advanced underwater acoustic systems and components used in the maritime surveillance, ocean science, defence, and energy sectors. Known for their innovation and collaborative culture, GeoSpectrum delivers highly customized, reliable technology solutions while fostering a workplace built on technical excellence, employee engagement, and continuous growth.

## Role Description:

Reporting to the Manager of Systems Engineering, the Systems Engineer plays a critical role across the full lifecycle of complex system development, from initial requirements definition through integration, testing, and final delivery. This position is responsible for developing system architectures, managing requirements and interface documentation, and leading verification and validation activities.

The Systems Engineer works cross-functionally with multidisciplinary teams spanning mechanical, electrical, software, and acoustics engineering to ensure seamless integration of complex systems. The role also supports field operations, including system testing and sea trials, ensuring performance and reliability in real-world conditions.

By joining GeoSpectrum Technologies, you will work alongside a highly skilled and innovative team contributing to cutting-edge ocean technology solutions. In return for your skills and expertise, you will receive a competitive compensation and benefits package, along with strong opportunities for career development and professional growth.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Develop and manage system requirements, including creation and maintenance of Verification Cross-Reference Matrices (VCRMs).

• Define system architectures and prepare Interface Control Documents (ICDs) across mechanical, electrical, controls, and software domains.

• Lead and coordinate system integration, testing, verification, and commissioning activities.

• Plan and execute functional and environmental testing programs and support customer verification processes.

• Oversee requirements management across complex, multidisciplinary system projects.

• Establish and validate system interfaces, ensuring proper integration with external systems.

• Support field activities, including sea trials and system deployment.

• Contribute to product development roadmaps, research initiatives, and innovation activities.

• Assist business development efforts through technical input to proposals and documentation.

• Support safe system design through hazard identification and development of safety requirements.

## Your Qualifications:

The ideal candidate is a proactive and analytical engineering professional with strong systems thinking abilities and experience working with complex, integrated technologies. You bring a solid technical foundation, combined with the ability to collaborate across disciplines and drive projects forward in a dynamic environment.

Your qualifications should include:

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Computer Science.

• Minimum of 5 years of professional engineering or computer science experience.

• Experience in system architecture development, requirements management, and verification activities.

• Experience working with complex systems involving electrical, mechanical, and software integration.

• Experience in marine, defence, or aerospace sectors is considered an asset.

• Familiarity with military standards is considered an asset.

• Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation is considered an asset.

• Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify challenges and implement solutions.

• Demonstrated ability to effectively collaborate with diverse stakeholders across all levels of an organization.

• Excellent organizational, communication, and prioritization abilities.

• Demonstrated initiative, attention to detail, and commitment to continuous learning.

• Eligible to apply for and maintain Canadian Controlled Goods and Canadian Government Security Clearances.

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online by clicking "Apply Now" below.

For more information contact Rick Neima, Senior Consultant, at 902-488-2534 or rneima@kbrs.ca, or Nick Leadbetter, Senior Recruitment Specialist, at nleadbetter@kbrs.ca, or please apply online by clicking the "Apply Now" button below. Owned and operated by IMP Group Limited, IMP Aerostructures is a leading Canadian manufacturer of complex aircraft structural assemblies and detail components, supporting major fixed and rotary wing platforms for world class OEM and Tier 1 customers. With advanced machining, fabrication, assembly, and vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities, IMP Aerostructures has earned a reputation for quality, reliability, and long term customer partnerships.

Part of a highly successful portfolio of market leading companies, IMP Group has been recognized as one of Nova Scotia's Top Employers, one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers, and a Platinum Member of Canada's Best Managed Companies program for more than a decade.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with IMP Aerostructures to recruit a senior leader to join their team as Director of Operations/Assistant General Manager, based at their facility in Amherst, Nova Scotia.

## Role Description:

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Director of Operations/Assistant General Manager will provide end to end leadership for the operational performance of IMP Aerostructures while contributing to overall business management and strategic execution. This role is primarily operations focused, with responsibility for translating strategic objectives into disciplined execution across production, engineering, and supply chain functions.

Working closely with executive leadership, finance, and operational teams, the Director of Operations/Assistant General Manager will drive operational excellence, ensure delivery against customer commitments, and cultivate a strong performance driven culture in a unionized manufacturing environment. This leader will play a critical role in continuous improvement, talent development, and supporting sustainable growth initiatives across the organization.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Lead and execute the organization's operational strategy in alignment with IMP Aerostructures' business goals and long term strategic plan.

• Provide direct leadership to the Production, Engineering, and Purchasing functions, ensuring effective cross functional collaboration and accountability.

• Ensure performance excellence across safety, quality, delivery, and cost, meeting contractual and customer requirements.

• Drive production planning and execution to support program schedules, capacity requirements, and operational priorities.

• Monitor operational performance using key metrics and Balanced Scorecard objectives, identifying risks, trends, and opportunities for improvement.

• Champion continuous improvement initiatives, including Lean manufacturing, change management, and operational best practices.

• Lead, coach, and develop leadership teams, fostering engagement, capability growth, and succession planning.

• Partner with internal stakeholders, customers, and suppliers to support program execution, operational risk management, and growth initiatives.

• Contribute to overall business and financial performance through disciplined cost management, forecasting, and operational decision making in collaboration with finance and executive leadership.

## Your Qualifications:

As the ideal candidate, you bring significant senior leadership experience in manufacturing or complex operational environments, along with a proven ability to lead multi functional teams in a unionized setting. You combine strong operational discipline with business acumen and are comfortable working at both strategic and executional levels of the organization.

Qualifications include:

• 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in operations, manufacturing, or general management; aerospace or complex manufacturing experience is considered a strong asset.

• Demonstrated success leading multi functional teams in a unionized environment.

• Strong operational and business acumen, including experience with production planning, cost management, budgeting, and performance reporting.

• Experience leveraging ERP systems and operational reporting tools to drive efficiency and decision making.

• Strong problem solving, analytical, and change management capabilities.

• Demonstrated ability to collaborate with and influence senior leaders and key stakeholders.

• Unwavering commitment to quality, safety, customer service, and continuous improvement.

• Knowledge of Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies is considered an asset.

title: Electrical Project Manager
Account Manager
description:
Build a Territory. Win Business. Grow Your Career.

Prime Material Handling is looking for a driven Account Manager who wants to build a successful career in equipment sales. This isn't a desk job. We're looking for someone who wants to get in front of customers, chase opportunities, build relationships, win deals, and grow their territory. Based out of our Dartmouth head office, you'll be backed by one of the strongest equipment, rental, parts, and service operations in Atlantic Canada. We'll give you the products, training, support, and customer base. What you do with the opportunity is up to you.

## The Opportunity

Prime represents some of the leading equipment brands in the industry, offering forklifts, warehouse equipment, telehandlers, rentals, parts, service, and more. Your job is to grow the business. Develop new accounts, grow existing customers, find opportunities our competitors are missing, and become the person your customers call when they need equipment or advice. The earning potential is significant for someone who performs. The more you sell, the more you earn.

## What You'll Be Doing

• Build, manage, and grow your own sales territory.

• Prospect for new customers and actively pursue new business.

• Grow existing accounts across equipment, rentals, parts, and service.

• Build strong relationships with business owners and decision makers.

• Understand your customers' operations and recommend the right equipment solutions.

• Stay on top of your market, competitors, and opportunities.

• Build a strong pipeline, negotiate deals, and close business.

• Meet and exceed your sales targets.

• Work with our Parts, Service, Rental, and Operations teams to deliver to your customers after the sale.

## Who We Want

We're looking for someone competitive, motivated, and hungry to succeed. You should be comfortable picking up the phone, walking into a new business, meeting customers, and creating opportunities. You don't need to be an equipment expert. We can teach you the equipment. What we can't teach is drive.

## Ideally, You Bring

• 2 to 5 years of sales experience.

• B2B, industrial, automotive, construction, or equipment sales experience is an asset.

• Strong communication and relationship building skills.

• Confidence in dealing with business owners and decision makers.

• A competitive personality and desire to achieve results.

• The ability to work independently and manage your territory.

• A willingness to prospect and develop new business.

• A strong work ethic and commitment to a long-term sales career.

## Why Prime?

• Uncapped earning potential. The more you sell, the more you earn.

• An established customer base with significant room to grow.

• Leading equipment brands and a broad product offering.

• One of Atlantic Canada's strongest service and support networks behind you.

• A family-owned company that makes decisions quickly.

• Training, support, and real opportunities for advancement.

• A sales culture that recognizes and rewards performance.

## Ready to Compete?

If you want to build a territory, compete for business, develop a strong customer base, and have your income reflect the results you produce, we want to talk to you.

Come build your career with Prime Material Handling.

JOB SUMMARY: Responsible for the vessel/installation's positioning and for the continuous on-duty scheme in the control room/bridge. They are also the responsible navigator and shall take the necessary navigational and reporting-related precautions as dictated by the rules of the sea.

## PRE-REQUISITES/QUALIFICATIONS:

• High School Diploma or Equivalent

• Canadian Watchkeeping Mate (Unlimited) License or STCW Equivalent

• Canadian Ballast Control Operator License or STCW Equivalent

• 1 year's experience as a Senior Dynamic Positioning Operator on a DP3 6th Generation Ultra-Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• 2 years experience as a Dynamic Positioning Operator on a DP3 6th Generation Ultra-Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• 5+ years previous experience in a role on a 6th Generation Ultra-Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• DP Unlimited Certificate

• GMDSS License

• Structured and organized mindset

• High level of integrity

• Good verbal and written communication skills in English

• Must pass Physical, Drug Screen and Background/Pre-Employment Screening Checks

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

As the responsible navigating officer, they shall carry out duties and responsibilities as required of a navigating officer on independent duty. The DP Operator console in the main control room (bridge) shall be manned by a qualified DP Operator/1 Officer continuously during all DP operations. This means that the DP Operator/1 Officer must not leave the DP-operator console even for shorter periods of time. The DP Operators/1 Officer relieve each other at the DP-operator console about once every hour.

The DP Operator/1 Officer at the DP-operator console has the following responsibilities and duties:

• Be well familiar with the limitations imposed in connection with dynamic positioning and well-related operations.

• Be responsible for ensuring that the responsible driller is kept continuously updated on the status of the DP system as well as any planned and/or ongoing maintenance/repair that may impact on the DP system.

• Be well familiar with the routines for emergency disconnect of the lower marine riser package (LMRP).

• Perform internal notification in accordance with the document "Well Specific Operating Guidelines (WSOG)".

• Be the area responsible and technical responsible for positioning according to the management system.

• Maintain good communication with the Engine Room Operator, Crane Operator and ROV operator to be able to exchange any important operational information.

• Keep the OIM / Marine Section Leader regularly informed about the operational conditions and consult them in the event of changes.

• In the absence of the OIM / Marine Section Leader or if there is no time, carry out all required actions to safeguard operations and if necessary, stop or interrupt operations.

• Ensure that the DP system, computers, reference systems and sensors are in good condition and are operated in accordance with the stipulated requirements and guidelines.

• Maintain continuous contact with any vessels operating alongside the installation.

• Brief the relieving DP Operator well, when relieved.

• Fill in checklists, keep the DP log and make any reports, while at the same time keeping their personal DP log updated.

The DP Operator/1 Officer who is not at the DP console shall act as a traditional Ballast Control Operator with the following duties and responsibilities:

• Be the area responsible person and have the technical responsibility for the control room/bridge as well as doing the continuous on-duty work in accordance with the marine operations manual.

• Maintain control of the stability and draught of the installation by keeping a constant check on the contents of tanks, weights, and their placing while at the same time helping with the stability calculations.

• Maintain good communication and assist the duty DP Operator when required.

• Keep the deck log, including arrivals and departures of helicopters, supply vessels and standby vessels.

• Be in charge of the daily maintenance and operation of the control room.

• Maintain continuous radio contact with supply vessels and standby vessels from when they arrive and until they depart.

• Be in charge of providing general information and information about safety exercises and emergency situations over the PA system.

• Sound the alarm in connection with emergency situations and safety exercises.

• Acquaint themself and perform their duties in connection with emergency situations in accordance with procedures and the safety plan.

• Be in charge of the continuous duty schedule in the radio station according to the GMDSS requirements if no other radio operator is present.

• They shall not leave the control room unless relieved.

• Observe any non-compliance and immediately report these to their superior.

• Responsible for ensuring that all work is done safely and professionally and actively take part in safety meetings and other meetings.

• Emergency duties according to the unit's emergency organization.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

The above is intended as a summary of the key requirements for the position and is not intended to be a complete list of all duties and responsibilities.

JOB SUMMARY: Responsible for the vessel/installation's positioning and for the continuous on-duty scheme in the control room/bridge. They are also the responsible navigator and shall take the necessary navigational and reporting-related precautions as dictated by the rules of the sea.

## PRE-REQUISITES/QUALIFICATIONS:

• High School Diploma or Equivalent

• Canadian Watchkeeping Mate (Unlimited) License or STCW Equivalent

• Canadian Ballast Control Operator License or STCW Equivalent

• 1 year experience as a Dynamic Positioning Operator on a DP3 6th Generation Ultra-Deepwater Semi-Submersible

• 1 year experience with Posmoor ATA operations on Semi-Submersible

• DP Unlimited Certificate

• GMDSS License

• Structured and organized mindset

• High level of integrity

• Good verbal and written communication skills in English

• Must pass Physical, Drug Screen and Background/Pre-Employment Screening Checks

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

As the responsible navigating officer, they shall carry out duties and responsibilities as required of a navigating officer on independent duty. The DP Operator console in the main control room (bridge) shall be manned by a qualified DP Operator/1 Officer continuously during all DP operations. This means that the DP Operator /1 Officer must not leave the DP-operator console even for shorter periods of time. The DP Operators /1 Officers relieve each other at the DP-operator console about once every hour.

The DP Operator/1 Officer at the DP-operator console has the following responsibilities and duties:

• Be well familiar with the limitations imposed in connection with dynamic positioning and well-related operations.

• Be responsible for ensuring that the responsible driller is kept continuously updated on the status of the DP system as well as any planned and/or ongoing maintenance/repair that may impact on the DP system.

• Be well familiar with the routines for emergency disconnect of the lower marine riser package (LMRP).

• Perform internal notification in accordance with the document "Well Specific Operating Guidelines (WSOG)".

• Be the area responsible and technical responsible for positioning according to the management system.

• Maintain good communication with the Engine Room Operator, Crane Operator and ROV operator to be able to exchange any important operational information.

• Keep the OIM / Marine Section Leader regularly informed about the operational conditions and consult them in the event of changes.

• In the absence of the OIM / Marine Section Leader or if there is no time, carry out all required actions to safeguard operations and if necessary, stop or interrupt operations.

• Ensure that the DP system, computers, reference systems, and sensors are in good condition and are operated in accordance with the stipulated requirements and guidelines.

• Maintain continuous contact with any vessels operating alongside the installation.

• Brief the relieving DP Operator well, when relieved.

• Fill in checklists, keep the DP log, and make any reports, while at the same time keeping their personal DP log updated.

The DP Operator/ 1 Officer who is not at the DP console shall act as a traditional Ballast Control Operator with the following duties and responsibilities:

• Be the area responsible person and have the technical responsibility for the control room/bridge as well as doing the continuous on-duty work in accordance with the marine operations manual.

• Maintain control of the stability and draught of the installation by keeping a constant check on the contents of tanks, weights, and their placing while at the same time helping with the stability calculations.

• Maintain good communication and assist the duty DP Operator when required.

• Keep the deck log, including arrivals and departures of helicopters, supply vessels, and standby vessels.

• Be in charge of the daily maintenance and operation of the control room.

• Maintain continuous radio contact with supply vessels and standby vessels from when they arrive and until they depart.

• Be in charge of providing general information and information about safety exercises and emergency situations over the PA system.

• Sound the alarm in connection with emergency situations and safety exercises.

• Acquaint themself and perform their duties in connection with emergency situations in accordance with procedures and the safety plan.

• Be in charge of the continuous duty schedule in the radio station according to the GMDSS requirements if no other radio operator is present.

• They shall not leave the control room unless relieved.

• Observe any non-compliance and immediately report these to their superior.

• Responsible for ensuring that all work is done safely and professionally and actively take part in safety meetings and other meetings.

• Emergency duties according to the unit's emergency organization.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

The above is intended as a summary of the key requirements for the position and is not intended to be complete list of all duties and responsibilities.

description:
## Job Posting Information

Nuclear Response Team - In Training (Security)
Current and future Term and Regular positions
Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station, New Brunswick, Canada
Competition # E21722-2025

At NB Power we are a team, committed to offering the best customer experience, ensuring energy security, and accelerating a sustainable clean energy transition. Why? Because we're New Brunswickers too, we care about our customers and future generations, and today we are actively looking for new members to join us.

NB Power's Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station is seeking candidates for its Nuclear Response Team (NRT). The Nuclear Response Team is responsible for the security of personnel and assets at the Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station, ensuring compliance of the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) Nuclear Security Regulations, and all applicable NB Power Security procedures and processes. Nuclear Response Team Officers provide armed, tactical response capabilities, on a shift basis, in addition to conducting general security and security-related administrative activities.

## Key functions include, but are not limited to:

• Carrying out foot and vehicle patrols of buildings, grounds, and fence lines. Responding to alarms on site and operate conventional and armored patrol vehicles.
• Be prepared to provide armed, tactical response to a Station security threat.
• Conducting searches of persons, packages, and vehicles entering and leaving the facility, using physical and technological methods to ensure no weapons, explosives or other prohibited items enter the facility and to prevent the unauthorized removal of nuclear material.
• Monitoring and recording all vehicle traffic and personnel entering the site in accordance with approved procedures and operating policies.
• Operating and monitoring surveillance video and intrusion detection equipment located within the Central Alarm Station.
• Investigating incidents and preparing condition reports involving breaches of security regulations or other incidents discovered during security patrols or as requested by the Nuclear Response Team Sergeant.

## Our ideal teammate will have:

• Post secondary certificate, diploma, degree or on track to graduate in June 2025, in one of the following: Police Foundations, Police Science, Law and Security, Criminal Justice, Corrections, Criminology, or a course deemed an equivalent level of education

OR

• Canadian Armed Forces Military Service* of either:

title: Police - Constable
description:
This is direct community contact work carried out in consultation and cooperation with citizens to provide public safety service to: preserve life, protect property, enforce statutes, prevent crime and detect / apprehend offenders / violators, investigate vehicle accidents, use effective problem-solving techniques for problem resolution, and respond to community concerns relative to enhancing the overall quality of life. Work is performed under supervision of senior constables or non-commissioned officers.

## Qualifications Required:

Graduation from a recognized Police Training Institution. The incumbent must meet departmental medical and physical standards, obtain security clearance, and qualify for appointment as a Police Officer in accordance with the New Brunswick Police Act, Regulation 91-498.

## What You'll Do:

Communicate with individuals and groups to prevent and solve criminal activities and address various crime prevention initiatives and respond to quality of life concerns.

Solve problems related to crime causation, community concerns and issues, prevention, protection and court action.

Crisis Intervention for conflict crisis, personal crisis, man-made and natural disasters.

Document and record information on activities for analysis research, legal and court requirements.

Manage information by entering, manipulating, and analyzing information for problem solving, research and investigative purposes.

Educator/Teacher of crime prevention, security, safety, knowledge, information, and skills for individuals and groups in the community.

Prepare cases and take legal action as a result of investigations, the collection of evidence, and the laying of charges pursuant to relevant legislation.

## What You'll Bring:

• Knowledge of and compliance with relevant legislation (Federal Criminal Code, CDS Act, Evidence Act, Provincial – Motor Vehicle, Liquor, Police, Mental Health)

• Standards, policy and procedure, geographic area;

• Skills - communication (interviewing), police vehicle operation, defense and control tactics, fitness (PARE), firearms, basic computer knowledge (RPIC), radar, Breathalyzer (SL2), accident investigation I, dispute (domestic) conflict intervention, documents (notes, reports, forms) incidents, non-complex investigations gather evidence and recognize procedures for complex/major investigations and takes appropriate step/procedures, crisis intervention.

• Bilingualism preferred minimum: French - Basic level (1).

Ethical Standards : Members of the Fredericton Police Force have a significant role in building and maintaining the public trust by upholding the highest ethical standards both on and off duty. Applicants to the Fredericton Police Force must be prepared to follow our core values and act professionally, respectfully, with integrity, and with compassion in accordance to the law and the New Brunswick Police Act and Regulations.

Perks :

• Competitive salary range ($2,755.66 - $4,305.72).

• Bi-weekly benefit spending allowance of $305.

• Health, Dental, and Pension plans.

• A broad range of policing opportunities within the department.

• Cutting-edge technology, training, and equipment.

Apply Now!
Please submit your application on or before December 31, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. AST.

If you have any questions email hr@fredericton.ca.

Please Include:

• Cover Letter - Please indicate your earliest possible start date.

• Up to date résumé - maximum 3 pages

• Proof of graduation from certified Police Training Academy or as a Career Officer. Military police provide QL status.

• Current contact information

• Complete Employment History

• Education and Qualifications

• Specialized Training

## The City of Fredericton is an equal opportunity employer.

We thank you for your application however, only those selected for screening will be contacted.
